risks.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule are maintained and disposed of according to the applicable schedule identified within application specific PIAs and the covering SORNs.
risks.rationale: Data retention without proper controls can increase the risk of prolonged exposure.

risks.description: Integration with third-party applications and cloud environments may introduce vulnerabilities.
risks.evidence_quote: Salesforce integrates with other CFPB-authorized third-party cloud system environments for purposes such as the storage of data.
risks.rationale: Third-party integrations can introduce new security risks and attack vectors.

risks.description: Limited user authentication controls may increase the risk of unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Salesforce is connected to Entra ID to authenticate access for internal CFPB users. Authorized external users must log in to the applications using an email, password, and multi-factor authentication.
risks.rationale: Reliance on multi-factor authentication for external users may not fully mitigate all authentication risks.

risks.description: Public-facing Salesforce applications may be vulnerable to unauthorized access or attacks.
risks.evidence_quote: Salesforce provides a selection of ‘out of the box’ functionality and custom tools to build internal and external facing applications that support various efforts such as consumer engagement and outreach.
risks.rationale: Public-facing applications increase the risk of exposure to external attacks.

risks.description: Data migration and storage in Salesforce may expose sensitive information if not properly secured.
risks.evidence_quote: The Salesforce Platform is connected to Entra ID to authenticate access for internal CFPB users.
risks.rationale: Data migration processes may introduce vulnerabilities if not properly secured.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security assessments and audits of Salesforce and its integrations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All third-party cloud systems that connect with Salesforce are assessed according CFPB’s assessment and authorization (A&A) processes to ensure risks are identified and mitigated prior to use.
mitigations.rationale: Security assessments help identify and mitigate risks in third-party systems.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for all PII at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data from unauthorized access during storage and transmission.

mitigations.description: Implement centralized logging and monitoring for all data collection points.
mitigations.rationale: Centralized logging enhances visibility and response to potential data handling issues.

mitigations.description: Limit access to Salesforce to only those with a business need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorized CFPB program managers, business product and system owners, system developers and business analysts, and other internal CFPB stakeholders and users, can access Salesforce to leverage these technical capabilities.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls reduce the risk of internal data misuse.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization practices to reduce the amount of PII shared externally.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of shared data minimizes the risk of exposure.

mitigations.description: Implement regular data audits to ensure compliance with retention schedules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Each collection of data at the application level has a records schedule that has been submitted to and approved by National Archives and Records Administration (NARA).
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits ensure data is retained only as long as necessary.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular vulnerability assessments on third-party integrations.
mitigations.rationale: Vulnerability assessments help identify and mitigate risks in third-party integrations.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for all user access, including internal users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorized external users must log in to the applications using an email, password, and multi-factor authentication.
mitigations.rationale: Multi-factor authentication enhances security for user access.

mitigations.description: Implement Web Application Firewalls (WAF) to protect public-facing applications.
mitigations.rationale: WAFs help protect against common web-based attacks.

mitigations.description: Implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls during data migration.
mitigations.rationale: DLP controls help ensure data is not lost or exposed during migration.

risks.description: The ICAM program collects and stores sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) directly from individuals, including personal cell numbers and home addresses, which could pose a risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects a very limited amount of PII directly from individuals by allowing customization of their CFPB digital identity profile, such as their preferred job title, preferred pronouns, and a primary phone number such as a personal cell number and personal address if the individual works from home.
risks.rationale: Direct collection of sensitive PII increases the risk of exposure if security measures fail.

risks.description: The ICAM program shares data with external parties, including third-party services like Login.gov, which may increase the risk of data exposure due to vulnerabilities in third-party systems.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program primarily uses PII collected by indirect sources such as CFPB employment applications and contractor onboarding forms housed within ABIS5 and HR Connect6, and from other federal agency sources such as USAstaffing7, USAccess8, and Login.gov.
risks.rationale: Third-party data sharing introduces risks associated with third-party security practices.

risks.description: The ICAM program collects more PII than necessary for its stated purposes, increasing the risk of misuse or unauthorized access to unnecessary data.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects a very limited amount of PII directly from individuals by allowing customization of their CFPB digital identity profile, such as their preferred job title, preferred pronouns, and a primary phone number such as a personal cell number and personal address if the individual works from home.
risks.rationale: Excessive collection of PII beyond what is necessary increases privacy risks.

risks.description: The ICAM program relies on access controls and authentication mechanisms, but the effectiveness of these controls depends on the adherence to RoBs and PUA, which may not be fully enforced or monitored.
risks.evidence_quote: RoBs and PUAs are approved by system owners.
risks.rationale: Inadequate enforcement of access controls can lead to unauthorized access to sensitive systems and data.

risks.description: The ICAM program's data retention policies are not explicitly detailed, which could lead to unnecessary retention of PII and increased risk of data exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB ICAM program comprises three structural areas: • Identity Governance and Administration – Monitors and ensures that user identities and access rights remain properly managed, secure, and monitored.
risks.rationale: Undefined retention periods increase the risk of prolonged data storage and potential breaches.

risks.description: The ICAM program's reliance on third-party authentication services like Login.gov may expose the system to vulnerabilities in these external services, potentially compromising the integrity of the CFPB's identity management system.
risks.evidence_quote: In the case of Login.gov, it creates a single digital trusted identity across multiple federal systems and services.
risks.rationale: Third-party authentication services can introduce risks beyond the control of the CFPB.

risks.description: The ICAM program does not explicitly state that encryption is used to protect PII during transmission and storage, which could increase the risk of data interception or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Information from these sources is collected via an application programming interface (API), and through other secure data transmission methods, and flat text files to connect the centralized ICAM data hub to these data sources.
risks.rationale: Lack of explicit encryption measures increases the risk of data breaches during transmission.

risks.description: The ICAM program's use of privileged access management (PAM) may not be fully effective if system owners do not consistently enforce RoBs and PUA, leading to potential unauthorized access to privileged accounts.
risks.evidence_quote: RoBs and PUAs are approved by system owners.
risks.rationale: Inadequate enforcement of privileged access controls can lead to unauthorized access to high-privilege accounts.

risks.description: The ICAM program's identity governance and administration functions may not provide sufficient transparency to data subjects regarding how their PII is used and shared, potentially violating privacy expectations.
risks.evidence_quote: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
risks.rationale: Lack of transparency can lead to individuals being unaware of how their data is used and shared.

risks.description: The ICAM program's authentication and authorization mechanisms may be vulnerable to phishing or social engineering attacks, given the complexity of managing access across diverse IT systems and external parties.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program manages a suite of enterprise tools and applications to create and manage digital IDs and access to CFPB IT resources.
risks.rationale: Complexity in managing access across diverse systems increases vulnerability to attacks.

mitigations.description: Implement strong encryption for all PII transmissions and storage to mitigate the risk of data interception.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption is a standard measure to protect data integrity and confidentiality.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits of third-party services like Login.gov to ensure they meet CFPB's security standards.
mitigations.rationale: Third-party audits can identify and mitigate vulnerabilities in external systems.

mitigations.description: Adopt data minimization practices by collecting only the PII necessary for identity verification and access management.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary data reduces exposure in case of a breach.

mitigations.description: Implement continuous monitoring and automated enforcement of RoBs and PUA to ensure adherence to access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Automated enforcement reduces reliance on manual processes and increases compliance.

mitigations.description: Establish clear and defined data retention policies to ensure PII is retained only for the necessary duration.
mitigations.rationale: Defined retention periods reduce risks associated with prolonged data storage.

mitigations.description: Diversify authentication services and maintain contingency plans in case of third-party service disruptions.
mitigations.rationale: Diversification reduces reliance on a single point of failure.

mitigations.description: Encrypt all PII transmissions and storage to prevent unauthorized access during data movement.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data from interception during transmission.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged access to reduce the risk of unauthorized access.
mitigations.rationale: MFA adds an additional layer of security for privileged accounts.

mitigations.description: Provide clear and accessible privacy notices to data subjects explaining how their PII is used and shared.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency builds trust and ensures compliance with privacy expectations.

mitigations.description: Train staff on phishing and social engineering awareness to reduce vulnerabilities in the authentication process.
mitigations.rationale: Awareness training reduces human error in security practices.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to the Supervision and Examination System (SES) due to the inclusion of external users and state regulators.
risks.evidence_quote: This portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators.
risks.rationale: The inclusion of external users increases the potential for unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches due to the use of a cloud-based platform (Salesforce).
risks.evidence_quote: The SES resides within the Salesforce2 cloud platform and leverages the capabilities of the cloud architecture including the automated collection of information requests, concurrent collaboration between internal assessments, and tracking of document reviews during the examination process.
risks.rationale: Cloud platforms are often targeted by malicious actors due to their centralized nature and valuable data.

risks.description: Risk of excessive data collection beyond what is necessary for supervision activities.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is required by statute to primarily use, to the fullest extent possible, information available from other agencies or reported publicly before contacting the supervised entity to gather additional information.
risks.rationale: The requirement to use existing data may lead to over-collection of PII.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate access controls for the SES application.
risks.evidence_quote: Identification and provisioning of these entity representatives is completed within the SES application by limited sets of CFPB users designated
risks.rationale: Limited user provisioning may not adequately restrict access to the application.

risks.description: Risk of data retention without clear retention policies.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB also collects PII directly from consumers of supervised entities, from consumer complaints, and from employees of the CFPB.
risks.rationale: The system does not explicitly state a data retention schedule, leading to potential over-retention of PII.

risks.description: Risk of third-party vendor risks associated with the Salesforce platform.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES resides within the Salesforce2 cloud platform and leverages the capabilities of the cloud architecture including the automated collection of information requests, concurrent collaboration between internal assessments, and tracking of document reviews during the examination process.
risks.rationale: Third-party vendors may introduce vulnerabilities or comply inadequately with privacy standards.

risks.description: Risk of data exposure through the CFPB Supervision Portal.
risks.evidence_quote: This portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators.
risks.rationale: Data transmitted through the portal may be intercepted or exposed if communication is not secured.

risks.description: Risk of lack of consumer consent for data collection.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may use PII to contact consumers to collect and verify additional information required for supervision activities.
risks.rationale: Consumers may not be adequately informed or consent to the collection and use of their PII.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate monitoring of access to PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES contains PII regarding consumers of depository and non-depository entities products as well as employees of those entities serving as points of contact.
risks.rationale: Without continuous monitoring, unauthorized access or misuse of PII may go undetected.

risks.description: Risk of data integrity issues due to concurrent collaboration features.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES resides within the Salesforce2 cloud platform and leverages the capabilities of the cloud architecture including the automated collection of information requests, concurrent collaboration between internal assessments, and tracking of document reviews during the examination process.
risks.rationale: Concurrent access by multiple users may lead to accidental or intentional data corruption.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for external users accessing the SES.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced authentication reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit within the Salesforce platform.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data from unauthorized access and breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization practices to collect only necessary PII.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary data reduces the risk of exposure.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits of user access and permissions within the SES application.
mitigations.rationale: Audits ensure that access controls are effective and up-to-date.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear and published data retention schedule for PII.
mitigations.rationale: A retention schedule ensures that data is not retained longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular third-party risk assessments of Salesforce and other cloud providers.
mitigations.rationale: Risk assessments identify and mitigate third-party vulnerabilities.

mitigations.description: Implement secure communication channels for data transmitted through the Supervision Portal.
mitigations.rationale: Secure channels prevent data interception during transmission.

mitigations.description: Provide clear privacy notices and obtain explicit consent from consumers before collecting PII.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and consent reduce the risk of privacy violations.

mitigations.description: Implement continuous monitoring for access to PII within the SES.
mitigations.rationale: Continuous monitoring detects unauthorized access promptly.

mitigations.description: Implement version control and access logging for collaborative documents in the SES.
mitigations.rationale: Version control and logging reduce the risk of data integrity issues.

risks.description: The system handles sensitive personal information such as Social Security Numbers (SSNs), which are optional but can be submitted.
risks.evidence_quote: Social Security Numbers are not submitted for all complaints and is not required. For some complaints, submission of a Social Security Number can be helpful to validate the consumer’s identity and their association with a particular account, such as a credit report.
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive personal data that, if mishandled, could lead to identity theft or fraud.

risks.description: The system is vulnerable to potential data breaches due to its reliance on a vendor-provided cloud platform.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform.
risks.rationale: Cloud platforms, while secure, are not immune to breaches, and the lack of explicit encryption or access controls is a concern.

risks.description: Consumer complaints and inquiries are shared with third parties, including financial service providers and government agencies, increasing the risk of misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: In addressing a complaint or inquiry, Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the CFPB for further administrative action.
risks.rationale: Sharing data with third parties increases the attack surface and the risk of unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: The long retention period of 60 years for consumer complaints and inquiries increases the risk of data exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform2.
risks.rationale: Storing data for an extended period increases the likelihood of data breaches or leaks over time.

mitigations.description: Implement strong encryption for Social Security Numbers and other sensitive data stored in the CRS.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures that even if data is accessed, it remains protected and unreadable.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for the cloud platform to mitigate breach risks.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls and encryption reduce the risk of unauthorized access to the cloud platform.

mitigations.description: Require data sharing agreements with third parties to ensure they comply with privacy and security standards.
mitigations.rationale: Data sharing agreements can enforce security measures and limit misuse of shared data.

mitigations.description: Review and shorten the retention period for consumer complaints and inquiries to reduce exposure risks.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the retention period minimizes the time window during which data is vulnerable to breaches.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data stored in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: The use of a contractor-owned environment introduces potential risks of unauthorized access or mishandling of sensitive data.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches due to inadequate security measures in the contractor's environment.
risks.evidence_quote: The support services described in this PIA Appendix are otherwise covered by the LTST PIA. The categories of individuals and records; the purpose and uses for collection; and associated privacy risks, mitigations, and controls, are identified and covered by the PIA.
risks.rationale: Inadequate security measures in the contractor's environment could lead to unauthorized access or data breaches.

risks.description: Risk of exposure of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) through improper redaction.
risks.evidence_quote: eDiscovery tools provide redaction capabilities which allows for and automates the identification of protected information (e.g., personally identifiable information) by searching for names, phrases, and terms (collectively, “keywords”) that are input by the reviewing attorney.
risks.rationale: Improper redaction of PII could lead to accidental exposure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Risk of metadata exposure through processing and analysis of electronic records.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats and identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process.
risks.rationale: Metadata can contain sensitive information that, if exposed, could lead to privacy violations.

risks.description: Risk of overretention or improper disposal of sensitive data due to unclear retention policies.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: Overretention of data increases the risk of exposure and potential misuse.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access during forensic data collection from external entities.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: Forensic data collection from external entities could introduce vulnerabilities if not properly secured.

risks.description: Risk of dependency on third-party tools and services for data processing and management.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB employs the Legal Technology Support Team (LTST), which hosts and provides Enforcement with a suite of eDiscovery applications and tools to process and manage these legal activities.
risks.rationale: Dependency on third-party tools increases the risk of data breaches or mismanagement.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate oversight and auditing of contractor's data handling processes.
risks.evidence_quote: The support services described in this PIA Appendix are otherwise covered by the LTST PIA.
risks.rationale: Inadequate oversight of the contractor's data handling processes could lead to privacy violations.

risks.description: Risk of accidental exposure of sensitive information due to human error during data processing.
risks.evidence_quote: eDiscovery tools provide redaction capabilities which allows for and automates the identification of protected information (e.g., personally identifiable information) by searching for names, phrases, and terms (collectively, “keywords”) that are input by the reviewing attorney.
risks.rationale: Human error during data processing could lead to accidental exposure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Risk of insufficient encryption or data protection during transmission and storage.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: Insufficient encryption or data protection measures could lead to unauthorized access or data breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement strong access controls and authentication mechanisms for the contractor's environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB employs the Legal Technology Support Team (LTST), which hosts and provides Enforcement with a suite of eDiscovery applications and tools to process and manage these legal activities.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access controls reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments of the contractor's environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The support services described in this PIA Appendix are otherwise covered by the LTST PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits and assessments help identify and mitigate security vulnerabilities.

mitigations.description: Implement automated redaction tools with strict keyword validation processes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: eDiscovery tools provide redaction capabilities which allows for and automates the identification of protected information (e.g., personally identifiable information) by searching for names, phrases, and terms (collectively, “keywords”) that are input by the reviewing attorney.
mitigations.rationale: Automated redaction tools with keyword validation reduce the risk of improper redaction.

mitigations.description: Sanitize metadata before processing and analysis to remove sensitive information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats and identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process.
mitigations.rationale: Sanitizing metadata reduces the risk of exposure of sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Establish clear retention policies and implement automated data disposal processes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: Clear retention policies and automated data disposal reduce the risk of overretention.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit during forensic data collection.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data during forensic collection and reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular third-party risk assessments and vendor audits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The support services described in this PIA Appendix are otherwise covered by the LTST PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Regular third-party audits reduce the risk of data breaches or mismanagement.

mitigations.description: Establish a robust oversight framework with regular monitoring of the contractor's data handling processes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The support services described in this PIA Appendix are otherwise covered by the LTST PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Robust oversight and monitoring reduce the risk of privacy violations.

mitigations.description: Provide comprehensive training and awareness programs for staff handling sensitive data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: Training and awareness programs reduce the risk of human error.

mitigations.description: Implement end-to-end encryption for all data transmission and storage processes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this Appendix to the LTST Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to document and assess the privacy risks associated with maintaining CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: End-to-end encryption protects data from unauthorized access during transmission and storage.

risks.description: Collection of sensitive personal and business information that could be used for identity theft or fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: Once the user or POC accesses the SBL system though Login.gov, they are directed to create the User Profile within the SBL system. This information includes full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address.
risks.rationale: The collection of personal identifiers increases the risk of identity theft or fraud if the data is compromised.

risks.description: Potential inaccuracies in the collected data affecting fair lending enforcement and community development efforts.
risks.evidence_quote: The data that will be collected by covered financial institutions from small business credit applicants includes... gross annual revenue for the preceding fiscal year; ... the number of workers that the applicant has; the applicant’s time in business; and the number of principal owners the applicant has.
risks.rationale: Inaccuracies in collected data could lead to incorrect conclusions about business needs and opportunities.

risks.description: Risk of data retention without a specified retention period, potentially leading to data accumulation and increased privacy risks.
risks.evidence_quote: RETENTION [No information provided in the input.]
risks.rationale: Undefined retention periods can result in unnecessary data storage and increased exposure risks.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access or breaches due to reliance on Login.gov without additional security measures.
risks.evidence_quote: Once the user or POC accesses the SBL system though Login.gov, they are directed to create the User Profile within the SBL system.
risks.rationale: Single-factor authentication increases vulnerability to unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of data being shared with third parties without adequate privacy protections, potentially exposing sensitive information.
risks.evidence_quote: enabling communities, governmental entities, and creditors to identify business and community development needs and opportunities of women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses.
risks.rationale: Sharing data with third parties increases the attack surface and exposure risks.

risks.description: Risk of collecting more data than necessary, increasing privacy risks and potential misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: However, for purposes of beta-testing, any information submitted beyond user or POC business contact information, including information regarding small business loan application filing, is only fake data.
risks.rationale: Excessive data collection beyond what is necessary increases privacy risks.

risks.description: Risk of lack of transparency and user awareness regarding data collection and use.
risks.evidence_quote: What is the purpose? ... Are there controls to enforce accountability? Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply. What opportunities do I have for participation? Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
risks.rationale: Users may not be fully informed about how their data is collected and used.

risks.description: Risk of non-compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, leading to legal consequences.
risks.evidence_quote: Section 1071 of the Consumer Protection Act of 2010... amended the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA), 15 U.S.C. 1691 et. seq. (hereinafter Section 1071) to require covered financial institutions to collect data regarding applications for credit for women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses and report it to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
risks.rationale: Failure to comply with legal requirements can result in penalties and legal action.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit to protect sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures that even if data is intercepted, it remains unreadable.

mitigations.description: Implement data validation and verification processes to ensure accuracy.
mitigations.rationale: Accurate data collection reduces the risk of incorrect conclusions.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear data retention policy with specific retention periods and data deletion procedures.
mitigations.rationale: Defined retention periods minimize the risk of data accumulation and exposure.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for accessing the SBL system in addition to Login.gov.
mitigations.rationale: MFA adds an additional layer of security against unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Implement data sharing agreements with third parties that include privacy protections and data use limitations.
mitigations.rationale: Data sharing agreements ensure third parties handle data responsibly.

mitigations.description: Adopt data minimization practices to collect only the minimum necessary information.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary data reduces privacy risks.

mitigations.description: Provide clear privacy notices and obtain user consent for data collection and use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: What opportunities do I have for participation? Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and user consent reduce the risk of privacy violations.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Audits help identify and address compliance gaps.

risks.description: Risk of data breach due to collection of sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) from nonbank representatives and executives.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System collects information on authorized representatives, attesting executives, and in documents uploaded to the system (i.e., the covered order, related public records, or other documents), individuals listed or included in the covered order, such as a consumer or respondent.
risks.rationale: The system collects extensive PII, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or data breach.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information due to third-party access to the NBR System.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share information in the NBR System directly with other federal, state, tribal, and local regulators to facilitate the work of those agencies, in accordance with its existing information-sharing agreements and protocols.
risks.rationale: Third-party access increases the risk of data exposure.

risks.description: Risk of data minimization concerns as the system collects more PII than necessary for its stated purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System collects information on authorized representatives, attesting executives, and in documents uploaded to the system (i.e., the covered order, related public records, or other documents), individuals listed or included in the covered order, such as a consumer or respondent.
risks.rationale: Excessive collection of PII beyond what is necessary for registration and compliance monitoring.

risks.description: Risk of data aging and potential misuse due to the lack of a defined records retention schedule.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently, there is no NARA-approved records retention schedule for NBR records. Therefore, the records are unscheduled and considered permanent in nature until NARA’s approval to disposition is obtained.
risks.rationale: Permanent retention increases the risk of outdated data being exposed or misused.

risks.description: Risk of public exposure of sensitive information through publication in the public registry.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may publish some of the information collected from nonbanks for use by members of the public as well as other regulatory agencies.
risks.rationale: Public publication could inadvertently expose sensitive details from covered orders.

risks.description: Risk of insider threats or misuse of data by CFPB staff with access to the NBR System.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is responsible for regulating (among other things) the offering and provision of consumer financial products and services under federal consumer financial laws.
risks.rationale: Staff access to sensitive data increases the risk of internal misuse.

risks.description: Risk of insecure storage of data in the Salesforce environment.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System resides within the CFPB Salesforce environment and leverages the capabilities of cloud architecture.
risks.rationale: Cloud storage introduces risks associated with third-party infrastructure.

risks.description: Risk of insufficient encryption for data at rest or in transit.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System resides within the CFPB Salesforce environment and leverages the capabilities of cloud architecture.
risks.rationale: Lack of encryption could lead to unauthorized access during transmission or storage.

risks.description: Risk of social engineering attacks targeting the helpdesk feature.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System provides a helpdesk feature that allows members of the public to ask questions about the Orders Rule and for NBR account users to submit a question to the CFPB to help resolve a technical issue or issue related to the submission of information.
risks.rationale: Public-facing helpdesk increases vulnerability to phishing or social engineering.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate audit logging for system access and activities.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is responsible for regulating (among other things) the offering and provision of consumer financial products and services under federal consumer financial laws.
risks.rationale: Insufficient logging could hinder detection and response to unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Implement strong encryption for data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data from unauthorized access during transmission and storage.

mitigations.description: Limit third-party access to the minimum necessary for regulatory compliance.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing third-party access minimizes exposure risks.

mitigations.description: Adopt data minimization practices to collect only necessary PII.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only essential data reduces the risk of exposure.

mitigations.description: Develop and implement a records retention schedule approved by NARA.
mitigations.rationale: Scheduled retention ensures timely disposal of outdated records.

mitigations.description: Implement redaction protocols for sensitive information in published orders.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction prevents exposure of sensitive details in public records.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular insider threat training and monitoring for CFPB staff.
mitigations.rationale: Training and monitoring reduce the risk of internal misuse.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits of the Salesforce environment.
mitigations.rationale: Audits ensure cloud infrastructure meets security standards.

mitigations.description: Require multi-factor authentication for all system access.
mitigations.rationale: MFA adds an extra layer of security against unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of unintended PII sharing through collaboration features in the GIS system.

risks.description: Potential lack of notice to individuals when their information is collected from third-party sources, which may violate privacy expectations and legal requirements.

risks.description: Inadequate verification of data accuracy and completeness from third-party sources, which may lead to errors or outdated information in the Directory Database.

risks.description: Sensitive personal information, including Social Security Numbers (SSNs), is stored and used in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The Administrative Billing and Collections (ABCO) system provides billings for administrative accounts receivable on a weekly basis. It uses HR data of federal employees who have outstanding debts, including their name, their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as 'Debtor ID' in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).
risks.rationale: Storing SSNs increases the risk of identity theft if the data is compromised.

risks.description: The system does not provide individuals with notice before collecting their personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: 6.1 Was notice provided to the individual prior to collection of information? No. The ABCO system uses personal data provided by agencies to generate reports or notices. These are used by each agency to notify the individual of the status of debts owed. Only authorized agency users have access to ABCO data.
risks.rationale: Lack of notice violates privacy expectations and legal requirements for data collection.

risks.description: The system allows multiple federal agencies and external organizations to access personal information, increasing the risk of unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: 5.1 With which external organization(s) is the information shared, what information is shared, and for what purpose? Approximately 160 Federal agencies payroll by the NFC have access to their specific agency information. Information collected by ABCO is owned by each agency. Each agency determines the use and sharing of their information. NFC maintains and secures the information on behalf of our customers. Access is determined by agencies functional managers and submitted to agency security officers.
risks.rationale: Broad access increases the attack surface and potential for misuse of sensitive data.

risks.description: The system retains data indefinitely, which may exceed necessary retention periods and increase breach risks.
risks.evidence_quote: 3.1 How long is information retained? The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA General Records Schedule GRS-1-1 (Financial Management and Reporting Records). ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the likelihood of data breaches over time.

risks.description: Individuals do not have access to their personal information in the system, limiting their ability to verify accuracy.
risks.evidence_quote: 7.1 What are the procedures that allow individuals to gain access to their information? Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Denying individuals access undermines transparency and their right to verify data accuracy.

risks.description: The system relies on agencies to determine data sharing and access, which may not consistently enforce privacy protections.
risks.evidence_quote: 5.1 With which external organization(s) is the information shared, what information is shared, and for what purpose? Approximately 160 Federal agencies payroll by the NFC have access to their specific agency information. Information collected by ABCO is owned by each agency. Each agency determines the use and sharing of their information. NFC maintains and secures the information on behalf of our customers. Access is determined by agencies functional managers and submitted to agency security officers.
risks.rationale: Agency-level decisions may not always prioritize robust privacy protections.

risks.description: The system uses SSNs as 'Debtor ID,' which may not be the minimum necessary for billing purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: The Administrative Billing and Collections (ABCO) system provides billings for administrative accounts receivable on a weekly basis. It uses HR data of federal employees who have outstanding debts, including their name, their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as 'Debtor ID' in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).

risks.description: Risk of data breaches due to the storage and processing of sensitive personal information (PII) in a centralized data warehouse.
risks.evidence_quote: The Farm Service Information Management System (FSIMS) allows FSA to efficiently store, organize and manage large amounts of information, which can be used for auditing, analysis and reporting purposes. FSIMS is comprised of the following applications: o Enterprise Data Warehouse (Data Vault) (EDW DV) o Legacy Informix Reporting Systems (INFOR) o Oracle Reporting Systems (ORAC)
risks.rationale: Centralized storage of sensitive data increases the risk of unauthorized access and breaches.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information due to potential vulnerabilities in legacy systems.
risks.evidence_quote: The EDW DV is a consolidated data warehouse that provides information to FSA national, state, and county personnel. The EDW DV is designed to facilitate data retrieval and reporting by providing a central stable location for data storage across FSA’s business enterprise.
risks.rationale: Legacy systems like Informix and Oracle may have outdated security protocols, making them more susceptible to attacks.

risks.description: Risk of data exposure due to sharing information with external organizations, including commercial entities.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV does not directly share information with external entities; However, FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Sharing data with external entities increases the risk of unintended disclosures and potential misuse.

risks.description: Risk of data integrity issues due to the use of multiple data sources and ETL processes.
risks.evidence_quote: The EDW DV will extract transform and load information from multiple SAP source systems including MIDAS, WBSCM and FMMI, as well as non-SAP systems, such as Farm Records, GIS, Eligibility, and Financial data from SQL Server systems.
risks.rationale: ETL processes can introduce errors or inconsistencies if not properly managed, affecting the accuracy of the data.

risks.description: Risk of excessive data retention leading to unnecessary exposure of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Excessive retention of data increases the risk of exposure over time.

risks.description: Risk of insider threats due to access controls not being adequately enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Unauthorized access by internal personnel could lead to intentional or accidental exposure of sensitive data.

risks.description: Risk of data loss or corruption due to the use of multiple data marts and databases.
risks.evidence_quote: The EDW DV consists of five major architectural components: • Oracle database – This is the database that houses the migrated and new data marts. • Oracle Data Integrator (ODI), IBM DataStage, Informix Stored Procedures/Scripts – These are the ETL component used to transform the data from the sources into the Oracle database.
risks.rationale: Multiple data marts and databases increase the complexity of data management and the risk of data loss.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate retention period oversight for DOL case numbers.

mitigations.description: Enhance security measures for data in transit beyond HTTPS.

mitigations.description: Implement logging and monitoring for data flow through FPAC CASP.

mitigations.description: Document routine uses in SORNs for sharing PII with external agencies.

mitigations.description: Ensure retention periods are approved by records officers.
mitigations.rationale: Approval ensures compliance with regulatory requirements.

risks.description: The system collects and stores a wide range of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), including sensitive data such as Social Security Numbers (SSNs), financial data, and health information.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS data may include a wide range of PII in the areas of financial, natural resources, and general information. Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
risks.rationale: The system handles sensitive PII, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.

risks.description: The system allows access to PII for a variety of internal users, including auditors and records managers, which could potentially lead to unauthorized disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights. Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Broad access increases the risk of accidental or intentional misuse of PII.

risks.description: The system stores PII in multiple databases, including MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, and Elasticsearch database, which could pose risks if these databases are not adequately secured.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
risks.rationale: Multiple databases increase the attack surface and potential points of failure in security measures.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely for some records, which could lead to prolonged exposure of PII beyond its original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long-term retention increases the risk of data exposure over time.

risks.description: The system allows contractors to access sensitive information, which could pose a risk if contractors do not adhere to the same security standards as internal staff.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? • Yes. Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Third-party access increases the risk of data breaches or misuse.

mitigations.description: Implement strong encryption for all PII stored in databases.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields. Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data at rest from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit access to PII to only those with a verified need-to-know and enforce strict access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access granted to end users, is approved by IAL2 and are given privileges based on a least privileged model. Administrators, access to the TeamMate Plus application is restricted to 5 number of people.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege model reduces the risk of accidental or intentional misuse.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments on all databases to ensure they are adequately secured.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits help identify and mitigate security gaps in database systems.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear data retention policy with specific time limits for retaining PII, ensuring data is deleted after a set period.
mitigations.rationale: Time-limited retention reduces the exposure period of PII.

mitigations.description: Require contractors to sign non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) and conduct background checks before granting access to the system.
mitigations.rationale: NDAs and background checks reduce the risk of third-party misuse.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive PII such as SSNs and EINs due to the use of a VPN for data transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: This data is transmitted via a dedicated VPN line
risks.rationale: The use of a VPN line may not provide sufficient security against advanced persistent threats or insider threats.

risks.description: Risk of exposure of PII to external entities due to sharing with Approved Insurance Providers (AIPs) and RMA’s Strategic Data Analysis Division.
risks.evidence_quote: The data is primarily shared with the RMA Strategic Data Analysis Division... Policy information is shared only with the Approved insurance Providers (AIP).
risks.rationale: Sharing PII with multiple external and internal entities increases the risk of unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: Risk of long-term retention of PII without a clear need, potentially increasing privacy exposure over time.

risks.rationale: Indefinite retention of PII increases the risk of data exposure over time, especially if data is not properly secured.

risks.description: Risk of over-collection of PII due to the inclusion of multiple applications with varying PII requirements.

risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Third-party contractors accessing the system may pose a risk if their security practices are not adequately vetted or controlled.

mitigations.description: Enhance VPN encryption and implement multi-factor authentication for VPN access.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger encryption and MFA can reduce the risk of unauthorized access to the VPN line.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization practices to collect only the PII necessary for each application's purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of PII collected minimizes the risk of exposure when sharing with external and internal entities.

mitigations.description: Establish a periodic review process to assess the necessity of indefinite retention of PII and implement a data archiving policy with a retention schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic reviews can ensure that PII is only retained as long as necessary, reducing long-term exposure risks.

mitigations.description: Conduct a data inventory and assessment to identify and remove unnecessary PII collection across applications.

mitigations.description: Require third-party contractors to undergo background checks and sign non-disclosure agreements before granting access to the system.

risks.description: Exposure of sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers and financial data to unauthorized parties.
risks.evidence_quote: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”) administers the housing counseling program2, which provides counseling to consumers on seeking, financing, maintaining, renting, or owning a home. The HUD housing counseling assistance program (“HUD housing counseling program”) enables anyone who wants to (or already does) rent or own housing to get the counseling they need to make their rent or mortgage payments, and to
risks.rationale: The system collects and makes available sensitive personal information, increasing the risk of unauthorized exposure.

risks.description: Potential data breach due to inadequate security measures protecting the sensitive information stored and transmitted by the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB housing counselor locator tool and HUD API connection to its counselor dataset are intended for use by the public. The API, owned and managed by HUD, enables users to retrieve the HUD counselor dataset and use that data for their own applications or systems outside of CFPB.
risks.rationale: Public access and third-party integration increase the attack surface, necessitating strong security measures.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to the system's data due to lack of proper authentication mechanisms for API access.
risks.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov. There is no authorization process for read‐only access to the dataset or for use of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool. Users cannot write to the system. The CFPB relies on the HUD API to make the dataset available and to populate results in the locator tool. CFPB employees do not have the ability to write to the system.
risks.rationale: Public and API access without authentication increases the risk of unauthorized data extraction.

risks.description: Risk of third-party misuse of data collected through the API, as third-party developers may not implement adequate security measures.
risks.evidence_quote: The HUD API and the CFPB housing counselor locator tool also enables users to download or share data in the HUD counselor dataset in a variety of formats. HUD hosts the API, and users who develop a program and incorporate the API can present the HUD data in a variety of formats. It is likely that lenders or third‐party developers will develop formats that are in compliance with the interpretive rule.
risks.rationale: Third-party developers may lack security protocols, risking exposure of sensitive data.

risks.description: Risk of data retention exceeding necessary periods, leading to prolonged exposure and potential misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: HUD’s schedule for records contained in the HUD counselor dataset is outlined in HUD’s SORN for the records, HUD/DEPT‐22 – Housing Counseling. Additionally, records collected through consumerfinance.gov (user analytics and ZIP codes entered in the locator tool) are being managed as permanent records until the disposition schedule for these records is approved by the National Archives and Records Administration, at which time, the CFPB will dispose of such files in accordance with the schedule.
risks.rationale: Data retention without a clear schedule increases exposure risk over time.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate access controls, allowing unauthorized individuals to access sensitive information without proper authorization.
risks.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov. There is no authorization process for read‐only access to the dataset or for use of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool. Users cannot write to the system. The CFPB relies on the HUD API to make the dataset available and to populate results in the locator tool. CFPB employees do not have the ability to write to the system.
risks.rationale: Lack of access controls increases the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data.

risks.description: Risk of individuals' personal information being shared publicly without their consent, potentially leading to identity theft or other privacy violations.
risks.evidence_quote: HUD and its authorizing statutes and regulations for the housing counseling program allow the public disclosure of the HUD counseling dataset. The CFPB is republishing this publicly available data on its website and creating a tool by which users can more easily search the dataset in order to locate HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies in their area.
risks.rationale: Public disclosure without consent risks individual privacy and identity theft.

risks.description: Risk of lenders or other entities misusing the information collected through the system for purposes beyond compliance with regulations.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is increasing access to the HUD counselor dataset in an effort to make the information more useful to the public, and in order to help lenders comply with the requirements outlined in the Dodd‐Frank Act and the 2013 Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (“HOEPA”) Final Rule.
risks.rationale: Lenders may misuse the data for non-compliant purposes without proper oversight.

risks.description: Risk of ZIP codes being used in conjunction with other data to infer individuals' identities or locations, potentially leading to privacy breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: PII collected from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool includes:  ZIP code entered for search results. Additionally, consumerfinance.gov collects other non‐identifying information from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool as part of normal operations supporting website functionality and security, (e.g. visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed and time on site, etc.) for consumerfinance.gov, and to evaluate usability of the tool.
risks.rationale: ZIP codes can be used to infer personal details when combined with other data.

risks.description: Risk of inaccurate or outdated information being included in the dataset, leading to privacy issues for individuals when the incorrect information is made public.
risks.evidence_quote: The information contained in this dataset is provided by housing counseling agencies to HUD per OMB No. 2502‐0573 (HUD‐9900, Application for Approval as a Housing Counseling Agency) and OMB No. 2502‐0261 (HUD‐9902, Housing Counseling Agency Activity Report).
risks.rationale: Inaccurate data can lead to privacy issues if incorrect information is publicly disclosed.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for all sensitive data at rest and in transit to protect against unauthorized access.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures that even if data is intercepted, it remains protected.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments to identify and mitigate potential security flaws.
mitigations.rationale: Security audits help maintain strong protective measures against breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for API access to ensure only authorized parties can retrieve data.
mitigations.rationale: MFA adds an extra layer of security against unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Require third-party developers to sign binding agreements ensuring they comply with data protection standards.
mitigations.rationale: Agreements ensure third parties handle data responsibly.

mitigations.description: Develop and implement a clear data retention schedule to minimize the amount of data stored over time.
mitigations.evidence_quote: HUD’s schedule for records contained in the HUD counselor dataset is outlined in HUD’s SORN for the records, HUD/DEPT‐22 – Housing Counseling.
mitigations.rationale: A retention schedule reduces prolonged exposure risks.

mitigations.description: Implement role-based access controls to limit who can access sensitive data within the system.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent from individuals before publicly disclosing their personal information.

mitigations.description: Include terms in agreements with lenders that prohibit misuse of the data and require compliance with privacy standards.

mitigations.description: Mask or aggregate ZIP codes to prevent inference of individuals' identities.
mitigations.rationale: Masking ZIP codes reduces their utility for identity inference.

mitigations.description: Implement data validation processes to ensure accuracy and update records as needed.
mitigations.rationale: Validation processes maintain data accuracy and integrity.

risks.description: Risk of data breach due to handling sensitive personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The system includes Name and other biographic information (e.g. date of birth), Contact Information (address, zip code, telephone number, email address), Social Security number (SSN) or other identifier, Financial Information, User and Online Information, Third Party Information, and Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information).
risks.rationale: The presence of sensitive information increases vulnerability to breaches.

risks.description: Impact on a large population due to the inclusion of data from federal employees, contractors, consultants, and the public.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB does not track the financial habits or activities of any individual consumer. However, Administrative Data may pertain to consumers who use particular consumer financial products or particular consumer financial service providers.
risks.rationale: Affecting many individuals increases potential harm from a breach.

risks.description: Risk from third-party data sources which may have varying security standards.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB collects Administrative Data only from third parties, commercial sources, and public databases, not directly from consumers.
risks.rationale: Third-party data introduces external vulnerabilities.

risks.description: Risk of long-term data retention without a defined schedule.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases exposure risk over time.

risks.description: Risk of accidental exposure during data matching and aggregation processes.
risks.evidence_quote: Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets... After the matching is complete, a de-identified copy of the matched dataset will be used for conducting research and analysis.
risks.rationale: Temporary use of PII during processing poses exposure risk.

risks.description: Risk of insider threats due to employee access.
risks.evidence_quote: Only CFPB personnel with a need to know are granted access to Administrative Data used for Market Research.
risks.rationale: Access without strict controls can lead to misuse.

risks.description: Risk of lack of notice to individuals about data collection and sharing.

risks.description: Risk of re-identification from aggregated data.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate access controls to the data system.

mitigations.rationale: Reduces long-term exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls during data processing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only CFPB personnel with a need to know are granted access to Administrative Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Controls during processing reduce exposure.

mitigations.description: Monitor and audit access logs regularly.

mitigations.description: Develop a notice mechanism for affected individuals.

mitigations.description: Ensure aggregated data is truly anonymized.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for access.

mitigations.description: Limit shared aggregated data to non-sensitive information.
