risks.evidence_quote: For each inquiry, the OLA Tracker maintains contact information for the staffer, their congressperson, and the OLA CS representative.
risks.rationale: Contact details can be used for phishing, impersonation, or unauthorized contact if leaked.

risks.description: The system receives and stores information about people who are not the requesting staffer, including constituents and other third parties, which may be disclosed without their direct involvement.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM Office of Legislative Affairs (OLA) Constituent Services (CS) handles inquiries from congressional staffers (staffers) asked on behalf of their congressperson or constituents. These constituents are often annuitants, survivor annuitants, or current or former federal employees.
risks.rationale: Third-party personal information can be collected and processed without the data subject directly interacting with the system.

risks.description: Inquiry records are routed to appropriate OPM program offices and may be shared with other federal agencies, creating a risk of unnecessary internal and external disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA CS uses the OLA Tracking & CS Portal system to log the inquiries from staffers, route the inquiries to the appropriate OPM program offices for action, track when and how OPM responded to the staffers, and create reports about that work.
risks.rationale: Routing and reporting expand access to personal data beyond the original intake point.

risks.description: Using cloud-based Microsoft services for case tracking and document storage increases the risk of unauthorized access or data exposure through the hosting environment.
risks.evidence_quote: The new system uses a cloud-version of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems introduce additional access and configuration risks that can affect sensitive records.

risks.description: The CS Portal allows staffers to submit inquiries, messages, and documents, so improper account access could expose sensitive case materials even though the portal itself does not retain them.
risks.evidence_quote: CS Portal is a secure web interface where congressional staffers can submit the inquiries and other messages to the Office of Personnel Management.
risks.rationale: A compromised portal account could be used to view or submit sensitive information tied to an inquiry.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of sensitive identifiers and financial data by requiring staffers to submit only the specific fields needed to resolve the inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of sensitive data collected lowers the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply strict document-handling rules to limit uploads and stored attachments to materials directly relevant to the inquiry, and redact unnecessary PII before storage.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and redacting documents reduces the amount of personal information retained in case files.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to linked constituent histories to staff with a demonstrated need to know and log each access to linked records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to aggregated case histories reduces the risk from consolidated profiles.

mitigations.description: Protect staffer, congressional, and OLA contact information with role-based access controls and audit logging.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls and logging help prevent and detect misuse of contact data.

mitigations.description: Provide notice and obtain or verify authorization before processing constituent or third-party information, and limit use to the specific inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Clear authorization and purpose limits help ensure third-party data is handled appropriately.

mitigations.description: Limit routing and reporting to the minimum necessary data and apply access controls to program offices and any other recipients.
mitigations.rationale: Sharing only necessary information reduces unnecessary disclosure during case handling.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong cloud security configuration, encryption, and vendor access restrictions for Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
mitigations.rationale: Cloud security controls reduce the chance of unauthorized access to hosted records.

mitigations.description: Maintain multifactor authentication and approval for portal accounts, and review account access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
mitigations.rationale: Strong account verification and approval reduce the risk of unauthorized portal access.

risks.description: ROVR collects and maintains a broad set of personally identifiable enrollment and health-related data about many people, creating a risk of overcollection and unnecessary exposure of sensitive information.
risks.evidence_quote: ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program
risks.rationale: The more categories of people and sensitive records held in one repository, the greater the privacy impact if access or use is not tightly limited.

risks.description: The system links records over time into person-level longitudinal files, which increases the risk of re-identification and deeper profiling of individuals across plan changes.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
risks.rationale: Linking records over time makes it easier to trace an individual's history and infer more about that person than any single record would reveal.

risks.description: ROVR may reveal erroneous or exceptional dual enrollments, which could expose enrollment mistakes or special coverage circumstances to unauthorized or inappropriate scrutiny.
risks.evidence_quote: For example, enrollment data may reveal instances where an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract. Generally, that is an erroneous enrollment that may be revealed through enrollment files included in ROVR, but in limited circumstances dual enrollments may be permitted when the enrollee or family member would otherwise lose coverage.
risks.rationale: Enrollment anomalies can disclose personal coverage status and potentially sensitive family or eligibility circumstances.

risks.description: ROVR analyzes claims, utilization, providers, geography, and disease conditions, creating a risk of detailed health profiling and inference about individuals or small groups.
risks.evidence_quote: These analyses may include examination of the cost of care, utilization of services, and comparing these across specific population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions.
risks.rationale: Even when used for administration, granular analytics can reveal health status and behavior patterns about identifiable people or small cohorts.

risks.description: The system includes pharmacy manufacturer payments and rebate information, which could expose commercially sensitive and potentially personal prescription-related details if mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Pharmacy claims data also includes pharmacy manufacturer payments and rebate information to allow for a comprehensive assessment of pharmacy benefits in the FEHB program.
risks.rationale: Pharmacy-related data can reveal treatment patterns and financial details that should not be broadly disclosed.

risks.description: Using the data to detect fraud, waste, and abuse or to investigate specific individuals creates a risk of secondary use beyond routine benefits administration.
risks.evidence_quote: Further, the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
risks.rationale: Fraud analytics can expand the scope of review and increase the chance that personal data are examined for purposes beyond ordinary coverage administration.

risks.description: ROVR receives data from multiple internal and external systems and agencies, which creates a risk of disclosure errors or inconsistent safeguards during data sharing.
risks.evidence_quote: These systems include the FEHB Data Hub ... the Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) warehouse ... and the Centralized Enrollment Reconciliation Privacy Impact Assessment Research and Oversight Repository (ROVR) OPM Form 5003 other Federal agencies through data sharing agreements.
risks.rationale: Each additional source or exchange point increases the number of places where privacy controls must work correctly.

risks.description: Service use and cost data from CMS about Medicare-enrolled family members may be combined with FEHB data, increasing the risk of cross-program linkage and broader exposure of health information.
risks.evidence_quote: Pursuant to an Information Exchange Agreement (IEA), Centers for Medicare Clearinghouse System (CLER) operated for OPM by NFC ... provides service use and cost data3 to OPM, including health claims information for FEHB enrollees and their eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare programs.
risks.rationale: Combining claims from multiple programs can create a more complete and sensitive picture of a person's health coverage and use.

risks.description: Because OPM uses identifiable data for longitudinal and analytical purposes, there is a risk that data collected for administration will be reused in ways that exceed what individuals reasonably expect.
risks.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred
risks.rationale: Broad administrative analytics can blur the line between program management and individual-level review if use limits are not enforced.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and retention to the minimum data needed for FEHB and PSHB administration and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the volume and sensitivity of stored data lowers the privacy impact if the repository is accessed or disclosed improperly.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified or aggregated data whenever identifiable person-level records are not necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data, OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
mitigations.rationale: The system already states that many analyses can be done without identifiers, which reduces re-identification risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict review of dual-enrollment cases to authorized staff and use the data only to resolve enrollment issues permitted by OPM rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Enrollment data included in ROVR will not be used to affect the enrollment of any individual except to the extent that information is already used for such a purpose in accordance with OPM statutes, regulations, and guidance.
mitigations.rationale: The stated use limitation helps prevent enrollment anomalies from being used beyond authorized administration.

mitigations.description: Apply strong access controls and cohort-size review rules before releasing or analyzing detailed subgroup, geographic, provider, or disease-condition outputs.
mitigations.rationale: Granular analytics are more privacy-sensitive when they concern small or distinctive groups.

mitigations.description: Treat pharmacy payment and rebate data as sensitive administrative data and restrict access to staff with a need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to those who need the data reduces the chance of exposing prescription-related and commercial details.

mitigations.description: Confine fraud, waste, and abuse review to cases where OPM suspects or has confirmed improper activity and document the basis for each use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred with respect to services rendered or payments made in connection with the FEHB Program.
mitigations.rationale: The system already limits individual-level use to suspected or confirmed wrongdoing, which narrows secondary use.

mitigations.description: Use data sharing agreements to define permitted uses, retention, and storage protocols for each source and recipient.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agreements constitute the methods of use and applicable retention and storage protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Written agreements can standardize safeguards across the multiple data sources feeding the repository.

mitigations.description: Limit CMS-linked data to the minimum needed for Medicare-related FEHB analysis and keep the linkage confined to authorized administrative uses.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OPM uses this data in its administration of the FEHB Program, including examining patterns of service use, statistical analyses of service use, risk and cost for dual FEHB and Medicare enrollees, and the relationship between FEHB and Medicare coverage more generally.
mitigations.rationale: The stated purpose supports restricting the combined data to FEHB administration and related analysis.

mitigations.description: Enforce the stated rule that ROVR data are not disclosed outside OPM unless permitted under the Privacy Act.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No disclosure of information in ROVR related to service use and cost data will be made outside of OPM unless permitted under the Privacy Act.
mitigations.rationale: The disclosure limitation directly reduces the chance of unauthorized external reuse.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal identifiers and debt information, including SSNs, mailing addresses, and debt amounts, which could expose individuals to identity theft or financial harm if mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: it uses HR data of federal employees who have outstanding debts, including their name, their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers combined with debt data increase the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Many USDA agencies can access the data, which increases the chance that more users than necessary could see debtor information or use it beyond the minimum needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users of approximately 35 USDA agencies have access to this data.
risks.rationale: Broader access across many agencies raises the likelihood of unnecessary exposure.

risks.description: The system shares debtor information with external federal systems and a records contractor, creating additional disclosure points outside the originating agency.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO provides data to the following:  Department of Treasury – Treasury Offset Program  Department of Treasury – Intra Governmental Payment and Collection System  Iron Mountain - Digital Records Center for Images System
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient expands the number of parties that can handle sensitive data.

risks.description: Contractors at a local facility convert payroll reports into PDF files and transmit them onward, which creates handling and transfer risk during file preparation.
risks.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
risks.rationale: Manual conversion and contractor handling increase the chance of accidental disclosure or processing error.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to ABCO data, which limits their ability to review, correct, or verify information held about them.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Without direct access, affected people may be unable to detect or correct inaccurate or outdated records.

risks.description: ABCO retains mainframe data indefinitely, which increases the long-term exposure of personal and debt information beyond the period needed for collection and reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which data can be misused or breached.

risks.description: The system relies on agency-provided data and periodic updates, so incorrect or stale debt records could be used to bill or report on the wrong amount or status.
risks.evidence_quote: As personnel actions and payroll documents are processed each pay period, updated data replaces existing data elements on the ABCO database.
risks.rationale: Frequent updates from multiple sources can propagate errors if records are not fully accurate.

risks.description: Debt-related notices are generated from personal data and used by agencies to notify individuals, so any inaccuracy or disclosure in those notices could affect the wrong person or reveal debt status.
risks.evidence_quote: The ABCO system uses personal data provided by agencies to generate reports or notices. These are used by each agency to notify the individual of the status of debts owed.
risks.rationale: Notices based on personal data can expose sensitive financial status if misdirected or incorrect.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs and other direct identifiers to the minimum necessary for billing and debt collection, and mask them wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of direct identifiers lowers the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing least-privilege access and periodic access reviews so each user retains only the minimum agency data needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least Privacy Impact Assessment Administrative Billings and Collections System (ABCO) Page 7 privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege directly limits unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Use formal data-sharing agreements and role-based restrictions for each external recipient to limit what data is exchanged and for what purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Recipient-specific restrictions reduce the amount of sensitive data disclosed outside USDA.

mitigations.description: Require contractor handling of reports to follow documented secure processing procedures and verify encryption before any transmission.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
mitigations.rationale: Secure handling and encryption reduce the risk of disclosure during contractor processing.

mitigations.description: Provide individuals a controlled process to request their records through the responsible agency and to seek correction of inaccurate debt information.
mitigations.rationale: A review-and-correction path helps affected people identify and fix errors even when they lack direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition rules to eliminate or archive mainframe data when no longer needed, rather than retaining it indefinitely.
mitigations.rationale: Retention limits reduce the duration of privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Strengthen reconciliation and validation checks with routine exception review for mismatched or stale records before they are used for billing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ABCO application code provides reconciliation routines at the application level.
mitigations.rationale: More robust validation helps prevent inaccurate data from driving debt actions.

mitigations.description: Add a notice quality review step before debt notices are sent so reports are checked for correct recipient, amount, and status.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-send review reduces the chance that sensitive debt information is disclosed to the wrong person.

risks.description: The system may over-collect PII from correspondence, including extra details that individuals voluntarily include even when they are not needed to process the request.
risks.evidence_quote: In a few cases, it may also include other information about the individual voluntarily provided by that individual in the correspondence.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly expects some correspondence to contain additional volunteered information beyond basic contact details.

risks.description: Historical correspondence can be searched and analyzed with NLP and machine learning, which may surface or infer more personal information than is necessary for the current business purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
risks.rationale: Searching across historical content increases the chance that sensitive details embedded in prior correspondence are exposed or reused.

risks.description: The centralized workflow lets multiple users and user groups access package records and track movement, creating a risk of unnecessary internal exposure of PII.
risks.evidence_quote: AgWrite supports the OES mission by providing a centralized system where users can access and interact with information
risks.rationale: A centralized system with multi-user workflow access can expose correspondence data to more personnel than needed.

risks.description: The system maintains physical and email addresses and phone numbers for correspondence, so unauthorized or excessive access could expose direct contact information to misuse or unwanted contact.
risks.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes. Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Contact details are directly identifying and can be misused if accessed beyond authorized correspondence handling.

risks.description: Reports, dashboards, and search data about workflow status and congressional inquiries may reveal sensitive correspondence patterns or case details beyond the original contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Search data produced could pertain to correspondence as they progress through workflows within the system (e.g., stage/status agency, priority or categorization, time in a particular status, time to progress from initiated to completed, congressional inquiries, etc.).
risks.rationale: Operational metadata can still reveal private or sensitive information about a person's interaction with USDA.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and retention to the minimum correspondence details needed to process the request, and redact or exclude unnecessary volunteered personal information before storing it.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is stored reduces the chance that unnecessary personal details are retained or exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict NLP and ML search and analysis to approved use cases, and suppress or mask unnecessary personal details in returned results and reports.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting model-driven retrieval and output reduces the risk that historical personal information is surfaced beyond what is needed.

mitigations.description: Enforce the stated role-based access controls so users can access only the package records and metadata needed for their specific duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: supporting standardized processes and role-based access
mitigations.rationale: Role-based access reduces unnecessary internal viewing of correspondence PII.

mitigations.description: Apply access controls and handling rules to physical addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers so they are used only for correspondence purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes. Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting use of contact information to the stated purpose reduces misuse risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict dashboards, reports, and workflow metadata views to authorized staff and minimize the detail shown in status and inquiry reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing detail in operational reporting lowers the chance that sensitive correspondence patterns are exposed.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive civil rights complaint records that could expose complainants if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The information includes complaints of discrimination against USDA programs and services and employee complaints. It uses complainant personal information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and miscellaneous identification numbers (generates a case number).
risks.rationale: Complaint files can reveal identity and sensitive allegations, so unauthorized access would harm privacy and confidentiality.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a risk that non-federal personnel could view or mishandle complainant PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? YES
risks.rationale: Granting contractors access increases the number of people who can see the data and raises insider misuse risk.

risks.description: Internet-connected hosting increases the chance of unauthorized remote access or interception of complaint data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
risks.rationale: Public Internet connectivity expands the attack surface for external intrusion or traffic interception.

risks.description: The system may retain complaint records longer than necessary if destruction is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES’s files are destroyed, based on the judicial’ s regulations.
risks.rationale: Without a clearly defined retention period, personal data may remain available longer than needed for the complaint process.

risks.description: Collecting information by mail, email, telephone, and interviews can expose data during intake if those channels are not protected.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake channels create opportunities for accidental disclosure before the information is entered into the system.

risks.description: Broad access by approved users and management could lead to unnecessary internal exposure of complaint details.
risks.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
risks.rationale: If access is not limited by role or need-to-know, more personnel than necessary may see sensitive records.

risks.description: Using complaint data for tracking and reporting could reveal individuals through trends or case patterns if reports are not sufficiently aggregated.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies use the data to track the number of complaints and trends. It supports the complaint process.
risks.rationale: Even if names are not in reports, small counts or detailed trends can still expose identities in a complaint context.

mitigations.description: Restrict complaint records to designated users only and apply strict access logging and review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive complaint details are viewed without authorization.

mitigations.description: Apply contractor-specific least-privilege access, confidentiality obligations, and periodic access recertification.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the risk that non-federal personnel mishandle complainant PII.

mitigations.description: Encrypt data in transit and harden the Internet-facing gateway and firewalls with continuous monitoring and patching.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting network traffic and the exposed perimeter lowers the risk of interception or unauthorized remote access.

mitigations.description: Define a specific retention schedule and automate deletion when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes.
mitigations.rationale: A clear schedule ensures records are not kept longer than necessary for legal and operational purposes.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for mail, email, telephone, and interviews, including verification before entry and secure handling of paper and electronic submissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the intake process reduces the chance of accidental disclosure before data reaches the system.

mitigations.description: Limit access by role so users see only the minimum complaint information needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces unnecessary internal exposure of sensitive complaint records.

mitigations.description: Publish only aggregated or de-identified reporting outputs and suppress small-cell counts where necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and suppression reduce the chance that reporting data can be linked back to an individual complainant.

risks.description: Users can enter unrestricted free-text personal information in the "About Me" field, which may lead to collection of unnecessary or sensitive personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: Unrestricted free-text fields can capture more personal information than the system needs and increase privacy exposure.

risks.description: Optional profile photos combined with a name create identifiable personal profiles that increase the risk of unnecessary identification and exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: A photo paired with a name makes the user more directly identifiable and can heighten privacy impact if disclosed.

risks.description: The system collects address information and miscellaneous identification numbers such as parking permit and building permit numbers, which could expose location or permit-related details if mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: - Name - Address information - Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
risks.rationale: These fields can reveal where a person works or what permissions they hold, so unauthorized disclosure would be privacy-relevant.

risks.description: User information is shared across multiple USDA administrative domains through dashboards and reports, creating a risk of broader internal dissemination than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Sharing across many domains expands the audience and the chance that personal data is seen by people who do not need it.

risks.description: Transmitting data to the USDA Data Lake and then publishing Tableau dashboards creates a risk of secondary use or aggregation of personal data beyond the original parking-permit and service-request purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
risks.rationale: Moving data into a central lake and reporting layer can make it easier to combine and reuse personal data in ways users may not anticipate.

risks.description: Department contractors can access the system, which creates a risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse if access is not tightly limited to the minimum necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system.
risks.rationale: Contractor access increases the number of people who can see personal data and requires strict controls to prevent misuse.

risks.description: The system retains records under a general records schedule based on subject matter, which may keep personal data longer than needed for the specific user purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Items are retained per the General Records Schedule 24: Information Technology Operation and Management Records. Records are destroyed based on the subject matter.
risks.rationale: Broad retention categories can leave personal data available for longer than necessary unless records are actively minimized and disposed of on time.

risks.description: Because the system is web-based and cloud-based, personal data is exposed to the risks of cloud or web application compromise if security controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: DM-OO OSCAR is a web-based information system on a cloud-based platform.
risks.rationale: Web and cloud systems are accessible remotely, so strong security is needed to prevent unauthorized access to personal information.

mitigations.description: Restrict or remove the free-text "About Me" field, or implement validation and guidance to prevent entry of unnecessary personal or sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting unrestricted text reduces the chance that users disclose personal data the system does not need.

mitigations.description: Keep profile photos optional and provide clear notice that photos are PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.rationale: Optional collection and notice help reduce unnecessary identification and make the privacy impact clearer to users.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of address information and permit numbers to only what is necessary for parking permits and request handling.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected to issue parking permits to various personnel, and to identify individuals making requests within the OSCAR application and managing the data within OSCAR.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only the minimum needed reduces exposure of location and permit-related details.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and publish only the minimum necessary data in Tableau dashboards and reports.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting dashboard content and access lowers the risk of broad internal overexposure.

mitigations.description: Before loading data into the USDA Data Lake, segregate or redact personal data that is not needed for reporting.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing personal data before central aggregation limits downstream reuse and exposure.

mitigations.description: Require that contractors retain security clearances and specific authorization, and limit their access to the lowest level needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
mitigations.rationale: Tight authorization reduces the chance that contractors access personal data beyond their job needs.

mitigations.description: Apply subject-matter-specific retention and destruction procedures to ensure records are deleted when no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are destroyed based on the subject matter.
mitigations.rationale: Timely destruction limits how long personal data remains exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong cloud and web security controls for the hosted system, including secure transmission methods already used for data transfers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and platform protections reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access to cloud-hosted personal data.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains a broad set of identity and employment data for cardholders and visitors, which increases the privacy impact if the data is misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS generally handles physical access Security Management Information including: x Physical access card status x Physical access card category x Physical access card expiration date x Physical access card holder emergency response responsibilities
risks.rationale: The more personal and operational data held in one system, the greater the harm if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Visitor background-check and registration data may be collected for USDA NCR Headquarters visitors, creating a privacy risk for non-employees who may not expect their information to be used beyond entry control.
risks.evidence_quote: With the addition of the VMS to ePACS, visitor data will be registered when meetings are scheduled by the meeting sponsor. The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
risks.rationale: Visitor information used for screening can be sensitive because it is collected from people who are not part of the workforce.

risks.description: Manual collection of non-authoritative data at card issuance can lead to inaccurate or inconsistent records, which may cause improper access decisions or incorrect identity records.
risks.evidence_quote: Also, Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
risks.rationale: Manually entered data is more prone to error than authoritative data sources.

risks.description: Internal sharing of card read activity and employee status for executive management and credit card disabling creates a secondary-use risk beyond the original physical-access purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity and the Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
risks.rationale: Sharing access-activity data for management purposes can reveal movement or work patterns unrelated to facility access.

risks.description: Daily transfer of limited ePACS data to EDAPT and delivery of the Fleet report by email increases the risk of unauthorized disclosure during internal transmission or downstream dashboard use.
risks.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily. ... The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
risks.rationale: Each additional transfer point creates another opportunity for exposure or misuse.

risks.description: Contractors with access to the system could view sensitive access-control records, creating a risk of insider misuse or excessive access.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Even screened contractors can pose a privacy risk if access is broader than necessary.

risks.description: Rare external sharing of ePACS data still creates a risk that personal information could leave USDA and be exposed or used in ways not anticipated by the data subject.
risks.evidence_quote: If information contained in ePACS is shared outside of USDA it is consistent with applicable laws and policy. ... As information shared to external organizations is rare, any data from ePACS before release to an external organization must be approved by the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel.
risks.rationale: Any external disclosure raises the stakes because USDA no longer fully controls the recipient environment.

risks.description: Retaining live and archived access records for 5.5 years increases the duration of exposure and the amount of historical movement data available if the system is breached or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which records can be accessed or repurposed.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and retention to the minimum fields needed to issue and validate physical access credentials.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected data reduces the privacy impact if records are accessed or disclosed.

mitigations.description: Restrict visitor data collection to the NCR Headquarters rollout and apply the same access controls and approval limits used for other ePACS data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The VMS will only include visitors arriving at USDA National Capitol Region (NCR) Headquarters (HQ includes South, Whitten, and Yates buildings).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the visitor module to a narrow location scope reduces unnecessary collection and exposure.

mitigations.description: Validate manually collected issuance data against authoritative sources before it is stored or used to make access decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The authoritative data elements provided to ePACS are provided by USDA’s ICAM Shared Services identity management system.
mitigations.rationale: Checking manual entries against authoritative data reduces the chance of inaccurate records.

mitigations.description: Use only summary or aggregated access-activity outputs for executive management and disable credit cards only from the minimum employee-status data needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity and the Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the detail in secondary uses reduces unnecessary disclosure of personal movement or status information.

mitigations.description: Replace email delivery of the Fleet report with a secure file transfer or similarly controlled channel and restrict dashboard access to authorized users only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily.
mitigations.rationale: A controlled transfer channel lowers the risk of interception or unintended forwarding compared with email.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based, need-to-know access reviews for contractors and remove contractor access when it is no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access governance reduces the chance that contractors can see more data than necessary.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing director and Office of General Counsel approval requirement for any external disclosure and document the routine use basis before release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: any data from ePACS before release to an external organization must be approved by the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-release approval helps ensure external sharing stays limited and legally justified.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether the 5.5-year retention period is still necessary and purge records at the end of the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review and timely deletion reduce the amount of historical data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of employee travel and identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: Based on the Privacy Threshold Assessment submitted in December 2023, this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees, and therefore, a PIA is necessary.
risks.rationale: Collecting PII means a breach or improper access could expose identifiable employee information.

risks.description: Enterprise-wide use and shared access by authorized USDA agency users increase the risk that more people than necessary can see travel and voucher data.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users.
risks.rationale: Broader access raises the likelihood of unnecessary exposure of personal travel and financial details.

risks.description: Transmitting authorization and voucher data to FMMI creates a risk of disclosure or compromise while the data moves between systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Any inter-system transfer expands the attack surface and can expose sensitive data in transit.

risks.description: The system's retention of user and billing data for years creates a risk that personal information will remain available longer than needed and be exposed in a later breach.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the amount of time sensitive data can be misused or compromised.

risks.description: The system analyzes traveler preferences and creates predictive patterns, which can reveal behavioral profiles about employees beyond the immediate travel transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Profiling travel preferences can expose patterns about an individual's habits and choices.

risks.description: Storing traveler preferences in profiles for future reference creates a risk that sensitive preference data will be reused in ways the employee did not expect.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference.
risks.rationale: Persistent preference storage can lead to secondary use or overexposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and access to only the PII needed for travel, booking, and voucher processing, and protect it with the existing role-based and transport protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles. Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access and using the stated protections reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege role assignments so users only see the travel data needed for their job.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Restrictive roles reduce unnecessary exposure from enterprise-wide access.

mitigations.description: Continue to encrypt and authenticate all data transfers to FMMI and other systems using the stated TLS and session protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport protection lowers the risk of interception or tampering during transmission.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retention to ensure only records required by the approved schedule are kept and delete expired records promptly.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of sensitive information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice and user controls for preference-based profiling, and limit predictive use to the stated travel convenience purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and control help prevent unexpected secondary use of behavioral data.

mitigations.description: Allow travelers to review and edit stored preferences and remove them when no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: User control over retained preferences reduces unnecessary persistence of personal data.

risks.description: Travel, authorization, voucher, and bill-related personal data could be exposed to unauthorized users because the system is used enterprise-wide and supports access by authorized USDA agency users and internal users.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-SS/FMS internal users.
risks.rationale: Broader access increases the chance that users see more personal travel and payment data than they need.

risks.description: Personal and financial travel data could be intercepted or disclosed in transit when shared to other systems, including the financial management system.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Any data transfer creates a risk of exposure if transmission controls fail or are misconfigured.

risks.description: The system retains user and bill-related information for long periods, which increases the impact of any later misuse, breach, or unauthorized internal access.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention keeps sensitive travel and billing data available for a longer time than is necessary for immediate processing.

risks.description: The system creates and retains predictive patterns from traveler preferences, which could reveal behavioral details about employees beyond the original travel transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference profiling can expose personal habits and choices that employees may not expect to be reused in this way.

risks.description: Mobile and web access expands the attack surface for account compromise and unauthorized access to travel records.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: More access methods generally mean more opportunities for credential theft or session compromise.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the minimum necessary through restrictive roles and periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Role restrictions reduce the number of users who can view sensitive travel and payment information.

mitigations.description: Protect all data transfers with strong encryption and authenticated transport controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and authenticated transport lower the risk of interception or tampering during transmission.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce the approved NARA/USDA retention schedule and delete records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: General Records Schedule (GRS) for USDA Travel and supporting documents.
mitigations.rationale: Retention limits reduce the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear privacy notice and limit preference-based profiling to travel-booking functions only.
mitigations.rationale: Users should understand that preferences are retained and analyzed, and limiting use reduces secondary privacy impact.

mitigations.description: Harden web and mobile access with multifactor authentication and session protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication helps prevent unauthorized access through browser or mobile channels.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal and financial data that could expose individuals to identity theft or financial fraud if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly identifying and financially sensitive, so unauthorized disclosure would likely cause significant harm.

risks.description: The system's debt-collection and payroll functions could lead to unfair or harmful decisions if the recorded data is inaccurate or incomplete.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: Administrative decisions based on incorrect records can wrongly affect debts, payments, or employee records.

risks.description: Keeping the data for 10 years increases the period during which the information can be exposed, misused, or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention expands the window of vulnerability and the number of opportunities for improper access.

risks.description: Using the system to record, process, and report personnel and payroll data for multiple agencies can create a risk of unnecessary internal disclosure across organizations.
risks.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Cross-agency processing can broaden access and increase the chance that data is shared beyond what is needed.

risks.description: Collecting statistical information alongside identifiable records may create a risk that individuals are re-identified from supposedly aggregated data.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: If statistical outputs are linked back to underlying records, individuals may be identifiable even when the intent is analysis.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the sensitive personal and financial fields to authorized personnel only and apply strong authentication and auditing.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers and bank data are exposed.

mitigations.description: Implement data quality checks and a human review process before debt-collection or payroll actions are taken.
mitigations.rationale: Verification before action helps prevent harm from incorrect or incomplete records.

mitigations.description: Periodically review records during the 10-year retention period and delete or archive information when it is no longer needed under the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
mitigations.rationale: Applying the approved schedule consistently reduces the time sensitive data remains exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit interagency reporting to the minimum necessary data elements and document the purpose of each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing shared fields and documenting disclosures reduces unnecessary spread of personal data.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified or aggregated statistical outputs whenever possible so individuals are not directly identifiable in reports.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing identifiability lowers the privacy risk of statistical reporting.

risks.description: The system retains appellant and case information indefinitely, which increases the chance of unnecessary long-term exposure of personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps personally identifiable and case-related information available far longer than needed for the stated case-tracking purpose.

risks.description: The system stores audio files and case determinations together with personally identifiable information, creating a risk of exposing sensitive case content if the system is misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: NAD case-related data: • Audio files and case determinations • Personally Identifiable Information (P11) such as full name, address, phone number, fax number, email address, and signature.
risks.rationale: Combining identity data with case audio and determinations increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: Appellants can view their transaction history and submitted documents through the eFile portal, which exposes residence and contact information to any account holder who gains access to the portal.
risks.evidence_quote: an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted. At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
risks.rationale: Portal access to residence and contact information creates privacy risk if credentials are compromised or if the portal reveals more than necessary.

risks.description: Only a secure login page is mentioned for collection and access, so unauthorized access remains a risk if authentication or account controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack collects data through the Web interface, behind a secure login page
risks.rationale: A secure login page helps, but the input does not describe stronger controls such as multi-factor authentication or session protections.

risks.description: Contractor employees have access to the system, which broadens the number of people who can view appellant data and increases insider access risk.
risks.evidence_quote: authorized users are USDA employees, contractor employees who access the system via eAuthentication, and the public who eFile appeal requests.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond federal staff increases the chance of inappropriate viewing or handling of personal information.

risks.description: Reports generated from the system may expose personally identifiable information to management, creating a risk of unnecessary internal disclosure through analytics or review outputs.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
risks.rationale: Even with a warning, report outputs can disseminate PII beyond the original case file view if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system collects data from public eFile submissions, so appellants may provide more personal information than is necessary for case tracking.
risks.evidence_quote: the public who eFile appeal requests
risks.rationale: Public self-submission can lead to overdisclosure if users include extra details in forms or attachments.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce a retention schedule that limits storage to the minimum period needed for case tracking and reporting, with secure deletion after that period.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and encryption to audio files, determinations, and PII so only authorized personnel can access sensitive case content.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and protecting the most sensitive records lowers the impact of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit the eFile portal to the minimum information needed for appellants to track their own appeal and protect access with strong authentication and session controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted. At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing portal exposure and strengthening account security lowers the chance of unauthorized viewing of appellant details.

mitigations.description: Add stronger authentication and account monitoring for the secure web interface, including measures such as multi-factor authentication and login anomaly detection.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication reduces the likelihood that a compromised login page or account leads to data exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access reviews for contractor accounts and periodically validate that contractor access remains necessary for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting contractor access to only what is needed reduces insider and misuse risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict report distribution and suppress or mask PII in management reports unless the data is required for a specific operational need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All reports with PII display a PII warning.
mitigations.rationale: Warnings help, but masking or limiting report content better prevents unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide clear submission guidance and form design that discourages appellants from entering unnecessary personal information in eFile requests.
mitigations.rationale: Guidance and form constraints can reduce overcollection from public submissions.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal and employment data, including names, SSNs, time and attendance records, teleworking agreement information, and payroll data, so a breach or misuse could expose individuals to identity theft or improper disclosure of work and payroll details.
risks.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data
risks.rationale: SSNs and payroll-related records are sensitive identifiers that increase harm if disclosed.

risks.description: Multiple parties can access or enter data on behalf of individuals, including HR staff, agency payroll/personnel offices, contractors, and system/security officers, creating a risk of unauthorized or overbroad access if role controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf.
risks.rationale: When many actors can handle the same records, access control failures can expose data beyond what is needed.

risks.description: WebTA shares PII with other USDA systems and transmits certified time and attendance data to the PPS TIME application, which creates a risk that data will be disclosed more broadly than necessary across internal systems.
risks.evidence_quote: NFC shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below. 1. EmpowHR: WebTA uses human resources data provided by EmpowHR. 2. Insight: WebTA generates files for transmission to the Insight hosting environment for processing. 3. OCIO eAuthentication (eAuth) application: The eAuthentication application provides authentication services for some WebTA customers. 4. TIME: WebTA transmits certified T&A data to the PPS TIME application.
risks.rationale: Each additional system connection expands the number of places where PII can be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: Agencies determine the use and sharing of the information, so privacy protections may vary by customer agency and create inconsistent handling of the same records.
risks.evidence_quote: The customer agency determines the use and sharing of the information.
risks.rationale: Agency-specific discretion can lead to uneven privacy practices for similar data.

risks.description: Users may run predefined and custom reports against the data, which can reveal more information than needed if report access is not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
risks.rationale: Reporting tools can aggregate and expose PII at a scale greater than ordinary record viewing.

risks.description: Information is retained under NARA schedules and customer agency requirements, which may keep PII available for long periods and increase the impact of any later misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule. Civilian Personnel Records have various retention periods for specific types of data. These retention periods are adhered to per customer agency requirements and memorandum of understanding.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window during which records can be accessed, disclosed, or repurposed.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs and other sensitive fields to only what is required for time, attendance, and payroll processing, and mask them wherever full values are not operationally necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of sensitive identifiers lowers the harm from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing role-based access with least privilege and unique user credentials for all users, including HR staff and contractors, and periodically review those roles for necessity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the chance that users can see records beyond their job needs.

mitigations.description: Restrict inter-system sharing to only the fields required by each receiving system and document each transfer so that downstream systems receive the minimum necessary PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NFC shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing fields shared across systems reduces the privacy impact of each transfer.

mitigations.description: Apply a uniform agency-wide privacy and access standard for WebTA data handling, rather than relying solely on each customer agency's discretion.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The customer agency determines the use and sharing of the information.
mitigations.rationale: A common standard helps prevent inconsistent protections across agencies.

mitigations.description: Restrict custom reporting to authorized personnel and apply output controls so reports expose only the data elements needed for the approved purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report output reduces the chance of bulk disclosure of PII.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retained records and purge or archive them according to the approved records schedule and customer agency requirements as soon as they are no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition shortens the period during which old PII remains exposed to risk.

risks.description: Customer PII may be exposed when it is transmitted internally by email to SME contacts, because email is a less controlled sharing channel than the core system. This creates a risk of misdelivery or unauthorized disclosure of names, addresses, phone numbers, and case details.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: Email transmission increases the chance that personal information is sent to the wrong recipient or handled outside the intended access controls.

risks.description: PII may be exposed through internal sharing to all USDA Mission Areas for escalated inquiries, which broadens access beyond the original contact center need. This increases the number of people who can see sensitive contact and inquiry information.
risks.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII information with all USDA Mission Areas part of AskUSDA Contact Center for escalated inquiries that require mission area expertise to respond
risks.rationale: The more internal recipients who can access the data, the greater the risk of unnecessary disclosure.

risks.description: The system retains information for at least seven years, which can preserve personal data longer than needed for a customer inquiry process. Long retention increases the impact of any later misuse, breach, or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained at minimum of 7 years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention keeps personal data available for a longer period, increasing cumulative privacy exposure.

risks.description: There is currently no purging or archiving setup for the PII available through third-party websites or applications, so personal data may accumulate without timely deletion. This can leave older records exposed even when they are no longer operationally necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival
risks.rationale: Without deletion or archiving controls, the system may retain more personal data than necessary and make it harder to limit exposure.

risks.description: The system allows contractors to have access, which creates a risk that more people than necessary can view customer PII. Even with role-based controls, contractor access expands the population with potential access to sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control.
risks.rationale: Contractor access increases the number of authorized users and therefore the chance of improper access or disclosure.

risks.description: PII is collected through multiple channels, including webform, email, chat, and phone, which increases the chance of inconsistent handling across intake paths. Different channels can create uneven privacy protections for the same personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is collected through a combination of manual and structured system data loads of knowledge articles and user supplied data collected through secure web pages, email, chat and Cisco telephony integration.
risks.rationale: Multiple collection channels can lead to inconsistent controls and greater risk of accidental disclosure or capture of more information than intended.

risks.description: The system collects a combination of name, address, and phone number in Salesforce, which can directly identify customers and link them to inquiry history. If accessed improperly, this set of data could reveal both identity and the nature of the customer's contact with USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: PII data will be captured within Salesforce of the combination of Name, Address and Phone number information of contacts within the Salesforce Government Cloud Application.
risks.rationale: Combining direct identifiers with case information makes the records more sensitive if they are disclosed.

mitigations.description: Replace or supplement email transmission of PII with a secure internal case-sharing workflow that keeps the information inside the authenticated Salesforce environment and logs access.
mitigations.rationale: A controlled workflow reduces the chance that PII is misdirected or exposed through ordinary email handling.

mitigations.description: Limit internal sharing of PII to only the specific mission area personnel needed for each escalated inquiry, rather than all USDA Mission Areas.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the minimum necessary users reduces unnecessary disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Apply a records retention schedule that deletes or archives customer inquiry records as soon as the approved business need ends, rather than keeping them for the full minimum period by default.
mitigations.rationale: Shortening the active life of records lowers the amount of personal data exposed to future misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Implement automated purging or archiving for third-party application data on a recurring schedule and verify it before the pilot phase ends.
mitigations.rationale: Automated deletion or archival helps ensure old records do not remain unnecessarily available.

mitigations.description: Tighten contractor access approvals and periodically review role-based permissions and EEMS access assignments to confirm contractors retain only the access needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS). The standard ISSPM SAAR process will be followed for requesting internal access.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review supports the existing access-control process and helps prevent unnecessary contractor access.

mitigations.description: Standardize privacy controls and disclosure notices across webform, email, chat, and telephony intake so each channel handles customer information consistently.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent controls across channels reduce the chance that one intake path becomes a weaker privacy point.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection to only the contact details needed to resolve the inquiry and avoid retaining unnecessary combinations of identity and case information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The customer has the ability up and until the point at which they submit the inquiry to AskUSDA Contact Center (webform, email, chat or phone call) to decide whether they provide their contact information or not.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only what is needed reduces the sensitivity of the stored record and limits harm if it is exposed.

risks.description: The system creates broad surveillance of employees, contractors, visitors, and passersby across USDA facilities and nearby areas, which can chill movement and activity even when no wrongdoing is suspected.
risks.evidence_quote: The PIA is being conducted because the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
risks.rationale: Continuous recording of identifiable people in and around federal buildings can reveal routine behavior and create a pervasive monitoring effect.

risks.description: The cameras may capture sensitive personal data beyond ordinary video, including facial images, license plates, and driver’s license information such as names, addresses, and dates of birth.
risks.evidence_quote: The VSS cameras may capture facial images of employees and visitors to USDA buildings and images of license plates that are parked or driving through the parking lot.
risks.rationale: Collecting more identifying detail increases the privacy impact and the harm if footage is viewed, shared, or misused.

risks.description: The system can record people on public streets and use zoom, low-light, and tracking features to follow individuals, which expands surveillance beyond USDA-controlled spaces and can capture bystanders who are not the focus of security operations.
