risks.evidence_quote: The cameras may record passersby on public streets and USDA personnel accessing a secured area.
risks.rationale: Capturing bystanders and using tracking tools increases the scope of collection beyond the intended security target.

risks.description: Video may be used for disciplinary actions as well as criminal investigations, creating a secondary-use risk that footage collected for security could be repurposed against employees or others.
risks.evidence_quote: it will be used to review events that have taken place in a post investigative nature and may be exported to be used later for criminal or disciplinary actions.
risks.rationale: Using surveillance data for employment-related consequences can exceed what subjects expect from building security monitoring.

risks.description: Footage can be shared outside USDA with federal agencies and local law enforcement, which increases the risk of broader dissemination and loss of control over who sees identifiable video.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with external organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions Information from the VSS cameras will be used by federal agencies and local law enforcement to detect and respond to potentially unlawful activities in the areas surrounding federal facilities.
risks.rationale: External sharing widens the audience for sensitive footage and can expose individuals to additional uses beyond the original collection.

risks.description: Contractors and select non-employees may access the system, which creates an insider-access risk if access is broader than necessary or if non-employees view footage unrelated to their duties.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Any additional class of users increases the number of people who can view identifiable surveillance data.

risks.description: Footage is retained for up to six months and may be kept longer when tied to suspected criminal activity, which increases the risk of prolonged exposure and secondary use of historical surveillance data.
risks.evidence_quote: The intent is a 6-month retention period for all video footage, however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which footage can be accessed, disclosed, or repurposed.

risks.description: Because the system can identify individuals through video and other captured data such as license plates, there is a risk of mistaken identification or overreliance on footage in investigations and prosecutions.
risks.evidence_quote: USDA uses VSS’s images to identify individuals and may try to identify individuals through other data elements like a license plate number captured by a VSS camera feed.
risks.rationale: Identification from video and partial identifiers can be inaccurate or incomplete, creating privacy and fairness concerns.

mitigations.description: Limit camera placement and viewing practices to security-relevant areas only and continue avoiding locations where people have a reasonable expectation of privacy.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Cameras are not placed in places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as inside a bathroom or changing room.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting placement reduces unnecessary surveillance of everyday activity.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization controls such as limiting zoom, masking where feasible, and restricting use of captured license-plate or identity details to cases where they are needed for security or investigations.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing capture and use of extra identifiers lowers the privacy impact of the footage.

mitigations.description: Constrain manual tracking, automatic tracking, and low-light monitoring to documented security incidents or active threats, with oversight of when those features are used.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting advanced tracking features helps prevent unnecessary monitoring of bystanders.

mitigations.description: Restrict exports and secondary use of footage to documented criminal or disciplinary matters with supervisory approval and a stated need-to-know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: may be exported to be used later for criminal or disciplinary actions.
mitigations.rationale: Tightening approval for secondary use reduces the chance that footage is used for unrelated personnel purposes.

mitigations.description: Share footage externally only in response to formal requests and only the minimum relevant segment needed for the specific investigation or prosecution.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with external organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions
mitigations.rationale: Limiting disclosure to formal, narrow requests reduces unnecessary external dissemination.

mitigations.description: Keep contractor and non-employee access tightly limited to approved roles, and review access regularly to ensure it remains necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Regularly reviewing access helps ensure only authorized users can view sensitive footage.

mitigations.description: Enforce the six-month automatic deletion limit except for footage formally preserved for an active investigation, with supervisor approval for any extension.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored for a maximum of six months and then is automatically deleted. Records which are retrieved pursuant to suspected criminal activity will be retained until any investigative or enforcement action is completed. To retain the footage after the retention period, a supervisor must approve the request and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.rationale: Short retention and controlled exceptions reduce the amount of historical surveillance data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use footage as investigative leads only and require corroboration before making decisions based on identity matches from video or license-plate data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: VSS records may assist investigators in identifying persons who were in the area when a crime occurred, or identify suspects or vehicles fleeing the area.
mitigations.rationale: Requiring corroboration reduces the risk of privacy harms from mistaken or overconfident identification.

risks.description: Customer feedback can include directly identifying information, creating a risk that people are identifiable from comments or associated metadata even when the tool is meant for feedback collection.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Collecting names, email addresses, and zip codes makes it possible to identify respondents.

risks.description: The system may collect more identifying information than needed for general feedback, increasing the risk of unnecessary exposure of personal details.
risks.evidence_quote: This request for PII is asked in order to better meet the needs of the customer.
risks.rationale: Requesting PII in feedback flows can create avoidable privacy exposure if the information is not strictly necessary.

risks.description: Broad internal sharing of dashboard data across leadership and program staff could expose sensitive feedback to more employees than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
risks.rationale: Internal aggregation still creates access risk if too many personnel can view the dashboards.

risks.description: A small number of users can access all data across all mission areas, which increases the risk of cross-program overexposure and unnecessary linkage of feedback.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: Concentrated access to all mission-area data increases the impact of misuse or mistakes.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to the system, which raises the risk of disclosure beyond federal staff with a mission need.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of people who can see customer feedback and any associated PII.

risks.description: The system supports migration from multiple existing USDA tools into one cohesive product, which creates a risk of combining data in ways that increase identifiability or reuse beyond the original context.
risks.evidence_quote: In addition to launching the VoC tool, appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
risks.rationale: Consolidating data sources can make it easier to connect feedback across programs and identify individuals.

risks.description: Using demographic and geographic analysis of feedback could lead to profiling or inference about groups or individuals from customer sentiment data.
risks.evidence_quote: VoC data will be used to: • Assess USDA audience sizes and segments • Identify current program volumes and performance metrics • Identify current contact channel volumes and preferences • Gather customer insights and feedback geographically, demographically and ethnographically in order to identify areas in need of improvement
risks.rationale: Segmenting and analyzing feedback by demographic and geographic characteristics can create privacy risks if results are linked back to people.

risks.description: Retention governance is incomplete because the retention period has not been approved, creating a risk that data may be kept longer than intended or inconsistently disposed of.
risks.evidence_quote: 3.2 Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Unapproved retention periods weaken control over how long personal data remains in the system.

risks.description: The system relies on role- and permission-based access controls, but the presence of broad dashboards and all-data access means misconfiguration or excessive permissions could expose PII to unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: All appropriate security and accessibility measures will be implemented to limit, and control access based on user’s roles and permission levels.
risks.rationale: Access controls reduce risk only if they are correctly designed and enforced.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of name, email address, and zip code to only cases where follow-up contact is explicitly requested, and keep PII out of standard feedback fields.
mitigations.evidence_quote: On some occasions, a customer may request to be contacted by a USDA official and this information will allow contact to be made.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting PII to follow-up cases reduces the amount of identifying information collected.

mitigations.description: Use a data minimization rule that asks for PII only when it is necessary to meet a specific customer need or contact request.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary identifiers lowers unnecessary privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Continue to share only aggregated dashboard data internally and ensure PII is excluded from those dashboards.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII will not be included in these dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and exclusion of PII reduce the chance that staff see identifiable customer feedback.

mitigations.description: Restrict all-data access to the smallest possible set of users and periodically review whether those users still have a mission need.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting all-data access reduces the impact of a breach or inappropriate browsing across mission areas.

mitigations.description: Apply the same role-based access controls, training, and documented permission process to contractors before granting access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Approved USDA employees will undergo in-person training on platform functionality, privacy, and security controls. Before users gain access to the system, they must be provided a license and their permission will be documented in a database file.
mitigations.rationale: Documented access approval and training help reduce contractor misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Perform privacy review before migrating data from Salesforce, AskUSDA, and EDAPT so that only necessary fields are consolidated and linked.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing migrations limits the chance that combining systems will create unnecessary identifiability.

mitigations.description: Use aggregated or de-identified outputs for demographic, geographic, and ethnographic analysis whenever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation reduces the risk that analysis results can be tied back to specific people.

mitigations.description: Obtain component records officer and NARA approval for the retention period and document disposal procedures before full deployment.
mitigations.rationale: Approved retention schedules provide clearer limits on how long personal data may be kept.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege permissions and regularly audit role assignments to verify that access remains limited to mission need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users of the VoC platform will be selected based on their mission need to access the system and their permission levels.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access helps prevent unauthorized viewing of customer feedback and any PII.

risks.description: The system requires mandatory collection of identifying contact information, so individuals cannot avoid providing PII to obtain access.
risks.evidence_quote: First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Mandatory collection increases privacy exposure because users must provide PII even when they may prefer not to.

risks.description: Because the service is a third-party cloud system hosted outside the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary, USDA contact information is exposed to cloud-provider storage and operational risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Hosting PII in an external cloud environment increases the risk of unauthorized access or mishandling by the provider environment.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, which increases the risk of unauthorized or excessive access to user account information.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors broadens the population that can view or handle PII.

risks.description: The system retains PII for 75 months, which prolongs the period during which the data could be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window of risk for any account or contact information stored in the system.

risks.description: The system is used to prepare documents that are publicly accessible, so personal information could be exposed if it is entered into those documents.
risks.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data.
risks.rationale: Public accessibility creates a disclosure risk if PII is included in the report content.

risks.description: Access is based in part on supervisor or higher-level approval, which creates a risk of over-provisioning if approvals are not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
risks.rationale: Approval-based access can lead to unnecessary permissions if approvers do not apply least-privilege standards consistently.

mitigations.description: Minimize the account data collected to only what is strictly necessary for provisioning and avoid collecting additional contact details unless required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of mandatory PII lowers the privacy impact of account creation.

mitigations.description: Continue to use a cloud service only with strong contractual, technical, and administrative safeguards for hosted USDA data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Workiva Wdesk enterprise cloud
mitigations.rationale: Strong safeguards are needed because the system is hosted in a third-party cloud environment.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary roles and review contractor permissions regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the chance that contractors can view unnecessary PII.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved retention schedule and purge records when the 75-month retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are retained in accordance with NARA policies (OMB/NARA M-12-18).
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved retention policy limits how long PII remains exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Train users to exclude personal information from publicly accessible reports unless it is explicitly required and authorized.
mitigations.rationale: User training helps prevent accidental public disclosure of PII in report content.

mitigations.description: Use the system’s logged access approvals to review and audit elevated permissions for necessity and appropriateness.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All access transactions, including approvals, additions, or removals of access are fully logged by the system.
mitigations.rationale: Auditing approval-based access helps detect and correct excessive permissions.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, so a compromise could expose SSNs/TINs, signatures, salary data, and other personal details about applicants, grantees, vendors, and personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: This may include the vendor’s name, address, email IDs, and SSN/TIN.
risks.rationale: The presence of direct identifiers and financial details increases harm if the data is accessed without authorization.

risks.description: Grant-related PII may be shared outside USDA with a broad set of external parties, increasing the chance of over-disclosure beyond what each recipient needs.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS award results related information can be shared with a number of external parties, including, but not limited to, non-profit organizations, state and local organizations, individuals, corporations, and entities outside the US.
risks.rationale: Wide external dissemination raises the likelihood that personal information reaches parties not necessary for the original purpose.

risks.description: PII may be disclosed in common office formats or on paper, which creates a risk of accidental forwarding, loss, or viewing by unauthorized people.
risks.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
risks.rationale: Multiple manual and file-based disclosure methods are easier to mishandle than tightly controlled system-to-system transfers.

risks.description: Contractors have operational access to the system for backup, support, and account management, which creates insider-access risk if their access is too broad.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Giving contractors multiple administrative functions increases the number of people who can access sensitive records.

risks.description: The system receives data from external applications and users, so inaccurate or unnecessary personal data may be imported and retained without proper minimization.
risks.evidence_quote: The data sources for FNS FM-GSS are sourced through the applications hosted in FNS FM-GSS and transferred to connecting systems that process such data.
risks.rationale: Data flowing in from multiple systems and manual entry can introduce excess or incorrect personal information.

risks.description: Using application data for reporting and award decisions can expose more personal and business information than the individuals may expect from the original submission.
risks.evidence_quote: This information is used to establish grant opportunities, receive applications, distribute applications for review, determine award and funding decisions, generate awards, maintain official grant file documentation and activities throughout the life of an award.
risks.rationale: Repurposing application data across the full award lifecycle expands the privacy impact of the original collection.

risks.description: Retention for six years after closeout or final payment means sensitive records remain available for a long period, increasing the window for unauthorized access or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time during which stored personal data could be exposed.

mitigations.description: Continue encrypting sensitive PII before distribution and keep the database encrypted at rest.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the likelihood that exposed data can be read by unauthorized parties.

mitigations.description: Limit external sharing to approved recipients and require Grants Director approval before any disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Transmissions/disclosures typically require approval by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Approval gates can reduce unnecessary or excessive disclosure outside the Department.

mitigations.description: Restrict disclosure of PII in Excel, Word, PDF, and hard-copy formats to only authorized recipients and use encrypted electronic transmission where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter handling of exportable formats lowers the chance of accidental exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role-based access for contractors and review their access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GIMS also has the capability to check-in/check-out documents; manage version control for simple and compound documents; track audit trails; perform comprehensive searches; and manage user, group, and role-based access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based access can limit contractor visibility to only the functions they need.

mitigations.description: Validate incoming data and minimize manual entry to ensure only necessary and accurate personal data is stored.
mitigations.rationale: Input validation and minimization reduce the amount of unnecessary or incorrect data entering the system.

mitigations.description: Limit reporting and external reporting to the minimum data needed for the approved purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data in GIMS is used to support the discretionary grants award process at FNS.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited reporting reduces exposure of personal information beyond what is needed for award processing.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved retention schedule and archive or dispose of records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, GRS 1.1, Item 010 see GRS 1.2, Item 010.
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved schedule limits how long sensitive records remain exposed.

risks.description: The database centralizes highly sensitive participant information, creating a risk that a breach or unauthorized access would expose detailed personal, financial, and transactional SNAP data for many people at once.
risks.evidence_quote: SNAP participant data to be contained in the SNAP Information Database will include detailed and sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed, as well as financial data (e.g., amount of benefit received).
risks.rationale: A centralized store of sensitive data increases the impact if access controls fail or the environment is compromised.

risks.description: The system collects data from all participants since 2000 and keeps quarterly updates, which creates a risk of retaining more historical information than is necessary for current integrity checks.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Long historical retention expands the amount of personal information exposed and can exceed what is needed for the stated purpose.

risks.description: The system uses data for cross-state and inter-agency matching beyond ordinary benefit administration, creating a risk of secondary use or function creep if the information is reused more broadly than participants expect.
risks.evidence_quote: This also includes sharing, where permitted by law and consistent with this notice, information with State agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify fraudulent or otherwise improper or illegal SNAP enrollments or transactions.
risks.rationale: Sharing data across agencies for multiple checks increases the chance it will be used in additional ways over time.

risks.description: Automated scripts and matching algorithms may incorrectly flag people as duplicates, ineligible, or fraudulent, creating a risk of false positives that can lead to improper investigation or benefit disruption.
risks.evidence_quote: Integrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database, using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
risks.rationale: Even with efforts to reduce errors, automated matching can still misidentify individuals when records are incomplete or inconsistent.

risks.description: The system shares information to verify immigration status eligibility, which creates a risk that highly sensitive immigration-related information will be disclosed or used in ways that could harm affected individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: verifying immigration status eligibility
risks.rationale: Immigration-related data is especially sensitive and can cause significant harm if improperly disclosed or misused.

risks.description: The system collects and matches household composition and age information, creating a risk that family or household details will be exposed or inferred beyond what is needed for SNAP integrity checks.
risks.evidence_quote: Age and household composition validation
risks.rationale: Household and age data can reveal intimate family relationships and living arrangements.

risks.description: Data moves from state agencies and EBT processors through file transfer tools into AWS, creating a risk of exposure during transfer or through misconfiguration of external sharing channels.
risks.evidence_quote: Data will be sent via the secure MoveIt or Box managed file transfer application.
risks.rationale: Any multi-system transfer path introduces opportunities for interception, misrouting, or access control mistakes.

mitigations.description: Restrict database access to authorized personnel only, enforce strong authentication, and apply least-privilege controls and logging for all access to the SNAP Information Database.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls reduce the chance that centralized sensitive data will be exposed to unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Apply a retention schedule that limits historical data kept in the database to the minimum needed for integrity checks and purge records when they are no longer required.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of legacy personal information held and the harm from any later disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit use and sharing of the data to the specific integrity-check purposes described in the notice and document any inter-agency disclosures and approvals.
mitigations.evidence_quote: where permitted by law and consistent with this notice
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation helps prevent secondary use beyond the stated fraud-prevention and eligibility-check functions.

mitigations.description: Add human review and an appeals or correction process before adverse action is taken on the basis of an automated match.
mitigations.rationale: Human review can catch false matches and reduce the chance that automation harms the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Limit access to immigration-related fields to staff with a documented need to know and segregate those fields from less sensitive data where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Extra protection for highly sensitive immigration data reduces the risk of unnecessary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize household composition and age data to only the fields necessary for validation and mask or redact those fields in routine views and reports.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and masking reduce exposure of intimate family details.

mitigations.description: Continue using secure transfer tools and require encryption in transit and file integrity checks for all inbound state and processor submissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data will be sent via the secure MoveIt or Box managed file transfer application.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and integrity controls lower the risk of interception or tampering during data movement.

risks.description: The system holds personally identifiable information about non-employee affiliates, so unauthorized access could expose their names, business contact details, and Affiliate IDs.
risks.evidence_quote: Names, business address and contact information, and Affiliate ID of Contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Government employees, Resource Conservation & Development Council employees, Volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organization personnel (referred to as Affiliates).
risks.rationale: If these records are improperly accessed, the affected affiliates could face unwanted disclosure of identifying and contact information.

risks.description: Because NRCS employees enter affiliate information into the system, there is a risk that inaccurate or incomplete data will be stored and used for access control decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: An NRCS employee enters the Affiliates information into the Affiliates database.
risks.rationale: Errors introduced during manual entry could lead to incorrect identity records or role assignments.

risks.description: The system shares affiliate information with zRoles, so any mistake or misuse in that internal exchange could grant the wrong access privileges.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
risks.rationale: Because the data is used to assign access, inaccurate or improperly handled sharing can affect least-privilege decisions.

risks.description: Long retention of affiliate records increases the chance that personal information will remain available longer than necessary for the access purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Extended retention enlarges the window during which the records could be misused, disclosed, or retained after they are no longer needed.

risks.description: The system links an affiliate's Level 2 eAuth account to the affiliate record, creating a risk that identity and access credentials could be associated too broadly if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record.
risks.rationale: Linking identity records to authentication accounts can increase the impact of any unauthorized access or account misuse.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the Affiliates application to authorized NRCS employees and enforce strong role-based access controls and audit logging.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to authorized staff reduces the likelihood of unauthorized disclosure of affiliate PII.

mitigations.description: Validate affiliate information with the individual before it is saved and correct errors promptly when identified.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is provided directly to an NRCS employee by the affiliate
mitigations.rationale: Direct confirmation with the data subject helps reduce manual entry errors in the stored record.

mitigations.description: Apply access-control checks and periodic review before sharing affiliate data with zRoles to ensure only current and necessary role information is transmitted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing the data before internal sharing helps prevent incorrect or excessive access assignments.

mitigations.description: Regularly review records against the approved retention schedule and purge records when the retention trigger no longer applies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? • Yes
mitigations.rationale: Scheduled disposal limits how long personal information remains exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Limit linkage between the affiliate record and the Level 2 eAuth account to the minimum necessary identifiers and protect the link with access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and protecting the linkage reduces the privacy impact if the record is viewed or misused.

risks.description: The warehouse holds highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers that could cause identity theft or other harm if exposed. The data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, tax IDs, policy numbers, and agent and adjuster social security numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: Producer name, address, phone numbers, tax ID, ID type, and entity type, as well as any associated farm numbers. Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc. Policy data includes name, address, phone number, policy number, unit, Approved Insurance Provider (AIP), crop, insurance plan, coverage level, indemnity, liability, premium, fund placement, acres, agent name, agent social security number, adjuster name, adjuster social security number, and etc.
risks.rationale: This combination of identifiers and insurance data is highly sensitive and can be misused if disclosed.

risks.description: Geolocation-linked farm information could reveal precise property locations and operational details about producers. The CLU data contains latitude and longitude and is combined with crop and policy records.
risks.evidence_quote: Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc.
risks.rationale: Location data tied to farm and policy records can expose where a producer operates and what is insured there.

risks.description: Broad internal and external access increases the risk of unnecessary disclosure of personal data. The system shares information with USDA components and allows access to authorized users in RMA, FSA, and AIPs through HyDRA.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently the information described previously is provided to FSA, RMA, and OIG within USDA. There have been limited OIG users that have access to the system, this was to obtain reports and transmit products and is a routine use. Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs.
risks.rationale: More recipients and more user groups create more opportunities for data to be seen beyond what is needed.

risks.description: External approved insurance providers may see policy-associated data that could be broader than necessary if access controls are not tightly enforced. The system says AIPs can access data associated with their policies for reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
risks.rationale: Policy-linked access still exposes personal and insurance information to outside organizations.

risks.description: Long-term retention of detailed personal data increases the chance of future misuse or breach impact. The information is retained for the life of the project and kept for historical analysis.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
risks.rationale: Keeping sensitive data longer expands the window in which it can be exposed or used inappropriately.

risks.description: The system does not collect information directly from individuals, so affected people may not receive direct notice or have a practical opportunity to correct or limit the data before it is used. The data comes from FSA and RMA instead.
risks.evidence_quote: The BAD data warehouse does not collect information directly from individuals; information is obtained from FSA and RMA.
risks.rationale: Indirect collection can reduce transparency and individual control over personal information.

risks.description: Combining data from multiple years into a single production database can increase the impact of any unauthorized access by concentrating records in one place. The system moves annual databases into a single production database.
risks.evidence_quote: RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years. Data from all years is moved into a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
risks.rationale: Centralizing records makes a larger volume of personal data available from one system.

risks.description: Data cleansing and standardization processes can alter source records and create the risk of inaccurate or mismatched personal information if changes are not carefully controlled. The system removes characters and standardizes names and other fields for analysis.
risks.evidence_quote: Data was cleansed and standardized. Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data. For example, “Mr.” will appear in some records with a period and in others without a period. Consistency changes are achieved by including/removing the period, thus eliminating the one-character difference that would be problematic in data analysis where unique individuals must be identified.
risks.rationale: Transforming source data can introduce errors that affect how individuals are represented in the warehouse.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the sensitive fields to only users with a documented need to know and apply field-level masking or redaction for tax IDs and social security numbers in reports.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of the most sensitive identifiers reduces the harm if reports or accounts are misused.

mitigations.description: Limit access to CLU latitude and longitude data to users who need geospatial analysis and suppress or generalize location details in standard outputs.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing precision of location data lowers the chance of revealing exact farm locations unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access reviews for FSA, RMA, OIG, and AIP users and periodically verify that each account still needs access to the specific data it can see.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure that authorized access remains limited to legitimate business need.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege filtering so each AIP can only retrieve the minimum policy data needed for reporting and no cross-policy or unrelated producer information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing external access reduces the amount of personal information exposed to third parties.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce a deletion or archival schedule for records that are no longer needed for active historical analysis, while still honoring the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention when records are no longer needed limits the duration of privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear upstream notice and correction process through FSA and RMA so individuals can understand the data flow and request fixes where permitted.
mitigations.rationale: Because the warehouse does not collect directly from individuals, upstream notice and correction are the practical way to improve transparency and accuracy.

mitigations.description: Segregate annual datasets or logically partition the production database so a compromise of one area does not expose all years at once.
mitigations.evidence_quote: RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years. Data from all years is moved into a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
mitigations.rationale: Partitioning reduces the blast radius of any unauthorized access or operational error.

mitigations.description: Add change-control and audit logging for ETL and cleansing scripts so any transformation of personal data is reviewable and reversible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data was cleansed and standardized. Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data.
mitigations.rationale: Logging and change control help detect unintended data alteration and support accountability for transformations.

risks.description: CoLab retains identifiable user profile information for as long as the application remains in production, which can keep personal data available longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the chance that personal data will be exposed, misused, or remain in the system after it is no longer needed.

risks.description: Authorized contractors and partners can access the system, creating a risk that more people than necessary may view user profile PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Any additional internal or partner access expands the pool of people who can see personal data and increases insider-access risk.

risks.description: Users can modify their own profiles, which creates a risk that profile contact information may become inaccurate or incomplete.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: If profile data is wrong, the system may rely on inaccurate personal information for access and administration.

risks.description: CoLab stores personal contact information beyond work identity data, including phone and company address, which increases the sensitivity of the profile record.
risks.evidence_quote: Personal Contact Information is comprised of the following elements: o First name o Last name o Email o Phone o Company Address
risks.rationale: Collecting more contact details than the minimum needed raises the impact if the profile is accessed inappropriately.

risks.description: The system relies on eAuthentication and access requests to create profiles and authorize access, so any weakness in identity verification could allow unauthorized profile creation or access.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile.
risks.rationale: If the identity source or access-request process is compromised, personal data could be associated with the wrong person or exposed to an unauthorized user.

mitigations.description: Delete or erase application-specific PII when it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: This reduces the amount of personal data retained and limits the duration of exposure.

mitigations.description: Keep contractor and partner access limited to their roles and responsibilities and enforce role-based access control.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to only what each user needs lowers the chance of unnecessary viewing of PII.

mitigations.description: Require review or confirmation of profile updates before they are used for access administration.
mitigations.rationale: A confirmation step would help prevent inaccurate user-entered contact information from persisting in the profile.

mitigations.description: Limit profile fields to the minimum contact information needed for authorization and administration.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less personal information reduces the privacy impact if a profile is accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Continue using eAuthentication as the identity source and require a USDA eAuth User ID before CoLab membership is granted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User gets a USDA User ID and password. 2. User requests CoLab Membership. USDA eAuth User ID from step 1 is required.
mitigations.rationale: Strong identity verification helps ensure profiles and access are tied to the correct person.

risks.description: Stored vendor PII in the IDEA DataMart could be exposed to unauthorized internal access if access controls are too broad. Because the system maintains names and contact information for report generation, an internal misuse or overbroad permission set could reveal vendor data beyond what is needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Maintained PII creates a persistent target that can be accessed if internal controls fail.

risks.description: Periodic refreshing of vendor PII from SCIMS could pull in more data than needed or keep data current longer than necessary. Repeated synchronization increases the chance that outdated or unnecessary personal data remains available in IDEA.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Regular refreshes expand the amount of PII copied into IDEA and can perpetuate unnecessary retention.

risks.description: Contractor access could expose vendor PII to personnel who do not need it for their specific duties. Even with a need-to-know requirement, contractors represent an additional access path to sensitive business contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access increases the number of people who can view PII and therefore the exposure surface.

risks.description: Application-specific information may be retained for the life of the production system, which could keep vendor PII available longer than necessary. Long retention increases the chance of misuse, unauthorized access, or disclosure after the data is no longer needed for reports.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases privacy risk because data remains exposed for a longer period.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the IDEA DataMart PII to only users with a documented need to know and review permissions regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and reviewing access reduces the chance that stored vendor PII is seen by unauthorized internal users.

mitigations.description: Minimize the SCIMS fields copied into IDEA and refresh only the specific PII needed for reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of synchronized PII lowers the privacy impact of periodic refreshes.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing need-to-know and background investigation controls for contractors and verify contractor access is limited to assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: The stated contractor vetting and need-to-know controls help reduce the risk of unnecessary access to PII.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA deletion authority as soon as application-specific information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Timely deletion shortens the period during which vendor PII remains exposed in the system.

risks.description: Unauthorized users could access linked customer records because the system relies on a shared SCIMS view and multiple internal systems exchanging data.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: A shared view and multiple access paths increase the chance that access controls are misapplied or bypassed.

risks.description: The system could expose sensitive identifiers by associating requests to specific clients using data that can be linked to a Social Security number or tax identification number.
risks.evidence_quote: SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number
risks.rationale: A customer identifier that can be linked to SSNs or tax IDs raises the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Returning requested information in JSON format to client applications could disclose more personal data than needed for a given request.
risks.evidence_quote: will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: Machine-readable responses can make it easier to copy, store, or over-share personal data if the response is not minimized.

risks.description: Administrative and transactional information stored by Core Services may create a record of user activity and customer interactions that can be misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
risks.rationale: Even if PII is not stored there, transaction records can still reveal sensitive behavior or relationships.

risks.description: Contractor access could expose personal data to personnel outside the core federal workforce if need-to-know restrictions are not tightly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of people who can see or handle the data.

risks.description: Internal sharing across many USDA systems increases the chance that personal data will be propagated beyond the original purpose or retained in multiple places.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
risks.rationale: Each additional system that receives the data creates another place where misuse, retention, or exposure can occur.

risks.description: Requests entering through a single external-facing gateway create a concentrated point of failure that could expose data if the gateway is attacked or misconfigured.
risks.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: A single entry point concentrates risk because compromise there can affect many downstream services.

risks.description: Replicated access to SCIMS data can increase the risk of stale or broader-than-necessary exposure of customer information.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication.
risks.rationale: Replicated copies can expand the attack surface and may not always reflect the latest access restrictions.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access and strong authentication for every SCIMS-linked request, and review access rights regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and tightly scoped access reduce the chance of unauthorized retrieval of linked customer records.

mitigations.description: Minimize use and display of identifiers that can be associated with SSNs or tax IDs, and mask them wherever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number
mitigations.rationale: Masking and minimization lower the impact of any disclosure involving highly sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Return only the minimum fields needed for the requesting application and suppress unnecessary personal data in JSON responses.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting response content reduces the amount of personal information exposed to client applications.

mitigations.description: Limit retention and logging of administrative and transactional records to what is necessary for operations and audit needs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention and narrower logging reduce the chance that operational records become a privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict contractor access to specific duties, enforce background checks, and periodically recertify need-to-know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know limits and background investigations reduce the likelihood of improper access by contractors.

mitigations.description: Apply data-sharing minimization and documented purpose limits for each internal USDA system receiving the data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limits and minimization reduce unnecessary propagation of personal data across systems.

mitigations.description: Harden and continuously monitor the CA API Gateway, including threat protection and access control, because it is the single entry point.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CA API Gateway – Used for threat protection, access control, and other sharedservices as defined during the architecture build out.
mitigations.rationale: Gateway protections are essential because compromise at the entry point would affect many requests.

mitigations.description: Limit replication access to only authorized users and ensure replicated data follows the same security rules as the source.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication.
mitigations.rationale: Treating replicated data with the same controls as the source reduces the risk created by additional copies.

risks.description: Emergency Action Plans contain home addresses and telephone numbers, so a disclosure could expose responders and property owners to unwanted contact, targeting, or other privacy harms.
risks.evidence_quote: EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: The system stores direct contact and location information about identifiable individuals, which is sensitive if disclosed.

risks.description: PII is disclosed outside the Department to state and local emergency responders, creating a risk of over-disclosure or misuse by external recipients.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII contained within the EAPs is shared with state and local emergency responders in the event of activation of an EAP.
risks.rationale: Sharing personal data with external organizations increases the chance it is seen or used beyond the minimum necessary purpose.

risks.description: PII may be disclosed in hardcopy or electronic copy during review cycles or when an EAP is activated, which creates a risk of interception, loss, or accidental distribution.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Multiple disclosure formats increase the opportunities for accidental or unauthorized exposure.

risks.description: NRCS personnel, contractors, and assigned state and local emergency responders can access EAPs, so too many users with legitimate roles could still see PII that is not needed for every task.
risks.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
risks.rationale: Broader role-based access expands the number of people who can view personal data.

risks.description: The system retains information for periods ranging from less than one year to more than ten years, which prolongs the time that PII remains available for disclosure or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which personal information can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit the EAP to the minimum personal contact details needed for execution and exclude any nonessential names, addresses, or phone numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of personal data stored lowers the impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Continue restricting disclosure to state and local emergency responders only when an EAP is activated and document the minimum necessary recipients for each site.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII contained within the EAPs is shared with state and local emergency responders in the event of activation of an EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting sharing to authorized responders reduces unnecessary external exposure.

mitigations.description: Use the stated secure communications methods for all hardcopy and electronic disclosures and maintain controlled-document handling procedures for review cycles and activations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and controlled handling reduce the risk of interception or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Keep access on a strict need-to-know basis and review user assignments regularly so only personnel assigned to a particular dam site or project duty can view the EAPs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps ensure that only necessary users retain access to PII.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule and purge or archive records as soon as the applicable retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal shortens the period during which personal information remains exposed.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal data, so any unauthorized access could expose identity, financial, and farm-related information. The records include SSNs, tax IDs, bank account numbers, and farm ownership details.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers make harm from unauthorized disclosure especially serious.

risks.description: Centralizing scanned paper records in a cloud-based system increases the risk of unauthorized internal access or misuse by users who have legitimate system access. Authorized FPAC staff and contractors can access documents maintained in DRMS.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
risks.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces exposure, but any broad or improperly enforced internal access could reveal records to more people than necessary.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a privacy risk if contractors are not adequately screened or controlled, because they may view records as part of their duties. The system explicitly allows contractor access.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
risks.rationale: Contractors add another privileged user group, so strong vetting and oversight are necessary to limit misuse.

risks.description: Because records are scanned from paper into databases, errors during scanning or metadata extraction could create inaccurate records that affect individuals. The system stores digitized forms and related metadata.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk digitization can introduce mistakes that may persist in the system and affect retrieval or decision-making.

risks.description: Long retention of records increases the chance that personal data will remain available longer than needed and be exposed by future misuse or compromise. Records may be kept for more than ten years and as long as a person qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017. Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
risks.rationale: The longer records are retained, the longer the privacy exposure window remains open.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DRMS, which can make it harder for them to verify, correct, or understand what records are held about them. The system relies on staff-mediated requests instead.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Limited direct access can slow corrections and reduce transparency for affected individuals.

risks.description: The use of third-party capture software and cloud hosting introduces supply-chain and platform risk even if the system says no PII is shared externally. The system uses KOFAX for capture and resides on FPAC_AWS_Shared_GSS.
risks.evidence_quote: The KOFAX application enables the capture of paper documents to transferred to electronic.
risks.rationale: Third-party components and hosted infrastructure can expand the attack surface for stored records.

mitigations.description: Encrypt scanned records and metadata at rest and restrict access to only those users with an operational need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and strict access limits reduce the likelihood and impact of exposure of highly sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Enforce documented access controls, role-based permissions, and periodic access reviews for all DRMS users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS has documented Access Control (AC) Procedures, in compliance with FISMA and USDA directives.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure need-to-know access stays limited to current duties.

mitigations.description: Continue mandatory background investigations for contractors and add regular oversight of contractor activity in DRMS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Vetting and oversight reduce the risk that contractor access will be misused.

mitigations.description: Validate scanned documents and extracted metadata before they are made available for retrieval, with error correction by authorized staff.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-release validation helps prevent inaccurate digitized records from persisting in the system.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA and records-schedule disposition rules consistently so records are deleted or transferred when no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition limits how long personal data remains exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear request and correction process for individuals so they can obtain or amend their records without direct system access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A structured request path helps offset the lack of direct user access.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong security controls and monitoring for the cloud host and the document-capture application, including patching and vendor oversight.
mitigations.rationale: Third-party components and hosted infrastructure need continuous security management to reduce platform risk.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial information in documents, creating a risk of harm if those records are exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored data make unauthorized disclosure especially harmful to affected individuals and businesses.

risks.description: Authorized users can view, upload, version, and delete documents, which creates a risk of unauthorized alteration, accidental deletion, or integrity loss affecting records about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS features will allow users to view documents and/or upload new documents, version documents, and delete documents within the scope for those locations where their role has jurisdiction.
risks.rationale: Document management functions can change the content or existence of records, so mistakes or misuse could affect privacy and record accuracy.

risks.description: The system relies on direct user uploads and web-service transfers from multiple source systems, creating a risk that sensitive documents are ingested or transmitted improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected is transmitted primarily from ProTracts - Fund Manager, CST, and CCG via DMS web services. In addition, DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake paths increase the chance that data could be sent, uploaded, or handled in an unintended way.

risks.description: DMS uses name and address data from FSA SCIMS to identify the correct producer, which creates a risk of misidentification or linking records to the wrong person.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Using limited identity attributes for matching can lead to incorrect association of records with an individual.

risks.description: External disclosure to contractors or technical service providers could expose personal information beyond the original collection context if authorization or purpose limits are not properly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
risks.rationale: Even authorized disclosures expand the number of parties handling sensitive records and therefore increase privacy exposure.

risks.description: Contractors and conservation district employees can access the system, creating a risk of insider misuse or overbroad access to sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
risks.rationale: Any role with access to sensitive documents can misuse or overexpose them if controls are insufficient.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DMS, which creates a risk that they may be unable to promptly review or correct inaccurate records affecting them.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Without direct access, affected individuals must rely on staff to identify and correct errors in their records.

risks.description: Records are retained for long periods, increasing the chance that personal information will remain available longer than necessary for privacy-sensitive documents.
risks.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window during which records can be accessed, disclosed, or breached.

mitigations.description: Limit stored documents to the minimum necessary and continue encrypting sensitive files at rest and in transit.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and protecting the stored data reduces the impact of any exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based permissions and change controls for viewing, versioning, and deletion, with audit logging of document changes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS features will allow users to view documents and/or upload new documents, version documents, and delete documents within the scope for those locations where their role has jurisdiction.
mitigations.rationale: Tight change controls and logs reduce the chance of unauthorized or mistaken record modification.

mitigations.description: Validate uploads and web-service transfers before ingestion to ensure only authorized, complete, and correctly formatted documents enter DMS.
mitigations.rationale: Input validation and transfer checks reduce the risk of improper or accidental ingestion of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Use stronger identity matching and manual review for ambiguous cases before associating documents with a producer.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
mitigations.rationale: Additional verification lowers the risk of linking records to the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Require documented authorization and purpose checks before any external disclosure, and limit contractor access to the specific records needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited disclosure and authorization reduce unnecessary sharing outside USDA.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews and background investigations for all contractor and district employee accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege and vetting help reduce insider misuse and excessive access.

mitigations.description: Provide an accessible correction and access request process so individuals can obtain and amend their records without relying solely on staff discretion.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A formal request path helps individuals exercise access and correction rights even without direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply retention schedules narrowly and purge records when they are no longer needed for conservation program eligibility or under the applicable NARA schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Shorter, rules-based retention reduces the amount of time sensitive records remain exposed.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive borrower PII and financial information indefinitely, which increases the harm if the records are later misused, exposed, or no longer needed for the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: Permanent retention of identifying and financial data expands the window of exposure and potential harm.
