risks.description: Manual input by field agents can introduce inaccurate or incomplete borrower data, which may lead to incorrect debt restructuring decisions affecting the subject’s financial outcome.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manually entered financial data is vulnerable to human error, and the system’s calculations depend on that input.

risks.description: The system consolidates multiple borrower-related data sources and internal databases, creating a more complete profile that could be exposed if access controls fail or are misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Determining and evaluating the effects of primary loan servicing - Completing a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information - Restructuring the borrower's debt and maximize their repayment ability - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Combining borrower, loan, and other internal records increases sensitivity and the impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: As an intranet web-based application used by field office employees, the system may be vulnerable to unauthorized internal access or misuse of borrower PII by users with legitimate network access.
risks.evidence_quote: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) is an Intranet web-based program developed to assist authorized agency officials
risks.rationale: Internal systems still require strong access controls because authorized environments can be misused by unauthorized users or overbroad permissions.

risks.description: The system uses borrower financial and loan-status data to make restructuring recommendations, so an inaccurate or opaque calculation could adversely affect a borrower’s repayment plan.
risks.evidence_quote: eDALR$ completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status.
risks.rationale: When personal financial data drives decision support, errors in the underlying data or calculations can produce harmful outcomes.

mitigations.description: Limit retention to the approved records schedule and apply periodic review to confirm records are still needed for the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention where allowed lowers the amount of long-lived sensitive data exposed to future risk.

mitigations.description: Add validation and supervisory review for manually entered borrower data before calculations are used for servicing decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Independent review helps catch entry errors that could distort restructuring outcomes.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the minimum necessary internal databases and fields needed for restructuring analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting data aggregation reduces the amount of sensitive information exposed through the application.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and audit logging for all users who can access borrower records in the intranet application.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) is an Intranet web-based program developed to assist authorized agency officials
mitigations.rationale: Role-based controls and logs help prevent and detect unauthorized internal access.

mitigations.description: Provide decision-support documentation and a review step so employees can verify the calculated restructuring result before acting on it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To support field office employees in determining the most optimal servicing solutions applicable and available concerning the restructuring of customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
mitigations.rationale: Human review helps ensure that automated calculations do not drive incorrect borrower decisions unchecked.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive personal and financial data that could be exposed if access is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: This information is highly sensitive and would cause harm if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Sharing Name and Tax ID with Microbilt creates a risk of external disclosure of identifying information for credit checks.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: External transfer of identifying data increases the chance of misuse or unauthorized disclosure outside USDA.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower data increases the risk that personal information will be kept longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database.
risks.rationale: Keeping data without a clear end point increases exposure time and the impact of any future breach or misuse.

risks.description: County office staff entry of borrower data creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records being used for loan decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual entry can introduce errors that affect financial assessment and eligibility determinations.

risks.description: Using borrower data to determine credit worthiness and loan servicing can create a risk of secondary use beyond the borrower’s immediate submission.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Broad operational use of the data can increase privacy impact because the information is used for multiple decisions and processes.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the system and the underlying database to authorized personnel only, with role-based permissions for county staff and loan officers.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive borrower data will be viewed or altered by unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Minimize the data shared with Microbilt to only the Name and Tax ID needed to obtain creditworthiness, and document the disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting external disclosure reduces the amount of identifying information exposed to a third party.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce records schedules so data is not kept indefinitely unless a specific approved retention requirement applies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Using approved retention schedules helps ensure data is retained only as long as needed for official purposes.

mitigations.description: Use validation and review procedures for county office data entry to reduce errors before the information is used in loan processing.
mitigations.rationale: Verification steps help ensure that decisions are based on accurate borrower information.

mitigations.description: Provide borrowers with clear notice that their information will be used for creditworthiness, loan making, and loan servicing.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice supports transparency about how borrower information is used across the loan process.

risks.description: The system exposes highly sensitive borrower identifiers, including Social Security Numbers, which could lead to identity theft or misuse if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: ADPS uses the customer’s name, address, Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive and increase harm if exposed.

risks.description: Borrower information is shared with many internal and external organizations, creating a broad disclosure surface and increasing the chance of unnecessary or excessive disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers. Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
risks.rationale: The more recipients that receive the data, the greater the chance of overdisclosure.

risks.description: The system allows access to borrower data through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number, which could enable broad lookup and unauthorized access if controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Searchable access by direct identifiers can make sensitive records easier to retrieve improperly.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the amount of personal data exposed over time and lengthens the harm if the records are misused, breached, or no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping records forever increases cumulative privacy risk.

risks.description: Reporting delinquent borrower information to Treasury, IRS, and credit bureaus can negatively affect borrowers’ financial privacy and may reveal debt status beyond the original program context.
risks.evidence_quote: The DCIA processes evaluate accounts for amount and date of delinquency and reported to Treasury for offset.
risks.rationale: Debt-related disclosures can have significant privacy and reputational consequences.

risks.description: Sharing borrower information with credit bureaus and HUD can spread account details across additional systems, making correction and control of the data harder for borrowers.
risks.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
risks.rationale: Once shared to multiple reporting systems, borrower control over the information is reduced.

mitigations.description: Limit the use and display of Social Security Numbers to the minimum necessary and mask or truncate them wherever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and misuse.

mitigations.description: Restrict disclosures to only the specific internal and external recipients needed for each purpose and document each sharing arrangement.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers. Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting recipients reduces unnecessary dissemination of borrower data.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and audit logging for online queries and batch processing that use name or Social Security Number.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access controls and logs help prevent and detect improper record access.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review and disposition schedule to reduce retention where permitted, rather than keeping all data indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the volume of legacy data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice and procedural safeguards for delinquency, offset, and tax reporting disclosures before information is sent to Treasury, IRS, or other reporting recipients.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The DCIA processes evaluate accounts for amount and date of delinquency and reported to Treasury for offset.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and safeguards help ensure borrowers understand and can contest sensitive financial disclosures where appropriate.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and validation controls with credit bureaus and HUD to ensure only accurate, necessary borrower information is disclosed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
mitigations.rationale: Controls on shared data improve accuracy and limit unnecessary spread of borrower information.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable contact information that could be exposed if internal access is broader than necessary. Because the system is used across County, State, Regional and National FLP staff, improper access could reveal staff names, mailing addresses, and phone numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
risks.rationale: Contact information is directly identifiable and should be protected from unnecessary internal exposure.

risks.description: Manual system input creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete personal data being entered into appraisal records. Errors in names, addresses, or phone numbers could affect the correctness of records used to facilitate and track appraisals.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Manual entry is more prone to human error than automated collection.

risks.description: Indefinite retention increases the privacy impact of any future unauthorized access or misuse because the personal data remains available permanently. Long-lived records also increase the chance that outdated contact information will persist unnecessarily.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time window in which data can be exposed or become stale.

risks.description: Centralizing appraisal-related information in a web application can concentrate sensitive operational records in one place, increasing the impact of a system compromise. Even though the collected data is limited, a breach could expose multiple staff members' contact details at once.
risks.evidence_quote: The enterprise web application will help to standardize the loan appraisal process and give the FLP community a user-friendly tool to aid in day to day activities.
risks.rationale: Centralized systems can magnify the consequences of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the contact information to only those FLP staff who need it for appraisal work, and enforce role-based access controls and logging.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that identifiable contact data is viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Add validation and review steps for manually entered names, mailing addresses, and phone numbers before records are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Quality checks help prevent inaccurate personal data from being stored and used in appraisal records.

mitigations.description: Apply periodic records review and purge or archive records when no longer needed, consistent with the approved schedule, to reduce unnecessary long-term exposure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Even with an approved schedule, periodic review can limit unnecessary retention of personal data.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong system security controls for the web application and database, including access monitoring and regular security testing.
mitigations.rationale: Security controls reduce the likelihood and impact of a compromise of centralized records.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains highly sensitive identifiers and financial data, creating a risk of identity theft or financial harm if the data is misused or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: SSNs/TINs, credit reports, and credit card numbers are high-impact data elements that increase harm if exposed.

risks.description: Collecting race, ethnicity, and gender for loan processing creates a risk of sensitive demographic information being improperly used or disclosed beyond the stated loan servicing purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number.
risks.rationale: Demographic data can cause privacy harm if used or revealed outside the narrow administrative need.

risks.description: The system relies on data from many internal, state, local, and third-party sources, which creates a risk that inaccurate or outdated information will affect loan eligibility, servicing, or restructuring decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected directly from farm loan borrower and information is received from other FSA applications, state and local agencies and other third party financial sources.
risks.rationale: More sources increase the chance that inconsistent or stale records will be used in decisions affecting borrowers.

risks.description: Manual input by field staff creates a risk of human error or unauthorized alteration in debt restructuring and loan servicing decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: eDALR$ Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual entry can introduce mistakes or intentional changes that affect borrower outcomes.

risks.description: Permanent retention of borrower records creates a long-term exposure risk because sensitive data remains available indefinitely.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention extends the window in which records can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

risks.description: The system supports broad loan-making, servicing, and creditworthiness analysis, which creates a risk of function creep if data is reused for purposes beyond the original loan administration need.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: A system used for multiple related decisions can drift into broader use unless purpose limits are enforced.

risks.description: The system gives producers access to their Farm Loan Program account information, creating a risk of unauthorized access if authentication or session controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
risks.rationale: User-facing access to account data requires strong identity verification to prevent account takeover.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and storage of SSNs, TINs, credit reports, and other high-risk identifiers to only what is necessary for the loan function, and protect them with strong access controls and encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing and hardening the most sensitive fields lowers the impact of any misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to race, ethnicity, and gender data to staff with a documented need and audit their use.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the chance that sensitive demographic data is viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Implement data validation and reconciliation checks when importing information from other FSA applications, state and local agencies, and third-party sources.
mitigations.rationale: Validation helps prevent incorrect or outdated source data from driving loan decisions.

mitigations.description: Require review and approval of manually entered restructuring data before it is used in final decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: eDALR$ Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
mitigations.rationale: A second review step can catch entry mistakes and reduce the impact of improper manual changes.

mitigations.description: Apply records management controls that periodically review whether permanent retention remains necessary for each record type and restrict access over time.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Even permanent records benefit from periodic review and tighter access to reduce long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce purpose-specific use limits so the data is used only for loan making, servicing, and restructuring decisions described in the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The collected information will be used to service existing loans, answer farm loan borrowers’ inquiries and provide data on servicing of loans to manage the program.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit purpose limits reduce the risk of reuse for unrelated or excessive processing.

mitigations.description: Use strong authentication and session protections for producer access to FLP account information.
mitigations.rationale: Strong login and session controls help prevent unauthorized access to borrower account data.

risks.description: The system holds identifiable personal information that could be exposed if access controls are insufficient, including names and mailing addresses in one application. Because the system is web-based and used for oversight and workflow, unauthorized viewing or disclosure would affect the affected staff or trainees.
risks.evidence_quote: DDORS Name FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
risks.rationale: The presence of directly identifying data means any access failure could reveal personal information about named individuals.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely, which increases the chance that personal information remains available longer than needed and could be misused or exposed over time. Permanent retention also expands the impact of any future security incident.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases cumulative exposure and the consequences of a breach or improper access.

risks.description: Multiple internal offices enter and use the data, creating a risk of inaccurate or inconsistent personal information being recorded and then relied on for oversight or workflow decisions. If names or addresses are entered incorrectly, the system may propagate those errors across the applications.
risks.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
risks.rationale: Distributed manual entry increases the chance that personal data will be incorrect or inconsistent.

risks.description: The system uses web-based applications for oversight, training, and directives workflows, which can broaden internal access to personal data beyond the original collectors. Even without external sharing, more users and more functions increase the chance of overexposure within USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: consists of multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
risks.rationale: Web-based workflow systems typically expand the number of users and access points that can see personal data.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which may create a risk that individuals provide information without fully understanding its status or how it will be handled. That can affect notice and expectation of privacy for public contributors.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Collecting public input before approval can create privacy and notice concerns if contributors are not clearly informed.

mitigations.description: Limit access to names and mailing addresses to only the users who need them for the stated oversight, training, or workflow functions, and enforce role-based access reviews.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that identifiable data is viewed or used by unauthorized personnel.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review process to minimize what is kept permanently and confirm that permanent retention is limited to records that truly require it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Records scheduling provides a basis to ensure retention is justified and appropriately controlled.

mitigations.description: Validate and verify entries at the point of data entry, especially for names and mailing addresses entered by county and state offices.
mitigations.rationale: Input validation and verification help prevent incorrect personal data from being stored and reused.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access and periodic access reviews across the web-based applications so users only see the personal data needed for their role.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting role-based visibility reduces unnecessary internal exposure in a web-based environment.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear privacy notice to public contributors explaining what information is collected and how it will be used in SDMS before they submit information.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps individuals understand the collection and make informed decisions about disclosure.

risks.description: The system holds a large volume of identifiable producer and farm records, so a breach or misuse could expose sensitive personal and business information at scale.
risks.evidence_quote: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities, who voluntarily provided their customer data on an OMB approved form prior to, or during a program application process.
risks.rationale: A large centralized repository increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive identifiers and contact details, which could enable identity theft or unwanted contact if disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: ☒ Social Security number ☒ Employee Identification Number ☒ Taxpayer Identification Number ☒ Business Taxpayer Identification Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Personal Mobile Number ☒ Business Mobile Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Name (including nicknames) ☒ Gender ☒ Business Mailing Address (sole proprietor)
risks.rationale: These data elements can directly identify people or be used to impersonate or contact them.

risks.description: The system shares Farm Record and Business Partner data across multiple USDA agencies, creating a risk of overexposure or secondary use beyond the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Broader internal sharing increases the number of users and systems that can access the data.

risks.description: Because access is tied to organizational roles and workflows, incorrect role assignments could allow users to create, edit, or view more data than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
risks.rationale: Access control mistakes can lead to unnecessary disclosure or unauthorized changes.

risks.description: The system retains 20 years of historical data and archives older records, which increases the chance that outdated or unnecessary personal data remains exposed for longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which records can be accessed, breached, or misused.

risks.description: Historical records may contain outdated information, and keeping them for long periods could cause decisions or communications based on stale data.
risks.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
risks.rationale: Old records can become inaccurate over time and create privacy and administrative harm if relied upon.

risks.description: Geospatial boundary data linked to farm records can reveal detailed information about a producer's land and operations, increasing the sensitivity of the record set.
risks.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
risks.rationale: Location-linked farm boundaries can disclose operational details even when not obviously personal.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the centralized records repository to only personnel with a demonstrated program need and monitor for unusual access patterns.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the likelihood and impact of a large-scale exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply field-level minimization and masking for sensitive identifiers and contact information wherever full values are not required for program delivery.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of direct identifiers lowers identity theft and contact privacy risks.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and purpose limitations so receiving USDA agencies access only the specific Farm Record and Business Partner data needed for program delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation helps prevent unnecessary secondary use and over-sharing.

mitigations.description: Perform periodic access reviews to verify that each user's create, edit, and view permissions match current job duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps catch misassigned roles before they lead to unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Enforce a retention schedule that deletes or de-identifies records once they are no longer required, including archived records older than the approved period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
mitigations.rationale: Shortening retention reduces the amount of personal data available for breach or misuse.

mitigations.description: Implement data quality review and record update procedures so historical customer and farm records remain accurate before they are used for decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
mitigations.rationale: Keeping records current reduces harms from stale information.

mitigations.description: Treat geospatial boundary data as sensitive and limit its disclosure to users who need it for farm record maintenance and program delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
mitigations.rationale: Location-linked farm boundaries can reveal sensitive operational information and should not be broadly exposed.

mitigations.description: Continue using encrypted transmission for inter-agency transfers and ensure encryption is required for all shared data flows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data transmission is protected by encryption including Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the risk of interception during data sharing.

risks.description: The system retains producer records indefinitely, which increases the long-term privacy impact if the data is misused, breached, or accessed for purposes beyond the original program need.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention keeps personal and program data available far longer than the immediate eligibility and payment need.

risks.description: Department contractors can access the system, creating a risk that personal and program data could be exposed to more people than necessary if need-to-know controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of individuals who can view sensitive producer information.

risks.description: Internal sharing with shared services and notification components can expose producer data across multiple systems, increasing the chance of unnecessary dissemination or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: Data flowing to shared services or other components creates additional points where privacy controls must be enforced.

risks.description: The system generates and mails notices to producers, which can reveal that a person is participating in or affected by a disaster-assistance program to anyone who handles the mail.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
risks.rationale: Physical mailing of program notices can disclose sensitive participation information outside the system.

risks.description: Some components store or process producer payment history, overpayments, and debt-related information, which can reveal financial distress or program compliance details.
risks.evidence_quote: Retain producer payment history information
risks.rationale: Payment and overpayment records are sensitive because they expose financial and administrative details about the producer.

risks.description: County office users can access and process records using identifiers such as last four digits of an ID, producer ID, or last name, which may increase the chance of misidentification or unauthorized lookup if controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
risks.rationale: Using partial identifiers for access or processing can make records easier to search but also easier to query incorrectly.

risks.description: The system stores names and street addresses for many programs, so a compromise could directly identify producers and link them to disaster, revenue-loss, or assistance status.
risks.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers combined with program participation can make the records personally sensitive.

risks.description: The system relies on SCIMS as the source for all PII, so any inaccuracies or stale data in that source could propagate into FPDS and affect eligibility or payment decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: All PII, however, is pulled from SCIMS and is not requested or received directly from producers.
risks.rationale: When one source feeds all PII into multiple applications, source errors can affect many downstream records.

mitigations.description: Conduct periodic retention reviews and purge or archive records when no longer needed, even where the current schedule treats them as permanent records.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the active footprint of old records lowers the amount of data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict need-to-know role approval, background investigations, Level 2 eAuthentication, and NDA requirements for contractors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: The stated controls limit contractor access to only those with a justified business need.

mitigations.description: Limit internal disclosure to the minimum necessary data fields and apply access controls and logging to shared-service interfaces.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting shared-service flows reduces the chance that data will be reused beyond the intended program purpose.

mitigations.description: Use privacy-protective mail handling and minimize the information shown in printed notices to what is necessary for delivery and program administration.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what appears on mailed notices reduces disclosure to mail handlers and others who may see the envelope or contents.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to payment history and overpayment records to staff who need them for payment administration and debt notification.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Retain producer payment history information
mitigations.rationale: Payment history is sensitive and should only be visible to personnel with a direct administrative need.

mitigations.description: Require stronger identity verification before permitting record lookup or payment processing based on partial identifiers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
mitigations.rationale: Additional verification helps prevent mistaken or unauthorized access when weak identifiers are used.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization to names and street addresses by collecting, processing, and printing them only when required for the specific program function.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing direct identifiers reduces the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Validate and periodically reconcile SCIMS-sourced PII before it is used in FPDS decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All PII, however, is pulled from SCIMS and is not requested or received directly from producers.
mitigations.rationale: Checking source data helps prevent inaccurate records from affecting eligibility and payment outcomes.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data that could cause identity theft or financial harm if exposed. This includes SSNs or last 4 SSN digits, names, addresses, farm tract numbers, and payment amounts.
risks.evidence_quote: ARCPLC Name, mailing address, last 4 digits SSN SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: SSNs and payment data are sensitive identifiers that increase the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: ARCPLC displays producer PII retrieved from SCIMS, which increases the chance that users may see more personal data than they need for the task. Even if ARCPLC does not maintain the data, displaying it still creates an exposure surface.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application. We do not maintain or collect but do display the data retrieved from SCIMS.
risks.rationale: Displaying PII inside the application can expose it to users who only need limited information to determine eligibility.

risks.description: SWIMS is a shared database accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees, so internal misuse or unauthorized internal access could expose producer PII. The shared nature of the database broadens the number of insiders who can reach the data.
risks.evidence_quote: a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: Any shared internal repository increases the risk of inappropriate access by authorized users or compromised accounts.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, which increases the amount of time PII remains available for breach, misuse, or secondary exposure. Permanent retention also increases the volume of records that must be protected over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases cumulative exposure risk because records remain available for future compromise.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of sensitive identifiers to the minimum needed for eligibility and payment processing, and mask or truncate identifiers where full values are not required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To determine eligibility.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing use of SSNs and payment data reduces the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Restrict ARCPLC screens so users only see the producer data necessary for their role, and apply role-based access controls to the displayed SCIMS data.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based display limits reduce unnecessary exposure of PII within the application.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access controls and periodic access reviews for the limited set of FSA employees who can use SWIMS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access governance lowers the chance of inappropriate internal viewing or misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule consistently and purge or archive records according to retention rules instead of keeping active copies indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved schedule reduces the number of records exposed over time while still meeting records-management requirements.

risks.description: County office users can access a broad set of farmer and producer PII, including contact, entity, and demographic information, which creates a risk of unnecessary exposure or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: the other application (FSAfarm+) does contain PII. This PIA is required since FSAfarm+ uses personal information of farmers and producers.
risks.rationale: The more personal data available to users, the greater the chance of improper viewing or use.

risks.description: The system allows SSN/EIN to be used in a search screen and as a second authentication method, creating a risk of exposing highly sensitive identifiers.
risks.evidence_quote: EIN / SSN (via a search screen)
risks.rationale: SSN and EIN are highly sensitive identifiers, so using them in user-facing functions increases harm if disclosed.

risks.description: County office users may search for a specific farmer or producer, which creates a risk of unauthorized lookups or insider curiosity access.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII allows County Office users to search for a specific user as well as a second authentication method to validate farmers and producers.
risks.rationale: Search capability can be misused to retrieve records unrelated to an employee's legitimate work need.

risks.description: Contractors supporting the system may have access to the application, which creates a risk that PII could be seen by personnel who do not need it for routine operations.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any non-user access to a system handling PII increases the number of people who could encounter the data.

risks.description: PII is pulled from SCIMS in another system boundary, which creates a risk of unauthorized access during retrieval or of using data beyond the minimum needed in FSCOMS.
risks.evidence_quote: FSAfarm+ requests and receives PII from SCIMS, which resides in the FPCMS system.
risks.rationale: Cross-system retrieval expands the attack surface and can expose data during transfer or lookup.

risks.description: Although the system says memory and cache are cleared on logout, any failure in that process could leave PII available in session memory or cache.
risks.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: Transient storage can still expose data if clearing does not occur as intended.

mitigations.description: Restrict county office users to the minimum PII needed for their task and enforce role-based access controls for viewing records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that users see or use more personal data than necessary.

mitigations.description: Minimize SSN/EIN use in the search screen and second-authentication flow, and mask or partially redact these identifiers wherever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing visible use of sensitive identifiers lowers the risk of disclosure.

mitigations.description: Require a documented business need and audit logging for each farmer or producer search by county office users.
mitigations.rationale: Logging and need-to-know controls deter and detect inappropriate lookups.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the smallest set of support personnel and require the same PII handling and access controls applied to government users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting support access reduces the number of people who can encounter PII.

mitigations.description: Protect requests to SCIMS with strong authentication, authorization, and secure transport, and retrieve only the specific fields needed for the user’s task.
mitigations.rationale: Secure and minimal cross-system access reduces exposure while data is being retrieved.

mitigations.description: Verify and test that logout always clears memory and cache as stated, and monitor for any residual PII after session termination.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
mitigations.rationale: Testing and monitoring help ensure transient data is not left behind.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive personal and demographic information, including race and ethnicity, which could expose producers to privacy harm if improperly accessed or used.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: Race and ethnicity are sensitive data elements, so their collection and maintenance increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system keeps producers’ election-related records permanently, increasing the chance that older personal data will remain available longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention expands the window in which records can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: County office staff enter producer data, so mistakes or incomplete entries could cause incorrect eligibility decisions or inaccurate election records.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual data entry creates a risk that the system will store inaccurate information and use it for election-related decisions.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to identify who may vote in committee elections, which could reveal a producer’s participation or eligibility status in a sensitive local election process.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
risks.rationale: Eligibility determinations tied to named producers can disclose sensitive participation information if improperly accessed.

risks.description: The system stores the current organizational structure of elected COC members and election results, which could expose governance information about individuals if accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: stores current organizational structure of elected COC members.
risks.rationale: Member and election records can reveal personal association with committee service and terms.

risks.description: Although the system says it does not share outside USDA, any unauthorized disclosure outside the department would expose producer data beyond the intended use.
risks.evidence_quote: No application information is being shared outside of the USDA environment.
risks.rationale: The absence of intended external sharing does not eliminate the privacy harm if data are disclosed improperly.

mitigations.description: Limit access to race and ethnicity data to only personnel with a documented need to know and enforce role-based access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive demographic data will be viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records must remain indefinitely and, where permitted by the records schedule, minimize retention to the approved period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Using the approved records schedule to minimize retention reduces long-term exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Implement validation and review checks for county office data entry before records are used for eligibility or ballot generation.
mitigations.rationale: Verification steps can catch errors before they affect election-related decisions.

mitigations.description: Limit visibility of eligibility lists and related election data to authorized election staff and use the information only for the stated election purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is being used to identify/select producers eligible to vote in committee elections, send ballots, and collect results.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the stated purpose reduces the risk that eligibility status is exposed beyond what is necessary.

mitigations.description: Apply access controls and audit logging to committee member and election result records so only authorized users can view or change them.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Create the COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms. • Track Election results and COC Member data.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting member and election records limits unauthorized disclosure of governance-related personal information.

mitigations.description: Maintain the stated boundary of no external disclosure and monitor for unauthorized export or transmission of producer records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No application information is being shared outside of the USDA environment.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring and enforcing the no-external-sharing rule helps prevent accidental or unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive identifiers and financial information, so a breach or misuse could expose people to identity theft or financial harm.
risks.evidence_quote: Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: These data elements are sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure could directly harm the affected individuals.

risks.description: Because the warehouse combines farm, loan, commodity, human resources, and financial data into one reporting environment, it increases the impact of any unauthorized access or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: All Program and financial data for the Agency is stored in the EDW. This includes Farm Program, Farm Loan, Commodity Operations, Human Resources and Financial data.
risks.rationale: Consolidating multiple categories of personal data creates a larger privacy impact if access is compromised.

risks.description: Internal sharing of PII across multiple agencies and through batch processes can disclose more information than needed or expose data during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Broad internal sharing expands the number of people and systems handling the data.

risks.description: External disclosures to other entities, including IRS, Treasury, a university, and Dunn and Bradstreet, create a risk of secondary use or disclosure beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW does not directly share information with external entities; However, FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Each external disclosure increases the chance that data will be used in ways the individuals did not expect.

risks.description: The system uses data for congressional, program level, and end user reporting, which may reveal personal details to users who do not need full-identifiable information.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the EDW is used for Congressional, program level and end user reporting.
risks.rationale: Reporting use can expose personal information to a wider audience than operational necessity requires.

risks.description: Retaining the data under the NARA schedule for an extended period may keep personal information available longer than needed, increasing the chance of later misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window during which data can be accessed, copied, or lost.

mitigations.description: Encrypt sensitive identifiers and account data at rest and in transit, and restrict access to users with a documented need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the most sensitive fields lowers the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and field-level access restrictions so users only see the data needed for their specific reporting function.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access within the warehouse reduces the harm from a centralized data store.

mitigations.description: Use secure batch-transfer controls, including integrity checks and access logging, for all internal data exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Controls on batch transfers reduce the chance of interception, tampering, or unauthorized reuse.

mitigations.description: Require data-sharing agreements and data minimization for each external disclosure, especially for one-time or validation-only exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EDW does not directly share information with external entities; However, FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the scope and terms of external sharing reduces secondary-use risk.

mitigations.description: Provide reporting users with aggregated or de-identified outputs whenever identifiable data is not necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing identifiability in reports limits unnecessary exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retained records and delete or archive them according to the approved NARA schedule and any approved deviations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any deviations from the NARA Retention Schedule will be approved by NARA when the archiving and retention strategy is defined..
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps ensure records are not kept longer than authorized.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive identity and financial data that could cause significant harm if exposed or misused, including SSN/TIN, bank account numbers, routing numbers, and signatures. This creates a high-impact privacy risk because the data supports payments, debt collection, and tax reporting for many individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: FDIS Images could contain information such as: Name, street address, SSN/TIN, phone number, Claim/NRRS number, agency case number, promissory number. bank account number, schedule of deposit numbers and image of the signature.
risks.rationale: Sensitive financial and identity data increases the potential harm from unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: Public-facing and producer-accessible applications increase the risk of unauthorized access to personal financial information. If authentication or session protections fail, producers or outsiders could view payments, collections, debt, or banking information.
risks.evidence_quote: The Financial Services System resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is public facing, with producers and farmers able to update their own information (i.e. banking and assignment information).
risks.rationale: Public-facing access expands the attack surface for unauthorized viewing or modification.

risks.description: County office employees and producers can view financial information in the same format, which can expose more detail than necessary to users who only need limited information. This raises a risk of overexposure of personal financial records within the USDA environment.
risks.evidence_quote: County Office employees also have access to FI so employees can answer producer's questions and view financial information in the same format the producer is viewing.
risks.rationale: Broad internal visibility can reveal more personal data than a user's role requires.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure of personal data. Even with need-to-know controls, contractor access expands the number of people handling sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: More authorized users means more opportunities for improper access or handling.

risks.description: The system sends delinquent debt status to commercial credit bureaus, which can affect individuals' creditworthiness and expose debt information beyond the original payment context. This creates a privacy risk because debt data is used for a secondary purpose with external reporting consequences.
risks.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
risks.rationale: Credit reporting can significantly affect individuals and increases the sensitivity of the disclosure.

risks.description: The system transmits payment and debt information to Treasury for offset, wage garnishment, and referral to collection agencies, which may reveal financial distress and debt status. These disclosures can affect individuals' privacy and financial standing outside the originating program.
risks.evidence_quote: The Department of the Treasury will use the information to offset Federal payments, wage garnishment, and referral to collection agencies.
risks.rationale: Debt-related disclosures can have substantial privacy and financial consequences.

risks.description: Permanent retention of records increases the risk that outdated or unnecessary personal information will remain available indefinitely. Long-term retention magnifies the impact of any future breach, misuse, or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping personal data forever increases exposure over time.

risks.description: The system stores and processes images and faxed or scanned materials, which may include full financial documents and signatures. Document imaging and manual ingestion can create a risk that sensitive information is captured more broadly than needed or retained in image form longer than expected.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from document storage, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Imaged documents can contain more personal information than structured records.

risks.description: The system generates letters and statements for producers, including debt and tax-related notices, which may be exposed if mailed or handled improperly. This creates a risk of disclosure through correspondence containing personal financial information.
risks.evidence_quote: NRRS generates letters to customers associated with a receivable and records the receipt of monies that have been collected to satisfy a receivable.
risks.rationale: Paper or statement-based communications can reveal sensitive account information.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive fields to only users with a demonstrated need to know and maintain role-based approval for access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the number of users who can see highly sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Use strong authentication and tightly controlled update permissions for the public-facing banking and assignment functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Financial Services System resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is public facing, with producers and farmers able to update their own information (i.e. banking and assignment information).
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and limited write access reduce the chance of unauthorized account changes.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls so county office employees can only see the minimum financial detail needed to assist producers.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting visible detail reduces unnecessary internal exposure of personal financial information.

mitigations.description: Continue mandatory background investigations, eAuthentication, and nondisclosure obligations for contractors before granting access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access
mitigations.rationale: Screening and authentication help reduce insider misuse by contractors.

mitigations.description: Restrict credit bureau reporting to only the delinquent debt information necessary for the authorized purpose and maintain encrypted transmission.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing the reported data and protecting transmission lowers disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Limit Treasury and collection-related disclosures to the minimum information needed to perform offsets, garnishment, and referrals.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Department of the Treasury will use the information to offset Federal payments, wage garnishment, and referral to collection agencies.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information shared for collection actions.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic review and disposal controls for records that no longer need to be retained, even if the schedule allows permanent retention.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing records for continued need can reduce the amount of old data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Apply strict handling controls to scanned, faxed, and imaged documents, including limiting who can upload and retrieve them.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from document storage, faxed, and scanned materials.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter document handling reduces the chance that sensitive images are improperly captured or accessed.

mitigations.description: Use secure mailing and statement controls for producer letters and tax notices so only the intended recipient receives the information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: RMO prints and mails the letters to the producers.
mitigations.rationale: Secure delivery helps prevent accidental disclosure through correspondence.

risks.description: The system stores identifiable employee information that could be exposed if access controls are weak or misconfigured. Even limited fields like name and mailing address can create privacy harm if unauthorized users can view authorization records.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS Name & mailing address
risks.rationale: Any stored PII creates exposure risk if the system is not tightly access-controlled.

risks.description: The system maintains authorization data about employees’ roles, groups, offices, and attributes, which could reveal sensitive access patterns or job relationships if improperly accessed. That information can be used to infer internal responsibilities and system privileges.
risks.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes to business applications
risks.rationale: Authorization metadata can itself be privacy-sensitive because it reveals how individuals are positioned within the organization.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, increasing the chance that outdated or unnecessary employee information remains available longer than needed. Long-term retention also expands the window for unauthorized access or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases cumulative privacy exposure over time.

risks.description: Administrators can manage security access rights in real time, which creates a risk of excessive privilege or mistaken role assignment affecting employee data access. If role changes are not carefully controlled, users may gain access they should not have.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS allows administrators to use a web browser to manage security access rights, assigning and removing roles/groups/attributes to users on-line in real time.
risks.rationale: Real-time administrative changes can cause unauthorized access if not governed by strong procedures.

risks.description: The system is designed to support access to business applications, so any compromise of the role-based access control function could broaden access across multiple applications. A failure in this central authorization service could therefore affect many users’ privacy at once.
risks.evidence_quote: Facilitate Role-Based Access Control system.
risks.rationale: A central access-control system has broad downstream privacy impact if misused or breached.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access and strong authentication for all users who can view or administer authorization records.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that name and mailing address data are exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Limit visibility of role, group, office, and attribute data to personnel with a documented need to know, and log all access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and auditing reduce the risk of privacy-invasive inspection of authorization metadata.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether permanently retained records are still required and archive or suppress access to records no longer needed for operations.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review can reduce unnecessary exposure even when records must be retained under schedule.

mitigations.description: Require approval workflows or dual review for high-impact role changes and regularly reconcile assigned roles against authoritative personnel records.
mitigations.rationale: Additional review helps prevent accidental or excessive privilege assignments.

mitigations.description: Harden the central authorization service with monitoring, change control, and periodic security testing because it supports access to business applications.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the core access-control function limits the privacy impact of a compromise.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal data, so any unauthorized access or exposure could cause significant harm to individuals. The data includes direct identifiers and especially sensitive categories such as financial, health, biometric, and criminal history information.
risks.evidence_quote: Full name, mother’s maiden name, maiden f h i di id i k li ) Date and/or place of birth. Address Information (street & email address). Personal identification number (social security number, tax identification number, passport number, driver’s license number or a unique identification number, etc.) Financial data (Credit card numbers, bank account etc.) Health data (including height, weight, blood pressure, etc.) Biometric data (fingerprints, iris scans, voice signature, facial geometry, DNA, etc.) Criminal history
risks.rationale: The broader and more sensitive the stored PII, the greater the harm if it is accessed or disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Permanent retention increases the privacy impact of any breach or improper access because the records remain available indefinitely. Long-term storage also increases the chance that outdated or unnecessary personal information will persist beyond operational need.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention extends the exposure window and makes later misuse or compromise more consequential.

risks.description: Browser-based client access to stored images can create a risk of unauthorized viewing if access controls are weak or misconfigured. Because users can retrieve images from a network device managed by the server, improper authorization could expose records to staff who do not need them.
risks.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.rationale: Any retrieval interface that exposes stored images needs strong access restrictions to prevent unnecessary access to PII.

risks.description: Workflow functions can expose personal data to more people or systems than are necessary for simple storage and retrieval. When the system controls workflows associated with financial information, data may be routed through multiple processing steps, increasing the chance of internal overexposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.rationale: Workflow processing often expands access paths, so limiting who can see records at each step reduces privacy risk.

risks.description: Imported faxed, scanned, and emailed documents may contain inaccurate, incomplete, or misdirected personal information, which could lead to improper storage or retrieval of the wrong record. If the wrong document is imaged or indexed, individuals may be associated with incorrect financial or identity information.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from electronically stored documents, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Manual ingestion from multiple sources raises the chance of human error that can misfile or misassociate personal data.

risks.description: The system holds historical archive images, including records that are no longer actively updated, which may increase the chance of unnecessary continued access to old personal information. Historical records can still reveal sensitive details about debtors, claims, and check images long after the original business need has passed.
risks.evidence_quote: It is used to store and view FRB check images and pertinent information on CCC checks. It is used to pull up images of CCC checks. The KCFRB system is used to research historical archives of treasury checks.
risks.rationale: Historical archives can remain sensitive even when no new content is added, so access should be tightly limited.

risks.description: The system stores financial records, debts, debtors, and other information, so unauthorized disclosure could enable financial fraud, identity theft, or reputational harm. The presence of account-related and debt-related data makes the consequences of exposure especially serious.
risks.evidence_quote: Storage of financial records, debts, debtors, and other information to the server uses Netapp Snaplock which is controlled by the server software.
risks.rationale: Financial and debt information is highly sensitive and can be misused if disclosed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the sensitive imaging records to only authorized users with a documented need to know, and enforce role-based permissions for the different subsystems and document types.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access is the most direct way to reduce the risk from highly sensitive PII.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review process to confirm whether any subsets of the indefinite-retention records can be archived, minimized, or disposed of when no longer required by the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review reduces unnecessary long-term exposure while respecting approved retention requirements.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and least-privilege authorization for browser-based retrieval, and log all image access so unauthorized viewing can be detected and investigated.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access control and auditability help prevent and detect inappropriate viewing of stored images.

mitigations.description: Limit workflow visibility so each user or role can see only the records needed for that workflow step, and separate workflow functions from broader retrieval permissions where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting workflow visibility reduces unnecessary internal exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Add validation and quality checks for scanned, faxed, and emailed documents before they are indexed, including verification of document-to-person matching and correction of indexing errors.
mitigations.rationale: Verification at ingestion reduces the chance that incorrect or misfiled personal information is stored and later retrieved.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter access controls and periodic access reviews for historical archive systems so only users with a specific archival or investigative need can retrieve old records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The KCFRB system is used to research historical archives of treasury checks.
mitigations.rationale: Historical records remain sensitive, so narrowing access lowers the chance of unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Protect financial and debt records with encryption and monitoring controls for storage and retrieval, especially for the server and database components that manage document indexes and workflow.
mitigations.rationale: Technical safeguards help reduce the impact of unauthorized access to financial and debt information.

risks.description: Users may see more personal information than is necessary for the PSS task because the system includes names, addresses, application and contract identifiers, and multiple eligibility and status fields tied to individual records.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII that is used, processed or maintained by FA Tracker includes name, address, as well as the following: o Application # o Contract # o Contract Item # ... o Contract Modification Reason ... o Status of a Payment ... o AD-1026 (Y/N) ... o AGI (Y/N) ... o Member AGI (%) ... o Application Status ... o Adequacy Status ... o Obligation Status
risks.rationale: The broader the displayed record content, the greater the chance of unnecessary internal exposure of sensitive program information.

risks.description: Exporting work lists to Excel can create uncontrolled local copies of personally identifiable information on user devices.
risks.evidence_quote: Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Local files are easier to copy, retain, or mishandle than data kept inside the controlled application.

risks.description: E-mail alerts can disclose personally identifiable information through a channel that may be forwarded, stored, or accessed outside the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
risks.rationale: Email delivery increases the chance that sensitive data will persist in inboxes or be shared beyond the intended recipient.

risks.description: Users with access to PT-FM can reach FA Tracker data, so a broader-than-necessary access grant could expose records to people who only need limited information.
risks.evidence_quote: If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Tying access to PT-FM eligibility may allow more users to see FA Tracker data than a narrower role-based need would require.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system and therefore view PII, creating a risk of misuse or accidental disclosure by non-federal users.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the set of people handling personal data and increases the importance of strong access controls and behavior rules.
