risks.description: The system relies on data replicated from SCIMS, so any stale or inaccurate copied information could affect individuals’ records and work-list decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via the National Planning and Agreements Database (NPAD) [which resides on PT-FM] and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: Replicated data can lag behind the source system, which can lead to incorrect treatment of a person’s eligibility or status.

risks.description: The system includes demographic-related information from SCIMS, which can increase sensitivity if used or viewed beyond the stated conservation-program purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Demographic information is especially sensitive and should be tightly limited to authorized, legitimate uses.

risks.description: Long retention of records increases the period during which personal information remains available for internal access, disclosure, or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years
risks.rationale: The longer personal data is kept, the longer it is exposed to operational and security risks.

mitigations.description: Limit the work lists to the minimum fields needed for PSS intervention and keep the current minimal-display approach.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FA Tracker does this by running specific queries over the data and displays minimal information to users in the form of work lists.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing displayed fields reduces unnecessary internal exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Restrict or disable Excel export for records containing PII, or require stronger controls such as approved secure storage and audit logging for any exported file.
mitigations.rationale: Preventing or tightly controlling exports reduces the risk of uncontrolled local copies on user devices.

mitigations.description: Limit e-mail alerts to the smallest possible data set and avoid including direct identifiers where feasible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the content of email alerts lowers the chance of disclosure through a less secure communication channel.

mitigations.description: Keep access tied to role-based, need-to-know authorization and verify that FA Tracker roles are narrower than PT-FM access where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based filtering helps ensure users only see records necessary for their duties.

mitigations.description: Continue requiring background investigations, Level 2 eAuthentication, NDAs, and Rules of Behavior for contractors, and enforce those conditions with periodic review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access ... Through the USDA Rules of Behavior, they are not allowed to download, share, store or print any USDA specific data ... Contractors are required to sign NDAs
mitigations.rationale: Strong onboarding and conduct requirements reduce the likelihood of contractor misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use procedures to reconcile replicated data against the source system and flag records that may be outdated before they are used in work lists.
mitigations.rationale: Checking replicated data for freshness helps prevent decisions based on stale or inaccurate information.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to demographic reports and related SCIMS-derived fields to authorized users with a documented need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access to sensitive demographic data reduces the chance of inappropriate use or exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition schedules consistently and delete records when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: External users can access and review their program information through the public interface, creating a risk that weak authentication or authorization could expose other participants' data.
risks.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
risks.rationale: Any public-facing interface that handles participant records can expose data if access controls fail.

risks.description: The system holds tax identification numbers and payment bank information, which are sensitive financial identifiers that could be misused if disclosed or accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions.
risks.rationale: Financial identifiers increase harm if exposed because they can be used for fraud or identity misuse.

risks.description: Reports and nightly files are used by internal teams and submitted to auditors and other departments, creating a risk of over-disclosure beyond the minimum necessary information.
risks.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA. Reports are for internal use only by Government employees and contractors; however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
risks.rationale: Broader distribution of reports increases the chance that more personal or business contact data is shared than needed.

risks.description: Department contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of unauthorized access, misuse, or secondary disclosure by non-federal personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of people who can view or handle the data.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, increasing the chance that data will be exposed, misused, or kept longer than needed for the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window of exposure and the consequences of any future breach or improper use.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong role-based access controls and authentication for the public interface so users can only enter and review their own program information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the user's own records directly reduces the risk of cross-account disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit access to tax identification numbers and payment bank information to only personnel who need it, and mask or redact those fields in reports and screens where full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing visibility of sensitive financial identifiers reduces the harm from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and disclosure review before generating or distributing reports and nightly files to ensure only necessary fields are included.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing outputs before sharing helps prevent unnecessary disclosure to auditors and other departments.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be limited by least privilege and subject to monitoring and periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access and review reduce the chance that contractors can access more data than needed.

mitigations.description: Use a records review process to confirm that permanently retained records remain necessary and are protected with strong safeguards over time.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Ongoing review and protection are important because indefinite retention extends the exposure period.

risks.description: Uploaded files may contain highly sensitive personal data, so unauthorized disclosure could expose identity, financial, employment, criminal, or signature information. Because the system stores documents rather than collecting only narrow fields, a single file can reveal extensive PII.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box contains documents stored in a file repository that may include a wide range of PII.
risks.rationale: The system holds many categories of sensitive PII in one place, increasing the impact of any access failure.

risks.description: Internal and external collaboration can expose PII to more people than necessary if sharing is not tightly limited to a need-to-know basis. The system is intended to support sharing with employees, contractors, affiliates, partners, and customers.
risks.evidence_quote: allowing internal / external collaboration from partners and customers
risks.rationale: Broader collaboration increases the chance that PII is viewed or copied by unintended recipients.

risks.description: Manual sharing of files creates a risk of human error, such as sending or granting access to the wrong file or recipient. Since sharing is performed by authorized users rather than automatically controlled by the system, mistakes may be harder to detect.
risks.evidence_quote: that ‘sharing’ is a manual process of authorized users accessing the data files, and not an automated function of the FPAC Box system/application.
risks.rationale: Manual access decisions are more prone to accidental over-disclosure than automated controls.

risks.description: External partners and contractors may access PII through the system, which increases the risk of disclosure outside USDA if access is misused or improperly managed. The system explicitly allows access for partners and contractors consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.evidence_quote: authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Every additional external user group expands the trust boundary around the data.

risks.description: PII stored in a third-party cloud service may be exposed if the vendor mishandles security or access controls. The agency states that third-party PII will be maintained and secured by the vendor.
risks.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
risks.rationale: Outsourcing custody of PII creates dependency on the vendor's security practices.

risks.description: PII available through third-party applications is not periodically purged, which can leave sensitive information exposed longer than necessary. Longer availability increases the chance of unauthorized access over time.
risks.evidence_quote: 10.6 Is the PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications purged periodically? • No
risks.rationale: Data that is retained longer than needed has a longer window for misuse or compromise.

risks.description: Long retention periods can keep personal data available for years after it is no longer needed for a current purpose. The system retains information for five to ten years, and in some cases as long as the individual qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years
risks.rationale: Extended retention increases the amount of historical PII that could be exposed in a breach or misuse.

risks.description: User profile information derived from LDAP may be inaccurate or outdated if users do not update it, which can cause incorrect identity or access records. The system also allows users to update their own PII, which could introduce inconsistent records if not validated.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box uses the PII that was initially obtained from LDAP to establish the user’s profile. FPAC Box can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Profile data used for administration should be accurate to avoid improper access or misidentification.

mitigations.description: Restrict file access with role-based authorization and strong encryption for stored and transmitted documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to FPAC Box is controlled through role-based authorization, eAuthentication, and DRM, which includes FIPS 140-2 certified encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting data cryptographically reduces the chance that sensitive file contents are exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing to authorized users with a need-to-know and enforce role-based access controls for collaboration.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII information is stored within FPAC Box and shared with authorized USDA employees, contractors, and affiliates with a need-to-know to conduct the business of the organization.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know sharing reduces unnecessary exposure during collaboration.

mitigations.description: Add stronger sharing safeguards such as mandatory recipient verification or approval before a file can be shared externally.
mitigations.rationale: Extra verification would reduce the chance of accidental disclosure from manual sharing.

mitigations.description: Constrain contractor and partner access to the minimum permissions needed for their assigned tasks and review those permissions regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Minimum necessary access lowers the risk of unauthorized use by external collaborators.

mitigations.description: Require the vendor to maintain documented security controls and oversight for any PII hosted in the third-party service.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
mitigations.rationale: Vendor security controls are essential when the vendor is responsible for protecting the hosted PII.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic purging of PII stored in third-party applications when it is no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Regular purging shortens the exposure window for data held in third-party systems.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce records schedules so files are deleted or archived as soon as the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Following approved retention schedules prevents unnecessary long-term storage of PII.

mitigations.description: Validate profile updates before they are accepted, especially when users modify their own PII.
mitigations.rationale: Validation helps ensure that profile records remain accurate and reliable.

risks.description: User information is transmitted through the portal to DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov, creating a risk that sensitive application data could be exposed if those communications are intercepted or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: As a result, information will be sent to (and from) users (farmers and producers) to DOL and USCIS, even though FPAC CASP / H2A does not assess or perform any actions on the data.
risks.rationale: Any system that relays user information to external agencies increases exposure during transit and at the receiving systems.

risks.description: The system stores a producer’s DOL case number for 90 days, which can create a link between a user and their inquiry even if the system says it does not store other PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The only user information that is stored on FPAC CASP is a producer’s DOL case number; this information does not identify the specific user or contain any user information. This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
risks.rationale: A retained case number can still function as an indirect identifier when combined with external records or context.

risks.description: Because the portal is a single entry point to multiple agencies, users may not clearly understand which organization is collecting and using their information at each step.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: A shared entry point can blur responsibility and make privacy notices and consent expectations less clear.

risks.description: The system depends on third-party federal services for authentication and processing, so privacy protections may vary across Login.gov, DOL, and USCIS rather than being controlled solely by USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is an application specifically designed to allow farmers and producers to access Login.gov, DOL, and USCIS.
risks.rationale: Using external systems expands the privacy risk surface beyond the hosting system's direct control.

risks.description: Although the system says no PII is stored, it still expects PII to be present within the system boundary, which creates a risk of accidental logging, caching, or other unintended retention.
risks.evidence_quote: The H2A application is used by farmers and producers to access DOL and UCSIS, therefore the H2A application is expected to have PII inside its system boundary.
risks.rationale: Data that passes through a system can be inadvertently captured by logs, caches, or support tools even when not intended for storage.

mitigations.description: Continue to require HTTPS for all communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and the external agencies, and verify that strong TLS configurations are enforced end to end.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov occur using HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Encrypted transport reduces the likelihood that transmitted user information can be intercepted in transit.

mitigations.description: Minimize the stored case-number record by keeping it only as long as needed for the inquiry workflow and then deleting it promptly at the end of the 90-day period or sooner if no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention lowers the chance that an indirect identifier can be used to link a user to their inquiry later.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice at the single entry point explaining which agency collects each piece of information and how it will be used before the user is routed onward.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
mitigations.rationale: Clear disclosure helps users understand who is responsible for collecting and using their information.

mitigations.description: Limit the data shared with Login.gov, DOL, and USCIS to the minimum needed for authentication and application processing, and document those interfaces.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is an application specifically designed to allow farmers and producers to access Login.gov, DOL, and USCIS.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the privacy impact of relying on external systems.

mitigations.description: Prevent accidental retention by ensuring that logs, caches, and temporary files do not capture user PII or other transmitted application data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The H2A application is used by farmers and producers to access DOL and UCSIS, therefore the H2A application is expected to have PII inside its system boundary.
mitigations.rationale: Controls against unintended storage reduce the chance that pass-through data becomes a persistent privacy record.

risks.description: DRMS contains highly sensitive personal and financial information that could expose individuals if access controls fail or are misused. The stored records can include SSNs, tax IDs, bank routing numbers, deposit account numbers, and other detailed PII in scanned documents.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored PII increases the harm if the data is improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: TeamMate+ contains audit materials about programs, administrative areas, and customers that may include personal and operational details, creating a privacy risk if those records are exposed. The system may hold information from many FPAC divisions and external parties, including private individuals and other governments.
risks.evidence_quote: The data could be produced by any Division, Branch, State, County, or National Office of FPAC this includes FBC (FPAC Business Center), NRCS, FSA, or RMA. The data could also be produced by customers of FPAC, this can include private individuals, cooperatives, other local, state, and federal governments and it could include non-government organizations
risks.rationale: A broad set of contributors and subjects means audit records can reveal information about many different individuals and entities.

risks.description: Many staff can upload and search DRMS documents, which creates a risk of unnecessary internal access to personal records. Although access is role-based, the system states that all staff can search documents within their organizational role and rights.
risks.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights.
risks.rationale: Search capability across stored records can increase the chance that users view information beyond what is needed for their duties.

risks.description: Specialized DRMS users can perform unconstrained searching for legal and audit purposes, which increases the risk of overbroad access to personal information. This capability is specifically available for records managers and legal staff.
risks.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Unconstrained searching expands the amount of personal information a privileged user can retrieve.

risks.description: The system allows contractor access, which raises the risk of privacy harm from a larger population of users handling PII. Contractors are explicitly permitted access if they have a need-to-know.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Adding contractors increases the number of people who can see sensitive records and the likelihood of mishandling.

risks.description: DRMS retains records for long periods and many applications retain information indefinitely, which increases the risk of unnecessary prolonged exposure of PII. The retention strategy includes permanent records and retention that can extend beyond ten years.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time during which records can be accessed, misused, or disclosed.

risks.description: TeamMate+ audit records can be uploaded directly by customers or by auditors, which creates a risk that incorrect or excessive personal information could be entered into the system. The system relies on human upload paths rather than only controlled automated ingestion.
risks.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
risks.rationale: Multiple upload paths increase the chance that sensitive information is added without sufficient review or minimization.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing need-to-know access controls and least-privilege authorization for all users handling DRMS and TeamMate+ records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS access is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to authorized duties reduces the chance that highly sensitive PII is viewed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit audit record access to the Internal Auditing Branch and keep TeamMate+ information for internal use only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Everything generated or held by the Internal Auditing Branch is for internal use only.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting the audience for audit records lowers the risk that personal or sensitive information is exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Maintain role-based permissions so staff can only upload and search documents within their organizational role and rights.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based limits reduce unnecessary access while preserving needed business functions.

mitigations.description: Restrict unconstrained searching to records managers and legal staff only, and require it only for approved audit, legal discovery, litigation hold, or FOIA purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing the use of broad search privileges reduces the chance of overcollection or excessive internal viewing.

mitigations.description: Apply the same documented access control procedures and need-to-know review to contractors before granting access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Verifying contractor need-to-know helps ensure only necessary personnel can handle sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Retain records only for the approved NARA schedule and avoid indefinite retention unless a specific records schedule requires it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention to approved schedules reduces the period during which personal data remains exposed.

mitigations.description: Require review of uploaded audit materials to ensure only necessary information is entered and that incorrect completion or incompleteness is corrected before use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: humans (auditors) are used to review the data for incorrect completion, incompleteness, conflicts with policy, etc.
mitigations.rationale: Review before use helps prevent unnecessary or inaccurate personal data from being stored in the system.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive identifiers, including SSNs and EINs, which would create significant harm if exposed through any compromise of the platform or its applications. Because the platform hosts many HVA applications, a breach could affect a large amount of identity-linked crop insurance data at once.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, Address, Phone Numbers, SSN, EIN number, eAuth JD/Name, Farm IDs
risks.rationale: SSNs and EINs are sensitive identifiers that increase the impact of unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Data is shared with an internal fraud-analysis group, creating a risk that PII will be used more broadly than needed for eligibility, claims, or reimbursement purposes. Even legitimate investigative access can expand exposure if not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: The data is primarily shared with the RMA Strategic Data Analysis Division. This group performs the forensic data mining of RMA's data, looking for indications of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse.
risks.rationale: Fraud analytics can require broad access, which raises the risk of secondary use or over-collection.

risks.description: External sharing with Approved Insurance Providers exposes PII outside USDA, increasing the chance of unauthorized disclosure or misuse by non-federal entities. The system sends SSNs and EINs back to the same entities that collected them, so any weakness at the AIP side affects the data subjects.
risks.evidence_quote: Policy information is shared only with the Approved insurance Providers (AIP). These are the very entities that collect the information.
risks.rationale: Sharing outside the Department expands the trust boundary and the number of parties handling the data.

risks.description: The system retains most application records indefinitely, which increases the duration of exposure and the amount of historical personal data available if the system is breached or misused. Long retention also raises the chance that data will outlive its original need.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases cumulative privacy risk and the impact of any later compromise.

risks.description: The system relies on multiple contractors and many applications, which can broaden access to PII and make least-privilege enforcement harder. More users and more components increase the chance of unauthorized internal access or accidental disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Additional non-owner access paths increase the attack surface and insider-risk exposure.

risks.description: The system uses hard copy forms and e-forms submitted through AIPs, which creates collection and transmission risk before the data reaches the platform. Paper and intermediary handling can lead to loss, misrouting, or incomplete security controls.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected via hard copy forms and e-forms completed by the insured producer, insurance agent, or adjustor. The AIP sends this information to RMA on their behalf.
risks.rationale: More collection channels and intermediaries increase the chance of mishandling personal data.

risks.description: Because the system uses PII to determine eligibility and payment calculations, inaccurate data could cause improper benefit decisions or incorrect reimbursement amounts. Errors in submitted policy data could affect producers, agents, and loss adjusters financially.
risks.evidence_quote: This data is being collected to determine the eligibility of producers, agents and loss adjusters for the Federal Crop Insurance Program, to detail the amount and types of claims to be processed and/or paid by the RMA on behalf of the FCIC
risks.rationale: Eligibility and payment decisions depend on correct personal and policy data.

risks.description: The system shares data for actuarial trend analysis and program viability, which can create a risk of using personal information for purposes beyond the individual’s immediate insurance transaction. Even if permitted, this increases privacy sensitivity because data may be repurposed for broader program analytics.
risks.evidence_quote: to track certain actuarial trends and data to determine viability of current and future insurance products.
risks.rationale: Analytical reuse can expose personal data to broader internal processing than the original collection purpose.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong role-based access controls and encryption for SSNs, EINs, and other sensitive identifiers, with regular review of who can view or export them.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is transferred via an encrypted VPN tunnel. AIP access is controlled via the same 586 identification process as used by RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and protecting access reduces the likelihood and impact of exposure of the most sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Limit the fraud-analysis team to the minimum data necessary and log all queries, exports, and case reviews for periodic oversight.
mitigations.rationale: Minimization and auditability reduce the chance that investigative access becomes broader secondary use.

mitigations.description: Continue to require encrypted transmission to AIPs and verify that AIP access is controlled and limited to the policies they collected.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is transferred via an encrypted VPN tunnel. AIP access is controlled via the same 586 identification process as used by RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and controlled access lower the risk of unauthorized disclosure to external recipients.

mitigations.description: Apply records-management rules to purge or archive data when no longer required, instead of retaining all applications indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for applications on Pipeline RMA HVA will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Retention limits reduce the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use least-privilege access for contractors and separate duties across applications so contractor access is limited to specific functions and datasets.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Constraining contractor access reduces the number of people who can see PII.

mitigations.description: Standardize secure submission procedures for hard copy and e-form intake, including validation and secure handling by AIPs before transmission to RMA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected via hard copy forms and e-forms completed by the insured producer, insurance agent, or adjustor. The AIP sends this information to RMA on their behalf.
mitigations.rationale: Secure intake controls reduce the risk of loss or mishandling before data reaches the system.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen validation and review of submitted policy data so errors are detected before eligibility or payment decisions are made.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PASS contains processes that edit and validate detail policy data submitted by the approved insurance providers to provide reasonable assurance that the data is accurate and timely
mitigations.rationale: Validation helps prevent incorrect personal or policy data from driving bad decisions.

mitigations.description: Document and limit analytic use of PII to the stated program purposes, and prefer de-identified or aggregated data for actuarial trend analysis where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: to track certain actuarial trends and data to determine viability of current and future insurance products.
mitigations.rationale: Using less identifiable data for analytics reduces unnecessary privacy exposure.

risks.description: The system may collect identifiable personal information from people who interact with CFPB on social media, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure of names, usernames, email addresses, IP addresses, geographic information, or demographic information.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may collect or use a limited amount of Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) when using social media to further its ability to interact with the public. PII is any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity such as name, username, email address, Internet Protocol (IP) address, geographic information, or demographic information.
risks.rationale: Any collection of PII creates privacy risk because the information can identify or trace a person.

risks.description: Because the system uses social media platforms that are controlled by third parties, users’ information may be subject to privacy practices and exposure outside CFPB’s direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: Social media platforms are generally controlled and operated by non-government third parties.
risks.rationale: Third-party control increases the chance that data handling will depend on external platform practices rather than CFPB protections alone.

risks.description: Public interactions on social media can reveal PII in a way that makes individual users more visible to others, including through posts, comments, usernames, or other platform metadata.
risks.evidence_quote: Social media helps us meet that goal by working with the public in a transparent way.
risks.rationale: Transparency in public-facing channels can expose user information to broader audiences than the user may expect.

risks.description: Collected PII could be retained or reused in ways that extend beyond the immediate social media interaction if not tightly limited to the stated purpose and SORN coverage.
risks.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB may collect PII through social media interactions, this information would be covered by the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System (CFPB.006) System of Records Notice.
risks.rationale: When PII is placed into a records system, retention and reuse controls become important to prevent unnecessary persistence.

risks.description: If users do not clearly understand when PII is collected through social media, they may share more information than intended or without fully informed participation.
risks.evidence_quote: The public expects certain privacy protections when interacting with the Bureau through social media.
risks.rationale: Expectations of privacy can be undermined if notice about collection is unclear or incomplete.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and use of PII to only what is necessary for social media engagement.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB may collect or use a limited amount of Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) when using social media to further its ability to interact with the public.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing PII reduces the amount of sensitive information exposed or stored.

mitigations.description: Apply standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls to all social media interactions and collected data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Security and privacy controls help reduce the risk created by third-party platform environments.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice to users that social media interactions may be public and may expose their information to others.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Notice helps users make informed choices about what they disclose in public channels.

mitigations.description: Use the System of Records Notice to govern any collected PII and keep it subject to the CFPB.006 records controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: this information would be covered by the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System (CFPB.006) System of Records Notice.
mitigations.rationale: A records notice establishes formal handling rules that can constrain retention and reuse.

mitigations.description: Offer opportunities for consent, access, and redress so users can understand and respond to CFPB’s handling of their information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: These participation rights help users control and correct how their information is handled.

risks.description: Public release of agency personnel names and contact details can expose individuals to unwanted contact, profiling, or other privacy harms because the dataset is openly available.
risks.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov.
risks.rationale: Open public access increases the likelihood that personally linked contact information will be reused in ways the individuals did not intend.

risks.description: The locator tool and API let users download or share the dataset in multiple formats, which can make it easier to copy, aggregate, and republish the information at scale.
risks.evidence_quote: The HUD API and the CFPB housing counselor locator tool also enables users to download or share data in the HUD counselor dataset in a variety of formats.
risks.rationale: Broader redistribution increases the chance of secondary uses beyond the original public-service purpose.

risks.description: Third-party developers or lenders can build their own applications from the API, creating downstream uses of the public data that CFPB does not control.
risks.evidence_quote: users who develop a program and incorporate the API can present the HUD data in a variety of formats.
risks.rationale: Once data leave the CFPB interface, the agency has less visibility into how they are combined or disclosed.

risks.description: ZIP codes entered by locator-tool users are collected and used for analysis, which creates a record of a user's search behavior and approximate location.
risks.evidence_quote: ZIP codes entered by users of the locator tool are collected in order to provide users with a list of HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies within a specified range of their input ZIP code. Additionally, ZIP codes entered are used to evaluate use of the tool.
risks.rationale: Even limited location data can reveal a user's area of interest and search activity.

risks.description: Consumerfinance.gov collects usage analytics such as visit timestamps, browser version, operating system, pages viewed, and time on site, which can support tracking or profiling of site visitors.
risks.evidence_quote: consumerfinance.gov collects other non‐identifying information from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool as part of normal operations supporting website functionality and security, (e.g. visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed and time on site, etc.)
risks.rationale: Operational metadata can still be sensitive when combined with other information or retained over time.

risks.description: ZIP codes and analytics are being kept as permanent records until a retention schedule is approved, increasing the period during which user activity data can be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: records collected through consumerfinance.gov (user analytics and ZIP codes entered in the locator tool) are being managed as permanent records until the disposition schedule for these records is approved by the National Archives and Records Administration
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases the cumulative risk of access, breach, or secondary use.

mitigations.description: Limit the public dataset to the minimum contact and organizational details needed for locating housing counselors, and keep the existing read-only access model.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing exposed fields reduces the amount of personal information available for unwanted contact or misuse.

mitigations.description: Keep the tool's design that always returns ten closest results and prevent record-level isolation through the locator interface.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The locator tool is programmed to always return the ten closest results, meaning users may not isolate a single record using the tool.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting query precision makes bulk extraction and targeted isolation harder.

mitigations.description: Publish clear reuse terms and developer guidance for API consumers so downstream applications handle the public data consistently and lawfully.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit guidance can reduce uncontrolled or misleading downstream reuse of the republished dataset.

mitigations.description: Collect only the ZIP code needed to return nearby counselors and avoid retaining it beyond the immediate search function unless needed for approved analytics.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ZIP codes entered by users of the locator tool are collected in order to provide users with a list of HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies within a specified range of their input ZIP code.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting collection and retention of location data lowers the privacy impact of user searches.

mitigations.description: Use only the non-identifying analytics necessary for website functionality, security, and usability evaluation, and avoid adding more detailed tracking data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: consumerfinance.gov collects other non‐identifying information from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool as part of normal operations supporting website functionality and security, (e.g. visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed and time on site, etc.) for consumerfinance.gov, and to evaluate usability of the tool.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting analytics to operational needs reduces the chance that browsing metadata becomes a tracking record.

mitigations.description: Approve and implement a NARA disposition schedule for consumerfinance.gov ZIP codes and analytics as soon as possible, then dispose of them according to that schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: records collected through consumerfinance.gov (user analytics and ZIP codes entered in the locator tool) are being managed as permanent records until the disposition schedule for these records is approved by the National Archives and Records Administration, at which time, the CFPB will dispose of such files in accordance with the schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A formal retention limit shortens exposure and aligns storage with the stated purpose.

risks.description: The system can collect directly identifying and highly sensitive information, so a data breach or misuse could expose names, contact details, financial account numbers, biometric information, or health information. Even if some datasets are later stripped of direct identifiers, the remaining data can still be sensitive and personally revealing.
risks.evidence_quote: In certain circumstances, Administrative Data collected for Market Research may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number ... Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: Sensitive and identifying data increases the harm if it is improperly accessed, disclosed, or re-identified.

risks.description: Matching records across datasets and using unique record locators can create new profiles or re-identify people from data that was not originally direct-identifying. This increases the risk that individuals become more identifiable than the source datasets intended.
risks.evidence_quote: Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets. For example, the CFPB may obtain updates or supplements to a dataset and, in those circumstances, may use record locators unique to the entity providing the update in order to update or supplement the individual records.
risks.rationale: Cross-dataset linkage can increase identifiability and expand what can be inferred about a person.

risks.description: The system uses PII to proxy population characteristics, weight samples, and generate survey frames, which can create inferred data about individuals or groups beyond the original collection purpose. Those inferences may affect how people are represented in research outputs even when the CFPB says it does not track individual habits.
risks.evidence_quote: When the CFPB collects and uses PII, it does so in order to proxy based on population characteristics; match across datasets; update data sets; weight samples; and generate frames for surveys on consumer experiences with consumer financial products and services.
risks.rationale: Using data for inference can reveal or amplify information about individuals beyond what was directly collected.

risks.description: Individuals may not receive notice from the CFPB because the data is collected from third parties, commercial sources, and public databases rather than directly from consumers. This creates a transparency risk because affected people may not know their information is being used for Market Research.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB collects Administrative Data only from third parties, commercial sources and public databases, not directly from consumers, and it is those third parties’ responsibility to determine whether notice is required and to provide any requisite notice.
risks.rationale: When notice depends on third parties, affected individuals may be unaware of collection or use.

risks.description: The system may share research results with the general public, the source of the data, and federal financial regulators, which creates a risk that supposedly aggregate outputs could still reveal information about small groups or unique cases. Even without direct identifiers, disclosure of detailed results can enable inference.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the results of Market Research with the general public, the source of the Administrative Data, and/or federal financial regulators. Any such results do not include information that directly identifies any individual.
risks.rationale: Aggregate releases can still be sensitive if they are detailed enough to permit inference about individuals.

risks.description: The CFPB may share information under applicable Privacy Act routine uses, which expands the potential for secondary disclosure beyond the core research purpose. This creates a risk that data could be used in ways not originally expected by the individuals whose information is included.
risks.evidence_quote: to the extent that information is contained in a Privacy Act system of records, the CFPB may share information as outlined in the Routine Uses of each applicable SORN.
risks.rationale: Broader sharing pathways increase the chance of secondary use and disclosure.

risks.description: The records are retained indefinitely until NARA approves a disposition schedule, which increases the chance of unnecessary long-term exposure, stale data, and future misuse. Longer retention also increases the window in which the data can be breached or repurposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Keeping data longer than necessary increases cumulative privacy and security risk.

risks.description: The system includes information about the public, consumers, federal employees, contractors, and consultants, so data from different populations may be combined in one system. Mixing these groups can create context confusion and increase the risk that information about one group is used or interpreted in another group's context.
risks.evidence_quote: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES INFORMATION ABOUT: Federal Employees Contractors Consultants The Public
risks.rationale: Combining multiple populations in one system can increase the chance of inappropriate use or disclosure across contexts.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum necessary and continue stripping direct identifiers before analysis whenever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: At times, the Bureau will analyze account-, loan-, or transaction- level data stripped of direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Removing direct identifiers reduces the likelihood that sensitive records can be tied back to a person.

mitigations.description: Use record matching only when necessary and keep matched datasets de-identified for research and analysis after linkage is complete.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de-identified copy of the matched dataset will be used for conducting research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: De-identifying the matched dataset lowers the risk that linked records remain directly attributable to individuals.

mitigations.description: Restrict use of PII-driven proxying and weighting to cases where it is necessary for the research purpose, and rely on aggregate outputs rather than individual-level outputs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Products of Market Research consist of aggregate information, such as tabulations and statistical results, that are included in internal reports, CFPB whitepapers and studies, and other policy output, and do not contain direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting analysis to aggregate outputs reduces the chance that inferences about specific people are exposed.

mitigations.description: Provide CFPB notice or public-facing collection notices where feasible, rather than relying only on third parties to decide whether notice is required.
mitigations.rationale: Direct notice improves transparency for people whose data is used even when the CFPB does not collect it directly.

mitigations.description: Review public and external research outputs to ensure they remain aggregated and cannot reasonably identify individuals before release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any such results do not include information that directly identifies any individual.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-release review helps prevent detailed outputs from enabling inference about specific people.

mitigations.description: Apply the disclosure limits in the CFPB’s confidential-information rules and applicable SORN routine uses before any external sharing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Where applicable, information is treated in accordance with the CFPB’s rules on the disclosure of confidential information, including 12 CFR 1070.41(c).
mitigations.rationale: Using established disclosure controls narrows the circumstances under which data can be shared.

mitigations.description: Approve and implement a records disposition schedule as soon as possible and dispose of records according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition reduces the period during which old records remain exposed.

mitigations.description: Continue limiting access to personnel with a need to know and separate access controls by dataset or population where feasible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only CFPB personnel with a need to know are granted access to Administrative Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the likelihood that data from one population is inappropriately used in another context.

risks.description: People in the dataset could be re-identified or singled out because the public can query, filter, and download loan-level records even though direct identifiers are removed. The dataset includes detailed loan and property information that may still be linkable to a person or household.
risks.evidence_quote: Users may be able to isolate a single record, but the record will not contain any direct identifiers.
risks.rationale: A record without direct identifiers can still be privacy-sensitive if it is unique enough to be linked back to an individual.

risks.description: Sensitive loan, property, and demographic-related information about applicants and borrowers is made public, which can expose financial circumstances and housing activity to anyone. The dataset includes application year, loan purpose and amount, action taken and denial reason, HOEPA flag, rate spread, and census tract information.
risks.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset includes loan-level information concerning applications for home loans and home loans originated or purchased for dwellings in the United States and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico during each calendar year.
risks.rationale: Publishing detailed loan-level data broadens the number of people who can learn private financial and housing information.

risks.description: Location information in the dataset can reveal where a person lives or sought credit, increasing the risk of household identification and unwanted profiling. The inclusion of census tract, county, state, and property type makes geographic inference easier.
risks.evidence_quote: Property data • Census tract, Metropolitan Statistical Area or Metropolitan Division, State, County • Property type
risks.rationale: Fine-grained geographic data can be enough to narrow a person or household to a small set of possible matches.

risks.description: Because the CFPB republishes the dataset without independently verifying its accuracy and completeness, individuals may be exposed to incorrect or misleading public information about their loan activity. Errors could affect how the public interprets a person's borrowing history or denial reasons.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB accepts the HMDA Public Use Dataset from the FFIEC as accurate and complete, and does not alter the data or independently verify the accuracy and completeness of the dataset before republishing it on consumerfinance.gov.
risks.rationale: Public dissemination of unverified data can amplify harm if the dataset contains inaccuracies.

risks.description: The dataset is available to the public, including federal and state agencies and private sector organizations, so third parties can reuse it for their own purposes without any authorization process. This broad redistribution increases the chance of secondary uses that may be adverse to the data subjects.
risks.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset will be available to the public, including federal and state agencies and private sector organizations.
risks.rationale: Once broadly available, the data can be copied and used in ways the original subjects cannot control.

risks.description: The system retains the dataset until a CFPB records schedule is approved by NARA, which may prolong exposure of public loan-level information. Longer retention increases the window for re-identification and secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB will continue to retain these records until a CFPB records schedule is approved by NARA.
risks.rationale: Keeping the data available for an extended period increases cumulative privacy risk.

risks.description: The public API enables users to retrieve the dataset for their own applications or systems, which can facilitate bulk harvesting and automated reuse of the data. That increases the scale at which individuals' loan records can be copied and analyzed.
risks.evidence_quote: The API hosted on consumerfinance.gov enables users to retrieve the Dataset and use it for their own applications or systems.
risks.rationale: An API can make large-scale collection and downstream reuse easier than manual access.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen the redaction and modification of fields before publication to reduce the chance that a single record can be linked back to a person.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information reported to regulators pursuant to HMDA and Regulation C is modified to protect loan applicant privacy and is made available to the public annually on the FFIEC’s website.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing identifying detail lowers the risk that users can isolate or re-identify a person from a record.

mitigations.description: Limit the public dataset to only the information needed for the publication purpose and avoid adding any new fields or derived data that would increase sensitivity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes. The CFPB is not collecting new information.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing the published data reduces the amount of sensitive information exposed.

mitigations.description: Keep geographic detail as coarse as possible in the published dataset and preserve the existing privacy redactions for location fields.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information reported to regulators pursuant to HMDA and Regulation C is modified to protect loan applicant privacy and is made available to the public annually on the FFIEC’s website.
mitigations.rationale: Coarser location data makes it harder to infer a specific household or applicant.

mitigations.description: Use automated and manual quality checks before republication to catch errors in the source dataset and flag known limitations to users.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and disclosure of limitations would reduce the chance that inaccurate public data harms individuals.

mitigations.description: Publish clear user notices that the dataset is public and may be reused by third parties, along with guidance on the privacy limits of the data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Both HMDA and Regulation C provide notice to the public that the data that comprises the HMDA Public Use Dataset will be made public.
mitigations.rationale: Notice helps set expectations and can reduce surprise when the data is reused broadly.

mitigations.description: Adopt a NARA-approved retention schedule as soon as possible and delete or archive the dataset according to that schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention limit reduces the period during which the public dataset remains exposed.

mitigations.description: Maintain access controls and infrastructure protections for the non-public database layer that supports the API.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data publishing API is supported by a non-publicly available database layer that is not accessible by external users. CFPB Operations staff has access to the database layer for maintenance purposes. Access to this layer is granted through the CFPB Access Control Process and in accordance with the CFPB Acceptable Use Policy.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting backend access helps prevent unauthorized access or misuse of the underlying data store.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive direct identifiers and special-category information, so a breach or misuse could expose respondents to identity theft, stigma, or other harms. The inclusion of SSNs, biometric information, and health or medical information increases the sensitivity of any disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES: Name and other biographic information (e.g. date of birth) Contact Information (address, zip code, telephone number, email address) Social Security number (“SSN”) or other identifier Financial Information User and Online Information Third Party Information Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: The broader and more sensitive the collected data, the greater the harm if it is exposed or misused.

risks.description: Matching records and combining administrative data with response data can create new, more revealing profiles about respondents. Even if the final research dataset is de-identified, the linking process itself increases the chance of re-identification or unintended inference.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases, Consumer Experience Research may involve the matching of records, such as credit score to Response Data, creating new assemblies of information about the Respondent.
risks.rationale: Linking datasets can reveal more about a person than any single source alone.

risks.description: The system may use administrative data to identify potential survey recipients and to analyze nonresponse bias, which means people can be contacted or profiled based on third-party data they did not directly provide for this research. This creates a risk of using information beyond respondents' expectations or without sufficient notice.
risks.evidence_quote: the CFPB may use Administrative Data collected from a third party to identify potential recipients of surveys, to provide auxiliary information for research, and to support nonresponse analyses.
risks.rationale: Using third-party data for targeting and analysis can affect individuals who have not directly engaged with the project.

risks.description: Some systems and contractor/vendor transfers occur outside direct CFPB integration, which increases the risk of unauthorized access or transmission errors during data movement. Although encrypted tunnels and encrypted email are used, non-automated transfers still create exposure points.
risks.evidence_quote: Any system interactions are pushed, non-automated data transfers between contractor systems and/or vendor websites and CFPB internal systems, which take place via encrypted tunnels. These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
risks.rationale: Manual or semi-manual transfers are more prone to handling mistakes and access mistakes than tightly integrated flows.

risks.description: External sharing of research products could still reveal respondents indirectly if aggregation, rounding, variable exclusion, or observation exclusion is insufficient. This is especially relevant when results are disseminated to the general public or when case studies or quotes are shared with consent.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share products of Consumer Experience Research externally, including by disseminating research results to the general public. These external products are subject to disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations, and typically do not include direct identifying PII.
risks.rationale: Even de-identified public outputs can sometimes be re-identified through residual detail.

risks.description: The system retains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves a disposition schedule, which prolongs the period during which sensitive information could be accessed, breached, or repurposed. Long retention also increases the chance that data will outlive its original necessity.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: The longer information is kept, the longer it remains exposed to privacy risk.

risks.description: The system includes populations such as lower-income and vulnerable consumers, older consumers, students, and people with health or public-benefits information, which raises the risk of disproportionate harm if data are disclosed or misused. These groups may be more affected by stigma, financial harm, or coercion.
risks.evidence_quote: Populations of particular interest include:  Current and former military members;  Students;  Working-age consumers;  Older consumers;  Lower-income and vulnerable consumers;
risks.rationale: Sensitive populations may face greater consequences from privacy incidents than the general public.

risks.description: The system may collect and use direct identifiers for follow-up, compensation, and matching, which creates a risk of function creep if identifiers are later used beyond those stated purposes. Any expansion of use would increase exposure without clear necessity for analysis.
risks.evidence_quote: Direct identifying PII is used in Consumer Experience Research, where applicable, to schedule participation in the Consumer Experience Research, conduct follow-up, provide compensation for participation, or match across data sets, as appropriate.
risks.rationale: Identifiers collected for operations can be repurposed unless use is tightly limited.

mitigations.description: Store direct identifying PII separately from research data and keep it secured with strict access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When direct identifying PII is necessary to facilitate Consumer Experience Research rather than necessary to the analysis, the direct identifying PII is stored and secured separately.
mitigations.rationale: Separating identifiers from research content reduces the chance that a compromise exposes the full dataset.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified copies of matched datasets for research and analysis after matching is complete.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de- identified copy of the matched dataset is used for conducting research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Removing direct identifiers after linkage lowers the risk that linked data can be traced back to individuals.

mitigations.description: Obtain respondent consent before collecting additional information from third parties and limit third-party data use to the stated research purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Consumer Experience Research primarily relies on information collected directly from the individual and subject to the individual’s consent for the CFPB to collect additional information from third parties
mitigations.rationale: Consent and purpose limitation help ensure third-party data use matches expectations.

mitigations.description: Continue using encrypted tunnels and encrypted email for transfers between contractor/vendor systems and CFPB systems.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any system interactions are pushed, non-automated data transfers between contractor systems and/or vendor websites and CFPB internal systems, which take place via encrypted tunnels. These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the likelihood that data intercepted in transit will be readable.

mitigations.description: Apply disclosure-protection procedures to all external outputs, including aggregation, rounding, exclusion of some variables, and exclusion of observations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These external products are subject to disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations
mitigations.rationale: These techniques reduce the chance that published results can be linked back to a person.

mitigations.description: Dispose of records according to an approved NARA records schedule as soon as the applicable schedule permits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal shortens the period during which retained records can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Apply disclosure-protection procedures and limit externally shared content so that sensitive population characteristics are not unnecessarily exposed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These external products are subject to disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations, and typically do not include direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing detail in outputs helps protect vulnerable groups from targeted or stigmatizing disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit direct identifying PII to scheduling, follow-up, compensation, and record matching, and keep it separate from analysis data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Direct identifying PII is used in Consumer Experience Research, where applicable, to schedule participation in the Consumer Experience Research, conduct follow-up, provide compensation for participation in the Consumer Experience Research, or match across data sets, as appropriate.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting identifiers to necessary operational uses reduces the chance of broader reuse.

risks.description: Individuals generally do not receive notice when their information is collected or how it will be used or disclosed, which reduces transparency and informed awareness.
risks.evidence_quote: individuals generally will not receive notice that the information is being requested and therefore how such information will be used or disclosed.
risks.rationale: A lack of notice can leave people unaware that sensitive information about them is being used for government research and enforcement-related purposes.

risks.description: The system can contain direct identifiers and sensitive information, creating a risk of unauthorized identification or re-identification if data are mishandled or linked.
risks.evidence_quote: In most cases, SEFL Data used for Market Research will not contain direct identifying PII. However, in some cases they may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number • Social Security number
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers and sensitive fields increase the harm if records are exposed or improperly matched.

risks.description: Matching records across datasets and updating datasets can create more detailed profiles about individuals than any single source contains.
risks.evidence_quote: Use of SEFL Data for Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets.
risks.rationale: Linking datasets increases the chance of combining information into a more revealing record about a person.

risks.description: The Bureau may contact potential recipients of surveys using direct identifying PII, which could expose individuals to outreach they did not expect.
risks.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does use direct identifying PII in analyses, it does so in order to a) match across datasets; b) update data sets; and c) contact potential recipients of surveys
risks.rationale: Using identifiers to contact people extends the use of their data beyond analysis and can reveal their association with consumer financial issues.

risks.description: Market Research outputs may be shared with the general public and federal financial regulators, creating a risk of disclosure if aggregation is insufficient or if context allows inference.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the products of Market Research with the general public and federal financial regulators.
risks.rationale: Even when direct identifiers are removed, published or shared results can sometimes enable inference about individuals or small groups.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely until a NARA-approved disposition schedule exists, increasing the time during which data could be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window for unauthorized access, accidental disclosure, or secondary use.

risks.description: The system includes biometric and health or medical information, which could cause heightened harm if disclosed or used beyond the intended purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: Highly sensitive data types can create greater privacy and dignity harms if exposed or analyzed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Provide direct notice to individuals whenever practicable, and otherwise make the constructive notice more prominent and specific about collection, use, and disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In cases where notice cannot be provided or is not required, the CFPB has provided constructive notice of how it may use such information through this PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Improving notice reduces the transparency gap created when people are not directly informed.

mitigations.description: Continue stripping direct identifying PII from Market Research datasets and limit access to only personnel with a need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, direct identifying PII has been stripped from SEFL Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Removing direct identifiers lowers the chance that records can be tied back to specific people.

mitigations.description: Limit record matching to cases where it is necessary for the stated research purpose and use de-identified copies after matching is complete.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de-identified copy of the matched dataset is used for conducting Market Research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting linkage and using de-identified copies reduces the amount of identifiable information retained in analysis.

mitigations.description: Use direct identifying PII for survey outreach only when necessary and minimize the data used for contact to the smallest set needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does use direct identifying PII in analyses, it does so in order to a) match across datasets; b) update data sets; and c) contact potential recipients of surveys
mitigations.rationale: Limiting identifier use for outreach reduces unnecessary exposure of personal contact information.

mitigations.description: Release only aggregate Market Research products and continue excluding direct identifying PII from public-facing outputs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Products of Market Research consist of aggregate information, such as tabulations and statistical results, that are included in internal reports, CFPB whitepapers and studies, and other policy output, and do not contain direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation lowers the chance that shared results can be tied to named individuals.

mitigations.description: Adopt and obtain approval for a records disposition schedule as soon as possible, and dispose of records according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention schedule shortens the period during which records remain exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened safeguards and stricter access controls to biometric and health or medical information, including limiting its use to cases where it is necessary for the research purpose.
