risks.description: Forensic collection from external entities may capture more information than is needed for the legal purpose, including unrelated personal data on storage media.
risks.evidence_quote: Enforcement requires the capability to forensically collect data from external entities when immediate access is granted by a court
risks.rationale: Forensic extraction can sweep in broad data sets, some of which may be irrelevant to the case.

risks.description: Trial and investigative hearing support may expose personal information to broader audiences when exhibits are displayed in court or hearings.
risks.evidence_quote: These events require the use of various specialized trial presentation software tools, which display exhibits, either during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
risks.rationale: Displaying exhibits in hearings or trial can reveal personal information to participants and observers beyond the immediate case team.

risks.description: Cloud-based or vendor-owned tools may create additional confidentiality risk because CFPB records are processed and maintained in systems not directly owned by the Bureau.
risks.evidence_quote: LTST’s application suite is comprised of these customized commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) tools and cloud-based solutions (on-premises or vendor-owned)
risks.rationale: Vendor-managed platforms can increase exposure if access controls or hosting protections are not tightly enforced.

risks.description: Contractor personnel may have access to CFPB records and personal information, creating a risk of unauthorized internal disclosure or mishandling.
risks.evidence_quote: To supplement CFPB’s eDiscovery workload, Enforcement has procured the services of a federal contractor to provide eDiscovery and litigation support services.
risks.rationale: Adding contractor support expands the number of people who can encounter sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Store and process CFPB records in a secure and forensically sound manner with access limited to authorized personnel.
mitigations.evidence_quote: eDiscovery tools allow CFPB Staff1 to forensically extract data from storage media to use as evidence in legal proceedings and to gather and store information in a secure and forensically sound manner, including electronic and non-electronic (e.g., paper) information.
mitigations.rationale: Secure, forensically sound handling reduces the risk of unauthorized access or alteration in the contractor-owned environment.

mitigations.description: Review metadata during document processing and use it to identify sensitive content before disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats
mitigations.rationale: Inspecting metadata helps identify hidden personal details that should not be disclosed.

mitigations.description: Use attorney-selected keyword searches and automated flagging to identify protected information for manual review before production.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The tool uses that information to automatically flag files that contain those keywords for the attorney, who will review and determine if the files or information therein should be protected from disclosure.
mitigations.rationale: Automated flagging plus attorney review lowers the chance that protected information is disclosed.

mitigations.description: Identify and eliminate duplicate documents during review to reduce unnecessary handling of personal information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats and identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process.
mitigations.rationale: Removing duplicates minimizes the amount of personal information processed and exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit forensic collection to data authorized by the court and use triage to narrow the material that must be reviewed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Early case assessment tools are used in conjunction with other tools to process forensically collected data to identify the types of data collected and conduct triage on a large quantity of information to determine what must be reviewed.
mitigations.rationale: Triage helps reduce the scope of data reviewed after a broad forensic collection.

mitigations.description: Use specialized trial presentation tools to control how exhibits are displayed during hearings and trial.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These events require the use of various specialized trial presentation software tools, which display exhibits, either during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled presentation tools help manage what information is shown in public or semi-public proceedings.

mitigations.description: Apply the same privacy coverage and controls to the contractor-owned and vendor-owned tools used in the LTST suite.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PIA Appendix documents the privacy risks associated with housing CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment that are not addressed explicitly by the LTST PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Extending the PIA coverage and controls to vendor-hosted systems helps reduce risks from non-Bureau infrastructure.

mitigations.description: Restrict contractor access to the minimum necessary for eDiscovery and litigation support tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To supplement CFPB’s eDiscovery workload, Enforcement has procured the services of a federal contractor to provide eDiscovery and litigation support services.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting contractor access reduces the number of people exposed to sensitive CFPB records.

risks.description: The system collects identifiable business contact information for users or points of contact, creating a privacy risk if that information is exposed or misused. Even though the beta-testing scope is limited, full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address are still personal data that can identify and contact a person.
risks.evidence_quote: Once the user or POC accesses the SBL system though Login.gov, they are directed to create the User Profile within the SBL system. This information includes full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address.
risks.rationale: Contact details are personally identifying and could harm users if accessed by unauthorized parties.

risks.description: If beta-testing data entry is not strictly constrained, the system could end up holding real applicant or associated-person information even though the stated intent is to use fake data only. That would expand the privacy impact to actual individuals whose lending data is not supposed to be collected in beta-testing.
risks.evidence_quote: for purposes of beta-testing, any information submitted beyond user or POC business contact information, including information regarding small business loan application filing, is only fake data. No information related to actual applicants or individuals associated with applicants is collected by the CFPB during beta-testing activities.
risks.rationale: The text shows a reliance on users entering only fake data, so real-person data could be introduced if controls fail.

risks.description: The program is intended to receive detailed small-business lending data from covered financial institutions, which can create privacy risk through aggregation and re-identification even when direct applicant PII is excluded. Fields such as census tract, revenue, industry code, workers, time in business, and number of principal owners can still make businesses easier to identify or profile.
risks.evidence_quote: The data that will be collected by covered financial institutions from small business credit applicants includes the type of credit being applied for; the credit purpose; and the amount applied for; census tract based on an address or location provided by the applicant; gross annual revenue for the preceding fiscal year; the 3-digit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the applicant; the number of workers that the applicant has; the applicant’s time in business; and the number of principal owners the applicant has.
risks.rationale: Detailed business attributes can still reveal sensitive information about a small business or enable re-identification.

risks.description: The system is designed to support disclosure and use of lending data by communities, governmental entities, and creditors, which creates a risk of broader secondary use than the data subjects expect. Even if the purpose is legitimate, wider access increases the chance of misuse or overexposure.
risks.evidence_quote: enabling communities, governmental entities, and creditors to identify business and community development needs and opportunities of women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses.
risks.rationale: More recipients and uses increase the number of parties who can see or reuse the information.

risks.description: The system relies on general privacy protections and security controls, but the input does not describe data minimization, masking, or role-based restrictions specific to this system. Without more specific controls, there is a risk of unauthorized access or overcollection beyond what beta-testing requires.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
risks.rationale: General controls may be insufficiently specific to prevent unnecessary collection or access in this use case.

risks.description: Users may not fully understand what information is collected and how it will be used, because the system depends on access through Login.gov and a profile-creation flow but the input does not describe system-specific disclosures. That creates a notice risk for people entering contact information or fake test data.
risks.evidence_quote: What opportunities do I have for participation? Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
risks.rationale: The system states that notice exists generally, but does not describe a specific disclosure tied to the data collection flow.

mitigations.description: Apply strong access controls and security protections to the user profile data, and limit use of the contact information to account administration and beta-testing support.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the stored contact data reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure or misuse.

mitigations.description: Enforce beta-testing rules that block submission of real applicant or associated-person data and require only fake data beyond user or POC business contact information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: for purposes of beta-testing, any information submitted beyond user or POC business contact information, including information regarding small business loan application filing, is only fake data.
mitigations.rationale: Preventing real-person data from entering the system avoids privacy harm to actual applicants.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum fields needed for the statutory purpose and suppress or aggregate outputs where feasible to reduce re-identification risk.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing detail in stored or shared data lowers the chance that a small business can be singled out.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to lending data to authorized recipients only and provide clear purpose limitations for any sharing with communities, governmental entities, and creditors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: enabling communities, governmental entities, and creditors to identify business and community development needs and opportunities of women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can see the data and why they can use it reduces secondary-use risk.

mitigations.description: Add system-specific privacy controls such as role-based access, logging, and periodic review of what data are collected during beta-testing.
mitigations.rationale: Specific operational controls help ensure only necessary data are collected and only authorized users can access them.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear system-specific notice at login and profile creation that explains what information is collected, why it is collected, and that beta-testing submissions beyond contact information must be fake data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps users understand the collection and avoid submitting unnecessary or real personal information.

risks.description: Uploaded covered orders and related documents may disclose more personal information than is necessary, including information about consumers, respondents, counsel, officers, or other representatives.
risks.evidence_quote: Documents uploaded to the NBR System may include the following PII on individuals (e.g., consumer, consenting party, defendant) identified or listed in documents provided to the registry (e.g., covered orders): • Full name;13 • Title; • Work address; • Email address; • Telephone number. • Any other information pertaining to the covered order (e.g., violation of consumer financial law) that may be associated with the individual.
risks.rationale: The system ingests full legal documents that can carry broader personal data than the core registration fields.

risks.description: Public publication of registry information could expose personal information to anyone viewing the public registry or website.
risks.evidence_quote: Finally, the Orders Rule allows the CFPB to publish some of the information collected from nonbanks for use by members of the public as well as other regulatory agencies.
risks.rationale: Publishing registry data expands access beyond the agency and increases the chance that personal information is broadly disclosed.

risks.description: Sharing registry information with other federal, state, tribal, and local regulators can spread personal data beyond the CFPB and create additional disclosure risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Finally, the CFPB may share information in the NBR System directly with other federal, state, tribal, and local regulators to facilitate the work of those agencies, in accordance with its existing information-sharing agreements and protocols.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the number of systems and people handling the information.

risks.description: The helpdesk feature collects names, email addresses, and issue descriptions from members of the public and nonbank users, which may reveal unnecessary personal details in support requests.
risks.evidence_quote: The information submitted also includes PII such as the full name of the individual submitting the question and an email address that the CFPB uses to reply to questions or provide assistance as appropriate.
risks.rationale: Support requests can contain sensitive context beyond the minimum needed to answer a question.

risks.description: User accounts and credentials for nonbank representatives and CFPB staff create a risk of unauthorized access if passwords or usernames are compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System maintains the following PII about the executive(s) associated with and authorized by the nonbank to submit written annual statements under the Orders Rule for covered orders: 11 44 U.S.C. § 3501 note.
risks.rationale: The system depends on account-based access and stores credentials, so compromise could expose all associated records.

risks.description: Records are currently unscheduled and considered permanent, which increases the risk that personal information will be retained longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently, there is no NARA-approved records retention schedule for NBR records. Therefore, the records are unscheduled and considered permanent in nature until NARA’s approval to disposition is obtained.
risks.rationale: Without an approved retention schedule, personal data may remain in the system indefinitely.

risks.description: The system may maintain personal information about individuals named in public orders even when they are not the direct registrant, creating a risk of secondary collection without direct participation.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System collects information on authorized representatives, attesting executives, and in documents uploaded to the system (i.e., the covered order, related public records, or other documents), individuals listed or included in the covered order, such as a consumer or respondent.
risks.rationale: People named in legal documents may have their information collected even though they are not using the registry themselves.

risks.description: Internal access by CFPB employees, contractors, and consultants could expose personal data more widely than necessary if role-based limits are not tightly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: information may only be shared with CFPB employees, contractors, or consultants when such disclosure is relevant to the performance of their assigned duties.
risks.rationale: The system relies on internal access controls, so overbroad access would increase exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Continue requiring nonbanks to redact nonpublic portions of covered orders before submission and remove any inadvertently uploaded or irrelevant documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To prevent the unnecessary disclosure of information maintained in covered orders, covered nonbanks are instructed in the Orders Rule to redact any nonpublic portions of the covered orders before submitting them to the registry.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction and removal reduce the amount of personal information collected and stored.

mitigations.description: Limit publication to non-confidential information and use a publication format designed to protect confidential information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the CFPB has sole discretion in determining whether to publish certain information maintained in the NBR System and the format of publication designed to protect confidential information in accordance with the Orders Rule.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting what is published lowers the chance of unnecessary public disclosure.

mitigations.description: Share registry information with other regulators only under existing information-sharing agreements and protocols.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the CFPB may share information in the NBR System directly with other federal, state, tribal, and local regulators to facilitate the work of those agencies, in accordance with its existing information-sharing agreements and protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled sharing helps ensure external recipients receive information only under defined conditions.

mitigations.description: Limit helpdesk collection to the minimum needed to respond and keep using secure web forms for submissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The NBR System provides a secure web form where representatives provide their full name and email address, along with a question or description of the issue that requires resolution by the CFPB.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only basic contact details and using a secure form reduces exposure in support interactions.

mitigations.description: Require multi-factor authentication for account creation and access, and maintain audit logs to verify compliance with privacy and security policies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After registering the nonbank, the system will require the representative to create a password and proceed through multi-factor authentication process for identity management purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Multi-factor authentication and audit logging reduce the risk of unauthorized account access.

mitigations.description: Obtain and implement a NARA-approved records retention schedule for NBR records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Currently, there is no NARA-approved records retention schedule for NBR records.
mitigations.rationale: An approved retention schedule would establish when records should be disposed of instead of keeping them permanently.

mitigations.description: Keep requiring the nonbank to upload only the final public covered order needed for registration and avoid collecting unrelated documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: You will need the final public covered order (Order) to complete this registration.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting uploads to the required order reduces secondary collection of information about third parties.

mitigations.description: Restrict internal disclosure to CFPB employees, contractors, or consultants whose assigned duties require access, and continue mandatory privacy training and acceptable-use obligations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: information may only be shared with CFPB employees, contractors, or consultants when such disclosure is relevant to the performance of their assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based access and training help prevent unnecessary internal exposure of personal information.

risks.description: The system can expose sensitive enforcement-matter information to too many people because it contains detailed records and reports that may include PII, confidential matter status, and legal documents.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may generate various reports from the Enforcement Matter Management System that identify enforcement matters, related entities and individuals including CFPB Staff, and different elements of the matter. The amount or type of information in these reports, including PII, varies depending on the purpose of the report. For example, some reports may include confidential information about the status of a matter.
risks.rationale: Detailed reports increase the chance that people who do not need full context could learn sensitive information.

risks.description: Sharing matter records with FTC staff creates a risk of unnecessary disclosure or editing of CFPB enforcement information across agencies.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB-FTC Matter Sharing Community module is a portal that allows authorized users at the FTC to input and edit FTC enforcement matters into a secured module within the Enforcement Matter Management System. The FTC enforcement matter records can be accessed by authorized CFPB Staff through ENForce as needed.
risks.rationale: Cross-agency access expands the number of users who can view or modify records.

risks.description: Providing information in response to FOIA requests could disclose personal or confidential enforcement information to the public.
risks.evidence_quote: Information maintained in the Enforcement Matter Management System is shared in accordance with all laws, regulations, policies, and applicable CFPB SORNs, or in response to FOIA requests.
risks.rationale: FOIA responses can create public exposure of records that contain PII or sensitive matter details.

risks.description: Sharing witness names, entity affiliations, and contact information with court reporting vendors creates a risk of disclosure to third parties outside the agency.
risks.evidence_quote: a limited amount of information collected through the ENFund application is shared with court reporting vendors, specifically witness names and entity affiliation, as well as names, addresses, and other business contact information for opposing counsel, and CFPB Staff.
risks.rationale: Third-party vendors receiving participant information may increase exposure beyond the agency.

risks.description: Reporting tax information such as TINs to the IRS creates a risk of unnecessary exposure of highly sensitive identifiers if collection or sharing is broader than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this updated PIA to document the collection and use of the TIN for transparency.
risks.rationale: Tax identifiers are highly sensitive and warrant strict minimization and handling controls.

risks.description: The system may hold personal information about people who are only indirectly involved in a matter, such as consumers, witnesses, opposing counsel, and government employees, creating a risk of collecting more data than each person expects.
risks.evidence_quote: Names and contact information of certain members of the public such as, individuals associated with a related entity (e.g., directors, officers and employees); recipients of civil investigative demands (CIDs); opposing counsel; potential witnesses; experts; relevant consumers; related federal, state, and local government employees; and judges;
risks.rationale: Collecting data on many categories of non-target individuals increases the chance of unnecessary privacy impact.

risks.description: The system may retain and link large numbers of source documents, such as complaints, tips, transcripts, correspondence, and legal filings, which can concentrate sensitive personal information in one place.
risks.evidence_quote: These documents include data, information, and documents relevant to the specific matter, such as, legal memoranda, consumer complaints, whistleblower tips, responses to CIDs, transcripts, correspondence, and legal filings.
risks.rationale: Centralizing many source documents increases the impact if access is misused or if records are over-retained.

risks.description: Internal access by multiple CFPB offices for coordination can broaden exposure of matter data beyond the primary enforcement team.
risks.evidence_quote: certain other CFPB Staff, who have a demonstrated need to know, have limited access to the ENForce application (e.g., T&I, Legal, Supervision, Markets, and Regulations).
risks.rationale: Even limited internal access increases the number of staff who can view sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Limit reports to the minimum information needed for the specific business purpose and keep confidential matter-status details restricted to users with a demonstrated need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB distributes reports derived from the system internally only to CFPB Staff with a need to know to carry out their assigned job responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know distribution reduces the chance of unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use the secured CFPB-FTC Matter Sharing Community module and restrict FTC access to authorized users only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB-FTC Matter Sharing Community module is a portal that allows authorized users at the FTC to input and edit FTC enforcement matters into a secured module within the Enforcement Matter Management System.
mitigations.rationale: A secured, authorized-only portal reduces cross-agency exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply FOIA review and redaction before release so personal and confidential matter information is withheld when permitted by law.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction and exemption review are necessary to prevent avoidable public disclosure of PII.

mitigations.description: Share only the limited participant and contact information needed for scheduling and documenting testimony with court reporting vendors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB also shares with court reporting vendors the names of witnesses, entity affiliation, and the names and contact information of opposing counsel and CFPB Staff as necessary to schedule and document testimony for investigational hearings and depositions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting vendor disclosures to scheduling needs reduces third-party exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict TIN collection and IRS reporting to cases where it is necessary for tax reporting obligations and use it only for that purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the Taxpayer Identification Number 6 the ENForce and ENFund applications, and the CFPB-FTC Matter Sharing Community module. The primary application within the system is ENForce, which includes the functionality of the previous Matter Management System.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing TIN use lowers the risk associated with handling highly sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Collect only information that is directly relevant and necessary to the enforcement matter or contract activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CFPB only collects information that is relevant and necessary to investigating potential violations of federal consumer financial law and pursuing administrative or civil enforcement actions.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces unnecessary collection about indirectly involved individuals.

mitigations.description: Use the integrated document storage system to avoid duplicating records and keep linked source documents in controlled repositories.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Enforcement Matter Management System will also be integrated with Enforcement’s document storage system to limit the duplication of records and information.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing duplication helps limit the spread and persistence of sensitive documents.

mitigations.description: Keep internal access limited to CFPB staff with a demonstrated need to know for their assigned responsibilities.
mitigations.evidence_quote: certain other CFPB Staff, who have a demonstrated need to know, have limited access to the ENForce application (e.g., T&I, Legal, Supervision, Markets, and Regulations).
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access limits the number of internal users who can see sensitive records.

risks.description: Geocoded consumer records can expose sensitive location and loan-related PII if accessed by users who do not need it for their duties.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to data that is geocoded by the GIS technology, such as HMDA data, may be granted to Bureau users who request it and have a business purpose or need to know.
risks.rationale: Because the system holds address-level and other PII, broader-than-necessary internal access could reveal sensitive consumer information.

risks.description: Sharing maps, CSVs, or outputs across teams and groups increases the chance that sensitive data will be copied or exposed beyond the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: the Enterprise instance allows for multiple-user groups where information can be shared within a team or across the Bureau.
risks.rationale: More internal sharing paths create more opportunities for accidental or inappropriate disclosure.

risks.description: Granting additional users access to private folders can expose outputs to more people than originally intended.
risks.evidence_quote: a user can request an administrator to add an additional user to a private folder for collaborative purpose.
risks.rationale: Expanding access on request can weaken least-privilege protections if not tightly reviewed.

risks.description: Publishing geospatial outputs could allow re-identification if aggregation or de-identification is insufficient for the underlying location data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB typically only publishes aggregated and de-identified information that includes GIS technology output.
risks.rationale: Geospatial data can still be identifying in small areas or narrow populations even when labeled aggregated.

risks.description: The system retains PII long enough for analysis that could increase exposure if the data are not deleted on schedule.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII is retained on the server for analysis until the final output is transmitted to permanent program-appropriate data storage on the CFPB network.
risks.rationale: Any retention window increases the time during which stored PII could be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: Staff account data and audit logs create a record of employee identity and activity that could be misused if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII collected regarding CFPB Staff is required to create user accounts, manage billing, authenticate users, provide support, and deliver specialized services. The information is also used in audit logs that may be used to verify compliance with the CFPB’s privacy and security policies.
risks.rationale: Identity and activity logs can reveal employee behavior and access patterns beyond what is needed for ordinary use.

risks.description: Contractors and employees both have access, which can broaden the insider-threat surface for sensitive consumer and staff data.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized GIS users are comprised of Bureau employees and contractors.
risks.rationale: More categories of authorized users increase the number of people who can potentially mishandle data.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access controls so staff only access the system and information necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB employs role-based access controls to ensure CFPB Staff only have access to the system and/or information necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to need-to-know users reduces the chance of unnecessary exposure of consumer PII.

mitigations.description: Restrict sharing to approved internal users and keep outputs in private folders unless a business need for broader sharing is documented.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In the desktop instance, outputs are stored in private folders on the CFPB network that are only accessible by the user and GIS administrators.
mitigations.rationale: Private storage reduces uncontrolled redistribution of sensitive outputs.

mitigations.description: Require administrator review before any additional user is added to a private folder, and limit that access to the specific collaboration need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: a user can request an administrator to add an additional user to a private folder for collaborative purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Administrative approval helps ensure access expansion is justified and narrowly scoped.

mitigations.description: Publish only aggregated and de-identified outputs and review them before release to confirm no identifying information is included.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB typically only publishes aggregated and de-identified information that includes GIS technology output.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and de-identification reduce the risk that published geospatial results identify individuals.

mitigations.description: Delete PII from the GIS server within a week after the final output has been transmitted to permanent program-appropriate data storage.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Within a week after the final output has been transmitted, the PII is deleted from the GIS server.
mitigations.rationale: Short retention limits the period during which stored PII is exposed to misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Limit staff account data and audit logs to what is necessary for authentication, support, billing, and compliance monitoring, and protect those logs with access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII collected regarding CFPB Staff is required to create user accounts, manage billing, authenticate users, provide support, and deliver specialized services. The information is also used in audit logs that may be used to verify compliance with the CFPB’s privacy and security policies.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and protecting logs reduces the privacy impact of employee account and activity records.

mitigations.description: Apply the same role-based access controls and need-to-know review to contractors as to employees before granting GIS access.
mitigations.rationale: Treating contractors as equally controlled users reduces insider-risk from the broader authorized user base.

risks.description: The database contains highly sensitive identifiers that could cause harm if disclosed or misused, including SSNs and other government identifiers tied to names and contact information. Because the system is searchable by personal identifier, a compromise could expose individuals to identity theft or unwanted tracking.
risks.evidence_quote: The Directory Database includes PII regarding employees or others associated with institutions under the CFPB’s authority, including: • Name; • Age and date of birth • Contact information such as address, email address, and phone number; • Social Security number (SSN), alien number, passport number, driver’s license or state identification number, or other unique number used to establish identity of the owner or responsible person;
risks.rationale: Combining direct identifiers with unique government numbers increases the sensitivity and impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system may collect personal information from third parties and other agencies without individuals receiving actual notice. This creates a risk that people will not know what data CFPB holds about them or how it is used.
risks.evidence_quote: In such cases, individuals may not receive actual notice that the CFPB has collected information about them.
risks.rationale: Lack of actual notice reduces transparency and makes it harder for individuals to understand or respond to collection.

risks.description: The CFPB currently gathers information from federal, state, and local sources and does not take steps to verify accuracy or completeness of such data. Inaccurate records could affect supervision, enforcement, or other decisions about the people and organizations in the database.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB presently gathers the information from federal, state, and local data sources and does not take steps to verify the accuracy or completeness of such data.
risks.rationale: Unverified data can lead to incorrect records being stored and used in official activities.

risks.description: The system may share PII externally with institutions and other state and federal agency employees, which creates a risk of broader disclosure beyond CFPB staff. Even if shared through secure channels, more recipients increase the chance of secondary misuse or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Externally, the Bureau may disclose reports to a limited group of employees at an institution being supervised and, as necessary, to other state and federal agency employees whose job functions allow them to review the information contained in such reports.
risks.rationale: Each additional external recipient expands the exposure surface for the personal information.

risks.description: The Directory Database is a central repository and other CFPB systems may connect to or derive information from it, which can spread PII across multiple internal systems. This increases the risk of overexposure or inconsistent access controls once data is reused elsewhere.
risks.evidence_quote: Other systems within the CFPB may connect to or derive information from the Directory Database to perform any of their functions, like supervision, enforcement, or consumer education and engagement.
risks.rationale: Data propagation into connected systems makes it harder to limit access to only those who need it.

risks.description: The system retains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the disposition schedule. Keeping PII longer than necessary increases the chance of future misuse, breach, or disclosure of outdated records.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase cumulative exposure to privacy and security risks.

risks.description: Because reports can include names and contact information, internal or external recipients could use the data for purposes beyond the minimum needed for their job functions if access is not tightly controlled. This creates a risk of unnecessary exposure of individuals' business and contact details.
risks.evidence_quote: For example, such reports may include a list of names and contact information for organizations under the CFPB’s supervision, or a list of registered depository institutions under the CFPB’s authority in a specific area of the country.
risks.rationale: Reports that bundle identifying details can reveal more than is needed for a particular task.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to authorized personnel only, using non-transferrable access codes and passwords, and limit access to the minimum needed for assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: As a general matter, the CFPB grants Directory Database access only to authorized personnel who have been issued non-transferrable access codes and passwords and have completed appropriate training on confidentiality and privacy.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive identifiers will be viewed or misused by unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Provide constructive notice through the PIA and the SORN, and where practicable obtain information directly from individuals so they have a better opportunity to know what is collected.
mitigations.evidence_quote: However, this PIA and the associated SORN, CFPB.007 –Directory Database, provide constructive notice of the CFPB’s information collection practices.
mitigations.rationale: Notice improves transparency even when actual notice is not feasible.

mitigations.description: Verify accuracy and completeness where practicable by contacting supervised institutions and individuals or using third-party data sources, and allow individuals to amend or correct records under the Privacy Act.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB will attempt, where practicable to verify the accuracy and completeness of such information by contacting supervised institutions and individuals or by using third party data sources. The CFPB also offers a means through the Privacy Act for individuals to amend or correct CFPB records that pertain to them.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction rights help prevent inaccurate records from being used in official activities.

mitigations.description: Share external reports only through secure channels and only when supported by appropriate data sharing agreements.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share PII from the Directory Database externally, under certain circumstances, through secure channels, such as encrypted email, with appropriate data sharing agreements in place.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transmission and formal agreements reduce the chance of unauthorized disclosure outside CFPB.

mitigations.description: Restrict connected-system access on a need-to-know basis and document any future external-facing connections in future PIA updates.
mitigations.evidence_quote: For data that is tagged for use in connected internal systems, information access is restricted based on a need-to-know basis.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know limits and documented updates help prevent unnecessary spread of personal information across systems.

mitigations.description: Dispose of records according to the applicable NARA-approved schedule once available, rather than keeping them indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Continue limiting internal distribution of reports to employees with a bona fide need and ensure external reports are appropriately protected and securely transmitted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Bureau distributes its reports internally only to employees with a bona fide need for such reports to carry out their assigned job responsibilities. Even then, CFPB employees only have access to the PII contained within these reports to the extent that they need to see it to perform their jobs. All reports distributed externally will be appropriately protected and securely transmitted.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting report access and protecting transmission reduces unnecessary disclosure of personal information.

risks.description: Users may disclose directly identifiable contact information on a public-facing site and have it exposed if they provide it knowingly or without understanding the consequences.
risks.evidence_quote: we may collect information such as your contact information
risks.rationale: Contact information is personally identifying, and the site is public-facing, so disclosure can create privacy harm if users share more than intended.

risks.description: User-submitted comments, videos, links, and images may reveal sensitive personal details or opinions beyond what the user expects.
risks.evidence_quote: input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images
risks.rationale: Free-form content can contain highly revealing information even when the system does not explicitly request it.

risks.description: The site may make some collected information public, creating a risk of broader disclosure of user-provided data.
risks.evidence_quote: you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website
risks.rationale: If users can control only part of what becomes public, there is still a risk that personal information is exposed to unintended audiences.

risks.description: The site collects demographic information and information about consumer financial products used by users and others, which could create profiling or inference risks.
risks.evidence_quote: demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used
risks.rationale: Combining demographic and financial-product information can reveal patterns about individuals or groups beyond the immediate purpose of the site.

risks.description: Website usage data and analytics may enable tracking or linkage of user activity across pages or sessions.
risks.evidence_quote: information about your use of the website
risks.rationale: Usage data can be used to infer behavior or build browsing histories even when the stated purpose is aggregate analysis.

risks.description: Data shared with Google Analytics may be disclosed to an external recipient outside the CFPB.
risks.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov
risks.rationale: Sending traffic data to a third-party analytics provider introduces an external disclosure risk.

risks.description: Consumer complaint intake routed through the site may transmit personal information into another system, increasing exposure across systems.
risks.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system
risks.rationale: Moving users into a separate intake system can expand the number of places where personal information is stored or processed.

mitigations.description: Continue limiting collection of directly identifiable PII to information users knowingly provide, and present clear notice before submission.
mitigations.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting collection to knowingly provided information reduces the chance of unexpected disclosure of contact details.

mitigations.description: Warn users not to include personal or sensitive information in comments, videos, links, or images, and provide submission guidance before posting.
mitigations.rationale: Guidance at the point of submission can reduce accidental disclosure in user-generated content.

mitigations.description: Give users a clear choice about what information is public and default to the least public setting possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website
mitigations.rationale: User control over public exposure helps prevent unintended publication of personal data.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of demographic and consumer financial product information to what is necessary for the site’s public education purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: we may collect information such as ... demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only what is necessary reduces the chance of profiling and inference from combined data.

mitigations.description: Use only aggregate web-traffic analytics and avoid retaining or using page-level identifiers longer than needed for site improvement.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov
mitigations.rationale: Aggregate analytics limit the extent to which individual browsing behavior can be tracked.

mitigations.description: Apply a data-sharing agreement and privacy controls for Google Analytics to limit use of traffic data to aggregate measurement.
mitigations.rationale: Contractual and technical limits can reduce the privacy impact of external analytics processing.

mitigations.description: Provide a privacy notice and security safeguards before users are transferred from ConsumerFinance.gov to the online complaint intake system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system
mitigations.rationale: Notice and safeguards at the handoff reduce surprise and limit exposure when data moves to another system.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive identifiers and personal details, increasing the harm if the data is exposed or misused. This includes Social Security Numbers, health records, driver’s license numbers, home addresses, and personal credit card information.
risks.evidence_quote: The following PII information is collected when a user registers for GSAFleet.gov:  First and Last Name  Email address  Telephone number  IP Address  Social Security Numbers ... The following PII information ... include: ... Health records ... Driver’s License Number ... Personal credit card information
risks.rationale: Collecting sensitive identifiers and health/financial data raises the privacy impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Third-party accident data is collected from people who may not be able to meaningfully control the collection, and the system says an accident case cannot be entered if they refuse. This creates a privacy risk because individuals may be compelled to provide personal information through a police report.
risks.evidence_quote: The third party individual is required to provide the PII information need to complete the case/claim. ... If the third party individual refuses to provide such information, an accident case cannot be entered in GSAFleet.Gov.
risks.rationale: When participation is effectively required, individuals have limited ability to avoid collection of their personal information.

risks.description: Accident and sales PII are shared with external federal systems and private-sector services, creating disclosure risk during transmission or processing. The system sends data to OCFO, FMESB, EDMS, and Experian.
risks.evidence_quote: a file of requisite data is transmitted to OCFO ... The PII information is transmitted ... to Financial Management Enterprise Services Bus (FMESB) ... Social security numbers are transmitted to Experian to determine a user's credit worthiness to purchase a vehicle
risks.rationale: Each external transfer expands the number of systems and parties that can access or mishandle the information.

risks.description: The system aggregates new data about individuals, which can create more detailed profiles than any single source alone. This increases the privacy impact of misuse or unauthorized access because accident, insurance, and sales information can be combined.
risks.evidence_quote: 3.2: Will the system, application, or project create or aggregate new data about the individual? Yes
risks.rationale: Aggregation makes it easier to infer additional facts about a person beyond the original collection purpose.

risks.description: Accident-related documents are moved through multiple channels and formats, including email, fax conversion, web service calls, and storage in EDMS, which increases the chance of interception or mishandling. The system also relies on attachments and uploads rather than keeping all records in one controlled store.
risks.evidence_quote: The Police report and SF91 are sent electronically (i.e., as attachments) to the Accident Management Center's (AMC) inbox. Documents faxed from the police station are converted to digital format and emailed to the AMC account. The AMC uploads the Police Report and SF91 ... the system does not store these documents or associated data locally.
risks.rationale: More handoffs and formats create more opportunities for accidental disclosure or unauthorized access.

risks.description: Only authorized users can access transferred accident records in EDMS, but the system still stores sensitive files there, so any access-control failure could expose third-party PII. The risk is heightened because the files include home addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, and insurance details.
risks.evidence_quote: Once transferred to the EDMS server, the information is only accessible by authorized users.
risks.rationale: Sensitive records remain exposed if authorization, account security, or permissions are compromised.

risks.description: User and employee transactions are logged, which can reveal detailed activity patterns about GSA employees or contractors. Audit logs themselves become a privacy-sensitive record if retained or accessed beyond need.
risks.evidence_quote: GSA employees or contractors with the ability to log into system transactions are logged via the audit logs.
risks.rationale: Audit logs can expose who did what and when, so they need protection like other sensitive records.

risks.description: The system depends on user-provided or police-report-provided information for accuracy, and some updates are made by users with appropriate permission. Incorrect or incomplete data could lead to wrongful collection, disclosure, or decisions affecting individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: It is the responsibility of the individual or the police report that provides this information ... The system users with appropriate permission can update the information through an online screen in the application to fix any erroneous data reported.
risks.rationale: If source data is wrong, the system may store and share inaccurate personal information.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum data needed for each transaction and keep the Privacy Act Statement before collection. Where possible, avoid collecting especially sensitive fields unless they are required for the specific accident or sales purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. §552a (e) (3) GSA provides what is commonly referred to as a Privacy Act Statement to all persons asked to provide personal information about themselves, which will go into a system of records.
mitigations.rationale: Notifying individuals and minimizing collection reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice explaining why third-party accident information is required and allow access/amendment through the Accident Management Center. If feasible, collect only the fields needed for the claim and recovery process.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The individuals or the third party involved in the accident can reach the GSA Fleet Accident Management Center to access/amend their PII information.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice and access rights help reduce the privacy burden on individuals whose data is required for a claim.

mitigations.description: Maintain formal agreements and secure transfer controls for every external recipient, including OCFO, FMESB, EDMS, and Experian, and ensure encryption is used for all transmissions. Review recipient access to confirm they receive only the data needed for their role.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is AES-256 encrypted with a private key updated annually when transmitted to Financial Management Enterprise Services Bus (FMESB), which then decrypts the data on their end.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and formal sharing controls lower the risk of exposure during inter-system transfers.

mitigations.description: Apply purpose limitation and separate accident, sales, and account data so combined profiles are not broader than necessary. Review any new data aggregation before deployment to confirm it is justified by the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 3.2: Will the system, application, or project create or aggregate new data about the individual? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Controlling aggregation limits the creation of unnecessary composite records.

mitigations.description: Reduce email and fax handling of accident documents where possible and route submissions through controlled secure workflows instead. Preserve encryption in transit for all document transfers, including uploads to EDMS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All PII files are sent securely to EDMS and stored in the EDM Server encrypted. Once transferred to the EDMS server, the information is only accessible by authorized users.
mitigations.rationale: Fewer ad hoc transfer methods reduce the chance of interception or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access in EDMS and periodically review who can access accident files. Monitor access to sensitive records so unauthorized access can be detected and investigated quickly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Once transferred to the EDMS server, the information is only accessible by authorized users.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized viewing.

mitigations.description: Protect audit logs as sensitive records, limit who can view them, and retain them only as long as needed for security and accountability. Review log access periodically to ensure logs are not used for unrelated monitoring.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GSA employees or contractors with the ability to log into system transactions are logged via the audit logs.
mitigations.rationale: Audit logs can themselves reveal personal activity and should be controlled accordingly.

mitigations.description: Use verification and correction procedures before sharing or acting on accident or sales data, especially when the source is a police report or winning bidder. Continue allowing users with appropriate permission to correct erroneous data and document the basis for changes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system users with appropriate permission can update the information through an online screen in the application to fix any erroneous data reported.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction help prevent inaccurate personal data from being stored or disclosed.

risks.description: The system may expose highly sensitive identifiers and financial information if case files are accessed improperly or compromised. It can contain SSNs, claim numbers, military serial numbers, and bank routing and account numbers tied to individual inquiries.
risks.evidence_quote: That may include additional personally identifiable information (PII) information, Social Security Number (SSN), annuitant claim numbers, compensation claim numbers, insurance account numbers, insurance claim numbers, military serial numbers, birth date, financial institution routing number, and financial institution account number.
risks.rationale: This creates a high-impact privacy risk because a single case file can contain data that enables identity theft or financial fraud.

risks.description: The system links all inquiries submitted by or on behalf of the same constituent, which can reveal a broader profile of a person's interactions and issues over time. This aggregation increases the privacy impact of any single access or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also links together all the inquiries submitted by or on behalf of the same constituent.
risks.rationale: Linking multiple cases makes it easier to infer sensitive patterns about a person beyond the immediate inquiry.

risks.description: Communications and documents stored in the case system may include non-public records and additional PII about the constituent and others, increasing the chance of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive third-party information. The system stores letters, emails, attachments, and other records connected to the inquiry.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also stores all communications and documents connected to the inquiry. This may include letters, emails, and attachments between OPM and the staffer, constitution, or other parties that may have information to help answer the inquiry (e.g., other federal agencies). This may also include legal, administrative, or similar non-public agency records relevant to the inquiry. These communications and documents can include additional PII about the respondent, constituent, and others.
risks.rationale: Storing broad case correspondence and attachments increases the amount of sensitive information exposed if the system is misused or breached.

risks.description: The portal allows external congressional staffers to submit inquiries and documents, so improper account approval or compromised accounts could expose case information to unauthorized users. Staffer accounts are approved by OLA CS staff, but the portal is still an external entry point for sensitive data.
risks.evidence_quote: CS Portal is a secure web interface where congressional staffers can submit the inquiries and other messages to the Office of Personnel Management.
risks.rationale: Any externally accessible submission channel creates a risk of unauthorized access if identity proofing or account controls fail.

risks.description: Using cloud services to process and store case data may increase exposure if cloud configurations, vendor access, or service vulnerabilities are not tightly controlled. The system uses Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.evidence_quote: The new system uses a cloud-version of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems can broaden the attack surface and require strong configuration and access management to protect sensitive records.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal data than necessary for a given inquiry because it can include broad categories of information from staffers and other parties. The description shows that the case file can accumulate many different types of identifiers and records beyond the initial request.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking creates a new case file for each inquiry. It tracks the receipt and processing of the inquiry, records connected to the inquiry, relevant inquiry and any records gathered to help respond).
risks.rationale: Collecting and retaining broad case materials increases privacy risk unless data collection is limited to what is needed.

risks.description: The system stores contact information for staffers, congresspersons, and OLA CS representatives, which could expose personal and professional contact details if accessed improperly. Those details are maintained for each inquiry and associated case file.
risks.evidence_quote: For each inquiry, the OLA Tracker maintains contact information for the staffer, their congressperson, and the OLA CS representative.
risks.rationale: Routine contact data can still create privacy harm if it is disclosed or misused in a case-management environment.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive case fields such as SSNs and financial account numbers to only staff who need them, and protect those fields with strong authentication and role-based permissions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to the most sensitive identifiers reduces the chance of identity theft or financial misuse.

mitigations.description: Limit or compartmentalize cross-case linking so staff can see only the minimum history needed to respond to the current inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary linkage lowers the risk of building an overly detailed profile of a constituent.

mitigations.description: Apply strict document handling rules, including access controls and redaction where feasible, for letters, emails, attachments, and other non-public records stored with the case.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting stored correspondence and attachments helps prevent disclosure of sensitive third-party and agency information.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing identity verification and approval process for portal accounts, and periodically review approved accounts for continued need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and approval help prevent unauthorized users from submitting or viewing case information.

mitigations.description: Maintain tight cloud security controls, including least-privilege access, secure configuration, and monitoring of the Microsoft cloud services used by the system.
mitigations.rationale: Cloud-hosted records require strong configuration and access management to reduce exposure from misconfiguration or compromise.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and retention to records needed to respond to the inquiry and create reports, and discard unnecessary supporting material once it is no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and retention limits reduce the amount of personal information at risk in the case system.

mitigations.description: Protect stored contact information with role-based access controls and only disclose it to personnel involved in handling the inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to contact details reduces the chance of improper disclosure or misuse.

risks.description: ROVR collects and retains sensitive health and enrollment information about many people, creating a risk of privacy harm if the repository is accessed or handled improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program
risks.rationale: The system stores PII about a large population tied to health benefits, so misuse or exposure would affect many individuals.

risks.description: The system aggregates detailed medical, pharmacy, encounter, provider, and rebate data, which increases the risk that individuals could be identified or their health status inferred from analytics.
risks.evidence_quote: service use and cost data” includes, but is not limited to, medical claims data, pharmacy claims data, encounter data, and provider data.
risks.rationale: Combining multiple detailed data types makes re-identification and sensitive inference more likely.

risks.description: ROVR creates person-level longitudinal records, which increases the risk of tracking individuals over time and linking their coverage history across plans.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records. Longitudinal records are necessary because individuals may change plans over the years while remaining in the FEHB Program.
risks.rationale: Linking record-level data over time expands the privacy impact beyond any single claim or enrollment event.

risks.description: Data from multiple internal systems and external agencies may be combined in ways that create broader exposure or inconsistent handling across sources.
risks.evidence_quote: These systems include the FEHB Data Hub ... the Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) warehouse ... and the Centralized Enrollment Reconciliation Privacy Impact Assessment Research and Oversight Repository (ROVR) OPM Form 5003 other Federal agencies through data sharing agreements.
risks.rationale: The more systems and agencies that feed the repository, the greater the chance of mismatched protections or excessive linkage.

risks.description: Enrollment data may reveal dual enrollments or other coverage irregularities, creating a risk of adverse impact if the data are used beyond authorized administrative purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: enrollment data may reveal instances where an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract.
risks.rationale: Coverage anomalies are sensitive and could affect benefits if not handled carefully.

risks.description: The system is used to detect fraud, waste, and abuse and may be used when OPM suspects or has confirmed such conduct, which creates a risk of intrusive scrutiny or mistaken suspicion about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
risks.rationale: Fraud analytics can incorrectly flag legitimate behavior or lead to heightened review of individuals.

risks.description: Service use and cost data are analyzed across population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions, which creates a risk of re-identification in small or unusual groups.
risks.evidence_quote: These analyses may include examination of the cost of care, utilization of services, and comparing these across specific population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions.
risks.rationale: Comparisons across narrow slices of data can make individuals easier to infer.

risks.description: CMS and Medicare-linked data introduce a risk that health information about dual-enrolled individuals will be combined across programs and disclosed more broadly than expected.
risks.evidence_quote: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) provides service use and cost data3 to OPM, including health claims information for FEHB enrollees and their eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare programs.
risks.rationale: Cross-program linkage increases the sensitivity of the dataset and the consequences of any disclosure.

risks.description: The system states that no disclosure will be made outside OPM unless permitted under the Privacy Act, but external disclosures still pose a risk if the legal limits or agreements are not followed.
risks.evidence_quote: No disclosure of information in ROVR related to service use and cost data will be made outside of OPM unless permitted under the Privacy Act.
risks.rationale: Even limited external disclosure can create privacy harm if controls are not strictly enforced.

mitigations.description: Limit access to ROVR to authorized OPM HI personnel who need the data for administration, oversight, and analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: to assist the Office of Personnel Management’s (OPM) Healthcare and Insurance office (HI) to oversee, manage, and analyze the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program and the Postal Service Health Benefits (PSHB) Program by being a repository for enrollee data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to need-to-know users reduces the chance of improper handling of sensitive PII.

mitigations.description: Use non-identifiable data for analyses whenever possible and reserve identifiable data only for the limited longitudinal linking that is necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data, OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing identifiable use lowers the risk of re-identification and unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply strict controls to person-level longitudinal records, including limiting their use to the stated analysis purpose and avoiding use for decisions about specific individuals except where fraud, waste, or abuse is suspected or confirmed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred
mitigations.rationale: Constraining individual-level use reduces the privacy impact of longitudinal tracking.

mitigations.description: Use the data-sharing agreements to enforce consistent use, storage, and retention rules across all contributing systems and agencies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agreements constitute the methods of use and applicable retention and storage protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent contractual controls help prevent mismatched handling across sources.

mitigations.description: Handle dual-enrollment findings outside ROVR except where analysis is needed, and use the repository only as part of the analysis rather than as the sole basis for enrollment action.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, such an occurrence would be identified and addressed outside of ROVR, but data from ROVR may be used as part of the analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Separating analysis from action reduces the risk of inappropriate or premature adverse effects on coverage.

mitigations.description: Limit fraud, waste, and abuse review to cases where OPM suspects or has confirmed such conduct, and avoid using the data for unrelated individual-level decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred with respect to services rendered or payments made in connection with the FEHB Program.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing investigative use helps prevent unnecessary scrutiny of innocent individuals.

mitigations.description: Suppress or aggregate outputs for small population slices, narrow geographies, or rare disease conditions before reporting results.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation reduces the chance that analysis across small groups will identify a person.

mitigations.description: Restrict Medicare-linked data to the specific reconciliation, statistical analysis, and coverage-administration purposes described in the PIA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OPM uses this data in its administration of the FEHB Program, including examining patterns of service use, statistical analyses of service use, risk and cost for dual FEHB and Medicare enrollees, and the relationship between FEHB and Medicare coverage more generally.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the risk that cross-program health data will be reused more broadly.

mitigations.description: Enforce Privacy Act disclosure limits and review any external release against the applicable legal authority before sharing data outside OPM.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No disclosure of information in ROVR related to service use and cost data will be made outside of OPM unless permitted under the Privacy Act.
mitigations.rationale: Checking disclosures against the Privacy Act helps prevent unauthorized external sharing.

risks.description: The system stores and uses highly sensitive identifiers, including SSNs, which increases the harm if the records are exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: their name, their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).
risks.rationale: SSNs and debt data are sensitive because disclosure can enable identity theft and financial harm.

risks.description: Broad access across many USDA agencies and authorized users creates a risk of unnecessary internal disclosure of debtor information.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users of approximately 35 USDA agencies have access to this data.
risks.rationale: More users and organizations with access increases the chance of misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: External sharing with Treasury systems and a records contractor creates a risk that personal data could be disclosed beyond USDA or handled by third parties with insufficient protection.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO provides data to the following:  Department of Treasury – Treasury Offset Program  Department of Treasury – Intra Governmental Payment and Collection System  Iron Mountain - Digital Records Center for Images System
risks.rationale: Each external recipient expands the attack surface and the number of entities that can access the records.

risks.description: Transmission of data over networked interfaces and file transfers creates a risk of interception or unauthorized access during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via connect direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection.
risks.rationale: Any system that moves personal data across networks can be exposed if transport controls fail or are misused.

risks.description: Contractors converting payroll reports into PDF files and transmitting them to Iron Mountain create a risk of mishandling or exposure during manual processing.
risks.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
risks.rationale: Manual handling by contractors adds opportunities for copying, loss, or unauthorized viewing.

risks.description: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data, which creates a risk that they cannot review or correct inaccurate debt records affecting them.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Without direct access, affected people may be unable to identify or challenge errors in their records.

risks.description: The system’s reliance on agency-provided data and automated updates creates a risk that inaccurate or outdated information will be used for billing and collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Federal agencies and employees can provide data for use in the system.
risks.rationale: If source data are wrong or stale, the system may generate incorrect debt notices or collection actions.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of mainframe data creates a risk of keeping personal information longer than necessary, increasing exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window for unauthorized access, secondary use, or breach impact.

mitigations.description: Limit use of SSNs to the minimum necessary and substitute non-SSN identifiers wherever possible in reports and operational workflows.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN exposure lowers the harm if records are accessed improperly.
