mitigations.description: Continue enforcing least privilege and need-to-know access reviews for all agency users, with periodic revalidation of access rights.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least Privacy Impact Assessment Administrative Billings and Collections System (ABCO) Page 7 privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to only necessary users reduces the chance of internal misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use written data-sharing agreements and contractor controls that limit external recipients to authorized purposes and require equivalent safeguarding of the records.
mitigations.rationale: Clear obligations and limits help ensure external recipients handle the data only as intended.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong transport protections for all file transfers, including VPN, secure FTP, and encryption in transit, and monitor transfers for anomalies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via connect direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transmission security reduces the likelihood that data will be intercepted or altered in transit.

mitigations.description: Apply strict contractor access controls, handling procedures, and auditing for any manual file conversion or transmission tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter controls on contractor workflows reduce the chance of mishandling during manual processing.

mitigations.description: Provide an individual access and correction process for debt records, even if the system itself remains agency-user only.
mitigations.rationale: A review and correction path helps affected people challenge inaccurate records that may impact them.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen validation, reconciliation, and error-checking routines, including periodic data quality reviews against source systems.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ABCO application code provides reconciliation routines at the application level. These are maintained on the mainframe and applied to data entered and data transferred there. As personnel actions and payroll documents are processed each pay period, updated data replaces existing data elements on the ABCO database. Extensive error-checking routines are built into applications including edits of data received, record counts and database status checking.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and reconciliation reduce the chance that incorrect data will drive billing or collection actions.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition rules to the mainframe data so that only records required by the approved schedule are retained, rather than retaining all data indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA General Records Schedule GRS-1-1 (Financial Management and Reporting Records). ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time and lowers long-term risk.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal information than is necessary because correspondence can include extra details voluntarily provided by the sender beyond basic contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: In a few cases, it may also include other information about the individual voluntarily provided by that individual in the correspondence.
risks.rationale: Voluntary correspondence can contain unnecessary personal details that increase exposure if they are stored and processed.

risks.description: The system may expose correspondence PII to multiple internal users and groups as packages are reviewed and moved through workflows.
risks.evidence_quote: tracking the movement of the packages between different users and user groups.
risks.rationale: Each additional user or group that handles a package increases the number of people who can view the PII.

risks.description: The system may use personal information for secondary analytical purposes, including NLP and machine learning, beyond the original correspondence request.
risks.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
risks.rationale: Analytical reuse of correspondence content can expand access and processing of personal data beyond the immediate response need.

risks.description: Search results, dashboards, and reports may reveal sensitive correspondence details or status information to users who do not need the full underlying content.
risks.evidence_quote: To analyze data, Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used. Search data produced could pertain to correspondence as they progress through workflows within the system (e.g., stage/status agency, priority or categorization, time in a particular status, time to progress from initiated to completed, congressional inquiries, etc.).
risks.rationale: Aggregated workflow outputs can still disclose personal or case-specific information if broadly accessible.

risks.description: Maintaining physical and email addresses and phone numbers creates a risk of unnecessary retention of contact information after the correspondence purpose is complete.
risks.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes. Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Keeping contact details in a centralized CMS can prolong exposure if they are not minimized or removed when no longer needed.

mitigations.description: Limit intake and storage to only the personal information needed to process the correspondence, and redact or exclude extraneous voluntary details before they are stored.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is stored directly reduces the amount of unnecessary PII in the system.

mitigations.description: Enforce the stated role-based access controls so only users and user groups with a business need can view each package record.
mitigations.evidence_quote: supporting standardized processes and role-based access.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to need-to-know users lowers the chance of internal overexposure.

mitigations.description: Limit NLP and machine-learning use to approved correspondence-processing functions and apply data minimization to the historical content used for search and classification.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining analytical reuse helps prevent broader processing of correspondence PII than is necessary.

mitigations.description: Restrict dashboards and reports to authorized staff and suppress or aggregate identifiers and case details where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To analyze data, Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting detail in reporting reduces the chance that status or content information is exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Apply retention limits and delete contact information when it is no longer needed for correspondence processing or follow-up.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the time contact information remains vulnerable in the system.

risks.description: Sensitive discrimination complaint records could be exposed through unauthorized access because the system is web-based and connected to the public Internet.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway
risks.rationale: Internet connectivity increases the attack surface for records that include complainant identities and complaint details.

risks.description: Contractor access could lead to unnecessary disclosure or misuse of complaint PII because contractors have access and the system is co-located with a contractor.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES is co-located at MicroPact Engineering, Inc. MicroPact Engineering provides system, network, development, and administrative security under contract with The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
risks.rationale: A contractor operating the environment and having access to the system creates a privacy risk if access is broader than needed.

risks.description: Approved user access may still be too broad because management determines user levels and the description does not state role-based limits or least-privilege controls.
risks.evidence_quote: The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES.
risks.rationale: If access levels are not tightly constrained, users may see more complaint information than necessary for their duties.

risks.description: Complaint PII may be exposed during collection because it is received through multiple channels such as mail, email, telephone, and interviews.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake channels increase the chance of interception, misdelivery, or overhearing before the data is entered into the system.

risks.description: The system may retain complaint records longer than necessary if destruction is only described as occurring based on judicial regulations without a specific retention schedule in the PIA.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES’s files are destroyed, based on the judicial’ s regulations.
risks.rationale: Unclear retention limits can result in keeping sensitive complaint data longer than needed.

mitigations.description: Restrict Internet-exposed access with strong network security controls, including hardened gateways, firewalls, and continuous monitoring of web access to CRES.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
mitigations.rationale: Network protections are necessary because the system is reachable through the public Internet.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary, require background screening and confidentiality obligations, and audit contractor actions in the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote:
Privacy Impact Assessment OASCR, CRES Page 10

10.8 Who will have access to PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications? Only designated/approved users have access to the system Privacy Impact Assessment OASCR, CRES Page 12
mitigations.rationale: Contractor access should be tightly controlled because contractors can access the environment and approved users handle sensitive PII.

mitigations.description: Implement role-based, least-privilege access controls with periodic review of user permissions and immediate removal of unnecessary access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based limits reduce the chance that users can view complaint data beyond what they need.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for mail, email, phone, and interview submissions, such as verified recipient addresses, secure email handling, and privacy scripts for interviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews.
mitigations.rationale: Secure intake reduces the risk of exposing complainant information before it is entered into CRES.

mitigations.description: Publish and follow a specific records retention and destruction schedule approved by records officials and NARA, with documented destruction procedures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The OASCR Records Manager and Department Records Manager have developed the goals and timelines for reporting and adhering to records management requirements issued by the National Archive Records and Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Office of Personnel Management.
mitigations.rationale: A clear approved retention schedule helps ensure complaint records are not kept longer than necessary.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal information than is needed because PII is not required and users can voluntarily provide it, including free-text personal details. This increases the chance of unnecessary exposure of sensitive or identifying information.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
risks.rationale: Voluntary collection of unnecessary personal data creates avoidable privacy exposure.

risks.description: The unrestricted “About Me” field can capture arbitrary personal information, which may include highly identifying or sensitive details not needed for the system's purposes. This creates a risk of oversharing and inconsistent handling of user-entered content.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: An unrestricted free-text field can collect more personal information than intended.

risks.description: User profile photos combined with names create an identifiable image record that could be exposed unnecessarily. Because photos are optional and not required, their collection expands the amount of personal data held without being essential to operation.
risks.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: Photos increase identifiability and therefore increase disclosure risk.

risks.description: The system stores address information and miscellaneous identification numbers such as parking permit and building permit numbers, which can link individuals to specific facilities and services. If disclosed, these identifiers could reveal where a person works or their access status.
risks.evidence_quote: - Address information - Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
risks.rationale: Location- and permit-linked identifiers can expose operational and personal associations.

risks.description: Personal information is shared internally through Tableau dashboards and reports across multiple administrative domains, which broadens access beyond the original collection purpose. This raises the risk of overexposure to personnel who do not need individual-level data.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Broad internal sharing increases the number of people and systems that can see the data.

risks.description: Data is transferred to the USDA Data Lake and then shared through dashboards, creating a larger aggregation point where personal information may be combined with other administrative data. Aggregation can increase the privacy impact of any access or disclosure event.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
risks.rationale: Centralized aggregation increases the consequences of unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: Authorized Department contractors can access the system, which introduces the risk of insider misuse or excessive access if permissions are broader than necessary. Even with clearance, contractors may see personal information not needed for their tasks.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the population that can view personal information.

risks.description: The system uses personal information to maintain access control lists, so identity data may be used to grant or manage access to system resources. If access control records are inaccurate or overly permissive, users could receive inappropriate access or be misidentified.
risks.evidence_quote: It is also used to maintain the integrity of the system through ACLs (Access Control Lists).
risks.rationale: Identity-based access control depends on accurate and limited personal data.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection by making all nonessential personal fields optional and limiting them to what is needed for parking permits, limousine dispatch, or access control.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
mitigations.rationale: If PII is not required, limiting collection reduces unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict the “About Me” field with validation, content guidance, or removal of free-text entry so users cannot enter unnecessary personal details.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining free-text input reduces the chance of collecting unnecessary personal information.

mitigations.description: Keep profile photos optional and do not require them for account creation or system use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo
mitigations.rationale: Optional collection limits the number of identifiable images stored in the system.

mitigations.description: Limit use of address and permit numbers to the specific operational purpose for which they are collected and avoid exposing them in reports unless necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected to issue parking permits to various personnel, and to identify individuals making requests within the OSCAR application and managing the data within OSCAR.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the chance that identifiers are reused or disclosed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and data minimization to Tableau dashboards so senior leadership only sees the least amount of personal information needed for decision-making.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting dashboard detail reduces broad internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified or aggregated data in the USDA Data Lake and dashboards whenever individual-level data is not necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation or de-identification lowers the privacy impact of centralized sharing.

mitigations.description: Maintain strict authorization and security-clearance checks for contractors and review their access regularly to ensure it remains limited to what they need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps keep contractor access narrowly scoped.

mitigations.description: Review and validate access control list data regularly to ensure personal information used for identity and authorization remains accurate and current.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It is also used to maintain the integrity of the system through ACLs (Access Control Lists).
mitigations.rationale: Accurate access-control data helps prevent inappropriate access decisions.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains a broad set of personally identifiable information, including identity, employment, location, photo, and emergency-response-related data, which increases the impact of any misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS generally handles physical access Security Management Information including: x Physical access card status x Physical access card category x Physical access card expiration date x Physical access card holder emergency response responsibilities
risks.rationale: The more sensitive and varied the stored data, the greater the privacy harm if it is improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Visitor data is collected for background checking and meeting access, which can create privacy concerns if visitors do not expect their information to be used beyond entry control.
risks.evidence_quote: The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
risks.rationale: Background checking uses personal data in a way that can be more intrusive than simple visitor registration.

risks.description: The system receives data from multiple sources, including HR databases and manual card-issuance collection, which can increase the risk of inaccurate or outdated information being stored and used for access decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: The non-authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and multiple upstream sources increase the chance of errors that can affect individuals' access and records.

risks.description: The system uses an integrated background checker for visitors, which may expose visitor information to additional screening processes and third-party or external data sources.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS will use an integrated background checker for visitor to USDA NCR HQs.
risks.rationale: Background screening can expand the privacy footprint beyond the original access-control purpose.

risks.description: Internal sharing of credential-read activity and employee status can reveal movement patterns and employment status to personnel who do not need full individual-level access.
risks.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity and the Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
risks.rationale: Even limited internal sharing can still expose sensitive behavioral or employment information.

risks.description: Limited ePACS data is transmitted daily to EDAPT and to the Credit Card Service Center, creating additional disclosure points and increasing the risk of unauthorized access during transfer or downstream use.
risks.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily.
risks.rationale: Each additional transfer and recipient increases the number of places where personal data can be exposed.

risks.description: Use of Tableau dashboards and daily reports can broaden access to credential-read activity and employee status beyond the original access-control context.
risks.evidence_quote: Once in the EDAPT, the data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards with summary PIV card access for executive management.
risks.rationale: Reporting tools can make personal data easier to view and redistribute to a wider audience.

risks.description: The system allows access for USDA employees and select contractors, which creates insider-risk exposure to personal data held in ePACS.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: More people with access means more opportunities for misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: Retention of live and archived records for 5.5 years can keep personal data available longer than necessary for some access-control purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which data can be breached, misused, or repurposed.

risks.description: Rare external sharing of PII, even if approved, creates a disclosure risk because the system contemplates sending information outside USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: If information contained in ePACS is shared outside of USDA it is consistent with applicable laws and policy.
risks.rationale: Any external disclosure of PII creates additional privacy risk beyond internal USDA controls.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and maintenance to the minimum data elements needed for physical access control and avoid storing unnecessary fields.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information exposed if the system is misused or breached.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice to visitors about background checking and limit visitor data use to the stated access-control purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and purpose limitation reduce surprise and overuse of visitor information.

mitigations.description: Validate and periodically reconcile manually collected issuance data against authoritative sources before it is used for access decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The authoritative data elements provided to ePACS are provided by USDA’s ICAM Shared Services identity management system.
mitigations.rationale: Checking manual entries against authoritative data helps prevent inaccurate records from affecting access.

mitigations.description: Restrict visitor background checking to the minimum necessary screening and document what data the checker may use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ePACS will use an integrated background checker for visitor to USDA NCR HQs.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting screening scope reduces unnecessary exposure of visitor information.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing need-to-know access and restrict dashboards and reports to aggregated or role-based views only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based access and aggregation reduce the chance that internal users learn more than necessary.

mitigations.description: Keep secure transmission controls for all daily transfers and verify that downstream recipients apply equivalent access controls and handling rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and downstream controls reduce exposure during movement and processing.

mitigations.description: Limit dashboard content to summary information and suppress unnecessary identifiers in reporting tools.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity
mitigations.rationale: Summary-only reporting lowers the risk of tracking individuals' movements or status.

mitigations.description: Maintain background checks and security clearances for contractors and review contractor access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Screening and periodic review help reduce insider misuse of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved retention schedule and delete or archive records as soon as they are no longer needed for access control.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes
mitigations.rationale: Enforcing retention limits reduces the time personal data remains exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Require approval from the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel before any external disclosure and keep all outbound data encrypted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: any data from ePACS before release to an external organization must be approved by the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and encryption help ensure external disclosures are limited and protected.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information about USDA employees, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of employee travel and identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: This PIA is being created for the front-end, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) instance of SAP Concur CCPS. Based on the Privacy Threshold Assessment submitted in December 2023, this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees, and therefore, a PIA is necessary.
risks.rationale: Any system that collects PII can expose employees to privacy harm if that information is improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Travel profile preferences are retained and analyzed to create predictive patterns, which could reveal personal behavior or preferences beyond what is needed for travel transactions.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Retained preference data can support profiling and expose sensitive behavioral patterns about individual travelers.

risks.description: Authorization and voucher data are shared enterprise-wide and sent to FMMI, increasing the risk that travel-related personal data is exposed to more systems and users than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Broader sharing expands the number of places where personal data can be accessed, copied, or mishandled.

risks.description: Authorized USDA agency users can access the system the same way as internal users, so there is a risk of overbroad access if restrictive roles are not properly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users. Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
risks.rationale: If role restrictions are misconfigured or too permissive, users may see travel data they do not need.

risks.description: Data is transmitted over multiple network components and to external cloud services, creating a risk of interception or session compromise during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer. The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall. Web connections are secured using TLS
risks.rationale: The presence of multiple transmission paths and external infrastructure increases exposure if any control fails.

risks.description: User information is retained under records schedules and bill-related data for at least six full years, which may keep personal data available longer than some users expect.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the time window for unauthorized access, secondary use, or breach impact.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and access to only the PII needed for travel reservation, booking, authorization, and payment/voucher processing, and apply privacy review to any additional data fields.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected data reduces the harm if employee PII is exposed.

mitigations.description: Provide a way for travelers to review, edit, and clear stored preferences, and limit predictive use of profile data to travel-booking functions.
mitigations.rationale: Giving users control over retained preferences reduces unnecessary profiling and stale personal data.

mitigations.description: Continue using audit checks before transmitting authorization and voucher data, and restrict the shared fields to only what FMMI needs for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Audit checks and data minimization reduce the amount of personal information shared beyond the system.

mitigations.description: Enforce restrictive roles and periodically review them to confirm authorized USDA agency users only see the data required for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Role review helps ensure access stays aligned with job responsibilities.

mitigations.description: Maintain encrypted transmission and session protections such as TLS 1.2, multifactor authentication, VPN, NACLs, DNSSEC, Site Shield, and web application firewall controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer. The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall. Web connections are secured using TLS
mitigations.rationale: These controls lower the likelihood that data in transit or sessions will be intercepted or hijacked.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA and USDA retention schedule consistently and purge records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal limits how long personal data remains exposed to access or breach risk.

risks.description: The system collects and holds personally identifiable travel and payment information about USDA employees, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure if access is broader than needed for travel processing.
risks.evidence_quote: this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees
risks.rationale: PII in a travel and expense system can reveal sensitive movement and financial details if improperly accessed.

risks.description: Enterprise-wide access increases the chance that users who do not need a particular record could view employee travel and voucher data.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide.
risks.rationale: Broader user populations increase the risk of overbroad access to personal data.

risks.description: Sharing authorization and voucher data with FMMI creates a risk that personal travel and financial information will be disclosed outside the originating system.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Each transmission to another system expands the exposure surface for personal information.

risks.description: Traveler preferences are retained and analyzed to predict preferred airlines, seats, rental car companies, and hotels, which creates a risk of profiling or reuse of behavioral data beyond the original booking purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Persistent preference data can reveal habits and choices that users may not expect to be profiled over time.

risks.description: Long retention of user and bill-related data increases the risk that personal information remains available longer than necessary and may be exposed in a future incident.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: The longer personal data is kept, the longer it can be misused or compromised.

risks.description: Use of mobile applications and web access creates a risk of interception or session compromise if transport or session protections fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: Remote access paths are common points for unauthorized interception or account takeover.

mitigations.description: Limit access to PII to only the minimum roles needed to perform travel, authorization, and voucher functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Role restriction directly reduces unnecessary exposure of employee PII.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing least-privilege role assignments and periodically review who has enterprise access to ensure only authorized users can see records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps prevent role creep in an enterprise-wide system.

mitigations.description: Protect data sent to FMMI with encrypted transmission and audit checks before transfer.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation. Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and encryption reduce the risk of unauthorized disclosure or corrupted transfers.

mitigations.description: Allow travelers to control whether preference data is retained and used for predictive suggestions, and minimize the preference fields kept for future reference.
mitigations.rationale: User control and data minimization reduce the privacy impact of profiling and repeated use of preference data.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA/GRS retention schedule and delete records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Retention limits reduce how long personal information remains exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Maintain secure remote access protections such as MFA, TLS, VPN, and session-authenticity controls for browser and mobile access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall. Web connections are secured using TLS
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport and session protections lower the chance of interception or account compromise during remote access.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, creating a risk of identity theft or financial harm if the data is misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly usable to impersonate a person or access financial accounts.

risks.description: The system contains delinquent debt and accounts receivable information, which could expose individuals to stigma or unnecessary disclosure of financial distress.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and payment information about accounts receivable (Document Tracking System) (DOTS), informational display system of delinquent debts to Treasury (Salary Offset Agency Process (SOAP)
risks.rationale: Debt-related records can reveal sensitive information about a person's financial status.

risks.description: The system records and reports personnel and payroll data for USDA and other federal agencies, increasing the risk that data is used or shared beyond the minimum necessary purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Broader reporting and interagency use can expand exposure of personal information.

risks.description: The system retains the data for a long period, increasing the chance that outdated personal information remains available and can be misused over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which stored data can be accessed, breached, or used improperly.

risks.description: The system includes batch job processing details, which could reveal operational information about processing schedules and system activity if disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: batch jobs processing details (Scheduling Information Tracking System);
risks.rationale: Operational metadata can help an attacker or unauthorized user understand when and how sensitive processing occurs.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the SSNs, bank account numbers, and check data to authorized personnel only and encrypt these fields at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting the most sensitive fields reduces the chance of identity theft and financial misuse.

mitigations.description: Limit disclosure of delinquent debt information to only the staff and systems that need it for debt collection and related processing.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing access reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive financial distress information.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and role-based access controls so only the minimum personnel and payroll information needed for each reporting purpose is shared.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is shared and who can see it reduces over-disclosure across agencies.

mitigations.description: Review records during the 10-year retention period and delete or archive data as soon as the approved schedule allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal data exposed to future misuse.

mitigations.description: Protect batch job processing details through logging controls and restricted administrative access.
mitigations.rationale: Operational details should be limited to reduce the risk of revealing system activity patterns.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive case records, including audio files and personally identifiable information, which creates risk if the data is improperly accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack system handles case- related data, audio files and determinations as well as participant and agency contact and/or identifier information is tracked and recorded.
risks.rationale: A system holding audio files and PII presents a meaningful privacy risk because unauthorized access could reveal detailed case and identity information.

risks.description: Public eFilers can view appeal transaction details and submitted documents, which may expose more personal information than necessary to the appellant's account holder or anyone with access to that account.
risks.evidence_quote: the public who eFile appeal requests. ... an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted. At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
risks.rationale: A self-service portal that exposes residence and contact information increases the risk of unauthorized disclosure through account compromise or overbroad visibility.

risks.description: Authorized USDA employees and contractor employees can access the system, which creates insider and contractor-access privacy risk if access is misused or exceeds a need to know.
risks.evidence_quote: These authorized users are USDA employees, contractor employees who access the system via eAuthentication, and the public who eFile appeal requests.
risks.rationale: Broad authorized access expands the number of people who can see appellant data and increases the chance of inappropriate viewing or misuse.

risks.description: Reports generated from the system may contain PII and could be exposed to management or others if handled improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
risks.rationale: Report generation creates a secondary disclosure channel for personal data, especially if reports are distributed or stored insecurely.

risks.description: The system retains information in perpetuity, which increases the risk of long-term unnecessary exposure, secondary use, or breach impact over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps personal data available far longer than the active case may require, increasing cumulative privacy risk.

risks.description: The system includes contact and residence information that can be used to identify or locate appellants, creating risk of unwanted disclosure of sensitive location data.
risks.evidence_quote: At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
risks.rationale: Residence and contact details are directly identifying and can reveal where and how a person may be reached.

mitigations.description: Limit access to case records and audio files to users with a documented need to know and enforce strong audit logging and periodic review of access.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the chance that sensitive case materials are viewed or copied without authorization.

mitigations.description: Minimize what the eFile portal displays to appellants and mask residence or contact details unless they are necessary for the current transaction.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing visible data limits exposure if an account is accessed by someone other than the appellant.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions for USDA employees and contractor employees, with access granted only through eAuthentication.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
mitigations.rationale: Tighter role-based permissions reduce the number of users who can see appellant data and lower insider-risk exposure.

mitigations.description: Continue to flag reports containing PII and require secure handling, limited distribution, and retention controls for those reports.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All reports with PII display a PII warning.
mitigations.rationale: PII warnings help remind users that reports contain personal data and should be handled carefully.

mitigations.description: Establish a records retention schedule and delete or archive data when it is no longer needed for case tracking and reporting.
mitigations.rationale: A finite retention period reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time and limits the impact of future incidents.

mitigations.description: Protect residence and contact information with field-level access restrictions or redaction where those details are not necessary for the user's task.
mitigations.rationale: Extra protection for direct identifiers helps prevent unnecessary disclosure of an appellant's location and contact details.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive direct identifiers and payroll-related records, so a breach could expose employees to identity theft or financial/privacy harm. The presence of SSNs increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data needed to conform to all applicable laws, Government regulations and procedures, and the needs of the Department and agencies in carrying out their personnel management responsibilities.
risks.rationale: SSNs and payroll data are high-impact personal data if improperly disclosed.

risks.description: Multiple groups can enter or handle data on behalf of individuals, which creates a risk of inaccurate or unnecessary disclosure if someone enters the wrong information or accesses data beyond what they need. This is especially sensitive because HR staff may act for an individual and agencies control access.
risks.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf. Agencies may submit and receive data via Connect Direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection. Only individuals with an established "need-to-know" may access their specific profiled data.
risks.rationale: Delegated entry and profile-based access can lead to mistaken or overbroad handling of personal information.

risks.description: Authorized agency personnel can run predefined and custom reports, which can expose more personal information than needed if report access is not tightly controlled. Reports may aggregate time, attendance, and payroll details in ways that increase privacy impact.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
risks.rationale: Reporting features often broaden exposure beyond routine transactional access.

risks.description: The system shares customer data with other USDA applications and external agency processes, creating a risk that personal data will be disclosed more widely than intended. Each customer agency determines the use and sharing of the information, so privacy protections may vary by agency.
risks.evidence_quote: NFC shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below. 1. EmpowHR: WebTA uses human resources data provided by EmpowHR. 2. Insight: WebTA generates files for transmission to the Insight hosting environment for processing. 3. OCIO eAuthentication (eAuth) application: The eAuthentication application provides authentication services for some WebTA customers. 4. TIME: WebTA transmits certified T&A data to the PPS TIME application.
risks.rationale: Inter-system sharing increases the number of places where personal data can be exposed or mishandled.

risks.description: Data is transmitted through several channels, including file transfers and web access, so interception or misconfiguration could expose personal information in transit. Even though secure methods are described, any failure in those controls would affect sensitive employee records.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
risks.rationale: Transmitting sensitive records across networks creates exposure if encryption or VPN protections fail.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system, which creates a risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse if contractor roles are too broad or not well monitored. Contractor access expands the set of people who can reach employee records.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases the number of potential insiders.

risks.description: The retention schedule allows records to be kept for varying periods under agency requirements, which could leave personal data available longer than necessary for some users or purposes. Longer retention increases the window for misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule. Civilian Personnel Records have various retention periods for specific types of data. These retention periods are adhered to per customer agency requirements and memorandum of understanding.
risks.rationale: Keeping personal data longer increases exposure over time.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs to the minimum necessary and protect them with strong access controls and secure storage.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only individuals with an established "need-to-know" may access their specific profiled data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to sensitive identifiers reduces the impact of any compromise.

mitigations.description: Require validation and supervisory review for HR-entered or delegated entries, and keep access limited to the minimum profile needed for each role.
mitigations.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf. Only individuals with an established "need-to-know" may access their specific profiled data.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing delegated edits and limiting profile access helps prevent erroneous or excessive disclosure.

mitigations.description: Restrict custom and predefined report access to authorized users and apply least privilege to reporting permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege reduces the amount of personal data a user can retrieve through reports.

mitigations.description: Use formal sharing agreements and routine-use/SORN controls for each data exchange, and limit each recipient system to the minimum data needed for its function.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, the sharing of PII outside the Department is compatible with the original collection and covered by a SORN. Please see Section 5.1 above.
mitigations.rationale: Documented legal and purpose limits help constrain secondary use and sharing.

mitigations.description: Continue to require secure transmission methods such as SFTP over VPN and HTTPS for all data exchanges, including any transmission to external systems.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agencies submit and receive data via Connect: Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Encrypted, authenticated transmission reduces the chance of interception in transit.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based authorization and periodic access review for contractors so contractor accounts remain limited to approved duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review of contractor roles helps ensure access does not exceed business need.

mitigations.description: Enforce the approved records schedule and purge records when retention periods expire.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Record Control Schedule N1-016-10-7 has been approved.
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved schedule limits unnecessary long-term retention of personal data.

risks.description: PII may be exposed when it is sent by email to subject matter experts for escalated inquiries, since email is a less controlled disclosure channel than the core case system. This could reveal names, contact details, and inquiry details to the wrong recipient if misaddressed or forwarded.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: Email transmission increases the chance of accidental disclosure of sensitive contact and case information.

risks.description: PII may be exposed through the Cisco telephony integration because contact data moves between the contact center and the call center environment. If the integration is misconfigured or accessed inappropriately, call-related personal data could be disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: An integrated telephony path expands the number of systems handling personal data and therefore the exposure surface.

risks.description: Authorized USDA users and contractors may have broader access to PII than is necessary for their role, creating insider-access risk. The system includes role-based access control, but the data is available to all USDA users with valid credentials in the environment.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS).
risks.rationale: Even with access controls, broad internal availability can lead to unnecessary viewing or misuse of personal data.

risks.description: PII may be retained longer than necessary because no current purging or archiving process is set up for the third-party application data. Extended retention increases the amount of personal information at risk over time.
risks.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival, since this is a pilot this will would be reassess after the pilot phase to get a better idea of data storage required.
risks.rationale: Holding personal data longer than needed increases the impact of any future misuse or breach.

risks.description: The system collects direct identifiers and case details that can be combined to profile a person’s inquiries and interactions with USDA. This creates a risk of overexposure if case history is accessed beyond the immediate service need.
risks.evidence_quote: General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
risks.rationale: Case histories linked to contact information can reveal more about a person than simple contact data alone.

risks.description: Users may be identifiable through the combination of name, address, and phone number stored in Salesforce, which increases the sensitivity of the contact records. If those fields are exposed together, the records can directly identify and locate individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: PII data will be captured within Salesforce of the combination of Name, Address and Phone number information of contacts within the Salesforce Government Cloud Application.
risks.rationale: Combining multiple identifiers makes re-identification and targeted misuse easier.

mitigations.description: Use secure case-management sharing methods instead of ordinary email for transmitting PII to SME contacts, or encrypt and restrict any email containing personal data.
mitigations.rationale: A more controlled transfer method reduces the chance of accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit Cisco telephony integration access to only the minimum necessary users and monitor integration activity for unauthorized disclosure or unusual access.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access and monitoring reduce the risk created by the telephony data path.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role assignments through EEMS and review access requests regularly so contractors and internal users only retain access needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS).
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access limits unnecessary viewing of personal information.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic purging or archiving rules before the seven-year minimum retention period ends, and reassess retention needs after the pilot phase.
mitigations.rationale: Scheduled disposal reduces the volume of retained personal data and the duration of exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to inquiry case history to staff who need it to resolve the specific case, and avoid using case content for unrelated purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Customer information is used for submitting and resolving customer inquiries into the AskUSDA Contact Center and how USDA can better serve customer in the future.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting use to the stated purpose reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive inquiry details.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of contact fields to only what is needed for the inquiry and provide clear notice about why name, address, and phone number are collected.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less identifying information lowers the harm if records are accessed improperly.

risks.description: The system enables broad surveillance of employees, contractors, visitors, and passersby in and around USDA facilities, which can intrude on privacy even when people are only entering, leaving, or traversing the buildings.
risks.evidence_quote: the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
risks.rationale: Capturing people’s movements around federal facilities creates a privacy risk because it records their presence and behavior without limiting collection to suspects.

risks.description: The system can identify individuals through facial images, license plates, and other captured details, creating a risk of re-identification and tracking across time and locations.
risks.evidence_quote: The VSS cameras may capture facial images of employees and visitors to USDA buildings and images of license plates that are parked or driving through the parking lot.
risks.rationale: The footage includes direct and indirect identifiers that can be used to single out specific people or vehicles.

risks.description: Some cameras capture driver’s license information and other textual details, which increases the sensitivity of the collected footage beyond ordinary video surveillance.
risks.evidence_quote: The video footage includes images of people, information found on drivers licenses such as full names, addresses, date of birth, as well as license plate numbers.
risks.rationale: Recording identity document details creates a higher risk of exposing personal information if the footage is viewed, exported, or disclosed.

risks.description: Manual and automatic tracking and zooming can intensify surveillance of particular individuals, increasing the risk of excessive monitoring of people in crowded or public areas.
risks.evidence_quote: Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
risks.rationale: Targeted tracking can reveal detailed movement patterns and associations that are not necessary for general security monitoring.

risks.description: Video footage may be retained longer than the stated six-month period, which increases the risk that personal data will be kept longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
risks.rationale: Longer retention expands the window in which footage can be accessed, reused, or disclosed.

risks.description: Footage retrieved for suspected criminal activity can be kept until investigative or enforcement action is completed, which may create open-ended retention for some records.
risks.evidence_quote: Records which are retrieved pursuant to suspected criminal activity will be retained until any investigative or enforcement action is completed.
risks.rationale: Indefinite or case-based retention can preserve personal data far beyond routine operational needs.

risks.description: Video footage may be shared outside USDA with federal agencies and local law enforcement, creating a risk of secondary disclosure and use beyond the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: Information from the VSS cameras will be used by federal agencies and local law enforcement to detect and respond to potentially unlawful activities in the areas surrounding federal facilities.
risks.rationale: External sharing increases the number of parties that can access the footage and raises the risk of broader dissemination.

risks.description: Internal sharing for criminal investigations and disciplinary actions can expose employees and others to use of their footage in employment-related decisions beyond security monitoring.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions.
risks.rationale: Using surveillance footage in disciplinary matters creates a privacy risk because the data can affect individuals beyond the original security purpose.

risks.description: Contractors and select non-employees can access the system, which creates a risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse by non-government personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond USDA employees increases the number of people who can see sensitive footage.

mitigations.description: Limit camera placement and viewing practices to security-relevant areas and avoid locations with a reasonable expectation of privacy.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Cameras are not placed in places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as inside a bathroom or changing room.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting camera placement reduces unnecessary surveillance of private activities.

mitigations.description: Restrict use of the footage to security and investigative purposes and limit identification attempts to cases where they are necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: USDA uses the VSS’s video feeds captured through cameras to aid in crime prevention and criminal investigations, enhance officer safety, secure physical access, promote cost savings, and assist in terrorism investigation or terrorism prevention.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting identification to defined security purposes reduces the chance of routine tracking or profiling.

mitigations.description: Minimize capture and export of footage that contains driver’s license details and other textual identifiers unless needed for a specific investigation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The video footage includes images of people, information found on drivers licenses such as full names, addresses, date of birth, as well as license plate numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention and dissemination of highly identifying details lowers the risk of unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Require supervisory approval or documented justification before using manual or automatic tracking on a specific individual.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
mitigations.rationale: Approval controls help ensure tracking is used only when justified and not for excessive monitoring.

mitigations.description: Enforce the six-month deletion schedule consistently and document any exceptions when storage constraints cause longer retention.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The intent is a 6-month retention period for all video footage, however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent deletion limits how long routine footage remains available for misuse or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Require a supervisor to approve any extended retention and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To retain the footage after the retention period, a supervisor must approve the request and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and relevance checks reduce unnecessary long-term retention of footage tied to investigations.

mitigations.description: Share footage outside USDA only in response to formal requests tied to criminal investigations or disciplinary actions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with external organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions
mitigations.rationale: Limiting external disclosure to formal requests reduces unnecessary secondary use of the footage.

mitigations.description: Limit internal disclosure to formal requests and use the footage only for the stated investigative or disciplinary purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-bound internal sharing helps prevent broader employment-related use of the footage.

mitigations.description: Allow access only to personnel with appropriate background checks and security clearances.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Screening access holders reduces the likelihood that unauthorized or unsuitable personnel can view the footage.

risks.description: The system may collect more personally identifiable information than is needed for ordinary feedback, increasing the chance that customers are identified when they only intended to submit comments. The presence of name, email address, and zip code in free-form comment boxes creates avoidable privacy exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; and • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Collecting direct identifiers raises the sensitivity of otherwise routine feedback and increases the chance of unintended identification.

risks.description: The system may re-identify individuals or link feedback to their associated PII when a customer requests follow-up, which can reveal identity alongside opinions or complaints. This creates a risk that sensitive feedback becomes attributable to a named person.
risks.evidence_quote: Data will never be inquired or manipulated to identify individuals or their associated PII unless a customer specifically asks to be contacted by a USDA official for a follow-up conversation.
risks.rationale: Linking feedback to a person makes the content more sensitive because it can be tied back to an identifiable individual.

risks.description: Broad internal sharing of dashboard reports across USDA leadership and program offices may expose customer sentiment to more people than necessary, even if the dashboards omit direct PII. Aggregated feedback can still be sensitive when combined with context or small populations.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
risks.rationale: Internal aggregation reduces but does not eliminate privacy risk because sensitive feedback can still be inferable in small or specific segments.

risks.description: A small number of users having access to all data across all mission areas creates a concentration-of-access risk, because those users could see a large volume of feedback and any associated PII. This increases the impact of misuse or unauthorized curiosity access.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: The broader the access concentration, the greater the potential harm if one account is misused or compromised.

risks.description: Contractor access to the system introduces an additional privacy risk because non-federal personnel may handle customer feedback and any associated identifiers. If contractor access is not tightly controlled, the likelihood of improper disclosure increases.
risks.evidence_quote: 8.2 Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond federal employees increases the number of people who can see or handle the data.

risks.description: Migrating data from other USDA tools into one cohesive VoC product can combine records from multiple sources and create a more complete profile of a customer. This consolidation increases the risk of secondary use or broader inference about a person’s interactions with USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: In addition to launching the VoC tool, appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
risks.rationale: Combining datasets can increase identifiability and the amount of information associated with one person.

risks.description: Collecting feedback through multiple channels, including social media and unstructured comments, can capture unexpected personal details that were not intended for the system. This raises the risk of overcollection and disclosure of sensitive information in free-text fields.
risks.evidence_quote: This feedback will be collected in real-time across a customer’s journey and will be placed in the VoC tool. The data is structured or unstructured, solicited, or unsolicited feedback from customers through multiple channels, including but not limited to surveys, web forms, email, contact centers, in-person visits, and social media.
risks.rationale: Unstructured and unsolicited inputs are more likely to contain incidental personal data than tightly constrained forms.

risks.description: The retention period has not been approved by the component records officer and NARA, which creates a governance risk that records may be kept longer than necessary or disposed of inconsistently. Unclear retention approval can prolong exposure of identifiable feedback.
risks.evidence_quote: 3.2 Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Without approved retention governance, the system may retain personal data longer than intended or required.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of direct identifiers by making name, email address, and zip code optional and collecting them only when needed for a specific follow-up purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing collection of direct identifiers lowers the amount of personally identifiable information in the system.

mitigations.description: Keep feedback separated from identity data by default and only link a submission to a person when the customer explicitly requests contact, with strict controls on that linkage.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data will never be inquired or manipulated to identify individuals or their associated PII unless a customer specifically asks to be contacted by a USDA official for a follow-up conversation.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting identity linkage to explicit follow-up requests reduces unnecessary attribution of feedback to individuals.

mitigations.description: Limit dashboard access to the smallest set of USDA staff needed for their duties and suppress or further aggregate small-cell data before sharing reports internally.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Smaller access sets and additional aggregation reduce the chance that sensitive feedback can be traced to a person or small group.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls, periodic access reviews, and heightened logging for users who can access all mission-area data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All appropriate security and accessibility measures will be implemented to limit, and control access based on user’s roles and permission levels.
