mitigations.rationale: Tighter controls and monitoring reduce the risk associated with concentrated access.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be limited to mission need, trained, and reviewed just like employee access, with explicit authorization before access is granted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users of the VoC platform will be selected based on their mission need to access the system and their permission levels. Approved USDA employees will undergo in-person training on platform functionality, privacy, and security controls.
mitigations.rationale: Applying the same need-to-know and training controls to contractors lowers the chance of improper handling.

mitigations.description: Before migrating data from legacy tools, conduct a data mapping and minimization review so only necessary records and fields move into the new VoC environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In addition to launching the VoC tool, appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting migrated data prevents unnecessary consolidation of personal information.

mitigations.description: Use form design and input filtering to discourage or remove incidental personal details from unstructured feedback channels, especially free-text fields and social media intake.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is structured or unstructured, solicited, or unsolicited feedback from customers through multiple channels, including but not limited to surveys, web forms, email, contact centers, in-person visits, and social media.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining free-text collection reduces the chance that unnecessary personal details are captured.

mitigations.description: Obtain formal retention approval from the component records officer and NARA and document the approved schedule before continuing long-term storage.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained for varying periods of time, and temporary records are disposed of by deleting when the retention period is complete.
mitigations.rationale: Approved retention rules help ensure personal data is not kept longer than necessary.

risks.description: The system requires mandatory PII for account creation, which increases the amount of identifiable information collected even when users cannot decline to provide it.
risks.evidence_quote: First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Mandatory collection of identifiable account data creates privacy exposure because users cannot limit what is collected to use the system.

risks.description: Storing USDA email addresses and other account data in a third-party cloud service outside the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary creates exposure to cloud-hosting and boundary-control risks.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Hosting PII outside the agency boundary can increase the chance of unauthorized access or loss of direct agency control.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, which broadens the set of people who may see account information and document content.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of authorized users and therefore the risk of inappropriate viewing or handling of personal data.

risks.description: The system retains information for 75 months, which prolongs the period during which account data remains exposed to misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the time window in which retained PII can be accessed improperly or compromised.

risks.description: The system is used to create and publish reports that are meant to be publicly accessible, so there is a risk that identifiable information could be exposed if public-facing content is not properly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data.
risks.rationale: If public-access publishing is misconfigured or overly broad, data subjects could be exposed beyond what is necessary.

risks.description: Access is based on identity records, elevation, and supervisor approval, which creates a risk of inappropriate access if approvals are overly broad or not sufficiently reviewed.
risks.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
risks.rationale: Approval-based access can lead to excessive privileges if decisions are not tightly controlled.

mitigations.description: Minimize account data collection by limiting mandatory fields to the smallest set needed for provisioning and using non-PII identifiers where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing required PII lowers the privacy impact of account creation.

mitigations.description: Maintain the system's controlled collaboration, granular permissions, and full audit trail to restrict access and support accountability in the cloud environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Workiva wDesk is a software as a service (Saas) cloud solution, offering controlled collaboration, data integration, granular permissions and a full audit trail.
mitigations.rationale: Granular permissions and audit logging help limit and detect unauthorized access in a hosted cloud service.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary and review contractor permissions regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting contractor access reduces the number of people who can see account data and documents.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule and delete or archive records as soon as the retention requirement allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are retained in accordance with NARA policies (OMB/NARA M-12-18).
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved retention schedule limits how long PII remains available for misuse.

mitigations.description: Use publication review and access controls to ensure only information intended for public release is placed in the report.
mitigations.rationale: Review before publication helps prevent unintended disclosure in publicly accessible content.

mitigations.description: Require documented approval criteria and periodic access recertification for supervisor-granted and higher-level access.
mitigations.rationale: Recertification and clear approval standards help prevent excessive or stale access rights.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, so a breach or misuse could expose applicants, grantees, vendors, and personnel to identity theft or financial harm.
risks.evidence_quote: This information may include the vendor’s name, address, email IDs, and SSN/TIN.
risks.rationale: SSN/TIN and similar identifiers materially increase the harm if the records are improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Grant files can be shared with internal and external parties, creating a risk of over-disclosure beyond what is needed for the grants process.
risks.evidence_quote: It may also be shared with external parties at the discretion of the Grants Director.
risks.rationale: Discretionary sharing increases the chance that personal data will be disclosed more broadly than necessary.

risks.description: PII may be transmitted in common document formats or hard copy, which raises the risk of interception, forwarding, or accidental exposure during disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
risks.rationale: Document-based sharing is easier to mishandle than tightly controlled system-to-system exchange.

risks.description: External sharing with review panelists and other recipients could expose applicant PII if access controls or redaction are insufficient.
risks.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII is limited to review panelists involved in the grants process. Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications. Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
risks.rationale: The need to redact and encrypt indicates a residual disclosure risk when information leaves the system.

risks.description: Contractors have operational access to the system, which creates insider and third-party access risk if their privileges are excessive or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the number of people who can view or handle sensitive records.

risks.description: The system ingests data from external sources and connected systems, so inaccurate or mismatched personal data could be used in decisions or records without the subject's knowledge.
risks.evidence_quote: The data sources for FMAT include the following: (1) vendor data from FMMI; collection extract from Treasury’s Collections Information Repository (CIR) system; and check images from Treasury’s Electronic Check Processing (ECP) system.
risks.rationale: Multiple source systems increase the chance that incorrect data will be propagated into official records.

risks.description: Manual entry by approved users can introduce unauthorized, excessive, or erroneous personal data into official files.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally information entered by approved FNS FM-GSS users are maintained in the GSS.
risks.rationale: Human entry into official records can create privacy harm if users add data that should not be collected or retained.

risks.description: The system retains personal information for long periods, increasing the impact of any later breach or unnecessary continued storage.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window during which records can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit access to SSN/TIN and other sensitive fields to only the roles that need them, and keep the existing encryption for those fields in transit and at rest.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications. Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction and encryption reduce the chance that highly sensitive identifiers are exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Require documented approval and a minimum-necessary review before any external disclosure of grant data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Transmissions/disclosures typically require approval by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Approval gating helps prevent unnecessary or excessive sharing.

mitigations.description: Use secure, controlled electronic transfer methods instead of ad hoc Excel, Word, PDF, or hard-copy disclosure whenever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing document-based sharing lowers the risk of interception and accidental exposure.

mitigations.description: Continue to redact EIN/TIN and encrypt other PII before sharing with review panelists, and limit sharing to panelists involved in the grants process.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII is limited to review panelists involved in the grants process. Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications. Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting recipients and protecting the data before disclosure directly reduces exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role-based access and review contractor access regularly so contractors only have the access needed for their assigned support tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting contractor privileges lowers insider and third-party access risk.

mitigations.description: Validate and reconcile data received from FMMI, CIR, ECP, and Grants.gov before it is used in official records or decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data sources for FMAT include the following: (1) vendor data from FMMI; collection extract from Treasury’s Collections Information Repository (CIR) system; and check images from Treasury’s Electronic Check Processing (ECP) system.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps prevent incorrect external data from being propagated into sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Restrict manual entry to approved users and apply review or audit checks for user-entered changes to official files.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Additionally information entered by approved FNS FM-GSS users are maintained in the GSS.
mitigations.rationale: Controls on manual entry reduce the chance of inappropriate or inaccurate personal data being added.

mitigations.description: Enforce the stated retention schedule and archive or dispose of records when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting how long records remain active reduces the exposure window for sensitive data.

risks.description: The database aggregates highly sensitive SNAP participant information from all states into one place, creating a large concentration of personal, transactional, and financial data that would be valuable if improperly accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: SNAP participant data (including personal information and transactional data) from all 53 SNAP state agencies via their Electronic Beneﬁt Transfer (EBT) payment processors, through secure channels, to be stored in a database
risks.rationale: Centralizing sensitive data increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.

risks.description: Collecting data from 2000 to present may retain far more information than is necessary for current integrity checks, increasing privacy exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Long lookback periods expand the amount of historical personal data held and exposed to review.

risks.description: Automated matching and scripts can generate false positives, which could wrongly flag participants as ineligible, duplicate, or fraudulent and lead to improper adverse action or investigation.
risks.evidence_quote: Integrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database, using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
risks.rationale: Automated identity and eligibility matching can misclassify people when records are incomplete or inconsistent.

risks.description: Sharing information with state agencies for investigations can disclose sensitive eligibility and immigration-related information beyond the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: sharing, where permitted by law and consistent with this notice, information with State agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify fraudulent or otherwise improper or illegal SNAP enrollments or transactions.
risks.rationale: Interagency disclosure increases the number of entities that receive sensitive participant data.

risks.description: The system performs immigration status checks, which can expose highly sensitive information about participants and their household members if handled or matched incorrectly.
risks.evidence_quote: performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies. ... • Immigration status check;
risks.rationale: Immigration-related information is especially sensitive and can cause harm if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: Household composition and age validation can reveal intimate family information and create privacy harm if the data are inaccurate or shared more broadly than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: • Age and household composition validation;
risks.rationale: Family structure and household details are sensitive personal information in a benefits context.

risks.description: Using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across multiple federal agencies creates a risk that data collected for one purpose will be reused for other purposes without clear limits.
risks.evidence_quote: using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Broader sharing increases the chance of secondary use beyond the participant's original SNAP administration context.

mitigations.description: Restrict database access to authorized personnel only and keep transfers limited to secure channels and the authorized AWS environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: through secure channels
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and using secure transport reduces the chance of unauthorized exposure of the centralized dataset.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and retention limits so only the historical data needed for integrity checks is retained.
mitigations.rationale: Holding less historical data reduces unnecessary privacy exposure while still supporting the stated integrity purpose.

mitigations.description: Use matching algorithms designed to minimize false positives and require human review before any adverse action is taken.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using matching algorithms to minimize false positives
mitigations.rationale: False-positive reduction and review help prevent erroneous harm from automated matches.

mitigations.description: Limit disclosures to state agencies to cases that are necessary for investigation and consistent with the notice and law.
mitigations.evidence_quote: sharing, where permitted by law and consistent with this notice, information with State agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify fraudulent or otherwise improper or illegal SNAP enrollments or transactions.
mitigations.rationale: Tying disclosure to necessity and legal limits reduces unnecessary sharing of sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Limit immigration-status access and use to the specific fraud-prevention check and protect it with strict access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Immigration status check;
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing access to immigration data reduces the risk of sensitive disclosure and misuse.

mitigations.description: Validate household and age data carefully and limit use of those fields to the stated integrity checks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Age and household composition validation;
mitigations.rationale: Careful validation and purpose limitation reduce harm from inaccurate or overly broad use of family information.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce purpose limitations for all interagency data matches so data are used only for SNAP integrity checks and related investigations.
mitigations.rationale: Clear purpose limits reduce the risk that shared data will be repurposed beyond the program administration and enforcement context.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information about non-employee affiliates, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of names, business contact details, and affiliate identifiers.
risks.evidence_quote: Names, business address and contact information, and Affiliate ID of Contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Government employees, Resource Conservation & Development Council employees, Volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organization personnel (referred to as Affiliates).
risks.rationale: The system maintains direct identifiers and contact information for multiple categories of non-employees, which is sensitive if improperly accessed.

risks.description: Only NRCS employees can access the system, so insider misuse or excessive employee access could expose affiliate records without the affiliates' direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
risks.rationale: Limiting access to employees reduces the user base but still leaves internal users who could misuse or overreach access.

risks.description: Affiliate information is linked to Level 2 eAuth accounts and used to assign roles, which could lead to improper access if the linkage is wrong or abused.
risks.evidence_quote: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record. The zRoles application is then used to assign specific roles to the Level 2 account, which allows the affiliate access to various NRCS applications.
risks.rationale: Because the record directly drives access privileges, errors or misuse can affect both privacy and system access.

risks.description: NRCS employees enter the information provided by affiliates, so transcription or validation errors could create inaccurate records that affect access control decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: An NRCS employee enters the information about the individual non-employee affiliate, which is populated from information that was provided by the non-employee.
risks.rationale: Manual entry introduces the possibility of inaccurate data being stored and then used for authorization.

risks.description: The system shares affiliate information with zRoles, creating an internal disclosure path that could expand exposure if that connected system is compromised or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
risks.rationale: Internal sharing increases the number of systems handling the data and therefore the attack surface.

risks.description: The records are retained for long periods, increasing the chance that outdated personal information remains available longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time during which records can be exposed, misused, or become stale.

risks.description: Retention tied to program participation may keep records after an affiliate no longer needs access, which can preserve unnecessary personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs”.
risks.rationale: Keeping records until a program-qualification condition ends may outlast the immediate need for access administration.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and storage to the minimum personal information needed for access administration and protect it with strong access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing the data stored reduces the harm if the record is exposed.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and periodic review of employee access to the Affiliates system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
mitigations.rationale: Since only employees can access the system, tighter internal access governance helps reduce insider risk.

mitigations.description: Require verification of the affiliate-to-eAuth linkage and role assignment before access is granted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record. The zRoles application is then used to assign specific roles to the Level 2 account, which allows the affiliate access to various NRCS applications.
mitigations.rationale: Verification before role assignment helps prevent incorrect or excessive access from being granted.

mitigations.description: Use a second-person review or validation step for manually entered affiliate data.
mitigations.rationale: A review step can catch transcription and entry errors before they affect authorization decisions.

mitigations.description: Protect the interface and data exchange with zRoles using authenticated, authorized, and logged system-to-system controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
mitigations.rationale: Securing the internal sharing path reduces the risk created by moving data between systems.

mitigations.description: Apply records management controls to purge or archive records when they are no longer needed under the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Disposition controls help prevent unnecessary long-term retention of personal information.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retained affiliate records to confirm the person still qualifies for the program need that justifies retention.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure records are not kept longer than the stated retention trigger requires.

risks.description: The system stores a large amount of sensitive personally identifiable information, including tax IDs and social security numbers, which increases the harm if the data is exposed. The combination of identity, policy, and farm-related details can make individuals highly identifiable.
risks.evidence_quote: Producer name, address, phone numbers, tax ID, ID type, and entity type, as well as any associated farm numbers. Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc. Policy data includes name, address, phone number, policy number, unit, Approved Insurance Provider (AIP), crop, insurance plan, coverage level, indemnity, liability, premium, fund placement, acres, agent name, agent social security number, adjuster name, adjuster social security number, and etc.
risks.rationale: This data set contains direct identifiers and sensitive financial and location-linked information that would be damaging if disclosed.

risks.description: The system exposes personal data to multiple internal organizations and limited OIG users, creating a risk of unnecessary or mistaken disclosure beyond the minimum needed for a user's role. Broader sharing increases the number of people who can see sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently the information described previously is provided to FSA, RMA, and OIG within USDA. There have been limited OIG users that have access to the system, this was to obtain reports and transmit products and is a routine use.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the chance of misuse, error, or unauthorized access.

risks.description: Authorized external users, including Approved Insurance Providers, can access data associated with their policies, which still creates a risk of disclosure if access controls are bypassed or misconfigured. Web-based access also increases exposure to account compromise.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs. AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
risks.rationale: A web-accessible system with external users requires strong access controls to prevent unauthorized viewing of personal records.

risks.description: The system relies on eAuthentication and HyDRA authentication for access, but the PIA does not describe additional safeguards such as least-privilege review or multi-factor authentication. If credentials are compromised, sensitive records could be disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
risks.rationale: Authentication alone does not eliminate the risk of account takeover or excessive access.

risks.description: The system keeps the information for the life of the project, which creates a retention risk because personal data may remain available long after the original operational need has passed. Long retention increases the window for unauthorized access and secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases exposure over time and makes any future breach more consequential.

risks.description: The system consolidates annual RMA databases into a single production database, which can concentrate many years of personal information in one place. That aggregation increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years. Data from all years is moved into a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
risks.rationale: Combining records into one repository increases the amount of personal data at risk in a single incident.

risks.description: The system uses ETL and cleansing steps that alter source files to remove characters and standardize records, which creates a risk of inaccurate or mismatched personal data if transformation logic is wrong. Inaccurate data can affect individuals in analysis and reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: ETL tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data. For example, “Mr.” will appear in some records with a period and in others without a period. Consistency changes are achieved by including/removing the period, thus eliminating the one-character difference that would be problematic in data analysis where unique individuals must be identified.
risks.rationale: Data transformation errors can lead to incorrect identification or incorrect reporting about a person.

risks.description: The system uses weather data to validate claims and supports research and fraud analysis, which creates a risk of secondary use beyond the expectations of the original data subjects. Individuals may not expect their information to be used in broad analytics and fraud-related review.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program. The objective is to provide tools, information, and analysis proven effective in the private sector in reducing insurance waste, fraud, and abuse.
risks.rationale: Analytical reuse can expand how personal data is applied beyond the operational purpose of collection.

mitigations.description: Limit the data stored and displayed in HyDRA to the minimum necessary fields, and mask or redact tax IDs and social security numbers wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing direct identifiers lowers the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Restrict sharing to role-based, need-to-know access and periodically review whether each internal recipient still needs access to the specific reports or records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting recipients and reviewing access reduces unnecessary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege authorization for external users so AIPs can access only the specific policy records needed for reporting, and regularly validate that access boundaries are working as intended.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Tight scope on external access reduces the chance of overexposure.

mitigations.description: Add stronger account protections such as periodic access reviews and multi-factor authentication for web access to reduce the risk of credential compromise.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and review controls make unauthorized access harder.

mitigations.description: Apply a shorter retention schedule for working copies and purge or archive records once they are no longer needed for the project or required by the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the time during which personal data can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Segment the production database or tightly control access to historical years so users only retrieve the minimum historical data needed for a task.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to aggregated historical data reduces the blast radius of a breach.

mitigations.description: Strengthen validation of ETL and cleansing scripts with change control, test cases, and exception review to ensure transformations do not alter identity or policy data incorrectly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ETL tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data.
mitigations.rationale: Better testing and change control reduce the chance of introducing inaccurate personal data.

mitigations.description: Document and limit secondary uses of the data to approved purposes, and ensure users understand that analytics and fraud-related review are restricted to the authorized program purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program. The objective is to provide tools, information, and analysis proven effective in the private sector in reducing insurance waste, fraud, and abuse.
mitigations.rationale: Clear purpose limits help prevent function creep and unexpected reuse.

risks.description: Unauthorized users or insiders could access user profile PII because the system is Internet-based and supports access for multiple user groups, including contractors and partners.
risks.evidence_quote: The CoLab system is accessible to NRCS employees and affiliates.
risks.rationale: Internet-accessible systems with multiple authorized user groups increase the chance that access controls are misused or bypassed.

risks.description: Authorized contractors and partners may see more personal information than necessary if role-based access is not tightly scoped to job duties.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities. Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
risks.rationale: Role-based access reduces exposure only if roles are narrowly defined and consistently enforced.

risks.description: Users can modify their own profiles, which could lead to inaccurate or unnecessary personal data being stored if changes are not validated.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Self-service editing can create privacy and integrity issues if users enter incorrect or excessive contact information.

risks.description: PII is retained for as long as the application remains in production, which may keep personal data longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the amount of personal data exposed over time and prolongs the impact of any breach.

risks.description: Disabled accounts may still leave residual profile data in the system after a user leaves, creating unnecessary persistence of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
risks.rationale: Disabling access does not necessarily remove stored PII, so dormant records may remain exposed.

risks.description: The system maintains personal contact details such as email, phone, and company address, which could expose users to unwanted contact or identification if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: Personal Contact Information is comprised of the following elements: o First name o Last name o Email o Phone o Company Address
risks.rationale: Contact details are directly identifying and can be misused for phishing, harassment, or profiling.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to CoLab to authenticated users with approved need-to-know access and periodically review those permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and access review reduce the chance of unauthorized viewing of profile PII.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor and partner access to the minimum roles required for their responsibilities and review those roles regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing role scope reduces unnecessary exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Validate and audit user-edited profile changes before they become authoritative records.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing edits helps prevent inaccurate or excessive personal information from being stored.

mitigations.description: Delete application-specific PII when it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Deletion when no longer needed reduces unnecessary retention and limits exposure.

mitigations.description: Disable accounts promptly when users leave and ensure associated profile data is reviewed for deletion or archival according to retention rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
mitigations.rationale: Prompt account closure and data cleanup reduce the persistence of stale personal data.

mitigations.description: Collect and retain only the contact fields needed to establish and manage CoLab access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab contains a minimal amount of contact information related to CoLab users.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization lowers the privacy impact if contact records are accessed inappropriately.

risks.description: Vendor PII is retained in the IDEA DataMart, which creates a risk of unnecessary persistence and exposure if the data is kept longer than needed for reporting. Even minimal names and contact information can create privacy harm if retained in a reporting store without strict minimization and deletion controls.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Storing PII in an application data mart increases the chance of over-retention and exposure beyond the original source system.

risks.description: Because the system allows contractors access, vendor PII could be viewed by users who do not need it for a specific report or task. This raises the risk of internal overexposure of contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access to a system holding PII creates a need to tightly limit who can see it and when.

risks.description: The use of read-only web service calls from SCIMS and periodic refreshes creates a risk that outdated or incorrect vendor PII may be used in reports. Inaccurate contact information can lead to privacy harm through misdirected communications or decisions based on stale data.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Periodic refreshes reduce but do not eliminate the risk that reports rely on stale data between updates.

risks.description: Reports can be produced using selectable criteria from drop-down menus, which could allow users to generate outputs that reveal more vendor-related PII than intended for a given business need. Even if the system does not search by personal identifier, broad report parameters can still increase exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
risks.rationale: Flexible reporting controls can unintentionally broaden access to PII if outputs are not constrained to the minimum necessary.

mitigations.description: Apply strict data minimization and automatic deletion controls to the IDEA DataMart so vendor PII is removed as soon as it is no longer needed for report generation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per NARA General Records Schedule 20, application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Deletion when no longer needed directly reduces the privacy impact of retaining PII in the DataMart.

mitigations.description: Restrict contractor access to the minimum set of reports and records needed for assigned duties, and review access regularly to ensure the need-to-know limitation is enforced.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access review lowers the chance that contractor access becomes broader than necessary.

mitigations.description: Use a more frequent synchronization schedule or validation checks for SCIMS-derived PII so reports rely on current vendor names and contact information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
mitigations.rationale: More timely updates reduce the risk of stale data being used in reports.

mitigations.description: Limit report parameters and output fields to the minimum necessary for the costing and budgeting purpose, and review report templates to prevent unnecessary disclosure of vendor PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The IDEA application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining report design helps prevent users from generating outputs that expose more PII than needed.

risks.description: The system can expose sensitive customer identifiers that may be linked to SSNs or tax IDs, creating a risk of identity theft or improper re-identification if accessed or returned beyond what is needed.
risks.evidence_quote: SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number
risks.rationale: An identifier that can be associated with SSNs or tax IDs is highly sensitive and increases harm if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: The system transmits customer data between multiple client applications, databases, and adjacent systems, which increases the chance of unauthorized disclosure across internal interfaces.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
risks.rationale: More internal hops create more opportunities for interception, misrouting, or excessive access.

risks.description: API responses are returned in JSON format, which may disclose more personal data than the requesting application or user needs if response controls are not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: Returning structured records can expose full data fields unless the response is minimized to the specific request.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, so there is a risk of insider misuse or unnecessary viewing of customer information by non-employee users.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the set of people who can see sensitive records.

risks.description: The system relies on a single external-facing gateway as the entry point for requests from outside the firewall, which creates a concentration risk if that control is bypassed or misconfigured.
risks.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: A single entry point is a critical control whose failure could expose many connected systems and data flows.

risks.description: Core Services accesses a replicated copy or view of SCIMS data, so privacy-sensitive customer data may be exposed in multiple places and become harder to govern consistently.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: Replicated or viewed data can broaden the footprint of personal information and complicate access oversight.

risks.description: The system stores administrative and transactional information even though it does not store PII, which may still reveal customer activity or case handling details if not properly protected.
risks.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
risks.rationale: Transactional records can be privacy-sensitive because they may reveal who interacted with the program and when.

mitigations.description: Limit exposure of customer identifiers by returning only the minimum identifier fields needed for the specific business function and masking or truncating identifiers whenever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing identifier exposure reduces the chance that linked SSN or tax ID information can be misused.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing secure transmission controls for all internal API and database traffic and restrict each interface to only the systems that require it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS
mitigations.rationale: Encrypted transport and limited interfaces reduce the chance of interception or unauthorized internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply response filtering so each JSON payload includes only the fields required by the requesting application and user role.
mitigations.rationale: Field-level minimization lowers the amount of personal data exposed in each API response.

mitigations.description: Keep the need-to-know restriction and mandatory background investigations for contractors, and review contractor access regularly to ensure it remains justified.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Access limitation and vetting reduce the likelihood of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Harden and continuously monitor the CA API Gateway because it is the single point of entry, including strict access control and threat protection rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CA API Gateway – Used for threat protection, access control, and other sharedservices as defined during the architecture build out.
mitigations.rationale: Strengthening the gateway protects the main choke point through which external requests enter the platform.

mitigations.description: Use eAuth-based access controls and periodic access reviews for all users who reach SCIMS data through NPAD or replicated views.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and access review help ensure replicated customer data is only visible to authorized users.

mitigations.description: Apply retention limits and logging review to administrative and transactional records so they are kept only as long as needed for the service purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting how long operational records are kept reduces the privacy impact of those records.

risks.description: Emergency Action Plans contain personal contact and location information that could expose responders and property owners if disclosed beyond the intended emergency purpose. The data includes names, home addresses, and telephone numbers, which are identifiable and potentially sensitive when linked to dam emergencies.
risks.evidence_quote: EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: Names, addresses, and phone numbers create a direct privacy risk if they are exposed or misused.

risks.description: The system allows disclosure of PII in hardcopy or electronic form during review cycles or when an EAP is activated, creating a risk of accidental or unauthorized exposure during transmission or handling. Because the information leaves the system in these forms, it can be copied, lost, or intercepted outside DamWatch.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Distributing PII in portable formats increases the chance of unintended disclosure.

risks.description: State and local emergency responders receive the PII in the EAPs, so more organizations than NRCS may see the personal data. Each additional recipient increases the chance that the information will be further disclosed or handled inconsistently.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII contained within the EAPs is shared with state and local emergency responders in the event of activation of an EAP.
risks.rationale: Sharing personal data with external responders expands the number of people who can access it.

risks.description: NRCS personnel and contractors can access EAPs containing PII on a need-to-know basis, which still creates insider-access risk if access is excessive, misused, or not properly monitored. The system also includes contractors, which broadens the set of authorized users handling the data.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS personnel may access EAPs containing PII, as needed; however, the USDA and NRCS does not share this PII outside the scope of DamWatch operations.
risks.rationale: Any system with authorized users handling personal data needs controls to prevent misuse and over-access.

risks.description: The system retains the information for potentially long periods, which increases the chance that outdated PII remains available after it is no longer needed. Long retention also lengthens the window in which the data could be exposed by a security incident or improper access.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases cumulative exposure risk.

risks.description: Because the system uses both publicly accessible information and information voluntarily submitted by individuals or organizations, there is a risk that people may not fully understand how their personal data will be used in emergency planning. This can create transparency and notice concerns, especially for telephone numbers that may not be publicly listed.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII can be obtained from publicly accessible information resources, from organizations involved in emergency response, or submitted voluntarily by individual responders or property owners.
risks.rationale: Mixed sources of collection can make it harder for individuals to understand the provenance and use of their data.

mitigations.description: Limit EAP PII to the minimum necessary fields required for execution, and review whether every name, address, and phone number is essential for each dam site.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII collected is only used during the execution of an EAP following the authorized activation of the EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing the data collected reduces the amount of personal information that could be exposed.

mitigations.description: Use secure transmission and controlled distribution procedures for all hardcopy and electronic EAP copies, including logging who receives each copy and when.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled and secure distribution reduces the chance of accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit external sharing to only the specific state and local emergency responders assigned to the relevant dam site, and ensure they receive only the EAP information needed for activation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting recipients to the smallest relevant group reduces unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Maintain the documented access control procedures and enforce need-to-know access for NRCS personnel and contractors, with background investigations for contractors as already required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DamWatch has documented Access Control (AC) Procedures, in compliance with FISMA and USDA directives.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access controls help prevent unauthorized insider access and misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply records management reviews to remove or archive EAP PII when it is no longer needed for an active dam owner, operator, producer, or participant, consistent with approved schedules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
mitigations.rationale: Regular retention review reduces the amount of stale personal data kept in the system.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice to responders and property owners about what PII is collected, the sources used, and that the information is used only for EAP execution.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII collected is only used during the execution of an EAP following the authorized activation of the EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice improves transparency and helps individuals understand the purpose of collection.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, so a compromise or misuse could expose individuals to identity theft, financial fraud, or other harm.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The listed data elements include direct identifiers and banking information that are sensitive if disclosed.

risks.description: Because the system is searchable and supports retrieval of records, users may access more information than is necessary for their duties.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.
risks.rationale: Search and retrieval increase the chance of unnecessary exposure if access is not tightly constrained.

risks.description: Authorized FPAC staff and contractors can access the records, so insider misuse or accidental disclosure is possible.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Any system with broad internal access to sensitive records faces insider privacy risk.

risks.description: Contractor access increases the number of people and organizations that can handle the records, which raises the risk of improper handling or unauthorized disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: This system has both front end applications (DRMS) as well as back-end computing /processing applications (inherited from the host GSS).
risks.rationale: Contractor-developed and hosted components can expand the attack and handling surface for PII.

risks.description: Scanned paper records and metadata are bulk transferred into the system, creating a risk that records could be captured, indexed, or stored with incorrect or excessive information.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk ingestion can propagate errors or oversharing at scale if the source documents or extracted metadata are not reviewed.

risks.description: Long retention periods increase the amount of time sensitive records remain available, which extends the window for misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: The longer records are kept, the longer they remain exposed to privacy risk.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DRMS, so they may be less able to review or correct their own records promptly.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS.
risks.rationale: Limited direct access can make it harder for individuals to detect and correct inaccurate personal information.

mitigations.description: Continue encrypting the documents and restrict access to only those with a documented need-to-know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and need-to-know access reduce the impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce the documented access control procedures so search and retrieval are available only to users with a valid need-to-know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS has documented Access Control (AC) Procedures, in compliance with FISMA and USDA directives.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to authorized duties reduces unnecessary viewing of records.

mitigations.description: Keep requiring Level 2 eAuth credentials and need-to-know authorization for all access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and role-based authorization reduce insider misuse risk.

mitigations.description: Require mandatory background investigations for contractors before granting access and maintain that control for all contractor users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Screening contractors helps reduce the risk of improper handling of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Review bulk-scanned records and extracted metadata for accuracy and necessity before they are loaded into the metadata stores.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-load review can prevent incorrect or unnecessary personal information from being ingested at scale.

mitigations.description: Apply the NARA-approved retention schedules and dispose of records as soon as they are no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing retention time limits the period during which records can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Use the published SORN request process to let individuals request access to records about them and seek corrections through authorized staff.
mitigations.evidence_quote: As published in NRCS-1 SORN: “Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A formal request process gives individuals a path to inspect and correct their records.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal and financial information, so unauthorized access could expose names, addresses, tax IDs, SSNs, bank routing numbers, and farm ownership details.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored data make unauthorized disclosure especially harmful to affected individuals.

risks.description: Authorized access by multiple user groups creates a risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure of documents beyond what each user needs.
risks.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
risks.rationale: Even restricted access still exposes sensitive records to multiple people who may not all need every document.

risks.description: Contractors and technical service providers may receive or access PII outside USDA, creating a disclosure risk if authorization is too broad or not properly limited to the stated purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
risks.rationale: External recipients increase the number of parties handling sensitive records and raise the chance of secondary misuse or over-disclosure.

risks.description: The system uses address and name data from FSA SCIMS to determine the correct producer, which creates a risk of misidentification or matching the wrong individual's records.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Using limited identity attributes for matching can lead to incorrect association of records with the wrong person.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DMS, which can make it harder for them to see, correct, or challenge inaccurate or improperly held information.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: When only staff can access the system, affected individuals depend on intermediaries to identify and fix errors.

risks.description: Records may be retained for long periods, increasing the amount of time sensitive PII remains available and the chance of exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017. Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which records can be accessed, breached, or misused.

risks.description: Because documents are stored in PDF files and viewed with Adobe PDF plug-ins, there is a risk that document content or metadata could be exposed through the file format or viewing environment.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields. ... Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents.
risks.rationale: Document-based storage and plugin-based viewing can expose more information than intended if files are mishandled or viewed insecurely.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the sensitive documents strictly to users with a documented need-to-know and apply role-based controls for the specific locations and documents they are authorized to handle.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS features will allow users to view documents and/or upload new documents, version documents, and delete documents within the scope for those locations where their role has jurisdiction.
mitigations.rationale: Role-scoped access reduces the number of people who can reach highly sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews and periodic user recertification for NRCS employees and conservation district employees who can access DMS.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access review helps ensure that only users who still need the data retain access.

mitigations.description: Require written authorization for each external disclosure and document the specific purpose and data elements shared with contractors or technical service providers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
mitigations.rationale: Tying disclosure to written authorization and purpose limitation narrows external sharing.

mitigations.description: Use additional verification checks when matching SCIMS data so that name and address alone do not determine the correct producer in cases of ambiguity.
mitigations.rationale: Adding a second verification step reduces the chance of misidentifying a producer.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear, timely correction and access request process so individuals can obtain information about records pertaining to them and request updates through the designated contact path.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A formal request path helps individuals exercise access and correction rights even without direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition rules to delete or archive records as soon as the applicable retention period ends, rather than keeping them longer than required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Harden the PDF viewing environment and restrict plug-in use to approved, patched versions only.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the document viewer reduces the chance of unintended exposure through the viewing tool.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive borrower financial and identity information, so unauthorized access could expose personal and financial details about distressed borrowers. This could cause privacy harm because the data includes names, tax IDs, loan information, and security property.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: The system stores direct identifiers together with financial and collateral data, which would be harmful if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Because the system is used by field office employees to evaluate debt restructuring, there is a risk that access could be broader than necessary for the specific employee role. If users can see more borrower information than they need, privacy exposure increases.
risks.evidence_quote: To assist field office employees in restructuring customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
risks.rationale: A role-based business process still creates unnecessary exposure if access is not limited to the minimum needed for each employee.

risks.description: Manual data entry by FSA field agents creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete borrower records, which could lead to incorrect restructuring decisions and improper handling of personal information. Errors in financial or identity data can affect the borrower directly.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manually entered records are more prone to error, and this system uses the data for consequential servicing decisions.

risks.description: The system accesses other internal databases and reference tables, which can increase the amount of personal data aggregated in one place and expand the privacy impact if the system is misused or compromised. Combining records can create a fuller profile of a borrower than any single source alone.
risks.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Pulling data from multiple systems increases the sensitivity of the combined borrower profile.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the long-term privacy risk because sensitive data remains available far beyond the period needed for servicing. The longer the records are kept, the greater the chance of misuse, breach, or outdated information being used.
risks.evidence_quote: How long is information retained? The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention extends exposure over time and can preserve sensitive data longer than operational need.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to authorized agency officials and field office employees who need the data to perform restructuring duties, and enforce strong authentication and audit logging for all access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: developed to assist authorized agency officials
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and logging access reduces the chance that sensitive borrower data is viewed or used improperly.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls so each user can view only the borrower information necessary for their assigned servicing function.
mitigations.rationale: Minimum-necessary access reduces unnecessary exposure of borrower information.

mitigations.description: Add validation and review procedures for manually entered borrower data before it is used in restructuring calculations.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps prevent inaccurate data from affecting privacy-sensitive servicing decisions.

mitigations.description: Limit cross-system data retrieval to the minimum fields needed for the calculation and document the necessity of each linked data source.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of data pulled from other systems lowers the privacy impact of aggregation.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records truly need indefinite retention and, where allowed by the approved schedule, apply records disposition controls to remove data when no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention to the approved business need reduces long-term exposure of sensitive records.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive borrower PII and financial data, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse if the application or database is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the stored data, the greater the privacy harm if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Borrowers' name and Tax ID are shared with an external credit bureau, which creates a privacy risk from third-party disclosure and downstream handling outside the agency.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: Sharing identifiers with an outside recipient expands the number of parties that can see or retain the data.

risks.description: The system makes creditworthiness determinations using borrower data, which can expose applicants to adverse decisions based on financial and credit information.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Using sensitive financial data for eligibility decisions can materially affect borrowers if the data are incomplete or inaccurate.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the risk that personal data will remain available longer than necessary and be exposed in future misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which records can be accessed, copied, or repurposed.

risks.description: County office staff enter data collected from borrowers, which creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records affecting privacy and loan decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual entry can introduce errors that propagate into the system's records and decisions.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to borrower PII and financial records to only authorized users who need it for loan processing, and enforce strong authentication and audit logging.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Minimize the data sent to Microbilt to only the name and Tax ID needed for creditworthiness, and document the disclosure purpose and recipient handling requirements.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the shared fields reduces exposure to the external recipient.

mitigations.description: Provide a review and correction process for borrowers to challenge inaccurate credit or financial information before it is used in eligibility decisions.
mitigations.rationale: A correction process helps prevent privacy harms from decisions based on inaccurate data.

mitigations.description: Apply a documented retention schedule to delete or archive records when they are no longer needed for the loan program, rather than storing them indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use validation checks and staff review procedures when county office staff enter borrower data to reduce errors in the records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
mitigations.rationale: Accuracy controls reduce the chance that incorrect data will be stored and used.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains highly sensitive borrower identifiers that could be exposed if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: ADPS uses the customer’s name, address, Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Names, addresses, and Social Security Numbers are sensitive identifiers that increase harm if disclosed.

risks.description: Borrower account information is broadly shared with multiple internal and external recipients, increasing the chance of over-disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers.
