Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
risks.rationale: The more recipients that receive the data, the greater the exposure surface and disclosure risk.

risks.description: Using name or Social Security Number for online queries and batch processing can expose borrower records to unauthorized access if those identifiers are misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Identifier-based retrieval can make it easier to locate and view records if access controls are not tightly enforced.

risks.description: Reporting delinquent borrower information to Treasury, IRS, HUD, and credit bureaus creates a risk of secondary use beyond the original loan-account purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The DCIA processes evaluate accounts for amount and date of delinquency and reported to Treasury for offset. ... IRS tax refund offset to delinquent borrowers ... Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian ... Housing and Urban Development Reporting – Provides information to HUD for Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System
risks.rationale: Information sent for debt collection or reporting can affect borrowers in other systems and contexts.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the duration of privacy exposure and the chance that outdated information remains accessible.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping records forever extends the window in which a breach or improper access could occur.

risks.description: The stated future customer self-service work could create a public-facing exposure risk if borrower data becomes accessible outside the agency.
risks.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
risks.rationale: Public-facing functionality typically increases the risk of unintended disclosure if not carefully designed and secured.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of Social Security Numbers to the minimum necessary and mask them wherever full display is not required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing visible exposure of sensitive identifiers lowers the harm if records are viewed improperly.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and data-sharing restrictions so each recipient only receives the borrower information needed for its specific purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers. Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access by role and purpose reduces unnecessary disclosure across many recipients.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication, logging, and audit review for all name- and SSN-based queries and batch access to borrower records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
mitigations.rationale: Auditability and strong authentication help detect and deter improper record access.

mitigations.description: Provide only the specific data elements required for each reporting or offset function and document the legal basis for each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used by ADPS to provide an accounting system of record and official reporting mechanism supporting loan and grant programs for insured, direct, and guaranteed loans. Information is reported to the IRS for taxation purposes as legally required by Section 6050J of the IRS Code.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited disclosure reduces the chance that data is reused more broadly than necessary.

mitigations.description: Implement records review and disposition controls to delete or archive records according to an approved schedule instead of keeping all records indefinitely online.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic disposition review can reduce unnecessary long-term exposure while preserving required records.

mitigations.description: Before any public-facing customer self-service release, perform a privacy and security review to ensure only the minimum borrower data is exposed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
mitigations.rationale: A pre-release review can prevent avoidable disclosure in a public-facing environment.

risks.description: The system stores identifiable contact information that could be exposed if internal users access it without a need to know or if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly identifying and would be sensitive if viewed or used by unauthorized staff.

risks.description: Manual entry by multiple FLP staff increases the chance of inaccurate or incomplete records being entered and then used in appraisal processing.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Manual input creates a risk of human error that can affect the privacy and integrity of the stored information.

risks.description: The system centralizes appraisal information for broad FLP use, which increases the impact if a user accesses more information than needed for their role.
risks.evidence_quote: provide County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members with the means to facilitate and track status of appraisals
risks.rationale: A shared enterprise application can expose more records to more users than a narrower workflow would.

risks.description: Keeping records indefinitely increases the long-term exposure of personal data and the chance that outdated information remains available longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which records could be misused, breached, or simply remain unnecessarily accessible.

risks.description: The system’s web-based design creates a general risk of unauthorized access through the application or database if technical safeguards fail.
risks.evidence_quote: The enterprise web application will help to standardize the loan appraisal process
risks.rationale: Any web application that stores PII depends on strong authentication, authorization, and secure configuration.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions so staff can only view the contact information needed for their appraisal duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the likelihood that identifiable contact data is viewed by unauthorized personnel.

mitigations.description: Add validation checks and supervisory review for manually entered records before they are finalized in the system.
mitigations.rationale: Review and validation help catch input errors before they affect the record set.

mitigations.description: Limit each user’s view to only the appraisals and fields needed for their specific county, state, regional, or national role.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the scope of visible records lowers the privacy impact of a centralized application.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition controls and periodic review to confirm indefinite retention remains necessary for each record class.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure records are kept only as long as required by the approved schedule.

mitigations.description: Use strong authentication, secure session management, and routine security monitoring for the web application and database.
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the chance of unauthorized access to PII in a web-based system.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains highly sensitive personal and financial information, including SSNs/TINs, race, ethnicity, gender, credit reports, and employment history, which could expose borrowers to identity theft or discrimination if misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: The sensitivity and breadth of the collected data increase harm if unauthorized access or disclosure occurs.

risks.description: The system relies on data from multiple external sources, including credit reporting agencies, tax records, courthouse records, and other lenders, which may contain inaccurate or incomplete information that can affect loan decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected directly from farm loan borrower and information is received from other FSA applications, state and local agencies and other third party financial sources.
risks.rationale: Decisions based on third-party and government records can be wrong if the source data is stale or inaccurate.

risks.description: The system uses personal and financial data to determine credit worthiness and restructure debt, creating a risk of unfair or opaque profiling if borrowers cannot understand or challenge the analysis.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Using sensitive data for eligibility and servicing decisions can materially affect borrowers, so transparency and review are important.

risks.description: Permanent retention of the records increases the long-term privacy impact of any unauthorized access, secondary use, or future disclosure because the data never ages out of the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping sensitive records forever expands the window in which they can be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: Field office staff and authorized agency officials can access and manually enter borrower data across web-based applications, which creates insider misuse and accidental disclosure risk if access is broader than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications and allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
risks.rationale: Human access to sensitive records is a common source of unauthorized viewing, copying, or mistakes.

risks.description: The system consolidates data from several applications into a unified view for loan processing and servicing, which can increase exposure if a user sees more information than needed for their task.
risks.evidence_quote: Loan Making provides a consolidated view of direct loan borrower data consisting of loan request information and loan obligation information which will allow Farm Loan personnel to enter and approve loan requests and create a loan obligation record.
risks.rationale: Aggregation of data across functions raises the risk of unnecessary internal access to sensitive details.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and storage to the minimum personal and financial data necessary for loan processing and servicing, and mask or tokenize SSNs/TINs and credit card numbers wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of sensitive data held lowers the impact of any exposure.

mitigations.description: Validate third-party and cross-system data before it is used in decisions, and provide a process for borrowers to review and correct disputed information.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction procedures reduce the chance that bad data drives adverse outcomes.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice of how creditworthiness and restructuring decisions are made, and require documented human review for adverse or high-impact decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and review help prevent unexplained or unfair decisions based on sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Apply a records lifecycle review and archive or segregate older records so only necessary personnel can access them, even if the records must remain permanent.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Segregating older records reduces exposure while preserving required retention.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege role-based access controls and audit logging for all field office and agency users who process or service loans.
mitigations.evidence_quote: provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications and allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and logging access helps prevent unauthorized internal use and supports accountability.

mitigations.description: Use field-level permissions or task-based views so personnel only see the borrower data needed for the specific loan-making or servicing action they are performing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Loan Making provides a consolidated view of direct loan borrower data consisting of loan request information and loan obligation information which will allow Farm Loan personnel to enter and approve loan requests and create a loan obligation record.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the visible data set reduces unnecessary exposure from consolidated records.

risks.description: PII is kept permanently, which increases the chance of long-term exposure, misuse, or secondary use beyond the original need. Indefinite retention also makes any future breach or unauthorized access more consequential because the data never ages out.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention extends the window in which names and addresses can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: The system holds personally identifiable information about individuals involved in loan oversight, trainee tracking, and directives workflows, creating privacy risk if internal users access more data than needed for their role. Even without external sharing, broad internal visibility can lead to unnecessary disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide District Directors (DD) the ability to oversee the management of the service centers and FLM users.
risks.rationale: Role-based access limits are needed because the data supports oversight functions that could otherwise expose personal information to too many users.

risks.description: Data is entered by county offices, state offices, and state personnel, so the system may store inaccurate or outdated personal information if those sources enter incorrect names or addresses. Inaccurate records can affect oversight, training, and workflow decisions about the individuals named in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
risks.rationale: Information quality is a privacy issue because incorrect PII can lead to mistaken decisions or disclosures.

risks.description: The system collects names and mailing addresses for some applications even though the described purposes are oversight, training, and directives management, which suggests a risk of collecting more personal data than necessary. If mailing addresses are not essential to every workflow, retaining them broadens privacy exposure without clear benefit.
risks.evidence_quote: FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
risks.rationale: Minimizing collected PII reduces the amount of personal information exposed if the system is accessed improperly.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which could expose public submitters' personal information in an approval workflow not yet finalized for public release. That creates a risk that sensitive submissions are handled before the underlying directive is approved.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Public submissions in an unapproved workflow should be tightly controlled to avoid premature disclosure or misuse.

mitigations.description: Replace indefinite retention with the shortest retention period allowed by records requirements, and periodically review whether permanent retention is still necessary for each application.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention time lowers the duration of exposure for stored PII.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to PII by role and need-to-know within USDA, with periodic access reviews for District Directors, State Offices, and other users.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance of unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Validate and periodically review records entered by county and state offices to correct inaccurate names and addresses.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps ensure the system does not propagate incorrect personal data.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of mailing addresses to the applications and workflows that truly require them, and omit them where names alone are sufficient.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary PII reduces privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter handling controls to public submissions in SDMS, including review before wider use and clear separation from routine internal workflow data.
mitigations.rationale: Extra controls are warranted when the system collects information from the public before OMB approval.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive identifiers that could cause identity theft or other harm if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: ☒ Social Security number ☒ Employee Identification Number ☒ Taxpayer Identification Number ☒ Business Taxpayer Identification Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Personal Mobile Number ☒ Business Mobile Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Name (including nicknames) ☒ Gender ☒ Business Mailing Address (sole proprietor)
risks.rationale: These fields are directly identifying and sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure could harm the individuals and entities in the system.

risks.description: Sharing Farm Record and Business Partner data across USDA agencies increases the risk of unauthorized disclosure or secondary use beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient and transfer expands the number of places where the data could be mishandled or accessed inappropriately.

risks.description: Long-term retention of historical records increases the amount of personal data exposed if the system is breached or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
risks.rationale: Keeping records for many years increases the volume and age of personal data available for unauthorized access.

risks.description: Maintaining historical data from 1999 to the current program year creates privacy risk because old records may no longer be necessary but remain available.
risks.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
risks.rationale: Older records can contain outdated or unnecessary personal information that should not be retained longer than needed.

risks.description: The system’s geospatial farm, tract, and field boundaries can reveal location-related information about producers' operations.
risks.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
risks.rationale: Location and boundary data can expose sensitive operational details about a farm or ranch.

risks.description: Centralizing customer and farm data as the system of record creates a high-value target if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records ... is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data which is shared with other applications and agencies across USDA
risks.rationale: A single authoritative repository concentrates valuable personal data, making unauthorized access more consequential.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and retention of sensitive identifiers to only what is required for the specific program purpose, and mask or suppress them when full values are not needed.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of sensitive identifiers lowers the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and sharing agreements that restrict agency access to only the data needed for program delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access by role reduces the chance that shared data will be viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Encrypt all inter-agency transmissions and verify that encryption is enforced for every shared data flow.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data transmission is protected by encryption including Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data in transit from interception during sharing.

mitigations.description: Implement and enforce data retention schedules that delete or dispose of records once they are no longer required.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Review archived historical records periodically and purge data that is no longer needed for legal or program purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review prevents outdated records from remaining available indefinitely.

mitigations.description: Limit access to geospatial boundary data to users who need it for farm record administration and program delivery.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to location data reduces the chance of revealing sensitive operational information.

mitigations.description: Continuously monitor access to the system of record and audit use of customer and farm data for inappropriate access patterns.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring helps detect misuse of a centralized repository before it causes broader harm.

risks.description: The system retains producer information permanently, which increases the risk that personal data will be exposed or misused long after it is needed for the program purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention expands the time window in which records can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, creating a risk of unauthorized viewing or mishandling of producer data by non-federal personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access broadens the number of people who can see sensitive producer records.

risks.description: Information is disclosed to internal shared services and external systems for certain NAP and TAP functions, which creates a risk that producer data will be exposed beyond the original application boundary.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: Each disclosure path increases the chance of unnecessary sharing or downstream mishandling.

risks.description: The system stores producer names and street addresses for many programs, so a compromise of the database would expose direct contact information for affected farmers and ranchers.
risks.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address
risks.rationale: Names and street addresses are directly identifying and can be used to locate or contact individuals.

risks.description: The system stores payment, overpayment, premium, and debt-related information, which could reveal a producer's financial status or disputes with the program if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: Payment/Overpayment processing
risks.rationale: Financial program records can reveal sensitive information about a person's economic situation and obligations.

risks.description: Some components generate letters that are physically mailed, which creates a risk of disclosure through postal handling or delivery to the wrong address.
risks.evidence_quote: AFC includes NAP Continuous Coverage which is a batch process which generates letters for the KC Print Shop that are physically mailed to NAP producers.
risks.rationale: Physical mail can be intercepted, misdelivered, or viewed by others at the delivery location.

risks.description: County office users can enter and manage producer information in several applications, creating a risk of inaccurate or excessive data entry that could affect the producer's privacy and program records.
risks.evidence_quote: AFC county users enters producer’s information.
risks.rationale: User-entered data can be overcollected or entered incorrectly, leading to privacy and record-quality problems.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition rules to avoid keeping producer records indefinitely when a shorter approved retention period is sufficient for the program need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the period during which old records can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to need-to-know roles, require background investigations, Level 2 eAuthentication, NDAs, and enforcement of the no-download/no-share/no-store/no-print rule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Through the USDA Rules of Behavior, they are not allowed to download, share, store or print any USDA specific data.
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the chance that contractors will mishandle producer information.

mitigations.description: Minimize disclosures through shared services by limiting them to the specific data needed for the receiving system and keeping internal interfaces restricted to authorized uses.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared data reduces the amount of producer information exposed across system boundaries.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to producer identity and address fields to authorized users only and protect those records with strong authentication and access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address
mitigations.rationale: Access controls help prevent unauthorized disclosure of directly identifying information.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to payment, overpayment, premium, and debt records to staff who need them for program administration and payment processing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Payment/Overpayment processing
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to financial records reduces the risk of exposing sensitive economic information.

mitigations.description: Use address verification and secure print/mail handling controls for letters that are physically mailed to producers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: generates letters for the KC Print Shop that are physically mailed to NAP producers.
mitigations.rationale: Mail controls reduce the chance that sensitive notices are sent to the wrong recipient or intercepted.

mitigations.description: Use validation and review procedures for county office data entry so producer information is collected only as needed and entered accurately.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AFC county users enters producer’s information.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and review reduce errors and unnecessary collection at the point of entry.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive identity and financial information, so a breach or misuse could expose producers to identity theft or fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: ARCPLC Name, mailing address, last 4 digits SSN SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: SSN/EIN, addresses, and payment amounts are sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure would create substantial harm.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of permanent records increases the chance that personal data will be exposed or used long after it is needed for program operations.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping PII forever expands the window in which a future breach, insider misuse, or secondary use could occur.

risks.description: A shared database accessible to a limited number of employees creates insider-access risk if users can view or export more producer data than they need.
risks.evidence_quote: using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: Even limited internal access can still result in unauthorized viewing, copying, or accidental disclosure if access is broader than job duties.

risks.description: The system relies on SCIMS data being displayed and used in FPISS, which can create accuracy and context risks if outdated or incorrect identity data is pulled into eligibility or payment decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
risks.rationale: If the source record is wrong or stale, the system may present incorrect PII during enrollment or payment processing.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to determine eligibility and identify sign-up participants, which creates a risk of using more personal data than necessary for the stated purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine eligibility.
risks.rationale: Eligibility screening can often be accomplished with less data than a full display of identity and payment information.

mitigations.description: Restrict viewing and export of SSN/EIN, addresses, and payment amounts to only users with a documented need to know, and mask or truncate these fields wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of sensitive identifiers reduces the impact of both insider misuse and accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review and deletion schedule so permanent retention is limited to the minimum period required by the approved records schedule, with periodic reassessment of whether each data element still needs to be kept.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review can reduce the amount of PII held over time and lower long-term exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls, audit logging, and periodic access reviews for the shared database used by National, State, and County Office employees.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter account governance helps ensure only authorized staff can access producer data and that inappropriate access can be detected.

mitigations.description: Validate and periodically reconcile SCIMS-sourced identity data before it is used in FPISS workflows that affect eligibility or payments.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
mitigations.rationale: Checking source-data quality reduces the risk that incorrect PII will drive program decisions or be shown to staff.

mitigations.description: Minimize the personal data displayed in FPISS to only what is necessary for the specific eligibility or sign-up task, and suppress fields not needed for that transaction.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information exposed during routine program processing.

risks.description: County office users can access farmers' and producers' PII to search for specific people, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure or misuse of names, addresses, email, phone, demographic data, and EIN/SSN.
risks.evidence_quote: the FSAfarm+ application uses PII to allow county office users to search for a specific farmer or producer. The specific user information is pulled from the SCIMS database (which resides on the FPCMS system); this information includes: • First Name, Last Name • Entity (business) information • Address Information • Email • Phone Number • Demographic Information • EIN / SSN (via a search screen)
risks.rationale: Broad search access to multiple identifiers increases the chance that sensitive personal information will be viewed or used beyond what is needed.

risks.description: Using SSN as a second authentication method creates a risk of identity theft or account compromise if the SSN is exposed or improperly handled.
risks.evidence_quote: If a farmer or producer has an eAuth account, the SSN can be used as a second authentication method to validate the farmer / producer
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive identifiers, so using them for authentication increases harm if they are disclosed or intercepted.

risks.description: Contractors supporting FSCOMS/FSAfarm+ may be able to access PII, creating a risk of broader insider exposure than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access to PII expands the set of people who can see sensitive data and increases insider-risk exposure.

risks.description: Although the system says PII is not stored, there is still a residual risk that PII remains in memory or cache if logout clearing does not work as intended.
risks.evidence_quote: When a user logs out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: If memory or cache is not fully cleared, residual data could be recovered after the session ends.

risks.description: FSAfarm+ depends on receiving PII from SCIMS, so any weakness in that internal data flow could expose or corrupt the personal data used by county office users.
risks.evidence_quote: FSAfarm+ requests and receives PII from SCIMS, which resides in the FPCMS system.
risks.rationale: A system that pulls live PII from another database inherits the confidentiality and integrity risks of that upstream source and connection.

mitigations.description: Restrict county office user access to only the minimum PII needed for the specific search task and log access to PII lookups.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive personal information is viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Replace SSN-based second authentication with a less sensitive authentication factor and avoid displaying SSN except when strictly required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN use lowers the risk of identity theft and the impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role-based access for contractors and require background checks, training, and audit logging for contractor access to PII.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the number of people who can access sensitive data and improve accountability.

mitigations.description: Verify that logout clearing reliably wipes session memory and cache and test that no PII persists after session termination.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When a user logs out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
mitigations.rationale: Validating the stated clearing behavior helps ensure residual PII is not left behind in volatile storage.

mitigations.description: Secure the SCIMS-to-FSAfarm+ data retrieval path with strong authentication and encryption and monitor for unauthorized access or tampering.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the source-to-destination flow reduces the risk that PII is exposed or altered while being retrieved.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive demographic information, including ethnicity and race, which could expose producers to privacy harm if mishandled or accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: Ethnicity and race are sensitive personal data, so misuse or disclosure would create a higher privacy impact.

risks.description: The system retains producers’ information indefinitely, increasing the chance that outdated records remain available longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention extends the window for unauthorized access, stale data use, and cumulative privacy exposure.

risks.description: County office staff enter data collected from producers at the county office, creating a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records being stored and used for election eligibility and ballot mailing.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual entry introduces the possibility of errors that can affect who is selected to vote and what is mailed.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to determine who is eligible to vote in committee elections and to send ballots, which could reveal participation-related information if access is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
risks.rationale: Election eligibility and ballot-related records can disclose a producer’s relationship to a committee election.

risks.description: The system maintains election results and COC member data, which could expose producers’ voting-related or organizational participation history if records are accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: Track Election results and COC Member data.
risks.rationale: Election and membership records can reveal participation in a government election process.

risks.description: The system builds and sends county-specific lists of eligible producers for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, which could expose mailing addresses if the lists are mishandled during preparation or printing.
risks.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
risks.rationale: Mailing lists combine identity and address data, so mishandling could directly disclose personal contact information.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to ethnicity and race fields to only staff with a documented need to know and apply strong access logging and review.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and auditing use reduces the chance that sensitive demographic data is viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether all retained records remain necessary and, where permitted by the approved schedule, remove or archive records that are no longer actively needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps reduce unnecessary exposure from records that no longer need active handling.

mitigations.description: Use validation checks and supervisor review for county office data entry before records are used for eligibility, ballots, or reports.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
mitigations.rationale: Verification at entry helps prevent inaccurate records from affecting election-related decisions.

mitigations.description: Limit access to eligibility lists and committee-code data to authorized election personnel and keep those lists segregated from unrelated records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
mitigations.rationale: Access limitation and segregation reduce the chance that eligibility information is exposed beyond the election function.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls to election results and COC member records and monitor access to those records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Track Election results and COC Member data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access helps protect participation-related records from improper disclosure.

mitigations.description: Protect ballot mailing lists during generation and printing by limiting who can handle them and ensuring secure handling of the printed forms.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
mitigations.rationale: Controlling handling of mailing lists reduces the risk that names and addresses are exposed during ballot production.

risks.description: The warehouse concentrates highly sensitive personal and financial data in one place, increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or breach. The stored data includes direct identifiers and account information, so a compromise could expose many people at once.
risks.evidence_quote: All Program and financial data for the Agency is stored in the EDW. This includes Farm Program, Farm Loan, Commodity Operations, Human Resources and Financial data. Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: Centralizing sensitive data increases harm because one incident can reveal a broad set of personal and financial details.

risks.description: Broad internal reporting access may expose personal data to more personnel than necessary for any one business need. The system provides information to national, state, and county personnel and supports end user reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: provides information to FSA national, state, and county personnel
risks.rationale: Wide internal availability raises the risk of unnecessary access and misuse of personal information.

risks.description: Batch transfers from source systems into the warehouse create a risk of interception, corruption, or unintended disclosure while data is moving between systems. The data flow includes extraction from multiple sources and loading into Oracle DB.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV will consolidate the data from source applications using the same process as current in the Informix DB (i.e. getting the data from source as flat files and using an extract transfer and load (ETL) process to load it into Oracle DB).
risks.rationale: Moving sensitive data through batch and ETL processes expands the number of points where it can be exposed or altered.

risks.description: Sharing PII with other federal agencies and external parties can disclose personal data beyond the original collection purpose. The context shows sharing with NRCS, RD, RMA, IRS, Treasury, and others.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the chance that data will be used or protected differently than intended.

risks.description: External disclosure for identity or address validation may expose data to entities that do not need full records, creating unnecessary privacy risk. The system notes a share with Dunn and Bradstreet for name and address validation.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Validation uses can often be satisfied with limited fields, so sharing broader data can be excessive.

risks.description: The system supports reporting and analysis beyond the original point of collection, which can lead to secondary use of personal data for purposes not obvious to the data subject. It is used for Congressional, program level, and end user reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the EDW is used for Congressional, program level and end user reporting.
risks.rationale: Repurposing collected data for multiple reporting audiences can create privacy expectations gaps.

risks.description: Retention of large historical data sets for an extended period can increase the chance of outdated or unnecessary personal data remaining available. The system retains information according to the NARA schedule and allows deviations when defined.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases exposure time and the likelihood that data outlives its operational need.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the warehouse to authorized users only and apply role-based access controls to sensitive fields such as TIN/SSN and account numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the number of people who can see the most sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege permissions and separate reporting views so personnel only see the minimum data needed for their job.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting internal visibility reduces the risk of unnecessary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Protect batch and ETL transfers with encryption in transit and integrity checks to prevent interception or tampering.
mitigations.rationale: Securing transfers lowers the chance that data is exposed or altered while moving between systems.

mitigations.description: Use formal data-sharing agreements and disclose only the minimum necessary information to each recipient.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and agreements help ensure recipients receive only what they need and understand their obligations.

mitigations.description: Limit validation exchanges to the specific fields needed for name and address matching, and avoid sending full records when not required.
mitigations.rationale: Sending only the minimum fields reduces unnecessary exposure during validation.

mitigations.description: Document and review each reporting use to ensure it is consistent with the stated purpose of meeting reporting needs and complying with law.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is being collected to meet the reporting needs of the agency and comply with federal regulations and legislative mandates.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose review helps prevent secondary uses that exceed the stated collection purpose.

mitigations.description: Apply the NARA retention schedule strictly and delete or archive records when they are no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of historical personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal and financial data, so any unauthorized access could expose identity, banking, payment, debt, and tax information. This creates a significant risk of identity theft or financial harm if the data is mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, street address, SSN/TIN, bank account number, schedule of deposit numbers and image of the signature.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly stores direct identifiers and bank data, which are sensitive if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Public-facing and producer-accessible functions increase the chance that users can view more financial detail than they need. Because producers and county employees can access the Financial Inquiry and Financial Services functions, a mistake in access control could expose detailed payment and debt records.
risks.evidence_quote: The Financial Inquiry Web Application (FI) ... designed to provide access to a producer's financial information on- line. ... Producers have access to both summary and detailed information. County Office employees also have access to FI
risks.rationale: Broad self-service and employee access to detailed records increases the impact of any authorization failure.

risks.description: Contractors with system access may mishandle USDA-specific data despite restrictions, creating a disclosure risk. Even with need-to-know access, the system allows contractor access to sensitive financial records and images.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access to sensitive records increases insider-risk exposure if controls fail or are bypassed.

risks.description: The system generates and transmits letters, statements, and reports about debt and payments, which could reveal sensitive information if intercepted, misdelivered, or handled improperly. This is especially sensitive for delinquent debt, bankruptcy, and collection-related notices.
risks.evidence_quote: NRRS generates letters to customers associated with a receivable
risks.rationale: Mailing and reporting debt information can disclose sensitive financial status outside the intended recipient.

risks.description: Debt information is shared for collection and creditworthiness purposes, which can harm privacy if delinquent debt status is disclosed too widely or in error. The system also sends delinquent debt status to commercial credit bureaus.
risks.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
risks.rationale: Credit-related disclosures can have lasting privacy and reputational consequences if not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely, so sensitive personal data remains available far longer than necessary for routine operational use. Long-term retention increases the impact of any future breach or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention extends the exposure window for sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive financial and identity data to need-to-know users and require strong authentication and background screening for all authorized users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers and banking data are exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Limit FI access so producers and county employees see only the minimum necessary fields and summaries needed for their tasks.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing detailed online disclosure lowers the privacy impact of public-facing self-service access.

mitigations.description: Enforce the existing contractor rules that prohibit downloading, sharing, storing, or printing USDA data, and monitor contractor activity for violations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Through the USDA Rules of Behavior, they are not allowed to download, share, store or print any USDA specific data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting contractor handling of data reduces insider disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Use secure delivery controls for letters and statements, and verify recipient addresses before mailing or printing debt-related notices.
mitigations.rationale: Careful delivery controls reduce the risk of exposing sensitive debt information to the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Continue using encrypted transmission for delinquent debt disclosures to credit bureaus and limit such disclosures to only the data required for the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and data minimization reduce the chance that credit-related disclosures are exposed in transit or beyond what is necessary.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether all permanent records still need indefinite retention and archive or segregate older records to reduce routine exposure.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing day-to-day exposure of older records lowers the risk created by permanent retention.

risks.description: The system permanently retains identifiable employee information, which increases the risk of long-term exposure or use beyond what is necessary for access control.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the chance that PII will be exposed, reused, or remain in the system after it is no longer needed.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains employee name and mailing address information, which could expose personal contact details if the authorization database is misused or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS Name & mailing address
risks.rationale: Contact information is personally identifying and can create privacy harm if accessed without a legitimate need.

risks.description: The system stores detailed authorization data about users’ roles, groups, offices, and attributes, which could reveal sensitive employment and organizational relationships if accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes
risks.rationale: Authorization data can reveal internal structure and a person's organizational affiliations, which should be limited to those with a need to know.

risks.description: Administrators can manage security access rights in real time, so privileged users could over-assign or remove access in ways that expose employee information or enable unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS allows administrators to use a web browser to manage security access rights, assigning and removing roles/groups/attributes to users on-line in real time.
risks.rationale: Privileged access management creates a risk of insider misuse or administrative error affecting confidentiality and access control.

risks.description: The system is an online application that lets users submit security requests and track status, which creates a risk that access-request information could be exposed through the application if controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: The Farm Service Security Services System (FSSSS) is an online security request application and approval system that allows users to submit security requests on line and track the status.
risks.rationale: Online request and status functions can reveal sensitive access-related information if not tightly protected.

mitigations.description: Apply a periodic records review and purge or archive records that are no longer needed for current access-control purposes, consistent with the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Even with approved retention, periodic review can reduce unnecessary exposure of older records.

mitigations.description: Limit access to employee name and mailing address information to users with a demonstrated need for role-based access administration.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood of unnecessary disclosure of personal contact information.

mitigations.description: Restrict viewing of roles, groups, offices, and attributes to authorized administrators and business users whose duties require that information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access limits the privacy impact of sensitive organizational metadata.

mitigations.description: Require strong administrative access controls and audit logging for all role, group, and attribute changes.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring privileged actions helps deter and detect unauthorized or erroneous access changes.

mitigations.description: Protect the online request and status functions with access controls that ensure users can only view their own authorized requests and statuses.
mitigations.evidence_quote: allows users to submit security requests on line and track the status
mitigations.rationale: Limiting status visibility to authorized users reduces the chance of exposing sensitive request information.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal data, so a breach or misuse could expose identity, financial, health, biometric, and criminal-history information. Because the records include images and signatures, harm could extend to impersonation and fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: What information is collected, used, disseminated or maintained in the system? Subsystem Name - Full name, mother’s maiden name, maiden f h i di id l i k li ) Date and/or place of birth. Address Information (street & email address). Personal identification number (social security number, tax identification number, passport number, driver’s license number or a unique identification number, etc.) Financial data (Credit card numbers, bank account etc.) Health data (including height, weight, blood pressure, etc.) Biometric data (fingerprints, iris scans, voice signature, facial geometry, DNA, etc.) Criminal history Employment history Miscellaneous identification numbers (agency assigned number, case number, accounts, permits, etc.) Photographic image/identifying characteristics. Handwriting or an image of the signature
risks.rationale: The listed data elements are unusually sensitive and would cause significant harm if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: Centralized browser-based access to stored images can expose records to unauthorized viewing if access controls are weak or misconfigured. The system allows client access from desktop browser to stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.rationale: Browser-based access to a centralized repository increases the impact of any access-control failure.

risks.description: The system ingests information from faxed, scanned, email, and desktop-scanner sources, which increases the chance that the wrong document or too much information is captured and stored. That can lead to inaccurate or excessive PII being retained in the imaging repository.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from electronically stored documents, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Multiple manual intake channels raise the risk of human error during document capture and indexing.

risks.description: Workflow functions can expose sensitive records to staff who only need limited information to perform their jobs. The system controls workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.rationale: Workflow routing can broaden internal exposure if role-based restrictions are not tight.

risks.description: Importing Federal Reserve Bank images into the system creates a risk that external-source records are brought in without sufficient validation or minimization. Those imported images may contain more personal data than needed for the stated purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: KCFRB Imaging (FRB) downloads and imports Federal Reserve Bank images into the system.
risks.rationale: External imports can introduce data that the system did not originally collect and may not need to retain in full.

risks.description: Permanent retention increases the privacy impact of any future breach or misuse because records never age out of the system. The information is retained indefinitely.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps sensitive records exposed for the longest possible period.

risks.description: A centralized SQL database for document indexes and workflow data creates a metadata privacy risk even if the underlying images are protected. Indexes can reveal who the records are about, what they concern, and how cases move through the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The server utilizes a SQL database to manage document indexes and workflow process.
risks.rationale: Index and workflow metadata can be sensitive because it enables discovery and correlation of records.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict role-based access controls and audit logging for all sensitive record types, with special restrictions for records containing health, biometric, financial, and identity data.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance that highly sensitive records are viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and least-privilege access for browser users, and review permissions regularly for the network device and server-managed image repository.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter authentication and permissions reduce the risk of unauthorized viewing through browser access.

mitigations.description: Add intake validation and quality-control checks for faxed, scanned, email, and manually entered documents before they are stored.
mitigations.rationale: Validation helps catch misfiled, duplicated, or excessive documents before they become permanent records.

mitigations.description: Constrain workflow visibility so users only see the minimum document content needed for their task, and limit workflow routing to authorized roles.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing workflow exposure lowers the number of people who can view sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Apply source-validation and data-minimization review to imported Federal Reserve Bank images before they are stored in the repository.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing imported records helps ensure only necessary and accurate information enters the system.

mitigations.description: Implement a documented retention review process to confirm permanent retention is still necessary for each record class and to segregate records that no longer need broad access.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review can reduce unnecessary long-term exposure even when some records must remain permanent.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to document indexes and workflow metadata separately from image content, and log all metadata searches and changes.
mitigations.rationale: Separating and logging metadata access reduces the chance that sensitive case relationships are exposed.

risks.description: Users may see more personal and eligibility-related information than is necessary for the immediate PSS task, because the system displays detailed contract and status fields and provides links to additional details in PT-FM. This increases the chance of unnecessary internal exposure of sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII that is used, processed or maintained by FA Tracker includes name, address, as well as the following: o Application # o Contract # o Contract Item # ... o Contract Modification Reason ... o Status of a Payment ... o Other Eligibility (Yes/No) o AD-1026 (Y/N) o FTE (Y/N) o AGI (Y/N) ... o Application Status ... o Adequacy Status ... o Obligation Status ... Additional information/details can be accessed via a link to NRCS’ ProTracts- FundManager (PT-FM) application.
risks.rationale: More detailed fields and drill-through access broaden exposure beyond the minimal work-list view.

risks.description: Exporting work lists to Excel can create uncontrolled copies of PII on users’ devices, increasing the chance of loss, unauthorized sharing, or retention outside the system. This is especially sensitive because the export contains the same work-list data.
risks.evidence_quote: Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Local exports are harder to govern than data kept inside the protected application.

risks.description: E-mail alerts can disclose PII beyond the application boundary and may be forwarded, stored, or accessed by unintended recipients. Because the alerts contain record deltas, they can reveal changes over time as well as the underlying personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
risks.rationale: E-mail is a less controlled channel than an authenticated web application and can expand disclosure risk.

risks.description: Client-side filtering and sorting may expose sensitive records on the user’s device or browser session, especially if the device is shared or compromised. This creates a risk that PII remains visible or recoverable outside the intended session.
risks.evidence_quote: A user can then filter and sort this data on the client side.
risks.rationale: Processing and manipulating records on the client increases the chance of local exposure.

risks.description: Because access depends on existing PT-FM permissions, any overly broad or misconfigured role could expose FA Tracker records to users who do not need them. The system relies on inherited access controls rather than describing additional fine-grained restrictions within FA Tracker itself.
risks.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
risks.rationale: Inherited access controls can propagate permission errors into the tracker.

risks.description: Contractors with PT-FM access may also obtain FA Tracker access, creating a risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure of USDA-specific data. Even with onboarding controls, contractor access expands the set of people who can view the records.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Broader access by non-federal personnel increases the number of potential privacy failure points.

risks.description: The system includes race, sex, national origin, and disability reporting capability through the shared SCIMS source, which raises sensitivity if such data is exposed or used beyond the intended program purpose. Even if FA Tracker does not list these fields directly, the source system supports them and the data flow can carry sensitive customer information.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Demographic and disability data are highly sensitive and warrant heightened protection.

risks.description: The system depends on replicated SCIMS data and encrypted web-service transfers, so any weakness in replication, web-service security, or authentication could expose customer information in transit or in copied databases. This creates a risk of unauthorized access to the underlying source records.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via the National Planning and Agreements Database (NPAD) [which resides on PT-FM] and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: Replicated databases and network transfers expand the attack surface for PII.

mitigations.description: Limit the work-list view to the minimum fields needed for PSS intervention and keep detailed PT-FM data behind stricter access checks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used to identify and classify Applications, Contracts, and Contract items in need of PSS intervention. FA Tracker does this by running specific queries over the data and displays minimal information to users in the form of work lists.
mitigations.rationale: A minimal display reduces unnecessary exposure while preserving the operational purpose.

mitigations.description: Restrict or disable Excel export unless there is a documented need, and require device-level safeguards for any approved export.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling exports reduces the creation of unmanaged local copies of PII.

mitigations.description: Send e-mail alerts only to authenticated, authorized users and limit the content to the minimum necessary fields, or replace e-mail with in-app notifications where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of PII in e-mail lowers the chance of disclosure through forwarding or mailbox compromise.

mitigations.description: Keep client-side filtering and sorting limited to non-persistent session data and avoid storing results locally in the browser or on the device.
mitigations.rationale: Preventing local persistence reduces the chance that sensitive records remain on the endpoint after the session ends.

mitigations.description: Perform periodic access reviews to confirm that zRoles and PT-FM permissions remain aligned with least privilege for FA Tracker users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps detect and correct overbroad access before it causes disclosure.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing need-to-know approvals, mandatory background investigations, Level 2 eAuthentication, and NDA requirements for contractors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access ... All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management ... Contractors are required to sign NDAs as per the USDA FPAC BC Onboarding process
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the likelihood of contractor misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened access controls and review for any reports or queries involving demographic or disability information drawn from the shared SCIMS source.
mitigations.rationale: Extra controls are appropriate because these data categories are especially sensitive.

mitigations.description: Maintain encryption for web-service transfers and enforce established security rules through eAuth for access to replicated SCIMS data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FA Tracker pulls NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM) data via encrypted web services on the USDA network. ... Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and authenticated access reduce the risk of interception or unauthorized database access.

risks.description: External users can access their program information over the Internet, so a compromised account could expose contact, tax identification, and payment bank information belonging to exporters and financial institutions.
risks.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
risks.rationale: Internet-facing access raises the likelihood that unauthorized parties could reach sensitive program data if credentials are stolen or misused.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which increases the risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse of participant and employee contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
risks.rationale: Each additional class of user expands the number of people who can see sensitive data and the chance of inappropriate access.

risks.description: Nightly files and ad hoc reports create additional copies of system data, increasing the chance that personal or financial information could be exposed through report handling or downstream storage.
risks.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA.
risks.rationale: Replication into files and reports broadens the attack surface and makes accidental disclosure more likely.

risks.description: Internal reports are submitted to auditors and other federal departments, which creates a risk that more information than necessary could be disclosed to recipients outside the original operational need.
risks.evidence_quote: Reports are for internal use only by Government employees and contractors; however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
risks.rationale: Sharing reports with multiple oversight recipients can lead to over-disclosure if the reports are not minimized.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, so personal and financial data remain exposed for a very long time if the data is ever breached or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the duration of exposure and the amount of historical data available to an attacker or unauthorized insider.

risks.description: The system stores tax identification numbers and payment bank information, which are highly sensitive identifiers that could be misused for fraud or financial harm if disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions
risks.rationale: Financial identifiers can be used to facilitate identity theft, payment diversion, or other harmful misuse.

risks.description: The system collects names, email addresses, and phone numbers for multiple external parties, creating a risk of unwanted contact or exposure of business relationships if those details are disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Point of contact names, email addresses, and phone numbers for exporters, US financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks.
risks.rationale: Basic contact data can still harm individuals and organizations when exposed beyond the intended program context.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and role-based access controls for the public GSM interface so users can access only their own program records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to the minimum necessary reduces the chance that a compromised account can reach unrelated records.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary and review contractor permissions regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing contractor access lowers the number of people who can view sensitive system data.

mitigations.description: Restrict report and file access to authorized users and protect nightly extracts and ad hoc reports with access controls and secure handling procedures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling access to derived files and reports reduces the chance of secondary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize report content before submission to auditors and other departments so only the information needed for the stated purpose is disclosed.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces unnecessary disclosure to external recipients.

mitigations.description: Apply periodic records review and purge any records that are no longer required under the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Even with permanent records, regular review helps ensure only approved records remain accessible and properly managed.

mitigations.description: Protect tax identification numbers and payment bank information with encryption and strict access restrictions.
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards are appropriate for highly sensitive financial identifiers.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to contact information to users who need it for program administration and monitor for inappropriate lookup or export activity.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and monitoring reduce the chance that contact details are misused or exposed.

risks.description: The system can hold highly sensitive personal information in uploaded files, so a breach or improper access could expose identifiers, financial data, criminal history, signatures, and other private records.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box contains documents stored in a file repository that may include a wide range of PII. Note: Any PII is stored on files that are uploaded and stored in FPAC Box.
risks.rationale: The broader and more sensitive the stored PII, the greater the privacy harm if it is exposed.

risks.description: Authorized users, contractors, affiliates, and partners can access shared files, creating a risk of overbroad internal or external disclosure beyond what a data subject expects.
risks.evidence_quote: PII information is stored within FPAC Box and shared with authorized USDA employees, contractors, and affiliates with a need-to-know to conduct the business of the organization.
risks.rationale: Any system that relies on multiple human recipients increases the chance of unnecessary access or misuse.

risks.description: External collaboration through a third-party cloud platform can expose PII to vendor-side handling or compromise, especially because the system says the vendor maintains and secures some PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
