risks.rationale: The system shares personal information with third-party vendors for operational purposes, which creates a risk of unnecessary external disclosure.

risks.description: The system may disclose tax identifiers and penalty information to the IRS, creating a risk of exposing highly sensitive identifiers tied to entities and individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB also reports to the IRS information regarding certain fines, penalties, and other amounts levied against entities and individuals resulting from the CFPB’s lawsuits and settlements.
risks.rationale: Tax-reporting disclosures involve sensitive financial and identity-related data that can have higher consequences if mishandled.

risks.description: FOIA release could expose personal information, including names, contact details, and matter details, to the public if records are not carefully reviewed and redacted.
risks.evidence_quote: Information maintained in the Enforcement Matter Management System is shared in accordance with all laws, regulations, policies, and applicable CFPB SORNs, or in response to FOIA requests.
risks.rationale: Public disclosure through FOIA creates a direct privacy risk because the system contains personal and case-related information.

risks.description: Collecting and linking information from consumer complaints, whistleblower tips, public sources, and other agencies can create a privacy risk of using information in ways individuals did not expect when they provided it.
risks.evidence_quote: Enforcement relies on a number of sources of information to identify potential activities that may warrant opening an investigation, including: • Consumer complaints; • The Bureau’s whistleblower hotline; • Referrals from federal regulators and other local, state, and federal agencies; • Market intelligence; and • The results of supervisory exams.
risks.rationale: The system aggregates information from many sources, which can expand context and secondary use beyond the original collection purpose.

risks.description: The system may retain personal data across the full matter lifecycle, including closed matters and linked documents, increasing the chance of prolonged exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The system allows users to create, track, manage, and report on enforcement matters throughout their lifecycle.
risks.rationale: Long-lived matter records increase the window during which personal information could be accessed or disclosed.

mitigations.description: Limit document uploads and linked records to only the information directly relevant and necessary for the specific enforcement matter, and keep sensitive documents in the separate document storage system when possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected and maintained in the Enforcement Matter Management System allows CFPB Staff to manage investigations and litigation by tracking the activity of an enforcement matter throughout the matter lifecycle.
mitigations.rationale: The system is already described as supporting matter management, so minimizing what is stored in the matter record reduces exposure of sensitive documents and PII.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based, need-to-know access controls for reports and ENForce data, with periodic review of who has access to internal reports and cross-program access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB distributes reports derived from the system internally only to CFPB Staff with a need to know to carry out their assigned job responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: The stated need-to-know limitation can be strengthened by regular access reviews to reduce unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict the FTC module to the limited information necessary for coordination and apply access logging and periodic audits of FTC and CFPB user activity in the shared portal.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This limited information on FTC enforcement matters is designed to support coordination between the CFPB and FTC, consistent with the governing coordination MOU.
mitigations.rationale: Because the system already says the module is limited and secured, logging and audits are a natural control to verify that limitation is followed.

mitigations.description: Share only the minimum personal information needed with court reporting vendors and use contractual privacy and security requirements for those vendors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the PII sharing is necessary for scheduling and documenting participants.
mitigations.rationale: The system already states the purpose is limited to scheduling and documenting participants, so vendor limits should match that narrow purpose.

mitigations.description: Transmit tax-reporting data to the IRS only when required and limit the shared fields to the specific information needed for reporting obligations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is publishing this updated PIA to document the collection and use of the TIN for transparency.
mitigations.rationale: The PIA itself identifies TIN collection as tied to tax reporting, so limiting the shared tax data to that obligation reduces sensitivity.

mitigations.description: Apply FOIA review procedures that redact personal information not required for disclosure before any public release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information maintained in the Enforcement Matter Management System is shared in accordance with all laws, regulations, policies, and applicable CFPB SORNs, or in response to FOIA requests.
mitigations.rationale: The input does not state a specific FOIA redaction step, but such review is necessary to prevent unnecessary public disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use data minimization and purpose limitation when pulling in consumer complaints, whistleblower tips, public records, and other agency data, so only information relevant to the matter is stored and used.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CFPB only collects information that is relevant and necessary to investigating potential violations of federal consumer financial law and pursuing administrative or civil enforcement actions.
mitigations.rationale: The system already states a relevance-and-necessity standard, which directly mitigates overcollection and secondary use risk.

mitigations.description: Apply retention schedules and disposition rules to closed matter records and linked documents so personal information is not kept longer than needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system allows users to create, track, manage, and report on enforcement matters throughout their lifecycle.
mitigations.rationale: The input describes lifecycle management but does not state retention limits, so a retention schedule would reduce prolonged exposure.

risks.description: Geocoding and mapping consumer data can expose sensitive location-linked personal information about borrowers and applicants, especially when home addresses are combined with demographic and loan data.
risks.evidence_quote: The data used by the GIS technology includes information, including personally identifiable information (PII), previously collected by CFPB programs such as location of loans (e.g., home or business address), loan application/borrower information, bank branch locations, address of loan applications, and analysis of trends and actions associated with type of loans
risks.rationale: Combining exact locations with loan and demographic attributes increases the privacy impact if the data is mishandled or overexposed.

risks.description: Internal sharing of geocoded outputs across users, teams, and programs could expose consumer data to staff who do not need the full underlying details for their work.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to data that is geocoded by the GIS technology, such as HMDA data, may be granted to Bureau users who request it and have a business purpose or need to know.
risks.rationale: Broader internal access increases the chance that more people than necessary can see sensitive location-based information.

risks.description: Contractors and other authorized GIS users may have access to consumer data, creating a risk of improper disclosure or misuse by non-employees.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized GIS users are comprised of Bureau employees and contractors.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond employees increases the number of parties who must be trusted to handle PII appropriately.

risks.description: Publishing aggregated GIS outputs could still allow re-identification or indirect disclosure if the maps or trend analyses are too detailed for small geographic areas or niche populations.
risks.evidence_quote: The GIS technology output may be shared, in aggregate, in various publications and to support regulatory requirements, as appropriate.
risks.rationale: Even aggregate geospatial results can reveal sensitive patterns when the geography is narrow or the population is small.

risks.description: PII is retained on the GIS server until final output is transmitted, which creates a temporary storage risk if the server is compromised or if deletion does not occur as intended.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII is retained on the server for analysis until the final output is transmitted to permanent program-appropriate data storage on the CFPB network.
risks.rationale: Any period of retained PII increases exposure if unauthorized access or a security incident occurs before deletion.

risks.description: Staff account data used for authentication, support, billing, and audit logging creates a risk of collecting and retaining more employee information than necessary for GIS use.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII collected regarding CFPB Staff is required to create user accounts, manage billing, authenticate users, provide support, and deliver specialized services. The information is also used in audit logs that may be used to verify compliance with the CFPB’s privacy and security policies.
risks.rationale: Operational account data can become privacy-sensitive when it is retained in logs and administrative records.

risks.description: Data imported from multiple CFPB source systems and hosted in on-premise and AWS environments may be exposed if transfers or integrations are not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: They include, but are not limited to, the CFPB’s systems for the HMDA program, SBL program, RMR, SUP, and ENF. These Bureau systems are maintained within on-premise servers and within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) hosted cloud.
risks.rationale: Moving data across several systems and hosting environments increases the number of places where it could be mishandled.

risks.description: Role-based access controls may still allow excessive access if roles are assigned too broadly or not reviewed regularly.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB employs role-based access controls. The CFPB uses role-based access controls to ensure CFPB Staff only have access to the system and/or information necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Role-based controls reduce risk only when permissions are accurate and kept current.

risks.description: Future integration of the online/public portals could increase exposure if public-facing functions are enabled before privacy controls and release standards are fully applied.
risks.evidence_quote: As part of this Enterprise deployment, the CFPB will enable the GIS Enterprise technology mentioned above. The online component will be integrated in the future for specific use cases and will be documented in separate privacy impact assessment (PIA) appendices or updates.
risks.rationale: Adding public or broader online functionality typically expands the privacy attack surface and should be controlled carefully.

mitigations.description: Limit GIS inputs to the location data and other fields strictly needed for the specific analysis, and delete PII from the GIS server within a week after final output is transmitted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the information used by GIS technology is limited to the location data needed to execute the required output or analysis. ... Within a week after the final output has been transmitted, the PII is deleted from the GIS server.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing inputs and promptly deleting PII reduces the amount of sensitive location-linked data at risk.

mitigations.description: Keep outputs in private folders and only add additional users when a specific collaborative need is documented.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In the desktop instance, outputs are stored in private folders on the CFPB network that are only accessible by the user and GIS administrators. However, a user can request an administrator to add an additional user to a private folder for collaborative purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to private folders limits unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply the existing role-based access controls to contractors and review contractor permissions to ensure they are limited to assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB employs role-based access controls to ensure CFPB Staff only have access to the system and/or information necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Extending least-privilege review to contractors reduces the risk of improper access by non-employees.

mitigations.description: Release only aggregated and de-identified GIS outputs after they are reviewed on a CFPB on-premise server for disclosure risk.
mitigations.evidence_quote: They CFPB typically only publishes aggregated and de-identified information that includes GIS technology output. Any GIS technology output must first be transmitted back to a CFPB on-premise server where it is analyzed and contextualized before being published or shared.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing and de-identifying outputs before publication lowers the chance of indirect identification.

mitigations.description: Maintain the stated deletion timeline and verify that temporary server copies are removed after final output is transmitted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Within a week after the final output has been transmitted, the PII is deleted from the GIS server.
mitigations.rationale: Verified deletion shortens the window in which retained PII could be exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit staff account data and audit logs to what is needed for authentication, support, billing, and security compliance, and retain them only for the life of the user account.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII collected regarding CFPB Staff is required to create user accounts, manage billing, authenticate users, provide support, and deliver specialized services. The information is also used in audit logs that may be used to verify compliance with the CFPB’s privacy and security policies. This information is retained for the life of the user account.
mitigations.rationale: Narrow retention and purpose limits reduce privacy impact from administrative records.

mitigations.description: Use the existing secure, browser-based enterprise environment and FedRAMP Moderate-certified online instance for hosted components and keep transfers between source systems and GIS tightly controlled.
mitigations.evidence_quote: provides a secure, browser-based enterprise system that allows users to control, store, and access data. ... The online instance of the GIS tool is FedRAMP Moderate certified and provided through Amazon Web Services (AWS).
mitigations.rationale: Using secured and certified environments reduces risk during storage and processing across systems.

mitigations.description: Regularly review role assignments so users keep only the access necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB uses role-based access controls to ensure CFPB Staff only have access to the system and/or information necessary and relevant to their assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review is needed to keep least-privilege controls effective over time.

mitigations.description: Document future online or public portal integrations in separate PIA updates before deployment and apply publication standards for any public output.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The online component will be integrated in the future for specific use cases and will be documented in separate privacy impact assessment (PIA) appendices or updates.
mitigations.rationale: Requiring updated privacy review before new functionality goes live helps prevent unreviewed exposure.

risks.description: The system collects and stores sensitive identifiers that could cause harm if exposed, including Social Security numbers and other government-issued identity numbers. Because the database also contains names, dates of birth, and contact information, a breach could enable identity theft or unwanted contact.
risks.evidence_quote: The Directory Database includes PII regarding employees or others associated with institutions under the CFPB’s authority, including: • Name; • Age and date of birth • Contact information such as address, email address, and phone number; • Social Security number (SSN), alien number, passport number, driver’s license or state identification number, or other unique number used to establish identity of the owner or responsible person;
risks.rationale: The presence of direct identifiers and government identity numbers increases the harm from unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The database is searchable by personal identifier, which increases the risk of broad internal or external lookup and retrieval of records about a person. Searchability by name and other identifiers can make it easier to compile profiles or find records that were not otherwise expected to be linked.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Information in ConsumerFinance.gov is searchable by PII, including: • Name; • Age and date of birth; • Contact information such as address, email address, and phone number; • Social Security number (SSN), alien number, passport number, driver’s license or state identification number, or other unique number used to establish identity of the owner or responsible person)
risks.rationale: Searchable PII makes it easier to locate and misuse records tied to a specific person.

risks.description: The CFPB may collect personal information from third parties and other agencies without individuals receiving actual notice, which can reduce transparency and make it harder for people to understand or challenge the collection. This creates a risk of unexpected collection and use of personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: In such cases, individuals may not receive actual notice that the CFPB has collected information about them.
risks.rationale: Lack of actual notice can leave people unaware that their data is being collected and used.

risks.description: The system may contain inaccurate or incomplete records because the CFPB presently gathers information from multiple sources and does not take steps to verify the accuracy or completeness of such data. Inaccurate directory information could affect supervisory, regulatory, or enforcement actions and could misidentify individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB presently gathers the information from federal, state, and local data sources and does not take steps to verify the accuracy or completeness of such data.
risks.rationale: Unverified records can lead to incorrect decisions and mistaken associations with individuals or institutions.

risks.description: Information collected from individuals, institutions, federal and state agencies, social media, consumer inquiries, and complaints may be used to confirm or combine records across sources, increasing the risk of overcollection or unexpected secondary use. Even though the system says it will not exclusively rely on those sources, the multi-source approach can still expand the amount of data held about a person.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB will also identify financial products and service providers through a variety of other channels, including third party research, social media, consumer inquiries or complaints, correspondence from the public, etc.
risks.rationale: Pulling data from many channels can increase the volume and sensitivity of information tied to a person.

risks.description: Internal reports can reveal names and contact information to employees who may not need the full record, creating a risk of unnecessary internal disclosure. Even though access is limited to a bona fide need, reports may still expose personal details to a broader set of staff than is strictly necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may generate reports from the Directory Database as necessary. For example, such reports may include a list of names and contact information for organizations under the CFPB’s supervision
risks.rationale: Reports that include personal contact details can expose data beyond the minimum needed for a task.

risks.description: External sharing with supervised institutions and other state or federal agencies creates a risk that personal information will be disclosed outside the CFPB. Even with secure transmission and data sharing agreements, the more recipients that receive reports, the greater the chance of misuse or mishandling.
risks.evidence_quote: Externally, the Bureau may disclose reports to a limited group of employees at an institution being supervised and, as necessary, to other state and federal agency employees whose job functions allow them to review the information contained in such reports.
risks.rationale: Each external disclosure increases the chance of unauthorized access or secondary use.

risks.description: The Directory Database is a central repository that other CFPB systems may connect to or derive information from, which increases the risk that data will spread across systems and be accessed in more places than intended. Future incorporation of NMLS elements also creates change-management and integration risk if controls are not updated.
risks.evidence_quote: Other systems within the CFPB may connect to or derive information from the Directory Database to perform any of their functions, like supervision, enforcement, or consumer education and engagement.
risks.rationale: System-to-system propagation can broaden access and make privacy controls harder to enforce consistently.

risks.description: The system retains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves a disposition schedule, which can keep personal data available far longer than necessary. Long retention increases the chance of later misuse, breach, or outdated information remaining in circulation.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Longer retention extends the window in which data can be exposed or become stale.

risks.description: Some information may be maintained in paper form in locked cabinets or rooms, which still creates a risk of physical access if controls fail or are bypassed. Physical records can be copied or viewed without the same technical logging and access controls as the electronic system.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of the information in the Directory Database may also be maintained in locked file cabinets or rooms with access limited to those personnel require access as part of their official duties.
risks.rationale: Paper records are vulnerable to physical mishandling and less-detectable disclosure.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to authorized personnel with a bona fide need, use non-transferrable access codes and passwords, and require privacy and confidentiality training.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB grants Directory Database access only to authorized personnel who have been issued non-transferrable access codes and passwords and have completed appropriate training on confidentiality and privacy.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and training users reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit access to PII in reports on a need-to-know basis and provide only the minimum information required for the task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Even then, CFPB employees only have access to the PII contained within these reports to the extent that they need to see it to perform their jobs.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the amount of searchable personal data visible to each user.

mitigations.description: Provide constructive notice through the PIA and SORN when actual notice is not feasible, and clearly describe the collection practices.
mitigations.evidence_quote: However, this PIA and the associated SORN, CFPB.007 –Directory Database, provide constructive notice of the CFPB’s information collection practices.
mitigations.rationale: Constructive notice helps address transparency gaps when direct notice is not provided.

mitigations.description: Verify information where practicable by contacting supervised institutions and individuals or using third-party data sources, and allow individuals to amend or correct records through the Privacy Act process.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB will attempt, where practicable to verify the accuracy and completeness of such information by contacting supervised institutions and individuals or by using third party data sources. The CFPB also offers a means through the Privacy Act for individuals to amend or correct CFPB records that pertain to them.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction rights help reduce the impact of inaccurate records.

mitigations.description: Use third-party and public-source information only to confirm information gathered from other sources rather than relying on it as the sole basis for records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB will not exclusively rely upon the data it gathers from these sources; rather, it will use the data to confirm the accuracy of information gathered from other sources.
mitigations.rationale: Using external sources for confirmation rather than primary collection limits overreliance on potentially noisy data.

mitigations.description: Distribute internal reports only to employees with a bona fide need and keep report access limited to the minimum necessary PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Bureau distributes its reports internally only to employees with a bona fide need for such reports to carry out their assigned job responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting report distribution lowers unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Share reports externally only through secure channels such as encrypted email and only with appropriate data sharing agreements in place.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share PII from the Directory Database externally, under certain circumstances, through secure channels, such as encrypted email, with appropriate data sharing agreements in place.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transmission and agreements reduce the risk of unauthorized external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Document any future enhancements, including external-facing connections, in future PIA updates before deployment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB will document any future enhancements to the Directory Database, including external facing connections, in future PIA updates for the system.
mitigations.rationale: Documenting future integrations helps ensure privacy review before data flows expand.

mitigations.description: Dispose of records according to an approved NARA records disposition schedule once available, rather than retaining them indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Following a disposition schedule reduces the duration of exposure for personal information.

mitigations.description: Keep paper records in locked file cabinets or rooms with access limited to personnel who require access as part of their official duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Some of the information in the Directory Database may also be maintained in locked file cabinets or rooms with access limited to those personnel require access as part of their official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Physical safeguards help prevent unauthorized viewing or copying of paper records.

risks.description: Users may disclose directly identifiable contact information or other personal details to a public website, creating a risk of unwanted exposure if they do not understand what is public.
risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
risks.rationale: The site collects identifiable and potentially revealing information from a public-facing service, so disclosure can occur if users share more than they intend.

risks.description: User comments, videos, links, and images may be made public and can reveal sensitive personal or financial information beyond what the user expected.
risks.evidence_quote: Depending on how you use ConsumerFinance.gov, you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly allows some user-provided information to become public, which can expose personal details or opinions.

risks.description: Website usage data and analytics may enable tracking or profiling of users across visits, especially when combined with other information collected by the site.
risks.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov to be able to inform future changes and upgrades to the site based on former trends and behaviors, and possibly add new resources or products when there is a demand.
risks.rationale: Even aggregate analytics can create privacy risk if visit patterns are linked back to individuals or devices.

risks.description: Information submitted through ConsumerFinance.gov may flow into the online complaint intake system, creating a risk that users do not realize their data is being used beyond the website itself.
risks.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system.
risks.rationale: A pathway from the website to another system increases the chance of unexpected secondary use or sharing.

risks.description: Demographic and consumer-product information collected about users and others may be more sensitive than ordinary web-usage data and could expose financial circumstances or characteristics.
risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used
risks.rationale: This data can reveal financial behavior or personal characteristics, which increases privacy impact if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: The site may collect directly identifiable PII if users knowingly provide it, so there is a risk of collecting more personal information than necessary for the public education purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
risks.rationale: Voluntary submission still creates a minimization risk if users provide unnecessary identifiers.

mitigations.description: Provide prominent, plain-language notice before submission explaining what information is collected, what may be public, and how users can limit disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps users make informed choices before sharing identifiable information.

mitigations.description: Give users strong controls to limit how much of their submitted content is made public and default to the least-public setting possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Depending on how you use ConsumerFinance.gov, you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting public exposure reduces the chance that user-generated content is unnecessarily disclosed.

mitigations.description: Minimize analytics collection and use only aggregated traffic data, with safeguards to prevent linking analytics data to individuals.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation reduces the likelihood that browsing behavior can be tied to a specific person.

mitigations.description: Tell users when information submitted on the website will be routed to the online complaint intake system and separate complaint-related data from general website activity where feasible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system.
mitigations.rationale: Specific notice and separation of data flows reduce surprise and unintended secondary use.

mitigations.description: Collect only the demographic and consumer-product information needed for the stated public education purpose and avoid unnecessary detail.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization lowers the sensitivity and impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use form design and submission warnings to discourage unnecessary entry of directly identifiable PII and collect it only when essential.
mitigations.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary identifier collection limits the amount of personal data at risk.

risks.description: The system collects and transmits highly sensitive personal data, including Social Security numbers, health records, driver’s license numbers, home addresses, and personal credit card information, creating a risk of harm if that data is exposed or misused. Because the same system also stores and transmits these records, a breach could affect both accident and sales participants.
risks.evidence_quote: The following PII information (data elements for accident investigation and recovery) for non government entities include: ... Health records ... Driver’s License Number ... Personal credit card information ... GSAFleet.gov collects, transmits, and stores social security numbers.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the collected data increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Social Security numbers are sent to an external credit bureau for creditworthiness checks, which creates a risk of unnecessary disclosure and secondary use outside the original GSAFleet.gov context. This external transmission expands the number of parties handling the most sensitive identifier in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Social security numbers are transmitted to Experian to determine a user's credit worthiness to purchase a vehicle.
risks.rationale: Sending SSNs to a third party increases exposure risk and makes control over downstream use harder.

risks.description: Accident records are created from police reports and other third-party sources, so the system may hold inaccurate or incomplete personal data about individuals. The context also says there is no other cross verification for some non-government third-party information.
risks.evidence_quote: It is the responsibility of the individual or the police report that provides this information ... No other cross verification is done for non-government 3rd party information collected where 3rd party is responsible for the accident.
risks.rationale: Reliance on third-party reports without broader verification can lead to incorrect records that affect individuals' rights and claims.

risks.description: The system aggregates personal data across accident management, vehicle sales, and external systems, which can create more detailed profiles about individuals than any single transaction requires. The PIA explicitly says the system will create or aggregate new data about the individual.
risks.evidence_quote: Will the system, application, or project create or aggregate new data about the individual? Yes
risks.rationale: Aggregation increases the risk of profiling and broader use of personal information than the person may expect.

risks.description: Accident documents are transferred to EDMS and stored there, and some information is also sent to OCFO/FMESB, creating multiple storage and transmission points that increase the chance of unauthorized access or disclosure. The more systems that handle the same records, the harder it is to control access and retention consistently.
risks.evidence_quote: All PII files are sent securely to EDMS and stored in the EDM Server encrypted. Once transferred to the EDMS server, the information is only accessible by authorized users.
risks.rationale: Each additional system or transfer point expands the attack surface and the number of users who may access the data.

risks.description: The system logs GSA employees and contractors who can log into system transactions, which creates a privacy risk of tracking user activity beyond what is necessary if audit logs are overly detailed or broadly accessible. Audit logs themselves can reveal sensitive operational or behavioral information about users.
risks.evidence_quote: GSA employees or contractors with the ability to log into system transactions are logged via the audit logs.
risks.rationale: Logging user actions is useful for accountability, but it can also expose user activity if not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Individuals may have limited practical ability to decline providing information for accident cases, because the system says an accident case cannot be entered without the required third-party information. This creates a privacy risk of compelled disclosure for people involved in accidents.
risks.evidence_quote: If the third party individual refuses to provide such information, an accident case cannot be entered in GSAFleet.gov.
risks.rationale: When participation is effectively required, individuals have little control over disclosure of their personal data.

risks.description: The system allows individuals to access or amend information through the Accident Management Center, but amendments rely on identity verification using police reports, case numbers, and vehicle information. If that verification is insufficient or misapplied, unauthorized changes or disclosure could occur.
risks.evidence_quote: The AMC will verify the individual’s identity from the police report received and also by case number, vehicle information etc. that was documented for the accident case.
risks.rationale: Identity checks based on case details can be effective, but they also create a risk of mistaken identity or over-disclosure if not rigorously applied.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and storage of sensitive fields to only what is required for the accident or sales process, and keep sensitive documents encrypted in transit and at rest with access restricted to authorized users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The following PII information ... is required for police reports, third-party insurance, and to recover the expenses for an accident/incident in which a 3rd party is at fault.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and protecting sensitive data reduces the impact of any exposure.

mitigations.description: Use the existing encrypted transmission path to Experian and ensure SSNs are shared only for the stated creditworthiness purpose, with annual key updates maintained.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is AES-256 encrypted with a private key updated annually when transmitted to Financial Management Enterprise Services Bus (FMESB), which then decrypts the data on their end.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and purpose limitation reduce the risk of unauthorized disclosure during external sharing.

mitigations.description: Add a formal data review step for accident records that compares police-report data with available source documents before finalizing the case record.
mitigations.rationale: A second review step can catch errors or omissions before inaccurate data is relied on for claims or reporting.

mitigations.description: Separate accident, sales, and management data sets where possible, and restrict cross-component aggregation to personnel with a documented business need.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting aggregation reduces the chance that data from different contexts will be combined into a broader profile.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing encryption and authorized-user controls for EDMS and OCFO transfers, and apply the same controls consistently to any additional systems that receive the records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All PII files are sent securely to EDMS and stored in the EDM Server encrypted. Once transferred to the EDMS server, the information is only accessible by authorized users.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent encryption and access controls reduce the risk created by multiple storage locations.

mitigations.description: Restrict audit-log access to authorized security and privacy personnel and limit the log fields to what is necessary for accountability.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting log visibility and content reduces the privacy impact of monitoring user activity.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice to third parties that the information is required to complete the case and that refusal may prevent the case from being entered.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The third party individual is required to provide the PII information need to complete the case/claim.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps individuals understand the consequences of not providing the information.

mitigations.description: Continue verifying amendment requests through the Accident Management Center and require corroborating case details before any change is made.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GSAFleet.gov users have the ability to amend PII by submitting an email request, written request or by phone call to the GSA Fleet Accident Management Center (AMC).
mitigations.rationale: Identity and case-detail verification help ensure that only the correct person can alter records.

risks.description: The system may expose highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers if unauthorized users gain access to the case files or documents. The stored data includes SSNs, claim numbers, military serial numbers, birth dates, and bank routing and account numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: That may include additional personally identifiable information (PII) information, Social Security Number (SSN), annuitant claim numbers, compensation claim numbers, insurance account numbers, insurance claim numbers, military serial numbers, birth date, financial institution routing number, and financial institution account number.
risks.rationale: These data elements can cause significant harm if disclosed because they can be used for identity theft, fraud, or account compromise.

risks.description: Linking all inquiries submitted by or on behalf of the same constituent can reveal a broader profile of that person than is necessary for a single inquiry. This increases the privacy impact if the linked case file is accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also links together all the inquiries submitted by or on behalf of the same constituent.
risks.rationale: Combining multiple matters into one profile increases the amount of personal information exposed in any single access event.

risks.description: The system stores communications and documents from multiple parties, which may include additional PII about respondents, constituents, and others who are not the primary subject of the inquiry. This can expose bystanders and third parties whose information is incidentally collected.
risks.evidence_quote: This may also include legal, administrative, or similar non-public agency records relevant to the inquiry. These communications and documents can include additional PII about the respondent, constituent, and others.
risks.rationale: Third-party information can be collected without those individuals directly engaging with the system, so disclosure risk extends beyond the intended subject.

risks.description: Storing full inquiry histories, correspondence, and supporting documents can create an over-collection and over-retention risk if information is kept longer than needed for the inquiry. The system describes no retention limit in the provided context.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking creates a new case file for each inquiry. It tracks the receipt and processing of the inquiry, records connected to the inquiry, relevant inquiry and any records gathered to help respond). OLA Tracking also stores all communications and documents connected to the inquiry.
risks.rationale: A complete case file can accumulate more personal information than is necessary, increasing the harm from any later access or breach.

risks.description: Because staffers can submit inquiries and documents through a web portal, the system may be exposed to unauthorized account access if authentication or account approval is bypassed or misused. The portal is a gateway to sensitive constituent information.
risks.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
risks.rationale: A portal that handles sensitive case information depends on strong access control, and any weakness could expose many records at once.

risks.description: Using cloud-based Microsoft services introduces a risk that sensitive case data could be exposed through misconfiguration, vendor access, or other cloud handling issues. The system relies on Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.evidence_quote: The new system uses a cloud-version of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems can increase the number of technical and administrative paths through which sensitive data may be exposed.

risks.description: Sharing inquiries and records with other federal agencies or external parties to help answer the inquiry can disclose personal information beyond OPM staff. The system explicitly includes communications with other parties that may have information to help answer the inquiry.
risks.evidence_quote: This may include letters, emails, and attachments between OPM and the staffer, constitution, or other parties that may have information to help answer the inquiry (e.g., other federal agencies).
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient or exchange increases the chance that sensitive information is disclosed outside the original collecting context.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive identifiers and financial data to only staff who need them for the inquiry, and apply strong encryption for data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting the data technically reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize cross-case linking by separating inquiries unless a shared record is operationally necessary, and limit visibility of linked cases to authorized staff.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary linkage limits how much of a constituent's history is exposed in any one case.

mitigations.description: Redact or segregate incidental third-party PII in documents and correspondence before storing or sharing them, unless that information is required to resolve the inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: This lowers the chance that information about unrelated individuals is retained or disclosed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce a records retention schedule that removes case files and attachments when no longer needed for the inquiry or applicable records requirements.
mitigations.rationale: A retention schedule prevents indefinite accumulation of sensitive information in case files.

mitigations.description: Continue requiring multifactor authentication and manual approval for staffer accounts, and review access rights regularly to ensure only authorized users can use the portal.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
mitigations.rationale: The stated controls directly reduce the risk of unauthorized portal access.

mitigations.description: Apply cloud security controls such as configuration management, least-privilege administration, logging, and vendor oversight for the Microsoft cloud services used by the system.
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the chance that cloud-hosted data is exposed through misconfiguration or inappropriate access.

mitigations.description: Limit external sharing to only the minimum information needed to answer the inquiry and track disclosures to other agencies or parties.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing shared content and tracking disclosures reduces unnecessary exposure to external recipients.

risks.description: ROVR holds highly sensitive health and benefits information that could harm individuals if exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program
risks.rationale: The system centralizes identifiable health-related and enrollment data about large populations, increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: Linking record-level identifiable data into person-level longitudinal records increases the risk of re-identification and detailed profiling over time.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
risks.rationale: Combining data over time makes it easier to identify individuals and infer their health and coverage history.

risks.description: Using the repository for broad analysis across population groups, geographic areas, providers, and disease conditions can reveal sensitive patterns about individuals and small groups.
risks.evidence_quote: These analyses may include examination of the cost of care, utilization of services, and comparing these across specific population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions.
risks.rationale: Even when the purpose is administrative, subgroup analysis can expose sensitive information about health status or utilization patterns.

risks.description: Fraud, waste, and abuse investigations may lead to targeted review of specific enrollees' claims and payments beyond ordinary administrative use.
risks.evidence_quote: the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
risks.rationale: Fraud-related use can create additional scrutiny of individuals whose records are flagged by analytic patterns.

risks.description: Enrollment reconciliation can expose mistaken or exceptional dual coverage situations, which may reveal sensitive coverage details about individuals and family members.
risks.evidence_quote: enrollment data may reveal instances where an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract.
risks.rationale: Detecting multiple coverage relationships can disclose personal insurance circumstances that individuals may not expect to be broadly visible.

risks.description: External data sharing with other federal agencies and systems creates a risk of disclosure beyond the originating purpose or environment.
risks.evidence_quote: other Federal agencies through data sharing agreements.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the number of places where the data may be accessed, retained, or mishandled.

risks.description: Sharing Medicare-related claims and service-use data with CMS and the clearinghouse expands the number of entities handling linked health information.
risks.evidence_quote: Centers for Medicare Clearinghouse System (CLER) operated for OPM by NFC ... and Medicaid Services (CMS) provides service use and cost data3 to OPM, including health claims information for FEHB enrollees and their eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare programs.
risks.rationale: Cross-system exchange of claims data increases the chance of inconsistent handling or unauthorized access across organizations.

risks.description: The system's broad analytical and policy uses may create secondary use concerns if data are applied to decisions affecting individuals beyond the stated administrative purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM may also use the data to assess the effects of new policy and legislative initiatives to improve its assessment of FEHB plan performance.
risks.rationale: When data are used for policy evaluation as well as administration, there is a risk that analysis could influence decisions in ways individuals did not anticipate.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the repository to personnel with a documented need to know and apply strong access controls to all PII and claims data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that sensitive health and enrollment data will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified or aggregated data whenever possible and keep record-level identifiable data only when longitudinal linking is necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data, OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
mitigations.rationale: The system already states that non-identifiable data are used for much analysis, which reduces re-identification risk.

mitigations.description: Apply minimum-cell-size and other disclosure-avoidance controls when reporting subgroup, geographic, provider, or disease-condition analyses.
mitigations.rationale: Disclosure controls reduce the chance that small-group analysis will reveal sensitive information about identifiable people.

mitigations.description: Use fraud, waste, and abuse flags only as triggers for limited review and document any follow-up access to individual records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting follow-up to documented, authorized review helps prevent unnecessary scrutiny of individuals.

mitigations.description: Confine dual-enrollment reconciliation to the smallest necessary set of staff and use it only for correcting coverage errors or permitted exceptions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, such an occurrence would be identified and addressed outside of ROVR, but data from ROVR may be used as part of the analysis.
mitigations.rationale: The context indicates dual enrollment issues are generally handled outside the repository, which supports limiting exposure within ROVR.

mitigations.description: Ensure every external data-sharing arrangement includes explicit use, storage, and retention limits and verify compliance with those limits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agreements constitute the methods of use and applicable retention and storage protocols.
mitigations.rationale: The system already relies on agreements to govern handling, which is a direct control for external sharing risk.

mitigations.description: Apply the same privacy and security requirements to CMS and clearinghouse exchanges as are used internally, including transmission protections and role-based access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Pursuant to an Information Exchange Agreement (IEA), Centers for Medicare Clearinghouse System (CLER) operated for OPM by NFC ... and Medicaid Services (CMS) provides service use and cost data3 to OPM
mitigations.rationale: Cross-agency exchange should be protected to the same standard as internal handling to reduce disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict policy and legislative analysis to aggregated results unless identifiable data are strictly necessary for the stated administrative purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred
mitigations.rationale: The system already states that individual-level use is generally limited, which supports keeping policy analysis aggregated.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive identifiers and debt information that could cause harm if exposed, including SSNs, mailing addresses, debt amounts, and tracking numbers tied to individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: it uses HR data of federal employees who have outstanding debts, including their name, their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).
risks.rationale: A breach of this data could enable identity theft, financial harm, and unwanted disclosure of debt status.

risks.description: Many USDA agencies can access the data, which increases the chance that more users than necessary may see debtor information.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users of approximately 35 USDA agencies have access to this data.
risks.rationale: Broader access increases the attack surface and the risk of inappropriate internal disclosure.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse by non-federal personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized by agency functional manager and submitted by the agency security officer.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the set of people who can see personal and financial information.

risks.description: Data is transmitted between agencies and to external recipients over network connections, which creates interception or misrouting risk during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via connect direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection.
risks.rationale: Even with secure channels, data in transit can be exposed if controls fail or are misconfigured.

risks.description: ABCO shares debtor information with external Treasury systems and a records contractor, which could disclose personal data outside USDA beyond what individuals expect.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO provides data to the following:  Department of Treasury – Treasury Offset Program  Department of Treasury – Intra Governmental Payment and Collection System  Iron Mountain - Digital Records Center for Images System
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient creates another point where personal data may be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data, so they may be unable to review or correct inaccurate debt records that affect them.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Without individual access, errors in debt or identity data may persist and affect collection actions.

risks.description: The system retains mainframe data indefinitely, which increases the amount of personal information exposed over time and raises long-term misuse risk.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Long retention keeps personal data available for longer than necessary and increases cumulative exposure.

risks.description: The system uses personal data to generate notices without prior notice to the individual, which can reduce transparency about how debt information is used.
risks.evidence_quote: Was notice provided to the individual prior to collection of information? No. The ABCO system uses personal data provided by agencies to generate reports or notices.
risks.rationale: Lack of prior notice limits individuals' awareness of how their information is being processed.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs and other direct identifiers to the minimum necessary for billing and collections, and mask them wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of direct identifiers lowers the harm if records are accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing least privilege and periodically review each agency user's access to ensure only the minimum required data is available.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least Privacy Impact Assessment Administrative Billings and Collections System (ABCO) Page 7 privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces unnecessary internal viewing of debtor records.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be time-limited, role-specific, and logged, with additional review before access is granted.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the risk from non-federal access to sensitive financial data.

mitigations.description: Maintain encrypted transport for all file transfers and add transmission logging and integrity checks for agency and external exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via connect direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and integrity controls reduce the chance of interception or tampering in transit.

mitigations.description: Apply data-sharing agreements and recipient-specific access limits so external recipients receive only the fields needed for their authorized purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NFC maintains and secures the information on behalf of our customers.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting what each recipient gets reduces the privacy impact of external sharing.

mitigations.description: Provide a controlled process for individuals to request access or correction through their employing agency or records owner.
mitigations.rationale: A correction path helps ensure debt records remain accurate even when direct individual access is unavailable.

mitigations.description: Apply a finite retention schedule to the mainframe copy and periodically purge records that are no longer required by the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA General Records Schedule GRS-1-1 (Financial Management and Reporting Records).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Provide notice to individuals when debt data is collected or used for notices, or ensure the employing agency gives clear notice on ABCO's behalf.
mitigations.rationale: Notice improves transparency and lets individuals understand how their debt information is being used.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal information than is necessary because correspondence can include additional information voluntarily provided by the individual beyond basic contact details. This creates a risk of overcollection of public PII in letters and attachments.
risks.evidence_quote: In a few cases, it may also include other information about the individual voluntarily provided by that individual in the correspondence.
risks.rationale: Voluntary correspondence can contain unnecessary sensitive details that are not needed to process the request.

risks.description: Using NLP and machine learning on historical correspondence can expose personal information to broader analytical processing than needed for handling a specific request. The system may infer or surface information from similar inquiries in ways that expand use of the data.
risks.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
risks.rationale: Automated analysis increases the scope of processing beyond the original correspondence transaction.

risks.description: Centralized access to package records, metadata, and workflow tracking creates a risk that more USDA users and user groups can view personal correspondence information than necessary. Movement of packages between users increases the chance of unauthorized or excessive internal disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: AgWrite supports the OES mission by providing a centralized system where users can access and interact with information to promote expedient facilitation of correspondence receipt and processing.
risks.rationale: A centralized workflow system can broaden internal exposure if access controls are not tightly limited.

risks.description: The system may retain and expose physical and email addresses and phone numbers for correspondence purposes even when those details are not needed for the substantive response. This creates a risk that contact information is maintained longer or more broadly than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes. Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Contact details are directly identifying and should be minimized to what is needed for the transaction.

risks.description: Tracking the movement of packages, status, priority, and processing times can create detailed records about individuals' interactions with USDA. Those operational metadata may reveal sensitive information about congressional inquiries or the nature of a person's request.
risks.evidence_quote: Search data produced could pertain to correspondence as they progress through workflows within the system (e.g., stage/status agency, priority or categorization, time in a particular status, time to progress from initiated to completed, congressional inquiries, etc.).
risks.rationale: Workflow metadata can be privacy-sensitive even when the correspondence content itself is not disclosed.

risks.description: The system may be used to document proposed policies and program activities for approval by USDA officials, which could expose correspondence-derived personal information to decision makers who do not need the individual's identity. This creates a risk of secondary use beyond answering the original correspondence.
risks.evidence_quote: Other information in the system will be used to document proposed policies and program activities for approval by USDA officials.
risks.rationale: Reusing correspondence information for policy documentation expands the original purpose of collection.

mitigations.description: Limit intake and review procedures to collect only the minimum personal information needed to process the correspondence, and redact or exclude unnecessary details from the record where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted to ensure that personally identifiable information (PII) voluntarily provided by public individuals and organizations is properly safeguarded and controlled while being handled and managed in the system.
mitigations.rationale: Minimization directly reduces the amount of unnecessary personal information entering the system.

mitigations.description: Restrict NLP and ML outputs to correspondence-processing purposes and review search results so they do not expose unnecessary personal details from historical content.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting analytical use and reviewing outputs reduces the chance that automated processing reveals more personal information than needed.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls so users and user groups can only access the package records and metadata needed for their assigned correspondence tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The new system will implement advanced technology to transform how correspondence is processed in OES, supporting standardized processes and role-based access.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the number of people who can view personal correspondence information.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and retention limits to contact details, keeping physical addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers only as long as needed to complete the correspondence process.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention of contact data reduces the risk of unnecessary long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit reporting and dashboard access to aggregated or task-specific workflow data whenever possible, and avoid displaying identifiers in status reports unless necessary for processing.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the granularity of workflow reporting lowers the privacy impact of operational metadata.

mitigations.description: Separate correspondence records used for policy approval from direct identifiers where possible, and only provide USDA officials the minimum information needed for approval decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation and selective disclosure help prevent secondary use of personal information.

risks.description: Sensitive discrimination and employee complaint information could be exposed if unauthorized parties gain access to the web-based system or its internet-connected environment. The system holds complaint records with personal identifiers and is connected to the public Internet through a managed gateway.
risks.evidence_quote: The information includes complaints of discrimination against USDA programs and services and employee complaints. It uses complainant personal information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and miscellaneous identification numbers (generates a case number). ... The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway
risks.rationale: A web-facing environment holding complaint PII increases the harm if access controls or perimeter defenses fail.

risks.description: Contractor access could broaden the number of people able to view complaint PII, increasing the chance of misuse or accidental disclosure. The system explicitly allows Department contractors to access CRES.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? YES
risks.rationale: Each additional class of user increases insider-risk and the need for strict access governance.

risks.description: Access may be granted too broadly or inconsistently because user access levels are determined by management rather than described role-based rules. This could expose complaint data to staff who do not need it for their duties.
risks.evidence_quote: The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES.
risks.rationale: Without explicit least-privilege controls, access decisions can become overbroad or uneven.

risks.description: Complaint information may be collected through email, telephone, mail, and interviews without a stated secure intake method, which can expose PII during collection and transfer into the system. The system says the information is then inputted by approved users, but does not describe protections for the intake channels.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
risks.rationale: Unprotected intake channels can leak PII before it ever reaches the system.

risks.description: The system retains complaint files for an unclear period because the retention description is vague, which can keep PII longer than necessary and increase exposure over time. The stated retention basis is not specific enough to show when records are actually destroyed.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES’s files are destroyed, based on the judicial’ s regulations.
risks.rationale: Longer or unclear retention increases the amount of data available to be breached or misused.

risks.description: The system relies on approved users and contractors, but the description does not state whether logging, monitoring, or auditing is used to detect inappropriate access. That creates a risk that unauthorized viewing of complaint records could go unnoticed.
risks.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
risks.rationale: Access control alone is weaker if the system cannot detect or investigate misuse.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong perimeter security and secure web access controls for the internet-connected environment, including firewall protection and authenticated access for all users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
mitigations.rationale: Perimeter and authentication controls reduce the chance that external actors can reach complaint PII.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary and require the same public-trust and security screening, training, and approval process as for employees.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Support staff security requirements are based on public trust requirements. The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES. ... Will Department contractors have access to the system? YES
mitigations.rationale: Tight contractor controls reduce the insider-risk created by expanding access beyond USDA employees.

mitigations.description: Implement documented role-based access rules and periodic access reviews so users can only access complaint records needed for their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based least privilege is the clearest way to prevent unnecessary access to complaint PII.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for mail, email, telephone, and interview submissions, including guidance for staff on handling sensitive complaint information before it is entered into CRES.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the intake path reduces the chance that PII is exposed before it is entered into the system.

mitigations.description: Define and document a specific retention schedule tied to applicable records rules, and destroy records on that schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes.
mitigations.rationale: A clear retention schedule limits how long sensitive complaint records remain exposed.

mitigations.description: Add audit logging and periodic review of access to complaint records so inappropriate viewing or use can be detected and investigated.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring access is a standard control that helps identify misuse that access restrictions alone may miss.

risks.description: The system may collect and store more personal information than is needed for its stated purpose, including optional photos and unrestricted free-text personal details. This increases the chance of unnecessary exposure if the data is accessed or shared.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
risks.rationale: Optional collection of nonessential personal data creates avoidable privacy exposure without being necessary for the system's operation.

risks.description: Users can enter unrestricted personal information in the "About Me" field, which may lead to collection of sensitive or excessive data. Because the field is not restricted, the system may retain personal details beyond what is needed for business purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: An unrestricted free-text field can capture more personal information than intended and make privacy management harder.

risks.description: Photographs combined with names create identifiable profile information that could expose users if accessed by unauthorized parties. The system explicitly treats the photo as PII when combined with a name.
risks.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: Combining a photo with a name increases identifiability and the impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: Personal information is shared internally through Tableau dashboards and reports across multiple administrative domains, which may expose data to more personnel than necessary. The broad sharing increases the risk of secondary use beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Broad internal dissemination across many domains can reveal personal information to users who do not need it for the original request.

risks.description: The system transmits data to the USDA Data Lake through interfaces that could expose PII if improperly configured or intercepted. Moving data into a centralized lake also increases the number of places where personal information is stored and accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
