risks.rationale: Centralized transfer and downstream sharing expand the attack surface and the number of authorized viewers.

risks.description: Only contractor access controls are described, but the system does not state detailed role-based limits for all users who can view or manage PII. Without tighter access boundaries, authorized users may see more personal information than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
risks.rationale: Authorization alone does not show that access is minimized to the least amount of data needed for each role.

mitigations.description: Require users to provide only the minimum personal information needed for the business process and keep photos and other PII optional unless strictly necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
mitigations.rationale: The system already states that PII is not required, so minimizing collection is consistent with the existing design.

mitigations.description: Restrict the "About Me" field with input guidance or field controls so users cannot enter unnecessary sensitive personal information.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting free-text entry reduces the chance that the system will collect excessive personal details.

mitigations.description: Keep profile photos optional and limit who can view them to users with a clear operational need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.rationale: Optional collection and tighter viewing limits reduce the identifiability of users.

mitigations.description: Redact or aggregate personal information in Tableau dashboards and reports so senior leadership sees only the minimum detail needed for decision-making.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing detail in reports lowers the risk of unnecessary internal exposure while preserving analytics value.

mitigations.description: Apply strong access controls and data governance to the USDA Data Lake and Tableau outputs so only authorized users can retrieve PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and controlled downstream access help protect data as it moves into shared environments.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls that limit each contractor and employee to the smallest set of records needed for their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based limits make the existing authorization approach more privacy-protective by reducing unnecessary access.

risks.description: Centralized storage of detailed identity and access data creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse affecting many USDA employees, contractors, and visitors if the database is compromised or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS maintains individuals' personal individual verification (PIV) information to support the USDA’s efforts related to protecting USDA facilities
risks.rationale: The system holds multiple identifiers and access attributes in a centralized infrastructure, which increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: Visitor registration and background checking can collect more information than is necessary for a simple meeting visit, creating a risk of over-collection and heightened privacy intrusion for visitors.
risks.evidence_quote: The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
risks.rationale: Background checking of visitors expands the privacy footprint beyond basic entry management.

risks.description: Manually collected non-authoritative data at card issuance can be inaccurate or incomplete, leading to incorrect access decisions or erroneous records about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Also, Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
risks.rationale: Manual collection increases the chance of error, which can affect both access control and the accuracy of personal records.

risks.description: Internal sharing of card read activity and employee status for executive management and credit card services creates a risk that access data will be used for purposes beyond physical access control.
risks.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity and the Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
risks.rationale: Sharing access and employment data with other offices increases the risk of secondary use or unnecessary visibility into individual activity.

risks.description: Daily transfer of personal data to EDAPT and reporting by email to the Credit Card Service Center creates a risk of disclosure during transmission or in downstream analytics and reporting tools.
risks.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily. ... The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
risks.rationale: Even limited data can be exposed if transfer, storage, or dashboard/report access is mishandled.

risks.description: Contractor access to ePACS creates a risk that non-federal personnel could view or misuse sensitive identity and access information.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Allowing contractors into the system expands the number of people who can access personal data.

risks.description: Long retention of live and archived records increases the risk that personal data will remain exposed for longer than necessary and be available for future misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Longer retention extends the window in which records can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

risks.description: The system’s use of multiple authoritative HR sources and a staging table creates a risk that identity data may be combined, propagated, or synchronized incorrectly across systems.
risks.evidence_quote: This identity data is provided from a series of USDA Human Resources databases which are consolidated into ICAM Shared services.
risks.rationale: Consolidating identity data across systems can spread errors or expose more data than needed if controls fail.

risks.description: Sharing only under a pending SORN creates a risk of insufficiently clear notice or legal basis for some collected or disclosed data until the routine uses are finalized.
risks.evidence_quote: A SORN is pending to cover the collection of data for ePACS, see section 6.1.
risks.rationale: If notice and routine uses are not fully finalized, affected individuals may not have complete transparency about how their data is used.

mitigations.description: Limit access to authorized users on a strict need-to-know basis and keep data encrypted in storage and transmission.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and encryption reduce the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize visitor data collection to only what is necessary for scheduling and entry, and restrict the background checker to approved use cases.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting visitor collection and screening reduces unnecessary exposure of visitor information.

mitigations.description: Validate and review manually collected card-issuance data before it is stored or used to make access decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Verification steps can reduce errors introduced by manual collection.

mitigations.description: Restrict internal sharing to the minimum fields needed for each recipient and document the permitted purpose for each report or dashboard.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity and the Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared fields and purpose helps prevent secondary use beyond the stated need.

mitigations.description: Use secure transfer methods for all outbound data and limit downstream recipients' access to the smallest dataset needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer lowers interception risk, and data minimization reduces exposure in recipient systems.

mitigations.description: Continue granting contractor access only after background checks and security clearances, and review contractor permissions regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Screening and periodic review help reduce the chance of inappropriate contractor access.

mitigations.description: Enforce the approved retention schedule and purge archived records when the 5.5-year period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes
mitigations.rationale: Removing records when no longer needed reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Keep the staging table and consolidated identity feeds protected with strong access controls and data-quality checks before dissemination.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The staging table then disseminates the current identity data to the information systems as applicable.
mitigations.rationale: Controls around staging and validation help prevent incorrect or excessive propagation of identity data.

mitigations.description: Finalize the SORN and ensure external disclosures occur only under the approved routine uses and legal review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is not permitted to be shared outside the USDA except for what is covered by the routine uses in the ePACS SORN.
mitigations.rationale: A finalized SORN and controlled routine uses improve transparency and constrain disclosure.

risks.description: Travel and voucher information may be exposed to too many users because the system is used enterprise-wide and authorized agency users access it the same way as internal users. Even with roles, broad internal access increases the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse of employees' travel data.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation. Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users. Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
risks.rationale: Enterprise-wide access and shared access paths increase the number of people who can encounter sensitive travel records.

risks.description: Personal and financial travel records are retained for a long time, which increases the risk of secondary use, breach impact, or unnecessary exposure after the data is no longer needed for the trip. Bill-related data retained for six full years can still reveal travel history and spending patterns long after the travel event.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which records can be accessed, misused, or disclosed.

risks.description: The system profiles travelers by analyzing retained preferences to predict preferred airline seating, rental car companies, and hotel details. This creates a privacy risk because travel behavior can be inferred and reused beyond the immediate transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference-based prediction turns routine travel data into a behavioral profile.

risks.description: Travel authorization and voucher data are transmitted to another financial system, creating a disclosure risk during data sharing. Even though the transfer is for validation, it still moves personal travel and spending information outside the original application.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Any inter-system transmission increases the chance that data will be exposed or handled inconsistently.

risks.description: The system depends on centralized authentication and cloud/mobile access, which increases the impact if credentials or session controls are compromised. If an attacker gains access through the web browser or mobile app, they could reach employee travel records and preferences.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications. USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
risks.rationale: Remote access and centralized authentication concentrate risk around login and session security.

mitigations.description: Keep restrictive roles and audit checks in place, and limit access further to only the users who need each record for a specific travel or financial task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the number of people who can see sensitive travel data.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA and USDA records schedule consistently and delete or archive records as soon as the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Following a defined retention schedule limits unnecessary long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Allow travelers to control whether preference data is retained for future reference and used for predictive patterning.
mitigations.rationale: User control over profiling data reduces unnecessary behavioral inference.

mitigations.description: Continue to validate authorization and voucher data with audit checks before transmission to FMMI, and ensure the transfer remains encrypted end to end.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation. Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and encryption reduce the risk of improper disclosure during system-to-system sharing.

mitigations.description: Maintain multifactor authentication, VPN protections, and session-authenticity controls for browser and mobile access to reduce the chance of unauthorized account takeover.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and network controls lower the likelihood of unauthorized access through remote channels.

risks.description: The system retains traveler preference data and uses it to create predictive patterns, which can reveal personal habits and enable profiling beyond the immediate travel transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Persistent preference-based profiling increases the privacy impact of otherwise routine travel data.

risks.description: Enterprise-wide access creates a risk that more users than necessary can view USDA employee travel and voucher information.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide.
risks.rationale: Broader access increases the chance of unnecessary disclosure of personal travel information.

risks.description: Sharing authorization and voucher data with FMMI exposes employee travel information to another system, creating additional disclosure and linkage risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Transmitting personal travel records to another system expands the number of places where the data can be accessed or correlated.

risks.description: Long retention of user and billing data increases the risk that personal information will remain available longer than needed and be exposed in a future incident or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which stored personal data can be accessed improperly or breached.

risks.description: Because the system is accessed through web browsers and mobile applications, travel data may be exposed if endpoints or sessions are compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: Browser and mobile access enlarge the attack surface for unauthorized access to personal information.

mitigations.description: Limit traveler preference retention to the minimum necessary and provide a clear way for users to review and delete stored preferences.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the persistence of preference data lowers the risk of unnecessary profiling.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing restrictive role-based access and periodically review role assignments to ensure users only have access to the data needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces unnecessary viewing of employee travel information.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and field-level access controls before transmitting authorization and voucher records to FMMI, so only required data elements are shared.
mitigations.rationale: Sharing fewer data elements lowers the privacy impact of inter-system transmission.

mitigations.description: Enforce the approved retention schedule and conduct periodic data disposition reviews to delete records when they are no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong session and endpoint protections for browser and mobile access, including multifactor authentication and encrypted transport.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall. Web connections are secured using TLS
mitigations.rationale: Stronger access and transport protections reduce the chance of unauthorized interception or account compromise.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, so unauthorized access or disclosure could expose employees' identities and banking information.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: A breach of this data could directly harm affected individuals through identity theft or financial fraud.

risks.description: The system appears to combine multiple personal data elements in one administrative environment, increasing the risk of overexposure if access is broader than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The NFC ADMIN MA is composed of NFC-managed applications performing a variety of Government Employees Services Division (GESD) administrative functions using (Integrated Database Management System and DB2 databases on the NFC Mainframe.
risks.rationale: Consolidating multiple functions and data types in one system can increase the impact of any improper access.

risks.description: The system's use for debt collection could lead to inappropriate disclosure or use of delinquent-debt information about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: Debt-related information is sensitive and can cause financial or reputational harm if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Personnel and payroll data may be used for purposes beyond the original collection context, creating a risk of secondary use that is broader than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Broader routine use increases the chance that data will be shared or used in ways individuals do not expect.

risks.description: The 10-year retention period extends the time the system holds personal data, increasing the window for unauthorized access or stale-data exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases cumulative privacy risk because data remains available for misuse longer.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the sensitive personal and financial fields to authorized staff with a need to know, and protect the data with strong technical and administrative safeguards.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and strengthening protections reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure of highly sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and separate duties across the different administrative functions so users only see the data needed for their specific task.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting cross-functional access reduces the impact of having multiple datasets in one shared environment.

mitigations.description: Minimize the debt-collection information displayed or shared to only what is necessary for the collection task, and log access to delinquent-debt records.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and auditing reduce the risk of inappropriate disclosure or use of debt information.

mitigations.description: Limit routine use and reporting to the specific personnel and payroll purposes stated, and review any sharing with other Federal agencies for necessity and authorization.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining routine use to documented purposes helps prevent unnecessary secondary use.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved retention schedule consistently and delete or archive records when the 10-year period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system stores a broad set of personally identifiable and case-related information, including audio files, which could expose appellants and other participants if the data is mishandled or overexposed.
risks.evidence_quote: NAD case-related data: • Audio files and case determinations • Personally Identifiable Information (P11) such as full name, address, phone number, fax number, email address, and signature. • Metadata relating to the case process (e.g. date case was filed)
risks.rationale: The more sensitive data the system holds, the greater the privacy impact if access controls or handling fail.

risks.description: Only OHA-NAD personnel and contractors can access the electronic case tracking system, so insider misuse or unnecessary access could expose appellant data.
risks.evidence_quote: Only Office of Hearing and Appeals (OHA)-National Appeals Division (NAD) personnel have access to the electronic case tracking system.
risks.rationale: Restricting access helps, but any internal user with access can still see personal case information.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a risk that non-federal users could improperly view or handle personal case information if controls are not consistently enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
risks.rationale: Contractors are a distinct access population and need the same protections as employees to avoid unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Public e-filers can view their appeal transaction history and submitted documents, which could expose residence and contact information if account access is compromised or if the portal reveals more than intended.
risks.evidence_quote: an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted. At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
risks.rationale: Self-service access to personal case details increases the impact of account compromise or interface design errors.

risks.description: Reports generated for management review may disclose PII beyond the minimum needed for oversight, creating a secondary exposure path for personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
risks.rationale: Reporting can broaden access to personal data unless the reports are tightly limited and reviewed carefully.

risks.description: Information is retained forever even though it is not the official record, which increases the long-term risk of unnecessary exposure, stale data, and future misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention extends the time window in which personal data can be compromised or used beyond its original need.

risks.description: The system collects data through a web interface behind a secure login page, so any weakness in authentication or session protection could expose case information during online submission and access.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack collects data through the Web interface, behind a secure login page
risks.rationale: A web-based portal concentrates sensitive data access in a login-controlled interface that must be strongly protected.

mitigations.description: Minimize the data collected and stored to only what is necessary for case tracking and reporting, and apply strong access controls to audio files and PII.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing and tightly controlling sensitive data lowers the harm from any misuse or exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit internal access to only personnel with a demonstrated need to know and review access permissions regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the number of insiders who can view appellant data.

mitigations.description: Apply the same authentication, authorization, and monitoring controls to contractors as to federal employees, including periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
mitigations.rationale: The system already states contractors are subject to the same controls, which directly addresses contractor access risk.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication for the eFile portal and limit the portal to only the appellant's own case data and submitted documents.
mitigations.rationale: Strong account protection and strict data scoping reduce the chance that public users can see another person's information.

mitigations.description: Continue displaying PII warnings on reports and restrict report contents to the minimum needed for management review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All reports with PII display a PII warning.
mitigations.rationale: The existing warning helps alert users to sensitive content, and minimizing report detail further limits exposure.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce a finite retention schedule, with periodic deletion or archival review, even if the system is not the official record.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention limit reduces the long-term privacy risk created by perpetual storage.

mitigations.description: Harden the secure web login page with strong session management, multi-factor authentication, and continuous security monitoring.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger web authentication and monitoring reduce the chance that the portal becomes an entry point for unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive employee identity and payroll-related records that could be exposed if access controls fail. The collected data includes names, SSNs, time and attendance information, teleworking agreements, and payroll data.
risks.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data needed to conform to all applicable laws, Government regulations and procedures, and the needs of the Department and agencies in carrying out their personnel management responsibilities.
risks.rationale: SSNs and payroll records are highly sensitive and would cause harm if disclosed.

risks.description: Agency personnel and HR staff may enter or access data on behalf of individuals, which creates a risk of unauthorized or mistaken disclosure of an employee’s information. The system relies on multiple human intermediaries rather than only direct self-service by the data subject.
risks.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf.
risks.rationale: Third-party entry increases the chance that people other than the subject can see or mishandle the data.

risks.description: Access is determined by agencies and supervisors, so users may receive broader access than necessary if least-privilege controls are not strictly enforced. The system explicitly allows access to profiled data based on agency requests and access privileges.
risks.evidence_quote: Only individuals with an established "need-to-know" may access their specific profiled data.
risks.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces exposure, but it also shows that access is role-based and could be over-granted if not carefully managed.

risks.description: WebTA shares certified time-and-attendance and payroll data with other USDA systems, which increases the number of places where personal data can be accessed or misused. Each additional system connection expands the disclosure surface.
risks.evidence_quote: WebTA shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below. 1. EmpowHR: WebTA uses human resources data provided by EmpowHR. 2. Insight: WebTA generates files for transmission to the Insight hosting environment for processing. 3. OCIO eAuthentication (eAuth) application: The eAuthentication application provides authentication services for some WebTA customers. 4. TIME: WebTA transmits certified T&A data to the PPS TIME application.
risks.rationale: More internal recipients create more opportunities for unauthorized access or secondary use.

risks.description: Data is transmitted between agencies and systems over network connections, so interception or misrouting could expose PII in transit. Although secure methods are described, the system still depends on correct use of those channels.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection.
risks.rationale: Any system that moves PII across networks has transmission-risk if protections are misconfigured or bypassed.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to the system, which creates a risk that non-government personnel could view or mishandle employee data. Contractor access broadens the set of people who can reach PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases insider-risk and the need for strict role controls.

risks.description: Individuals may access their data through assigned user IDs and passwords, so account compromise could expose personal records. If credentials are stolen or weakly protected, an attacker could view time, attendance, and payroll information.
risks.evidence_quote: individuals may be assigned a unique user id and password that allows them access to their own data in WebTA.
risks.rationale: Credential-based access means account security directly affects confidentiality.

risks.description: The system retains records for periods governed by records schedules and agency requirements, so personal data remains available for a long time. Longer retention increases the window in which an access or breach incident could affect individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule. Civilian Personnel Records have various retention periods for specific types of data.
risks.rationale: The longer data is kept, the longer it can be exposed through misuse or compromise.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs and payroll details to only what is necessary for time-and-attendance processing, and protect those fields with strict access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data needed to conform to all applicable laws, Government regulations and procedures, and the needs of the Department and agencies in carrying out their personnel management responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing exposure of sensitive fields lowers the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Require logged, authorized workflows when HR staff enter information on behalf of individuals and verify the subject’s identity before updates are made.
mitigations.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf.
mitigations.rationale: Identity verification and auditability reduce the chance of mistaken or unauthorized entry.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews so users only retain the minimum access needed for their duties and specific profiled data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Regularly enforcing least privilege reduces unnecessary exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Restrict inter-system sharing to approved business purposes and document each downstream recipient’s access and use of the shared data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: WebTA shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter governance over internal sharing reduces the risk of secondary use and over-disclosure.

mitigations.description: Continue to require secure transmission methods such as SFTP over VPN and HTTPS for all data exchanges, and verify that no unencrypted channels are used.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agencies submit and receive data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Strong encrypted transport reduces the chance that PII can be intercepted in transit.

mitigations.description: Grant contractors access only when a valid role is approved and review contractor privileges regularly to ensure they remain necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review of contractor access helps prevent unnecessary exposure by non-government users.

mitigations.description: Require strong password practices and account protection for assigned user IDs, and limit access to the user’s own data unless a separate authorization exists.
mitigations.evidence_quote: individuals may be assigned a unique user id and password that allows them access to their own data in WebTA.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting credentials and scoping access to self-service reduces the impact of account compromise.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule consistently and remove records when their retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: Customer contact information and inquiry details may be exposed to a wide internal audience when escalated inquiries are shared across USDA Mission Areas. This increases the chance that staff who do not need the information could see names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and case history.
risks.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII information with all USDA Mission Areas part of AskUSDA Contact Center for escalated inquiries that require mission area expertise to respond
risks.rationale: Sharing PII across multiple mission areas expands the number of people who can access sensitive customer data.

risks.description: PII may be disclosed in transit when sent by email to SME contacts or passed through Cisco telephony integration. These transfer methods can create exposure if messages are misaddressed, intercepted, or handled outside the intended workflow.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: Email and telephony integrations create additional transmission points where PII can be exposed.

risks.description: The system may retain customer PII longer than necessary because no purging or archiving is currently configured. Long retention increases the amount of data available if the system is compromised and extends the period during which old contact details remain exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival
risks.rationale: Keeping records for years without automated disposal increases the privacy impact of stale data and any security incident.

risks.description: The system stores directly identifying contact information together with inquiry and case history, which could reveal sensitive details about a person's interaction with USDA programs. Even if the data is not inherently highly sensitive, combining identity and case information can create a fuller profile of the individual.
risks.evidence_quote: General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
risks.rationale: Linking identity with inquiry content makes the records more revealing than contact details alone.

risks.description: Authorized users with valid Linc Pass credentials can access PII in the Salesforce environment, so a compromised or misused account could expose customer data. The system relies on user authentication and role-based access, but the PII is still available to internal authorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: PII data is only available through E-auth login of authorized users (all USDA users with a valid Linc Pass credentials) into the USDA contact center Salesforce Government Cloud Environment
risks.rationale: Any system that concentrates PII behind user accounts remains vulnerable if credentials are stolen or access is misused.

mitigations.description: Limit escalated inquiry access to only the specific mission area staff needed to resolve the case, rather than sharing PII with all USDA Mission Areas.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting distribution reduces unnecessary exposure of customer PII.

mitigations.description: Use secure, approved transmission methods for PII instead of ordinary email, and apply safeguards to the Cisco telephony integration to minimize disclosure during transfer.
mitigations.rationale: Safer transmission channels lower the chance that PII is intercepted or sent to the wrong recipient.

mitigations.description: Implement automatic purging or archiving rules tied to the approved retention schedule so records are removed or archived when no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Automated disposal reduces the amount of legacy PII kept in the system and the duration of exposure.

mitigations.description: Minimize the case details stored with contact records by collecting only what is needed to resolve the inquiry and separating identity data from narrative case history where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the sensitivity of each record and limits what can be learned from a breach or misuse.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and periodic access reviews for all authorized users and contractors, with prompt removal of access when it is no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS). The standard ISSPM SAAR process will be followed for requesting internal access.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access governance helps ensure only users with a current need can reach PII.

risks.description: The system creates broad surveillance of employees, contractors, and visitors as they enter and move through USDA facilities, which can reveal their movements and associations over time. This can chill ordinary activity and expose sensitive presence information even when no wrongdoing is suspected.
risks.evidence_quote: the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
risks.rationale: Continuous location-based monitoring of identifiable people creates privacy intrusion even when the footage is collected for security.

risks.description: The cameras can capture highly identifying details beyond simple video, including facial images, license plates, and information from drivers licenses such as names, addresses, and dates of birth. This increases the chance of identifying and tracking individuals across places and events.
risks.evidence_quote: The VSS cameras may capture facial images of employees and visitors to USDA buildings and images of license plates that are parked or driving through the parking lot.
risks.rationale: Collecting multiple direct identifiers makes the footage more sensitive and more useful for identification and tracking.

risks.description: Some cameras use zoom, manual tracking, and automatic tracking to follow a single individual or capture text on belongings, which can intensify surveillance beyond general security monitoring. This raises the risk of intrusive focus on particular people without a specific need.
risks.evidence_quote: Zooming capability allows for the recording of textual information such as license plate numbers or text written on a person’s belongings. Most cameras are fixed but others use pan/tilt/zoom capability with manual tracking, which allows the individual monitoring with the VSS feed to adjust the camera in real time to gain the best image of any suspicious or illegal activity of interest that is occurring.
risks.rationale: Enhanced tracking and zoom make it easier to collect more personal detail about a person than is necessary for general observation.

risks.description: Footage may be used and exported for criminal or disciplinary actions, creating a secondary-use risk that the data will be applied beyond simple facility security. People recorded by the system may face consequences based on footage collected for monitoring purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: it will be used to review events that have taken place in a post investigative nature and may be exported to be used later for criminal or disciplinary actions.
risks.rationale: Using surveillance footage for later enforcement or discipline expands the privacy impact beyond the original collection context.

risks.description: The system shares video with internal and external organizations, including federal agencies and local law enforcement, which increases the risk of broader dissemination and loss of control over the footage. Once shared, the footage may be used for investigations and prosecutions beyond USDA's direct oversight.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions Information from the VSS cameras will be used by federal agencies and local law enforcement to detect and respond to potentially unlawful activities in the areas surrounding federal facilities.
risks.rationale: Disclosure to multiple recipients raises the risk that sensitive footage will be reused or retained outside USDA's control.

risks.description: Contractors and select non-employees can access the system, so more people than USDA staff may view sensitive footage. This expands the number of authorized users and the chance of misuse or unauthorized viewing.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Wider access increases exposure of sensitive surveillance data even when users are screened.

risks.description: Although the system intends a six-month retention period, footage may be kept longer when storage, camera counts, or suspected criminal activity require it. Extended retention increases the amount of historical surveillance data available for later access or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The intent is a 6-month retention period for all video footage, however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases privacy risk because more footage remains available for access, disclosure, or secondary use.

risks.description: The cameras record passersby on public streets and people accessing secured areas, so the system may collect information about individuals who are not the primary focus of security monitoring. This can capture bystanders and people with no connection to a specific incident.
risks.evidence_quote: The cameras may record passersby on public streets and USDA personnel accessing a secured area.
risks.rationale: Recording bystanders and unrelated individuals broadens the privacy impact beyond intended targets.

mitigations.description: Limit camera placement and viewing to security-relevant areas and avoid unnecessary coverage of routine movement areas where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: USDA places the VSS cameras around the perimeter and inside of USDA facilities and buildings, including parking lots, entrance and exits, and secured areas.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing coverage to necessary areas lowers the amount of routine movement captured.

mitigations.description: Restrict capture of identifying details to situations where they are needed for security or investigation, and avoid using zoom or plate-reading features unless justified by an incident.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Zooming capability allows for the recording of textual information such as license plate numbers or text written on a person’s belongings.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting capture of direct identifiers reduces the sensitivity of the footage.

mitigations.description: Require documented justification and supervisory approval before using manual tracking or zoom on a person or vehicle, except during an active security incident.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To retain the footage after the retention period, a supervisor must approve the request and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.rationale: Approval controls help ensure enhanced surveillance is used only when necessary.

mitigations.description: Use footage for criminal or disciplinary actions only when there is a documented investigative need and limit exports to the minimum relevant segments.
mitigations.evidence_quote: it will be used to review events that have taken place in a post investigative nature and may be exported to be used later for criminal or disciplinary actions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting secondary use and export reduces the chance of overuse of surveillance data.

mitigations.description: Share footage only in response to formal requests and only with recipients whose need is tied to a specific investigation or prosecution.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions
mitigations.rationale: Formal-request gating already described in the system helps constrain external and internal disclosures.

mitigations.description: Keep access limited to screened personnel and apply least-privilege access so contractors and non-employees can view only what they need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Screening is already in place, and least-privilege access would further reduce unnecessary viewing.

mitigations.description: Enforce the six-month automatic deletion rule and require documented approval for any extension tied to suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored for a maximum of six months and then is automatically deleted. Records which are retrieved pursuant to suspected criminal activity will be retained until any investigative or enforcement action is completed.
mitigations.rationale: Automatic deletion and approval for exceptions are the stated controls for limiting retention.

mitigations.description: Use camera placement and operational review to minimize capture of passersby and unrelated individuals where feasible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The cameras may record passersby on public streets and USDA personnel accessing a secured area.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing incidental capture lowers privacy impacts on people not involved in a security event.

risks.description: The system may collect identifiable customer information in feedback channels, creating a risk that customers are identified when they did not expect to provide PII. The tool explicitly allows collection of names, email addresses, and zip codes in free-form comments.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Collecting direct identifiers increases the chance that feedback can be tied to a person.

risks.description: The system may reveal sensitive or identifying information through free-form feedback that is later analyzed and retained. The tool collects both structured and unstructured feedback from multiple channels, which can contain personal details beyond the listed PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The data collected, used, disseminated, or maintained in the VoC tool is feedback from customers through multiple channels including, but not limited to; surveys, web forms, email, contact centers, in-person visits, and social media
risks.rationale: Unstructured feedback can include unexpected personal information that is harder to control and redact.

risks.description: Combining feedback across USDA mission areas can create a broader profile of an individual’s interactions and preferences. The system is designed to collect and analyze data across all mission areas and offices and to migrate existing tools into one cohesive product.
risks.evidence_quote: The VoC tool is designed to collect survey data across all the USDA mission areas.
risks.rationale: Centralizing data increases the risk of linkage and profiling across otherwise separate interactions.

risks.description: Geographic, demographic, and ethnographic analysis can create privacy risks by inferring characteristics about customers from their feedback. The system explicitly uses data to gather such insights for improvement purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: Gather customer insights and feedback geographically, demographically and ethnographically in order to identify areas in need of improvement
risks.rationale: Inference-based analysis can expose attributes that customers may not expect to be derived from their feedback.

risks.description: A small number of users with access to all data across mission areas creates a risk of excessive internal access. This broad access could expose more customer information than is necessary for a user’s role.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: Broad access increases the impact of any misuse or mistake by privileged users.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a risk that non-federal personnel may see customer feedback and any included PII. The system states that contractors will have access, but does not describe separate limits in the provided text.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the set of people who can view sensitive customer feedback.

risks.description: Permissioning and access control weaknesses could expose data to unauthorized users if role-based restrictions are not consistently enforced. The system relies on mission need, permission levels, licensing, and documented permissions.
risks.evidence_quote: Users of the VoC platform will be selected based on their mission need to access the system and their permission levels.
risks.rationale: Role-based access only protects privacy if permissions are correctly assigned and maintained.

risks.description: The retention program is not fully approved, which creates a risk that records may be kept longer than intended or not governed consistently. The PIA states the retention period has not been approved by the component records officer and NARA.
risks.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Unapproved retention increases the chance that personal data is retained without adequate records governance.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of direct identifiers and only request PII when a customer explicitly asks for follow-up contact.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data will never be inquired or manipulated to identify individuals or their associated PII unless a customer specifically asks to be contacted by a USDA official for a follow-up conversation.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting PII collection reduces the chance that feedback can be tied to a named person.

mitigations.description: Review and redact free-form submissions before they are used broadly in dashboards or analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction helps prevent accidental exposure of personal details embedded in unstructured feedback.

mitigations.description: Limit cross-mission-area access to only users with a demonstrated mission need and keep views aggregated where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and need-based access reduce the ability to link feedback to specific individuals across programs.

mitigations.description: Use the geographic, demographic, and ethnographic outputs only in aggregated form and suppress small cells or outliers.
mitigations.rationale: Suppressing small groups reduces the chance that inferred characteristics can be tied to a person or small cohort.

mitigations.description: Restrict all-data access to the smallest possible number of users and review those privileges regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting privileged access reduces the privacy impact of misuse or errors by high-access users.

mitigations.description: Apply the same privacy and security training, licensing, and documented permission controls to contractors as to federal users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Approved USDA employees will undergo in-person training on platform functionality, privacy, and security controls. Before users gain access to the system, they must be provided a license and their permission will be documented in a database file.
mitigations.rationale: Training and documented permissions help reduce inappropriate access by non-federal users.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and permission reviews before granting or renewing access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All appropriate security and accessibility measures will be implemented to limit, and control access based on user’s roles and permission levels.
mitigations.rationale: Regularly controlled access helps ensure users only see data needed for their role.

mitigations.description: Obtain formal approval of the retention schedule from the component records officer and NARA.
mitigations.rationale: Formal approval ensures retention and disposal of personal data are governed by an authorized records schedule.

risks.description: The system collects more personal information than appears necessary for account provisioning, including contact numbers, which increases the amount of PII exposed if the cloud system is compromised or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Workiva Wdesk collects name, email address, and contact numbers.
risks.rationale: Collecting extra identifiers increases privacy impact because more personal data is stored in the third-party cloud service.

risks.description: Users cannot decline to provide mandatory account fields, so individuals have no practical choice about providing their name, email address, and username to use the system.
risks.evidence_quote: No First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Mandatory collection without an opt-out limits individual control over personal information.

risks.description: PII is stored in a third-party cloud service hosted outside the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary, which creates exposure to cloud-provider security or administrative risks.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Hosting outside the agency boundary can increase the risk of unauthorized access or mishandling by the service environment.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, which may broaden access to employee PII beyond USDA staff who strictly need it.
risks.evidence_quote: 8.2 Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors can increase the number of people who can view or handle personal information.

risks.description: Access is granted through customizable workflows and approvals, so there is a risk that users may receive more access than necessary if access controls are not tightly configured.
risks.evidence_quote: The system contains automated workflows that can be customized to provide a minimum level of compliant access. ... Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
risks.rationale: Customizable approval-based access can lead to overbroad access if not consistently limited to least privilege.

risks.description: The system retains PII for 75 months, which extends the time personal data remains available and increases the window for misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
risks.rationale: Longer retention keeps personal data exposed for a longer period and increases cumulative risk.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection by removing contact numbers unless they are strictly required for account provisioning or a documented business need.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing collected PII lowers the amount of sensitive data stored in the cloud system.

mitigations.description: Provide a less-privileged alternative account or workflow for users who cannot or should not supply the mandatory fields, where operationally feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Offering an alternative reduces the privacy burden created by mandatory disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply and verify strong cloud security controls, including encryption, access restrictions, and vendor oversight for the hosted environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
mitigations.rationale: Additional safeguards are needed when PII is stored outside the agency boundary.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to only those accounts and functions necessary for their assigned duties and review contractor access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 8.2 Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Restricting contractor access reduces the number of people who can view PII.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access settings and periodic access reviews to ensure customized workflows do not grant unnecessary permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system contains automated workflows that can be customized to provide a minimum level of compliant access.
mitigations.rationale: Using the system's access controls to keep permissions minimal reduces overexposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Review whether the 75-month retention period is the minimum necessary and purge records as soon as the approved retention schedule allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the time that personal data remains at risk.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal data, including SSNs/TINs, handwritten signatures, salary data, and legal names, so a breach or misuse could expose applicants, grantees, vendors, and personnel to identity theft or financial harm.
risks.evidence_quote: This information may include the vendor’s name, address, email IDs, and SSN/TIN.
risks.rationale: The presence of direct identifiers and tax identifiers increases the harm if the data is improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: GIMS data may be shared outside USDA with a broad set of external parties, which creates a risk of unnecessary disclosure of applicant and awardee information beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS award results related information can be shared with a number of external parties, including, but not limited to, non-profit organizations, state and local organizations, individuals, corporations, and entities outside the US.
risks.rationale: Sharing with many external recipients increases the chance that more personal information is disclosed than is necessary.

risks.description: Information may be disclosed in common office formats or hard copy, which can lead to accidental forwarding, printing loss, or other unauthorized exposure of personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
risks.rationale: Portable file formats and paper copies are easier to mishandle than tightly controlled system access.

risks.description: Review panelists can receive encrypted PII, and although some identifiers are redacted, other personal information still flows to external reviewers, creating a risk of over-disclosure during the grants review process.
risks.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII is limited to review panelists involved in the grants process. Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications. Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
risks.rationale: External review requires disclosure of personal data outside the core system, which can expose applicant information to more people than necessary.

risks.description: Contractors have access for backup, support, and account management, which creates a risk that non-government personnel could access or mishandle sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Broader operational access increases the number of people who can view or alter personal information.

risks.description: The system ingests data from external systems and manual user entry, so inaccurate or mismatched records could lead to incorrect award, vendor, or collection decisions that affect individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: FMAT is a Financial Management Support Solution that includes web-based custom-designed applications residing on the FNS intranet.
risks.rationale: When personal and financial data are combined from multiple sources, errors can propagate into decisions and records.

risks.description: The system retains GIMS and FMAT information for six years after closeout or final payment/cancellation, which may keep personal data longer than needed and extend the window of exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy. FMAT information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after final Payment or cancellation.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the amount of time sensitive records remain available to be accessed, copied, or breached.

risks.description: Because the system supports reporting to internal users and external reporting approved by the Grants Director, reports may reveal more personal or program information than intended if not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is also used for reporting purposes to both internal FNS users, as well as external reporting as approved by the Grants Director.
risks.rationale: Reporting expands dissemination beyond operational use and can surface personal details in aggregated or exported outputs.

mitigations.description: Encrypt sensitive PII before distribution and keep the data out of primary key fields used for tracking or identity matching.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists. The PII is not used as a key for tracking, as a primary key, or foreign key to identify an individual.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and avoiding identifier-based keys reduce the chance that sensitive data is exposed or overused.

mitigations.description: Limit external sharing to approved disclosures and require Grants Director approval before any release outside USDA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Transmissions/disclosures typically require approval by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Approval control helps ensure external disclosures are necessary and authorized.

mitigations.description: Apply stronger handling controls to exported files and paper copies, such as restricting distribution and using encrypted electronic delivery where possible.
mitigations.rationale: This reduces the risk that data leaves the system in an easily misused format.

mitigations.description: Continue limiting PII sharing to review panelists and redact unnecessary identifiers such as EIN/TIN before distribution.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII is limited to review panelists involved in the grants process. Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what reviewers receive lowers the amount of personal data exposed outside the core process.

mitigations.description: Keep contractor access restricted to the specific support functions listed and maintain direct supervision of computerized files.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to computerized files is password protected and under the direct supervision of the system manager.
mitigations.rationale: Supervised, password-protected access helps limit contractor misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Validate and reconcile incoming data from external systems and manual entries before using it for matching, awards, or vendor creation.
mitigations.rationale: Verification reduces the risk that incorrect personal data drives downstream decisions.

mitigations.description: Review whether all retained records still need to remain in primary storage for the full retention period and archive them according to approved records schedules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, GRS 1.1, Item 010 see GRS 1.2, Item 010.
mitigations.rationale: Using an approved records schedule helps keep retention aligned with legal and operational needs.

mitigations.description: Restrict report generation and external reporting to approved users and disclosures only, with the Grants Director controlling release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is also used for reporting purposes to both internal FNS users, as well as external reporting as approved by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled reporting reduces the chance that personal information is broadly disseminated.

risks.description: Centralizing detailed SNAP participant information in one database increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach because the system aggregates sensitive data from all states in one place.
risks.evidence_quote: The SNAP Information Database will collect SNAP participant data (including personal information and transactional data) from all 53 SNAP state agencies via their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) payment processors, through secure channels, to be stored in a database
risks.rationale: A single repository of highly sensitive data creates a larger privacy impact if it is misused or exposed.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive eligibility and financial details, which could reveal intimate information about participants if accessed or used beyond the intended checks.
risks.evidence_quote: detailed and sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed, as well as ﬁnancial data (e.g., amount of beneﬁt received).
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the data, the greater the privacy harm if it is improperly disclosed or repurposed.

risks.description: Sharing data across federal and state systems can expose participant information to multiple agencies, increasing the number of places where privacy controls must be enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: This initiative will focus on detecting duplicate enrollments across states, verifying immigration status eligibility, and performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient or system increases the risk of unauthorized use or inconsistent protections.

risks.description: Using automated scripts, queries, and matching algorithms to make integrity determinations can produce false positives that wrongly flag participants as ineligible, duplicate, or fraudulent.
risks.evidence_quote: Integrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database, using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
risks.rationale: Automated matching can still misidentify people, which can lead to unfair privacy and program harms.

risks.description: Collecting data from 2000 to the present creates a long historical record that may include people whose older information is no longer necessary for current program integrity checks.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Long retention of historical records increases the amount of personal information held and the consequences of misuse.

risks.description: The system's immigration status checks create a risk that highly sensitive citizenship or immigration-related information will be used in ways that participants may not expect.
risks.evidence_quote: verifying immigration status eligibility
risks.rationale: Immigration-related data is especially sensitive because improper disclosure can cause significant personal harm.

risks.description: Cross-state duplicate enrollment detection may link records about the same person across jurisdictions, increasing the chance of incorrect identity matching or unnecessary exposure of participation history.
risks.evidence_quote: detecting duplicate enrollments across states
risks.rationale: Linking records across systems can reveal more about a person than any single state record would.

mitigations.description: Store the data only in the authorized FNS AWS environment and maintain strong access controls and monitoring around the centralized database.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FNS’ Oﬃce of Information Technology (OIT) maintains a secure AWS environment that is authorized under the FNS Infrastructure General Support System (FNS I-GSS) Authority to Operate (ATO).
mitigations.rationale: A secure, authorized hosting environment reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and use to the data required for the stated integrity checks and avoid any unrelated secondary use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: detailed and sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed
mitigations.rationale: Restricting use to what is necessary lowers the privacy burden of sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Share information only when permitted by law and consistent with the notice, and only with state agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify improper enrollments or transactions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: sharing, where permitted by law and consistent with this notice, information with State agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify fraudulent or otherwise improper or illegal SNAP enrollments or transactions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting disclosures to lawful, necessary purposes reduces unnecessary spread of participant data.

mitigations.description: Use the described matching algorithms and add human review before any adverse action is taken on a participant record.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
mitigations.rationale: False positives are a known risk of automated matching, so review before action helps prevent harm.

mitigations.description: Apply a retention schedule that limits how long historical participant data is kept and deletes records when they are no longer needed for integrity checks.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the amount of personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to immigration-status-related data to personnel with a need to know and document the purpose for each use.
