mitigations.rationale: Tighter access controls help prevent unnecessary exposure of especially sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Use data-matching rules designed to minimize false positives and verify matches before treating records as duplicates across states.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
mitigations.rationale: Careful matching reduces the chance that cross-state linkage will incorrectly identify the wrong person.

risks.description: The system stores identifiable contact information about non-employee affiliates, so a breach or misuse could expose names, business addresses, contact information, and affiliate IDs.
risks.evidence_quote: • Names, business address and contact information, and Affiliate ID of Contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Government employees, Resource Conservation & Development Council employees, Volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organization personnel (referred to as Affiliates).
risks.rationale: These data elements directly identify affiliates and would be privacy-sensitive if accessed without authorization.

risks.description: NRCS employees are the only users of the application, so any misuse or unauthorized access by an employee could expose or alter affiliate records.
risks.evidence_quote: • The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
risks.rationale: Limiting access to employees reduces external exposure, but it still leaves the data dependent on internal user controls.

risks.description: The application shares affiliate information with zRoles to assign roles, creating a risk that incorrect or excessive access could be granted to affiliates in other NRCS systems.
risks.evidence_quote: • The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
risks.rationale: Role assignment based on stored affiliate data can affect access to multiple NRCS applications, so mistakes can have broader privacy consequences.

risks.description: Because affiliates provide their information to an NRCS employee and the employee enters it into the system, data entry errors or outdated information could cause inaccurate records and incorrect access decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: • Individual affiliates provide their information to an NRCS employee with the appropriate system access to the Affiliates application. The NRCS employee enters the information.
risks.rationale: Manual entry and indirect collection increase the chance that records do not reflect the affiliate's current information.

risks.description: The records may be retained for a long time, which increases the chance that unnecessary personal information remains available after it is no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: • All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which personal data can be accessed, misused, or disclosed.

risks.description: The system stores affiliate records as long as a person qualifies for conservation programs, which could keep personal information tied to an individual for an extended period beyond immediate access-control needs.
risks.evidence_quote: • Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs”.
risks.rationale: Retention tied to program eligibility may outlast the specific access-control purpose described for the system.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the Affiliates database to authorized NRCS employees only and enforce least-privilege access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the number of people who can view or misuse identifiable affiliate information.

mitigations.description: Require role-based access review, audit logging, and periodic monitoring of NRCS employee activity in the application.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring employee actions helps detect and deter unauthorized viewing or alteration of affiliate records.

mitigations.description: Validate affiliate records before they are used by zRoles and require periodic review of assigned roles for appropriateness.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
mitigations.rationale: Checking data quality before role assignment reduces the chance that incorrect records lead to improper access.

mitigations.description: Confirm the affiliate's submitted information with the affiliate before entry or when records are updated.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Information is provided directly to an NRCS employee by the affiliate
mitigations.rationale: Verification with the source helps reduce errors introduced during manual entry.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposal rules so affiliate data is deleted or archived when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? • Yes
mitigations.rationale: Following approved retention schedules prevents personal data from being kept longer than authorized.

mitigations.description: Review whether all retained fields are still necessary for access-control purposes and minimize stored data where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information retained over long periods.

risks.description: The warehouse holds highly sensitive personal and financial-identifying information, so a compromise could expose producers, agents, and adjusters to identity theft or other misuse. The stored data includes tax IDs, social security numbers, addresses, phone numbers, policy numbers, and location-linked farm information.
risks.evidence_quote: Producer name, address, phone numbers, tax ID, ID type, and entity type, as well as any associated farm numbers. Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc. Policy data includes name, address, phone number, policy number, unit, Approved Insurance Provider (AIP), crop, insurance plan, coverage level, indemnity, liability, premium, fund placement, acres, agent name, agent social security number, adjuster name, adjuster social security number, and etc.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers make unauthorized disclosure especially harmful.

risks.description: The system centralizes data from multiple years into a single production database, increasing the amount of personal information exposed if access controls fail or the database is breached. Consolidation also makes it easier to link records over time and build detailed profiles.
risks.evidence_quote: Although the RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years, it is moved to a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
risks.rationale: Centralizing large historical datasets increases the privacy impact of any single access or security incident.

risks.description: Authorized users in multiple organizations can access the data, creating a risk of overbroad internal disclosure or misuse beyond the minimum necessary. The system shares information with FSA, RMA, OIG, and authorized users in AIPs.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently the information described previously is provided to FSA, RMA, and OIG within USDA. There have been limited OIG users that have access to the system, this was to obtain reports and transmit products and is a routine use.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the chance that data will be accessed for purposes not strictly needed for the stated function.

risks.description: External Approved Insurance Providers can access information tied to their policies, which creates a risk that sensitive policy data could be disclosed outside USDA more broadly than intended. Even limited access still exposes personal and policy details to non-federal entities.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs. AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
risks.rationale: Sharing identifiable policy data with external organizations expands the exposure surface and the consequences of misuse.

risks.description: Users access the system through a web application on the RMA Extranet, so unauthorized access or interception of transmitted data could expose personal information. The need for dual authentication helps, but the web-based access path still presents a privacy risk if credentials are compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA and Approved Insurance Provider (AIP) HyDRA are accessible via caehydralink which resides on the RMA Extranet. An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
risks.rationale: Web-accessible systems are vulnerable to credential theft or misconfiguration, which can lead to unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The data is retained for the life of the project, which increases the amount of time personal information remains exposed to security incidents or inappropriate use. Long retention also increases the chance that data will be used beyond the period originally expected by the individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
risks.rationale: The longer personal data is kept, the longer it remains vulnerable and the more likely it is to be repurposed.

risks.description: The system uses data mining and analysis to support fraud and abuse detection, which can create privacy risk if individuals are profiled or decisions are influenced by incorrect or overly broad inferences. The warehouse combines many data elements for research and analysis purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: The BAD Data Warehouse system administered by the Center for Agribusiness Excellence (CAE) at Tarleton State University (TSU) is a data warehousing and data mining project for the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Risk Management Agency (RMA).
risks.rationale: Data mining can produce sensitive inferences that go beyond the original data collected from agencies.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the most sensitive fields, such as tax IDs and social security numbers, to only users with a documented need and mask or tokenize those fields in routine reports.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of the most sensitive identifiers lowers the impact of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Keep annual datasets segregated where possible and restrict cross-year joins or exports to approved analytical uses only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Although the RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years, it is moved to a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
mitigations.rationale: Segregation limits the amount of historical personal data exposed in any one query or incident.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege role-based access reviews for FSA, RMA, OIG, and other authorized users, with periodic recertification of who still needs access.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the minimum necessary reduces the chance of unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply contract and account-level controls so AIPs can only retrieve the specific policy records they are authorized to see, and log all external access for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining external users to their own records limits disclosure to third parties.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong authentication for HyDRA, require secure transport, and monitor for suspicious login activity or credential abuse.
mitigations.evidence_quote: An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and monitoring reduce the risk of unauthorized web access.

mitigations.description: Apply a documented retention schedule that minimizes storage to the shortest period compatible with the project and return or dispose of data when no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the window in which personal data can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Review data-mining outputs for necessity and accuracy before release, and document limits on how analytical results may be used to avoid unsupported inferences about individuals.
mitigations.rationale: Oversight of analytical outputs helps prevent privacy harms from inaccurate or overbroad profiling.

risks.description: CoLab stores identifiable user profile information, including names and personal contact details, which creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse if the system is compromised or access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Privacy related information is collected and maintained by CoLab in 'profiles' that include the individual's name and work contact information. For some individuals, personal contact information is maintained in their profile. • Personal Contact Information is comprised of the following elements: o First name o Last name o Email o Phone o Company Address
risks.rationale: The system maintains directly identifying contact data, so any unauthorized access would expose personal information about users.

risks.description: Because access is granted to authorized contractors and partners, there is a risk that more people than necessary can view or modify user profiles, increasing insider misuse or accidental exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: • Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities. Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
risks.rationale: Even role-based access creates privacy risk if roles are too broad or permissions are misapplied.

risks.description: CoLab uses PII obtained from eAuth to establish and update user profiles, so errors or outdated information in the source or profile can lead to inaccurate identity and contact records.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile. CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: If profile data is wrong or not kept current, users may be misidentified or contacted incorrectly.

risks.description: User profile information is retained for the life of the application, which creates a risk that personal data will remain longer than needed and increase exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the amount of time personal data is vulnerable to unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: Although the system says accounts are disabled when a user leaves, there is still a risk that departed users' profile data may persist unless it is actually erased or deleted when no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals have control of the shelf life for retention. If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
risks.rationale: Disabling an account does not necessarily remove stored personal data, so residual records may remain unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Limit the profile to the minimum contact fields needed for authorization and project administration, and restrict editing and viewing to authorized roles only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab contains a minimal amount of contact information related to CoLab users. This PII is used to establish a user's authorization to CoLab projects
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored data reduces the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege RBAC reviews for contractors and partners so their access remains limited to the duties they need to perform.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
mitigations.rationale: Regular least-privilege review reduces unnecessary internal access to profile data.

mitigations.description: Allow users to review and correct their own profile information and verify eAuth-derived identity data before it is used to create the profile.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
mitigations.rationale: User review and correction helps keep profile data accurate and current.

mitigations.description: Delete application-specific PII when it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes, rather than keeping it for the full life of the application.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Deleting data when it is no longer needed reduces the duration of privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: When a user leaves, disable the account and also remove or archive any associated profile data according to the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
mitigations.rationale: Disabling access and removing unneeded records prevents stale personal data from lingering in the system.

risks.description: Vendor PII is retained in the IDEA DataMart, which increases the risk of unauthorized access or exposure compared with purely transitory processing. The retained data includes names and contact information used for reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Storing PII beyond a one-time read increases the amount of data available to be compromised.

risks.description: Contractors can access the system, which creates a risk that vendor PII could be viewed or misused by personnel beyond direct government staff. The access description does not specify technical limits on what contractors can see.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any non-owner access expands the number of people who can encounter the PII.

risks.description: Periodic refreshes from SCIMS create a risk that stale or unnecessary PII may remain available between updates or after it is no longer needed. This can increase the chance of retaining more personal data than necessary for reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Regular synchronization can perpetuate data retention unless paired with deletion and minimization controls.

risks.description: Report generation using selectable criteria could allow users to infer or view vendor PII in outputs if access controls are weak. Even though the system says it does not retrieve records by personal identifier, reports still use vendor information.
risks.evidence_quote: the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
risks.rationale: Selectable reporting can expose personal data through report content even without direct record lookup.

risks.description: Keeping application-specific information while the application remains in production may extend the life of PII longer than necessary if deletion is not timely. Long retention increases the window for misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases privacy risk because data remains available for a longer period.

mitigations.description: Limit the DataMart to the minimum vendor fields needed for report generation and apply strict access controls and auditing to the stored PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored fields and monitoring access reduces the harm if the retained data is exposed.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege role-based access for contractors and review contractor access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting contractor access lowers the chance of unnecessary viewing or misuse of vendor PII.

mitigations.description: Delete refreshed PII from IDEA when it is no longer needed for reporting and verify that periodic updates do not preserve obsolete records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
mitigations.rationale: Removing outdated data prevents periodic synchronization from extending the life of unnecessary PII.

mitigations.description: Constrain report criteria and output so users only receive vendor information necessary for their assigned reporting task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report outputs reduces the chance that users can see more personal data than needed.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA deletion schedule promptly when the data is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per NARA General Records Schedule 20, application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Timely deletion shortens the period during which retained data can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: Core Services can expose highly sensitive customer identifiers because it handles a customer ID that can be associated with a Social Security number or tax identification number, along with names, addresses, and partial bank account numbers. If access controls fail, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized users or systems.
risks.evidence_quote: SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number • bank account numbers (last few digits only)
risks.rationale: Identifiers tied to SSNs or TINs increase the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Returning data to client applications in JSON can expose personal information to any client or user that receives the response, increasing the chance of over-disclosure if the request is not properly authorized or scoped. This is especially sensitive because the system responds to multiple applications and legacy systems.
risks.evidence_quote: will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: A formatted response can be widely reusable and easier to copy or forward than a narrowly controlled internal record.

risks.description: Core Services moves USDA application data and metadata between several internal systems, creating a broader internal sharing surface where data could be exposed through one of the connected applications, databases, or adjacent systems. More integrations increase the chance of unauthorized access or accidental disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems
risks.rationale: Each additional internal connection expands the number of places where data can be mishandled.

risks.description: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall enter through a single external-facing gateway, so a compromise of that entry point could affect multiple downstream systems and the personal data they retrieve. This creates a concentration risk at the gateway layer.
risks.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: A single entry point is a high-value target because it fronts many services and data sources.

risks.description: Contractors with need-to-know access may see personal information as part of their duties, which creates insider-access risk if their access is broader than necessary or if controls are not tightly enforced. Even with background investigations, contractor access increases the number of people who can view the data.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any additional workforce access increases the chance of misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: Core Services relies on replicated or copied access to SCIMS data rather than direct control of the source system, so stale or inconsistent data could be returned or used for the wrong person. That can cause privacy harms such as misidentification or disclosure of one customer’s information in response to another customer’s request.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth). NRCS users do not have direct access to SCIMS.
risks.rationale: Using a view or copy introduces a risk that the data presented is not the authoritative current record.

risks.description: The system depends on authentication and established security rules for access to customer data, so any weakness in eAuth or authorization rules could allow unauthorized viewing of personal information. Because access is mediated across several systems, a control failure in one layer could open access broadly.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
risks.rationale: Authentication and authorization are the primary barriers protecting the personal data in the connected systems.

mitigations.description: Limit returned identifiers to the minimum necessary and mask or suppress sensitive fields such as customer IDs, bank account fragments, and any values associated with SSNs or TINs unless they are strictly required for the specific request.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of sensitive identifier data lowers the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply response-level data minimization and authorization checks before generating JSON output so each client application receives only the fields needed for its approved function.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting the response content reduces the chance that a client receives unnecessary personal data.

mitigations.description: Use least-privilege interface permissions and periodic review of each internal system connection so only approved systems can exchange the specific data they need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems
mitigations.rationale: Tighter control of each integration reduces the number of places where personal data can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Harden and continuously monitor the external-facing CA API Gateway with strong threat protection, logging, and alerting, since it is the single entry point for outside requests.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CA API Gateway – Used for threat protection, access control, and other sharedservices as defined during the architecture build out.
mitigations.rationale: The gateway is the main choke point for inbound traffic and should be closely protected.

mitigations.description: Restrict contractor access to the minimum necessary, enforce periodic access reviews, and keep the required background investigations current for all contractor users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and screening reduce the likelihood of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Validate replicated SCIMS data against the source system and monitor for synchronization errors before returning records to users or downstream applications.
mitigations.rationale: Consistency checks help prevent privacy harms caused by outdated or mismatched customer records.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong authentication, role-based authorization, and regular review of security rules governing access through eAuth and related interfaces.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Strong identity and access management is necessary to prevent unauthorized viewing of customer information.

risks.description: Emergency Action Plan records contain names, home addresses, and telephone numbers, so a breach or improper disclosure could expose private contact and location information for responders and property owners.
risks.evidence_quote: EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: This information can directly identify and locate individuals, making unauthorized access or disclosure a meaningful privacy harm.

risks.description: PII is shared with state and local emergency responders and disclosed in hardcopy or electronic copies, creating a risk of wider dissemination than intended during review cycles or activation.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Each disclosure event increases the chance that sensitive data is copied, forwarded, or mishandled outside the original need-to-know audience.

risks.description: Contractors and multiple responder roles can access EAPs on a need-to-know basis, so there is a risk of unauthorized internal access or overbroad access if controls are not strictly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
risks.rationale: The more categories of users who can reach the records, the greater the chance of accidental or improper access.

risks.description: The system retains records for long periods, which increases the chance that outdated PII will remain available after it is no longer needed for an EAP or after a person’s role changes.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which stale records can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: Some telephone numbers may not be publicly listed, so collecting them from individuals or organizations can reveal nonpublic contact information that the person may not expect to be broadly retained.
risks.evidence_quote: All DamWatch EAP PII is publicly available, with the possible exception of telephone numbers that may not be publicly listed.
risks.rationale: Nonpublic phone numbers are more sensitive than already public information and deserve tighter handling.

mitigations.description: Continue using secure communications methods for all hardcopy and electronic disclosures of EAPs, and limit distribution to controlled documents only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transmission reduces the chance that sensitive contact and location data will be intercepted or misdirected.

mitigations.description: Restrict disclosure of EAP PII to authorized emergency response situations and review cycles only, and avoid any sharing outside the stated emergency purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII collected is only used during the execution of an EAP following the authorized activation of the EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting use and disclosure to the emergency purpose reduces unnecessary spread of personal data.

mitigations.description: Enforce documented access controls and need-to-know authorization for all users, including contractors and responders.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access control lowers the risk of unauthorized internal viewing of EAP records.

mitigations.description: Require mandatory background investigations for contractors before granting access to DamWatch.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Screening contractors helps reduce the chance that sensitive records are accessed by unsuitable personnel.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA retention schedule and remove records when they no longer qualify for conservation program purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
mitigations.rationale: Keeping records only as long as needed reduces the amount of stale PII exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Treat nonpublic telephone numbers as especially sensitive and collect or retain them only when necessary for EAP execution.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collection of nonpublic contact details reduces exposure of information that is not already publicly listed.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal data, so a breach or unauthorized access could expose Social Security numbers, tax IDs, bank account details, and other sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increases harm if the records are exposed.

risks.description: Bulk scanning and metadata extraction can capture more information than needed, including personal details embedded in paper records that were not originally intended for broad digital access.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk digitization can expand the amount of accessible PII beyond the original paper handling context.

risks.description: Because DRMS is a cloud-based system run by a contractor, cloud or contractor access failures could expose records to unauthorized parties or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The application is Cloud based, developed by a Contractor for use by the USDA.
risks.rationale: Third-party hosting and development increase the number of entities that must be trusted to protect the records.

risks.description: Authorized staff and contractors can access records on a need-to-know basis, so excessive internal access could lead to insider misuse or unnecessary viewing of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties. ... Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any system with broad internal access roles needs strong controls to prevent overexposure of PII.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DRMS, which can make it harder for them to review or correct their own records and may leave inaccurate PII in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: When data subjects cannot access their records directly, errors may persist unless staff actively correct them.

risks.description: Long retention periods increase the chance that outdated personal information will remain stored longer than necessary, expanding exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: The longer records are kept, the longer they remain vulnerable to unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: The system holds records about owners, operators, producers, and participants in conservation programs, so disclosure could reveal participation in government programs and related property or farm details.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS acts as the system of record for both electronic records and the metadata necessary to describe those records. DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.
risks.rationale: Searchable records tied to program participation can reveal more about a person than isolated documents would.

mitigations.description: Limit access to encrypted documents containing sensitive identifiers to only authorized users with a documented need-to-know, and enforce strong authentication and audit logging.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties. DRMS has documented Access Control (AC) Procedures, in compliance with FISMA and USDA directives.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing access reduces the chance that highly sensitive records are exposed.

mitigations.description: Minimize bulk scanning and metadata extraction to only the records and fields needed for business and records-management purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting digitization to necessary content reduces the amount of PII placed into searchable digital stores.

mitigations.description: Maintain contractor security requirements, including mandatory background investigations and least-privilege access, for all contractor personnel with system access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Contractor screening and least-privilege access help reduce the risk of misuse in a contractor-operated cloud environment.

mitigations.description: Review and recertify user access regularly so staff and contractors retain only the access needed for their current duties.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps prevent unnecessary internal exposure of PII.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear, timely process for individuals to request their records and correction of inaccuracies through the designated field office or records office.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A workable access and correction process helps subjects identify and fix errors in their records.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules and dispose of records when the approved retention period ends, rather than keeping them indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition reduces the amount of personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Restrict search and retrieval capabilities to operational, legal, and records-management uses, and avoid broad retrieval of records beyond the stated business need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retrieval to stated purposes reduces unnecessary disclosure through search and indexing.

risks.description: DMS may expose highly sensitive personal and financial data if a document repository is accessed inappropriately, because it stores a wide range of PII including SSNs, tax IDs, bank routing numbers, and deposit account numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored PII increases the harm if access is misused or compromised.

risks.description: Direct document uploads by NRCS users can introduce incorrect, unnecessary, or overly sensitive information into DMS without a structured data-entry review step.
risks.evidence_quote: In addition, DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Direct upload of documents increases the chance that sensitive information is stored without adequate validation or minimization.

risks.description: Information transmitted from multiple source systems into DMS could be intercepted or mishandled during transfer, especially because the system relies on web services and user uploads.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected is transmitted primarily from ProTracts - Fund Manager, CST, and CCG via DMS web services.
risks.rationale: Any transfer path carrying PII creates a privacy risk if transmission controls fail or are bypassed.

risks.description: Using address and name from FSA SCIMS to identify the correct producer creates a risk of mismatching records and associating the wrong person with a document.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Identity matching based on limited identifiers can lead to inaccurate linkage of records.

risks.description: Authorized NRCS employees, conservation district employees, and contractors may view documents beyond what is strictly necessary if access controls are too broad for their roles.
risks.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
risks.rationale: Even restricted access can create privacy risk if users can see more records than needed for their duties.

risks.description: External disclosure to contractors or technical service providers could reveal PII outside USDA if the written authorization or purpose limitation is not properly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII with outside parties increases the risk of unauthorized use or disclosure.

risks.description: Because individuals do not have direct access to DMS, they may have limited ability to review their records and detect privacy errors or misuse promptly.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS.
risks.rationale: Lack of direct access can delay correction of inaccurate or improperly maintained personal information.

risks.description: Long retention of records can keep personal data in the system for years after it is no longer needed for active processing, increasing exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.rationale: The longer PII is retained, the longer it remains available for misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Restrict document access to authorized users with a need-to-know and maintain encryption for stored and transmitted documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting data in storage and transit reduces the chance that highly sensitive PII is exposed.

mitigations.description: Require upload review and minimize retained content by rejecting documents that contain unnecessary sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: A review step before acceptance can prevent avoidable sensitive data from being stored in the repository.

mitigations.description: Keep the web-service transfers encrypted and controlled for all source-system exchanges and user uploads.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The FSA SCIMS web service is an encrypted and controlled interaction.
mitigations.rationale: Encrypted, controlled transmission lowers the risk of interception or unauthorized disclosure in transit.

mitigations.description: Use additional identity verification or matching checks before linking SCIMS data to a producer record.
mitigations.rationale: Additional checks reduce the chance that a document is associated with the wrong individual.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based, least-privilege access reviews so users only see the documents needed for their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS features will allow users to view documents and/or upload new documents, version documents, and delete documents within the scope for those locations where their role has jurisdiction.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces unnecessary viewing of personal information.

mitigations.description: Require and verify written authorization before any disclosure to contractors or technical service providers, and limit use to the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Such disclosure shall be made subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited, authorized sharing reduces the chance of unauthorized external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear, timely request process for individuals to obtain information about records pertaining to them and to seek corrections through the designated office.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A defined access and correction pathway helps individuals detect and remedy privacy errors.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule and delete records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Following a records schedule limits how long personal data remains exposed in the system.

risks.description: The system holds sensitive borrower financial and identity data that could be exposed if access controls are weak or misused. The data includes loan, financial, and security property information tied to identifiable borrowers.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: This information can directly identify borrowers and reveal sensitive financial circumstances, so unauthorized access would create meaningful privacy harm.

risks.description: Manual entry by field agents can introduce privacy risks from input errors or unnecessary collection. Because the system relies on staff-entered data, mistakes could place incorrect borrower information into restructuring decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual handling increases the chance that incorrect or excessive personal data will be recorded and then used in loan servicing decisions.

risks.description: The system’s access to other internal applications and databases can broaden exposure of borrower information across systems. Cross-system access increases the number of places where the data can be viewed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Each additional system connection expands the attack surface and the set of users or processes that may encounter the data.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the risk that personal data will remain available longer than necessary. Long-term storage raises the chance of future misuse, breach, or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: How long is information retained? The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping identifiable financial records permanently increases exposure over time even if the original business need has passed.

risks.description: The system is used to make debt restructuring decisions, so inaccurate borrower data could lead to unfair or incorrect servicing outcomes. Errors in cash flow, loan status, or security property data could affect repayment plans.
risks.evidence_quote: eDALR$ completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status.
risks.rationale: If the inputs are wrong, the resulting calculations can produce an incorrect restructuring recommendation that affects the borrower.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to authorized agency officials and field office employees only, with role-based permissions and audit logging for all borrower record access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: to assist authorized agency officials in determining and evaluating the effects of primary loan servicing
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and recording access reduces the chance that sensitive borrower data will be viewed or used improperly.

mitigations.description: Add validation and review controls for manually entered borrower data before it is saved or used in calculations.
mitigations.rationale: A review step can catch entry mistakes and reduce the privacy and fairness impact of incorrect personal data.

mitigations.description: Apply strict access controls and least-privilege rules to all connected internal databases and web applications, and limit data pulled from them to what is needed for restructuring.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
mitigations.rationale: Restricting cross-system access lowers the number of systems and users that can expose borrower information.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review process to confirm that permanent retention is still required for each record set and to segregate archived records with strong protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review and strong archival controls reduce unnecessary long-term exposure while preserving required records.

mitigations.description: Use data quality checks to verify borrower cash flow, loan status, and related inputs before restructuring calculations are performed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status
mitigations.rationale: Verifying inputs helps ensure the restructuring analysis is based on accurate personal and financial information.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal, financial, and credit information that could cause significant harm if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: Because the system holds identity, credit, and financial data, unauthorized disclosure would expose borrowers to identity theft and financial privacy harms.

risks.description: Sharing name and Tax ID with an external credit vendor creates a risk of unnecessary external exposure of identifying data.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: External transmission increases the number of parties handling the data and therefore the chance of misuse or breach.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the long-term risk of misuse, breach, or access beyond the original loan purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database.
risks.rationale: Keeping records longer than necessary expands the window in which old data can be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: Collecting and maintaining credit reports and credit numbers can expose borrowers to sensitive credit-history privacy harms if the data is accessed or used beyond eligibility decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: Credit history is especially sensitive and can reveal detailed financial behavior that borrowers may not expect to be broadly accessible.

risks.description: The system’s use of borrower data for loan making and servicing creates a risk of function creep if information is reused beyond the stated loan-assessment purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: When the same records support multiple processing steps, there is a risk that data will be used more broadly than needed for each step.

risks.description: County office staff enter borrower data, so inaccurate or incomplete entry could lead to incorrect financial or eligibility decisions that affect the borrower’s privacy and interests.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry can introduce errors that may cause improper decisions or incorrect records to persist.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to borrower records to only personnel with a need to know and apply strong authentication and audit logging for all access to sensitive fields.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance that sensitive financial and credit data will be viewed or used improperly.

mitigations.description: Minimize the data shared with Microbilt to only the specific fields required for creditworthiness checks and document the purpose of that exchange.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
mitigations.rationale: Sharing only what is necessary lowers the privacy impact of the external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce a records schedule that deletes or archives borrower records when they are no longer needed for the approved retention period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition reduces the amount of stale personal data retained and therefore reduces exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Limit access to credit reports and related credit identifiers to staff directly involved in eligibility and servicing decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the most sensitive credit data helps prevent unnecessary disclosure of detailed financial history.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce purpose-specific use rules so the collected information is used only for loan eligibility, loan making, and loan servicing activities described in the PIA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the chance that borrower data will be repurposed in ways that exceed the stated mission.

mitigations.description: Validate borrower-entered information with the borrower before final processing and use data quality checks to reduce entry errors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and quality checks help prevent inaccurate records from affecting decisions or persisting in the system.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive borrower identifiers and account information, including Social Security Numbers, which creates risk if the data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: ADPS uses the customer’s name, address, Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Social Security Numbers and loan account data are sensitive identifiers that can be misused for identity theft or fraud if compromised.

risks.description: Borrower data can be accessed through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number, increasing the chance of unauthorized lookup or overbroad access.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Using direct identifiers for retrieval can make it easier for users to locate records without a narrower need-to-know control.

risks.description: The system shares borrower information with a wide set of internal organizations and support personnel, which expands the number of people who can see personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers.
risks.rationale: Each additional internal recipient increases the exposure surface and the chance of inappropriate access or disclosure.

risks.description: Borrower information is disclosed externally to multiple agencies and private entities, creating risk of secondary use or disclosure beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
risks.rationale: Sharing with many external recipients increases the likelihood that data will be reused, retained, or protected inconsistently.

risks.description: The system reports borrower information to IRS and credit bureaus, which can adversely affect borrowers through tax refund offsets and credit reporting if the data is inaccurate or outdated.
risks.evidence_quote: IRS Reporting/Administrative Offset – Provides information to IRS for various reporting requirements which includes IRS tax refund offset to delinquent borrowers
risks.rationale: Incorrect or stale account data can lead to improper financial consequences and reputational harm.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the risk that personal information will remain available long after it is needed for active servicing or reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which records can be breached, misused, or disclosed.

risks.description: The stated work on a public-facing Customer Self Service capability could expose borrower information to a broader audience if not carefully controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
risks.rationale: A public-facing interface can increase exposure risk if authentication, authorization, and data minimization are not tightly designed.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of Social Security Numbers to the minimum necessary and mask or truncate the number wherever full display is not operationally required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of the most sensitive identifier lowers the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Restrict online queries and batch access to role-based, need-to-know users and require additional verification before searching by Social Security Number.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access controls reduce the chance of inappropriate record lookups.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access controls and logging for internal users, support staff, and developers who can access borrower records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing internal access helps prevent unnecessary exposure of borrower data.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and disclosure controls for each external recipient so only the minimum necessary borrower information is sent for the stated purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited disclosures reduce the risk of downstream misuse by external organizations.

mitigations.description: Validate and reconcile account data before IRS and credit bureau reporting, and provide a process to correct disputed borrower information promptly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
mitigations.rationale: Accuracy controls help prevent harmful financial or credit consequences from incorrect reporting.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records truly require indefinite retention and, where permitted by records schedules, delete or archive records that are no longer needed for operational or legal purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention time lowers the amount of personal data exposed over the life of the system.

mitigations.description: Design the public-facing Customer Self Service feature with strong authentication, authorization, and data minimization before it is launched.
mitigations.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
mitigations.rationale: Public access requires stronger controls to prevent unauthorized disclosure of borrower information.

risks.description: PII could be exposed to too many internal users because the system is available to County, State, Regional, and National FLP staff and stores contact information. Broad internal availability increases the chance that staff with no need to know could view or misuse names and contact details.
risks.evidence_quote: The Farm Loan Appraisal System (FLAS) provides County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals in support of Direct and Guaranteed loans.
risks.rationale: A system used by multiple levels of staff creates a need to limit access to only those with a business need.

risks.description: The system may retain PII longer than necessary because the information is kept indefinitely as permanent records. Long-term retention increases the amount of historical contact information available for misuse or accidental disclosure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping PII forever increases exposure duration and the consequences of any future access problem.

risks.description: Manual system input can introduce inaccurate, incomplete, or unnecessary personal data into the record. If staff enter incorrect contact information, it can affect appraisal processing and create privacy harm by maintaining wrong data about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Manual entry is more error-prone than automated collection and can degrade both data quality and privacy protections.

risks.description: Centralizing appraisal-related information in a single enterprise web application can create a larger concentration of PII than a distributed process. If the system is compromised or misused, the impact could extend across many loan cases and staff levels.
risks.evidence_quote: The enterprise web application will help to standardize the loan appraisal process and give the FLP community a user-friendly tool to aid in day to day activities.
risks.rationale: Central repositories increase the impact of any security or access-control failure because more records are exposed at once.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls so each FLP staff level can only view and edit the records needed for its duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access by role reduces the chance of unnecessary internal viewing or misuse of PII.

mitigations.description: Apply periodic records review and purge or archive PII that no longer needs to remain active, consistent with the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Records scheduling supports lawful retention while reducing unnecessary exposure of old data.

mitigations.description: Add validation and supervisory review for manually entered contact information before it is finalized in the system.
mitigations.rationale: Review and validation help catch input errors before they become part of a permanent record.

mitigations.description: Segment the database and apply strong administrative controls, logging, and monitoring around access to the centralized appraisal records.
mitigations.rationale: Additional safeguards are appropriate because a centralized system concentrates the impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system collects and stores highly sensitive identifiers and financial data, creating a significant risk of harm if those records are accessed improperly or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: SSNs/TINs, credit reports, and financial details are highly sensitive and can be misused for identity theft or financial harm.

risks.description: The system includes race, ethnicity, and gender data for loan processing, which creates a risk of sensitive demographic information being exposed or used inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number.
risks.rationale: Demographic data is sensitive personal information and should be tightly limited to avoid unnecessary privacy impact.

risks.description: The system aggregates borrower information from many internal, government, and private sources, increasing the risk that inaccurate or outdated data will affect loan servicing and credit decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS The information is collected directly from farm loan borrower and information is received from other FSA applications, state and local agencies and other third party financial sources. See question 1.2 above
risks.rationale: When data is pulled from multiple sources, errors can propagate and lead to incorrect eligibility, servicing, or restructuring outcomes.

risks.description: The system uses external financial and property-related sources such as credit reporting agencies, tax records, and courthouse records, which creates a risk that data collected for one context will be used more broadly than borrowers expect.
risks.evidence_quote: State and Local Agencies: County offices, Tax records, Courthouse Records (UCC filings) and Deed Recorder. Other Sources: Other lenders, credit reporting agencies, private appraisers, Crop insurance companies, multi list data, Farm Credit System, sales data, Ag Lenders, and business owners.
risks.rationale: Combining data from many external sources can expand the privacy footprint beyond the immediate loan application.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, creating a long-term privacy risk because sensitive borrower data remains available far longer than the active loan relationship may require.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention increases the duration of exposure and the likelihood that old data will be misused or breached.

risks.description: Field office staff and county office staff can process, service, and analyze borrower information, creating an insider-access risk if access is broader than necessary or not carefully controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications and allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
risks.rationale: Systems used by operational staff need strong access controls because insiders can view large amounts of sensitive data.

risks.description: Borrowers can access their FLP account information through the web-based system, which creates a risk of unauthorized account access if authentication or session protections fail.
risks.evidence_quote: allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
risks.rationale: Any producer-facing account portal can expose sensitive loan information if account access is not properly secured.

risks.description: The system uses manual input for debt restructuring and business-plan data entry, creating a risk of human error or inconsistent handling of sensitive borrower information.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual entry increases the chance of mistakes that can affect privacy, accuracy, and decision-making.

risks.description: The system combines financial, employment, and business-planning information to determine credit worthiness and loan eligibility, creating a risk of overly broad profiling of borrowers.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Using detailed personal and financial data for eligibility analysis can create intrusive profiles if not minimized.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to SSNs, TINs, credit reports, and other sensitive fields to staff with a documented need to know, and apply strong authentication and audit logging for all access.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and logging access reduces the chance of improper viewing or misuse of highly sensitive identifiers and financial data.

mitigations.description: Limit demographic fields to the minimum necessary for program administration and mask them in routine views and reports.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing visibility of race, ethnicity, and gender reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive demographic data.

mitigations.description: Validate, reconcile, and periodically review data received from other FSA applications and third-party sources before it is used in servicing or restructuring decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Data quality checks help prevent inaccurate or outdated information from driving adverse loan outcomes.

mitigations.description: Limit use of external source data to clearly defined loan-processing purposes and document why each source is necessary for the specific decision being made.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the privacy impact of combining data from many outside sources.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules that delete or archive records when no longer needed for operational purposes, even if some records are authorized as permanent.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary live retention lowers the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access controls for field office and county office staff and review access rights regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications
mitigations.rationale: Role-based controls help ensure staff can only see the borrower information needed for their duties.

mitigations.description: Require strong user authentication and session protections for producer access to FLP account information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication reduces the risk that someone other than the producer can access the account.

mitigations.description: Use data-entry validation and supervisory review for manually entered restructuring and business-plan information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and review can catch errors introduced during manual entry before they affect privacy or decisions.

mitigations.description: Limit the fields used in credit-worthiness and eligibility analysis to those directly needed for the loan decision and avoid retaining unnecessary analytical outputs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
mitigations.rationale: Using only necessary data for analysis reduces the scope of borrower profiling.

risks.description: Personal data is retained indefinitely, which increases the chance of unnecessary long-term exposure, misuse, or secondary use over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps names and mailing addresses available far longer than needed for day-to-day operations.

risks.description: The system holds personally identifiable information that is used across multiple web-based applications, creating a risk of internal overexposure if access is not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: consists of multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
risks.rationale: Multiple applications increase the number of places where the same personal data may be accessed or handled.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which could expose individuals to premature disclosure or handling of information tied to unapproved materials.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Collecting public input before approval can create privacy and sensitivity concerns if the material is not yet finalized.

risks.description: The system stores mailing addresses for FLOTrack and SDMS users, which creates a risk of unnecessary collection if those addresses are not essential to the stated oversight and workflow purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
