risks.rationale: Mailing addresses are more sensitive than names alone and should be limited to what is necessary.

mitigations.description: Replace indefinite retention with a documented retention schedule that deletes or archives records when they are no longer needed for operations, subject to records requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the period during which personal data can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls so users can only see the names and addresses needed for their specific oversight, training, or workflow duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access within the USDA environment lowers the chance of internal overexposure.

mitigations.description: Do not collect or publish public input tied to directives or policies until the OMB approval process is complete, or clearly segregate unapproved material with limited access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
mitigations.rationale: Delaying or segregating handling of unapproved materials reduces the risk of premature disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of mailing addresses unless they are necessary for the specific application purpose, and remove them where names alone are sufficient.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information held and the harm if it is exposed.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains direct identifiers and contact information that could expose farmers, ranchers, and business partners if mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: ☒ Social Security number ☒ Employee Identification Number ☒ Taxpayer Identification Number ☒ Business Taxpayer Identification Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Personal Mobile Number ☒ Business Mobile Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Name (including nicknames) ☒ Gender ☒ Business Mailing Address (sole proprietor)
risks.rationale: These data elements can directly identify individuals and businesses and create privacy harm if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: The system stores a very large volume of records, increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities
risks.rationale: A larger dataset increases the number of affected people and the consequences of any breach or improper access.

risks.description: Farm, tract, and field boundary data can reveal detailed location and property information about participants.
risks.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
risks.rationale: Location-linked records can expose sensitive information about land holdings and operational patterns when tied to named customers.

risks.description: Historical retention of customer and farm records increases the period during which outdated or unnecessary personal information remains exposed to risk.
risks.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which data can be accessed improperly or become stale and unnecessary.

risks.description: Sharing Farm Record and Business Partner data across USDA agencies creates a risk of broader internal exposure than is needed for a single program purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient expands the number of systems and users that may access the information.

risks.description: Role-based access failures could allow users to view or change records beyond what their job requires.
risks.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
risks.rationale: If access controls are misconfigured or bypassed, sensitive records could be exposed or altered inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of direct identifiers and contact information to only what is required for program administration, and protect it with strong access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The business purpose of the information technology (IT) system is to capture producer and farm records data for farmers and ranchers in the US who have requested to participate in Farm Service Agency (FSA), National Resource Conservation System (NRCS), and other USDA agencies per program requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only program-required data reduces the amount of sensitive information at risk.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access and monitoring to the full dataset so only authorized personnel can access records needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access lowers the likelihood that a large record set is exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit access to geospatial farm boundary data and ensure it is used only for the stated farm-record purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining access to location data reduces the chance of unnecessary disclosure of property and operational details.

mitigations.description: Review retention schedules regularly and archive or dispose of records according to the shortest applicable retention period for each data type and program.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Retention of some data is for shorter periods and varies by data type and by Program.
mitigations.rationale: Applying the shortest lawful retention period reduces the amount of personal data kept over time.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and need-to-know controls for interagency transfers so each recipient receives only the information necessary for program delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared data reduces unnecessary internal exposure while still supporting the stated purpose.

mitigations.description: Continuously review and test role assignments and approval workflows to confirm users can only create, edit, and view records consistent with their responsibilities.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic validation helps prevent overbroad access caused by configuration errors or role drift.

risks.description: The system keeps producer information permanently, which increases the risk of long-term exposure, secondary use, or breach impact over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention lengthens the period during which the information can be misused or compromised.

risks.description: County office users and contractors can access producer data, creating insider misuse or overexposure risk even when access is intended to be limited.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any broad human access path raises the chance of unauthorized viewing or handling of personal data.

risks.description: NAP notifications are physically mailed, which creates a risk that names and addresses could be exposed through printed letters or mail handling.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
risks.rationale: Physical mailing introduces handling points where personal information can be seen, lost, or misdelivered.

risks.description: The system discloses NAP data to other internal systems, which can expand access beyond the original collection purpose and increase the chance of unnecessary sharing.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: System-to-system disclosure can spread personal data to additional environments and users.

risks.description: Producer information is pulled from SCIMS rather than directly from the producer, which creates a risk that outdated or incorrect source data could affect eligibility or payment decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: All PII, however, is pulled from SCIMS and is not requested or received directly from producers.
risks.rationale: Using a source database instead of direct confirmation can propagate inaccuracies into downstream decisions.

risks.description: Payment, overpayment, premium, and revenue-related records can reveal financial status and disaster impacts, creating a sensitivity risk if accessed or inferred by unauthorized parties.
risks.evidence_quote: The LFP-Payments program pays producers authorized for payments through the LFP-Signup software. Processing functions include: • Payment/Overpayment processing
risks.rationale: Financial and loss records are especially sensitive because they expose personal economic circumstances.

risks.description: The system stores and uses producer name and street address across many programs, which increases the amount of identifiable information exposed if any component is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address LFP Name, street address LIP Name, street address NAP Name, street address TAP Name, street address CFAP Name, street address CFAP 2.0 Name, street address QLA Name, street address PARP Name, street address PLIP Name, street address PATHH Name, street address OTECP Name, street address SMHPP Name, street address ELRP Name, street address
risks.rationale: Repeated collection of direct identifiers across programs increases the consequences of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply records minimization and periodic review so only records that must be kept indefinitely remain accessible, with archived records tightly restricted.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing routine access to older records lowers the risk created by permanent retention.

mitigations.description: Keep the stated need-to-know approval, background investigation, Level 2 eAuthentication, and NDA controls for all contractor access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know approval and authentication reduce the chance of unnecessary insider access.

mitigations.description: Limit mailing to the minimum necessary information and use controlled print-and-mail handling procedures for NAP letters.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing printed content and controlling mail handling reduces exposure during physical delivery.

mitigations.description: Restrict disclosures to only the internal systems that need the data and document the purpose of each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting system-to-system sharing reduces unnecessary spread of personal data.

mitigations.description: Validate SCIMS-derived data before use and provide a correction process when producer information appears inconsistent.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All PII, however, is pulled from SCIMS and is not requested or received directly from producers.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction help prevent inaccurate source data from driving decisions.

mitigations.description: Apply stronger access controls and audit logging to payment, overpayment, premium, and revenue-related records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Retain producer payment history information
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced controls are appropriate because these records reveal sensitive financial information.

mitigations.description: Protect names and street addresses with role-based access and avoid unnecessary duplication across components.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name, street address
mitigations.rationale: Limiting copies and access points reduces the chance that direct identifiers will be exposed.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data that could cause harm if exposed, including names, mailing addresses, SSNs/EINs, farm tract numbers, and payment amounts.
risks.evidence_quote: ARCPLC Name, mailing address, last 4 digits SSN SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly identifying and financially sensitive, so unauthorized disclosure would create privacy and fraud risks.

risks.description: The system may expose PII to a broad internal user base because it is accessible to National, State, and County Office FSA employees through a shared database.
risks.evidence_quote: using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: Even a limited internal audience increases the chance of unnecessary access or misuse of personal data.

risks.description: Because ARC/PLC displays PII retrieved from SCIMS rather than collecting it directly, errors in the source data could be shown to users and affect eligibility or sign-up decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
risks.rationale: Displaying source data without local validation can propagate inaccurate records into eligibility workflows.

risks.description: Permanent retention of records increases the long-term exposure of personal data and the chance of future misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: The longer sensitive data is kept, the longer it remains available for unauthorized access or secondary use.

risks.description: The system’s use of payment history and earnings-related records can reveal detailed financial behavior about producers over time.
risks.evidence_quote: retaining producer payment history information, producer payment history print and payment registers, producer earnings report
risks.rationale: Longitudinal payment records can disclose sensitive economic status and participation in assistance programs.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the minimum necessary users and enforce strong authentication and role-based access controls for records containing SSNs/EINs, addresses, and payment data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that highly sensitive identifiers are viewed or misused unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Continue restricting the shared database to only the minimum set of National, State, and County Office FSA employees who need the data for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the audience directly reduces internal exposure of PII.

mitigations.description: Add a data-quality review step or periodic reconciliation against SCIMS so users can correct inaccurate identity or eligibility information before it is relied on.
mitigations.rationale: Validating source data before use helps prevent incorrect personal information from affecting program decisions.

mitigations.description: Apply records management controls to periodically review whether all permanently retained records remain necessary and whether any records can be archived or otherwise limited under the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Even with an approved schedule, periodic review can reduce unnecessary exposure of old records.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to payment history and earnings reports to users with a clear program need and provide handling guidance for these sensitive financial records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: retaining producer payment history information, producer payment history print and payment registers, producer earnings report
mitigations.rationale: Payment histories are sensitive financial information, so tighter access and handling reduce privacy risk.

risks.description: The system exposes highly sensitive identifiers, including EIN and SSN, which could cause serious harm if viewed by unauthorized users or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: • EIN / SSN (via a search screen)
risks.rationale: Sensitive identifiers increase the impact of any unauthorized access because they can be used for identity theft or improper verification.

risks.description: County office users can search for a specific farmer or producer using PII, which creates a risk of unnecessary access or lookup of records without a legitimate need.
risks.evidence_quote: the FSAfarm+ application uses PII to allow county office users to search for a specific farmer or producer.
risks.rationale: Search capability over personal data can expose information to users who do not need it for the task at hand.

risks.description: Using SSN as a second authentication method creates a risk that a sensitive identifier is overused for authentication and exposed during login or verification.
risks.evidence_quote: If a farmer or producer has an eAuth account, the SSN can be used as a second authentication method to validate the farmer / producer
risks.rationale: Authentication workflows that rely on SSN can increase the chance of disclosure or misuse of that identifier.

risks.description: Contractor access to the system creates a risk that support personnel could see or mishandle PII while assisting the application.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any non-user access path increases the number of people who may encounter the data and therefore the chance of improper access.

risks.description: PII is pulled from SCIMS in another system, which creates a risk of unauthorized exposure during retrieval or of relying on data outside FSCOMS’s direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: FSAfarm+ requests and receives PII from SCIMS, which resides in the FPCMS system.
risks.rationale: Cross-system retrieval increases the attack surface and depends on the security of the source system and the transfer path.

risks.description: Although the system says it clears memory and cache on logout, PII may still be exposed during a session if a user fails to log out properly or if the clearing fails.
risks.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: Session-resident data can remain accessible until logout or successful cache clearing, so failures in that process can expose data.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to EIN and SSN to only the minimum users and use masking or partial display where full values are not needed.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting visibility of sensitive identifiers reduces the harm from unauthorized viewing or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access and need-to-know controls for county office searches so users can only search records necessary for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting search capability to authorized job functions reduces unnecessary exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Replace SSN-based second authentication with a less sensitive verification factor or add stronger controls around its use.
mitigations.rationale: Using a less sensitive factor lowers the chance that SSNs are disclosed or misused during authentication.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be time-limited, logged, and approved only for specific support tasks involving FSCOMS/FSAfarm+.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the likelihood that support access becomes unnecessary or excessive.

mitigations.description: Protect requests and responses between FSAfarm+ and SCIMS with strong access controls and monitoring.
mitigations.rationale: Securing cross-system retrieval helps prevent unauthorized exposure of PII while it is being obtained from the source system.

mitigations.description: Ensure automatic logout and cache-clearing are tested and verified so session-resident PII is reliably removed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
mitigations.rationale: Verifying the stated clearing behavior reduces the chance that PII remains available after a session ends.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains sensitive demographic information, including ethnicity and race, which could expose producers to privacy harm if mishandled or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: Race and ethnicity are sensitive personal data, so storing them increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system stores producers' names and mailing addresses to build and send ballot mailings, creating a risk of unwanted disclosure of contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
risks.rationale: Mailing lists necessarily expose contact details, which could be misused if access controls fail.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to determine eligibility to vote in committee elections, which could lead to unfair exclusion or inclusion if the underlying data are inaccurate.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes recorded in the name and address file.
risks.rationale: Eligibility decisions depend on the accuracy of the source data, so errors could affect a producer's participation rights.

risks.description: The system maintains election results and COC member data, which could create a persistent record of individuals' participation and committee affiliation over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Track Election results and COC Member data.
risks.rationale: Long-term retention of participation records can reveal ongoing political or organizational involvement.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, increasing the exposure window for any future unauthorized access or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention means the data remain available for misuse far longer than necessary for a single election cycle.

risks.description: County office staff enter producer data into the system, creating a risk of unauthorized internal access or improper handling during collection and entry.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry by staff can expose data to insider mistakes or misuse.

mitigations.description: Limit access to race and ethnicity fields to only staff who need them for the stated election functions, and audit access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive demographic data will be viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Protect ballot mailing lists with role-based access controls and minimize the use of mailing information to only the ballot-printing function.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can view or export mailing data reduces the risk of contact information disclosure.

mitigations.description: Validate and periodically review committee and LAA code records against source records before eligibility decisions are made.
mitigations.rationale: Checking the source data helps prevent incorrect voting eligibility determinations.

mitigations.description: Apply retention and access controls to election results and COC member records so only authorized personnel can view historical participation data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to historical election records lowers the risk of long-term tracking or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records are still required for operational purposes and, where allowed by the approved schedule, limit retention to the minimum necessary period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary retention lowers the amount of data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Train county office staff on proper handling of producer information and require supervisory review of entered records.
mitigations.rationale: Training and review reduce the risk of staff mishandling data during collection and entry.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal identifiers and financial data, so a breach or improper access could expose individuals to identity theft, fraud, or other harm.
risks.evidence_quote: Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly identifying and financially sensitive, so unauthorized disclosure would have significant privacy impact.

risks.description: Consolidating data from multiple programs and source systems into a central warehouse increases the risk that information will be used or accessed beyond the original purpose for which it was collected.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV defines, collects, validates, and stores data from various computer sources for each application to provide business users a single source for data used to resolve business inquiries.
risks.rationale: Centralized aggregation makes it easier to combine data across contexts, which can expand access and secondary use.

risks.description: Broad reporting access for national, state, and county personnel creates a risk of unnecessary internal exposure to personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV is a consolidated data warehouse that provides information to FSA national, state, and county personnel.
risks.rationale: Wider internal availability increases the number of users who may see data they do not need.

risks.description: Batch transfers from source systems to the warehouse create a risk that personal data could be intercepted, corrupted, or improperly disclosed during transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems shares the information through batch processes.
risks.rationale: Bulk transfers are a common point of exposure if transport and handling controls are weak.

risks.description: Sharing information with other federal agencies and external entities creates a risk of disclosure beyond the originating system's direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases information is collected via other federal agencies which provide this information to the FSA.
risks.rationale: Once data is exchanged across organizations, privacy protections depend on multiple parties' controls.

risks.description: Using the data for Congressional, program level, and end user reporting may reveal more personal information than individuals expect from the original collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the EDW is used for Congressional, program level and end user reporting.
risks.rationale: Reporting can expose personal details in aggregated or individualized outputs if minimization is not enforced.

risks.description: Keeping the data under the NARA retention schedule without a clearly defined archiving strategy in the description creates a risk of retaining personal information longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Retention that is not tightly implemented can extend exposure time and increase the impact of any later misuse or breach.

risks.description: Name and address validation sharing with external parties can expose personal contact information to entities that may not need the full underlying record.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Even limited validation sharing still discloses identifiable contact data outside the agency.

mitigations.description: Apply strict access controls and encryption for sensitive identifiers and financial data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the most sensitive fields reduces the harm if data is accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Limit warehouse access and reporting views to the minimum data needed for each business purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the privacy impact of central aggregation.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access controls and need-to-know permissions for national, state, and county personnel.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access by role lowers the chance that users see data outside their duties.

mitigations.description: Protect batch transfers with secure transport, integrity checks, and monitoring for failed or unusual loads.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer controls reduce the risk of interception or tampering during bulk movement.

mitigations.description: Use written data-sharing agreements and confirm recipient privacy safeguards before exchanging information with other agencies or external entities.
mitigations.rationale: Formal controls help ensure recipients handle shared data consistently with the original privacy protections.

mitigations.description: Review reporting outputs to suppress unnecessary personal identifiers and provide only the minimum information needed for the report.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report content reduces disclosure through routine analytics and reporting.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce retention and deletion procedures so records are removed or archived when the NARA schedule allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A clear retention process limits how long personal data remains exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Limit validation exchanges to the minimum fields needed, such as only name and address, and document the one-time purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing shared fields reduces unnecessary disclosure in external validation activities.

risks.description: The system stores a broad mix of highly sensitive personal and financial data, so unauthorized access or misuse could expose identity, banking, payment, debt, and tax information. This includes SSNs/TINs, bank account and routing numbers, and debt-related records for producers and vendors.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is collected, used, disseminated or maintained in the system. CORE The CORE system occasionally contains Name as a DSUB fields. The CORE system almost never contains SSN. It won’t contain SSN once the FSFL system is converted to DSL and no longer sends to CORE. FDIS Images could contain information such as: Name, street address, SSN/TIN, phone number, Claim/NRRS number, agency case number, promissory number. bank account number, schedule of deposit numbers and image of the signature. FI Name, SSN/TIN, financial institution account number, check number, and routing number.
risks.rationale: Because the system aggregates multiple sensitive identifiers and financial attributes, a compromise would have broad privacy impact.

risks.description: Public-facing and online inquiry functions can expose detailed financial information to the wrong person if access controls or authentication are weak. The system provides producers and county office employees access to summary and detailed financial information online.
risks.evidence_quote: The Financial Inquiry Web Application (FI) ... is a web application designed to provide access to a producer's financial information on- line. ... Producers have access to both summary and detailed information. County Office employees also have access to FI so employees can answer producer's questions and view financial information in the same format the producer is viewing.
risks.rationale: Detailed online access increases the chance that unauthorized users could see sensitive account and debt information.

risks.description: The system allows producers and farmers to update banking and assignment information, creating a risk of account takeover or fraudulent changes if identity verification is insufficient. Incorrect changes could redirect payments or alter financial instructions.
risks.evidence_quote: The Financial Services System resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is public facing, with producers and farmers able to update their own information (i.e. banking and assignment information).
risks.rationale: If an attacker or impersonator can change banking data, the privacy and financial harm to the subject can be immediate and significant.

risks.description: Paper, faxed, scanned, and imaged documents can expose personal data if they are mishandled during capture, storage, or retrieval. The system explicitly stores financial information images and accepts data from document storage, fax, and scanned materials.
risks.evidence_quote: FDIS Images could contain information such as: Name, street address, SSN/TIN, phone number, Claim/NRRS number, agency case number, promissory number. bank account number, schedule of deposit numbers and image of the signature.
risks.rationale: Document imaging and fax/scanned inputs create opportunities for accidental disclosure beyond the core application.

risks.description: Debt collection and delinquency functions can disclose sensitive debt status to Treasury, collection agencies, and credit bureaus, which may affect subjects beyond the original payment purpose. This includes reporting delinquent debt for creditworthiness.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected and used by the Receivable Systems to offset Federal payments, wage garnishment, and referral to collection agencies. Also, the information is used to report delinquent debt for the purposes of creditworthiness. Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
risks.rationale: Sharing debt status with collection and credit entities increases the privacy impact of the data and the consequences of any disclosure.

risks.description: Tax reporting and earnings statements expose payment history to the IRS and other recipients, which can reveal income-related information about producers. This creates privacy risk if the data is shared more broadly than necessary or if statements are intercepted.
risks.evidence_quote: Payment data is summarized and provided to the IRS for payments made to producers. A statement of earnings is prepared for each producer for tax reporting purposes.
risks.rationale: Income and tax information is highly sensitive and can be misused if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a risk that non-government personnel could view or handle sensitive records during assigned duties. Even with restrictions, contractors are still granted access to the applications and data.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the number of people who can see sensitive personal and financial data.

risks.description: Permanent retention of sensitive records increases the harm if data is later breached, misused, or accessed without authorization. The system retains the information indefinitely.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention keeps sensitive data available for a much longer period, increasing cumulative privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive fields by role and apply data minimization so users only see the identifiers and financial details needed for their task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to necessary data reduces the chance of unauthorized exposure of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and role-based authorization for FI, and restrict detailed views to users with a demonstrated business need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: County Office employees also have access to FI so employees can answer producer's questions and view financial information in the same format the producer is viewing.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter authentication and authorization reduce the risk of unauthorized viewing of detailed financial information.

mitigations.description: Add step-up verification or dual approval before any banking or assignment updates take effect.
mitigations.rationale: Extra verification would reduce the chance that fraudulent or mistaken changes redirect payments or alter financial instructions.

mitigations.description: Encrypt stored images and enforce secure handling procedures for faxed, scanned, and document-storage inputs, including restricted access to image repositories.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FDIS resides at NITC, however is hosted by CEC Client Services and is a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) client-server Major Application (MA) that stores financial information images in the form of Tiff files.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting imaged documents at rest and during handling reduces the chance of accidental or unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize debt disclosures to only the recipients necessary for collection, and keep encrypted transmission for any external debt-status sharing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting recipients and encrypting transmissions reduces the privacy impact of debt reporting.

mitigations.description: Limit tax-reporting disclosures to the minimum required by law and protect statements during generation and delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Payment data is summarized and provided to the IRS for payments made to producers. A statement of earnings is prepared for each producer for tax reporting purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and protecting tax disclosures reduces unnecessary exposure of income-related information.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen contractor controls, including background investigations, Level 2 eAuthentication, NDAs, and rules prohibiting downloading, sharing, storing, or printing USDA data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access - As part of the FPAC onboarding process, contractors must meet all requirements for access to applications. Through the USDA Rules of Behavior, they are not allowed to download, share, store or print any USDA specific data. - All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management - Contractors are required to sign NDAs as per the USDA FPAC BC Onboarding process
mitigations.rationale: These controls directly reduce the likelihood that contractor access leads to improper disclosure.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records truly need indefinite retention and dispose of records when no longer required by the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention where legally permissible lowers the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system holds employee identity and contact information that could be exposed if access controls are too broad or misconfigured. Because the data is used to manage role-based access, unauthorized access could reveal who has access to which applications and how to reach them.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS Name & mailing address
risks.rationale: Name and mailing address are personally identifiable and should be protected from unnecessary access.

risks.description: The system maintains authorization data about users’ roles, groups, offices, and attributes, which can reveal employees' organizational relationships and access privileges. If disclosed improperly, this could enable profiling of internal access rights or targeted attacks against users with elevated permissions.
risks.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes to business applications
risks.rationale: Access-rights data is sensitive because it can expose internal structure and privilege information.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, creating a long-term accumulation of personal and authorization data. Over-retention increases the amount of data available for misuse or breach and may preserve information longer than needed for the access-control purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases exposure time and the potential harm from any future access incident.

risks.description: The system supports administrators who can manage security access rights in real time, which creates a risk of inappropriate role changes or insider misuse. If administrative actions are not tightly controlled and audited, users could gain or lose access improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS allows administrators to use a web browser to manage security access rights, assigning and removing roles/groups/attributes to users on-line in real time.
risks.rationale: Real-time administrative changes can affect many users quickly and require strong oversight.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to employee name and mailing address to only personnel with a documented need to administer access control, and log all access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that identity data is viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions to the authorization data itself so only authorized administrators can view or modify roles, groups, offices, and attributes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Facilitate Role-Based Access Control system.
mitigations.rationale: The stated purpose supports using role-based controls to protect sensitive access-rights data.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether all permanently retained records are still required and delete or archive any data no longer needed under the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: A records review process helps ensure retention remains limited to what the schedule requires.

mitigations.description: Require change logging and supervisory review for administrative role assignments and removals, with periodic audits of access changes.
mitigations.rationale: Auditability and review help detect and deter improper privilege changes.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive personal data, so any unauthorized access could expose identity, financial, health, biometric, or criminal history information. This increases the impact of a breach because the system includes multiple forms of directly identifying and sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Full name, mother’s maiden name, maiden f h i di id l i k li ) Date and/or place of birth. Address Information (street & email address). Personal identification number (social security number, tax identification number, passport number, driver’s license number or a unique identification number, etc.) Financial data (Credit card numbers, bank account etc.) Health data (including height, weight, blood pressure, etc.) Biometric data (fingerprints, iris scans, voice signature, facial geometry, DNA, etc.) Criminal history Employment history Miscellaneous identification numbers (agency assigned number, case number, accounts, permits, etc.) Photographic image/identifying characteristics. Handwriting or an image of the signature
risks.rationale: The broader and more sensitive the stored data, the greater the harm if confidentiality is lost.

risks.description: Browser-based access to stored images could allow unauthorized viewing if access controls are weak or misconfigured. Because the system allows client access from a desktop browser, a user may reach large volumes of records remotely within the network.
risks.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.rationale: Browser access expands the attack surface and makes strong authentication and authorization essential.

risks.description: Faxed and scanned documents entering the system may be misdirected, intercepted, or improperly handled before storage. The system accepts data from faxed and scanned materials, which can expose records during ingestion.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from electronically stored documents, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Document ingestion channels are common points for accidental disclosure and should be tightly controlled.

risks.description: Workflow functionality can expose sensitive records to more users or process steps than are necessary for simple retrieval. Because FileNet controls workflows associated with the financial information being imaged, data may be routed through multiple internal processes.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.rationale: Workflow routing can create unnecessary internal exposure unless access is minimized by role.

risks.description: Indefinite retention increases the chance that outdated records will remain available long after they are needed. Permanent storage of sensitive records makes any future compromise more damaging and prolongs exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases cumulative exposure time and the potential impact of later misuse or breach.

risks.description: Imported Federal Reserve Bank images and archived check records could be exposed if retrieval functions are misused or over-broad. The system stores and retrieves historical check images and related information, which may be highly sensitive financial records.
risks.evidence_quote: KCFRB Imaging (FRB) check images are downloaded and imported in the system. It is used to store and view FRB check images and pertinent information on CCC checks.
risks.rationale: Historical financial images remain sensitive and need strict retrieval controls even when no new content is added.

risks.description: The presence of multiple subsystem types and mixed data sources increases the risk of inconsistent protection across components. Different subsystems are read-only, workflow-enabled, or input-capable, which can lead to uneven security controls and accidental overexposure.
risks.evidence_quote: KCFRB only makes calls to the IBM/FileNet Content Process Engine to retrieve images for display. It has no workflow function. Receivable Case Management Application is a FileNet imaging system which allows the input of documents for storage and retrieval.
risks.rationale: When components have different functions, security controls must be consistent to avoid the weakest link exposing records.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive records using role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions for each subsystem and workflow step.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can see each record reduces the impact of unauthorized access to highly sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication for browser access and log all access to stored images for review and anomaly detection.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and auditability help prevent and detect unauthorized viewing through the web interface.

mitigations.description: Secure fax and scanning intake with validated transmission endpoints, controlled ingestion procedures, and verification of document destination before import.
mitigations.rationale: Controls at intake reduce the chance that sensitive documents are intercepted or sent to the wrong place.

mitigations.description: Configure workflow routes so only users with a business need can access records at each step, and minimize the number of workflow participants.
mitigations.rationale: Workflow-specific access limits unnecessary exposure during processing.

mitigations.description: Review whether all permanent records still need indefinite retention and apply records schedules and archival controls to minimize active exposure where allowed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Records scheduling is the stated control for retention and helps ensure records are kept only as required.

mitigations.description: Limit retrieval of archived check images to authorized users and monitor access to historical financial records.
mitigations.rationale: Historical records remain sensitive, so access controls and monitoring reduce the risk of misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply a common security baseline across all FileNet subsystems so read-only and workflow-enabled components are protected consistently.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent controls prevent weaker subsystem configurations from becoming a path to broader disclosure.

risks.description: Users may see more personal information than is necessary because FA Tracker displays work lists containing names, addresses, and detailed contract and eligibility status fields. Even though the system says it shows minimal information, the field set still includes sensitive operational and compliance details tied to individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII that is used, processed or maintained by FA Tracker includes name, address, as well as the following: o Application # o Contract # o Contract Item # o State o County o Field Office o Number of days until/passed a specific date of interest o Contract Modification Reason o Contract Modification Status o Status of a Payment (E.g. "Waiting for participant signed date") o Other Eligibility (Yes/No) o AD-1026 (Y/N) o FTE (Y/N) o AGI (Y/N) o Member AGI (%) o Vendor Code (E.g. "Pending") o Application Status (E.g. "Eligible") o Adequacy Status (E.g. "Pending") o Obligation Status (E.g. "Pending")
risks.rationale: The breadth of displayed fields increases the chance of unnecessary disclosure about applicants and landowners.

risks.description: Client-side filtering and sorting can expose personal data on a user's device or through unintended local handling. Because the user can manipulate the work list locally, sensitive records may be more easily copied, cached, or observed outside controlled system boundaries.
risks.evidence_quote: A user can then filter and sort this data on the client side. Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Local processing increases the chance that data leaves the protected web application environment.

risks.description: Exporting work lists to Excel on a device creates a risk of uncontrolled local copies of PII. Once exported, the data may be stored, shared, or retained outside the system's access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Device exports are harder to govern than data kept inside the application.

risks.description: E-mail alerts can disclose personal data if messages are misdirected, forwarded, or accessed from insecure mail systems or devices. The alerts contain the same data and fields as the work lists, so the risk includes repeated exposure of the same PII over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
risks.rationale: Email is a common channel for accidental disclosure and persistent copies.

risks.description: Users with access to ProTracts-FundManager may gain access to FA Tracker data, which can broaden access to PII beyond the minimum necessary. This creates a risk that contractors or other authorized users may see records they do not need for their specific duties.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Shared access across systems can widen the audience for sensitive records.

risks.description: The system relies on replicated SCIMS data, so any compromise or misuse of the copy could expose customer information beyond the source system. Because FA Tracker uses a database copy rather than direct source access, there is an additional data store containing PII that must be protected.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via the National Planning and Agreements Database (NPAD) [which resides on PT-FM] and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: Replicated copies expand the attack surface and the number of places PII can be exposed.

risks.description: The system processes race, sex, national origin, and disability information through SCIMS-related reporting capabilities, which could create sensitivity and discrimination concerns if accessed inappropriately. Even if FA Tracker itself is mainly for work lists, the underlying source includes highly sensitive demographic data.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Sensitive demographic data requires tighter controls because misuse can cause significant harm.

risks.description: Although the system says access is constrained by zRoles and eAuth, any failure in those controls could expose records beyond a user's authorization level. Because the system displays real-time data and links to additional details, unauthorized access would reveal current applicant and contract information.
risks.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
risks.rationale: Role-based access controls are essential because the system contains identifiable and status-based records.

mitigations.description: Limit work lists to the minimum fields needed for PSS intervention and keep additional details behind the PT-FM link only when necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used to identify and classify Applications, Contracts, and Contract items in need of PSS intervention. FA Tracker does this by running specific queries over the data and displays minimal information to users in the form of work lists.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing displayed fields reduces unnecessary exposure of personal and program data.

mitigations.description: Apply client-side controls that prevent caching or persistence of filtered work lists and ensure users are reminded that local manipulation may expose data on their device.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing local persistence lowers the risk that device-level handling exposes PII outside the system.

mitigations.description: Restrict or disable Excel export for users who do not need it, and if export is allowed, require approved secure storage and handling of the file.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling exports reduces the chance that PII is copied into unmanaged local files.

mitigations.description: Send e-mail alerts only to verified recipients and limit the content to the smallest necessary subset of fields, with clear handling rules for the messages.
mitigations.rationale: Recipient verification and content minimization reduce the chance of accidental disclosure through email.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing need-to-know approval process and review PT-FM-linked access regularly to ensure users only receive FA Tracker access when required for their role.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps ensure shared system access does not become overbroad.

mitigations.description: Protect the replicated SCIMS copy with strong access controls, encryption, and monitoring, and limit access to established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Strong controls on the replicated copy reduce the risk of exposure from a secondary data store.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened access restrictions and audit logging to reports or views that can expose race, sex, national origin, or disability information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Sensitive demographic information warrants tighter controls and traceability.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing zRoles and eAuthentication, and periodically test that the access constraints still limit each user to records they are authorized to see.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
mitigations.rationale: Verifying role enforcement helps prevent unauthorized disclosure of current records.

risks.description: External users can access the online application over the Internet, creating a risk that personal and financial information could be exposed if access controls are weak or an account is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
risks.rationale: Internet-facing access increases the chance of unauthorized viewing or manipulation of the information held for program participants.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of broader internal disclosure or misuse of participant and employee contact and banking information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
risks.rationale: Any additional user population increases the number of people who can see sensitive records and the chance of misuse.

risks.description: Nightly files are used to create ad hoc queries and canned reports posted to the intranet, which could expose more information than needed to internal users.
risks.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA.
risks.rationale: Reporting and warehouse use can broaden access beyond the minimum necessary if outputs are not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Reports are submitted to auditors and other departments, creating a risk that information could be further disclosed or reused outside the original program context.
risks.evidence_quote: however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the chance of secondary disclosure or use beyond the initial purpose.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, which increases the risk that personal and financial data will remain available longer than necessary and be exposed in a future breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window during which data can be accessed, misused, or lost.

risks.description: The system collects tax identification numbers and payment bank information, which creates a risk of financial harm if those records are improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions
risks.rationale: Financial identifiers can be used for fraud or unauthorized financial activity if exposed.

risks.description: The system collects names, email addresses, and phone numbers for multiple external parties, creating a risk of contact information exposure and unwanted contact.
risks.evidence_quote: Point of contact names, email addresses, and phone numbers for exporters, US financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks.
risks.rationale: Contact data can be misused for phishing, spam, or other unwanted communications.

risks.description: The system also stores names and business email addresses for USDA employees and contractors, which could expose staff identities and business contact details if the system is improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: Names and business email addresses for USDA employees and contractors who are users of the GSM system
risks.rationale: Employee and contractor contact details can be sensitive when linked to system access and business roles.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong authentication, role-based access controls, and logging for the public-facing GSM interface so users can access only their own program records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to specific records reduces the chance of unauthorized exposure through the Internet-facing application.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary and require access approval, training, and periodic review of contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and reviewing contractor access reduces the likelihood of unnecessary disclosure or misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and output review to nightly files, ad hoc reports, and canned reports before posting them to the intranet.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing outputs and limiting fields reduces unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Share only the minimum necessary report data with auditors and other departments and document the permitted purpose for each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited sharing reduces secondary use and further disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review and disposition process even for permanent records so information is retained only as long as needed and archived securely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review and secure archival reduce the amount of active data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Protect tax identification numbers and payment bank information with encryption, strict access controls, and monitoring for unusual access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards are warranted because financial identifiers can cause harm if disclosed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to contact information and use it only for program administration and communication related to the export guarantee programs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Point of contact names, email addresses, and phone numbers for exporters, US financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting use and access reduces the chance of misuse of contact details.

mitigations.description: Apply the same access controls and need-to-know restrictions to USDA employee and contractor contact information as to participant records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Names and business email addresses for USDA employees and contractors who are users of the GSM system
mitigations.rationale: Protecting staff contact details helps prevent unnecessary exposure of internal personnel information.

risks.description: The system may expose highly sensitive personal information if access is misused or overly broad, because it stores documents containing identifiers, financial data, criminal history, signatures, and other PII.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box contains documents stored in a file repository that may include a wide range of PII.
risks.rationale: A repository holding many sensitive data elements creates meaningful harm if access controls fail or are abused.

risks.description: Authorized users can share PII with employees, contractors, affiliates, and partners, which increases the chance of unintended disclosure beyond the minimum necessary audience.
risks.evidence_quote: PII information is shared with FPAC employees, contractors, and partners when deemed required to complete assigned task.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient group increases the number of people who can see sensitive records.

risks.description: Because sharing is described as a manual process, users may accidentally disclose files to the wrong person or share more than intended.
risks.evidence_quote: this ‘sharing’ is a manual process of authorized users accessing the data files, and not an automated function of the FPAC Box system/application.
risks.rationale: Manual sharing creates a human-error risk that can lead to improper disclosure.

risks.description: The system retains records for long periods, which can keep PII available longer than needed and increase the impact of any later breach or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which stored PII can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: PII available through third-party applications is not periodically purged, so outdated or unnecessary personal data may remain accessible indefinitely.
risks.evidence_quote: 10.6 Is the PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications purged periodically? • No
risks.rationale: If stale data is not removed, it remains exposed without a continuing business need.

risks.description: Storing PII in a vendor-managed cloud service creates a dependency on the third-party provider to maintain and secure the data.
risks.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
risks.rationale: Vendor control introduces privacy risk if the provider's safeguards or operations are insufficient.

risks.description: The system can be used to disseminate public information, which could lead to accidental release of documents that contain PII if files are not properly classified before sharing.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box can be used to disseminate public information such as documents, PDF forms, diagrams or announcement details.
risks.rationale: A platform used for public dissemination can inadvertently expose private content if users misfile or mislabel documents.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive files using role-based authorization, eAuthentication, DRM, and encryption in transit and at rest.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to FPAC Box is controlled through role-based authorization, eAuthentication, and DRM, which includes FIPS 140-2 certified encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting data cryptographically reduces the chance that sensitive PII is exposed.

mitigations.description: Enforce need-to-know access reviews so only authorized employees, contractors, affiliates, and partners receive the minimum data required for the task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII information is stored within FPAC Box and shared with authorized USDA employees, contractors, and affiliates with a need-to-know to conduct the business of the organization.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access limits unnecessary disclosure to additional recipients.

mitigations.description: Add sharing confirmations and periodic user training to reduce mistaken manual disclosure of files.
mitigations.rationale: Manual sharing is vulnerable to user error, so extra confirmation and training would reduce accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules and disable accounts when users leave so records are not retained longer than required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017. ... If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
mitigations.rationale: Following approved retention limits and disabling departed users' accounts reduces unnecessary long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic purge or deletion controls for PII in third-party applications.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic purging would remove stale personal data that otherwise remains accessible indefinitely.

mitigations.description: Use vendor oversight, contractual security requirements, and periodic security reviews for Box Inc. to verify the cloud provider protects stored PII.
mitigations.rationale: Because the vendor maintains the data, oversight helps ensure the provider's safeguards remain adequate.

mitigations.description: Require users to verify that files intended for public dissemination contain no PII before publishing them.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-publication checks help prevent private information from being released as public content.

risks.description: User information sent through the pass-through could be exposed during transmission to DOL, USCIS, or Login.gov if transport security fails.
risks.evidence_quote: As a result, information will be sent to (and from) users (farmers and producers) to DOL and USCIS, even though FPAC CASP / H2A does not assess or perform any actions on the data.
risks.rationale: The system forwards user data to external agencies, so any weakness in transit protection could disclose that data.

risks.description: The stored DOL case number could be misused to retrieve or link a producer's inquiry if it is accessed by an unauthorized party.
risks.evidence_quote: The only user information that is stored on FPAC CASP is a producer’s DOL case number; this information does not identify the specific user or contain any user information. This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
risks.rationale: Even limited retained identifiers can enable access to related case information if improperly used.

risks.description: Because the system is a single entry point to multiple federal agencies, it may collect or pass more information than necessary for the H2A function.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is, however, used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: A common entry point can increase the amount of data exposed through one interface beyond what the system itself needs to store.

risks.description: Users' inquiry data may be exposed to external agencies beyond USDA's direct control, creating a privacy dependency on third-party handling.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: When data is handled by external recipients, privacy depends on those recipients' handling and safeguards.

risks.description: If the stored case number is retained longer than needed or not properly purged, it could create unnecessary persistence of a user-linked record.
risks.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
risks.rationale: Retention increases the time window in which a stored reference can be accessed or misused.

mitigations.description: Continue to require HTTPS for all communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov, and verify that certificate validation is enforced.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov occur using HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: HTTPS is the stated control for protecting data in transit, so enforcing it reduces interception risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the stored DOL case number to only authorized users and protect it with strong authentication and logging.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that a retained case number can be used to retrieve inquiry information.

mitigations.description: Minimize the information passed through the common entry point to only what is required for the user to access DOL or USCIS.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information exposed through the shared access path.

mitigations.description: Establish and document clear data-sharing controls with DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov, including purpose limitation and handling requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Formal controls help ensure external recipients handle forwarded information consistently with the stated purpose.

mitigations.description: Delete the stored DOL case number as soon as it is no longer needed, and verify the 90-day retention period is enforced.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention limits the period during which the stored reference exists and can be accessed.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial information, including SSNs, tax IDs, bank routing numbers, deposit account numbers, and records about producers, employees, and contractors, creating a high-impact breach risk if the data is exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
risks.rationale: A compromise would expose highly sensitive identifiers and financial details that can cause serious harm to affected individuals.

risks.description: DRMS allows all staff to upload and search documents, which can expose personal information to more users than necessary if role restrictions are not tightly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights.
risks.rationale: Broad search and upload capability increases the chance that users will encounter PII beyond their legitimate need.

risks.description: Specialized records-manager and legal-staff functions allow unconstrained searching for audit, legal discovery, litigation holds, and FOIA inquiries, which increases the risk of over-disclosure of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Unconstrained searching can surface more personal information than is necessary for a given request or case.

risks.description: TeamMate+ data can be uploaded directly by customers or, in rare cases, by auditors, creating a risk that inaccurate or unnecessary personal information is introduced into the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
risks.rationale: Multiple upload paths increase the chance of collecting or retaining incorrect or excessive PII.

risks.description: Contractors have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod, so personal information may be exposed to non-federal personnel with a need-to-know.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond federal staff increases the number of people who can view sensitive records.

risks.description: Records are retained for long periods and many applications retain information indefinitely, which increases the duration over which personal data could be misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window of risk and makes later misuse or breach more consequential.
