risks.description: The system may still contain indirectly identifying information even though direct identifiers are not required, creating a re-identification risk when combined with other data fields.
risks.evidence_quote: HMDA does not require the reporting of PII that directly identifies an applicant or borrower, and staff commentary to Regulation C applicable to data collected in 2017 strongly discourages institutions from including in identification numbers names or social security numbers, which are direct identifiers.
risks.rationale: A dataset can still be identifying through combinations of non-direct identifiers and contextual details.

mitigations.description: Limit access to age and credit score fields to only personnel and systems that need them for HMDA reporting and oversight, and apply the stated CFPB privacy protections and security controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Are there controls to enforce accountability? Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access and using existing controls reduces the chance that sensitive financial attributes are exposed.

mitigations.description: Collect disaggregated race and ethnicity only as required for HMDA reporting and protect it with strict access controls and standard CFPB privacy protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Are there controls to enforce accountability? Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access to sensitive demographic data lowers the risk of inappropriate disclosure.

mitigations.description: Release only the specific data elements required by Regulation C and suppress or aggregate fields that could make public records easier to link to individuals.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the granularity of public outputs lowers re-identification risk while still supporting disclosure requirements.

mitigations.description: Apply strong retention limits and deletion schedules to HMDA records once reporting and oversight needs are satisfied.
mitigations.rationale: Keeping records only as long as necessary reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use secure electronic submission methods and encryption for HMDA data in transit and at rest.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and secure transfer reduce the risk of interception or unauthorized access during submission and storage.

mitigations.description: Limit inter-agency access to the minimum necessary and require each recipient agency to maintain equivalent privacy and security safeguards.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining access across recipient agencies reduces the exposure created by broader sharing.

mitigations.description: Continue to exclude direct identifiers such as names and Social Security numbers from HMDA submissions and review data for other fields that could indirectly identify borrowers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: HMDA does not require the reporting of PII that directly identifies an applicant or borrower, and staff commentary to Regulation C applicable to data collected in 2017 strongly discourages institutions from including in identification numbers names or social security numbers, which are direct identifiers.
mitigations.rationale: Removing direct identifiers and screening for indirect identifiers reduces the chance of re-identification.

risks.description: The tool collects contact PII from regulated entities, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of names, phone numbers, and email addresses.
risks.evidence_quote: The OMWI Diversity Assessment Tool contains information to include the PII of contacts for the submitting financial entities
risks.rationale: Collecting identifiable contact information increases the harm if the data is exposed or used beyond the intended assessment process.

risks.description: Free-text responses and attachments may contain additional contact PII beyond the limited fields, increasing the chance that sensitive information is over-collected or inadvertently shared.
risks.evidence_quote: any PII included in free text responses or attachments to a submitted assessment
risks.rationale: Unstructured fields are harder to control and can capture more personal information than the system's limited contact fields.

risks.description: The system collects employee and contractor information about Bureau users, which creates a privacy risk for internal personnel whose data is imported into the tool.
risks.evidence_quote: some information about employees and contractors working for the Bureau will be captured when it is imported into the system through Sailpoint
risks.rationale: Importing personnel data expands the set of individuals whose information is processed and exposed within the system.

risks.description: Entity contact PII is collected during onboarding to gain access, so access management failures could expose personal data to unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII pertaining to an entity contact is collected when the contact is onboarded to gain access to the system.
risks.rationale: When personal data is tied to account provisioning, weak access controls can lead to inappropriate system access and disclosure.

risks.description: Aggregated data is used in an annual report to Congress and internal dashboards, creating a risk that data may be re-identified or used in ways that exceed the original voluntary assessment purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Aggregated data from the tool will be used in an annual report to Congress as well as to create internal dashboards for data analytics.
risks.rationale: Even aggregated data can create privacy risk if it is not sufficiently de-identified or if downstream uses reveal more than intended.

risks.description: The system is a voluntary collection from regulated financial entities, which may lead to uncertainty about notice and consent if participants do not understand what personal data is collected and how it is used.
risks.evidence_quote: The OMWI Diversity Assessment Tool will be used to collect voluntary assessments submitted by financial entities regulated by the Bureau
risks.rationale: Voluntary submission does not by itself ensure that submitters understand the scope of personal data collection and downstream use.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of contact PII to the minimum necessary fields and apply standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls to the data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected within the OMWI Diversity Assessment Tool requires approval under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) as information collected through the Tool is a “collection of information” under 5 C.F.R. 1320.3(c) requiring OMB approval. The Office of Management and 1 “Final Interagency Policy Statement Establishing Joint Standards for Assessing the Diversity Policies and Practices of Entities Regulated by the Agencies,” 80 Fed Reg. 33016, June 10, 2015.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected PII and using the stated protections reduces the chance and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Review free-text fields and attachments for unnecessary personal data and provide instructions to submitters to avoid including PII unless required.
mitigations.rationale: Guidance and review help prevent accidental over-collection in unstructured fields that can contain unexpected PII.

mitigations.description: Restrict imported employee and contractor data to only the attributes needed for system administration and access, and protect it under the same privacy and security controls as other collected data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: some information about employees and contractors working for the Bureau will be captured when it is imported into the system through Sailpoint
mitigations.rationale: Limiting imported personnel data reduces exposure of internal users' information and narrows the privacy footprint.

mitigations.description: Use strong onboarding verification, role-based access controls, and periodic access reviews for entity contacts granted access to the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII pertaining to an entity contact is collected when the contact is onboarded to gain access to the system.
mitigations.rationale: Verifying identity and reviewing access helps ensure only authorized contacts can reach the personal data in the system.

mitigations.description: Apply aggregation thresholds and disclosure review before publishing reports or dashboards to reduce re-identification risk.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Aggregated data from the tool will be used in an annual report to Congress as well as to create internal dashboards for data analytics.
mitigations.rationale: Checking aggregated outputs before release helps ensure the data remains sufficiently aggregated and does not reveal individuals.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice at collection about what information is collected, how it will be used, and the available opportunities for consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice and participation rights help submitters understand the privacy implications of the voluntary collection.

risks.description: The system collects and processes personally identifiable information about requestors, Bureau staff, and other people in request records, creating a risk of exposure of sensitive personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Documents retrieved in response to a request and documents generated during the request’s processing may contain PII about the individual requestor, Bureau staff, and others.
risks.rationale: Any system that stores and processes PII for requests can expose individuals if access controls or handling are insufficient.

risks.description: Request-related information is entered by Bureau staff, so improper entry, handling, or disclosure by staff could expose requestor and third-party information.
risks.evidence_quote: Information related to requests is entered by Bureau staff who use the system to execute their job function.
risks.rationale: Human entry and handling of request data increases the chance of accidental or unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The public-facing portal allows requestors to create individual accounts, submit requests, access records, and communicate with the Bureau, which creates account and communications privacy risk if the portal is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The FOIAXpress Public Access Link (PAL) is a secure public-facing web portal that leverages Login.gov to provide the public with a single access point for requestors to create individual accounts, submit requests, access requested records and communicate with the Bureau about the status of a request.
risks.rationale: A single portal handling accounts, requests, records, and messages concentrates sensitive information in one place.

risks.description: Using Login.gov as an external authentication service introduces a privacy risk from sharing requestor identity and access data with another federal service operated outside the Bureau.
risks.evidence_quote: a new Public Access Link (PAL) add-on between it and the Federal service, Login.gov, which is owned and operated by the General Services Administration (GSA)
risks.rationale: When another service is involved in account access, more parties may receive or process personal information.

risks.description: The system supports the release of information to the public, so records could be disclosed more broadly than intended if release decisions or redactions are incorrect.
risks.evidence_quote: FOIAXpress is a third-party vendor-created tracking and management software that supports the Bureau in administering the entire lifecycle of FOIA and Privacy Act requests.
risks.rationale: A system that manages the full request lifecycle can affect what records are ultimately released.

risks.description: The system may contain documents about Bureau business operations as well as records about individuals, creating a risk that information about non-requestors is disclosed in response to FOIA requests.
risks.evidence_quote: an individual seeking information about other individuals or Bureau business operations is generally considered a FOIA request.
risks.rationale: FOIA processing can involve records that mention people who did not submit the request.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access controls, least-privilege permissions, and strong audit logging for all PII in request files and generated records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: all standard Bureau privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance that PII is exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Require staff privacy training and review procedures for entering, handling, and releasing request information.
mitigations.rationale: Training and review steps reduce the chance of accidental disclosure during staff processing.

mitigations.description: Use secure authentication, session protection, and encrypted communications for the public portal and associated account data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The FOIAXpress Public Access Link (PAL) is a secure public-facing web portal
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the portal and its sessions lowers the risk of account compromise and data interception.

mitigations.description: Minimize the personal information shared with Login.gov to only what is necessary for authentication and document the data exchange clearly.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization limits the privacy impact of involving an external identity service.

mitigations.description: Implement mandatory review and redaction checks before any records are released to the public.
mitigations.rationale: A second review helps prevent improper disclosure of information in released records.

mitigations.description: Apply disclosure review procedures that identify and protect information about third parties and Bureau operations before release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Documents retrieved in response to a request and documents generated during the request’s processing may contain PII about the individual requestor, Bureau staff, and others.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing for third-party information reduces the risk of releasing records that affect people who did not make the request.

risks.description: A third-party hosted cloud system could expose inquiry data if the vendor or hosting environment is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Entellitrak is an enterprise level commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) product hosted by a third party service provider
risks.rationale: Third-party hosting expands the attack surface beyond the Bureau's direct control.

risks.description: The system collects and stores names and inquiry summaries, which could reveal sensitive personal information about an individual's complaint or dealings with the Bureau.
risks.evidence_quote: When the Office receives an inquiry, it creates an inquiry record in Entellitrak that includes the inquirer’s first and last name, if an individual chooses to provide it, along with a summary of the inquiry.
risks.rationale: Even limited identifiers combined with the inquiry summary can identify a person and expose sensitive context.

risks.description: Contact information is retained outside the case system in original formats such as email, postal mail, and voicemail notes, which can increase exposure and make access control harder.
risks.evidence_quote: Rather the Ombudsman’s Office maintains contact information separately in the original format submitted by the inquirer (i.e., in the general Ombudsman Office email box, postal mail, or notes taken from the voicemail received).
risks.rationale: Keeping contact details in multiple repositories increases the chance of unauthorized access or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: The system supports analysis of individual inquiries and outreach activities, creating a risk that information could be used beyond simple case tracking if access or controls are insufficient.
risks.evidence_quote: Entellitrak also provides the Ombudsman’s Office with an integrated case management system with functionality to collect, track, manage and, process, as well as analyze information on individual inquiries to the Office.
risks.rationale: Analytical use of inquiry data can increase privacy impact if not tightly limited to the stated purpose.

risks.description: Access by staff through a secure web interface still creates insider-risk exposure because staff can view inquiry records and outreach information.
risks.evidence_quote: Entellitrak is a cloud-based solution accessed via a secure web interface used only by Ombudsman’s Office staff.
risks.rationale: Even restricted staff access can lead to misuse or accidental disclosure without strong role controls and monitoring.

risks.description: The system supports outreach activity, which may involve collecting or retaining information about individuals beyond their original inquiry, increasing the scope of personal data held.
risks.evidence_quote: Entellitrak also provides the Ombudsman’s Office with the ability to manage its independent outreach activity in an electronic format.
risks.rationale: Outreach functions can broaden collection and retention beyond the minimum needed for inquiry resolution.

risks.description: Because the Office receives inquiries by email, telephone, facsimile, and mail, personal information can be exposed while being transmitted or handled outside the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The Ombudsman’s Office also provides notice on its webpage that it has safeguards in place to preserve confidentiality.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake channels create more opportunities for misdelivery, interception, or handling errors.

mitigations.description: Require the third-party host to maintain strong contractual security, incident reporting, and audit obligations, and regularly assess the provider's controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Entellitrak is an enterprise level commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) product hosted by a third party service provider
mitigations.rationale: The risk comes from third-party hosting, so provider oversight and enforceable safeguards reduce exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit the inquiry record to the minimum necessary PII and continue allowing anonymous submissions when possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: If the inquirer wishes to remain anonymous, the Office creates a record in Entellitrak without the name of the inquirer, reflecting only a summary of the inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing identifiers reduces the privacy impact of the inquiry summary.

mitigations.description: Move contact information into a controlled case-management repository or apply equivalent centralized access controls and retention rules to the separate records.
mitigations.rationale: Centralizing or tightly controlling the separate contact records reduces the risk created by scattered storage.

mitigations.description: Restrict analytical use of inquiry data to the stated Ombudsman purpose and apply role-based access and logging to any reporting or analysis functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The purpose of collecting the PII is to enable the CFPB Ombudsman to assist consumers, financial entities, consumer or trade groups, and others in efficiently and securely resolving issues with the Bureau.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting analysis to the stated purpose helps prevent secondary use of inquiry information.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access for staff and monitor user activity in the secure web interface.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Entellitrak is a cloud-based solution accessed via a secure web interface used only by Ombudsman’s Office staff.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring staff access reduces insider misuse and accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Define and limit what outreach information is collected and retained, and separate outreach records from inquiry records where feasible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Entellitrak also provides the Ombudsman’s Office with the ability to manage its independent outreach activity in an electronic format.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing outreach collection limits expansion of personal data beyond inquiry handling.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for email, voicemail, fax, and mail, including staff handling instructions and verification before disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Ombudsman’s Office also provides notice on its webpage that it has safeguards in place to preserve confidentiality.
mitigations.rationale: Secure handling across intake channels reduces the chance of transmission or processing errors.

risks.description: Consumer complaint data may be shared with external companies or other government bodies beyond the original submission context, increasing the chance of unnecessary disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the Bureau for further administrative action.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly routes complaint information to multiple recipients, so limiting disclosure is a core privacy concern.

risks.description: Complaints can contain sensitive personal information tied to an identifiable consumer and their financial experiences, creating a risk of exposure if accessed or used beyond the response purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer complaints are submissions that express dissatisfaction with, or communicate suspicion of wrongful conduct by, an identifiable entity related to a consumer’s personal experience with a financial product or service.
risks.rationale: The data are directly linked to identifiable consumers and their financial issues, which raises privacy impact if mishandled.

risks.description: Physical mail is digitized by vendor staff before Bureau use, creating a risk of unauthorized access or disclosure during scanning and processing.
risks.evidence_quote: This refers to digitization of physical mail, where complaints and other documents are sent by consumers to a designated Bureau address for the CRC, processed by vendor staff and immediately scanned into CRS for Bureau use and documentation.
risks.rationale: Vendor handling adds an additional processing step where complaint information could be exposed.

risks.description: Vendor staff interact directly with consumers, which creates a risk that personally identifying or complaint information could be disclosed to individuals outside the Bureau.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer Guides are vendor staff working behalf of the Bureau, who are trained to process complaints and inquiries from consumers. They interact directly with consumers if they choose to speak to a person when calling the CRC contact center.
risks.rationale: Direct consumer contact by contractor staff increases the number of people who can hear or record complaint details.

risks.description: Staff authentication relies on email used for access to the CRC system, so compromised credentials could expose complaint records and consumer information.
risks.evidence_quote: WFM uses PII for identity verification of staff and the overall operation of the CRC. For example, the email of Bureau staff is used for authentication to obtain access to the CRC system to fulfill their duties.
risks.rationale: Authentication data protects access to the system, so weak or stolen credentials would directly threaten privacy.

risks.description: Voice communications may be captured and processed through call recording, IVR, and natural language processing, creating a risk of collecting more information than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Telephony refers to technology that facilitates communication over long distances through voice, text messages, video calling and conferencing, voicemail, call recording and fax. Specifically, when considering voice, this PIA refers to real time voice communications and their capture, including caller self-service, call routing for assisted services, call recording, and similar voice-type services.
risks.rationale: Recording and automated processing of calls can capture sensitive details beyond what is needed to answer the inquiry.

risks.description: Advanced analytics and operational use of complaint data may lead to secondary use of consumer information for performance assessment or process improvement beyond the immediate complaint response.
risks.evidence_quote: Tools include enhanced processing of voice communications such as interactive voice response (IVR) - a technology that allows humans to interact with a computer-operated phone system using voice and natural language processing - the automatic computational processing of human languages. Advanced data analytics is a used to assess performance and distill operation improvements.
risks.rationale: Using consumer interactions for analytics can expand processing beyond the purpose a consumer expects when submitting a complaint.

risks.description: Operational metadata is generated and leveraged for administrative purposes, which may still reveal patterns about consumer interactions or complaint handling.
risks.evidence_quote: Though not PII, metadata from operations is generated by the system and leveraged by the Bureau to assist in processing complaints when needed or for CRC administrative purposes.
risks.rationale: Metadata can indirectly expose behavioral or transactional information even when it is not labeled PII.

mitigations.description: Limit complaint sharing to the minimum necessary recipient and purpose, and apply role-based access and disclosure controls before sending information externally.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting who receives complaint data reduces unnecessary disclosure when the system routes cases outward.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection and retention of complaint details to only what is needed to answer, investigate, and resolve the complaint.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less sensitive detail lowers the privacy impact of identifiable complaint records.

mitigations.description: Require vendor personnel who digitize mail to follow strict handling controls, including access restrictions, logging, and confidentiality obligations.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter controls during scanning reduce the risk created by contractor handling of physical mail.

mitigations.description: Train vendor consumer guides on privacy, limit what they can view or disclose, and monitor calls for compliance with approved scripts and procedures.
mitigations.rationale: Training and oversight help prevent contractor staff from disclosing more information than necessary during live interactions.

mitigations.description: Use stronger authentication than email alone, such as multifactor authentication, and review access privileges regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication reduces the chance that unauthorized users can reach CRC records through compromised credentials.

mitigations.description: Provide notice before call recording or automated processing and offer a non-recorded or limited-recording path where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and alternatives reduce the privacy impact of capturing and processing voice communications.

mitigations.description: Constrain analytics use to aggregated or de-identified outputs whenever possible and prohibit using complaint data for unrelated purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting analytics to non-identifying outputs reduces the chance of secondary use of consumer information.

mitigations.description: Treat operational metadata as sensitive, apply access controls, and retain it only as long as needed for complaint processing or administration.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting metadata helps prevent indirect disclosure of consumer interaction patterns.

risks.description: The platform can collect and process sensitive personal data across many different CFPB uses, increasing the privacy impact if that data is misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The type and scope of PII collected varies depending on the CFPB use case.
risks.rationale: A broad, variable data set raises the privacy stakes because different applications may handle different sensitive attributes.

risks.description: The system may collect highly sensitive personal details such as military status, date of birth, sex, and race/ethnicity, which could create harm if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: the information may include first name, last name, associated entity, phone number, email address, mailing address, military information (including branch, rank, location, service status), employer, position/title, employer’s address, place of birth, date of birth, sex, and race/ethnicity.
risks.rationale: These attributes are sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure could create significant privacy and discrimination risks.

risks.description: The system supports case management and legal matters involving consumers, employees, and external parties, which can reveal sensitive dispute or enforcement information if access is too broad.
risks.evidence_quote: Creation, management, and reporting of case records and legal matters that are managed by automated workflows created with Salesforce to allow faster analysis and decision making by the CFPB.
risks.rationale: Legal and case records often contain highly sensitive context that should be limited to need-to-know access.

risks.description: The platform processes consumer complaints, inquiries, whistleblower tips, and other submissions, which may expose sensitive allegations or confidential reporting if not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Creating applications or forms to collect and manage feedback, correspondence, or submissions to CFPB, including but not limited to: o Consumer complaints or inquiries about financial products, services, and the entities providing them. ... o Whistleblower tips and contact information concerning companies or individuals that may be in potential violation of consumer protection laws.
risks.rationale: Complaint and tip data can identify individuals and contain sensitive allegations that warrant strong confidentiality protections.

risks.description: The system enables tracking, analysis, and correlation of large data sets, which can increase the risk of over-collection or profiling beyond the original purpose of collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Increased ability to perform trend, pattern, and correlation analysis of large data sets to provide faster consumer response, examination, and supervision processes.
risks.rationale: Analytic reuse of large datasets can reveal more about individuals than the original transaction required.

risks.description: The platform creates, sends, and tracks emails and texts to external stakeholders, which can expose personal information through communications channels and metadata.
risks.evidence_quote: Creating, sending, and tracking emails and/or texts to external stakeholders.
risks.rationale: Outbound messaging expands the number of places personal information can be seen, retained, or intercepted.

risks.description: Internal users authenticate through Entra ID using name and email address, and external users authenticate with email, password, and multi-factor authentication, creating account compromise risk if credentials are stolen or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: The Platform is connected to Entra ID for internal CFPB users, which uses name and email address to authenticate and provision access. Authorized external users must log in to the applications using an email, password, and multi-factor authentication.
risks.rationale: Authentication data and login credentials are a common target and can lead to unauthorized access if compromised.

risks.description: Salesforce integrates with other CFPB-authorized third-party cloud environments for storage, which increases the number of systems that could access or mishandle the data.
risks.evidence_quote: Salesforce also integrates with other CFPB-authorized third- party cloud system environments for purposes such as the storage of data.
risks.rationale: Each additional connected environment expands the attack surface and the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Records may be retained indefinitely until NARA approves a disposition schedule, which can keep personal data longer than necessary and increase exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Applications that collect, use, maintain, and/or share PII may retain records indefinitely until the NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase the likelihood that data will be accessed, breached, or reused in ways not originally intended.

mitigations.description: Limit each application to the minimum PII needed for its authorized purpose and review the design and purpose before collection.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When a program proposes a specific collection of data, the CFPB assesses the design and purpose of the system, to include a collection of PII, through system design documentation reviews to verify the CFPB has an authorized purpose to collect and use the information.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose review and data minimization reduce unnecessary handling of personal information.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter access controls and handling rules for sensitive attributes such as military information, date of birth, sex, and race/ethnicity.
mitigations.rationale: Extra protection is warranted because these fields are especially sensitive if exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict case and legal matter records to authorized staff only and log access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and auditability help prevent inappropriate viewing of sensitive legal information.

mitigations.description: Treat complaint and whistleblower submissions as confidential and limit sharing to need-to-know recipients identified in the applicable application-specific PIA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individual Salesforce applications may share with external entities on a need to know basis.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know sharing reduces the chance that sensitive allegations or identities are disclosed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Use privacy review and oversight before performing trend, pattern, or correlation analysis on large data sets.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Each programs use of PII is also assessed to determine the impact to privacy, and resulting risks are documented within application specific PIAs.
mitigations.rationale: Privacy impact review helps ensure analytics uses remain consistent with the authorized purpose.

mitigations.description: Limit email and text communications to the minimum necessary content and use secure, approved messaging workflows.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing message content reduces the chance of exposing personal information through communications.

mitigations.description: Keep multi-factor authentication in place for external users and maintain access management controls for the environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Salesforce manages CFPB’s technical cloud infrastructure on behalf of the CFPB, including ... access management tools.
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and access management reduce the risk of unauthorized account access.

mitigations.description: Continue assessing every third-party cloud environment through CFPB assessment and authorization processes before data is connected or stored there.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All third-party cloud systems that connect with Salesforce are assessed according CFPB’s assessment and authorization (A&A) processes to ensure risks are identified and mitigated prior to use.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-use security assessment helps identify and reduce risks from connected environments.

mitigations.description: Dispose of records according to approved NARA schedules as soon as the applicable retention period allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Each collection of data at the application level has a records schedule that has been submitted to and approved by National Archives and Records Administration (NARA).
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal lowers the amount of personal data retained and reduces long-term exposure.

risks.description: The system centralizes identity and access data for a broad workforce and external users, creating a high-value repository that could expose many people if compromised. Centralization increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access or misuse because it manages identities and access privileges across CFPB systems.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program centrally manages all staff (i.e., employees, contractors, detailees, volunteers, and interns) identification, authentication, and access privileges to all CFPB systems. It also manages the provisioning of access to CFPB IT resources by authorized external individuals.
risks.rationale: A centralized identity repository concentrates sensitive access data and therefore raises the impact of any security failure.

risks.description: The system collects directly supplied personal details that can reveal sensitive personal preferences and contact information, including pronouns and home-contact data. Even though the collection is limited, these fields can still expose personal characteristics and location-related information.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects a very limited amount of PII directly from individuals by allowing customization of their CFPB digital identity profile, such as their preferred job title, preferred pronouns, and a primary phone number such as a personal cell number and personal address if the individual works from home.
risks.rationale: Directly collected profile fields can disclose personal attributes and home contact details if improperly accessed or shared.

risks.description: The system pulls identity data from multiple internal and external sources, which increases the chance of inconsistent, excessive, or outdated information being incorporated into the identity record. Aggregating data from several systems can also broaden exposure if one source is compromised or contains inaccurate records.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program primarily uses PII collected by indirect sources such as CFPB employment applications and contractor onboarding forms housed within ABIS5 and HR Connect6, and from other federal agency sources such as USAstaffing7, USAccess8, and Login.gov.
risks.rationale: Using many upstream sources increases the likelihood of data quality problems and expands the number of systems that can contribute to exposure.

risks.description: The use of APIs, secure transmissions, and flat text files to connect the ICAM hub to source systems creates data-in-transit and interface risks. If those connections are misconfigured or intercepted, identity information could be exposed or altered.
risks.evidence_quote: Information from these sources is collected via an application programming interface (API), and through other secure data transmission methods, and flat text files to connect the centralized ICAM data hub to these data sources.
risks.rationale: Any system that moves identity data across interfaces must protect those channels from interception or tampering.

risks.description: The system creates digital IDs and manages authentication, which means a compromise could enable identity theft or unauthorized access to CFPB resources. Because the program is used to verify identity and grant access, incorrect or stolen credentials would have significant privacy consequences.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects information to verify individuals’ identities, establish a digital identification (ID), and grant privileged access to CFPB data to complete their responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Identity and credential systems are attractive targets because they can be abused to impersonate users and access sensitive data.

risks.description: Privileged access management exposes PII and system resources to elevated users, increasing the risk of insider misuse or overbroad access. Privileged accounts can view or manage more data than ordinary users, so misuse would have greater privacy impact.
risks.evidence_quote: Privileged Access Management – Focuses on the protection of privileged accounts at the CFPB where elevated access to systems and PII is managed using CFPB Rules of Behavior (RoBs) and Privilege User Access Requests (PUA) within specific environments.
risks.rationale: Elevated access creates a greater opportunity for misuse or accidental disclosure of sensitive information.

risks.description: The system maintains access rights for many categories of personnel, so stale or inappropriate access could persist if reviews are not timely and accurate. If identities or roles change and access is not updated, former users may retain access to personal data they no longer need.
risks.evidence_quote: Identity Governance and Administration – Monitors and ensures that user identities and access rights remain properly managed, secure, and monitored.
risks.rationale: Access that is not continuously governed can leave unnecessary exposure to personal information.

risks.description: The system supports access decisions and may use personal information from background, staffing, and credentialing sources, which can create fairness and notice concerns if individuals do not understand how their data is used. Even if the program says it does not make determinations about individuals, the underlying identity verification can still affect who receives access.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program primarily uses PII collected by indirect sources such as CFPB employment applications and contractor onboarding forms housed within ABIS5 and HR Connect6, and from other federal agency sources such as USAstaffing7, USAccess8, and Login.gov.
risks.rationale: When access depends on aggregated personnel data, individuals need clear notice and a way to challenge incorrect information.

mitigations.description: Limit centralized access to the identity hub to staff with a strict need to know, and enforce strong logging and monitoring for all access to the repository.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ICAM program centrally manages all staff (i.e., employees, contractors, detailees, volunteers, and interns) identification, authentication, and access privileges to all CFPB systems.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the chance that a centralized identity store is misused or broadly exposed.

mitigations.description: Minimize optional profile fields and collect home address or personal cell number only when necessary for work purposes, with clear notice to the individual.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects a very limited amount of PII directly from individuals by allowing customization of their CFPB digital identity profile, such as their preferred job title, preferred pronouns, and a primary phone number such as a personal cell number and personal address if the individual works from home.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary profile details lowers the privacy impact of directly supplied personal information.

mitigations.description: Validate incoming records against authoritative sources and perform routine data quality checks to prevent stale or inconsistent identity data from being used.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ICAM program primarily uses PII collected by indirect sources such as CFPB employment applications and contractor onboarding forms housed within ABIS5 and HR Connect6, and from other federal agency sources such as USAstaffing7, USAccess8, and Login.gov.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and reconciliation reduce the chance that aggregated records contain inaccurate or excessive information.

mitigations.description: Encrypt all API, file-transfer, and other transmission paths, and restrict flat text file exchanges to the minimum necessary with integrity checks and access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information from these sources is collected via an application programming interface (API), and through other secure data transmission methods, and flat text files to connect the centralized ICAM data hub to these data sources.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger transport and file protections reduce interception, alteration, and unauthorized disclosure risks.

mitigations.description: Use strong authentication controls, periodic credential renewal, and rapid revocation procedures for compromised accounts or digital IDs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ICAM program collects information to verify individuals’ identities, establish a digital identification (ID), and grant privileged access to CFPB data to complete their responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger credential lifecycle controls reduce the chance that stolen or stale identities can be used to access data.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access reviews and require documented approval for privileged access requests, with tighter monitoring of privileged account activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Privileged Access Management – Focuses on the protection of privileged accounts at the CFPB where elevated access to systems and PII is managed using CFPB Rules of Behavior (RoBs) and Privilege User Access Requests (PUA) within specific environments.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and reviewing elevated access reduces the privacy impact of insider misuse or overbroad permissions.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular recertification of identities and access rights so that changes in role, employment status, or need-to-know are reflected promptly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Identity Governance and Administration – Monitors and ensures that user identities and access rights remain properly managed, secure, and monitored.
mitigations.rationale: Routine recertification helps prevent lingering access to personal data after roles change.

mitigations.description: Provide clear privacy notices and a practical process for individuals to review and correct identity data used for access management.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and correction rights help individuals understand and fix data that affects access decisions.

risks.description: The system stores consumer PII collected from supervised entities, direct consumer contacts, and complaints, creating a broad repository of sensitive financial information that could be exposed if misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES contains PII regarding consumers of depository and non-depository entities products as well as employees of those entities serving as points of contact. It also contains information about CFPB staff assigned to duties related to the supervision of these entities.
risks.rationale: A centralized system holding multiple categories of PII increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: The system collects PII indirectly from supervised entities, which can limit transparency and make it harder for individuals to know what data is being gathered about them.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII collected by the SES is indirectly requested from entities the CFPB supervises.
risks.rationale: Indirect collection can reduce notice to affected individuals and weaken their ability to understand or challenge the collection.

risks.description: The CFPB may contact consumers directly to collect and verify additional information, which can reveal their involvement in a supervision activity and create privacy intrusion risk.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may use PII to contact consumers to collect and verify additional information required for supervision activities.
risks.rationale: Direct outreach can expose consumers to unnecessary contact and disclose that they are associated with an investigation or examination.

risks.description: The system facilitates collection and sharing of relevant information, which raises the risk of over-sharing or unauthorized dissemination of PII across users and entities.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB uses the Supervision and Examination System (SES) to conduct its supervision activities and facilitates the collection and sharing of relevant information.
risks.rationale: When a system is designed to share information, privacy risk depends on strict limits on who can receive what data.

risks.description: The Supervision Portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators, which could expose sensitive materials to external parties if access is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: This portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators.
risks.rationale: External access expands the number of people who can see sensitive supervisory information and increases the consequences of access-control failures.

risks.description: Identification and provisioning of entity representatives is performed by CFPB users, creating a risk that incorrect or excessive access could be granted to the wrong external user.
risks.evidence_quote: Identification and provisioning of these entity representatives is completed within the SES application by limited sets of CFPB users designated
risks.rationale: User provisioning errors can lead to unauthorized access or exposure of supervisory records.

risks.description: The system stores compliance rating information and Examination Reports, which may affect institutions and could be sensitive if disclosed beyond intended supervisory use.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB also uses it as an information repository for compliance rating information. Outcomes from a supervisory activity can include an Examination Report, which contains a compliance rating
risks.rationale: Supervisory findings are sensitive operational information and should be protected from unnecessary disclosure.

risks.description: The system relies on Salesforce cloud infrastructure, which introduces vendor and cloud-hosting privacy risk if the cloud environment is not configured and governed properly.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES resides within the Salesforce2 cloud platform
risks.rationale: Hosting sensitive data in a cloud platform requires strong configuration, contractual, and monitoring controls to prevent exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access, strong encryption, and monitoring to all PII stored in SES, with stricter controls for consumer complaint and supervisory data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply
mitigations.rationale: Protecting a centralized PII repository requires limiting access and reducing the impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice to consumers when PII is obtained indirectly from supervised entities and explain the source and purpose of the collection.
mitigations.rationale: Notice helps individuals understand indirect collection and supports transparency.

mitigations.description: Minimize direct consumer outreach to only what is necessary, and use approved scripts or notices that explain why CFPB is contacting the consumer.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and explaining outreach reduces unnecessary intrusion and confusion.

mitigations.description: Restrict sharing to the minimum relevant information needed for supervision and enforce role-based access and audit logging for all information exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: facilitates the collection and sharing of relevant information
mitigations.rationale: Sharing controls reduce the chance that PII is disseminated beyond authorized users.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication, authorization checks, and periodic access reviews for all external entity representatives using the Supervision Portal.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This portal allows authorized entity representatives to view and respond to requests for information, data, and documentation from state regulators.
mitigations.rationale: External portal access must be tightly governed to prevent unauthorized viewing of sensitive documents.

mitigations.description: Use a formal identity-proofing and approval workflow before provisioning entity representatives, with dual review for access grants and changes.
mitigations.rationale: A controlled provisioning process reduces the chance of assigning access to the wrong person or granting excessive permissions.

mitigations.description: Limit access to Examination Reports and compliance ratings to staff with a direct supervisory need and retain them only as long as required for supervision.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB also uses it as an information repository for compliance rating information.
mitigations.rationale: Sensitive supervisory findings should be available only to authorized personnel and kept no longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Apply cloud security governance for the Salesforce environment, including configuration reviews, vendor oversight, and logging of administrative activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The SES resides within the Salesforce2 cloud platform
mitigations.rationale: Cloud-hosted sensitive data needs governance and monitoring to reduce vendor and configuration risk.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains detailed consumer complaint records, including supporting documents, which can reveal sensitive personal and financial information about individuals' experiences.
risks.evidence_quote: The consumer complaints or inquiries themselves (including records about the complaint, details and supporting documents) are collected by Consumer Response and maintained in the Consumer Response System (CRS), which is the CFPB system of record for these interactions.
risks.rationale: A system of record for complaint details and supporting documents creates a broad privacy footprint because it centralizes personal information about consumers' financial problems.

risks.description: The system may collect Social Security Numbers for some complaints, creating a risk of identity theft or misuse if that highly sensitive identifier is exposed or retained unnecessarily.
risks.evidence_quote: For some complaints, submission of a Social Security Number can be helpful to validate the consumer’s identity and their association with a particular account, such as a credit report.
risks.rationale: Social Security Numbers are highly sensitive identifiers, so their collection increases the harm if the data is accessed or disclosed improperly.

risks.description: Complaints may be shared with companies, other government agencies, White House offices, Congressional offices, or other CFPB offices, which increases the chance of disclosure beyond the original consumer's expectations.
risks.evidence_quote: In addressing a complaint or inquiry, Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the CFPB for further administrative action.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient expands the number of entities that can see complaint information, increasing disclosure risk.

risks.description: Consumers can submit complaints by website, phone, and physical mail, which creates multiple intake channels and a larger attack surface for interception, misrouting, or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer Response accepts complaints about financial products and services from consumers via the CFPB’s website, www.ConsumerFinance.gov/complaint/, by phone, and physical mail.
risks.rationale: More intake channels generally mean more opportunities for data to be exposed during transmission, handling, or conversion into the system of record.

risks.description: The CRS operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform, so consumer complaint data may be exposed through third-party hosting or service-provider security failures.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform2.
risks.rationale: Using a vendor and cloud platform introduces dependency on external systems that can create additional privacy and security risks.

risks.description: Complaint data is analyzed and shared to identify trends, which can create a risk of secondary use beyond the original complaint-handling purpose if data is not properly limited or de-identified.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is also tasked with analyzing complaints to identify trends in service delivery to consumers.
risks.rationale: Analytical reuse can broaden how personal information is used, so safeguards are needed to prevent unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit the complaint fields and supporting documents collected to only what is necessary for complaint handling and response, and redact unnecessary personal details before storage.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of personal information collected lowers the privacy impact of keeping complaint records in a system of record.

mitigations.description: Collect Social Security Numbers only when strictly needed, mask them wherever possible, and apply enhanced access controls and encryption for any stored SSNs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: For some complaints, submission of a Social Security Number can be helpful to validate the consumer’s identity and their association with a particular account, such as a credit report.
mitigations.rationale: Because SSNs are only sometimes needed, restricting and protecting them reduces the risk from this sensitive identifier.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing limits, role-based access, and disclosure notices tailored to each recipient before sending complaint information outside Consumer Response.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In addressing a complaint or inquiry, Consumer Response may provide additional information to the consumer, send the complaint to the company or financial service provider that is the subject of the complaint, refer the complaint to another government agency, or direct the submission to other offices in the CFPB for further administrative action.
mitigations.rationale: Because the system already shares complaint data with multiple parties, controlling and explaining those transfers helps reduce unnecessary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Secure each intake channel with strong authentication, transport protection, and careful handling procedures for phone and mail submissions before they enter CRS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Consumer Response accepts complaints about financial products and services from consumers via the CFPB’s website, www.ConsumerFinance.gov/complaint/, by phone, and physical mail.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting all submission channels reduces the chance that complaint information is intercepted or mishandled before it reaches the system of record.

mitigations.description: Impose contractual security, privacy, and incident-response requirements on the vendor-provided cloud platform, including audit rights and continuous monitoring.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform2.
mitigations.rationale: Vendor and cloud dependencies require explicit controls to ensure the hosting environment protects complaint data appropriately.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified or aggregated complaint data for trend analysis whenever possible, and restrict analysts from accessing direct identifiers unless needed for a specific case.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is also tasked with analyzing complaints to identify trends in service delivery to consumers.
mitigations.rationale: Trend analysis can often be performed without direct identifiers, which reduces the privacy risk of secondary use.

risks.description: Housing CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment creates a risk that personally identifiable information will be exposed outside direct CFPB control. This is especially sensitive because the environment is explicitly described as contractor-owned rather than Bureau-owned.
risks.evidence_quote: This PIA Appendix documents the privacy risks associated with housing CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: Contractor ownership can reduce direct agency control over how records are protected and accessed.

risks.description: The system can store, process, and maintain a broad range of sensitive personal and case information, increasing the impact if access is mishandled. The records may include personally identifiable information and other evidence used in investigations and litigation.
risks.evidence_quote: This PIA Appendix, along with the PIA, provides coverage for the collection, use, sharing, and maintenance of personally identifiable information shared and maintained within the contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the data handled, the greater the privacy harm if it is improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Forensic collection from external entities can capture data beyond what is strictly necessary for a case, creating overcollection risk. The system is designed to extract data from storage media when immediate access is granted by a court.
risks.evidence_quote: Enforcement requires the capability to forensically collect data from external entities when immediate access is granted by a court, often in conjunction with a Temporary Consumer and Financial Protection Bureau Legal Technology and Support Team Privacy Impact Assessment July 2024 Restraining Order.
risks.rationale: Forensic extraction can sweep in large volumes of information, including unrelated personal data, unless tightly scoped.

risks.description: Bulk ingest, analysis, and review of large volumes of records increases the risk that irrelevant or nonresponsive personal information will be processed and retained. The tools are designed to organize bureau records for search, retrieval, review, correlation, flagging, and presentation in bulk.
risks.evidence_quote: These tools ingest, analyze, process, format, and organize bureau records for search, retrieval, review, correlation, flagging, and presentation in various data formats
risks.rationale: Bulk processing makes it easier to process more personal information than is needed for the legal task at hand.

risks.description: Metadata viewing can reveal sensitive contextual information about documents and communications, even when the content itself is not the focus of review. The system explicitly allows users to view metadata within files stored in varying file formats.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats
risks.rationale: Metadata can expose who created, sent, or modified a file and when, which can itself be sensitive.

risks.description: Duplicate-document identification and elimination may rely on processing multiple copies of records, increasing the spread of personal information across review sets and the chance of mishandling. The system specifically supports identifying and eliminating duplicate documents during review.
risks.evidence_quote: identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process.
risks.rationale: Handling multiple copies of the same record increases the number of places where personal information may be exposed.

risks.description: Keyword-based redaction and flagging can miss protected information if the attorney-selected keywords are incomplete or poorly chosen. The system depends on keywords input by the reviewing attorney to identify names, phrases, and terms that may indicate privileged or protected information.
risks.evidence_quote: This allows the reviewing attorney to customize keywords for each set of documents or cases that may indicate the existence of privileged or protected information.
risks.rationale: If the keyword set is too narrow, sensitive information may not be flagged for protection.

risks.description: Trial and investigative hearing support can expose personal information in courtroom or hearing presentations if exhibits are not properly limited or redacted. The system is used to display exhibits during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
risks.evidence_quote: These events require the use of various specialized trial presentation software tools, which display exhibits, either during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
risks.rationale: Presenting exhibits publicly or broadly can disclose personal information beyond the intended audience.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to CFPB records to the minimum necessary and require contractual privacy and security controls for the contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PIA Appendix documents the privacy risks associated with housing CFPB records in a contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing contractor access and imposing enforceable controls reduces the privacy impact of contractor ownership.

mitigations.description: Apply strict access controls, encryption, and role-based permissions to all personally identifiable information stored or processed in the environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: collection, use, sharing, and maintenance of personally identifiable information shared and maintained within the contractor-owned environment.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access and encryption controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Use court-authorized collection protocols that narrowly scope forensic extraction to the records needed for the matter and document chain of custody.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Enforcement requires the capability to forensically collect data from external entities when immediate access is granted by a court
mitigations.rationale: Narrow scoping and chain-of-custody controls help prevent unnecessary collection of unrelated personal data.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and relevance review before loading large record sets into the system, and purge nonresponsive material according to approved procedures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These tools ingest, analyze, process, format, and organize bureau records for search, retrieval, review, correlation, flagging, and presentation
mitigations.rationale: Filtering out irrelevant material early reduces unnecessary processing of personal information.

mitigations.description: Restrict metadata access to authorized reviewers and train staff to treat metadata as sensitive information during review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can view metadata within files stored in these varying file formats
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and training on metadata reduces the chance that contextual personal information is improperly exposed.

mitigations.description: Use deduplication controls that preserve a single controlled copy and prevent uncontrolled proliferation of duplicate records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: identify and eliminate duplicate documents during the review process.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling duplicates reduces the number of copies that can be mishandled or disclosed.

mitigations.description: Require iterative validation of keyword sets and secondary human review for flagged and unflagged records to catch missed protected information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: customize keywords for each set of documents or cases that may indicate the existence of privileged or protected information
mitigations.rationale: Testing and secondary review help compensate for keyword lists that may not capture all sensitive terms.

mitigations.description: Redact or otherwise limit personal information in exhibits before they are used in hearings or trial presentations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: which display exhibits, either during investigative hearings or at trial for courtroom presentations.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-presentation redaction reduces the risk of disclosing personal information to hearing participants or the public.

risks.description: The system collects user or point-of-contact contact details, which creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure of personally identifying business contact information. Although the beta uses only contact data, full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address are still sensitive if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: This information includes full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address.
risks.rationale: These fields directly identify and contact a person, so exposure would affect privacy even in beta testing.

risks.description: The system is designed to handle small business lending application information, which could reveal sensitive business and applicant details if real data were submitted or retained. The context says only fake data is used during beta, but the system purpose shows it is intended for data about credit applications.
risks.evidence_quote: any information submitted beyond user or POC business contact information, including information regarding small business loan application filing, is only fake data.
risks.rationale: A system built around lending application data can expose sensitive information if real applicant data is introduced or mishandled.

risks.description: The system's intended use includes information about women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses, which can create privacy risk if those characteristics are linked to identifiable entities. Even if used for fair lending analysis, such data can enable profiling or unwanted inference about business owners.
risks.evidence_quote: enabling communities, governmental entities, and creditors to identify business and community development needs and opportunities of women-owned, minority-owned, and small businesses.
risks.rationale: Demographic and business-ownership information can be sensitive when tied to identifiable applicants or owners.

risks.description: The system relies on standard privacy protections and security controls, but the context does not specify any special controls for beta testing or for preventing accidental entry of real applicant data. That leaves a risk of data quality or testing errors leading to unintended collection of real personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
risks.rationale: General controls may not be enough to prevent accidental submission of real data in a testing environment.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum contact fields needed for beta access and restrict access to those fields to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This information includes full name, business email, phone number, and mailing address.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and restricting access reduces the chance that identifiable contact information is exposed.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing the rule that only fake data may be entered beyond user or POC business contact information during beta testing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: for purposes of beta-testing, any information submitted beyond user or POC business contact information, including information regarding small business loan application filing, is only fake data.
mitigations.rationale: Using only synthetic data prevents real applicant information from being collected during testing.

mitigations.description: Keep applicant and owner data de-identified or otherwise excluded from disclosures to CFPB whenever possible, consistent with Section 1071's prohibition on including applicant PII in the data collection disclosed to CFPB.
mitigations.evidence_quote: financial institutions may not include the personally identifiable information (PII) of applicants as part of the data collection disclosed to CFPB.
mitigations.rationale: Excluding PII lowers the risk that sensitive business or owner characteristics are tied to named individuals.

mitigations.description: Add explicit beta-testing validation and user guidance that blocks or flags real applicant data before submission, in addition to standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls.
mitigations.rationale: A targeted safeguard is needed to reduce accidental entry of real personal information during testing.

risks.description: The system may collect and maintain sensitive personal information about consumers, respondents, counsel, officers, and other people named in covered orders, including contact details and other order-related facts. Because uploaded orders and related public records can include additional PII, the registry can expose more personal data than is necessary for registration.
risks.evidence_quote: Documents uploaded to the NBR System may include the following PII on individuals (e.g., consumer, consenting party, defendant) identified or listed in documents provided to the registry (e.g., covered orders): • Full name;13 • Title; • Work address; • Email address; and • Telephone number. • Any other information pertaining to the covered order (e.g., violation of consumer financial law) that may be associated with the individual.
risks.rationale: The input shows the system ingests documents that can contain multiple types of PII about third parties beyond the nonbank itself.

risks.description: The system may disclose personal information publicly through the registry, creating a risk that PII in covered orders becomes broadly accessible. Even though publication is discretionary, the system is designed to make some collected information available to the public and other regulators.
risks.evidence_quote: Finally, the Orders Rule allows the CFPB to publish some of the information collected from nonbanks for use by members of the public as well as other regulatory agencies.
risks.rationale: Public dissemination increases the chance that personal information is viewed or reused beyond the original regulatory purpose.

risks.description: The system may retain records indefinitely because there is no approved retention schedule yet. Unschedule and permanent handling increases the amount of personal data held over time and lengthens exposure if records are misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently, there is no NARA-approved records retention schedule for NBR records. Therefore, the records are unscheduled and considered permanent in nature until NARA’s approval to disposition is obtained.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases privacy risk because more data remains available for longer periods.

risks.description: The helpdesk feature collects personal information from members of the public and nonbank users, including names, email addresses, and questions that may reveal sensitive issues. Those questions could disclose details about a person's regulatory or technical problem that are not needed for account support.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System provides a helpdesk feature that allows members of the public to ask questions about the Orders Rule and for NBR account users (i.e., nonbank authorized representative) to submit a question to the CFPB to help resolve a technical issue or issue related to the submission of information. The information submitted also includes PII such as the full name of the individual submitting the question and an email address that the CFPB uses to reply to questions or provide assistance as appropriate.
risks.rationale: Free-text support requests can reveal more personal information than structured registration fields.

risks.description: The system collects usernames and passwords for nonbank representatives and CFPB staff, creating a risk that account credentials could be misused if improperly accessed or handled. Credential compromise could expose all information in the registry and associated user accounts.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System maintains all or some of the following PII about the authorized representative(s) associated with and authorized by the nonbank to manage the registration process under the Orders Rule for covered orders: • Full name; • Title; • Email address; and • Username and password.
risks.rationale: Credentials are highly sensitive because they can enable unauthorized access to the system.

risks.description: The system may collect unnecessary or inadvertently uploaded documents that contain sensitive information not relevant to the Orders Rule. If such documents are not promptly removed, they can expand the amount of personal data stored without a clear need.
risks.evidence_quote: Any documents identified as inadvertently uploaded to the NBR System or not relevant to the Orders Rule may be removed by CFPB Staff to prevent the unnecessary collection of PII or other sensitive information within the NBR System.
risks.rationale: The need to remove irrelevant uploads shows there is a risk of overcollection and unnecessary retention of sensitive data.

risks.description: The system shares registry information with other CFPB programs and with other regulators, which can spread personal data beyond the original collection context. Broader sharing increases the number of recipients who can access or use the information.
risks.evidence_quote: Finally, the CFPB may share information in the NBR System directly with other federal, state, tribal, and local regulators to facilitate the work of those agencies, in accordance with its existing information-sharing agreements and protocols.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient creates another point where privacy safeguards must hold.

mitigations.description: Require and verify redaction of all nonpublic portions of covered orders before upload, and continue limiting uploads to the minimum necessary order documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Orders Rule to redact any nonpublic portions of the covered orders before submitting them to the registry.
mitigations.rationale: Redacting nonpublic portions reduces the amount of third-party PII stored in the registry.

mitigations.description: Publish only non-confidential information and use a format that protects confidential information, with a case-by-case review before any publication.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Therefore, the CFPB has sole discretion in determining whether to publish certain information maintained in the NBR System and the format of publication designed to protect confidential information in accordance with the Orders Rule.
mitigations.rationale: Selective publication lowers the chance that personal data is made broadly public.

mitigations.description: Obtain and implement a NARA-approved retention schedule as soon as possible, and dispose of records when authorized.
