mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that sensitive complaint details are viewed or disclosed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Minimize stored identifiers by collecting only what is necessary for case processing and use the case number instead of direct identifiers whenever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of directly identifying data lowers the harm from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for mail, email, telephone, and interview submissions, including verification steps before data is entered into CRES.
mitigations.rationale: Secure intake and verification reduce interception, misrouting, and transcription errors across multiple collection channels.

mitigations.description: Implement quality-control review of manually entered complaint data to detect and correct errors before records are relied upon.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing manually entered data helps prevent inaccurate records from affecting complainants and investigations.

mitigations.description: Require contractor personnel to undergo privacy and security training and enforce contractual limits on access, monitoring, and sanctions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? YES
mitigations.rationale: Training and enforceable contract controls reduce the risk of misuse by non-federal users.

mitigations.description: Document role-based access rules and apply least-privilege permissions so each user can access only the functions and records needed for their job.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit least-privilege controls reduce unnecessary exposure of complaint PII.

mitigations.description: Harden the Internet-facing environment with continuous monitoring, timely patching, and firewall rule review to reduce external attack risk.
mitigations.rationale: A public Internet connection requires layered defenses to protect sensitive records from cyber intrusion.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong agency oversight of the contractor-hosted environment through security assessments, audits, and clear incident reporting requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Oversight helps ensure the contractor protects records in a way consistent with agency privacy expectations.

mitigations.description: Define and document specific retention and destruction schedules aligned to approved records requirements, and periodically verify deletion.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes.
mitigations.rationale: Clear schedules and verification reduce the risk that complaint records are kept longer than necessary.

risks.description: Users can enter unrestricted free-text personal information in the profile, which may lead to collection of sensitive or unnecessary data beyond what the system needs.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: Unrestricted free text increases the chance that users will disclose more personal information than intended.

risks.description: Profile photos combined with names create identifiable PII, increasing the risk of exposure if the system or downstream sharing is accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: A name-plus-photo combination directly identifies a person and is more privacy-sensitive than either element alone.

risks.description: The system collects names, addresses, and permit numbers for parking and building permit functions, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure of personally identifying records.
risks.evidence_quote: The system uses the following information about users of the system: - Name - Address information - Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
risks.rationale: These fields can identify individuals and link them to facility access or permit activity.

risks.description: Information is shared to the USDA Data Lake and Tableau dashboards across multiple administrative domains, which broadens access and increases the chance of overexposure or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Cross-domain reporting can reveal more information to more users than is necessary for the original purpose.

risks.description: The system transmits data to the USDA Data Lake through integrations such as SFTP, API, and Web Service, creating a risk of interception or improper transfer if those channels are misconfigured or weakened.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service.
risks.rationale: Any data transfer path carrying PII needs strong configuration and access controls to prevent exposure.

risks.description: Only authorized contractors have access, but the description does not state privacy training, creating a risk of insider mishandling by users with legitimate access.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system.
risks.rationale: Authorized access alone does not prevent accidental or inappropriate disclosure without privacy-focused handling practices.

risks.description: The system relies on ACLs to maintain integrity, but the PIA does not describe specific minimization or field-level restrictions, so users may see more PII than needed for their role.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
risks.rationale: If PII is optional, access should be tightly limited so unnecessary personal data is not broadly exposed.

risks.description: Retention is based on records schedules and destroyed by subject matter, which may leave personal information available longer than necessary if records are not correctly classified.
risks.evidence_quote: Items are retained per the General Records Schedule 24: Information Technology Operation and Management Records. Records are destroyed based on the subject matter.
risks.rationale: Subject-matter-based destruction can create retention inconsistency if records are not categorized correctly.

mitigations.description: Restrict the “About Me” field with validation, character limits, and user guidance so only business-relevant information can be entered.
mitigations.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining free text reduces the chance of collecting unnecessary or sensitive personal details.

mitigations.description: Make profile photos optional by default and clearly warn users that a photo combined with a name is PII before they upload it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice and optional participation reduce unnecessary disclosure of identifiable images.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of names, addresses, and permit numbers to the minimum necessary fields for parking and building permit processing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system uses the following information about users of the system: - Name - Address information - Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected identifiers lowers the impact if records are accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access and data filtering in Tableau dashboards so senior leadership sees only the specific data needed for each reporting purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting dashboard views reduces unnecessary exposure across administrative domains.

mitigations.description: Require encryption and strict authentication for SFTP, API, and Web Service transfers to the USDA Data Lake.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport protections reduce the chance that data is intercepted or altered in transit.

mitigations.description: Provide documented privacy training and acceptable-use requirements for all authorized contractors with access to the system.
mitigations.rationale: Training helps authorized users handle PII appropriately and reduces accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access rules so users can view only the PII needed for their specific OSCAR function.
mitigations.evidence_quote: it is also used to maintain the integrity of the system through ACLs (Access Control Lists).
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege reduces exposure when PII is optional and not required for operation.

mitigations.description: Review retention and destruction procedures periodically to ensure records are classified correctly and destroyed on schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Items are retained per the General Records Schedule 24: Information Technology Operation and Management Records. Records are destroyed based on the subject matter.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps prevent records from being kept too long because of misclassification or process errors.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains personally identifiable information needed to control physical access, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure of identity and location-related data if the access control system is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS collects information required to control physical access to USDA managed facilities and restricted areas within those facilities in all regions across the United States. ePACS maintains individuals' personal individual verification (PIV) information
risks.rationale: A centralized repository of PIV and access data can expose sensitive identity and access details if improperly accessed.

risks.description: Visitor data collected for the Washington, D.C. visitor management function may expose visitor identity and visit information to unnecessary retention or use beyond the immediate visit purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Incorporated into ePACS is the VMS which allows visitors to respond to meeting invites and registrar to visit USDA locations in Washington, D.C.
risks.rationale: Visitor records can be privacy-sensitive because they reveal where and when a person is seeking access.

risks.description: The system uses data from USDA human resources databases and manually collected card-issuance data, which creates a risk that inaccurate or outdated information could affect access decisions or credential issuance.
risks.evidence_quote: The authoritative data elements provided to ePACS are provided by USDA’s ICAM Shared Services identity management system. This identity data is provided from a series of USDA Human Resources databases which are consolidated into ICAM Shared services. The non-authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
risks.rationale: If source data is stale or manually entered incorrectly, access rights and credential status may be wrong.

risks.description: The system shares limited PII and access-activity data with internal analytics and management systems, which creates a risk of broader internal dissemination than cardholders expect.
risks.evidence_quote: The information shared from ePACS is with Office of Chief Information Officer for the system named Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT)and Office of Property Credit Card Service Center.
risks.rationale: Sharing even limited identifiers and access activity expands the number of systems and users that can see personal data.

risks.description: Credential read activity shared for executive management can reveal where and when an individual accessed facilities, creating a risk of employee monitoring or profiling.
risks.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity
risks.rationale: Access logs can be sensitive because they reveal movement and presence patterns.

risks.description: Employee status data sent in the Fleet report could be used for purposes beyond disabling credit cards, creating a risk of secondary use of employment information.
risks.evidence_quote: The Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
risks.rationale: Employment status is sensitive and should be limited to the stated operational need.

risks.description: The system allows access by contractors, which increases the number of people who can view or handle PII and access-control records.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: More users with access generally increases the chance of misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: The system relies on encrypted transmission and need-to-know controls, but the presence of multiple databases, reports, dashboards, and email-based sharing still creates exposure points for unauthorized access or interception.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS securely transmits data. The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
risks.rationale: Each transfer and downstream system is a potential point of failure even when controls are in place.

risks.description: The retention period of 5.5 years, including archived data, increases the amount of time personal access records remain available and therefore increases long-term privacy exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which records can be misused or breached.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to ePACS to authorized personnel on a least-privilege basis and continue encrypting stored and transmitted data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access. All data leaving the USDA will be encrypted.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and encrypting data reduces the chance that PIV information is exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit visitor records to the minimum data needed for the visit and apply the pending SORN/routine-use controls before any broader sharing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The VMS will only include visitors arriving at USDA National Capitol Region (NCR) Headquarters (HQ includes South, Whitten, and Yates buildings). The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing the visitor scope and governing use reduces unnecessary exposure of visitor data.

mitigations.description: Validate authoritative and manually collected data before use in credential issuance and access-rights generation.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps prevent inaccurate identity data from causing improper access decisions.

mitigations.description: Limit internal sharing to the minimum fields needed for each recipient and continue using secure file transfer and controlled dashboards.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily. Once in the EDAPT, the data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards with summary PIV card access for executive management.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing fields and using controlled transfer methods reduces unnecessary internal dissemination.

mitigations.description: Use aggregated or de-identified access-activity summaries for executive management whenever possible.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation lowers the risk that management reports can be used to track individual movements.

mitigations.description: Limit the Fleet report to only the employee-status fields needed to disable cards and prohibit any other use of that report.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting the report to operationally necessary fields reduces secondary-use risk.

mitigations.description: Review contractor access regularly and revoke access when no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review reduces the chance that contractors retain unnecessary access to sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Minimize the number of systems and transmission channels that receive ePACS data and keep all external disclosures within the stated routine uses.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is not permitted to be shared outside the USDA except for what is covered by the routine uses in the ePACS SORN.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing distribution paths lowers the number of places where data could be exposed.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce the approved retention schedule so archived records are deleted when the 5.5-year period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal limits how long personal access records remain vulnerable.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees, creating a direct privacy risk if that data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees
risks.rationale: Any system holding employee PII can cause privacy harm if access controls, transmission, or retention fail.

risks.description: Travel, reservation, booking, authorization, and payment/voucher records can reveal detailed movement and spending patterns about employees.
risks.evidence_quote: used for reservation, booking, authorization/obligation, and payment/voucher transactions for USDA mission critical TDY Travel
risks.rationale: Travel transaction data can disclose sensitive location and activity information about individual employees.

risks.description: The system retains user information and bill-related data for long periods, increasing the amount of time sensitive records remain available for misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases exposure time and the consequences of unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system analyzes traveler preferences and retains them for future reference, which can create a persistent profile of an employee's travel habits.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference profiling can reveal behavioral patterns beyond what is needed for a single transaction.

risks.description: Information is shared enterprise-wide and transmitted to another financial system, which expands the number of users and systems that can access employee travel data.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Broader sharing increases the attack surface and the chance of inappropriate access or secondary use.

risks.description: Authorized USDA agency users can access the system the same way as internal users, which may create overbroad access if role restrictions are not tightly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users. Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
risks.rationale: If roles are misassigned or too permissive, users may see more personal data than necessary.

risks.description: The system relies on cloud-hosted, multi-tenant infrastructure, which can increase the impact of configuration or tenant-isolation failures on employee data.
risks.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
risks.rationale: Multi-tenant environments can expose data across customers if isolation controls fail.

mitigations.description: Continue to enforce strong authentication, session protection, and encrypted transmission for all access to the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication • Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport layer • Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) • Akamai Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) • Akamai Site Shield • Virtual Private Network (VPN) Connection traffic flows through the Akamai content delivery network (CDN) leveraging the web application firewall feature, into the FortiGate edge firewall. Web connections are secured using TLS
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the likelihood that PII will be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties.

mitigations.description: Limit access to travel records to only personnel who need them for travel processing, audit, or payment validation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access helps ensure detailed travel data is not broadly visible inside the enterprise.

mitigations.description: Keep retention aligned to the approved records schedule and avoid retaining records beyond the NARA-approved period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data.
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved schedule reduces unnecessary exposure of personal data over time.

mitigations.description: Provide a way for travelers to review and update stored preferences so the profile data stays accurate and current.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference.
mitigations.rationale: Allowing users to correct or remove preferences reduces the risk of stale or inaccurate profiling.

mitigations.description: Minimize the information transmitted to the financial system to only what is required for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization lowers the amount of personal information exposed to downstream systems.

mitigations.description: Periodically review role assignments for authorized agency users to confirm they remain appropriate for each user's duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access reviews help prevent unnecessary access from accumulating over time.

mitigations.description: Maintain and test tenant-isolation and cloud security controls to ensure one tenant cannot access another tenant's data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
mitigations.rationale: Tenant-isolation testing reduces the risk of cross-tenant exposure in a shared cloud environment.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees for travel and expense processing, creating a risk of exposure if the data is mishandled or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees
risks.rationale: Travel and voucher processing requires sensitive employee data, so unauthorized disclosure would directly affect employee privacy.

risks.description: The system retains user information and bill-related data for long periods, increasing the amount of time the data could be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window during which retained records can be accessed improperly or lost.

risks.description: The system analyzes traveler preferences and retains them for future reference, which can reveal personal habits and travel patterns beyond what is strictly necessary for a trip transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference profiling can expose behavioral information that is more sensitive than a single reservation record.

risks.description: Authorization and voucher data are shared with another financial system, which creates a risk of broader dissemination of employee travel information across systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Each transmission to another system expands the number of places where the information is stored or processed.

risks.description: The system is multi-tenant and enterprise-wide, so a configuration or access-control failure could expose one customer's or user's data to another authorized party.
risks.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
risks.rationale: Multi-tenant systems must strictly separate data to prevent cross-customer or cross-user disclosure.

risks.description: Users access the system through web browsers and mobile applications, which increases the risk of interception or unauthorized access if endpoints or sessions are compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: Browser and mobile access broaden the attack surface and can expose data if devices or sessions are not protected.

risks.description: Centralized authentication through eAuthentication means a compromise of that identity service could affect access to this system and the associated employee data.
risks.evidence_quote: USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
risks.rationale: A centralized login service is a high-value target because it gates access to multiple USDA services.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of employee PII to only what is required for travel reservation, authorization, and voucher processing, and enforce role-based access to that data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PIA is being created for the front-end, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) instance of SAP Concur CCPS. Based on the Privacy Threshold Assessment submitted in December 2023, this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees, and therefore, a PIA is necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access and display reduces the chance that collected PII is unnecessarily exposed.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved records schedule and delete records as soon as the NARA retention period expires.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Deleting records on schedule reduces the time privacy-sensitive information remains available for misuse.

mitigations.description: Provide users with controls to limit preference retention and make predictive preference features optional or configurable.
mitigations.rationale: Allowing users to control preference storage reduces unnecessary retention of behavioral data.

mitigations.description: Continue validating authorization and voucher data before transmission and restrict the shared fields to only what FMMI needs for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Validating and limiting the data sent to another system reduces unnecessary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Maintain strict tenant isolation and restrictive role assignments so users can only access the data they are authorized to see.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Strong separation controls help prevent cross-tenant or cross-user exposure in a multi-tenant platform.

mitigations.description: Require strong session protection and encrypted transmission for browser and mobile access, including TLS and multifactor authentication.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer. The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and multifactor authentication reduce the chance that remote access sessions can be intercepted or hijacked.

mitigations.description: Harden the centralized authentication service with continuous monitoring and strong account protections because it is the entry point to the application.
mitigations.evidence_quote: USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the identity service lowers the risk that an attacker can use one compromise to access employee travel data.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial information, including identifiers, dates of birth, addresses, bank account numbers, and cancelled or returned check information, which creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: The more sensitive data stored in one system, the greater the harm if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system supports debt collection and maintains delinquent debt information, which can expose individuals to privacy harm if their financial difficulties or debt status are disclosed beyond authorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection
risks.rationale: Debt-related records can reveal sensitive financial circumstances and should be limited to need-to-know access.

risks.description: The system records and processes personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies, creating a risk that employee compensation and employment information could be accessed or used inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Personnel and payroll information is sensitive employment data and warrants strict access controls.

risks.description: The system maintains information for up to 10 years, which increases the chance that data will remain available longer than necessary for some individuals and raises the impact of any breach over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which records can be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: The system is used to gather statistical information, which can create privacy risk if data are aggregated or reported in a way that still reveals information about identifiable people.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: Statistical uses can still create privacy harm if outputs are not sufficiently de-identified or aggregated.

risks.description: The system includes batch job processing details, which may expose operational information about processing schedules and internal workflows if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: batch jobs processing details (Scheduling Information Tracking System)
risks.rationale: Operational metadata can aid unauthorized access or reveal when sensitive records are processed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive personal and financial fields using role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that highly sensitive data will be seen or used by unauthorized personnel.

mitigations.description: Limit debt-collection records to authorized staff and require auditing of access to delinquent debt information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection
mitigations.rationale: Access logging and authorization checks help prevent unnecessary exposure of debt-related information.

mitigations.description: Apply privacy training and strict need-to-know controls for personnel and payroll records shared or processed for USDA and other Federal agencies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
mitigations.rationale: Handling employee records carefully reduces the risk of improper internal disclosure or use.

mitigations.description: Periodically review the 10-year retention schedule and securely destroy records when they are no longer required under the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
mitigations.rationale: Timely destruction limits how long records remain exposed to breach or misuse.

mitigations.description: Ensure statistical outputs are aggregated and reviewed for disclosure risk before release or internal reporting.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and disclosure review reduce the chance that statistics can be traced back to individuals.

mitigations.description: Protect batch job details with access controls and operational logging so processing schedules are only visible to authorized administrators.
mitigations.evidence_quote: batch jobs processing details (Scheduling Information Tracking System)
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access to processing details lowers the risk of operational information leakage.

risks.description: The system retains case data, contact information, and audio files forever, creating a long-term privacy exposure if the data is no longer needed. Permanent retention increases the amount of sensitive information available for misuse, breach, or overexposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Keeping personally identifiable and case-related information indefinitely increases cumulative privacy risk without a stated end point.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information together with case determinations and audio files, which can expose sensitive appeal details if accessed inappropriately. The data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, signatures, and case materials.
risks.evidence_quote: NAD case-related data: • Audio files and case determinations • Personally Identifiable Information (P11) such as full name, address, phone number, fax number, email address, and signature. • Metadata relating to the case process (e.g. date case was filed)
risks.rationale: Combining identity data with case outcomes and recordings creates a richer and more sensitive profile of each appellant.

risks.description: Public users can submit appeals electronically and later view their submitted documents and appeal transaction details, which may expose residence and contact information through the portal. This creates a risk of unintended disclosure if portal access is misused or if account access is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The public are permitted to file appeals electronically. After they register and file an appeal electronically, customers receive electronic notifications that the appeal was received. Further, an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted. At this stage of the process, the data includes: case number, appellant residence, and contact information.
risks.rationale: Allowing individuals to retrieve detailed case information online increases the impact of any account compromise or improper access.

risks.description: Contractor employees have access to the system, which expands the number of people who can see appellant data. More users with access increases the chance of unauthorized viewing or mishandling of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack authorized users enter the data submitted to the USDA Office of Hearings and Appeals -National Appeals Division. These authorized users are USDA employees, contractor employees who access the system via eAuthentication, and the public who eFile appeal requests.
risks.rationale: Broader access among authorized users raises insider and operational privacy risk.

risks.description: Reports generated from the system are reviewed by management and may contain PII, which creates a disclosure risk if reports are shared too broadly or handled improperly. Even with a warning, report distribution can still expose sensitive information.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
risks.rationale: PII warnings help, but reports still concentrate sensitive information in a form that can be copied or forwarded.

risks.description: The system uses a secure web interface behind a login page, but the context does not describe other safeguards such as role-based access controls, encryption, or logging. Limited described protections leave a risk that unauthorized users could gain access if authentication is weakened or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack collects data through the Web interface, behind a secure login page
risks.rationale: A secure login page alone does not fully address the privacy risks of sensitive case and identity data.

risks.description: The system tracks and records participant and agency contact and identifier information, which may be more than is necessary for case tracking and reporting. Collecting and maintaining detailed identifiers can increase privacy exposure if the data is not minimized.
risks.evidence_quote: The NADTrack system handles case- related data, audio files and determinations as well as participant and agency contact and/or identifier information is tracked and recorded.
risks.rationale: Collecting more identifying detail than needed increases the amount of personal information at risk.

mitigations.description: Establish a documented retention schedule with disposal triggers and periodic review so data is deleted or archived when no longer needed for case tracking or legal purposes.
mitigations.rationale: A finite retention period reduces the time sensitive information remains exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to audio files, determinations, and PII to only the minimum personnel needed for adjudication and case administration.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that highly sensitive case content is viewed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Require strong account authentication for eFile users and protect portal sessions so appellants can only access their own records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After they register and file an appeal electronically, customers receive electronic notifications that the appeal was received. Further, an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted.
mitigations.rationale: Securing portal access is necessary because the system exposes residence and contact information to logged-in users.

mitigations.description: Apply the same access controls, training, and monitoring to contractor employees as to federal employees, and review contractor access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
mitigations.rationale: Equal controls and periodic review help reduce insider misuse and unauthorized access by contractors.

mitigations.description: Limit report contents to the minimum needed and distribute PII-containing reports only to authorized management on a need-to-know basis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting report distribution reduces the chance that compiled PII will be disclosed beyond intended reviewers.

mitigations.description: Document and implement additional technical safeguards such as role-based access control, audit logging, and encryption for data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Additional safeguards are needed to protect sensitive data beyond the stated secure login page.

mitigations.description: Review the data fields collected and remove any contact or identifier information that is not necessary for case tracking and reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only necessary identifiers reduces the privacy impact of the system.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive employee identifiers and work history, including names, Social Security numbers, time and attendance records, teleworking agreement information, and payroll data. If improperly accessed or disclosed, this could expose employees to identity theft, financial harm, or unwanted disclosure of personnel information.
risks.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data needed to conform to all applicable laws, Government regulations and procedures, and the needs of the Department and agencies in carrying out their personnel management responsibilities.
risks.rationale: The presence of SSNs and payroll/personnel data makes unauthorized disclosure especially harmful.

risks.description: The system allows human resources staff to enter information on an individual’s behalf, which creates a risk of inaccurate or over-collected records being entered without the subject’s direct review. Errors in time, attendance, or payroll data can affect pay and personnel records.
risks.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf.
risks.rationale: Third-party data entry increases the chance that incorrect or excessive information is recorded.

risks.description: WebTA shares certified time and attendance and payroll-related data with other USDA systems and customer agencies, which increases the number of places where PII may be exposed or misused. Each additional recipient expands the privacy impact if access controls or handling rules fail.
risks.evidence_quote: WebTA shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below. 1. EmpowHR: WebTA uses human resources data provided by EmpowHR. 2. Insight: WebTA generates files for transmission to the Insight hosting environment for processing. 3. OCIO eAuthentication (eAuth) application: The eAuthentication application provides authentication services for some WebTA customers. 4. TIME: WebTA transmits certified T&A data to the PPS TIME application.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII across multiple systems increases exposure points and misuse risk.

risks.description: The system permits customer agencies to determine the use and sharing of the information, which can lead to inconsistent privacy protections across agencies. Different agency rules may result in broader access or sharing than is necessary for the original collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Information collected by WebTA is owned by each customer agency. The customer agency determines the use and sharing of the information.
risks.rationale: Decentralized sharing decisions can produce uneven privacy safeguards.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system if authorized, creating a risk of broader internal access to PII than necessary. Contractor access can increase the chance of unauthorized viewing or mishandling if role assignments are not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access raises the need for strong role and oversight controls.

risks.description: Users may access predefined and custom reports and can see data elements depending on access privileges, which can expose more PII than needed if privileges are too broad. Reporting functions can also facilitate secondary use of personnel data beyond the immediate time-and-attendance purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
risks.rationale: Reporting and field-level access can reveal more information than a user strictly needs.

risks.description: The system relies on web-based collection and transmission over multiple interfaces, so any weakness in authentication, encryption, or secure transfer could expose PII in transit or at login. Although secure protocols are stated, the transmission paths still present a privacy risk if misconfigured or bypassed.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
risks.rationale: Networked collection and transfer of PII require strong controls to prevent interception or unauthorized access.

risks.description: Individuals may be given a unique user ID and password to access their own data, which creates a risk of account compromise if credentials are stolen or shared. Unauthorized access through compromised accounts could reveal time, attendance, payroll, or telework information.
risks.evidence_quote: At the customer agency's discretion and according to the agency's security policies, individuals may be assigned a unique user id and password that allows them access to their own data in WebTA.
risks.rationale: Credential-based access can be abused if passwords are weak, reused, or disclosed.

risks.description: The system retains records under NARA schedules and customer agency requirements, which may keep PII available for long periods. Longer retention increases the chance of unauthorized disclosure over time and can preserve data that is no longer needed for operations.
risks.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule. Civilian Personnel Records have various retention periods for specific types of data. These retention periods are adhered to per customer agency requirements and memorandum of understanding.
risks.rationale: The longer PII is kept, the longer it remains exposed to breach or misuse.

mitigations.description: Limit access to SSNs, payroll data, and telework agreement details to only those users with a documented need to know, and apply field-level masking where full values are not required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only individuals with an established "need-to-know" may access their specific profiled data.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers are unnecessarily exposed.

mitigations.description: Require individuals to review and confirm records entered on their behalf, and add validation or supervisory review for HR-entered changes that affect pay or attendance.
mitigations.rationale: A review step helps catch incorrect or excessive data before it is finalized.

mitigations.description: Apply strict data-sharing agreements and minimum-necessary data fields for each downstream system, with periodic review of what is transmitted to EmpowHR, Insight, eAuth, and TIME.
mitigations.evidence_quote: WebTA shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the content and purpose of each transfer reduces exposure across systems.

mitigations.description: Standardize agency sharing rules through written agreements and privacy review so that all customer agencies apply consistent minimum-necessary handling before any disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The customer agency determines the use and sharing of the information.
mitigations.rationale: Uniform rules help prevent overly broad sharing by individual agencies.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access reviews for contractors and remove contractor access promptly when it is no longer needed, with periodic recertification of valid roles.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review of contractor roles helps ensure access stays limited to authorized duties.

mitigations.description: Restrict custom reporting and sensitive data elements to approved roles, and log/report review activity to detect unusual access patterns.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter reporting controls reduce the chance of unnecessary disclosure through reports.

mitigations.description: Continuously verify that all external transfers use approved secure protocols and encryption, and prohibit any unencrypted or ad hoc transmission paths.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Ensuring only approved secure channels are used lowers interception risk.

mitigations.description: Require strong password standards and multi-factor authentication for user accounts that access personal data.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication makes account compromise less likely.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce retention and disposal schedules so records are deleted or archived when no longer required by the approved NARA schedule or customer agency need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of PII exposed over time.

risks.description: The system collects and shares contact information and inquiry details that could expose individuals if mishandled or disclosed beyond need-to-know. This includes names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and case history tied to USDA inquiries.
risks.evidence_quote: • First Name of the person contacting USDA • Last Name of the person contacting USDA • Phone number of the person contacting USDA • Email address of the person contacting USDA • Address of the of the person contacting USDA • General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
risks.rationale: The listed data elements are directly identifying and tied to inquiry content, so unauthorized disclosure would affect privacy.

risks.description: PII is transmitted by email to SME contacts, which can increase the risk of interception, misdelivery, or unauthorized forwarding. The system also uses Cisco telephony integration, adding another transmission path for sensitive contact data.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: Email is a common source of accidental disclosure, and multiple transmission channels increase exposure points.

risks.description: A broad internal audience may receive PII when inquiries are escalated across USDA mission areas, increasing the chance that more staff can access data than is necessary. This expands the number of people who can view contact information and case details.
risks.evidence_quote: Sharing of PII information with all USDA Mission Areas part of AskUSDA Contact Center for escalated inquiries that require mission area expertise to respond
risks.rationale: Sharing across many mission areas raises the risk of unnecessary internal exposure even when the purpose is legitimate.

risks.description: The system retains information for at least seven years, which increases the amount of time personal data remains exposed to breach, misuse, or secondary use. Long retention can also preserve outdated contact information and inquiry records longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained at minimum of 7 years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention extends the period during which the data must be protected and can be misused.

risks.description: No purging or archiving is currently set up for the PII available through third-party websites or applications, so data may accumulate without active lifecycle controls. This can leave older records accessible longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival, since this is a pilot this will would be reassess after the pilot phase to get a better idea of data storage required.
risks.rationale: Without automated purging, stale records can remain available and increase the privacy impact of retention.

risks.description: The system combines multiple identifiers in Salesforce, which can make records easier to link to a specific person and increase the sensitivity of the dataset. The PIA explicitly says name, address, and phone number combinations become available in the cloud environment.
risks.evidence_quote: PII data will be captured within Salesforce of the combination of Name, Address and Phone number information of contacts within the Salesforce Government Cloud Application.
risks.rationale: Combining several identifiers makes re-identification and profiling easier if access is compromised.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to the system, creating a risk of broader insider access if permissions are not tightly limited. The PIA indicates internal access is managed through role-based controls and an entitlement system, but contractor access still expands the trust boundary.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS).
risks.rationale: Any contractor access increases the number of authorized users who could improperly view or disclose PII.

risks.description: Users can submit inquiries through unauthenticated public channels, which may lead to collection of personal information from people who do not fully understand what data is being captured. The public-facing knowledge base is unauthenticated and the system collects information through webform, email, chat, and phone.
risks.evidence_quote: Public facing community knowledge base provides unauthenticated public users the ability to self-service existing USDA agency knowledge articles
risks.rationale: Public-facing intake increases the chance that individuals will submit more information than intended or without clear expectations.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and disclosure to the minimum contact and case details needed to answer the inquiry, and provide a clear privacy notice at intake explaining what is collected and why.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected data reduces the harm if records are accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Replace ordinary email transmission of PII with a secure case-sharing workflow or encrypted messaging, and restrict email content to non-sensitive references where possible.
mitigations.rationale: A more controlled transfer method reduces the chance of interception or misdelivery.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access and need-to-know limits so only the specific mission area staff needed for the escalation can view the related PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing internal access reduces unnecessary exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Review the seven-year retention period to confirm it is necessary for each record type and delete records when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is retained at minimum of 7 years.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter or better-justified retention lowers the time that PII remains at risk.

mitigations.description: Implement automated purging and archival controls for third-party application data so records are removed or archived on a defined schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Automated lifecycle controls prevent unnecessary accumulation of older personal data.

mitigations.description: Separate or tokenize identifiers where possible and restrict access to combined identity records to staff with a documented operational need.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing linkability limits the sensitivity of the stored dataset.

mitigations.description: Require periodic access recertification for contractors and other internal users, and remove access promptly when it is no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps ensure only authorized users retain access to PII.

mitigations.description: Add clear pre-submission guidance on public intake channels telling users what personal information is optional and what should not be submitted unless necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Better guidance can reduce overcollection from unauthenticated public users.

risks.description: The system captures identifiable video of employees, contractors, and visitors as they move through USDA buildings, creating broad surveillance of ordinary activity. This can reveal who was present, where they went, and when they were there.
risks.evidence_quote: the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
risks.rationale: Video surveillance of routine movement can expose sensitive location and presence information even when no wrongdoing is involved.

risks.description: The cameras may capture facial images and license plate numbers, allowing individuals and vehicles to be identified and tracked. This increases the privacy impact beyond simple anonymous footage.
risks.evidence_quote: The VSS cameras may capture facial images of employees and visitors to USDA buildings and images of license plates that are parked or driving through the parking lot.
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers make it easier to link footage to specific people and vehicles.

risks.description: Some cameras collect metadata such as camera name, location, time, and date, which can strengthen profiling and movement tracking when combined with video. Metadata can make it easier to reconstruct a person's activities across time.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, some VSS collect metadata. ... For example, camera name, location, time, and date.
risks.rationale: Time-stamped location metadata increases the ability to analyze patterns of presence and movement.

risks.description: The system can capture sensitive personal information from driver's licenses, including full names, addresses, and dates of birth. This creates a risk of collecting more personal information than is necessary for general security monitoring.
risks.evidence_quote: The video footage includes images of people, information found on drivers licenses such as full names, addresses, date of birth, as well as license plate numbers.
risks.rationale: Capturing detailed identity information increases the sensitivity of the footage and the harm from disclosure or misuse.

risks.description: Manual pan/tilt/zoom tracking and automatic tracking allow security personnel to follow a single individual in crowded areas. This creates a risk of intensive monitoring and persistent tracking of specific people.
risks.evidence_quote: Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
risks.rationale: Tracking features can turn general surveillance into person-specific monitoring.

risks.description: Footage may be shared with internal and external organizations for criminal investigations, disciplinary actions, and law enforcement purposes, increasing the risk of secondary use beyond the original collection context. Broader sharing can expose footage to additional handling and disclosure risks.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions.
risks.rationale: Sharing expands the number of people and organizations that can access sensitive footage.

risks.description: The system may retain video longer than six months depending on storage, camera counts, and other factors, which can extend the period of surveillance exposure. Longer retention increases the chance that footage will be used for purposes unrelated to the original event.
risks.evidence_quote: however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
risks.rationale: The longer footage is kept, the longer it remains available for review, reuse, or disclosure.

risks.description: Footage retrieved for suspected criminal activity is retained until investigative or enforcement action is completed, which can create open-ended retention. This may keep sensitive recordings available far longer than ordinary operational needs require.
risks.evidence_quote: Records which are retrieved pursuant to suspected criminal activity will be retained until any investigative or enforcement action is completed.
risks.rationale: Open-ended retention increases exposure time for sensitive recordings tied to specific individuals or events.

risks.description: Contractors and select non-employees can access the system if they have background checks and security clearances, which creates an insider-access risk. Any expanded access base increases the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse of footage.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: More authorized users means more opportunities for inappropriate access or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit camera placement and viewing to facility security needs and avoid areas with a reasonable expectation of privacy, as stated in the system design.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Cameras are not placed in places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as inside a bathroom or changing room.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting camera placement reduces unnecessary capture of private activity.

mitigations.description: Use access controls and formal request procedures before any sharing or review of footage that contains facial images or license plates.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting review and sharing helps reduce exposure of identifiable footage.

mitigations.description: Minimize use of metadata to only what is needed to manage feeds and footage files, and restrict access to that metadata to authorized administrators.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is used to manage the VSS feeds and footage files.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting metadata use reduces the ability to reconstruct detailed movement histories.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization by configuring cameras and review practices to avoid capturing driver's license details unless they are clearly necessary for a security purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The video footage includes images of people, information found on drivers licenses such as full names, addresses, date of birth, as well as license plate numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing capture of identity details lowers the sensitivity of the recordings.

mitigations.description: Require documented justification and supervisory approval for manual tracking or auto-tracking of a specific person, and limit such tracking to active security incidents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and incident-based limits help prevent unnecessary person-specific surveillance.

mitigations.description: Limit external disclosures to the minimum footage necessary for the stated criminal investigation or prosecution purpose and document each release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with external organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing disclosed footage reduces the privacy impact of secondary use.

mitigations.description: Enforce the six-month deletion schedule automatically and prohibit routine extensions unless a documented exception is approved.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored for a maximum of six months and then is automatically deleted.
mitigations.rationale: Strict deletion limits the amount of historical footage available for later review.

mitigations.description: Require a supervisor to approve any extended retention and confirm in writing that the footage is relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To retain the footage after the retention period, a supervisor must approve the request and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and relevance checks help ensure longer retention is tied to a legitimate need.

mitigations.description: Restrict contractor and non-employee access to the minimum necessary functions and periodically review their access rights.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and reviewing access reduces insider misuse risk among non-employee users.

risks.description: The system can collect limited personally identifiable information, which creates a risk of exposing names, email addresses, and zip codes if the feedback data is mishandled or over-collected.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Collecting identifiable contact information increases the privacy impact because the feedback can be tied to a person.

risks.description: Free-form comments may capture PII even when the system is intended to collect only feedback, increasing the chance that sensitive information is submitted unintentionally.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII
risks.rationale: Open-text fields are harder to control and can lead users to disclose more personal information than intended.

risks.description: The system may be used to gather customer insights geographically, demographically, and ethnographically, which can create profiling or inference risks about individuals or groups.
risks.evidence_quote: Gather customer insights and feedback geographically, demographically and ethnographically in order to identify areas in need of improvement
risks.rationale: Aggregating and analyzing these attributes can reveal patterns about people that go beyond the original feedback.

risks.description: A small number of users can access all data across all mission areas, creating a concentration-of-access risk if those accounts are misused or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: Broad access by a few users increases the impact of any unauthorized access or insider misuse.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to the system, which increases the risk of unauthorized disclosure or mishandling of feedback and any embedded PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond federal employees broadens the set of people who can view or process the data.

risks.description: The system supports migration from multiple existing USDA tools into one cohesive product, which creates a risk of combining data in ways that increase identifiability or unintended secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
risks.rationale: Consolidating data from multiple sources can make records easier to link to individuals.

risks.description: The system uses real-time analytics and broad internal dashboards, which can expose sensitive patterns if aggregated views are not sufficiently de-identified or access-controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
risks.rationale: Even aggregated dashboards can reveal sensitive information when combined with detailed analytics or broad access.

risks.description: Retention is not yet approved by the component records officer and NARA, creating a risk that records may be kept longer than authorized or disposed of improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Unapproved retention increases the chance of noncompliant storage or deletion practices.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of names, email addresses, and zip codes to cases where a customer explicitly requests follow-up, and otherwise collect feedback anonymously.
mitigations.evidence_quote: On some occasions, a customer may request to be contacted by a USDA official and this information will allow contact to be made.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting PII only when needed reduces the amount of identifiable data in the system.

mitigations.description: Add prominent notices and form design controls to warn users against entering unnecessary personal information in free-text fields.
mitigations.rationale: Preventing unnecessary disclosure at the point of collection reduces accidental submission of personal data.

mitigations.description: Restrict demographic and geographic analysis to aggregated reporting with thresholds that prevent singling out small groups or individuals.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation limits the chance that analysis will reveal identifiable patterns about specific people.

mitigations.description: Tighten role-based access so only users with a documented mission need can access cross-mission data, and review those privileged accounts regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users of the VoC platform will be selected based on their mission need to access the system and their permission levels.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and reviewing privileged access reduces the likelihood of misuse or unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Apply the same privacy and security training, licensing, and documented permission controls to contractors before they receive access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Approved USDA employees will undergo in-person training on platform functionality, privacy, and security controls. Before users gain access to the system, they must be provided a license and their permission will be documented in a database file.
mitigations.rationale: Extending access controls and training to contractors lowers the risk of improper handling by non-employee users.

mitigations.description: Perform a privacy review before migrating data from legacy tools and map fields to ensure only necessary data is consolidated into the new platform.
mitigations.rationale: A migration review helps prevent unnecessary combination of records that could increase identifiability.

mitigations.description: Keep dashboard outputs aggregated and suppress small-cell or highly detailed views before sharing them with internal users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII will not be included in these dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Suppressing detailed output helps ensure dashboards do not reveal personal information indirectly.

mitigations.description: Obtain records disposition approval from the component records officer and NARA before finalizing retention and disposal procedures.
mitigations.rationale: Formal approval helps ensure retention and deletion practices comply with records requirements.

risks.description: The system stores and processes PII in a third-party cloud service outside the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary, which creates privacy and oversight risk if the hosted environment is misconfigured or accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Moving PII to an external SaaS environment increases dependence on the provider's controls and agency visibility.

risks.description: Users must provide name, email address, username, and contact numbers, so the system collects identifiable contact information that could be exposed if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Workiva Wdesk collects name, email address, and contact numbers.
risks.rationale: The system maintains direct identifiers that can link records to specific individuals.

risks.description: Account creation requires mandatory PII with no option to decline, which limits user choice and may collect more identifying information than some users expect for access alone.
risks.evidence_quote: No First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Mandatory collection without an opt-out increases privacy impact because the individual cannot avoid disclosure to use the system.

risks.description: The system is used for the USDA Annual Financial Report and the document data is described as publicly accessible, so there is a risk that information entered into the platform may be disclosed more broadly than intended.
risks.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data.
risks.rationale: Public-facing content can create privacy exposure if personal information is included in report materials.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which expands the number of people who may view or handle PII and increases insider access risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Broader access populations raise the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse of identifiable information.

risks.description: Access can be granted with supervisor or higher-level approval, so inconsistent approval practices could result in users receiving more access than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
risks.rationale: Flexible approval paths can weaken least-privilege enforcement if not tightly governed.

risks.description: The system logs access transactions, approvals, additions, and removals, which means detailed activity records about users are retained and could themselves reveal sensitive access patterns.
