risks.evidence_quote: All access transactions, including approvals, additions, or removals of access are fully logged by the system.
risks.rationale: Audit logs can contain sensitive operational metadata about who accessed or was granted access to the system.

risks.description: Information is retained for 75 months, so PII remains available for a long period and may be exposed for longer than necessary if it is no longer needed for the stated purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window during which stored PII can be compromised or misused.

mitigations.description: Require and periodically verify strong cloud security controls, configuration reviews, and contractual safeguards for the third-party hosted environment.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
mitigations.rationale: Because the system is hosted externally, ongoing control assurance is needed to reduce cloud-specific privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum contact fields needed for account provisioning and restrict access to those fields to authorized users only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected is only used for account provisioning.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and tightly restricting use of contact information reduces exposure of identifiable data.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear privacy notice explaining why the mandatory fields are required and whether any alternatives exist for users who cannot provide them.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps individuals understand unavoidable collection before account creation.

mitigations.description: Review report content before publication to ensure no unnecessary personal information is included in publicly accessible materials.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-publication review reduces the chance that personal data is exposed in public reports.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access limits and contractor-specific least-privilege permissions, with periodic review of contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Limiting contractor access reduces the number of people who can view or handle PII.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce approval criteria for elevated access so supervisor approvals are consistent and tied to a verified business need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
mitigations.rationale: Standardized approval criteria help prevent unnecessary access grants.

mitigations.description: Restrict log access to authorized administrators and protect logs as sensitive records, with periodic review for inappropriate access patterns.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All access transactions, including approvals, additions, or removals of access are fully logged by the system.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting logs is necessary because they can reveal sensitive user and access information.

mitigations.description: Review whether the full 75-month retention period is necessary for all retained records and purge data as soon as records-management rules allow.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
mitigations.rationale: Shortening retention where permissible reduces the time PII remains exposed to risk.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, including SSNs, TINs, handwritten signatures, salary data, and legal names, which creates a risk of identity theft or other harm if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: This information may include the applicant’s employment history, key personnel salary data, or key personnel legal name, SSN, handwritten signatures, Grants.gov user ID, and address as well as pre-award, award and post-award details.
risks.rationale: The presence of direct identifiers and sensitive financial data increases the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Grant applicant and award information may be disclosed to external parties, including entities outside the United States, which creates a risk of over-disclosure or sharing beyond what applicants expect.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS award results related information can be shared with a number of external parties, including, but not limited to, non-profit organizations, state and local organizations, individuals, corporations, and entities outside the US.
risks.rationale: Broad external sharing expands the number of recipients who could receive personal information.

risks.description: PII may be transmitted or disclosed in common office formats or on paper, which raises the risk of accidental forwarding, loss, or unauthorized access during handling.
risks.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
risks.rationale: Multiple disclosure formats increase the chance that information will be mishandled outside the system.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system for backup, support, and account management, which creates a risk of insider misuse or unnecessary access to personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases the number of people who can view or handle sensitive records.

risks.description: The system allows manual entry of information by approved users, which creates a risk of inaccurate, incomplete, or excessive personal data being entered and then retained.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FNS FM-GSS application users have the ability to manually enter information in the processing application to assist them in managing their data.
risks.rationale: Manual entry can introduce errors or unnecessary data that later affect privacy and record accuracy.

risks.description: GIMS maintains official grant files for a long period, which creates a risk that personal information will remain accessible longer than needed for day-to-day operations.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window of exposure if access controls fail or records are improperly used.

risks.description: FMAT uses matching logic to identify vendors based on name, address, and case number, which creates a risk of misidentification or incorrect linkage of a person to a collection record.
risks.evidence_quote: This logic is used to determine the vendor against which the collection will be processed. In case of no matches, the system will use the information to create a new vendor to process the collections.
risks.rationale: Automated matching errors can connect personal data to the wrong individual or create duplicate records.

risks.description: The system shares data for award decisions and reporting, which creates a risk that personal information will be used for purposes beyond the original collection if controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: data from GIMS may be shared with internal FNS organizations for the purpose of making award decisions and/or announcing awards. It may also be shared with external parties at the discretion of the Grants Director.
risks.rationale: Using the same records for multiple downstream purposes increases the chance of secondary use beyond what the data subject expects.

mitigations.description: Continue encrypting sensitive personal data in transit and at rest, and limit the use of SSN/TIN to only what is necessary for the business process.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and data minimization reduce the impact of unauthorized access to highly sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Require Grants Director approval before any external disclosure and limit sharing to the smallest set of recipients needed for the grants purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Transmissions/disclosures typically require approval by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and recipient limitation help prevent unnecessary external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use encrypted transmission and restrict hard-copy handling to authorized staff only when disclosure outside the system is necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
mitigations.rationale: Extra handling controls reduce the chance of loss or unauthorized viewing in transit and on paper.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access controls and periodic access reviews for contractor accounts.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting contractor access to only required functions lowers the risk of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Add validation and review steps for manually entered records before they are saved or used in processing.
mitigations.rationale: Review controls can catch inaccurate or excessive entries before they affect downstream records.

mitigations.description: Apply retention and archival controls that automatically remove or archive records according to the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
mitigations.rationale: Automated retention enforcement helps ensure records are not kept accessible longer than authorized.

mitigations.description: Add human review for automated vendor matching and creation decisions when the system cannot confidently match a record.
mitigations.rationale: Human review can prevent incorrect identity linkage caused by automated matching errors.

mitigations.description: Limit reporting and award-related sharing to approved purposes and document the justification for each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data in GIMS is used to support the discretionary grants award process at FNS.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation and disclosure documentation reduce the chance of secondary use outside the stated grants function.

risks.description: The database centralizes detailed and sensitive SNAP participant information from all states, creating a high-value target and increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: SNAP participant data to be contained in the SNAP Information Database will include detailed and sensitive personally identiﬁable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed, as well as ﬁnancial data (e.g., amount of beneﬁt received).
risks.rationale: A centralized repository of sensitive PII and financial data raises the consequences of any security failure.

risks.description: The system collects historical data for a very long period, which increases privacy exposure for people whose older records may no longer be necessary for current checks.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Collecting decades of records expands the amount of personal information retained and exposed to use.

risks.description: Automated matching and integrity checks can produce false positives that may wrongly flag eligible participants as ineligible, duplicate, or fraudulent.
risks.evidence_quote: Integrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database, using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
risks.rationale: Automated matching can still misidentify people, so errors may affect benefits and privacy interests.

risks.description: The system shares information across federal and state systems and with state agencies, which can broaden access beyond the original collecting agency and increase secondary-use risk.
risks.evidence_quote: This initiative will focus on detecting duplicate enrollments across states, verifying immigration status eligibility, and performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Cross-agency sharing increases the number of entities handling the data and the chance of misuse or over-disclosure.

risks.description: The system includes immigration status checks, which can expose highly sensitive information and create stigma or harm if handled improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: verifying immigration status eligibility
risks.rationale: Immigration-related information is sensitive and can have serious consequences if disclosed or used incorrectly.

risks.description: The system performs identity and SSN validation, which increases the risk of identity-related harm if those identifiers are exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Identity and social security number (SSN) validation
risks.rationale: SSNs and identity data are highly sensitive identifiers that can be exploited if improperly accessed.

risks.description: The system includes household composition and age validation, which may reveal family structure and other personal details beyond what is needed for a narrow eligibility check.
risks.evidence_quote: Age and household composition validation
risks.rationale: Family and age information can expose intimate household details if broadly shared or retained.

mitigations.description: Restrict database access to authorized personnel only, enforce strong authentication and auditing, and keep the AWS environment secured under the existing ATO.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FNS’ Oﬃce of Information Technology (OIT) maintains a secure AWS environment that is authorized under the FNS Infrastructure General Support System (FNS I-GSS) Authority to Operate (ATO).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit retention to the minimum period needed for integrity checks and purge older records that are no longer necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing retention reduces the privacy impact of keeping decades of participant data.

mitigations.description: Require human review before any adverse action is taken based on an automated match and provide a process to correct mismatches.
mitigations.evidence_quote: using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
mitigations.rationale: Human review and correction procedures help prevent harm from automated errors.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing to only the data elements needed for each permitted integrity check and document each disclosure to state and federal recipients.
mitigations.evidence_quote: sharing, where permitted by law and consistent with this notice, information with State agencies when necessary to investigate and rectify fraudulent or otherwise improper or illegal SNAP enrollments or transactions.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and disclosure logging reduce unnecessary spread of participant information.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened access controls and purpose limitation to immigration-related data and restrict its use to the stated eligibility check.
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards are warranted because immigration information is especially sensitive.

mitigations.description: Protect SSNs and identity data with encryption in transit and at rest, and mask or truncate them where full values are not required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: via the secure MoveIt or Box managed ﬁle transfer application.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting identifiers in transit and limiting their display reduces identity theft risk.

mitigations.description: Collect only the minimum household and age information needed for validation and avoid broader use of those details outside the eligibility check.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization lowers the chance that family structure and age information will be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: The system stores identifiable personal and contact information about non-employees, which creates a privacy risk if that data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Names, business address and contact information, and Affiliate ID of Contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Government employees, Resource Conservation & Development Council employees, Volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organization personnel (referred to as Affiliates).
risks.rationale: The record contains direct identifiers and contact details for multiple categories of affiliates.

risks.description: NRCS employees manually enter affiliate information provided by the affiliate, which creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records being used for access decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: An NRCS employee enters the information about the individual non-employee affiliate, which is populated from information that was provided by the non-employee.
risks.rationale: Manual transcription and reliance on a third party increase the chance of error in records that drive authorization.

risks.description: The system links affiliate records to Level 2 eAuthentication accounts and uses them to assign roles, so a mistake or unauthorized change could grant improper access to NRCS systems.
risks.evidence_quote: The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record. The zRoles application is then used to assign specific roles to the Level 2 account, which allows the affiliate access to various NRCS applications.
risks.rationale: Because the data directly controls access privileges, errors or tampering can affect who can reach NRCS applications.

risks.description: The system shares affiliate information with the zRoles application, creating an internal disclosure risk across systems even though it stays within USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth to affiliates
risks.rationale: Inter-system sharing increases the number of places where the information can be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: The application is only accessible by NRCS employees, so insider misuse or excessive access by employees could expose affiliate information or alter access rights.
risks.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
risks.rationale: Limiting access to employees reduces exposure, but it also means any employee with access could misuse sensitive access-control data.

risks.description: The records may be retained for long periods, increasing the chance that outdated personal information remains stored longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase the window during which personal data can be exposed or become stale.

risks.description: Retention tied to whether a person qualifies for conservation programs could leave records in the system for the full duration of that relationship, extending privacy exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs
risks.rationale: Keeping records for the duration of program participation extends the period in which the information remains available.

mitigations.description: Limit stored fields to the minimum needed for access-control administration and review whether any contact details can be reduced or omitted.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected and retained personal data reduces exposure if the record is accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Require a verification step before records are saved or used for authorization, such as confirming the affiliate's details with the source submission.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is provided directly to an NRCS employee by the affiliate
mitigations.rationale: A confirmation step helps catch transcription errors before they affect access decisions.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic review of linked accounts and assigned roles to confirm that access remains appropriate.
mitigations.rationale: Regular recertification reduces the risk that incorrect or outdated role assignments persist.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access controls and audit logging to all internal transfers between Affiliates and zRoles.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application
mitigations.rationale: Controls and logs help ensure that only authorized internal processing occurs and that changes can be traced.

mitigations.description: Use least-privilege access for NRCS employees and monitor employee activity for unauthorized viewing or changes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege and monitoring reduce the likelihood and impact of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply retention schedules that remove records as soon as the approved records schedule permits and purge inactive records on schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal limits how long personal information remains exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Conduct periodic reviews to determine whether each record still needs to be retained for the person's current program status.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing ongoing need helps ensure records are not kept longer than necessary for program administration.

risks.description: The system stores and makes available highly sensitive personal and financial information about producers, policyholders, agents, and adjusters, creating a risk of harm if the warehouse is breached or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: The BAD Data Warehouse system administered by the Center for Agribusiness Excellence (CAE) at Tarleton State University (TSU) is a data warehousing and data mining project for the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Risk Management Agency (RMA). The BAD Data Warehouse provides access to and maintains weather and crop loss data by way of a web application known as Hyper Dynamic Reporting Application (HyDRA). This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted because of the vast amount of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) that is accessed through the BAD Data Warehouse.
risks.rationale: A large centralized repository of PII and policy data increases the impact of unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system combines multiple datasets into a single production warehouse, which can increase re-identification and aggregation risk by linking identity, farm, crop, and policy details.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all years is moved into a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
risks.rationale: Combining records into one warehouse makes it easier to associate different personal and operational details about the same people.

risks.description: The warehouse contains tax IDs, social security numbers, and precise location data, which are especially sensitive if exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The following data is imported from RMA and FSA: Producer name, address, phone numbers, tax ID, ID type, and entity type, as well as any associated farm numbers. Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc. Policy data includes name, address, phone number, policy number, unit, Approved Insurance Provider (AIP), crop, insurance plan, coverage level, indemnity, liability, premium, fund placement, acres, agent name, agent social security number, adjuster name, adjuster social security number, and etc.
risks.rationale: These identifiers and location details can enable identity theft or reveal sensitive business and property information.

risks.description: Authorized external users such as AIPs can access only their policy data, but the system still exposes information through a web application on the RMA Extranet, so unauthorized access or overbroad access could disclose records to the wrong party.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA and Approved Insurance Provider (AIP) HyDRA are accessible via caehydralink which resides on the RMA Extranet. An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL. Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs. AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
risks.rationale: Web-based access by multiple organizations creates a risk that access controls could fail or be misapplied.

risks.description: The system uses weekly loads and data cleansing steps that alter source files, which creates a risk that personal data could be changed incorrectly or that privacy-relevant details could be lost during processing.
risks.evidence_quote: Data was cleansed and standardized. Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data. For example, “Mr.” will appear in some records with a period and in others without a period. Consistency changes are achieved by including/removing the period, thus eliminating the one-character difference that would be problematic in data analysis where unique individuals must be identified.
risks.rationale: Transforming source data can introduce inaccuracies that affect individuals' records and downstream decisions.

risks.description: The system retains information for the life of the project, which increases the duration of exposure and the chance that data will be used beyond the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the time window in which sensitive data can be misused or disclosed.

risks.description: The system uses weather and crop loss data to support fraud and abuse analysis, which could lead to adverse effects on individuals if analytic outputs are inaccurate or over-interpreted.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program. The objective is to provide tools, information, and analysis proven effective in the private sector in reducing insurance waste, fraud, and abuse.
risks.rationale: Analytic use of personal and claim data can affect individuals if results are wrong or used too broadly.

risks.description: The system relies on validation and reporting copies of results being available to project staff and the RMA project manager, which can expose more information than necessary if reports are broadly shared or retained.
risks.evidence_quote: Validation logs of the restore procedure are used to verify that all data was successfully processed. Additional validations and edit checks are performed after the data integration to ensure completeness and accuracy of the final data. Privacy Impact Assessment – BAD Page 7 3. For the row count test, electronic copies of the results are filed and include a date and time stamp from Teradata. Results of the validation scripts are in an electronic format and are available to the RMA project manager.
risks.rationale: Operational reports can contain sensitive metadata and data summaries that should be limited to those who need them.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the warehouse and HyDRA to authorized users only, with strong authentication and least-privilege permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access control reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure of the large amount of PII in the system.

mitigations.description: Segregate datasets and limit cross-dataset linking to the minimum necessary for approved business purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting linkage reduces aggregation and re-identification risk in a centralized warehouse.

mitigations.description: Mask or redact tax IDs, social security numbers, and precise location data in user-facing reports unless those fields are strictly required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of the most sensitive identifiers lowers the harm from disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls so AIPs can view only their own policy records and periodically review entitlements for all external users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Tight entitlement review helps ensure users see only the records they are permitted to access.

mitigations.description: Add automated data-quality checks and exception review for cleansing and standardization steps before data is loaded into the production warehouse.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Additional validations and edit checks are performed after the data integration to ensure completeness and accuracy of the final data.
mitigations.rationale: Quality checks help prevent processing errors from altering personal data incorrectly.

mitigations.description: Apply a shorter retention schedule for identifiable records when historical analysis does not require full identifiers, and purge or return data promptly when the project ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention limits the period during which sensitive records are exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Require human review before any fraud-related action is taken from analytic outputs, and document the limits of the analysis in reports and training materials.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program. The objective is to provide tools, information, and analysis proven effective in the private sector in reducing insurance waste, fraud, and abuse.
mitigations.rationale: Human review and clear limitations reduce the chance of harmful decisions based on imperfect analytics.

mitigations.description: Limit validation logs and report files to operational staff who need them, and remove unnecessary timestamps or record-level details from stored outputs.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing the content and audience of operational reports reduces incidental disclosure.

risks.description: The system stores names, email addresses, phone numbers, and company addresses, which could expose employees or affiliates if the application is improperly accessed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Privacy related information is collected and maintained by CoLab in 'profiles' that include the individual's name and work contact information. For some individuals, personal contact information is maintained in their profile. • Personal Contact Information is comprised of the following elements: o First name o Last name o Email o Phone o Company Address
risks.rationale: Storing direct contact details creates a privacy risk if unauthorized users gain access or if the data is overexposed.

risks.description: CoLab relies on USDA eAuth identity information to create and manage user profiles, so errors or misuse of that identity data could affect access and profile accuracy.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile.
risks.rationale: Using external identity data as the basis for profiles makes correct handling of that data important to avoid inaccurate or inappropriate access decisions.

risks.description: Authorized contractors and partners can access the system, which increases the number of people who may view profile PII and raises insider misuse risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? • Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond direct employees increases the chance of unnecessary viewing or misuse of personal information.

risks.description: Users can modify their own profiles, so inaccurate or excessive personal information may be entered and retained if users update fields incorrectly.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Allowing self-service edits can create privacy harm if users enter more information than needed or make incorrect updates.

risks.description: PII is retained for as long as the application remains in production, which may keep personal data longer than necessary if deletion is not timely.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the period during which personal data could be exposed or misused.

risks.description: Although deletion is authorized when data is no longer needed, the system depends on administrative judgment, which could delay removal of obsolete personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
risks.rationale: A discretionary deletion trigger can leave personal information in the system longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Limit profile fields to the minimum contact information needed for authorization and access management, and restrict who can view those fields.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab contains a minimal amount of contact information related to CoLab users.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored contact details reduces the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Verify eAuth-derived identity information before creating or updating a profile, and require periodic review of profile accuracy.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and review reduce the risk that incorrect identity data will affect profile integrity or access decisions.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role assignments and periodically review contractor and partner access to ensure it remains necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access and reviews help limit unnecessary exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Add validation and field-level guidance for self-service profile edits so users can only change approved fields and are discouraged from entering unnecessary data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining self-service edits lowers the chance of inaccurate or excessive personal information being stored.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic review and automated deletion of inactive or no-longer-needed profiles before the application is retired.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
mitigations.rationale: Regular cleanup shortens the time personal data remains available and reduces exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Use a documented retention schedule with scheduled deletion checkpoints so records are removed promptly once they are no longer needed for operational, legal, or audit purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: A defined deletion process helps ensure obsolete personal data is removed without delay.

risks.description: IDEA retains vendor names and contact information in the DataMart, creating a risk of unauthorized access to stored PII if the repository is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Stored PII is more exposed than purely transitory use because it persists in the system.

risks.description: IDEA uses read-only web service calls to pull vendor PII from SCIMS, which creates a risk of overexposure or interception during data retrieval.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of these financial reports contain vendor PH that is obtained from the Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS) system via read-only web service calls.
risks.rationale: Any system-to-system transfer of PII can be exposed if the exchange is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Because IDEA produces reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus, there is a risk that users could generate reports exposing more vendor PII than necessary for a given task.
risks.evidence_quote: While IDEA does not process any transactions, the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
risks.rationale: User-selected reporting criteria can unintentionally broaden the scope of PII returned.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk that personnel beyond core employees may view vendor PII without sufficient need to know.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Broader access increases the number of people who can potentially see sensitive information.

risks.description: PII is retained while the application remains in production, which creates a risk that vendor data may persist longer than necessary if deletion is not timely.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window during which data can be misused or breached.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the DataMart PII to only authorized roles and log all access to stored vendor records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance of unauthorized viewing of retained PII.

mitigations.description: Encrypt SCIMS web service traffic and validate the source and destination endpoints for every read-only call.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the transfer channel reduces the risk of interception or misuse during retrieval.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based report controls and default the selectable criteria to the minimum necessary fields for each report.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining report parameters helps prevent unnecessary disclosure of vendor PII.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews for contractors and periodically recertify their need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access review helps ensure contractors retain access only when justified.

mitigations.description: Implement a scheduled deletion process that removes retained vendor PII as soon as it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per NARA General Records Schedule 20, application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Timely deletion reduces the amount of PII kept in the system and the duration of exposure.

risks.description: Core Services can expose sensitive customer identifiers and financial details if its API responses or internal data flows are accessed improperly. The system handles names, addresses, SCIMS IDs linked to SSNs or tax IDs, and bank account digits.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services accesses the following information for Program Participants, Farmers, Ranchers and Producers: • Full name or alias • Street Address or email address • SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number • bank account numbers (last few digits only) • case number (caseId, casename)
risks.rationale: This data can identify individuals and includes financial and government identifiers, so unauthorized disclosure would create meaningful privacy harm.

risks.description: The system relies on a shared customer database view and replicated access paths, which increases the chance that more users or systems can see customer data than necessary. NRCS users do not have direct access to SCIMS, but they do access a copy of the database through Core Services and related systems.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth). NRCS users do not have direct access to SCIMS.
risks.rationale: Shared views and replicated access paths can expand the number of places where personal data is available, increasing exposure risk.

risks.description: The system transmits PII between client applications, gateways, and databases, creating interception or misuse risk if transport protections or endpoint controls fail. Requests and formatted data move over HTTPS through a single entry point and internal gateway services.
risks.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS 4. Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: Any system that moves personal data across multiple components needs strong transport and gateway protections to prevent unauthorized access in transit.

risks.description: Returning data in JSON format to client applications may expose more personal information than necessary if responses are not tightly limited. Core Services gathers requested information and returns it to the user in JSON format.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services receives API requests from various client applications and responds to the requests by performing business logic, running database queries, and using programmatic interfaces necessary to gather the requested information and will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: Structured API responses can leak sensitive fields unless response content is minimized to the specific need of each request.

risks.description: Contractors with need-to-know access may still create insider privacy risk if access is not tightly limited and monitored. The system allows contractors to access Core Services as part of their regular duties.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Privileged internal access can lead to inappropriate viewing or use of personal data without strong controls.

risks.description: Administrative and transactional records stored in Core Services may still reveal user activity and client interactions even though the system does not store PII. The system explicitly stores administrative and transactional information for the services only.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services does not store PII; any PII stored is in the originating databases. The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
risks.rationale: Operational logs and transaction records can still create privacy risk by revealing who interacted with the system and when.

risks.description: The system supports sharing of data across multiple USDA internal systems, which can increase the number of places personal information is copied or exposed. Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
risks.rationale: Each additional internal recipient or integration point increases the attack surface and the chance of inappropriate disclosure.

risks.description: The system can support reports on sensitive demographic characteristics, which raises the risk of profiling or improper secondary use if those reports are not strictly controlled. SCIMS access allows NRCS managers to generate reports on race, sex, national origin, and disability.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Demographic reporting can be privacy-sensitive because it can reveal protected characteristics beyond basic contact information.

mitigations.description: Limit API responses to the minimum fields needed for each business function and mask or redact sensitive identifiers before returning them.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing returned data reduces the impact if a response is intercepted or misused.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and eAuth-based authorization on every view and replicated data path, with periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to the data is through established security rules via eAuth.
mitigations.rationale: Tight authorization helps ensure users only reach the SCIMS data they are allowed to see.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong HTTPS-only transport, gateway inspection, and monitoring at the external-facing and internal CA API Gateway points.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS 4. Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the transport path and entry points reduces the chance of interception or unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply response filtering and field-level data minimization so each JSON response contains only the data needed by the requesting client.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting response content lowers the risk of over-disclosure through APIs.

mitigations.description: Require need-to-know approval, background investigations, and audit logging for contractor access, with regular review of contractor activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Extra vetting and monitoring reduce the chance of insider misuse by privileged users.

mitigations.description: Define a retention schedule for administrative and transactional records and purge them when no longer needed for the service.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting how long operational records are kept reduces the amount of activity data available for misuse or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Restrict internal data sharing to documented business needs and minimize metadata shared between systems.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the scope of internal sharing lowers the number of systems that can expose personal data.

mitigations.description: Limit demographic reporting to authorized personnel and log/report access to protected-characteristic data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls and logging help prevent inappropriate use of sensitive demographic information.

risks.description: Emergency Action Plans contain personally identifiable information about emergency responders and property owners, so unauthorized disclosure could expose home addresses and telephone numbers during a dam emergency.
risks.evidence_quote: EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: The system stores sensitive contact and location information that could be misused if disclosed outside authorized emergency use.

risks.description: PII may be disclosed in hardcopy or electronic form during review cycles or activation, creating a risk of loss, interception, or improper handling outside the system.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Physical and electronic distribution increases the number of places the data can be exposed.

risks.description: The system relies on state and local emergency responders and contractors with access to EAPs, which increases the risk of access beyond the minimum necessary if need-to-know controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
risks.rationale: More authorized user groups create more opportunities for accidental or inappropriate access.

risks.description: DamWatch stores records for long periods, so personal information may remain available longer than needed for the specific emergency purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which stale personal information can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: The system uses publicly accessible information resources and voluntary submissions, which may lead to collecting more personal information than is necessary for EAP execution.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII can be obtained from publicly accessible information resources, from organizations involved in emergency response, or submitted voluntarily by individual responders or property owners.
risks.rationale: Using broad sources can result in overcollection if only a subset of the data is actually needed.

risks.description: Telephone numbers may be collected even when they are not publicly listed, creating a privacy risk for individuals whose contact information is not otherwise public.
risks.evidence_quote: All DamWatch EAP PII is publicly available, with the possible exception of telephone numbers that may not be publicly listed.
risks.rationale: Nonpublic phone numbers are more sensitive and deserve tighter handling.

mitigations.description: Limit access to EAP PII to authorized users with a documented need-to-know and require secure communications for any disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access and using secure communications reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use secure handling procedures for both hardcopy and electronic EAP distribution, including tracking, encryption, and controlled delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled, secure transmission lowers the risk of loss or interception during review and activation.

mitigations.description: Periodically review and recertify user access for NRCS staff, contractors, and emergency responders to ensure only current site-assigned personnel retain access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access recertification helps ensure the need-to-know limitation is actually enforced over time.

mitigations.description: Apply a records schedule that minimizes retention of EAP PII once it is no longer needed for the dam owner or participant's eligibility and emergency planning purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
mitigations.rationale: Shortening retention when the purpose ends reduces the period of exposure for personal information.

mitigations.description: Collect only the specific personal data elements required to execute an EAP and document why each element is necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces privacy impact when information is sourced from public or voluntary submissions.

mitigations.description: Treat nonpublic telephone numbers as more sensitive than publicly available information and restrict their use and disclosure to emergency execution only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All DamWatch EAP PII is publicly available, with the possible exception of telephone numbers that may not be publicly listed.
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards for nonpublic phone numbers reduce the risk of exposing information that was not already public.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and business identifiers, so a breach or misuse could expose SSNs, tax IDs, bank account details, and ownership information.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increases harm if unauthorized access occurs.

risks.description: Bulk scanning and metadata extraction create a risk of collecting or indexing more information than necessary from paper records.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk ingestion can capture extraneous or unnecessary personal information if controls are weak.

risks.description: The system is a cloud application hosted on a shared AWS environment, which increases exposure from shared infrastructure and cloud misconfiguration.
risks.evidence_quote: The Digital Record Management System (DRMS) is a cloud system that resides on FPAC_AWS_Shared_GSS (FPAC_AWS_GSS).
risks.rationale: Shared cloud hosting can expand the impact of access-control or configuration failures.

risks.description: Contractor access to the system creates insider-risk exposure because non-federal users can view records containing PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any additional user population with access increases the chance of unauthorized disclosure or misuse.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to their records in DRMS, which can make it harder for them to review or correct inaccurate information.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Limited direct access can delay corrections and reduce transparency for affected individuals.

risks.description: Records are retained for long periods, including potentially more than ten years, which increases the window of exposure and the amount of historical PII held.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the chance that records will be exposed, copied, or retained beyond operational need.

risks.description: The system relies on PDF documents and Adobe PDF plug-ins for viewing, which can expose records to client-side or document-rendering vulnerabilities if not managed carefully.
risks.evidence_quote: Only form data and JSON metadata will be produced. Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents
risks.rationale: Document viewers and plug-ins are a common attack surface for sensitive records systems.

risks.description: Scanning paper records into databases and using metadata stores creates a risk that source documents or metadata could be inaccurately indexed, leading to incorrect retrieval or disclosure of the wrong record.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases
risks.rationale: Digitization and indexing errors can cause privacy harm by associating records with the wrong person or file.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive fields and documents using least-privilege controls, strong authentication, and audit logging for all record access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties. DRMS has documented Access Control (AC) Procedures, in compliance with FISMA and USDA directives.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls reduce the chance that sensitive identifiers are viewed or copied without authorization.

mitigations.description: Validate scanned records and extracted metadata before ingestion, and minimize any fields that are not required for records management.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-ingestion review and minimization help prevent unnecessary personal data from being captured or indexed.

mitigations.description: Apply cloud hardening, configuration management, and periodic security assessments to the shared AWS environment hosting DRMS.
mitigations.rationale: Shared cloud systems need continuous configuration and security monitoring to reduce exposure from infrastructure mistakes.

mitigations.description: Require background investigations, need-to-know approval, and periodic access reviews for contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Contractor screening and access review reduce insider-risk exposure.

mitigations.description: Provide a documented request-and-correction process that lets individuals obtain their records and submit corrections without needing direct system access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: As published in NRCS-1 SORN: “Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A formal access and amendment path helps individuals correct inaccurate information despite not having direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules consistently and delete or transfer records as soon as the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per NARA Code of Federal Regulations - 36 CFR 1220, Subchapter B – Records Management and USDA OCIO Department Regulation 3080-001 accessible at: http://www.ocio.usda.gov/document/departmental-regulation-3080-001 NARA Approval: NARA approval is required for all official records schedules.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition limits how long sensitive records remain exposed in the system.

mitigations.description: Harden and patch PDF viewing components and restrict plug-in use to approved, updated versions.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing viewer vulnerabilities lowers the chance that documents can be exploited through the client application.

mitigations.description: Perform quality checks on scanned documents and metadata, including sampling and reconciliation against source records before records are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Verification steps reduce the chance that inaccurate scans or metadata cause privacy-impacting retrieval errors.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers in documents, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or harm if those documents are exposed. The repository may include SSNs, tax IDs, bank routing numbers, and deposit account numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increase the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Users can upload documents directly into DMS, which creates a risk that inappropriate or excessive personal data may be added without sufficient review. The system stores documents rather than structured fields, so sensitive content may be embedded in PDFs unexpectedly.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Direct document upload can introduce uncontrolled personal data into the repository.

risks.description: Sharing with contractors and technical service providers creates a risk of broader disclosure of PII outside USDA if access is not tightly limited to the authorized purpose. The system explicitly allows external disclosure when written authorization is received.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant.
risks.rationale: External access expands the number of parties who may view sensitive records.

risks.description: Conservation district employees and contractors with access may expose records beyond what is necessary if role-based limits are not enforced precisely. The system says access is restricted, but still permits multiple non-owners to handle the documents.
risks.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
risks.rationale: Any system with multiple authorized user groups needs strict least-privilege controls to prevent unnecessary viewing.

risks.description: Using PII from FSA SCIMS to identify the correct producer creates a risk of mismatched or unnecessary access to another person's record if the matching process is wrong. The system relies on name and address data for this determination.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Identity matching based on limited PII can result in misassociation or overexposure of records.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DMS, which creates a risk that they may be unable to promptly see or correct inaccurate records affecting them. The process depends on requests routed through staff or a district conservationist.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Limited direct access can make correction and transparency slower and more burdensome for affected individuals.

risks.description: Long retention periods increase the amount of time sensitive records remain available for misuse or breach. Records may be kept for many years or for as long as a participant qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017. Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
risks.rationale: The longer records are retained, the longer they remain exposed to privacy risks.

risks.description: The system is built around PDF documents and Adobe PDF plug-ins, which can increase the risk of hidden metadata, embedded content, or document-viewing vulnerabilities exposing PII. The use of a document viewer means the security of the files and viewer matters directly to privacy.
risks.evidence_quote: Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents.
risks.rationale: Document-based systems can leak information through file content or viewer weaknesses if not managed carefully.

mitigations.description: Encrypt the stored documents and apply strict access controls and auditing to all records containing sensitive identifiers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
mitigations.rationale: The input already states the documents are encrypted, and stronger access control and audit logging directly reduce exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Require review or validation of uploaded documents before they are accepted into the repository, so unnecessary personal data can be removed or rejected.
mitigations.rationale: A review step would reduce the chance that users upload documents containing avoidable sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Limit external disclosure to only the specific records and purposes covered by the written authorization, and log each disclosure to contractors or technical service providers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure shall be made subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited sharing and disclosure logging reduce the risk of overbroad external access.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege, role-based access reviews for NRCS employees, conservation district employees, and contractors so users can only see the records needed for their assigned duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
mitigations.rationale: The stated access restriction should be operationalized through regular role review to prevent unnecessary access.

mitigations.description: Use a more reliable identity-matching workflow and verify matches before associating SCIMS data with a producer record in DMS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
mitigations.rationale: Verification reduces the chance that one person's data is matched to another person's record.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear, timely correction and access request process for individuals so they can obtain or correct their records without unnecessary delay.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A clearer and faster request process would improve accuracy and individual access to their own information.

mitigations.description: Apply and periodically review retention schedules so records are deleted or archived as soon as they are no longer needed for the participant's program eligibility or legal obligations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention where permissible reduces the duration of privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Harden the PDF viewing environment and strip unnecessary document metadata before storage or viewing.
mitigations.rationale: Viewer hardening and metadata removal reduce the chance that document-based PII is exposed through the file format or plug-in.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive borrower financial and loan information that could harm individuals if exposed. The data includes loan status, financials, and security property, along with direct identifiers like name and tax ID.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: Financial and identity data together create a meaningful privacy impact if improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: The system retains borrower PII permanently, increasing the long-term exposure window for records. Indefinite retention raises the chance that outdated information remains available longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the duration over which misuse, breach, or secondary use could affect the subject.

risks.description: The system relies on manual data entry by field agents, which creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete borrower records. Errors in manually entered financial or identity data could affect debt restructuring decisions and borrower privacy.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual collection is more error-prone than automated validation and can propagate incorrect personal data.

risks.description: The system uses borrower data to make restructuring determinations, so inaccurate or excessive data collection could lead to unfair or incorrect servicing outcomes. Because the system performs complex calculations on borrower cash flow and loan status, any bad input can affect the result.
risks.evidence_quote: eDALR$ completes a series of complex mathematical calculations based on information regarding the borrower's cash flow and loan status.
risks.rationale: Decision support systems depend on data quality, and privacy harms can result when incorrect records drive consequential decisions.

risks.description: The system is an intranet web-based application that accesses other internal web applications and databases, which broadens the number of places borrower data may be exposed. Each connected system increases the chance of unauthorized access or overcollection if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Interconnected systems expand the attack surface and the number of users or processes that may encounter the data.

risks.description: The system description does not state any internal or external sharing, but it also does not describe specific transmission safeguards for the intranet application. Without explicit safeguards, borrower PII may be vulnerable during access or processing.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information transmitted or disclosed? N/A
risks.rationale: A lack of documented transmission controls makes it harder to verify that access and handling are adequately protected.

mitigations.description: Limit access to borrower loan, financial, and security-property data to authorized field office employees with a need to know, and enforce strong authentication and role-based access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To support field office employees in determining the most optimal servicing solutions applicable and available concerning the restructuring of customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive borrower data will be seen or used by unauthorized personnel.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review schedule to purge or archive records when no longer needed for operational or legal purposes, even if the retention schedule allows permanent records.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review reduces unnecessary exposure of stale personal information while preserving records that must be kept.

mitigations.description: Add validation and quality checks for manually entered borrower data, including review of key identifiers and financial fields before the record is used.
mitigations.rationale: Input validation helps prevent incorrect personal data from being stored and used in servicing decisions.

mitigations.description: Require a human review step for restructuring outputs before they are relied upon for borrower servicing decisions.
mitigations.rationale: A review step can catch bad inputs or anomalous calculations before they affect the borrower.

mitigations.description: Document and test access controls for all connected internal systems, and limit data exchange to only the fields needed for the restructuring task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing exchanged data and hardening connected systems lowers the risk created by multiple internal interfaces.

mitigations.description: Document encryption and secure transmission controls for the intranet application and any system-to-system access paths.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit transmission protections reduce the chance that borrower information is intercepted or exposed in transit.

risks.description: The system stores borrower data indefinitely, which increases the risk of unnecessary long-term exposure or misuse of sensitive personal and financial information.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which the data could be accessed, disclosed, or repurposed.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive identifiers and financial records, including tax ID numbers and credit reports, creating a risk of harm if the data is exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: These data elements are highly sensitive and could be used for identity theft or financial fraud.

risks.description: Sharing name and Tax ID with Microbilt for creditworthiness checks creates a disclosure risk to an external organization.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: External sharing increases the number of parties that can access personal data and the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Using Microbilt and commercial or publicly available data to determine credit worthiness may create a risk of inaccurate or incomplete decisions affecting borrowers.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Credit decisions based on external data can be affected if the underlying information is wrong or incomplete.

risks.description: County office staff enter borrower data, which creates a risk of unauthorized access, transcription errors, or inconsistent handling during collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
