risks.rationale: Manual entry by staff introduces human error and insider-handling risks.

risks.description: The system maintains detailed financial and business plan information about agricultural customers, which could reveal sensitive business conditions and operating plans if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: A completed FBP provides the business’s financial condition, operating plans, and actual summary for a specified time
risks.rationale: Business financial and operating information can be sensitive and reveal more than basic identity data.

risks.description: The system’s interaction with multiple loan-related systems expands the number of systems receiving business data, increasing the risk of broader exposure or secondary use beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: interaction with the Direct Loan Making, Direct Loan Servicing, FLPRA and eDALR$ systems to ensure that loan requests have approved Farm Business Plans and to provide those systems with business data.
risks.rationale: Each additional system connection creates another point where information could be accessed or retained.

mitigations.description: Apply a documented retention schedule and delete records when they are no longer needed for the approved records schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database. 5 years on average for some systems as per the procedures in FSA 25-AS Handbook.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the time sensitive records remain exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive borrower fields such as Tax ID numbers and credit reports to staff with a need to know and protect them with strong access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Access limitation is a direct control for highly sensitive personal and financial data.

mitigations.description: Use a written data-sharing agreement with Microbilt that limits use of the name and Tax ID to the stated creditworthiness purpose and requires appropriate safeguarding.
mitigations.rationale: A purpose-limited agreement reduces the risk of unnecessary external use or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement a process to review and correct disputed or outdated credit and financial data before it is used in loan decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Data quality checks help prevent unfair or inaccurate creditworthiness determinations.

mitigations.description: Provide staff training and validation checks for county office data entry to reduce errors and unauthorized handling.
mitigations.rationale: Training and validation reduce manual-entry mistakes and handling errors.

mitigations.description: Limit access to completed Farm Business Plans and related financial summaries to personnel involved in loan eligibility, making, and servicing.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access lowers the chance of improper disclosure of sensitive business information.

mitigations.description: Document and review data exchanges with the other loan systems so only the minimum business data necessary is shared.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing inter-system sharing reduces exposure across connected systems.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive borrower identifiers and account data, creating a risk of unauthorized access or misuse of personally identifiable information. Because access is based on online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number, exposure could directly affect borrowers.
risks.evidence_quote: ADPS uses the customer’s name, address, Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Names, addresses, and SSNs are sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure could cause identity theft or financial harm.

risks.description: The system shares borrower information, including loan account information, with many external entities, increasing the risk of over-disclosure or secondary use beyond the original purpose. The breadth of recipients raises the chance that data could be exposed outside the agency boundary.
risks.evidence_quote: Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
risks.rationale: More recipients means more points where privacy controls must hold to prevent unnecessary disclosure.

risks.description: Using name or Social Security Number for online queries and batch processing creates a risk that users can retrieve or process records with insufficient need-to-know controls. If access is not tightly restricted, the system could enable broad viewing of borrower status and detailed transaction history.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Direct lookup by SSN is powerful and should be limited to authorized users with a legitimate business need.

risks.description: The system maintains detailed borrower status information and transaction history, which creates a risk of excessive internal visibility into borrowers' financial affairs. Even if used for accounting, the level of detail could reveal more than necessary to staff or contractors who access it.
risks.evidence_quote: The application is also used to view borrower status information and detailed history of transactions processed to a borrower’s account.
risks.rationale: Detailed financial histories are highly revealing and should be minimized to the least necessary audience.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of borrower records increases the risk that personal data will remain available longer than necessary and be exposed in future incidents. Permanent retention also increases the amount of historical information available for secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: The longer data is kept, the greater the cumulative exposure to breach, misuse, or inappropriate access.

risks.description: Reporting delinquent borrower information to Treasury, IRS, and credit bureaus can negatively affect borrowers if inaccurate or outdated data is shared. Because the system supports offsets and credit reporting, errors could have direct financial consequences.
risks.evidence_quote: Treasury Reporting - The DCIA processes evaluate accounts for amount and date of delinquency and reported to Treasury for offset.
risks.rationale: Incorrect delinquency data can trigger harmful collection or credit actions against the wrong person or at the wrong time.

risks.description: The system's reporting to credit bureaus and HUD creates a risk of sensitive financial information being disseminated to organizations that may not need the full underlying record. This can broaden the impact of any disclosure and make borrower behavior more visible than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
risks.rationale: Credit reporting inherently expands dissemination of personal financial data beyond the originating agency.

risks.description: The mention of future public-facing Customer Self Service introduces a risk that borrower information could be exposed through an externally accessible interface if not securely designed. Public-facing functionality typically increases the attack surface for privacy incidents.
risks.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
risks.rationale: Public-facing systems require stronger controls because they are accessible outside the agency network.

mitigations.description: Limit access to borrower PII to only authorized roles that require it, and enforce strong authentication and audit logging for every lookup or batch action.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls reduce the chance that sensitive identifiers and account data are viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Apply data-sharing agreements and data minimization rules so each external recipient receives only the specific borrower information needed for its stated process.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is shared reduces the privacy impact of multi-party disclosures.

mitigations.description: Restrict SSN-based search and batch processing to approved users, and require role-based justification or dual approval for sensitive record retrieval.
mitigations.rationale: Extra controls around SSN-based access reduce the risk of unauthorized record lookup.

mitigations.description: Provide users with only the minimum borrower status and transaction history needed for their job function, and mask or suppress unnecessary fields in routine views and reports.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing displayed detail lowers the chance of unnecessary internal exposure of financial history.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether permanent retention is still required for each record type and, where legally permitted, archive or dispose of data according to an approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Even with approved schedules, periodic review helps ensure records are not kept longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Implement data quality checks and correction workflows before delinquency, offset, or credit-reporting data is sent externally.
mitigations.rationale: Validating data before disclosure reduces the risk of harmful reporting errors.

mitigations.description: Limit credit-reporting disclosures to the minimum fields required by the receiving bureau and document the exact data elements shared for each reporting purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Sharing fewer fields reduces the privacy impact of external credit reporting.

mitigations.description: Perform a privacy and security review before launching any public-facing Customer Self Service capability, including testing for authentication, authorization, and exposure of borrower data.
mitigations.rationale: A pre-launch review helps prevent avoidable disclosure in externally accessible services.

risks.description: The system retains PII indefinitely, which increases the chance that personal data will be exposed, misused, or become stale over time. Long-term retention also expands the impact of any future security incident or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps PII available far longer than needed for operational use, increasing exposure over time.

risks.description: PII is entered manually by County, State, Regional, and National FLP staff, which creates a risk of incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent records. Manual entry can also lead to accidental disclosure or overcollection if users enter more information than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Human data entry is prone to error and can introduce privacy harms through inaccurate or excessive records.

risks.description: The system stores names, mailing addresses, and phone numbers, which are direct identifiers that can be used to contact or locate individuals if exposed. Because the system supports loan appraisals, this information may be linked to sensitive financial or property-related records.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
risks.rationale: Direct contact information is sensitive enough that unauthorized disclosure could enable unwanted contact or targeting.

risks.description: The system centralizes appraisal information for County, State, Regional, and National staff, creating a broader internal access footprint than a local or siloed system. Broader access increases the risk of unauthorized viewing or use by personnel who do not need the information for their duties.
risks.evidence_quote: provide County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals
risks.rationale: The more users and organizational levels that can access PII, the greater the chance of unnecessary internal exposure.

risks.description: The system maintains case file storage, document management, and action alerts, which can concentrate personal information in a single application and make it more attractive if compromised. Centralized storage also increases the consequences of any access-control failure.
risks.evidence_quote: document management (approval tracking, action alerts, case file storage, etc.)
risks.rationale: Centralized repositories can amplify the impact of a breach because more data is exposed at once.

mitigations.description: Apply a records disposition schedule that deletes or archives PII when it is no longer needed for the appraisal and loan program purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of time personal data remains exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Require validation checks and supervisory review for manually entered records before they are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Review and validation reduce the chance that staff-entered data is inaccurate or incomplete.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection to only the contact fields required for appraisal processing and prohibit unnecessary notes or extra identifiers.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less personal information lowers the harm if records are accessed without authorization.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls so County, State, Regional, and National users can only view the records needed for their specific duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: provide County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access by role reduces unnecessary internal exposure of PII.

mitigations.description: Protect the centralized case files and document management functions with strong authentication, logging, and periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: document management (approval tracking, action alerts, case file storage, etc.)
mitigations.rationale: Stronger access controls and monitoring help detect and prevent unauthorized access to concentrated records.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive personal and financial data, including SSNs/TINs, race, ethnicity, gender, credit card numbers, credit reports, and employment history, creating a risk of harm if that information is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the data elements, the greater the privacy impact if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system relies on information from many external and internal sources, which increases the chance of inaccurate or outdated data being used in loan decisions and servicing.
risks.evidence_quote: Other FSA Applications: Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS), Farm Business Plan (FBP), Electronic Loan Deficiency Payments, Master Reference Tables (MRT), Appraisal System COTS (Appraisal), Program Loan Accounting System (PLAS) and Automated Discrepancy Processing System (ADPS).
risks.rationale: Using data from multiple sources raises the risk that records will not match or be current when decisions are made.

risks.description: Borrower data is manually entered by field staff and county office staff, which creates a risk of input errors or unauthorized viewing during handling.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual handling increases the likelihood of mistakes and unnecessary exposure compared with automated, validated collection.

risks.description: The system uses personal and financial information to determine credit worthiness and loan eligibility, which can lead to significant privacy impact if the analysis is unfair, incorrect, or not well explained to the borrower.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Credit and eligibility decisions based on detailed personal data can materially affect individuals if the underlying analysis is wrong or opaque.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely, which increases long-term exposure of personal information and the chance that outdated records will remain accessible.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention extends the period during which sensitive records could be breached or misused.

risks.description: The system includes race, ethnicity, and gender data in loan processing, which creates a risk of sensitive demographic information being used or disclosed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number.
risks.rationale: Demographic attributes are sensitive personal data and warrant extra safeguards to prevent inappropriate use or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive fields such as SSNs, TINs, credit reports, and demographic data to only staff with a documented need to know, and log all access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that highly sensitive data will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Implement validation and reconciliation checks across source systems and external records before the data is used in loan processing.
mitigations.rationale: Cross-checking source data helps prevent decisions based on inaccurate or inconsistent records.

mitigations.description: Require dual review or supervisory verification of manually entered borrower data before it is used in servicing or eligibility decisions.
mitigations.rationale: A second review can catch entry errors and reduce the privacy impact of incorrect records.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notices and an administrative review path for borrowers affected by credit-worthiness or eligibility determinations based on FLD CAS data.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and review rights help limit harm from decisions that rely on personal financial information.

mitigations.description: Periodically review permanent records to confirm they remain necessary and apply archival controls that limit routine access to older records.
mitigations.rationale: Even when records must be retained permanently, limiting routine access reduces long-term privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Separate demographic fields from operational loan data where possible and limit their use to authorized program purposes only.
mitigations.rationale: Segregating sensitive demographic data reduces the chance of inappropriate use in loan processing.

risks.description: The system retains PII indefinitely, which increases the chance of long-term privacy harm if the records are later misused, breached, or kept longer than needed for the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention expands the window in which the name and mailing address data can be exposed or used beyond current operational need.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains identifiable information about individuals involved in loan oversight, trainee monitoring, and directives workflows, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure of names and mailing addresses across multiple applications.
risks.evidence_quote: DDORS Name FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
risks.rationale: The same identifying data elements are stored in multiple web-based applications, increasing the number of places where they must be protected.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which could expose predecisional or sensitive policy information if improperly disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Information that is not yet approved may be more sensitive to premature disclosure than finalized materials.

risks.description: The system relies on manual entry by County Offices, State Offices, and State personnel, which creates a risk of inaccurate or outdated personal data being entered and then used for oversight or workflow decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
risks.rationale: Manually entered data is more likely to contain errors than automated collection, and errors can affect individuals' records.

risks.description: Because the applications are web-based and used for oversight and tracking, unauthorized access could reveal identifiable information about District Directors, trainees, and state personnel if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
risks.rationale: Web-based systems that maintain identifiable records need strong access controls to prevent inappropriate viewing or use.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review and disposal schedule to remove or archive records when they are no longer needed for operational, legal, or archival purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: A formal review process reduces the amount of PII kept over time while preserving records that truly require retention.

mitigations.description: Limit access to each application's PII to only the users who need it for their assigned duties and log access to the records.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing access reduces the chance that names and mailing addresses are viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Withhold or redact pre-OMB directives and policies until they are approved for release, and restrict access to staff with a legitimate need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling draft material lowers the risk of premature disclosure of nonfinal policy information.

mitigations.description: Use validation and supervisory review for manually entered records before they are relied on in oversight or training workflows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing manual entries helps catch errors before they affect individuals' records or program actions.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong authentication and role-based access controls for the web applications, and periodically review user permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access controls are a direct safeguard for web-based systems that store identifiable information.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and business identifiers that could expose individuals to identity theft or misuse if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is defined as information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual. Mark all applicable PII and data elements in the table. Please check any information listed below that your system collects, uses, disseminates, creates, or maintains: Identifying Numbers ☒ Social Security number ... ☒ Employee Identification Number ☒ Taxpayer Identification Number ☒ Business Taxpayer Identification Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Personal Mobile Number ☒ Business Mobile Number (sole proprietor)
risks.rationale: These identifiers are directly sensitive and can be used to identify or contact people and businesses.

risks.description: The system maintains a very large population-scale dataset, increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities, who voluntarily provided their customer data on an OMB approved form prior to, or during a program application process.
risks.rationale: A breach would affect a large number of current and former program participants.

risks.description: The system contains long-term historical records, which increases the amount of personal information exposed over time and the consequences of a compromise.
risks.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data which is shared with other applications and agencies across USDA
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the volume and age range of data that could be exposed.

risks.description: Sharing farm and business partner data across multiple USDA agencies creates a risk of broader disclosure than necessary for the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the number of systems and staff that can access the data.

risks.description: Geospatial farm, tract, and field boundary data can reveal sensitive location information about producers' operations and holdings.
risks.evidence_quote: National agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
risks.rationale: Location-linked agricultural boundaries can expose operational details about a participant's property and activity.

risks.description: The system centralizes employee access and roles, so incorrect role assignments could expose records to users who do not need them.
risks.evidence_quote: Organizational Structure – this application centralizes CRM employee access and roles to associated counties and positions from source systems.
risks.rationale: Access control mistakes in a centralized role system can lead to unnecessary internal access.

risks.description: County Office access to update customer and farm information may expose records to more locations and personnel than a single point of service model.
risks.evidence_quote: ease producer burden by allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
risks.rationale: Broader operational access can increase the chance of unauthorized viewing or handling.

risks.description: The system relies on data provided on forms during application processes, so inaccurate or outdated records could affect program decisions and create privacy harm to affected individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: who voluntarily provided their customer data on an OMB approved form prior to, or during a program application process.
risks.rationale: If participant-submitted data are incomplete or stale, the system may maintain incorrect personal records.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive identifiers with least-privilege controls and strong authentication, and monitor access to detect misuse.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can view or change identifiers reduces the chance of improper disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply stronger breach-prevention controls, including continuous monitoring and incident response planning, to protect the large record set.
mitigations.rationale: A dataset of this size warrants heightened safeguards because the impact of compromise is much larger.

mitigations.description: Enforce data minimization and archive protection for older records, and limit access to historical data to users with a documented need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
mitigations.rationale: Older records should be more tightly controlled because they remain retained for a long period.

mitigations.description: Use formal sharing agreements and role-based restrictions so each USDA agency receives only the data needed for program delivery.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared fields and recipients reduces unnecessary dissemination.

mitigations.description: Treat geospatial boundary data as sensitive and limit its disclosure and internal access to personnel who need it for program administration.
mitigations.evidence_quote: National agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
mitigations.rationale: Location-based farm boundaries can reveal operational details that should not be broadly exposed.

mitigations.description: Review and periodically recertify employee roles and permissions in the centralized organizational structure to prevent excessive access.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps catch role assignment errors before they expose records.

mitigations.description: Limit County Office access to the minimum necessary records and log all updates made from any County Office location.
mitigations.evidence_quote: allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining and auditing distributed access reduces the risk of inappropriate viewing or changes.

mitigations.description: Implement a data quality process for participant-submitted records so individuals can correct inaccurate or outdated information.
mitigations.rationale: A correction process helps ensure records remain accurate when they are used for program delivery.

risks.description: The system retains producer information indefinitely, which creates a long-term exposure risk if the data is later misused, breached, or requested for purposes beyond the original program need.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the amount of time sensitive producer data remains available for unauthorized access or secondary use.

risks.description: The system includes contractor access to producer data, which increases the number of people who can view sensitive information and raises insider misuse risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases the chance of improper viewing, handling, or disclosure of producer data.

risks.description: Some components disclose information to external systems, which creates a privacy risk from broader data sharing and possible downstream misuse or overexposure.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: Sharing data with other systems increases the number of environments where the information may be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: The system generates producer name and street address for printed forms and mailed letters, creating a risk of disclosure through physical mail handling or misdelivery.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
risks.rationale: Printed or mailed documents can be intercepted, misdelivered, or seen by unintended recipients.

risks.description: County office staff can access and enter producer information directly in several applications, which creates a risk of unauthorized internal access or errors by personnel with broad operational access.
risks.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
risks.rationale: Manual handling by office staff increases the chance of improper access, mistaken entry, or unnecessary viewing of producer information.

risks.description: The system stores and uses identity-linked payment history, overpayment, and eligibility data, which can reveal detailed financial and program participation information about producers.
risks.evidence_quote: Retain producer payment history information
risks.rationale: Payment and eligibility records can expose sensitive financial and operational details about individual producers.

mitigations.description: Establish and periodically review a records disposition schedule so information is not kept longer than required for the program and legal obligations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: A formal retention review reduces unnecessary long-term exposure of producer data.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary roles and continue enforcing background checks, eAuthentication, and NDAs for those with access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and vetting contractor access lowers insider privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Apply strict data-sharing controls and data minimization before any transfer to external systems, with logging and review of disclosures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and monitoring shared data reduces the privacy impact of system-to-system disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use address suppression or masking where possible and require secure mailing procedures for any printed producer notices.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
mitigations.rationale: Protecting address data in printed workflows reduces the chance of physical disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide role-based access controls and periodic access reviews for county office users who enter or view producer data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access controls reduce the risk of unnecessary internal exposure and handling errors.

mitigations.description: Limit retention and access to payment-history and overpayment records to only those staff who need them for program administration and audits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Retain producer payment history information
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to detailed financial records reduces the chance of inappropriate disclosure.

risks.description: The system maintains highly sensitive personal and financial records about producers, including names, addresses, SSN/EIN, farm tract numbers, and payment amounts, which creates a risk of identity theft or financial harm if improperly accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: These data elements are directly identifying and financially sensitive, so unauthorized disclosure would have significant privacy impact.

risks.description: ARCPLC displays producer PII retrieved from SCIMS within the application, so users may see more personal information than is necessary for the task if access controls or role restrictions are too broad.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
risks.rationale: Displaying PII inside the application increases exposure to users who can reach the screen or workflow.

risks.description: SWIMS uses a shared database accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees, which creates a risk of internal overexposure or misuse of producer information by a broad user group.
risks.evidence_quote: SWIMS is a centralized database that has been created for users to import and export the SURE Workbook .xml files using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: A shared database used across multiple office levels can widen access beyond the minimum needed.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely as permanent records, which increases the long-term risk of unauthorized access, secondary use, or harm from a future breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: The longer PII is kept, the longer it remains exposed to security and misuse risks.

risks.description: ARCPLC uses producer information to determine eligibility and identify the person signing up for ARC-PLC, which creates a risk that PII could be used for purposes beyond the original collection if governance is weak.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine eligibility.
risks.rationale: Eligibility and sign-up processing can invite secondary use unless use limitations are enforced.

risks.description: SWIMS supports import and export of workbook XML files, which creates a risk of accidental disclosure or unauthorized copying when files are moved in and out of the shared database.
risks.evidence_quote: users to import and export the SURE Workbook .xml files using a shared database
risks.rationale: Import/export functions can increase the chance that sensitive data is duplicated or mishandled.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to SSN/EIN, payment amounts, and other sensitive fields to only users with a documented need to know, and mask or redact those values wherever full display is not required.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of the most sensitive fields reduces the impact of unauthorized viewing or misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and field-level display rules so ARCPLC shows only the minimum producer information needed for the specific workflow.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is displayed lowers the chance that users see unnecessary PII.

mitigations.description: Limit SWIMS access by role, office, and transaction type, and periodically review user permissions for the National, State, and County Office FSA employees who can use the shared database.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access reviews help ensure the shared database remains limited to authorized users only.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review and disposal process to confirm that only records required to be permanent are retained indefinitely and that all others are deleted on schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Even with permanent records, a retention review reduces unnecessary accumulation of PII.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce purpose limitations so producer information collected for eligibility and sign-up is not reused for unrelated purposes without authorization.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the risk of secondary use beyond the stated program function.

mitigations.description: Validate and scan imported XML files before they enter SWIMS, and restrict export capabilities to authorized users with logging of file transfers.
mitigations.rationale: Controls on file import/export reduce the chance of accidental or unauthorized disclosure during data movement.

risks.description: County Office users can search for a specific farmer or producer using sensitive personal identifiers, which creates a risk of unauthorized lookup or overbroad access to farmer records.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII allows County Office users to search for a specific user as well as a second authentication method to validate farmers and producers.
risks.rationale: Search functionality increases the chance that users can view records beyond what they need for their duties.

risks.description: The system uses SSN as a second authentication method, which creates a risk of exposing a highly sensitive identifier during validation.
risks.evidence_quote: If a farmer or producer has an eAuth account, the SSN can be used as a second authentication method to validate the farmer / producer
risks.rationale: Using SSN for authentication increases the harm if the identifier is mishandled or observed by unauthorized persons.

risks.description: The application pulls PII from SCIMS, so any weakness in the source-to-use retrieval path could expose farmers' personal data within FSCOMS.
risks.evidence_quote: the other application (FSAfarm+) does contain PII. This PIA is required since FSAfarm+ uses personal information of farmers and producers.
risks.rationale: Moving personal data into another application creates a point where access controls and handling must be correct.

risks.description: Contractor access to the system creates a risk that non-government personnel could access farmer and producer PII while supporting FSCOMS/FSAfarm+.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the number of people who may encounter the data.

risks.description: Although FSCOMS says it does not retain PII, temporary memory and cache could still expose data if logout clearing fails or is bypassed.
risks.evidence_quote: When a user logs out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: Transient storage still creates exposure if clearing does not occur as intended.

mitigations.description: Limit search access to authorized County Office users and enforce role-based access controls for lookup functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII allows County Office users to search for a specific user
mitigations.rationale: Restricting lookup access reduces the chance of unauthorized or unnecessary searches.

mitigations.description: Replace SSN-based validation with a less sensitive second-factor identifier or token where possible.
mitigations.rationale: A less sensitive authenticator would reduce exposure of SSNs during validation.

mitigations.description: Apply strict access controls and audit logging to all PII retrieved from SCIMS and used in FSAfarm+.
mitigations.rationale: Controls and logs help ensure only authorized retrieval and use of transferred PII.

mitigations.description: Vet and train contractors on privacy requirements and limit their access to the minimum necessary for support.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and training contractor access reduces the likelihood of inappropriate viewing or handling of PII.

mitigations.description: Verify that logout clearing of memory and cache is tested and monitored so no residual PII remains after a session ends.
mitigations.rationale: Testing and monitoring help ensure temporary data is actually removed as stated.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains personally identifiable information about producers, including name, mailing address, ethnicity, and race, which creates a risk of privacy harm if that data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: These data elements are sensitive enough that unauthorized access or improper use could affect individuals' privacy.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to determine who is eligible to vote in committee elections, which could lead to improper inclusion or exclusion if the eligibility logic or source data is inaccurate.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
risks.rationale: Eligibility decisions based on coded data can be wrong if the underlying records are incomplete or outdated.

risks.description: County office staff collect data directly from producers and enter it into the system, creating a risk of transcription errors or unauthorized access at the point of collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry increases the chance that information is recorded incorrectly or viewed by unauthorized personnel.

risks.description: The system creates and sends county-specific lists of all eligible producers for ballot printing, which concentrates sensitive voter-related information in a form that could be misdirected or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
risks.rationale: Producing and distributing lists of eligible voters increases the risk of unintended disclosure if the lists are mishandled.

risks.description: The system collects and reports election data from returned ballot forms, which can reveal participation and voting-related information about individual producers.
risks.evidence_quote: Collect and report election data from returned ballot forms (the County Election and Media Outreach Report).
risks.rationale: Ballot-related records can expose sensitive participation information if not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system creates a COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms, which may expose governance and membership details beyond what is necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Create the COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms.
risks.rationale: A directory of members and terms can reveal structured personal and organizational information about elected individuals.

risks.description: The system tracks election results and COC member data, which can create a persistent record of individuals' election participation and status over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Track Election results and COC Member data.
risks.rationale: Longitudinal tracking increases the amount of personal history associated with each producer or member.

risks.description: Information is retained indefinitely as permanent records, which increases the duration of exposure if access controls fail or records are later no longer needed for active operations.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which records could be compromised or misused.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to producer records to authorized users only and apply encryption for data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting stored and transmitted data reduces the chance that sensitive personal information is exposed.

mitigations.description: Validate committee and LAA codes against authoritative source data before determining voter eligibility.
mitigations.rationale: Verification of eligibility inputs helps prevent incorrect inclusion or exclusion of producers.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access and data-entry validation for county office staff who collect and enter producer information.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling who can enter data and checking entries reduces manual error and unauthorized viewing.

mitigations.description: Limit distribution of county-specific eligible-producer lists to the minimum necessary recipients and apply secure handling procedures for ballot mailers.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing distribution and protecting mailing materials lowers the risk of unintended disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize the personal information retained in ballot and election reports and restrict access to election records.
mitigations.rationale: Keeping only necessary election details and limiting access reduces exposure of voting-related information.

mitigations.description: Limit the COC Directory to the minimum member and term information needed for official purposes and review it for unnecessary personal details.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal and organizational information that could be disclosed.

mitigations.description: Apply retention and access controls to election results and member tracking records so only authorized personnel can view historical records.
mitigations.rationale: Tight controls on historical records reduce the privacy impact of long-term tracking.

mitigations.description: Conduct periodic records reviews to confirm that permanently retained information is still required and that archival protections remain in place.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps ensure long-retained records remain appropriately protected over time.

risks.description: The warehouse stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, creating a risk of unauthorized access or exposure of PII at scale. Because the system centralizes many program datasets, a single breach could affect many individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: All Program and financial data for the Agency is stored in the EDW. This includes Farm Program, Farm Loan, Commodity Operations, Human Resources and Financial data. Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: Centralized storage of sensitive identifiers and financial data increases the impact of any access-control failure.

risks.description: The system consolidates data from multiple source systems, which increases the risk that data are used or combined beyond the original collection context. This can create broader profiling or secondary-use concerns for producers and other subjects.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV defines, collects, validates, and stores data from various computer sources for each application to provide business users a single source for data used to resolve business inquiries.
risks.rationale: Combining data into a single source makes it easier to infer more about a person than any one source would reveal.

risks.description: PII is collected from county offices and other federal agencies and then extracted into the EDW, creating a risk of inaccurate or outdated data being propagated across systems. Errors in source data could affect reporting and decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: Most PII data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff. In some cases information is collected via other federal agencies which provide this information to the FSA. This data resides in multiple source systems and is extracted from the source systems into the EDW.
risks.rationale: When data are copied from multiple sources, any source error can be replicated widely.

risks.description: The system uses batch processes to share information, which can increase the risk of unintended disclosure if transfer controls, file handling, or recipient restrictions are weak. Batch sharing also makes it harder to limit exposure to only the minimum necessary records.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems shares the information through batch processes.
risks.rationale: Bulk transfers are more likely than interactive transactions to expose large sets of records if a process fails or is misconfigured.

risks.description: Information is shared internally with multiple organizations, increasing the number of users and systems that can access sensitive records. Broader internal sharing raises the risk of unauthorized access or over-collection.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the attack surface and the chance of inappropriate access.

risks.description: Information is shared externally with IRS, Treasury, a university, and Dunn and Bradstreet, which creates disclosure risk outside the agency. Even limited external sharing can expose personal data to third parties with different controls and retention practices.
risks.evidence_quote: However, FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: External disclosure reduces direct agency control over how the data are handled after transfer.

risks.description: The system uses name and address validation with Dunn and Bradstreet, which may expose personal identifying information for matching or validation purposes beyond the original collection purpose. This creates a risk of unnecessary disclosure of identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Using identifiers for validation can reveal personal information even when the underlying business purpose is limited.

risks.description: The retention strategy follows the NARA schedule, but deviations are allowed when the strategy is defined, creating a risk that records may be kept longer than necessary if exceptions are not tightly controlled. Longer retention increases exposure over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Any deviations from the NARA Retention Schedule will be approved by NARA when the archiving and retention strategy is defined..
risks.rationale: The longer sensitive records are retained, the longer they remain vulnerable to misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access controls and strong authentication for EDW DV, with role-based restrictions for sensitive fields such as SSN, account numbers, and employment history.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to sensitive fields reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply purpose-based access controls and data minimization so users can only view the specific data elements needed for reporting or inquiry resolution.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what users can access and combine reduces secondary-use and profiling risk.

mitigations.description: Implement data quality checks and reconciliation controls at ingest to detect and correct source errors before records are loaded into the EDW.
mitigations.rationale: Validation before loading helps prevent inaccurate source data from propagating across the warehouse.

mitigations.description: Use secure transfer controls for batch processes, including encryption in transit, file integrity checks, and restricted transfer accounts.
mitigations.rationale: Secure batch handling lowers the chance that large file transfers expose PII.

mitigations.description: Document and limit internal sharing to the minimum necessary organizations and datasets, and periodically review internal access and sharing agreements.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the number of internal recipients lowers the risk of unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Establish data-sharing agreements and disclosure controls for external recipients, including limits on use, re-disclosure, and retention.
mitigations.rationale: Formal controls help ensure third parties handle the data consistently with agency requirements.

mitigations.description: For validation exchanges, share only the minimum fields required and avoid sending full identifiers when a partial or tokenized match will work.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing validation data reduces unnecessary exposure of identity information.

mitigations.description: Require documented approval and periodic review for any retention deviation, and automate deletion or archival according to the approved schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Tight retention governance helps prevent records from being kept longer than needed.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive financial and identity data for a very large population, creating a broad exposure if access is misused or the system is compromised. The system supports payments for approximately 1.4 million customers annually and contains names, SSNs/TINs, bank account numbers, routing numbers, and debt information.
risks.evidence_quote: “Program and loan benefits are processed and disbursed through these systems to approximately 1.4 million FSA customers annually.”
risks.rationale: Large-scale retention of sensitive financial and identity data increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Public-facing components let producers update banking and assignment information and view detailed financial information online, which increases the risk of unauthorized account access or exposure of detailed financial records. The FI application provides producers access to summary and detailed financial information, and FSAFS is public facing.
risks.evidence_quote: “The Financial Services System resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is public facing, with producers and farmers able to update their own information (i.e. banking and assignment information).”
risks.rationale: Public-facing access to sensitive financial records and bank details requires strong authentication and session protections to prevent misuse.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates insider and mishandling risk even though they are subject to controls. The PIA says contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.evidence_quote: “Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.”
risks.rationale: Any nonemployee access expands the number of people who can view sensitive PII and financial data.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, so sensitive personal and financial records may remain exposed long after they are needed for operations. The retention applies to all listed applications and is permanent records.
risks.evidence_quote: “The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).”
risks.rationale: Long-term retention increases the duration of harm if records are breached or later used inappropriately.

risks.description: Debt and delinquency information is used to report creditworthiness and is shared with commercial credit bureaus, which can affect individuals' financial reputation. The system also sends delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
risks.evidence_quote: “the information is used to report delinquent debt for the purposes of creditworthiness. Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.”
risks.rationale: Credit-related disclosures can cause lasting harm if inaccurate, excessive, or accessed by unauthorized parties.

risks.description: The system generates letters and statements about payments and debt, which can reveal sensitive financial status to anyone who intercepts or receives the mail. NRRS and NRRS Notes generate letters to customers and producers concerning debt and collections.
risks.evidence_quote: “NRRS generates letters to customers associated with a receivable”
risks.rationale: Mail and statement outputs can disclose private debt and payment information outside the system boundary.

risks.description: The system collects and stores bank account and routing information for direct deposit and payment processing, creating risk if that information is improperly displayed, copied, or accessed. Several components explicitly include bank account number and routing number data.
risks.evidence_quote: “FI Name, SSN/TIN, financial institution account number, check number, and routing number.”
risks.rationale: Banking data is highly sensitive and can be used for financial fraud if exposed.

risks.description: The system processes SSNs/TINs and other identifiers across multiple applications, increasing the risk of identity exposure through cross-system transfers and storage. Several components list SSN/TIN as collected or maintained information.
risks.evidence_quote: “NRRS Name, TIN/SSN”
risks.rationale: Using the same identifiers across many linked applications increases the blast radius of any access control failure.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive financial and identity data to the minimum necessary roles and monitor privileged access for unusual activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: “All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management”
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and monitoring reduce the chance of inappropriate viewing or misuse of large-scale sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Require strong multi-factor authentication and hardened session controls for all public-facing producer access, especially for banking and assignment updates.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and session protections reduce the risk of unauthorized online access to detailed financial records.

mitigations.description: Apply enhanced contractor oversight, including periodic access reviews and least-privilege role assignment, for all contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: “Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access”
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review and least privilege help ensure contractor access remains narrowly scoped and justified.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review and deletion schedule for any data not required to remain permanent, and periodically verify that indefinite retention is still justified.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing retention needs limits unnecessary long-term exposure while preserving records that truly must be kept.

mitigations.description: Validate delinquent debt data before any external reporting and provide a correction process for individuals affected by credit-related disclosures.
mitigations.rationale: Data validation and correction rights reduce harm from inaccurate or outdated creditworthiness reporting.

mitigations.description: Use secure mailing and statement handling controls, such as address verification and suppression of unnecessary details, for debt and payment letters.
mitigations.evidence_quote: “RMO prints and mails the letters to the producers.”
mitigations.rationale: Secure handling of mailed notices reduces the chance that private debt information is exposed in transit or to the wrong recipient.

mitigations.description: Encrypt bank account and routing data at rest and mask it in user interfaces except where full display is operationally required.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and masking reduce the likelihood that exposed banking details can be misused.

mitigations.description: Minimize the use and display of SSNs/TINs across applications by substituting internal identifiers where possible and restricting full-identifier visibility.
mitigations.evidence_quote: “The CORE system almost never contains SSN.”
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN/TIN exposure lowers the risk of identity theft if one linked system is compromised.

risks.description: The system retains employee information permanently, which increases the long-term privacy impact if the data is later misused, breached, or no longer needed for the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention extends exposure of name and mailing address information beyond the active need for access control.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information about employees, including names and mailing addresses, which can expose staff to identification or contact-related privacy harm if accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS Name & mailing address
risks.rationale: Names and mailing addresses are direct identifiers that should be limited to the minimum necessary for the access-control function.

risks.description: The system maintains authorization data tied to users’ roles, groups, offices, and specially defined attributes, which could reveal internal organizational relationships or job-related details if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes to business applications
risks.rationale: Role and office data can disclose more about an employee than basic contact information alone.

risks.description: Administrators can manage security access rights in real time, so excessive administrative access or misconfiguration could expose or alter employee authorization data.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS allows administrators to use a web browser to manage security access rights, assigning and removing roles/groups/attributes to users on-line in real time.
risks.rationale: Real-time administrative control raises the privacy impact of privileged access mistakes or abuse.

mitigations.description: Apply records management minimization by periodically reviewing whether any retained authorization records can be archived, redacted, or disposed of sooner when no longer needed for the access-control purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention duration lowers the amount of time the data remains exposed to privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of employee PII to only the fields necessary for role-based access control, and restrict access to those fields to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Facilitate Role-Based Access Control system.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access to direct identifiers reduces unnecessary exposure of employee contact information.

mitigations.description: Implement strict role-based permissions and audit logging for authorization records so only approved users can view or change role, group, office, and attribute data.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls and logging help prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive organizational details.

mitigations.description: Require change review or approval workflows for administrative updates to roles, groups, and attributes, especially for high-impact access changes.
mitigations.rationale: A review step reduces the chance that real-time administrative changes will improperly expose employee information.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial records, so unauthorized access could expose identities, account details, and other confidential information. The data types include PII, financial data, health data, biometric data, criminal history, and employment history.
risks.evidence_quote: What personally identifiable information (PII) will become available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications. N/A
risks.rationale: A repository containing multiple sensitive data categories creates significant harm if access controls fail.

risks.description: Indefinite retention of records increases the amount of sensitive information exposed over time and raises the impact of any future breach or misuse. The system states that information is kept permanently.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which records can be accessed, disclosed, or misused.

risks.description: The system accepts data from faxed and scanned materials, which can include misdirected, incomplete, or poor-quality documents that may expose the wrong person's information. This creates a risk of collecting or indexing information that should not be in the record set.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from electronically stored documents, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Manual ingestion from multiple sources increases the chance of human error and accidental disclosure.

risks.description: Because the system controls workflows for financial information, users may be able to see more records than needed for their job, creating unnecessary internal exposure of sensitive information. Workflow access can broaden visibility beyond the original document submitter.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.rationale: Workflow systems often increase the number of people who can view or handle records.

risks.description: The system allows desktop browser access to stored images on a network device, which could expose records if authentication, session handling, or endpoint security is weak. Browser-based access increases the attack surface for unauthorized viewing.
risks.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.rationale: Remote browser access requires strong access controls to prevent unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The use of a SQL database to manage document indexes and workflow process creates a risk that metadata about documents and cases could be exposed even if the image files are protected. Index data can reveal sensitive associations and search terms.
risks.evidence_quote: The server utilizes a SQL database to manage document indexes and workflow process.
risks.rationale: Index and workflow metadata can be sensitive even when the underlying images are not directly viewed.

risks.description: The system imports Federal Reserve Bank images, so any weakness in the import or retrieval process could expose externally sourced records beyond the intended audience. Imported archival images may contain sensitive financial or identity information.
risks.evidence_quote: KCFRB Imaging (FRB) downloads and imports Federal Reserve Bank images into the system.
risks.rationale: Data imported from another organization needs strong controls to preserve confidentiality and integrity.

risks.description: Read-only historical archives still contain sensitive personal information, and broad retrieval access can enable unnecessary viewing of legacy records. Systems used to research historical archives may expose old records to users who do not need them.
risks.evidence_quote: The KCFRB system is used to research historical archives of treasury checks.
risks.rationale: Historical records remain sensitive even when no new content is added.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the system and its records to authorized users only, with role-based permissions for each subsystem and record type.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive PII and financial data will be viewed by unauthorized personnel.

mitigations.description: Apply a records management review to determine whether all permanently retained records truly require indefinite retention, and segregate or archive inactive records with stricter access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Even when retention is approved, tighter handling of inactive records reduces long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Add document intake validation and quality checks for faxed and scanned submissions to confirm the correct subject, completeness, and readability before indexing.
mitigations.rationale: Validation at intake helps prevent misfiled or erroneous documents from being stored and exposed.

mitigations.description: Limit workflow visibility to the minimum necessary set of users and steps, and review workflow permissions regularly.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know workflow permissions reduce unnecessary internal access to sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and secure session controls for browser-based access, including timeout and device hardening for users accessing stored images.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
mitigations.rationale: Browser access is safer when users must authenticate strongly and sessions are protected.

mitigations.description: Protect the SQL index database with access controls and encrypt sensitive metadata at rest, with monitoring for unauthorized queries or exports.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the index database helps prevent disclosure of sensitive document relationships and search data.

mitigations.description: Use controlled import procedures and integrity checks for Federal Reserve Bank image imports, including verification that only authorized files are loaded.
mitigations.evidence_quote: KCFRB Imaging (FRB) downloads and imports Federal Reserve Bank images into the system.
mitigations.rationale: Controlled imports reduce the chance that unauthorized or altered records enter the system.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter read-only access rules for historical archive systems and periodically review who can search or retrieve archived records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The KCFRB system is used to research historical archives of treasury checks.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting archive retrieval limits unnecessary exposure of legacy sensitive records.

risks.description: The system makes PII available in work lists and via links to additional details, which could expose more personal information than necessary to users who only need to triage work items.
risks.evidence_quote: FA Tracker uses, processes and maintains PII data obtained from the SCIMS database copy by PT-FM at the Application, Contract, and Contract Item levels for identifying and classifying work items in need of PSS intervention.
risks.rationale: The system processes identifiable customer data at multiple levels and displays it to users for intervention.

risks.description: Client-side filtering, sorting, and Excel export can increase the chance that PII is copied, retained, or shared outside the controlled system environment.
risks.evidence_quote: A user can then filter and sort this data on the client side. Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Local manipulation and export create additional copies of the data beyond the application.

risks.description: E-mail alerts containing work-list data may disclose PII through a less controlled channel and create repeated copies of records in users' inboxes.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
risks.rationale: E-mail delivery expands the attack surface and persistence of the information.

risks.description: The system uses replicated customer data from SCIMS, so any replication or synchronization issue could expose inaccurate or outdated personal information in FA Tracker.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via the National Planning and Agreements Database (NPAD) [which resides on PT-FM] and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
risks.rationale: Replicated data can diverge from the source and still be shown to users.

risks.description: Because contractors may access the system, there is a risk that non-government personnel could view sensitive customer and eligibility information beyond what they need.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Broader access by contractors increases the number of people who can see the data.

risks.description: The system includes data about race, sex, national origin, and disability in the source SCIMS repository, which raises sensitivity and potential discrimination concerns if exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: These are highly sensitive categories that warrant heightened protection.

risks.description: The system retains information for long periods, increasing the amount of time that personal data remains available for unauthorized access or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases cumulative exposure over time.

mitigations.description: Limit the work-list display to the minimum fields needed for PSS intervention and gate access to additional details behind stricter role checks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: displays minimal information to users in the form of work lists. Additional information/details can be accessed via a link to NRCS’ ProTracts- FundManager (PT-FM) application.
mitigations.rationale: Showing less data by default reduces unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict or disable local export and enforce controls such as watermarking, audit logging, and approved-device-only export for any Excel downloads.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting local copies reduces the chance of uncontrolled retention or sharing.

mitigations.description: Offer e-mail alerts only for the minimum necessary fields and require users to opt in with clear warnings about inbox storage and forwarding risk.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing content and making the risk explicit lowers disclosure through e-mail.

mitigations.description: Implement routine reconciliation and data-quality checks between PT-FM and the SCIMS source copy to detect stale or inconsistent records.
mitigations.rationale: Regular validation helps ensure users see accurate information.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access reviews for contractors and periodically recertify that access remains need-to-know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know review reduces unnecessary contractor access.
