mitigations.description: Treat the sensitive demographic fields in the source system as heightened-risk data and restrict reports or views that expose them unless explicitly required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Extra restrictions are appropriate for sensitive demographic information.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules aggressively and purge data as soon as the approved retention period expires.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention after the approved period reduces exposure over time.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains personally identifiable contact and banking information for exporters, financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of sensitive business contact and payment data.
risks.evidence_quote: GSM Point of contact names, email addresses, and phone numbers for exporters, US financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks. Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions.
risks.rationale: This data can identify individuals and link them to financial activity, so exposure could harm privacy and financial confidentiality.

risks.description: External users can enter and review their own program information through the public interface, which creates a risk that weak authentication or authorization could expose another participant's program records.
risks.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
risks.rationale: Any failure in access control could allow one participant to see another participant's records.

risks.description: The system sends nightly files to a data warehouse and produces ad hoc and canned reports, which increases the risk that data may be overexposed through downstream reporting and query access.
risks.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA.
risks.rationale: More copies and more report users increase the chance of unintended access or secondary use beyond the original purpose.

risks.description: Reports are submitted to auditors and other departments, creating a risk that information could be shared more broadly than necessary for program administration and oversight.
risks.evidence_quote: however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient expands the exposure surface and the chance of misuse or onward disclosure.

risks.description: Department contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of insider misuse or excessive access to sensitive program and contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
risks.rationale: Contractor access requires strong controls because contractors are not permanent government employees.

risks.description: Information is retained indefinitely as permanent records, which creates a risk that personal and financial data will remain accessible longer than necessary and be exposed in future incidents.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which data can be compromised or repurposed.

risks.description: The system uses tax identification numbers and payment bank information, which creates a risk of financial fraud or identity-related harm if those records are exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions.
risks.rationale: These fields are sensitive because they can be used to facilitate fraud or unauthorized financial activity.

risks.description: The system tracks claims, defaults, and collections owed to CCC, which creates a risk that financial and compliance information about participants could be exposed through reports or access logs.
risks.evidence_quote: Using the online GSM applications, FAS and FPAC users can process and track agreements, deliveries, fees, foreign bank limits, subsidies, payments, commodities, assignments, defaults, claims, and collections owed to CCC.
risks.rationale: This information can reveal a participant's financial status and program performance.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to contact and banking data to users with a documented need to know and encrypt the data in transit and at rest.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting stored/transmitted data reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong authentication and object-level authorization so each external user can access only its own records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
mitigations.rationale: Tight authorization is necessary to make the stated access limitation effective.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and minimize fields in ad hoc and canned reports to only what each user group needs.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing report visibility and limiting report content lowers the risk of secondary disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit external report distribution to the minimum necessary recipients and use disclosure review procedures before sharing reports outside the core program team.
mitigations.evidence_quote: however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing and limiting disclosures helps ensure reports are shared only for authorized purposes.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access approvals, least-privilege roles, and periodic access reviews for all contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review and least privilege reduce the risk of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Reassess whether all records need permanent retention and, for records that can be separated, remove or archive nonessential personal data earlier in accordance with the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Shortening retention where allowed reduces the time personal data remains exposed.

mitigations.description: Mask or tokenize tax identification numbers and bank account information in user-facing screens and reports.
mitigations.rationale: Masking sensitive financial identifiers lowers the impact of unauthorized viewing.

mitigations.description: Apply report filters and access controls so claims, defaults, and collections information is visible only to staff who need it for program administration and oversight.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Using the online GSM applications, FAS and FPAC users can process and track agreements, deliveries, fees, foreign bank limits, subsidies, payments, commodities, assignments, defaults, claims, and collections owed to CCC.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know controls limit exposure of sensitive financial status information.

risks.description: The system stores documents that may contain highly sensitive personal data, so a compromise could expose names, identifiers, financial data, criminal history, and signatures. Because the system is a shared cloud repository, the privacy impact of unauthorized access is significant.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box contains documents stored in a file repository that may include a wide range of PII.
risks.rationale: A repository holding many sensitive data elements creates a broad exposure risk if access controls fail or data is misused.

risks.description: Users can upload and share files with other users, including external partners and customers, which increases the chance of unauthorized disclosure or over-sharing. The collaborative design makes it easier for a user to share PII beyond the intended audience.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can upload documents and photos to a shared files folder, determine how their content can be shared with other users, and invite others to view and/or edit shared files.
risks.rationale: User-controlled sharing can lead to accidental or excessive disclosure when permissions are set too broadly.

risks.description: External contractors and partners have access to the system, so PII may be exposed to a wider set of non-employee users than in a purely internal system. This raises the risk of misuse or access beyond the minimum necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Expanding access outside the agency increases the number of people who can see sensitive records.

risks.description: The system allows PII to be updated by users themselves, which can create integrity and privacy risks if users change profile data incorrectly or maliciously. Incorrect profile data could then be used for administration or access decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC Box can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Self-service updates can introduce inaccurate or unauthorized changes to personal records.

risks.description: PII is manually stored from FPAC web applications and other sources, which can create handling errors during ingestion and storage. Manual processes increase the chance that sensitive information is placed in the wrong file or shared improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: Information from the affected members of the public (i.e., farmers, landowners, etc.) may be entered in through FPAC Web applications, then is only manually stored in FPAC Box.
risks.rationale: Manual handling of PII is more error-prone than automated controls and can lead to misfiling or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: The system retains information for long periods, including up to ten years or as long as program participation continues, which increases the amount of time sensitive records remain exposed to risk. Longer retention also increases the volume of data that could be affected by a breach.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: The longer data is kept, the longer it remains vulnerable to unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: The system does not periodically purge PII made available through third-party applications, so stale records may accumulate and remain accessible longer than necessary. This can increase privacy risk if outdated data is no longer needed for the intended purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: 10.6 Is the PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications purged periodically? • No
risks.rationale: Failing to purge unnecessary data leaves more personal information exposed over time.

risks.description: The platform supports internal and external collaboration through a third-party cloud service, which means a vendor maintains PII on the agency’s behalf. This creates a vendor dependence risk if the vendor’s security or handling practices are insufficient.
risks.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
risks.rationale: When a third party holds the data, the agency depends on the vendor’s safeguards to protect privacy.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive files to only users with a documented need-to-know and enforce strong role-based authorization for all file access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to FPAC Box is controlled through role-based authorization, eAuthentication, and DRM, which includes FIPS 140-2 certified encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access control reduces the chance that sensitive PII in stored documents is exposed to unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Require sharing permissions to be reviewed before external sharing is enabled and provide user guidance to prevent over-sharing of files.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can upload documents and photos to a shared files folder, determine how their content can be shared with other users, and invite others to view and/or edit shared files.
mitigations.rationale: Review and guidance help ensure users do not disclose PII more broadly than intended.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access reviews for contractors and partners and remove access when their role no longer requires it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review limits exposure to only those external users who still need access.

mitigations.description: Add validation and approval controls for user profile changes so self-service updates to PII are checked for accuracy and appropriateness.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC Box can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
mitigations.rationale: Validation reduces the risk that incorrect or unauthorized self-edits corrupt personal records.

mitigations.description: Use standardized ingestion procedures and staff training for manually stored documents to reduce misfiling and accidental disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: then is only manually stored in FPAC Box.
mitigations.rationale: Standard procedures and training help prevent human error when handling PII manually.

mitigations.description: Apply retention schedules consistently and delete records as soon as the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention to approved periods reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic purge processes for PII in third-party applications so outdated records are removed on a regular schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Regular purging prevents unnecessary accumulation of stale personal data.

mitigations.description: Strengthen vendor oversight with contractual security requirements and periodic assurance reviews of the third-party provider’s handling of PII.
mitigations.rationale: Oversight helps ensure the vendor’s safeguards remain adequate for protecting agency-held PII.

risks.description: The system transmits user information to external agencies, so sensitive application data could be exposed if those transfers are intercepted or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: As a result, information will be sent to (and from) users (farmers and producers) to DOL and USCIS, even though FPAC CASP / H2A does not assess or perform any actions on the data.
risks.rationale: Any system that passes user data between agencies creates confidentiality risk during transmission and integration.

risks.description: The system stores a DOL case number for 90 days, which creates a retention and unauthorized-access risk even if the number is not itself full PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The only user information that is stored on FPAC CASP is a producer’s DOL case number; this information does not identify the specific user or contain any user information. This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
risks.rationale: Stored identifiers can still be misused or linked with other data if access controls fail.

risks.description: Users may enter and save an inquiry in the system, which could expose case-related information if the saved inquiry is accessed by an unauthorized party.
risks.evidence_quote: A producer can save their inquiry and a DOL case number in FPAC CASP / H2A; this will allow the producer to retrieve their information from DOL and continue with their inquiry.
risks.rationale: Saved inquiries may contain context about a user's agricultural application and should be protected from unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system relies on a single common entry point for multiple agencies, which increases the impact of account compromise or authentication failure.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is, however, used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: A shared entry point concentrates access and can magnify the harm of credential theft or session hijacking.

risks.description: Data is collected by third-party services rather than directly by FPAC CASP, so users may not have clear visibility into how their information is handled across systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Data transmitted through FPAC CASP is collected from farmers and producers by either Login.gov, DOL, or USCIS.
risks.rationale: When multiple external systems collect the data, privacy notices and user expectations can become harder to manage consistently.

risks.description: The system depends on external agencies and Login.gov, which means privacy protections outside USDA could affect the confidentiality of user information.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: Privacy risk extends to the external services that receive or process the transmitted information.

mitigations.description: Continue to enforce HTTPS for all communications and add certificate validation and periodic transport-security testing for the integrations with DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov occur using HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport protection reduces the chance of interception during data exchange.

mitigations.description: Limit retention of the stored DOL case number to the minimum needed and apply strict access controls and audit logging to any stored record.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention and restricted access reduce the chance that the stored identifier is misused.

mitigations.description: Minimize what can be saved in the inquiry function and provide clear user notice before saving any inquiry content.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting saved content and informing users reduces unnecessary exposure of case-related information.

mitigations.description: Require multi-factor authentication and session timeout controls for the common entry point used to reach external agencies.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and session controls reduce the risk that one compromised login exposes multiple agency services.

mitigations.description: Provide a consolidated privacy notice that explains which external systems collect the data and how it is used across the workflow.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps users understand the handling of their information when third-party systems collect it.

mitigations.description: Establish and review data-sharing and security agreements with DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov to ensure equivalent privacy safeguards.
mitigations.rationale: Formal agreements help ensure external recipients protect the information to a consistent standard.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and business information in long-lived records, including tax IDs, SSNs, bank routing numbers, deposit account numbers, and farm ownership details. If access controls fail or are misused, this could expose extensive sensitive PII and financial data.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
risks.rationale: The listed data elements include direct identifiers and financial account information that would be harmful if disclosed.

risks.description: DRMS allows broad internal searching and specialized unconstrained searching for records managers and legal staff, which increases the chance of overexposure of personal information to users who do not need all records. This creates a risk of excessive internal access beyond the minimum necessary for a given task.
risks.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights. Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Broader search capability increases the amount of personal information any one user can reach.

risks.description: TeamMate+ contains audit documents that may come directly from customers or be uploaded by auditors, so incorrect or unnecessary personal data could be added to the system. Because the system is used as proof of findings, inaccurate or excessive data could be retained and propagated in audit records.
risks.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
risks.rationale: Multiple upload paths increase the chance that sensitive information is introduced without consistent review.

risks.description: The system retains information for long periods, including records that may be permanent, which increases the duration of privacy exposure. Longer retention increases the chance that old records will be accessed, disclosed, or used beyond the original need.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: The longer records are kept, the longer they remain vulnerable to misuse or unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system is accessible to department contractors with a need-to-know, which expands the number of people who may encounter sensitive records. Contractor access can increase privacy risk if role assignment or oversight is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Adding non-employees to the access population increases the chance of improper viewing or handling.

risks.description: DRMS stores scanned documents and metadata across multiple databases, including PDF files, SQL, Alfresco, and Elasticsearch, which creates multiple repositories of the same sensitive information. More copies and indexes can increase the chance of unintended exposure if one repository is accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
risks.rationale: Duplicating sensitive records across several stores increases the attack and exposure surface.

risks.description: The system uses indexing and search capabilities over record metadata, which can make it easier to locate personal information quickly and at scale. This raises the risk that a user with access could retrieve more records than intended.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS acts as the system of record for all the metadata about these records and supports indexing and search capabilities.
risks.rationale: Searchable metadata can facilitate bulk retrieval of personal information.

risks.description: The system supports FOIA and legal discovery use cases, which can lead to disclosure of personal information outside the normal operational context if requests are mishandled. Such disclosures could reveal records about individuals contained in DRMS.
risks.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: FOIA and discovery workflows are disclosure-sensitive and require careful handling to avoid unnecessary release.

mitigations.description: Enforce strong encryption and field-level access restrictions for the most sensitive identifiers and financial account data, with monitoring for access to those records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields.
mitigations.rationale: Sensitive data stored in documents should be protected at the document and field level to reduce exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit broad search capabilities for records managers and legal staff to only the minimum records needed for the approved task, and log all unrestricted searches for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining and auditing powerful search functions reduces unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Require validation and privacy review before customer- or auditor-uploaded documents are accepted into TeamMate+, including checks for unnecessary personal data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
mitigations.rationale: Pre-ingestion review helps prevent unnecessary or erroneous personal data from entering audit files.

mitigations.description: Apply and periodically verify records retention schedules so records are deleted or archived when no longer required, rather than relying on indefinite retention by default.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention duration reduces the time sensitive records remain exposed.

mitigations.description: Use role-based approval and periodic recertification for contractor access, with heightened monitoring of contractor activity in the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review of contractor access helps ensure only necessary users retain access.

mitigations.description: Minimize redundant copies of scanned records and metadata across databases, and ensure each repository has the same access controls and encryption protections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing duplicate storage lowers the number of places sensitive data can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict search and indexing functions to authorized roles and apply query logging to detect bulk or unusual retrieval of records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS acts as the system of record for all the metadata about these records and supports indexing and search capabilities.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling and monitoring search activity reduces the risk of mass retrieval of personal information.

mitigations.description: Use a documented disclosure review process for FOIA and legal discovery requests to ensure only responsive personal information is released.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: A review process helps prevent unnecessary disclosure during legally sensitive releases.

risks.description: The system retains most application records indefinitely, which increases the chance that PII will be exposed or misused long after it is needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long-term retention expands the window during which sensitive records can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

risks.description: The system collects and stores highly sensitive identifiers such as SSNs and EINs, creating harm if those identifiers are improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, Address, Phone Numbers, SSN, EIN number, eAuth JD/Name, Farm IDs
risks.rationale: SSNs and EINs are high-impact identifiers that can enable identity theft or unauthorized linkage across records.

risks.description: PII is shared outside USDA with Approved Insurance Providers, which creates a disclosure risk if those external recipients mishandle the data.
risks.evidence_quote: Policy information is shared only with the Approved insurance Providers (AIP).
risks.rationale: External sharing increases exposure beyond the agency's direct control.

risks.description: PII is shared internally with a data-mining function that searches for fraud, waste, and abuse, which creates secondary-use and overcollection risk if access is broader than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: This group performs the forensic data mining of RMA's data, looking for indications of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse.
risks.rationale: Analytic reuse of PII can exceed the minimum needed for the original program purpose.

risks.description: The system relies on contractors, which may increase the number of people with access to PII and the risk of unauthorized use or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Adding contractor access broadens the set of users who must be trusted and controlled.

risks.description: The system uses manual hard-copy forms and e-forms submitted through multiple parties, which creates a risk of collection or transmission errors and unnecessary exposure during handling.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected via hard copy forms and e-forms completed by the insured producer, insurance agent, or adjustor. The AIP sends this information to RMA on their behalf.
risks.rationale: More collection paths and intermediaries raise the chance of misrouting, loss, or incomplete protection of records.

risks.description: The system uses common office tools such as Excel to analyze data, which can increase the risk of uncontrolled copies or accidental disclosure of PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The tools used are COTS office automation products (e.g. Excel) and no derivative data is produced.
risks.rationale: Spreadsheet-based handling can make it easier to duplicate and spread sensitive data.

risks.description: The system hosts many applications within a single security boundary, so a compromise of the platform could expose PII from multiple RMA applications at once.
risks.evidence_quote: The Pipeline RMA HVA serves as the security boundary for all former operational RMA HVA applications with a “Low” or “Moderate” FIPS assessment result.
risks.rationale: Consolidation increases the blast radius of a single security failure.

mitigations.description: Apply records minimization and purge or archive records according to a defined schedule instead of retaining most records permanently.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention limits the amount of PII exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of SSNs and EINs to cases where they are legally required, and mask them in user interfaces and reports whenever full values are not needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The collection of SSN/TINs is authorized by the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 USC§ 1501).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and masking high-risk identifiers reduces the impact of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and periodic access reviews for AIPs, and require them to follow documented privacy and security controls for any received PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data is transferred via an encrypted VPN tunnel. AIP access is controlled via the same 586 identification process as used by RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Formal controls and reviews help ensure external recipients protect the data they receive.

mitigations.description: Restrict forensic data-mining access to the minimum necessary records and log each query or export for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This group performs the forensic data mining of RMA's data, looking for indications of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access limits and auditability reduce unnecessary secondary use of PII.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be role-based, time-limited, and subject to the same authentication and monitoring controls as federal users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Strong access controls reduce the risk introduced by additional users.

mitigations.description: Standardize secure submission procedures for hard-copy and e-form intake, including validation checks and secure handling requirements for AIPs, agents, and adjustors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected via hard copy forms and e-forms completed by the insured producer, insurance agent, or adjustor. The AIP sends this information to RMA on their behalf.
mitigations.rationale: Secure intake procedures reduce the chance of errors and mishandling during collection.

mitigations.description: Use controlled, access-restricted analysis environments instead of general-purpose spreadsheets for PII-bearing data, and prohibit local exports unless approved.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting spreadsheet use lowers the risk of uncontrolled copies and accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Segment the hosted applications and enforce least-privilege access between them so a compromise of one application cannot readily expose all others.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Pipeline RMA HVA serves as the security boundary for all former operational RMA HVA applications with a “Low” or “Moderate” FIPS assessment result.
mitigations.rationale: Segmentation reduces the impact of a single compromise across the shared platform.

risks.description: Using social media can expose users' personal information because the platforms are controlled by third-party companies outside CFPB's direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: Social media platforms are generally controlled and operated by non-government third parties.
risks.rationale: Third-party platform control can create privacy exposure beyond CFPB's own systems and policies.

risks.description: CFPB may collect personally identifiable information from social media interactions, creating a risk of disclosure or misuse of identity-related data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may collect or use a limited amount of Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) when using social media to further its ability to interact with the public.
risks.rationale: Any collection of PII increases the chance that sensitive identity information could be exposed or mishandled.

risks.description: PII collected through social media may include contact, device, location, or demographic details, which can increase the sensitivity of the information collected.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity such as name, username, email address, Internet Protocol (IP) address, geographic information, or demographic information.
risks.rationale: Broader categories of identifiers and location-related data can make users more identifiable.

risks.description: Information shared through social media may be retained in a system of records, creating a risk of longer-term storage beyond the immediate interaction.
risks.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB may collect PII through social media interactions, this information would be covered by the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System (CFPB.006) System of Records Notice.
risks.rationale: System-of-records coverage implies structured retention and use that can extend the life of collected data.

risks.description: Public-facing social media interactions can reveal information about consumers' engagement with CFPB or consumer finance issues to others on the platform.
risks.evidence_quote: We encourage consumers to share the latest information about the agency and consumer finance issues.
risks.rationale: Posting or interacting publicly can make a person's participation visible to unintended audiences.

risks.description: Use of social media may create expectations of privacy that are not fully met unless users receive clear notice about how their information is handled.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB understands that the public expects certain privacy protections when interacting with the Bureau through social media.
risks.rationale: If privacy expectations are unclear, users may share more information than they otherwise would.

mitigations.description: Apply CFPB privacy protections and security controls when using social media.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, all standard CFPB privacy protections and security controls apply.
mitigations.rationale: Security and privacy controls help reduce exposure from third-party platform use.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and use of PII to only what is necessary for public interaction.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB may collect or use a limited amount of Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) when using social media to further its ability to interact with the public.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing PII reduces the amount of personal data at risk.

mitigations.description: Provide notice to users about what kinds of PII may be collected, including identifiers such as name, username, email address, IP address, geographic information, and demographic information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII is any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity such as name, username, email address, Internet Protocol (IP) address, geographic information, or demographic information.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps users understand the sensitivity of the information they may disclose.

mitigations.description: Apply the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System of Records Notice and its associated handling rules to any PII collected through social media.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB may collect PII through social media interactions, this information would be covered by the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System (CFPB.006) System of Records Notice.
mitigations.rationale: A governing SORN provides a defined framework for handling and retaining collected information.

mitigations.description: Offer appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress before or during social media interactions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: What opportunities do I have for participation? Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: These participation rights help users understand and control how their information is used.

mitigations.description: Publish clear privacy notices explaining how CFPB uses social media and what protections apply.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notices reduce misunderstanding about privacy protections in social media interactions.

risks.description: The system republishes a public dataset that includes personally identifiable contact details for individuals associated with housing counseling agencies, which can expose them to unwanted contact or profiling.
risks.evidence_quote: Information about individuals associated with HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies includes:  Names (individuals and organizations)  Organization address and contact information including: o Street address o City, state, ZIP code o Phone number o Fax number o Email addresses and website address
risks.rationale: Publishing contact information broadly increases the chance that it will be used in ways the individuals did not intend.

risks.description: The dataset may include sensitive identifiers and other sensitive personal information, increasing harm if the public release is broader than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES: Name and other biographic information (e.g. date of birth) Contact Information (address, ZIP code, telephone number, email address) Social Security number (“SSN”) or other identifier Financial Information User and Online Information Third party Information Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: Sensitive data elements raise the impact of any disclosure or misuse even when the system is intended for public access.

risks.description: ZIP codes entered by locator tool users are collected and retained, which can reveal where a user is searching from and potentially infer housing-related interests or circumstances.
risks.evidence_quote: PII collected from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool includes:  ZIP code entered for search results.
risks.rationale: A ZIP code is limited, but it can still be linked to a person’s location and intent when combined with use patterns.

risks.description: User analytics and ZIP codes are being held as permanent records until NARA approves a disposition schedule, creating a retention risk of keeping search data longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: records collected through consumerfinance.gov (user analytics and ZIP codes entered in the locator tool) are being managed as permanent records until the disposition schedule for these records is approved by the National Archives and Records Administration
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window for misuse, breach, or secondary use of the data.

risks.description: The tool collects non-identifying operational data such as visit timestamps, browser version, pages viewed, and time on site, which can still be used to profile or link user activity across visits.
risks.evidence_quote: consumerfinance.gov collects other non‐identifying information from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool as part of normal operations supporting website functionality and security, (e.g. visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed and time on site, etc.)
risks.rationale: Even non-identifying telemetry can become privacy-relevant when combined over time or with other data.

risks.description: The API and locator tool allow users to download, share, and reuse the dataset in other applications, which increases the risk of downstream misuse or re-identification through aggregation.
risks.evidence_quote: The HUD API and the CFPB housing counselor locator tool also enables users to download or share data in the HUD counselor dataset in a variety of formats. HUD hosts the API, and users who develop a program and incorporate the API can present the HUD data in a variety of formats.
risks.rationale: Broad reuse and redistribution make it harder to control how the data is combined and used after release.

risks.description: There is no authorization process for read-only access, so anyone can access the dataset and locator tool without gatekeeping or identity verification.
risks.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov. There is no authorization process for read‐only access to the dataset or for use of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool.
risks.rationale: Open access lowers barriers for automated harvesting, bulk collection, and misuse.

mitigations.description: Limit the public-facing fields to the minimum needed for locating a counselor, and suppress any unnecessary personal contact details where an organizational contact point is sufficient.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB is republishing this publicly available data on its website and creating a tool by which users can more easily search the dataset in order to locate HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies in their area.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposed fields lowers the chance of unwanted contact and privacy intrusion.

mitigations.description: Apply a strict data-minimization review to ensure sensitive elements are excluded from the public dataset and from any downloads or API outputs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES: Name and other biographic information (e.g. date of birth) Contact Information (address, ZIP code, telephone number, email address) Social Security number (“SSN”) or other identifier Financial Information User and Online Information Third party Information Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing sensitive fields reduces the harm if the public dataset is copied or misused.

mitigations.description: Shorten retention for ZIP codes and make user search analytics aggregate-only where possible, rather than storing individual-level ZIP code entries.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregating or deleting search inputs reduces the chance that search behavior can be tied back to a person or location.

mitigations.description: Establish and publish a NARA-approved disposition schedule for consumerfinance.gov analytics and ZIP code records, and dispose of them promptly when the schedule allows.
mitigations.evidence_quote: records collected through consumerfinance.gov (user analytics and ZIP codes entered in the locator tool) are being managed as permanent records until the disposition schedule for these records is approved by the National Archives and Records Administration, at which time, the CFPB will dispose of such files in accordance with the schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A formal retention limit reduces unnecessary long-term storage risk.

mitigations.description: Limit telemetry collection to what is needed for security and usability, and avoid retaining detailed page-view histories longer than necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: consumerfinance.gov collects other non‐identifying information from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool as part of normal operations supporting website functionality and security, (e.g. visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed and time on site, etc.)
mitigations.rationale: Less detailed operational logging reduces the ability to profile users over time.

mitigations.description: Add anti-scraping, rate-limiting, and clear reuse terms to discourage bulk harvesting and downstream misuse of API and download functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The HUD API and the CFPB housing counselor locator tool also enables users to download or share data in the HUD counselor dataset in a variety of formats.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling automated and bulk use helps limit uncontrolled redistribution of the dataset.

mitigations.description: Implement throttling or other lightweight abuse controls for public read-only access to reduce automated collection while keeping the tool public.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The public has read‐only access to dataset and CFPB housing counselor locator tool made available through consumerfinance.gov. There is no authorization process for read‐only access to the dataset or for use of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool.
mitigations.rationale: Even without user accounts, basic controls can reduce mass harvesting and misuse.

risks.description: The system may include direct identifiers and sensitive personal data, creating a risk of re-identification or misuse if the data is exposed or handled improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: In certain circumstances, Administrative Data collected for Market Research may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers combined with financial and other sensitive fields increase the privacy impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Matching records across datasets can create more complete profiles of individuals than any single source, increasing the risk of privacy intrusion.
risks.evidence_quote: Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets.
risks.rationale: Linking datasets can reveal additional information about a person beyond what was originally collected in one source.

risks.description: Using record locators and updates from source entities can enable persistent linkage of records over time, increasing the risk of tracking individuals across datasets.
risks.evidence_quote: the CFPB may obtain updates or supplements to a dataset and, in those circumstances, may use record locators unique to the entity providing the update in order to update or supplement the individual records.
risks.rationale: Unique record locators can make it easier to reconnect records and maintain longitudinal profiles.

risks.description: The system uses demographic information such as race, gender, age, education, and income, which can expose sensitive characteristics and create profiling risks.
risks.evidence_quote: Demographic information, such as race/ethnicity, gender, age, education level, and income
risks.rationale: Sensitive demographic attributes can be used to infer or analyze protected or highly personal characteristics.

risks.description: The CFPB relies on third parties, commercial sources, and public databases for notice, which may leave individuals unaware that their information is being collected or shared.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB collects Administrative Data only from third parties, commercial sources and public databases, not directly from consumers, and it is those third parties’ responsibility to determine whether notice is required and to provide any requisite notice.
risks.rationale: When notice depends on outside entities, affected individuals may not receive clear or timely awareness of the collection.

risks.description: The system collects information about consumers from sources other than the individuals themselves, which can create accuracy and fairness risks if source data are incomplete or outdated.
risks.evidence_quote: Administrative Data is not collected directly from the individual. Administrative Data is gathered from third parties, such as those that offer or provide consumer financial products or services, from commercial sources, and from public databases.
risks.rationale: Data collected indirectly is more likely to contain errors that individuals may not know to correct.

risks.description: The CFPB retains computer and paper records indefinitely until a NARA-approved disposition schedule exists, increasing the risk of unnecessary long-term retention.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the period during which data could be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: Sharing research results with the general public, source data providers, and federal financial regulators could still create disclosure risk if de-identification fails or if contextual details allow re-identification.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the results of Market Research with the general public, the source of the Administrative Data, and/or federal financial regulators.
risks.rationale: Even aggregate outputs can sometimes be linked back to individuals when combined with other information.

risks.description: The system may contain biometric information and health or medical information, which are highly sensitive and would cause greater harm if disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: Highly sensitive categories require stronger safeguards because disclosure can have serious personal consequences.

mitigations.description: Limit access to only CFPB personnel with a need to know and keep direct identifiers separate from analytical datasets whenever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only CFPB personnel with a need to know are granted access to Administrative Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access and separating identifiers reduces the chance that direct PII will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Use only the minimum necessary fields for record matching and delete or de-identify matched linkage keys after the matching is complete.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de-identified copy of the matched dataset will be used for conducting research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Removing linkage data after matching limits the ability to reconstruct cross-dataset profiles.

mitigations.description: Apply strict controls to record locators and purge or replace them with non-linkable tokens once updates are incorporated.
mitigations.rationale: This reduces the risk that unique locators can be used to reconnect records over time.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened review and minimization for sensitive demographic fields, and use them only when necessary for proxying, weighting, or analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the CFPB collects and uses PII, it does so in order to proxy based on population characteristics; match across datasets; update data sets; weight samples; and generate frames for surveys on consumer experiences with consumer financial products and services.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting use of sensitive demographics to necessary analytic purposes reduces profiling risk.

mitigations.description: Require documented notice obligations and data-sharing terms from third-party sources before ingesting their data.
mitigations.rationale: Placing notice obligations in source agreements helps ensure individuals are informed when the CFPB does not collect directly from them.

mitigations.description: Perform source-data quality checks and allow correction or annotation of inaccurate records before they are used in research.
mitigations.rationale: Validating indirect-source data reduces the chance that research conclusions rely on inaccurate personal information.

mitigations.description: Finalize and implement a NARA-approved retention schedule as soon as possible and dispose of records according to that schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention schedule limits how long personal data remains available for exposure or secondary use.

mitigations.description: Apply disclosure review and statistical suppression rules before releasing any research outputs outside the internal team.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Products of Market Research consist of aggregate information, such as tabulations and statistical results, that are included in internal reports, CFPB whitepapers and studies, and other policy output, and do not contain direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing outputs before release helps ensure aggregate information does not inadvertently identify individuals.

mitigations.description: Treat biometric and health-related records as highly sensitive data and apply enhanced access controls and minimization.
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards are warranted because disclosure of these data types can cause substantial harm.

risks.description: Even though direct identifiers are removed, users may still isolate a single loan record and infer information about a specific borrower or applicant. This creates a re-identification risk from the combination of loan and property details.
risks.evidence_quote: Users may be able to isolate a single record, but the record will not contain any direct identifiers.
risks.rationale: A single record can still be linked back to an individual when the surrounding context is unique enough.

risks.description: The dataset includes sensitive financial, location, and loan outcome information that can reveal private details about mortgage applicants and borrowers. Public release increases the chance of unwanted profiling or discrimination based on these details.
risks.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset includes the following information: • Loan data o Application year o Loan or application type, purpose, amount (rounded to nearest thousand) o Action taken and denial reason, if applicable o HOEPA flag o Lien status (first, subordinate, unsecured) o Rate spread on higher-priced mortgages o Purchaser type o Preapproval request • Property data o Census tract, Metropolitan Statistical Area or Metropolitan Division, State, County o Property type
risks.rationale: Detailed financial and geographic attributes can expose sensitive patterns about an individual’s borrowing and housing situation.

risks.description: Republishing the dataset on consumerfinance.gov broadens access beyond the original public source and makes mass download, sharing, and reuse easier. That increases the risk of large-scale secondary use or linking with other datasets.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is republishing this HMDA Public Use Dataset on consumerfinance.gov in an effort to make the Dataset easier for the public to understand and use.
risks.rationale: Easier access and reuse can amplify privacy harms even when the underlying data is already public.

risks.description: The API allows users to query, filter, visualize, download, and share the data in multiple formats, which can facilitate automated extraction and re-identification attempts. Those capabilities can also enable profiling at scale.
risks.evidence_quote: The data publishing API permits users to create visualizations from the Dataset and to query and filter the Dataset to create custom summary tables. The data publishing API also enables users to download or share data in the Dataset in a variety of formats.
risks.rationale: Powerful query and export tools make it easier to combine records into potentially identifying patterns.

risks.description: The CFPB does not independently verify the accuracy and completeness of the republished dataset before posting it, so any upstream errors or over-disclosure could be carried forward. If redaction or source data are imperfect, privacy protections may be weakened.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB accepts the HMDA Public Use Dataset from the FFIEC as accurate and complete, and does not alter the data or independently verify the accuracy and completeness of the dataset before republishing it on consumerfinance.gov.
risks.rationale: Republishing without independent verification can preserve mistakes that increase privacy exposure.

risks.description: The dataset is available to the public, including federal and state agencies and private sector organizations, which allows broad downstream use outside the original disclosure context. This creates a risk of secondary use that may not align with the applicant’s expectations.
risks.evidence_quote: the HMDA Public Use Dataset will be available to the public, including federal and state agencies and private sector organizations.
risks.rationale: Wide redistribution increases the chance that data will be reused in ways that intensify privacy harm.

risks.description: The system retains the dataset until a CFPB records schedule is approved by NARA, which may extend the period during which the data remains available. Longer retention increases the window for misuse, linking, or re-identification.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB will continue to retain these records until a CFPB records schedule is approved by NARA.
risks.rationale: The longer sensitive public data remains accessible, the more opportunity exists for harmful reuse.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen the existing redaction of fields before publication, with periodic review of whether the released fields could enable single-record identification.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The regulators redact certain fields for the purpose of protecting applicant and borrower privacy and then share it with the public on the FFIEC website.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the uniqueness of records lowers the chance that a person can be singled out.

mitigations.description: Limit publication to the minimum necessary fields and keep higher-risk attributes rounded or generalized where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset includes the following information: • Loan data o Application year o Loan or application type, purpose, amount (rounded to nearest thousand) o Action taken and denial reason, if applicable o HOEPA flag o Lien status (first, subordinate, unsecured) o Rate spread on higher-priced mortgages o Purchaser type o Preapproval request • Property data o Census tract, Metropolitan Statistical Area or Metropolitan Division, State, County o Property type
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing detail reduces the amount of sensitive information exposed to the public.

mitigations.description: Provide clear user guidance on privacy-safe use of the republished data, including warnings against attempting to identify individuals or combine the dataset with other sources for identification.
mitigations.rationale: Usage guidance can reduce harmful downstream analysis of a public dataset.

mitigations.description: Add technical safeguards to the API, such as rate limiting, query constraints, and download controls, to reduce bulk extraction and automated re-identification attempts.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining automated access makes it harder to harvest the dataset at scale for misuse.

mitigations.description: Implement a quality-review step before republication to check for over-disclosure, redaction failures, or anomalies that could increase identifiability.
mitigations.rationale: A targeted review can catch privacy-sensitive errors before they are republished.

mitigations.description: Publish the dataset with prominent notice that it is already public and that users should comply with applicable privacy and anti-discrimination laws when reusing it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Both HMDA and Regulation C provide notice to the public that the data that comprises the HMDA Public Use Dataset will be made public.
mitigations.rationale: Notice can discourage misuse and remind downstream users of legal and privacy obligations.

mitigations.description: Establish and publish a retention schedule for the republished copy as soon as feasible, and remove or archive the dataset when no longer needed for public access.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter, defined retention reduces the duration of public exposure and reuse risk.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive personal data, including SSNs, financial information, biometric information, health or medical information, and sensitive demographic or benefits-status information, which creates a high impact if exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: PROJECT/SYSTEM INCLUDES: Name and other biographic information (e.g. date of birth) Contact Information (address, zip code, telephone number, email address) Social Security number (“SSN”) or other identifier Financial Information User and Online Information Third Party Information Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the data increase harm if unauthorized access, disclosure, or secondary use occurs.

risks.description: The system creates new combined datasets by matching records such as credit score to response data, which can reveal more about individuals than any one source alone.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases, Consumer Experience Research may involve the matching of records, such as credit score to Response Data, creating new assemblies of information about the Respondent.
risks.rationale: Linking datasets can increase identifiability and sensitivity even when direct identifiers are removed later.

risks.description: The system may collect information from third parties and use administrative data to identify survey recipients and support analyses, which raises the risk of collecting or using data beyond what respondents expect.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer Experience Research primarily relies on information collected directly from the individual and subject to the individual’s consent for the CFPB to collect additional information from third parties, such as those that offer or provide consumer financial products or services.
risks.rationale: Third-party collection can reduce transparency and make it harder for individuals to understand what data is used about them.

risks.description: The system may track an individual's behavior during research and use administrative data for nonresponse bias and control group analysis, which can create monitoring concerns.
risks.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB follows an individual’s behavior in the course of conducting Consumer Experience Research, the CPFB obtains the individual’s consent. At times, the CPFB may use Administrative Data to analyze nonresponse bias or evaluate control groups.
risks.rationale: Behavioral monitoring and analytic reuse can reveal patterns beyond the original research purpose.

risks.description: The system can disclose direct identifying information in external products such as case studies or quotes, which could expose participants if consent or de-identification is incomplete.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases where the CPFB seeks to share direct identifying PII in an external product, e.g. case study or quote, the CFBP will obtain consent of the appropriate Respondents prior to disclosure.
risks.rationale: Publishing identifiable quotes or case studies can directly reveal a respondent's identity or circumstances.

risks.description: The system shares research outputs publicly and with other entities, so re-identification or disclosure of individual-level information remains possible even when direct identifiers are removed.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share products of Consumer Experience Research externally, including by disseminating research results to the general public.
risks.rationale: Public dissemination increases the chance that combinations of attributes could identify a person.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely until a NARA disposition schedule is approved, which increases the duration of exposure for sensitive data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which data can be breached, misused, or subject to future incompatible uses.

risks.description: The system uses non-automated transfers through encrypted tunnels and encrypted email between contractor, vendor, and CFPB systems, which still creates transfer and handling risk across multiple environments.
risks.evidence_quote: Any system interactions are pushed, non-automated data transfers between contractor systems and/or vendor websites and CFPB internal systems, which take place via encrypted tunnels. These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
risks.rationale: Manual transfers across systems are more error-prone and can increase the chance of misrouting or mishandling data.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and storage of sensitive fields to only those strictly needed for a specific research task, and keep direct identifiers stored separately from analysis data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When direct identifying PII is necessary to facilitate Consumer Experience Research rather than necessary to the analysis, the direct identifying PII is stored and secured separately.
mitigations.rationale: Separating and minimizing sensitive data reduces the amount exposed if a dataset is accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Use de-identified copies for analysis after matching and avoid retaining linked datasets longer than needed for the research purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de- identified copy of the matched dataset is used for conducting research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Using de-identified analysis files reduces the privacy impact of record linkage.

mitigations.description: Limit third-party data collection to cases covered by respondent consent and document the standards for accuracy and completeness in contracts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Consumer Experience Research primarily relies on information collected directly from the individual and subject to the individual’s consent for the CFPB to collect additional information from third parties... In addition, when the CFPB partners with a third party, the CFPB outlines in contracts appropriate standards for data accuracy and completeness.
mitigations.rationale: Consent and contractual standards help constrain third-party collection and improve data governance.

mitigations.description: Obtain consent before following an individual's behavior and use administrative data for bias analysis only under defined research controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB follows an individual’s behavior in the course of conducting Consumer Experience Research, the CPFB obtains the individual’s consent.
mitigations.rationale: Consent is the stated control for behavioral monitoring and helps align use with participant expectations.

mitigations.description: Require explicit consent before any external publication of direct identifying information and review all external products for disclosure risk before release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: If the CPFB seeks to share direct identifying PII in an external product, it will obtain consent of the appropriate Respondents prior to disclosure.
mitigations.rationale: Consent before disclosure is the key safeguard for identifiable case studies or quotes.

mitigations.description: Continue applying disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation, rounding, exclusion of some variables, and exclusion of observations before public release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These external products are subject to disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations, and typically do not include direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: These techniques reduce the chance that public outputs can be traced back to an individual.

mitigations.description: Approve and implement a NARA records disposition schedule as soon as possible and dispose of records according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Records that fall under a general records schedule will be disposed of according to the applicable schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A retention schedule limits how long sensitive records remain available for exposure.

mitigations.description: Standardize and minimize manual data transfers between contractor, vendor, and CFPB systems, and restrict transfers to encrypted channels only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any system interactions are pushed, non-automated data transfers between contractor systems and/or vendor websites and CFPB internal systems, which take place via encrypted tunnels. These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing manual transfer steps lowers the chance of handling mistakes and unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system can contain highly sensitive direct identifiers, including Social Security numbers, financial account numbers, home addresses, and phone numbers, creating a risk of unauthorized identification or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases, they may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number • Social Security number
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers and financial account data increase the harm if the data are exposed or mishandled.

risks.description: The system may include biometric and health or medical information, which raises the sensitivity of any disclosure or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
risks.rationale: Biometric and health data are especially sensitive because misuse can cause lasting privacy harm.

risks.description: The CFPB generally collects the data from third parties rather than directly from consumers, so individuals may not know their information is being collected or used.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB generally collects SEFL Data from third parties, not directly from consumers.
risks.rationale: Collection without direct notice reduces transparency and limits individuals' ability to understand or contest the use of their information.

risks.description: Individuals generally will not be informed when their information is collected through supervisory or enforcement activity, including how it will be used or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: where information is obtained in the exercise of CFPB’s supervisory and enforcement authorities, individuals generally will not receive notice that the information is being requested and therefore how such information will be used or disclosed.
risks.rationale: Lack of notice increases the risk of unexpected downstream sharing or use.

risks.description: The system can match records across datasets and update or supplement records, which can create more detailed profiles about individuals than any single source contains.
risks.evidence_quote: Use of SEFL Data for Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets.
risks.rationale: Linking datasets can increase re-identification and profiling risk even when some direct identifiers are removed.

risks.description: The CFPB may use direct identifying PII to contact potential survey recipients, which can reveal a person's relationship to consumer financial products and services.
risks.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does use direct identifying PII in analyses, it does so in order to a) match across datasets; b) update data sets; and c) contact potential recipients of surveys
risks.rationale: Using identifiers for outreach can expose sensitive financial-related contact information and participation status.

risks.description: The system may use demographic and financial data to make generalized inferences, which can still produce sensitive conclusions about individuals or groups.
risks.evidence_quote: such information include: • Type of product/service • Size of product/service • Participation rates • Participation terms • Fees • Geographic location • Unique record locators • Balances • Type of Financial Institution • Market share of Financial Institution • Credit score • Demographic information, such as race/ethnicity, gender, age, education level, and income
risks.rationale: Combining demographic and financial variables can enable inference of sensitive characteristics.

risks.description: Market research outputs may be shared with the general public and federal financial regulators, creating a risk of disclosure if aggregation or de-identification is insufficient.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the products of Market Research with the general public and federal financial regulators.
risks.rationale: Public release expands the audience and increases the consequences of any residual identifiability.

risks.description: The CFPB retains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves a disposition schedule, which increases the period during which the data could be exposed or repurposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases cumulative exposure and the chance that data outlive the original need.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection and storage of direct identifiers, and remove or tokenize them before analysis whenever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, direct identifying PII has been stripped from SEFL Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing direct identifiers lowers the likelihood of identification if the data are accessed or shared.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter access controls and handling rules for biometric and health or medical information, including limiting use to cases where it is necessary for the research purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other Information (including biometric information and health or medical information)
mitigations.rationale: Extra controls are appropriate because the data are highly sensitive.

mitigations.description: Provide clearer public-facing notice about third-party collection and downstream uses whenever notice can be given, including through the PIA and related disclosures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In cases where notice cannot be provided or is not required, the CFPB has provided constructive notice of how it may use such information through this PIA.
mitigations.rationale: Improved notice helps individuals understand how their information may be used.

mitigations.description: Limit supervisory and enforcement data use to the purposes authorized by law and document each disclosure under the applicable legal authority.
mitigations.evidence_quote: In these cases, the use and disclosure of information is controlled by applicable federal law, regulations, discovery rules, and court orders.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining use to legal authority reduces the chance of unexpected disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use privacy-preserving record linkage methods and re-identification review before combining datasets, and keep the matched dataset de-identified for analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: After the matching is complete, a de-identified copy of the matched dataset is used for conducting Market Research and analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Privacy-preserving linkage reduces the chance that combined records can identify people.

mitigations.description: Restrict outreach to survey recipients to the minimum necessary contact information and separate contact files from analytic files.
