mitigations.description: Perform regular security reviews of the cloud configuration and vendor-managed services, including access controls and sharing settings across Dynamics 365, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps catch misconfiguration and service-level exposure before sensitive records are disclosed.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce retention schedules for case files and related communications, and delete records when they are no longer needed for the inquiry or required by law.
mitigations.rationale: Clear retention limits reduce the privacy risk created by keeping inquiry records over the full lifecycle.

risks.description: ROVR stores large volumes of identifiable health and enrollment data about millions of enrollees, family members, and eligible non-enrollees, creating a broad privacy exposure if the repository is misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program
risks.rationale: The system aggregates sensitive PII and health-related information for a very large population, increasing the impact of any privacy incident.

risks.description: The repository contains detailed medical, pharmacy, encounter, provider, and cost information that can reveal highly sensitive health conditions and utilization patterns.
risks.evidence_quote: service use and cost data” includes, but is not limited to, medical claims data, pharmacy claims data, encounter data, and provider data.
risks.rationale: These data elements are inherently sensitive because they can disclose an individual's health status, treatment, and spending patterns.

risks.description: ROVR creates person-level longitudinal records that link data over time, which increases the risk of re-identification and deeper profiling of individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
risks.rationale: Linking records over time makes it easier to assemble detailed profiles about a person than using isolated records.

risks.description: Enrollment data may be used to identify and address possible erroneous or duplicate coverage, which could affect an individual's benefits if the data are inaccurate or misinterpreted.
risks.evidence_quote: enrollment data may reveal instances where an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract. Generally, that is an erroneous enrollment that may be revealed through enrollment files included in ROVR
risks.rationale: If duplicate coverage is flagged incorrectly, it could lead to improper administrative action affecting coverage.

risks.description: The system analyzes data across population groups, geographic areas, health plans, providers, and disease conditions, which can enable sensitive group profiling beyond individual administration.
risks.evidence_quote: These analyses may include examination of the cost of care, utilization of services, and comparing these across specific population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions.
risks.rationale: Cross-cutting analysis can expose patterns about particular groups or conditions that should be handled carefully to avoid unnecessary privacy impact.

risks.description: ROVR may be used to detect fraud, waste, and abuse and to analyze specific individuals when fraud is suspected or confirmed, creating a risk of expanded investigative use of health data.
risks.evidence_quote: the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
risks.rationale: Using claims data for investigative purposes can broaden access and increase the sensitivity of the information handled.

risks.description: ROVR receives data from multiple external systems and agencies, which increases the risk of inconsistent data handling or unauthorized disclosure during sharing and reconciliation.
risks.evidence_quote: These systems include the FEHB Data Hub ... the Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) warehouse ... and the Centralized Enrollment Reconciliation ... other Federal agencies through data sharing agreements.
risks.rationale: More sources and exchanges create more opportunities for privacy controls to fail across organizational boundaries.

risks.description: The system includes Medicare-related health claims for dual enrollees, which can expose additional sensitive coverage and utilization information across programs.
risks.evidence_quote: CMS provides service use and cost data3 to OPM, including health claims information for FEHB enrollees and their eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare programs.
risks.rationale: Combining FEHB and Medicare information can reveal more about a person's health and coverage than either source alone.

risks.description: The repository may be used to assess policy and legislative initiatives, creating a risk that data collected for administration will be repurposed for broader analytical uses.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM may also use the data to assess the effects of new policy and legislative initiatives to improve its assessment of FEHB plan performance.
risks.rationale: Secondary analytical use can expand the scope of processing beyond the core purpose of administering benefits.

mitigations.description: Limit access to ROVR to authorized personnel with a need to know and enforce strong access controls and auditing.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that the large sensitive repository will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Minimize the amount of detailed claims and provider data stored or shared when non-identifiable data will suffice.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data
mitigations.rationale: Using non-identifiable data where possible reduces exposure of highly sensitive health information.

mitigations.description: Use record-level identifiable data only when necessary to create longitudinal records and apply de-identification or pseudonymization for routine analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting identifiable linkage to necessary cases lowers re-identification and profiling risk.

mitigations.description: Verify suspected duplicate enrollments through a separate review process before any enrollment-related action is taken.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, such an occurrence would be identified and addressed outside of ROVR, but data from ROVR may be used as part of the analysis.
mitigations.rationale: A review step helps prevent incorrect data from affecting an individual's coverage.

mitigations.description: Apply aggregation and disclosure controls to population-level analyses so individual identities are not revealed unnecessarily.
mitigations.evidence_quote: much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation limits the chance that group analyses can be traced back to specific people.

mitigations.description: Use fraud, waste, and abuse data only for the stated investigative purpose and restrict further disclosure unless permitted under the Privacy Act.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Most service use and cost data in ROVR will be used for administrative and analytical purposes related to coverage of benefits; and otherwise is generally not used for purposes related to a specific individual except when OPM suspects or has confirmed that fraud, waste, or abuse has occurred with respect to services rendered or payments made in connection with the FEHB Program.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces the chance that investigative use expands beyond what is justified.

mitigations.description: Use data sharing agreements to specify permitted uses, retention, and storage protocols for all incoming data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agreements constitute the methods of use and applicable retention and storage protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Written agreements help ensure external data exchanges follow consistent privacy controls.

mitigations.description: Limit Medicare-linked analyses to the minimum necessary data needed for reconciliation and statistical review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OPM uses this data in its administration of the FEHB Program, including examining patterns of service use, statistical analyses of service use, risk and cost for dual FEHB and Medicare enrollees
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing Medicare-linked data reduces the sensitivity of combined coverage analysis.

mitigations.description: Document and review any policy or legislative analysis to ensure it remains tied to FEHB plan performance and does not expand into unrelated uses.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OPM may also use the data to assess the effects of new policy and legislative initiatives to improve its assessment of FEHB plan performance.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing secondary analyses helps keep processing aligned with the stated program purpose.

risks.description: The system stores Social Security numbers and uses them as debtor identifiers, creating a high-impact risk if the data is exposed or misused. This is especially sensitive because the same identifier is also embedded in another tracking number.
risks.evidence_quote: their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO), their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount, and other system defined tracking numbers such as Claim Number and Debtor Number (which also includes the individual’s SSN).
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive and their use as identifiers increases the harm from unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to ABCO data, which can limit their ability to review or correct information about their debts. This may increase the risk that inaccurate records persist and affect billing or collection actions.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Without individual access, errors may be harder to detect and remedy.

risks.description: The system sends debt-related notices based on agency-provided personal data, but no prior notice is provided to the individual before collection. This creates a transparency risk because people may not know their information is being used in ABCO until after billing or collection activity begins.
risks.evidence_quote: Was notice provided to the individual prior to collection of information? No. The ABCO system uses personal data provided by agencies to generate reports or notices. These are used by each agency to notify the individual of the status of debts owed.
risks.rationale: Lack of prior notice reduces transparency about how personal data is used.

risks.description: ABCO exchanges data with multiple internal and external systems, including Treasury systems and a digital records contractor, increasing the number of places where personal data may be exposed or mishandled. More sharing expands the attack surface and the chance of unauthorized disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO exchanges data with the following within USDA:  NFC Enterprise Infrastructure and Platforms  NFC Payroll/Personnel System Major Application  NFC Payroll Accounting System Major Application  NFC WebApps Major Application  NFC Miscellaneous Administrative Systems Group Major Application  NFC Insight Major Application  USDA OCFO/FMS - Financial Management Modernization Initiative  USDA OCFO/FMS - Reporting of IPAC Transactions for Agriculture
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient or interface increases privacy and security risk.

risks.description: Contractors at a local facility convert Payroll reports into PDF files and transmit them to Iron Mountain, which creates a risk of exposure during contractor handling or file conversion. This is a privacy risk because contractors may see personal debt information in the course of processing it.
risks.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
risks.rationale: Contractor processing introduces another point where sensitive data can be viewed or copied.

risks.description: ABCO retains data on the mainframe indefinitely, which increases the long-term risk of unauthorized access, secondary use, or breach over time. Keeping debt records forever also means sensitive information remains available long after it may be needed.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Long retention generally increases cumulative privacy risk.

risks.description: The system allows authorized agency users to run predefined and custom reports and access data elements based on privileges, which could enable broader internal disclosure than necessary if access controls are misconfigured or overbroad. This creates a risk of internal misuse or excessive access.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency security personnel.
risks.rationale: Report generation and broad data-element access can expose more information than a user needs.

risks.description: Access is managed through requests from agency functional managers and security officers across approximately 35 USDA agencies and about 160 Federal agencies payroll by the NFC, which creates a risk of inconsistent access approvals and privilege creep. Large-scale delegated access increases the chance that users retain access they no longer need.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users of approximately 35 USDA agencies have access to this data.
risks.rationale: Distributed access administration can make least-privilege enforcement harder.

mitigations.description: Mask SSNs in user-facing views and reports, and use a surrogate identifier that does not embed the SSN for routine processing.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing direct SSN exposure lowers the impact of unauthorized access or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide a controlled individual access and correction process, such as a secure request channel for debt record review and amendment through the responsible agency.
mitigations.rationale: Giving individuals a way to review records helps detect and correct inaccuracies.

mitigations.description: Add a notice step before data is collected or used for billing, explaining that agency-provided personal data will be used in ABCO for debt billing and collection.
mitigations.rationale: Advance notice improves transparency and lets individuals understand the use of their data.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing to the minimum necessary data fields for each recipient and document recipient-specific access rules for every interface and exchange.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the amount of personal information exposed through each sharing relationship.

mitigations.description: Require contractor handling of reports to occur under strict role-based access, logging, and confidentiality controls, with periodic review of contractor access.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the chance of unauthorized viewing or mishandling.

mitigations.description: Apply a finite retention schedule to mainframe records and delete or archive data when no longer needed for the stated financial purpose, consistent with approved records rules.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the window in which old records can be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Restrict custom reports and sensitive data elements to the minimum necessary and require approval for elevated reporting access.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting reporting capabilities reduces unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Perform periodic access recertification for all agency users and remove dormant or unnecessary accounts promptly.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps prevent overbroad or outdated access from persisting.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal information than is needed because correspondence can include extra details voluntarily provided by the public beyond basic contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: In a few cases, it may also include other information about the individual voluntarily provided by that individual in the correspondence.
risks.rationale: Public correspondence can contain unexpected sensitive details, so the system may retain unnecessary PII if intake is not limited.

risks.description: The system retains contact information such as physical, email, and phone details, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure of personal contact data.
risks.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes. Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Maintaining direct contact details increases the impact if access controls fail or data is exposed.

risks.description: Role-based access may still allow too many users to view correspondence records, exposing PII across business units that review and approve packages.
risks.evidence_quote: support the receipt and processing of correspondence and other artifacts that require ingestion, review, and approval by business units across USDA.
risks.rationale: Broader workflow access increases the number of people who can see personal information.

risks.description: Search, dashboards, and reports may surface personal information in ways that expand internal access beyond the original correspondence handling purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: To analyze data, Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used.
risks.rationale: Analytic tools can replicate and expose data to additional users or views if not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Machine learning and historical search may reuse prior correspondence content and responses in ways that reveal personal information from past inquiries.
risks.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
risks.rationale: Using historical content for retrieval can expose personal details from earlier correspondence to new users or searches.

risks.description: Metadata changes and tracking of package movement may create detailed logs of user activity and correspondence handling that could reveal sensitive information about individuals' interactions with USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: documenting changes to the metadata or producing research or a response to received correspondence, and tracking the movement of the packages between different users and user groups.
risks.rationale: Workflow tracking can indirectly expose who submitted what and how it was handled.

risks.description: The system may use phone numbers to contact individuals for more information, which could disclose correspondence-related details to the wrong person if contact information is inaccurate or outdated.
risks.evidence_quote: Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Using contact data for follow-up creates a risk of misdirected outreach if the data is wrong.

risks.description: Because the system processes correspondence addressed to the Secretary and other USDA officials, it may store sensitive or politically significant personal information submitted by the public.
risks.evidence_quote: The system will include information regarding individuals, primarily information such as the name, address, phone number, and email address incidental to their correspondence addressed to the Secretary of Agriculture and various other officers and employees of USDA.
risks.rationale: Correspondence to senior officials often contains personal or sensitive matters that warrant careful handling.

mitigations.description: Limit intake and retention to the minimum PII needed to process correspondence, and redact or remove unnecessary personal details from the record.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored content reduces exposure from voluntary over-sharing.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to contact information to staff with a documented need to know and protect it with role-based controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: supporting standardized processes and role-based access.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can view contact details lowers the chance of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege permissions and separate review/approval access so users only see the correspondence needed for their assigned task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: support the receipt and processing of correspondence and other artifacts that require ingestion, review, and approval by business units across USDA.
mitigations.rationale: Task-based access reduces unnecessary exposure across business units.

mitigations.description: Configure dashboards and reports to suppress or mask PII unless a user is specifically authorized to see it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To analyze data, Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting PII in analytic views prevents broad internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Govern NLP and ML search results so they return only necessary excerpts and exclude or mask personal information where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling what the search engine returns reduces reuse of personal details from prior records.

mitigations.description: Limit audit and workflow tracking data to operational needs and protect logs and metadata with access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: documenting changes to the metadata or producing research or a response to received correspondence, and tracking the movement of the packages between different users and user groups.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting operational tracking data helps prevent indirect disclosure of correspondence details.

mitigations.description: Verify and periodically update contact information before outreach, and use approved contact procedures to avoid misdirected communications.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
mitigations.rationale: Validating contact data reduces the chance that personal information is disclosed to the wrong recipient.

mitigations.description: Provide handling guidance and review procedures for correspondence that may contain sensitive or politically significant personal information before it is shared for approval or response.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system will include information regarding individuals, primarily information such as the name, address, phone number, and email address incidental to their correspondence addressed to the Secretary of Agriculture and various other officers and employees of USDA.
mitigations.rationale: Extra review for sensitive correspondence helps ensure it is handled appropriately.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive civil rights complaint information and complainant personal details, creating a risk of harm if the data is improperly accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information includes complaints of discrimination against USDA programs and services and employee complaints. It uses complainant personal information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and miscellaneous identification numbers (generates a case number).
risks.rationale: Complaint records and contact details can be sensitive and could affect individuals if disclosed inappropriately.

risks.description: Because the system is reachable through a web-based environment connected to the public Internet, it is exposed to external attack and interception risks.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
risks.rationale: Internet connectivity expands the attack surface for unauthorized access or data compromise.

risks.description: Contractor and vendor-managed access to the system creates a risk of overbroad or inappropriate access to complainant data.
risks.evidence_quote: MicroPact Engineering provides system, network, development, and administrative security under contract with The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
risks.rationale: Third parties involved in operations may see or handle PII unless access is tightly controlled.

risks.description: User access is determined by management rather than described role-based technical controls, which can lead to inconsistent or excessive access to PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The Program Directorate management determines levels for users of CRES.
risks.rationale: Manual assignment of access levels can increase the chance of granting more access than necessary.

risks.description: Information is collected by mail, email, telephone, and interviews before being entered into the system, creating a risk of insecure or misdirected collection of PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake channels increase the chance that personal information may be mishandled before it reaches the system.

risks.description: The system retains complaint files until destruction based on judicial regulations, but the exact retention period is unclear, which can increase the risk of keeping PII longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES’s files are destroyed, based on the judicial’ s regulations.
risks.rationale: Unclear retention timing can lead to unnecessary accumulation of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Limit access to complaint records to only designated users with a need to know and enforce strong authentication and audit logging for all PII access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and logging access reduces the chance that sensitive complaint data is viewed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Apply continuous network security monitoring, intrusion detection, and regular vulnerability and firewall configuration reviews for the Internet-facing environment.
mitigations.rationale: Ongoing monitoring and hardening help reduce the likelihood of external compromise of a web-based system.

mitigations.description: Require contractor personnel to have documented least-privilege access, background screening, and privacy/security training, with periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Support staff security requirements are based on public trust requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter contractor controls reduce the risk of unnecessary exposure of complainant information.

mitigations.description: Implement documented role-based access controls and periodic recertification of user permissions to ensure access stays limited to job duties.
mitigations.rationale: Formal role-based controls are more consistent than ad hoc assignment and help prevent excessive access.

mitigations.description: Use secure intake procedures for mail, email, telephone, and interviews, including verified recipient addresses, secure email handling, and staff guidance for collecting only necessary information.
mitigations.rationale: Secure intake practices lower the chance that PII is intercepted, misdirected, or collected unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Document a precise records schedule and automated deletion or destruction process tied to the approved retention period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The OASCR Records Manager and Department Records Manager have developed the goals and timelines for reporting and adhering to records management requirements issued by the National Archive Records and Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Office of Personnel Management.
mitigations.rationale: Clear schedules and automated disposal help ensure records are not retained longer than authorized.

risks.description: The system collects and shares personal information across multiple administrative domains and dashboards, increasing the risk of broader internal exposure than users may expect.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Cross-domain reporting expands the number of people and systems that can see user information.

risks.description: The system allows free-form user input in an unrestricted profile field, which can lead to collection of unnecessary sensitive or highly personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: Unrestricted text fields can capture more personal data than the system needs.

risks.description: User photos combined with names create identifiable profile data that may increase privacy exposure if accessed or disclosed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: A photo linked to a name makes a person easier to identify.

risks.description: The system collects personal information that is not required for proper operation, so users may provide more PII than is necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
risks.rationale: Collecting optional PII increases privacy risk without a clear operational need.

risks.description: Account creation by email and profile updates by users may result in inaccurate or outdated personal information being stored.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected by email from each user initially to create the account within Salesforce. Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo
risks.rationale: User-managed data can become stale if it is not actively reviewed and corrected.

risks.description: The system transmits personal information into the USDA Data Lake and Tableau dashboards, creating additional storage and access points that could be exposed if those downstream systems are misconfigured or overbroadly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
risks.rationale: Moving data into additional platforms increases the number of places where privacy controls must hold.

risks.description: Authorized contractors have access to the system, which creates insider-access risk if permissions are too broad or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access creates a need to tightly limit what each person can see and do.

risks.description: The system retains records under a general records schedule, but the description does not specify data minimization or deletion of optional PII, which could allow personal information to persist longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Items are retained per the General Records Schedule 24: Information Technology Operation and Management Records. Records are destroyed based on the subject matter.
risks.rationale: Without field-level minimization, optional personal data may remain in records longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Restrict Tableau dashboards and reports to the minimum necessary audience and apply role-based access controls to each administrative domain view.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting who can view cross-domain reports reduces unnecessary internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Add validation or character limits to the “About Me” field and prohibit entry of sensitive personal information.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining free-text input reduces the chance that unnecessary personal data is collected.

mitigations.description: Make profile photos optional by default and provide a clear warning that photos combined with names are PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.rationale: A warning and opt-in approach helps users understand the privacy impact of adding a photo.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to only the personal information needed for parking permits and access identification, and disable optional fields that are not operationally necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less optional data lowers privacy risk without affecting core functions.

mitigations.description: Provide a user review process so individuals can periodically confirm and correct their account information.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps keep user-provided data accurate and current.

mitigations.description: Apply access controls and auditing to the USDA Data Lake and Tableau outputs so only authorized users can see the transferred information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Downstream access controls are needed because the data is copied into additional systems.

mitigations.description: Use least-privilege access for contractors and review contractor permissions regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the chance of unnecessary insider exposure.

mitigations.description: Establish a process to remove optional PII when it is no longer needed, even if the underlying record must be retained under the records schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Separating retention of the record from retention of optional PII reduces long-term exposure.

risks.description: The system centralizes physical access and visitor identity data across USDA facilities, creating a broad privacy impact if the repository is misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS collects information required to control physical access to USDA managed facilities and restricted areas within those facilities in all regions across the United States. ePACS maintains individuals' personal individual verification (PIV) information to support the USDA’s efforts related to protecting USDA facilities which includes the USDA Washington DC Visitor Management System (VMS).
risks.rationale: A centralized system holding access-control and identity data increases the sensitivity and scale of any privacy incident.

risks.description: The system stores identity and credential attributes that can be used to profile or track individuals' movements and access behavior.
risks.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity
risks.rationale: Card-read activity can reveal where and when a person accessed facilities, which is privacy-sensitive behavioral data.

risks.description: Visitor data is collected through the VMS and may include background-check-related information, increasing the sensitivity of visitor privacy data.
risks.evidence_quote: The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
risks.rationale: Background-check processing can involve highly sensitive visitor information and deserves tighter controls.

risks.description: Non-authoritative data is manually collected at card issuance, creating a risk of inaccurate or inconsistent personal data in access records.
risks.evidence_quote: Also, Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
risks.rationale: Manually collected data is more prone to error, which can lead to incorrect access decisions and privacy harm.

risks.description: The system relies on data from multiple human resources databases consolidated into ICAM Shared Services, which may propagate errors or outdated information into ePACS.
risks.evidence_quote: This identity data is provided from a series of USDA Human Resources databases which are consolidated into ICAM Shared services.
risks.rationale: Upstream data quality problems can flow into access-control decisions and affect individuals' rights and access.

risks.description: Limited PII is shared with internal analytics and service-center recipients, creating additional disclosure points beyond the core access-control use.
risks.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily. Once in the EDAPT, the data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards with summary PIV card access for executive management. EDAPT receives last name, first name and credential card read activity. Limited ePACS data is provided through a daily report, called the Fleet report, to the Credit Card Service Center via email. The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient and transfer path expands the number of places where PII can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: Daily email transmission of employee status and names to the Credit Card Service Center increases the risk of interception or misdelivery.
risks.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is provided through a daily report, called the Fleet report, to the Credit Card Service Center via email.
risks.rationale: Email is a common source of accidental disclosure if messages are sent to the wrong recipient or handled insecurely.

risks.description: The system allows rare external sharing of PII, which can create privacy risk if approvals or routine-use limits are not strictly followed.
risks.evidence_quote: If information contained in ePACS is shared outside of USDA it is consistent with applicable laws and policy. A SORN is pending to cover the collection of data for ePACS, see section 6.1. As information shared to external organizations is rare, any data from ePACS before release to an external organization must be approved by the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel.
risks.rationale: External disclosure increases privacy exposure and requires strong governance to avoid improper release.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system, which increases the number of people who can view sensitive access-control and identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: More users with access means a larger insider-risk surface, even when screening is required.

risks.description: The system retains data for 5.5 years, including five years of archived data, which may keep personal information longer than necessary for some individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the duration of exposure if records are breached or later misused.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to ePACS to only personnel with a documented need-to-know and enforce role-based access controls with regular access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that sensitive centralized data is seen or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Minimize retention and sharing of card-read activity to only what is necessary for executive management, and keep it in summary form rather than individual-level detail where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The ePACS information that is shared for executive management is summary of credential card read activity
mitigations.rationale: Summaries reduce the amount of behavioral information exposed about specific individuals.

mitigations.description: Limit visitor background-check data collection to the minimum needed for the stated visitor screening purpose and apply strict access controls to visitor records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
mitigations.rationale: Background-check data is sensitive, so minimizing collection and access lowers privacy risk.

mitigations.description: Validate manually collected issuance data against authoritative sources before it is stored or used to issue access credentials.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Also, Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps prevent inaccurate personal data from affecting access decisions.

mitigations.description: Implement data-quality checks and periodic reconciliation with the source HR systems to detect stale or inconsistent identity records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This identity data is provided from a series of USDA Human Resources databases which are consolidated into ICAM Shared services.
mitigations.rationale: Reconciliation reduces the chance that upstream errors propagate into ePACS.

mitigations.description: Limit internal disclosures to the minimum necessary fields and review whether analytics recipients can use de-identified or aggregated data instead of named records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EDAPT receives last name, first name and credential card read activity. Limited ePACS data is provided through a daily report, called the Fleet report, to the Credit Card Service Center via email. The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the fields shared lowers the privacy impact of downstream internal uses.

mitigations.description: Replace email delivery of the Fleet report with a secure file transfer or secure portal that enforces recipient authentication and access logging.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is provided through a daily report, called the Fleet report, to the Credit Card Service Center via email.
mitigations.rationale: A secure delivery channel reduces the risk of accidental disclosure compared with email.

mitigations.description: Require documented approval and legal review before any external disclosure, and maintain a disclosure log for all releases outside USDA.
mitigations.evidence_quote: any data from ePACS before release to an external organization must be approved by the OSSP director and the Office of General Counsel.
mitigations.rationale: Formal approval and logging help ensure external sharing stays within authorized limits.

mitigations.description: Apply the same least-privilege access controls and periodic background-check validation to contractors as to USDA employees.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Equal access controls for contractors reduce insider and overexposure risk.

mitigations.description: Review whether archived records can be purged or anonymized sooner for records no longer needed for access-control or audit purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
mitigations.rationale: Shortening retention where feasible reduces the time personal data remains exposed.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of employee travel and payment data.
risks.evidence_quote: this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees
risks.rationale: PII in a travel and expense system can expose employees' identity and transaction details if mishandled.

risks.description: The system retains user information and billing-related data for long periods, increasing exposure if the data is later accessed improperly or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the amount of sensitive information available over time.

risks.description: The system analyzes traveler preferences and retains them for future reference, which can reveal personal travel habits and preferences beyond immediate business needs.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference profiling can create a persistent record of personal behavior.

risks.description: Information is shared enterprise-wide and transmitted to another financial system, increasing the number of places where data could be exposed or accessed by unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Broader sharing expands the attack surface and the risk of improper access.

risks.description: Authorized agency users and internal users access the same system, so role misconfiguration could allow users to see more personal data than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users. Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
risks.rationale: Shared access paths make least-privilege enforcement critical.

risks.description: The system is accessible through web browsers and mobile applications, which increases the risk of interception or compromise of travel data during remote access.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: Remote and mobile access can expose data if endpoint or session protections fail.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of employee PII to only what is necessary for travel, expense, authorization, and payment processing, and restrict access to approved roles.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected is used for reservation, booking, authorization/obligation, and payment/voucher transactions for USDA mission critical TDY Travel.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and restricting access reduces exposure of employee PII.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA/USDA retention schedule and securely delete records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Retention limits and timely disposal reduce the amount of data at risk.

mitigations.description: Provide a way for travelers to review and update stored preferences and limit predictive profiling to travel-related settings only.
mitigations.rationale: User control and scope limitation reduce unnecessary retention of personal preference data.

mitigations.description: Continue to validate authorization and voucher data before transmission and encrypt all data sent to FMMI and other recipients in transit.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and encryption lower the risk of improper or insecure data sharing.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege role assignments and periodically review restrictive roles to ensure users only access data needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Regular role review helps prevent overbroad access to personal information.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong transport security and session protections for browser and mobile access, including TLS and multifactor authentication.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport and authentication controls reduce the chance of interception or session compromise.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees, creating a direct privacy risk if that data is mishandled or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: This system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees, and therefore, a PIA is necessary.
risks.rationale: Any system that collects employee PII can cause privacy harm if access, use, or disclosure is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system retains user information and billing-related data for long periods, increasing the amount of time the information is exposed to misuse or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the window in which retained PII can be accessed improperly or compromised.

risks.description: The system analyzes traveler data to infer preferences and future choices, which can reveal behavioral patterns beyond the immediate travel transaction.
risks.evidence_quote: The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Predictive profiling can expose sensitive behavioral information and create privacy concerns if used beyond the traveler’s expectations.

risks.description: Travel authorization and voucher information is shared with another system for financial validation, which creates a disclosure risk during inter-system transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Transferring PII between systems expands the number of places where the data can be accessed or mishandled.

risks.description: The system is accessible through standard web browsers and mobile applications, which increases the risk of unauthorized access if endpoint security is weak or a device is lost or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: Multiple access methods broaden the attack surface and can expose data through compromised endpoints.

risks.description: The system is multi-tenant and enterprise-wide, so data from many customers and users shares the same platform, increasing the impact of any access-control failure.
risks.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
risks.rationale: A shared platform can expose more records if tenant isolation or role controls fail.

risks.description: Authorized users from different USDA agencies can access the system, so restrictive roles must be correctly implemented to prevent overbroad access to employee travel data.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-SS/FMS internal users. Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
risks.rationale: Broad user access combined with role-based permissions creates a risk of excessive internal visibility if roles are misconfigured.

risks.description: Session and communications security depend on multiple network and authentication controls, so any weakness in those controls could expose travel and PII data in transit.
risks.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer.
risks.rationale: If transport or session protections fail, intercepted communications could reveal sensitive travel information.

mitigations.description: Limit collection and display of employee PII to only the fields required for travel reservation, authorization, and payment processing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected is used for reservation, booking, authorization/obligation, and payment/voucher transactions for USDA mission critical TDY Travel.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing collected data reduces the amount of PII that could be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA and USDA records schedule and delete retained records as soon as the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal limits how long sensitive records remain available for unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Provide travelers with a clear notice and opt-out or control over profile-based preference retention and predictive use.
mitigations.rationale: User control over profiling reduces privacy concerns from inferred preferences and behavioral analysis.

mitigations.description: Continue to validate authorization and voucher data before transmission and restrict the shared fields to only what FMMI needs for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and data minimization reduce the chance of inaccurate or unnecessary disclosure during system-to-system transfer.

mitigations.description: Require strong device security for mobile access, such as MFA and secure session controls, and restrict access from noncompliant devices.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication
mitigations.rationale: Endpoint and session protections lower the chance that browser or mobile access is abused.

mitigations.description: Maintain and test tenant-isolation controls so data from one tenant cannot be accessed by another tenant or customer.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
mitigations.rationale: Strong tenant separation is necessary to prevent cross-tenant privacy exposure in a shared cloud platform.

mitigations.description: Regularly review and recertify restrictive roles to ensure USDA agency users only receive the minimum access needed for their duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps prevent unnecessary internal access to employee travel records.

mitigations.description: Enforce TLS 1.2 for all data transfers and monitor session integrity to detect tampering or interception attempts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas. SAP Concur controls and protects session authenticity at the Transport Layer.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport encryption and session protection reduce the risk of disclosure while data is in transit.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, including Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, and check information, which creates a risk of identity theft or financial fraud if exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: The more sensitive identifiers and banking details the system holds, the greater the harm if unauthorized access occurs.

risks.description: The system maintains personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies, creating a privacy risk of unauthorized access to employee records across agencies.
risks.evidence_quote: The purpose and routine use of the data include recording, processing, and reporting the personnel and payroll data for USDA and other Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Cross-agency personnel data increases the number of people and systems that may access the information.

risks.description: The system supports debt collection and displays delinquent debts to Treasury, which can expose individuals to sensitive financial status disclosure beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks. The following types of information are collected and maintained: batch jobs processing details (Scheduling Information Tracking System); Name and payment information about accounts receivable (Document Tracking System) (DOTS), informational display system of delinquent debts to Treasury (Salary Offset Agency Process (SOAP) and statistical data about documents processed by NFC (Statistical Tabulation Analysis (STAT).
risks.rationale: Debt-related information is particularly sensitive because it can reveal financial distress or obligations.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains date of birth, address, and personal identification numbers, which increases the risk of unnecessary retention of personal identifiers if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: The data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information).
risks.rationale: Basic identity attributes can be combined to profile or re-identify individuals if improperly accessed.

risks.description: The system retains data for 10 years, which increases the amount of time personal information remains exposed to breach, misuse, or outdated access.
risks.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which stored personal data can be compromised.

risks.description: The system is used to automate redundant tasks and process batch jobs, which can create privacy risk if automated processing propagates errors or exposes more records than necessary during routine operations.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: Automation can increase the scale of any mistake or unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: The system gathers statistical information and statistical data about documents processed by NFC, which could create a risk of secondary use if statistics are linked back to individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: These applications are used by NFC to aid in debt collection, gather statistical information, and/or to simplify/automate redundant tasks.
risks.rationale: Statistical uses can become privacy-invasive if data is not properly aggregated or de-identified.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, and check information to only staff with a documented need to know, and encrypt these fields at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting the most sensitive fields reduces the chance of identity theft or financial fraud.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and interagency data-sharing agreements that limit personnel and payroll access to authorized users only.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter authorization reduces the risk that cross-agency personnel records are viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Minimize disclosure of delinquent debt information to only the minimum necessary fields and recipients needed for debt collection.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is shared reduces the sensitivity of any debt-related disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization and periodic review to remove personal identifiers that are not necessary for the administrative function.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting and keeping fewer identifiers lowers the chance of unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Enforce the approved retention schedule with automated deletion or secure disposal when the 10-year period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data contained in this system is covered by NFC Schedule NC1-16-78-6, which identifies a retention period of 10 years.
mitigations.rationale: Deleting data when no longer needed reduces long-term exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Add quality checks and access logging around batch and automated processing so errors and unusual access can be detected quickly.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring automated processing helps catch privacy-impacting mistakes before they spread.

mitigations.description: Use aggregation or de-identification for statistical reporting so individuals cannot be readily identified from the statistics.
mitigations.rationale: De-identifying statistical outputs limits the chance of re-identification from analytics results.

risks.description: The system retains case-related information, including personally identifiable information and audio files, forever, which creates a long-term exposure risk if the data is no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the chance that sensitive data will be exposed, misused, or kept beyond its useful purpose.

risks.description: The system stores direct identifiers and contact details, so a breach could expose appellants' identities and ways to reach them.
risks.evidence_quote: Personally Identifiable Information (P11) such as full name, address, phone number, fax number, email address, and signature.
risks.rationale: These fields are sufficient to identify and contact individuals and are sensitive if disclosed improperly.

risks.description: The system stores audio files and case determinations, which may reveal detailed personal or case-specific information beyond basic contact data.
risks.evidence_quote: NAD case-related data: • Audio files and case determinations
risks.rationale: Audio recordings and determinations can contain more sensitive context than ordinary administrative records.

risks.description: Public users can submit appeals and then view their own appeal transaction details and submitted documents, which increases the risk of unauthorized disclosure if account access is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The public are permitted to file appeals electronically. After they register and file an appeal electronically, customers receive electronic notifications that the appeal was received. Further, an eFiling appellant can log into his or her eFile portal and view the transaction of the appeal request and the documents the appellant submitted.
risks.rationale: Self-service access to case information depends on account security, so account compromise could expose appeal records.

risks.description: Authorized users include USDA employees and contractor employees, so multiple user groups with access can increase the chance of improper access or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack authorized users enter the data submitted to the USDA Office of Hearings and Appeals -National Appeals Division. These authorized users are USDA employees, contractor employees who access the system via eAuthentication, and the public who eFile appeal requests.
risks.rationale: Broader access across employee and contractor groups expands the number of people who can view sensitive case data.

risks.description: Reports generated from the system may expose personally identifiable information to management, creating an internal disclosure risk even when no external sharing occurs.
risks.evidence_quote: NADTrack generates reports of information which is reviewed by OHA-NAD management. All reports with PII display a PII warning.
risks.rationale: PII warnings reduce but do not eliminate the risk that reports containing personal data will be viewed or handled inappropriately.

risks.description: The system is used for case tracking and reporting, so it may collect and maintain detailed process metadata that can reveal an individual's appeal history and status over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Metadata relating to the case process (e.g. date case was filed)
risks.rationale: Case-process metadata can be sensitive because it reveals when a person engaged with the appeals process and how the case progressed.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce a records retention schedule that limits storage to the minimum period necessary and disposes of data when no longer required.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to direct identifiers and contact details to only personnel with a documented need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access lowers the chance of unnecessary viewing or misuse of identifying data.

mitigations.description: Apply stronger access controls and review procedures for audio files and determinations, with separate handling for especially sensitive case content.
mitigations.rationale: Extra controls help protect the most revealing case records from inappropriate access.

mitigations.description: Use strong account authentication and session protection for appellant portal access, and require secure password reset and account recovery procedures.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting user accounts reduces the chance that outsiders can access appeal records through the portal.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary functions and periodically review contractor permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: OHA hires contract employees who have the same access requirements and controls as federal employees (i.e. via eAuthentication).
mitigations.rationale: Permission reviews and least-privilege access reduce the privacy impact of having both employees and contractors in the system.

mitigations.description: Keep the PII warning on reports and add handling rules that require users to verify need before opening or sharing reports containing PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All reports with PII display a PII warning.
mitigations.rationale: Warnings are more effective when paired with clear handling requirements for sensitive reports.

mitigations.description: Minimize and protect case-process metadata by collecting only what is needed for tracking and reporting and limiting who can view it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Case Tracking and Reporting
mitigations.rationale: Reducing and restricting metadata limits the amount of case history that can be inferred from the system.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and payroll information, including names, SSNs, time and attendance data, teleworking agreement information, and payroll data, creating a risk of harm if the data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The application consists of (name, SSN and time and attendance, information included in teleworking agreements), and payroll data needed to conform to all applicable laws, Government regulations and procedures, and the needs of the Department and agencies in carrying out their personnel management responsibilities.
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the stored data, the greater the privacy impact if access controls or transmission protections fail.

risks.description: Because HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf, the system risks inaccurate or incomplete records being created or updated without the individual directly reviewing the entry.
risks.evidence_quote: HR staff may enter information on an individual’s behalf.
risks.rationale: Third-party entry can introduce errors or omissions that affect the accuracy of personnel and payroll records.

risks.description: The system allows agencies and individuals to run predefined and custom reports, which creates a risk of broader internal disclosure than necessary if report access is not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
risks.rationale: Reporting features can expose more data to more users than is needed for their duties.

risks.description: WebTA shares customer data with multiple other USDA systems, which increases the risk that information will be disclosed beyond the original collection purpose if downstream access or use is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: NFC shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below. 1. EmpowHR: WebTA uses human resources data provided by EmpowHR. 2. Insight: WebTA generates files for transmission to the Insight hosting environment for processing. 3. OCIO eAuthentication (eAuth) application: The eAuthentication application provides authentication services for some WebTA customers. 4. TIME: WebTA transmits certified T&A data to the PPS TIME application.
risks.rationale: Each additional system connection creates another point where privacy safeguards must be preserved.

risks.description: The system permits external sharing outside USDA when allowed by customer agency policy and a SORN, which creates a risk of disclosure to parties the individual may not expect if agency controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, the sharing of PII outside the Department is compatible with the original collection and covered by a SORN. Please see Section 5.1 above.
risks.rationale: External sharing increases privacy risk because the data leaves the immediate control of USDA/NFC.

risks.description: Access is granted based on agency requests and role authorization, so there is a risk that excessive or inappropriate access could be approved if role definitions or approvals are insufficiently strict.
risks.evidence_quote: NFC grants authority to use/access WebTA to individual users at the request of the agencies approved by the user’s ASO.
risks.rationale: Access decisions driven by requests can lead to overbroad access unless least-privilege rules are rigorously enforced.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system if authorized, which creates a risk of privacy compromise if contractor access is not carefully limited and monitored.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized a valid role.
risks.rationale: Non-federal users can increase exposure of PII if their access is not constrained to specific duties.

risks.description: Although the system uses encrypted transmission, any failure to consistently require secure transfer methods for all exchanges could expose PII in transit.
risks.evidence_quote: Agencies submit data via Connect Direct and files transfers that use secure FTP over a VPN connection. The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
risks.rationale: Sensitive payroll and identity data needs strong transport protection on every transmission path.

risks.description: The system retains records under NARA schedules and customer agency requirements, which creates a risk of longer-than-necessary retention if those schedules are not applied correctly.
risks.evidence_quote: The retention periods of data contained in this system are covered by NARA Records Control Schedule. Civilian Personnel Records have various retention periods for specific types of data. These retention periods are adhered to per customer agency requirements and memorandum of understanding.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which records can be accessed, breached, or misused.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict access controls, encryption, and monitoring for SSNs, payroll data, and teleworking agreement information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The WebTA application uses 128-bit encryption HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Strong technical safeguards reduce the likelihood that highly sensitive data will be exposed.

mitigations.description: Require individuals to review and confirm records entered on their behalf, or provide a correction workflow before records are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: User review helps catch errors introduced by third-party data entry.

mitigations.description: Restrict predefined and custom reports to the minimum data elements needed and approve report access only for authorized roles.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individuals and agencies may run predefined and custom reports against the data and have the ability to access data elements depending on access privileges requested by authorized agency personnel.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report scope reduces unnecessary internal exposure of personal data.

mitigations.description: Apply system-to-system data-sharing agreements, access controls, and logging for each downstream USDA system that receives WebTA data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NFC shares our customers’ PPS data with other NFC MAs (Major Applications), as described below.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling each interface reduces the chance that shared data is reused beyond its intended purpose.

mitigations.description: Limit external disclosures to documented routine uses and agency-approved purposes, and verify that each recipient has an appropriate legal basis and safeguards.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, the sharing of PII outside the Department is compatible with the original collection and covered by a SORN.
mitigations.rationale: Documented limits and recipient safeguards help prevent unexpected external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use formal role-based access reviews to ensure each user receives only the minimum access needed for their job.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege reduces the chance of unnecessary access to PII.

mitigations.description: Apply the same least-privilege and periodic access review requirements to contractors as to federal staff.
mitigations.rationale: Contractor access should be constrained because contractors can otherwise broaden the exposure of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Require all agencies and systems to use approved secure transmission methods, such as SFTP over VPN or HTTPS, for every exchange of PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any information transmitted from PPS to external systems must be transmitted via secure transmission, such as SFTP, over a Virtual Private Network (VPN) or other secure transmission protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Mandatory secure transmission reduces the risk of interception during data transfer.

mitigations.description: Apply retention and disposal controls that automatically purge records when the approved NARA schedule or customer agency retention period expires.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of personal data retained and the associated exposure window.

risks.description: The system collects and stores direct contact information and inquiry details, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal data if the case system is compromised or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: • First Name of the person contacting USDA • Last Name of the person contacting USDA • Phone number of the person contacting USDA • Email address of the person contacting USDA • Address of the of the person contacting USDA • General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
