risks.rationale: These fields can identify a person and reveal the substance of their interaction with USDA.

risks.description: PII is shared internally by email to mission area subject-matter experts, which increases the chance of accidental misdelivery or interception during transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration
risks.rationale: Email transmission is a common point of exposure for misaddressed or improperly protected personal data.

risks.description: PII is accessible to all USDA users with valid Linc Pass credentials in the Salesforce Government Cloud environment, which may create overbroad access if roles are not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: PII data is only available through E-auth login of authorized users (all USDA users with a valid Linc Pass credentials) into the USDA contact center Salesforce Government Cloud Environment
risks.rationale: Broad authorized-user access can expose PII to personnel who do not need it for their duties.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which raises the risk of unnecessary exposure of PII beyond federal staff.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the population that can view or handle sensitive contact records.

risks.description: The system retains information for at least seven years, increasing the amount of personal data exposed over time if it is no longer needed for active casework.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained at minimum of 7 years.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window during which data can be accessed, breached, or misused.

risks.description: No purging or archiving is currently set up, so personal data may remain in active systems longer than necessary and accumulate without lifecycle controls.
risks.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival, since this is a pilot this will would be reassess after the pilot phase to get a better idea of data storage required.
risks.rationale: Without automated deletion or archival, records can persist unnecessarily and broaden exposure.

risks.description: The system uses multiple channels, including chat, email, webform, and telephony integration, which increases the risk of inconsistent collection practices and accidental disclosure across channels.
risks.evidence_quote: Customers can submit case inquiries through multiple channels: phone, email, chat and webform and government personnel can support all these channels through a single integrated platform
risks.rationale: More collection channels create more opportunities for privacy failures in handling and routing personal information.

risks.description: The system combines contact information with case history and account information, which can create a more detailed profile of an individual than the contact data alone.
risks.evidence_quote: General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
risks.rationale: Linking identity data with inquiry records increases the sensitivity of the stored profile.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to the minimum contact and case details needed to resolve the inquiry, and avoid storing unnecessary fields in the case record.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is being collected, used, and disseminated, or maintained to support external customer inquiry and responses.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less personal data reduces the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use a more secure approved transfer method than ordinary email for PII, or encrypt and restrict emailed records to named recipients only.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger transmission controls reduce the chance that PII is exposed in transit or sent to the wrong recipient.

mitigations.description: Narrow role-based access so users can view only the records needed for their assigned duties, with periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control. All internal AskUSDA access is managed through the USDA Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS).
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access limits the number of people who can see each record.

mitigations.description: Apply the same least-privilege controls and access approval process to contractors as to federal staff, and review contractor access regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, AskUSDA Contact Center Uses Role Based Access Control.
mitigations.rationale: Contractor access should be constrained to reduce unnecessary exposure of PII.

mitigations.description: Implement a records schedule that deletes or archives records as soon as the approved retention period expires.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is retained at minimum of 7 years.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of historical personal data at risk.

mitigations.description: Set up automated purging or archiving before the pilot ends and define a clear lifecycle rule for stored PII.
mitigations.rationale: Automated lifecycle controls prevent records from lingering in active systems without a purpose.

mitigations.description: Standardize privacy and security controls across all intake channels so each channel collects and transmits customer information consistently.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Customers can submit case inquiries through multiple channels: phone, email, chat and webform and government personnel can support all these channels through a single integrated platform
mitigations.rationale: Consistent controls across channels reduce the chance of channel-specific privacy gaps.

mitigations.description: Separate or minimize the linkage between contact data and case history when full identity linkage is not needed for resolution.
mitigations.evidence_quote: General Inquiry Case Information (Subject, Description – Inquiry Details/Case History, Case Number, Contact, Account, Nature of Inquiry)
mitigations.rationale: Reducing linkage lowers the sensitivity of the stored record set.

risks.description: The system records identifiable images of employees, contractors, and visitors as they move through USDA buildings, creating a broad surveillance risk. The footage can capture facial images and track people across entrances, exits, parking lots, and secured areas.
risks.evidence_quote: the Video Surveillance System is capturing and storing video footage of USDA employees, contractors and visitors as they enter and traverse the USDA NCR buildings.
risks.rationale: Continuous video collection in multiple facility areas can reveal who was present, when, and where they moved.

risks.description: The cameras may capture highly sensitive personal details beyond general video, including license plates and information from driver’s licenses. This increases the chance that the system collects more personal data than is strictly needed for security monitoring.
risks.evidence_quote: The video footage includes images of people, information found on drivers licenses such as full names, addresses, date of birth, as well as license plate numbers.
risks.rationale: Capturing detailed identifiers raises the privacy impact because the footage can directly identify individuals and their vehicles.

risks.description: The use of pan/tilt/zoom, manual tracking, and automatic tracking can enable persistent monitoring of specific individuals. That creates a risk of intrusive observation of people in public and workplace settings.
risks.evidence_quote: others use pan/tilt/zoom capability with manual tracking, which allows the individual monitoring with the VSS feed to adjust the camera in real time to gain the best image of any suspicious or illegal activity of interest that is occurring. Tracking, which can be manual or occur when the cameras automatically track people or other moving objects in the field of view is used so security personnel may follow the activity of a single individual within viewing areas that contain a large number of people.
risks.rationale: Tracking features make it possible to focus on a person over time rather than just record general area activity.

risks.description: The system may record people on public streets and around federal facilities, expanding surveillance beyond USDA-controlled interior spaces. This can affect bystanders who are not entering the buildings or otherwise expecting monitoring.
risks.evidence_quote: The cameras may record passersby on public streets and USDA personnel accessing a secured area.
risks.rationale: Recording people outside the facility perimeter increases the number of affected individuals and reduces their ability to avoid collection.

risks.description: Video footage can be shared outside USDA with federal agencies and local law enforcement, creating a disclosure risk. Once shared, the footage may be used for investigations, prosecutions, or other purposes beyond the original security monitoring context.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with external organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions Information from the VSS cameras will be used by federal agencies and local law enforcement to detect and respond to potentially unlawful activities in the areas surrounding federal facilities.
risks.rationale: External sharing increases the number of entities with access to identifiable footage and the chance of secondary use.

risks.description: Contractors and select non-employees may access the system, which creates insider access risk. Even with background checks and security clearances, broader access increases the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non- employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: More authorized users means more opportunities for inappropriate access to sensitive video records.

risks.description: Footage may be retained longer than the intended six months depending on storage, camera counts, and other factors. Extended retention increases the period during which people can be monitored or identified from historical footage.
risks.evidence_quote: the intent is a 6-month retention period for all video footage, however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer
risks.rationale: Longer retention expands the window in which sensitive recordings can be accessed, shared, or misused.

risks.description: Recordings retrieved for suspected criminal activity can be retained until investigative or enforcement action is completed, which may extend retention well beyond routine deletion. This creates a risk that footage linked to many people will remain available for an open-ended period.
risks.evidence_quote: Records which are retrieved pursuant to suspected criminal activity will be retained until any investigative or enforcement action is completed.
risks.rationale: Exception-based retention can keep sensitive video available for much longer than routine operational needs require.

mitigations.description: Limit camera placement and viewing angles to areas necessary for security, and continue avoiding locations where people have a reasonable expectation of privacy.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Cameras are not placed in places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as inside a bathroom or changing room.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting placement reduces unnecessary capture of people’s activities and identities.

mitigations.description: Mask or blur license plates and other nonessential identifying details in routine views, and restrict access to unredacted footage to authorized investigative staff only.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing visible identifiers lowers the privacy impact while preserving security uses.

mitigations.description: Require supervisory approval and documented justification before using manual or automatic tracking on an individual.
mitigations.rationale: Approval controls help ensure tracking is used only when needed for a specific security purpose.

mitigations.description: Configure cameras to minimize capture of public streets and other areas outside USDA facilities unless a specific security need exists.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The cameras may record passersby on public streets and USDA personnel accessing a secured area.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the field of view reduces collection of bystanders who are not part of the facility security mission.

mitigations.description: Use written sharing procedures that limit disclosures to formal requests and document the purpose, recipient, and footage released.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions
mitigations.rationale: Documented sharing controls help prevent unnecessary disclosure and secondary use.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and periodic access reviews for employees and contractors with VSS access.
mitigations.rationale: Tightening access to only those with a current need reduces the risk of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Enforce the six-month deletion schedule automatically and require approval for any extension beyond that period.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored for a maximum of six months and then is automatically deleted.
mitigations.rationale: Automatic deletion limits how long routine surveillance footage remains available.

mitigations.description: Require periodic review of criminal-activity holds to confirm the footage is still needed for an active investigation or enforcement action.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To retain the footage after the retention period, a supervisor must approve the request and confirm the recordings are relevant to actual or suspected criminal activity.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps prevent indefinite retention of footage kept under an exception.

risks.description: The system may collect limited PII in free-form feedback, creating a risk that customers disclose more personal information than intended. This increases the chance of unnecessary exposure of names, email addresses, and zip codes in feedback records.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Free-form fields can prompt or capture more personal data than the minimum needed for feedback collection.

risks.description: The system supports real-time collection and broad analysis of customer feedback across USDA mission areas, which can enable profiling or sensitive inference from feedback data. The stated uses include demographic and ethnographic analysis, which may reveal more about individuals or groups than they expect.
risks.evidence_quote: The data is structured or unstructured, solicited, or unsolicited feedback from customers through multiple channels
risks.rationale: Broad, multi-channel feedback combined with demographic analysis can create privacy risk even when direct identifiers are limited.

risks.description: A small number of users can access all data across all mission areas, creating elevated insider access risk. Centralized access increases the impact if a privileged user misuses or mishandles customer feedback or associated PII.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: Broader access by a few users increases the consequences of unauthorized viewing or misuse.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system, which raises the risk of unauthorized disclosure or secondary use if contractor access is not tightly controlled. The PIA does not describe contractor-specific restrictions beyond general role-based access.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Third-party access expands the number of people who may view sensitive feedback and PII.

risks.description: The system migrates data from multiple existing USDA tools into one cohesive platform, which increases the risk of over-collection, data merging, or retaining data longer than needed. Consolidation can also make it easier to link feedback across systems and mission areas.
risks.evidence_quote: appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
risks.rationale: Combining sources can increase identifiability and the blast radius of any privacy failure.

risks.description: The system uses dashboards and analytics to identify audience sizes, segments, and geographic, demographic, and ethnographic patterns, which can create re-identification or group-privacy risks. Even without PII in dashboards, small or unique segments may still be identifiable.
risks.evidence_quote: Gather customer insights and feedback geographically, demographically and ethnographically in order to identify areas in need of improvement
risks.rationale: Aggregated analytics can still expose sensitive patterns about small populations.

risks.description: The retention period has not been approved by the component records officer and NARA, creating a risk of improper or excessive retention. Without approved retention controls, records may be kept longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Unapproved retention increases the chance that data is held beyond lawful or necessary timeframes.

risks.description: Although the system says PII will not be shared outside the VoC system, internal sharing of aggregated dashboards still creates a residual disclosure risk if aggregation is insufficient or if unauthorized users gain access. The PIA also notes that PII will not be included in dashboards, but that does not eliminate risk from underlying data access.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards. PII will not be included in these dashboards.
risks.rationale: Aggregation reduces risk, but weak aggregation or unauthorized access can still expose personal information indirectly.

mitigations.description: Minimize free-form PII collection by using clear prompts, field validation, and notices that discourage unnecessary personal details; collect contact information only when a follow-up is requested.
mitigations.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; • Zip Code.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing optional PII collection lowers the amount of personal data stored in feedback records.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and suppress or redact sensitive details before analysis, especially for demographic and ethnographic reporting.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Gather customer insights and feedback geographically, demographically and ethnographically in order to identify areas in need of improvement
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is analyzed and reported reduces the chance of sensitive inference from feedback data.

mitigations.description: Restrict all-data access to the smallest possible set of users, require documented approval for elevated access, and review those privileges regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
mitigations.rationale: Tight privilege controls reduce insider exposure across mission areas.

mitigations.description: Impose contractor-specific access controls, including least-privilege permissions, background/role checks as applicable, and periodic access recertification.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Contractor access should be limited and reviewed because it expands the set of users who can see feedback data.

mitigations.description: Perform a data inventory and mapping before migration, and exclude any fields that are not needed for the VoC purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: appropriate steps will be taken to migrate existing USDA tools (SalesForce, AskUSDA, EDAPT) or collect data in one cohesive VoC product.
mitigations.rationale: Inventorying migrated data helps prevent unnecessary merging and retention of personal information.

mitigations.description: Use aggregation thresholds and suppress small-cell reporting in dashboards so that unique individuals or small groups cannot be singled out.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information collected in the Voice of the Customer platform will be shared internally within USDA as an aggregated representation of data depicted in visual dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Thresholds and suppression reduce the chance that aggregated analytics reveal identifiable patterns.

mitigations.description: Obtain records schedule approval from the component records officer and NARA and document the approved retention and deletion process.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
mitigations.rationale: Approved retention schedules ensure records are kept and deleted according to lawful requirements.

mitigations.description: Limit dashboard access to authorized users only and verify that aggregation rules prevent indirect identification before reports are released.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII will not be included in these dashboards.
mitigations.rationale: Even aggregated outputs need access controls and disclosure review to prevent indirect exposure.

risks.description: The system stores PII in a third-party cloud service that is hosted outside the USDA component boundary, which increases the risk of unauthorized access or exposure by the vendor environment.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Hosting PII outside the agency boundary creates an added privacy exposure surface that must be controlled through strong vendor and access safeguards.

risks.description: Users and contractors must provide mandatory identity fields to create accounts, so individuals cannot decline or minimize the PII collected for access.
risks.evidence_quote: No First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Mandatory collection of identity data increases privacy impact because the system does not allow data minimization at enrollment.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains contact information, including names, email addresses, and contact numbers, which could be exposed if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Workiva Wdesk collects name, email address, and contact numbers.
risks.rationale: Contact information is personally identifying and can be misused if improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Because the system is used to create and publish the Annual Financial Report and the document is described as publicly accessible, there is a risk that user-associated information could be exposed through public reporting content or metadata.
risks.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data. No, the data used on wDesk will be for the USDA Annual Financial Report. This information contains information that is mandated to be available to the public.
risks.rationale: Public-facing documents can inadvertently reveal more personal information than intended if content is not carefully reviewed.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which expands the number of people who can view or handle PII and increases insider-access risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
risks.rationale: Broader user populations increase the chance of inappropriate access, misuse, or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: Access can be granted with supervisor or higher-level approval, which may create inconsistent access decisions if approvals are not tightly controlled and reviewed.
risks.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
risks.rationale: Approval-based access can lead to overprovisioning unless the process is standardized and audited.

risks.description: The system retains information for 75 months, which prolongs the period during which PII could be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
risks.rationale: Longer retention extends the window of privacy risk and increases the importance of secure storage and deletion controls.

mitigations.description: Require and regularly assess vendor security controls for the cloud environment, including contractual privacy safeguards, access restrictions, and audit review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Wdesk is a third party hosted cloud-based solution. Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
mitigations.rationale: A hosted third-party environment needs explicit security and privacy controls to reduce exposure outside the agency boundary.

mitigations.description: Limit mandatory account fields to the minimum needed for provisioning and document why each required field is necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing required fields lowers the amount of PII collected at account setup.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and periodic access reviews so only authorized users can view contact information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The system contains automated workflows that can be customized to provide a minimum level of compliant access.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the minimum necessary helps protect stored contact information from unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Review documents before publication to ensure no unnecessary personal information or user metadata is included in public-facing materials.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data.
mitigations.rationale: Pre-publication review helps prevent accidental disclosure in documents intended for public access.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to only the functions and records needed for their assigned work and log their activity for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access reduces the privacy risk created by a larger user population.

mitigations.description: Require documented approval criteria and periodic audits of supervisor-granted access to detect overprovisioning.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other levels of access can be granted with supervisor approval or approval from a higher-level authority.
mitigations.rationale: Formal review of approval decisions helps ensure access is justified and consistent.

mitigations.description: Enforce retention and secure deletion controls so records are purged when the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 75 Months = 6.25 Years
mitigations.rationale: Deleting records when no longer needed reduces the time PII remains exposed in the system.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, including SSNs, TINs, handwritten signatures, salary data, and legal names, creating a significant risk if that information is exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: This information may include the vendor’s name, address, email IDs, and SSN/TIN.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly maintains direct identifiers and financial details that would be harmful if disclosed.

risks.description: GIMS information may be shared outside USDA with a wide range of external parties, increasing the risk of over-disclosure of applicant and awardee information.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS award results related information can be shared with a number of external parties, including, but not limited to, non-profit organizations, state and local organizations, individuals, corporations, and entities outside the US.
risks.rationale: Broad external sharing expands the number of recipients who could further disclose or mishandle the data.

risks.description: Information can be transmitted or disclosed in common office formats or on paper, which increases the risk of accidental forwarding, printing loss, or unauthorized copying.
risks.evidence_quote: The information as noted in 4.1 may be disclosed electronically via an Excel, Word, PDF document, or via hard copy.
risks.rationale: Using easily copied formats and hard copy creates more opportunities for unintended disclosure.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system for backup, support, account management, and file retrieval, which creates a risk of broader insider access to sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: • Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; • Back-Up of files and data; • Application and database support; • Account management; and • Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Contractor access increases the number of people who can view or handle personal data.

risks.description: The system receives data from external sources and manually entered user data, so inaccurate or mismatched information could lead to incorrect records, decisions, or disclosures about individuals and vendors.
risks.evidence_quote: Also other sources of data are entered by USDA FNS employees who have been approved for FNS FM-GSS access.
risks.rationale: Multiple input paths increase the chance that incorrect personal data will be stored and then reused.

risks.description: FMAT uses automated matching logic to identify vendors and create new vendor records, which could misassociate a collection with the wrong person or create an incorrect identity record.
risks.evidence_quote: AEROS is a custom solution providing the repository and mechanism for users to identify and match incoming collections to the appropriate customer and accounts receivable (AR) document.
risks.rationale: Automated matching based on personal data can produce false matches that affect the wrong individual.

risks.description: GIMS produces reports containing applicant, grantee, and award information, so reporting can expose more personal and organizational detail than is necessary for the immediate task.
risks.evidence_quote: Data that may be produced by GIMS includes the following: • Application data contained within the standard federal forms including SF-424, SF- 424A, , Farm to School coversheet and SF-LLL
risks.rationale: Reports can aggregate sensitive data into a format that is easier to distribute or misuse.

risks.description: The system retains records for years after closeout or final payment, which increases the duration of exposure to privacy incidents and unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
risks.rationale: Long retention keeps personal data available for a longer period, extending the risk window.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive fields such as SSNs, TINs, signatures, salary data, and legal names to only personnel with a documented need to know, and keep those fields encrypted at rest and in transit.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and using encryption reduces the chance that direct identifiers are exposed.

mitigations.description: Require case-by-case approval before any external disclosure and limit sharing to the minimum information needed for the approved purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Transmissions/disclosures typically require approval by the Grants Director.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and minimization help prevent unnecessary external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use secure electronic distribution controls such as access-restricted portals or encrypted file transfer instead of email attachments or paper whenever possible.
mitigations.rationale: More controlled delivery methods reduce the chance of accidental disclosure through common file formats or hard copy.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role-based access for contractors and review contractor access regularly for appropriateness.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GIMS also has the capability to check-in/check-out documents; manage version control for simple and compound documents; track audit trails; perform comprehensive searches; and manage user, group, and role-based access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege access limits contractor exposure to only the records needed for support tasks.

mitigations.description: Validate incoming and manually entered data before it is stored or used in reports, and reconcile records against authoritative source systems.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and reconciliation reduce the chance that incorrect personal information is stored or disclosed.

mitigations.description: Require human review of automated vendor matches before any collection is finalized or a new vendor record is created.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It provides a user interface for AR processors to view AR and collection-related data gathered from various systems, confirm data matches made by the system, and track and report on the status of collections throughout their lifecycle.
mitigations.rationale: Human confirmation helps catch false matches that could affect the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and redaction to reports so that only the fields needed for the recipient's role are included.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications.
mitigations.rationale: Redaction and minimization reduce the amount of personal information exposed in reports.

mitigations.description: Enforce the stated retention schedule and securely dispose of records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal limits how long personal data remains available for misuse or breach.

risks.description: The system creates a centralized database of detailed and sensitive SNAP participant information, which increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach. A single compromise could expose personal, transactional, and financial data for many participants across states.
risks.evidence_quote: SNAP participant data to be contained in the SNAP Information Database will include detailed and sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed, as well as financial data (e.g., amount of beneﬁt received).
risks.rationale: Centralizing sensitive data raises the harm from any security failure because more information is exposed at once.

risks.description: The system collects historical data from all participants since 2000, creating a large-scale repository of long-retained personal information that may exceed what is needed for current fraud checks. Long lookback periods increase privacy exposure even for people no longer actively interacting with the program.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Collecting extensive historical data increases the amount of personal information held and the time it remains exposed to risk.

risks.description: Automated matching and integrity checks can generate false positives that wrongly label participants as ineligible, duplicate, or fraudulent. Such errors can lead to inappropriate investigation or adverse action against individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Integrity checks will be executed using automated scripts and queries on the compiled database, using matching algorithms to minimize false positives.
risks.rationale: Automated data matching can misidentify people when records are incomplete or inconsistent.

risks.description: The system performs immigration status checks, which can reveal highly sensitive information about a person's immigration status and may create heightened privacy and stigma risks. This information is especially sensitive because it is used as part of eligibility verification.
risks.evidence_quote: verifying immigration status eligibility
risks.rationale: Immigration status is sensitive personal information and can have serious consequences if disclosed or misused.

risks.description: The system conducts inter-agency data matches and shares information with state agencies when needed for investigations, increasing the number of entities that can access participant data. More sharing expands the chance of unauthorized disclosure or secondary use beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient or matching partner increases privacy risk because more systems and people handle the data.

risks.description: States transmit participant data through secure file transfer tools and via EBT processors, creating multiple transmission and integration points where data could be intercepted or mishandled. Any weakness in these interfaces could expose sensitive participant information during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Data will be sent via the secure MoveIt or Box managed ﬁle transfer application.
risks.rationale: Data moving between organizations and systems is exposed to transfer and integration risks.

mitigations.description: Restrict database access to authorized personnel only, use strong role-based access controls, and encrypt the database and backups at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and protecting stored data reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply a data minimization and retention schedule that limits collection to the minimum historical period needed for integrity checks and deletes data when no longer required.
mitigations.rationale: Keeping less historical data for less time reduces the volume of personal information exposed to risk.

mitigations.description: Require human review before any adverse action or investigative referral based on an automated match, and provide a process to correct mismatched records.
mitigations.rationale: Human verification and correction procedures reduce the harm caused by false positives.

mitigations.description: Limit immigration-status access to staff with a specific need to know and log each access to that data for oversight and auditing.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access and auditability reduce unnecessary exposure of highly sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and purpose limitations that restrict inter-agency and state use of participant data to the stated integrity checks and investigations only.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limits help prevent broader secondary use once the data is shared.

mitigations.description: Validate secure file transfer configurations, monitor transfers for anomalies, and require integrity checks on received files before ingestion.
mitigations.rationale: Transfer controls and file validation reduce the chance that data is intercepted, altered, or mishandled in transit.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information about affiliates, including names, business addresses, contact information, and Affiliate IDs, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of identity and contact data.
risks.evidence_quote: • Names, business address and contact information, and Affiliate ID of Contractors, Conservation District employees, State/Local Government employees, Resource Conservation & Development Council employees, Volunteers, Lenders, County Committees, Technical Service Providers, and non-profit outreach organization personnel (referred to as Affiliates).
risks.rationale: Any system that maintains PII can expose individuals if access controls or handling are insufficient.

risks.description: Because NRCS employees manually enter affiliate information provided by the affiliate, there is a risk of transcription or input errors that could lead to inaccurate records and improper access decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: • An NRCS employee enters the information about the individual non-employee affiliate, which is populated from information that was provided by the non-employee.
risks.rationale: Manual data entry increases the chance that records will not exactly match what the affiliate provided.

risks.description: The system links the affiliate record to a Level 2 eAuthentication account and shares information with zRoles to assign roles, creating a risk that incorrect linkage or role assignment could grant inappropriate access to NRCS systems.
risks.evidence_quote: • The affiliate's (non-employee's) Level 2 eAuthentication (eAuth) account is linked to the affiliate record. The zRoles application is then used to assign specific roles to the Level 2 account, which allows the affiliate access to various NRCS applications.
risks.rationale: If the linkage or role assignment is wrong, access privileges may be granted to the wrong person or at the wrong level.

risks.description: The system retains affiliate records for long periods, which increases the risk that outdated or no-longer-needed PII will remain exposed or be used beyond the current relationship.
risks.evidence_quote: • All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017. • Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs”.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window during which records can be accessed, breached, or kept after they are no longer needed.

risks.description: Only NRCS employees can access the system, but the context does not describe specific technical safeguards for that access, creating a risk of unauthorized internal access or misuse by insiders.
risks.evidence_quote: • The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
risks.rationale: Limiting access to employees is not by itself a complete safeguard against insider misuse or overbroad access.

risks.description: The system relies on information provided directly by affiliates to an NRCS employee, which creates a risk that inaccurate or incomplete source information will be stored and used for authorization decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: • Individual affiliates provide their information to an NRCS employee with the appropriate system access to the Affiliates application. The NRCS employee enters the information.
risks.rationale: If the original information is incomplete or wrong, the stored record and downstream access decisions may also be wrong.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to affiliate records to authorized NRCS employees with role-based access controls and audit logging for all views and changes.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access and accountability reduce the chance that stored PII is improperly viewed or altered.

mitigations.description: Add a validation step where affiliates confirm their entered information before it is used for access control determinations.
mitigations.rationale: User confirmation helps catch transcription errors before they affect records or access decisions.

mitigations.description: Require a secondary review or approval before linking an eAuth account and assigning roles in zRoles.
mitigations.rationale: Independent review lowers the chance that an incorrect linkage or role assignment will grant improper access.

mitigations.description: Apply records-management controls to purge or archive affiliate data as soon as the approved retention period expires.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? • Yes
mitigations.rationale: Approved retention should be paired with timely disposition so records are not kept longer than authorized.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic access reviews for NRCS employee accounts that can access the Affiliates system.
mitigations.rationale: Regular reviews help ensure only employees with a current need retain access.

mitigations.description: Verify affiliate-provided information against supporting documentation before it is entered into the system.
mitigations.rationale: Checking source information before entry improves record accuracy and reduces downstream authorization errors.

risks.description: The system stores and makes accessible a large amount of personally identifiable information, creating a broad exposure risk if the warehouse or web application is compromised. The data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, tax IDs, policy numbers, and agent and adjuster Social Security numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted because of the vast amount of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) that is accessed through the BAD Data Warehouse.
risks.rationale: A large concentration of sensitive data increases the impact of unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: The system contains highly sensitive identifiers and financial insurance details that could cause harm if disclosed. This includes tax IDs, Social Security numbers, policy numbers, indemnity, liability, and premium information.
risks.evidence_quote: Policy data includes name, address, phone number, policy number, unit, Approved Insurance Provider (AIP), crop, insurance plan, coverage level, indemnity, liability, premium, fund placement, acres, agent name, agent social security number, adjuster name, adjuster social security number, and etc.
risks.rationale: Sensitive identifiers and financial details are especially damaging if exposed or misused.

risks.description: The system centralizes data from multiple years and sources into a single production database, which increases the risk of large-scale disclosure if access controls fail. Consolidation makes the warehouse a high-value target and can amplify the effect of any breach.
risks.evidence_quote: Although the RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years, it is moved to a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
risks.rationale: Centralizing data increases the amount of information available from one compromise.

risks.description: Authorized users outside the core administering organization can access the data, which creates a risk of overbroad disclosure or secondary misuse. Access is provided to USDA internal users and external Approved Insurance Providers for reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs. AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond the system owner increases the number of parties that must be trusted.

risks.description: The web application used to disseminate the data creates a risk of unauthorized access if authentication or authorization is misconfigured or bypassed. Users can reach the system through an extranet URL and must authenticate to gain access.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA and Approved Insurance Provider (AIP) HyDRA are accessible via caehydralink which resides on the RMA Extranet. An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
risks.rationale: Any web-accessible system with sensitive data depends heavily on strong access control.

risks.description: The system retains the information for the life of the project, which increases the duration of exposure and the chance that data will be used beyond the original operational need. Long retention also increases the amount of historical personal data available over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA. The information received is used in the data mining and data warehousing for the agency. The data is maintained for historical analysis, thus is retained for the life of the project.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which data can be breached or repurposed.

risks.description: The system uses data for data mining and fraud detection, which creates a risk of secondary use beyond the original source collection if governance is weak. Individuals do not provide the data directly to BAD, so they may not expect these downstream analytic uses.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program. The objective is to provide tools, information, and analysis proven effective in the private sector in reducing insurance waste, fraud, and abuse.
risks.rationale: Analytic reuse can broaden the privacy impact if limits on use are not tightly enforced.

risks.description: The warehouse includes precise location data for farm land, which can reveal sensitive property or production information about individuals or entities. CLU data contains latitude and longitude coordinates.
risks.evidence_quote: Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc.
risks.rationale: Precise geolocation can make records easier to identify and can expose sensitive operational details.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the minimum set of authorized users needed for each function and enforce strong role-based access controls with periodic access reviews.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the number of people who can see the large PII set.

mitigations.description: Mask or redact Social Security numbers, tax IDs, and other direct identifiers in reports and user-facing views unless a user has a documented need for the full value.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of direct identifiers lowers the harm from unauthorized viewing or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Separate datasets by year or purpose and limit cross-year access to users with a demonstrated need, rather than keeping all years in one broadly accessible production database.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Although the RMA data is maintained in separate annual databases by years, it is moved to a single production database within the BAD data warehouse.
mitigations.rationale: Segmentation reduces the amount of data exposed if one account or query is compromised.

mitigations.description: Apply policy-based access controls so AIPs can only retrieve policy-specific records needed for reporting, and log and review all external-user access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: AIPs are only allowed access to data associated with their policies for the purpose of reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Narrowing external access and auditing it helps prevent overdisclosure.

mitigations.description: Require multi-factor authentication and regular security testing for HyDRA and the extranet access path, including review of authentication and authorization settings.
mitigations.evidence_quote: An eAuthentication account as well as HyDRA authentication are required to gain access to this web URL.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and testing reduce the chance of unauthorized web access.

mitigations.description: Define and enforce data minimization and deletion schedules for analytic copies so records are not kept longer than necessary for approved historical analysis.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the time window in which personal data can be exposed.

mitigations.description: Document and approve specific secondary uses for the warehouse data, and periodically review whether each analytic use still aligns with the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is used to provide resources, training, and research for data warehousing and data mining of FSA and RMA data for the Federal Crop Insurance Program.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose review helps ensure data mining stays within authorized uses.

mitigations.description: Limit the precision of location data in routine outputs and reports unless exact coordinates are necessary for a validated claim review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Crop data includes state, county, crop, crop type, irrigation practice, intended use, share, field, and common land unit (CLU) which contains latitude and longitude, and etc.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing location precision lowers the risk of revealing sensitive farm-level details.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains identifiable user profile information, including names and work contact details, creating a privacy risk if those records are exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Privacy related information is collected and maintained by CoLab in 'profiles' that include the individual's name and work contact information.
risks.rationale: Any system that stores identifiable profile data can create privacy harm if access controls fail or the data is otherwise compromised.

risks.description: Some profiles may include personal contact information beyond basic work identity, increasing the sensitivity of the stored data.
risks.evidence_quote: For some individuals, personal contact information is maintained in their profile.
risks.rationale: Additional contact details expand the amount of personal information associated with each user.

risks.description: CoLab uses eAuthentication data to establish user profiles, so inaccurate or outdated identity data could be copied into the system and affect access or profile integrity.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile.
risks.rationale: When profile data is sourced from another system, any errors in that source can propagate into CoLab.

risks.description: Users can modify their own profiles, which creates a risk that unauthorized or incorrect changes could be made to personal information if the update process is not properly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Self-service updates can affect data accuracy and integrity if identity verification or change controls are weak.

risks.description: Authorized contractors and partners have access to the system, increasing the number of people who can view or handle personal information and raising insider misuse risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Broader access populations increase the chance of inappropriate viewing or handling of personal data.

risks.description: The system is Internet-based, which increases exposure to external attack or unauthorized access if web security is not strong.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab is the Internet-based "Collaborative Software Development Laboratory,"
risks.rationale: Internet-facing systems generally have a larger attack surface than non-networked systems.

risks.description: PII is retained for as long as the application remains in production, which can create unnecessary long-term retention risk if data is not deleted promptly when no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific PII information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the time window in which personal data can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: Although the system says accounts are disabled when users leave, disabled accounts may still leave residual personal data in the system unless deletion is also performed.
risks.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
risks.rationale: Disabling access does not necessarily remove stored personal information.

mitigations.description: Limit profile fields to the minimum necessary and restrict access to profile data to only authorized users with a need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab contains a minimal amount of contact information related to CoLab users.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored data and access reduces the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Do not collect or store personal contact information unless it is strictly required for the user's role, and periodically review whether those fields remain necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing optional personal contact details lowers sensitivity and privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Validate eAuth-derived identity data against authoritative records before creating or updating a profile.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps prevent inaccurate identity data from being imported into CoLab.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and audit logging for self-service profile changes, and review changes for unusual activity.
mitigations.rationale: Controls around self-service updates help prevent unauthorized or erroneous edits.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access control so contractors and partners can only access the specific records needed for their assigned tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access by role reduces the number of people who can see personal information.

mitigations.description: Harden the Internet-facing application and web portal with standard server and portal security configurations and continuous monitoring.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab is an NRCS application hosted on devices using common COTS hardware and software configured in accordance with USDA baseline configurations for servers and web portals.
mitigations.rationale: Baseline security configuration is a core control for reducing exposure of web-based systems.

mitigations.description: Delete or erase application-specific PII as soon as it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Prompt deletion shortens the period during which stored personal data can be exposed.

mitigations.description: When a user leaves, disable the account and also remove or anonymize the associated profile data unless retention is still required.
mitigations.rationale: Account disabling alone does not eliminate the privacy risk from retained personal data.

risks.description: IDEA stores vendor names and contact information in the DataMart, which creates a risk of unauthorized access to maintained PII if the repository is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Persisting PII in a data store increases exposure beyond purely transient processing.

risks.description: IDEA uses read-only web service calls to pull vendor PII from SCIMS, creating a risk that the data could be intercepted or exposed during retrieval.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of these financial reports contain vendor PH that is obtained from the Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS) system via read-only web service calls.
risks.rationale: Any data transfer path can expose PII if transport protections are weak or misconfigured.

risks.description: The application allows reports to be produced using selectable criteria from drop-down menus, which can enable broad internal access to vendor PII through report generation.
risks.evidence_quote: While IDEA does not process any transactions, the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
risks.rationale: Flexible report criteria can reveal more personal data than necessary if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Department contractors have access to the system, so vendor PII may be exposed to additional personnel beyond NRCS employees.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases the number of people who can view sensitive data.

risks.description: PII is refreshed periodically from SCIMS, so stale or inaccurate vendor information could persist between updates and be used in reports.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Periodic refreshes leave a window where outdated data may remain available.

risks.description: Because the system retains application-specific information while it remains in production, vendor PII stored in the DataMart may be kept longer than necessary if deletion is not timely.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the time period during which data could be accessed or misused.

mitigations.description: Limit DataMart retention of vendor PII to the minimum needed for reporting and apply strong access controls to the stored records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored PII and restricting access reduces the impact of a DataMart compromise.

mitigations.description: Protect SCIMS web-service calls with encrypted transport and authenticated service-to-service connections.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the retrieval channel reduces the chance that vendor PII is exposed in transit.

mitigations.description: Restrict report criteria and outputs to the least amount of vendor PII needed for the specific business purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting selectable criteria and output fields reduces unnecessary disclosure through reporting.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and periodic access reviews for contractors who can use the system.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and periodic review help ensure contractors only see data required for their duties.

mitigations.description: Synchronize vendor PII from SCIMS on a defined schedule and validate that refreshed records replace outdated values.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
mitigations.rationale: Regular, validated refreshes reduce the risk that stale information is used in reports.

mitigations.description: Delete or purge vendor PII from the DataMart when it is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Timely deletion shortens the period during which retained PII remains exposed.

risks.description: The system can expose sensitive customer identifiers and contact information while returning data to client applications, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure if a client request or response is mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services accesses the following information for Program Participants, Farmers, Ranchers and Producers: • Full name or alias • Street Address or email address • SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number • bank account numbers (last few digits only) • case number (caseId, casename)
risks.rationale: The returned data includes identifiers and contact details that would be harmful if disclosed beyond authorized users.

risks.description: Because Core Services relies on a shared USDA customer database view and replication, a compromise of the API path could reveal more current customer information than necessary to unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth). NRCS users do not have direct access to SCIMS.
risks.rationale: A shared view and replicated access path increases the number of places where access controls must work correctly.

risks.description: The system transmits PII between multiple internal systems and client applications, so interception or misuse of in-transit data is a privacy risk even though it uses HTTPS.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
risks.rationale: Any system that moves PII across many services has a larger attack surface for interception or unauthorized access.

risks.description: A single external-facing API gateway creates a concentrated entry point, so a gateway failure or misconfiguration could expose many requests and responses at once.
risks.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: Concentrating traffic through one entry point increases the privacy impact of a gateway security weakness.

risks.description: Contractors can access Core Services, which creates a risk of insider misuse or overbroad access to customer data.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the set of people who can view or handle sensitive records.

risks.description: Core Services returns data in JSON format to user applications, which can make downstream copying, logging, or unintended reuse of PII easier if the receiving application is not well controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: Machine-readable output can be easily stored or redistributed by consuming applications.

risks.description: The system shares data with document storage and retrieval services, which can increase the chance that PII is retained or exposed in documents beyond the original request.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS – Used for document storage and retrieval.
risks.rationale: Document systems often persist copies of records, so they can extend the life and reach of PII.

risks.description: The system supports reports on race, sex, national origin, and disability, creating a risk of sensitive demographic profiling if access is not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Demographic data is sensitive and can be misused for profiling or inappropriate decision-making.

mitigations.description: Limit returned fields to the minimum needed for each request and suppress unnecessary identifiers in API responses.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of PII returned lowers the impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access on the SCIMS view and regularly review who can query replicated customer data through Core Services.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth).
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access control reduces the chance that shared database access is misused.

mitigations.description: Continue requiring encrypted transmission and add monitoring for unusual API traffic patterns that may indicate interception or unauthorized access attempts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and monitoring together reduce the likelihood and detectability of in-transit exposure.

mitigations.description: Harden the external-facing CA API Gateway with strict configuration review, logging, and regular security testing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
mitigations.rationale: A heavily protected gateway reduces the privacy impact of a single entry point.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and periodic access recertification for contractors with need-to-know access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regularly validating contractor access helps prevent unnecessary or lingering access to PII.

mitigations.description: Require consuming applications to avoid logging JSON payloads containing PII and to store only necessary fields.
mitigations.rationale: Preventing downstream logging and storage reduces secondary disclosure of returned data.

mitigations.description: Apply document retention and access controls in DMS so only authorized users can retrieve documents containing PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS – Used for document storage and retrieval.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting document access helps prevent PII from being exposed through stored files.

mitigations.description: Restrict demographic reporting to authorized personnel and use aggregation or de-identification where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and aggregating sensitive demographic reporting reduces profiling and unnecessary exposure.

risks.description: The system stores emergency contact and property-owner PII that could be exposed if DamWatch is accessed or disclosed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: DamWatch contains Emergency Action Plans (EAPs) that will be activated in the event of an emergency involving an NRCS-managed dam. EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: Names, addresses, and telephone numbers are sensitive enough that unauthorized access or disclosure could affect personal safety and privacy.

risks.description: PII may be disclosed in hardcopy or electronic form during review cycles or when an EAP is activated, creating a risk of accidental exposure or loss in transit or handling.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Manual distribution increases the chance that copies will be mishandled, sent to the wrong recipient, or lost.

risks.description: State and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site can access the PII, which expands the number of external parties with access to personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
risks.rationale: Each additional authorized user group increases the exposure surface for the stored PII.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of insider misuse or overbroad access to PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DamWatch as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access introduces another class of users who could improperly view or use the information.

risks.description: The system relies on information from publicly accessible sources and voluntarily submitted information, which may include outdated or unnecessary personal data such as nonpublic telephone numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII can be obtained from publicly accessible information resources, from organizations involved in emergency response, or submitted voluntarily by individual responders or property owners.
risks.rationale: Using public and volunteered sources can lead to collecting more personal data than needed or data that is not current.

risks.description: PII is retained for long periods, which increases the window for misuse or exposure after the information is no longer needed for a specific emergency plan.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention keeps personal information available for longer, increasing cumulative privacy risk.

risks.description: The system includes emergency contact information for each dam, which could reveal personal contact details if the information is accessed beyond the intended emergency context.
risks.evidence_quote: The system will also include emergency contact information for each dam.
risks.rationale: Emergency contact details are personal data and should be tightly limited to authorized emergency use.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to EAP PII to users with a documented need-to-know and enforce access controls and background checks for contractors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties. Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that sensitive contact information is seen by unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Continue using secure communications methods for all hardcopy and electronic disclosures of EAPs and require recipient verification before release.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and recipient verification reduce the likelihood of accidental disclosure during manual sharing.

mitigations.description: Limit responder access to only the dam site assignments they support and review those assignments regularly.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Site-specific access helps ensure responders only see the PII needed for their duties.

mitigations.description: Maintain mandatory background investigations for contractors and periodically revalidate their need-to-know access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Background screening and periodic revalidation lower the risk of insider misuse.

mitigations.description: Verify and minimize collected PII so only the information required for EAP execution is retained, and confirm nonpublic telephone numbers before inclusion.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII collected is only used during the execution of an EAP following the authorized activation of the EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting only what is necessary reduces privacy impact and limits the chance of storing outdated or unnecessary personal data.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review schedule to remove or archive EAP PII when it is no longer needed for active dam emergency planning, consistent with approved retention rules.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review and timely disposition reduce the amount of personal information retained over time.

mitigations.description: Treat emergency contact information as controlled PII and limit its disclosure to authorized EAP review cycles and activations only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting disclosure to defined emergency processes reduces unnecessary exposure of contact details.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, so unauthorized access could expose SSNs, tax IDs, bank account details, and other sensitive records.
