risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increases the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Bulk scanning and metadata extraction from paper records can capture more information than intended or introduce errors into the digital record set.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk ingestion increases the chance that sensitive content is over-collected or that inaccurate metadata is associated with records.

risks.description: Because individuals do not have direct access to DRMS, they may be unable to review or correct their records without relying on staff processes.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Limited direct access can make it harder for affected individuals to identify and correct inaccuracies in their records.

risks.description: Granting access to contractors expands the set of people who can see sensitive records and creates a risk of misuse or accidental disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Each additional authorized user increases the exposure surface for confidential records.

risks.description: The system relies on a cloud environment and inherited back-end processing, which can create confidentiality and access-control risks if those components are misconfigured or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The Digital Record Management System (DRMS) is a cloud system that resides on FPAC_AWS_Shared_GSS (FPAC_AWS_GSS).
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems depend on correct configuration and strong controls across shared infrastructure.

risks.description: Stored records may be retained for many years, increasing the duration over which personal information could be exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase the window of risk for unauthorized access and secondary misuse.

risks.description: The system contains records about conservation program participants, so keeping records as long as someone qualifies may preserve personal data longer than necessary for some records.
risks.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
risks.rationale: Retention tied to program eligibility can extend the life of personal records beyond the period of active use.

risks.description: The system supports indexing and search across records, which can make it easier for authorized users to retrieve large amounts of personal information quickly.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.
risks.rationale: Searchable repositories can amplify the privacy impact of any improper access by enabling rapid discovery of records.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access controls, strong encryption at rest and in transit, and enhanced auditing for records containing SSNs, tax IDs, bank information, and similar sensitive fields.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the likelihood and impact of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Use quality-control review of scanned documents and extracted metadata before records are committed to the metadata stores.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing bulk ingested records helps catch over-collection and metadata errors before they become part of the system of record.

mitigations.description: Provide a documented request and correction workflow for individuals to access and amend their records without needing direct DRMS access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
mitigations.rationale: A clear workflow helps individuals exercise their access and correction rights even when the system itself is staff-only.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary records, require periodic access recertification, and reinforce background screening and confidentiality obligations.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and periodically revalidating contractor access lowers the chance of unnecessary exposure or misuse.

mitigations.description: Perform regular cloud security reviews, configuration hardening, and continuous monitoring of the shared AWS environment and inherited processing components.
mitigations.rationale: Ongoing review of cloud and inherited components helps prevent misconfiguration and detect compromise early.

mitigations.description: Enforce records schedules and disposition reviews so records are deleted or transferred as soon as the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition reduces the amount of personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Periodically review whether records tied to program eligibility still need to be retained and dispose of records that no longer have a valid business or legal need.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
mitigations.rationale: Periodic retention review can prevent keeping personal records longer than necessary.

mitigations.description: Restrict search and indexing features to authorized roles and log searches involving sensitive records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS offers indexing and search capabilities that allow manual or automated uploading of electronic records and subsequent retrieval of relevant records for operational, legal and records management purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing search access reduces the chance of broad internal exposure through powerful retrieval tools.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers in documents, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure if the repository is accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers makes exposure particularly harmful to affected individuals and businesses.

risks.description: Users can upload documents directly into the application, which creates a risk that unauthorized or excessive personal information may be introduced into DMS.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Direct uploads can bypass structured data controls and increase the chance that sensitive information is stored unnecessarily.

risks.description: The system relies on documents rather than data-entry fields, which makes it harder to enforce minimization and may lead to collection of more PII than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields.
risks.rationale: Unstructured document storage reduces the system's ability to limit fields to only what is necessary.

risks.description: DMS uses name and address data from FSA SCIMS to identify the correct producer, creating a risk of misidentification or inappropriate association of records.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Matching people using limited identifiers can cause records to be linked to the wrong individual.

risks.description: The system permits disclosure to contractors and technical service providers, which creates a risk that PII will be shared beyond the agency if authorization or purpose limits are not properly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
risks.rationale: External sharing expands the number of parties who may see sensitive records and increases the chance of misuse or over-disclosure.

risks.description: Contractors have access to DMS, which creates a risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure by non-federal personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes. Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DMS as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Granting access to contractors increases the insider-threat surface for sensitive records.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DMS, which creates a risk that they may be unable to promptly review or correct inaccurate records affecting them.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: When people cannot directly see their records, errors may persist longer and affect decisions about them.

risks.description: The system retains records for long periods, which increases the chance that outdated personal information remains exposed longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time during which a breach or improper access could affect the data.

mitigations.description: Restrict document access to authorized NRCS employees, conservation district employees, and need-to-know contractors, and keep the repository encrypted and access-controlled.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data includes a variety of documents relevant to and required by the Farm Bill programs
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the likelihood that highly sensitive documents are disclosed to unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Require upload review and guidance so users only upload documents needed for the program and do not include unnecessary sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: A review step can reduce the chance that irrelevant or excessive PII is introduced through direct uploads.

mitigations.description: Use document intake rules or scanning controls to limit or flag documents containing unnecessary sensitive data before they are stored.
mitigations.rationale: Controls at intake can partially compensate for the lack of structured data-entry fields.

mitigations.description: Validate SCIMS-based matching with additional review when name and address do not produce a clear match.
mitigations.rationale: Extra verification helps prevent records from being linked to the wrong producer.

mitigations.description: Require written authorization to be verified and logged before any disclosure to contractors or technical service providers, and limit the disclosure to the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and logging help ensure external disclosures stay within the authorized scope.

mitigations.description: Keep the existing need-to-know access model and maintain mandatory background investigations for contractors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DMS as part of their regular assigned duties. Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and screening reduce the risk of contractor misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear process for individuals to request access and correction through the district conservationist or designated office, and ensure staff promptly handle those requests.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A defined request path helps individuals review and correct records even without direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules and purge records when they no longer need to be retained under the applicable NARA schedule and SORN.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.”
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposition limits how long sensitive records remain at risk.

risks.description: The system contains highly sensitive borrower financial and identity information, so unauthorized access could expose personal and financial details. This includes name, tax ID, borrower case ID, loan information, financials, and security property.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: The more sensitive the data, the greater the harm if it is accessed by someone without authorization.

risks.description: The system relies on manual input from FSA field agents, which creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete data being entered and then used in debt restructuring decisions. Errors in borrower information could lead to improper servicing outcomes.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual entry increases the chance that privacy-relevant data will be recorded incorrectly and then propagated through the system.

risks.description: The system retains borrower information indefinitely, which increases the amount of time sensitive records are exposed to breach, misuse, or unauthorized disclosure. Long-term retention also increases the volume of historical records that must be protected.
risks.evidence_quote: How long is information retained? The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping PII forever expands the window during which the data can be compromised or improperly used.

risks.description: The system uses borrower information to make or support debt restructuring determinations, so incorrect or excessive use of the data could affect a borrower's financial treatment. This creates a risk of privacy harm from decisions based on sensitive personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: To support field office employees in determining the most optimal servicing solutions applicable and available concerning the restructuring of customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
risks.rationale: Using personal financial data for decision support can materially affect the individual if the data is mishandled or misinterpreted.

risks.description: The system accesses other internal databases and web applications, which can expand exposure of borrower data across multiple systems and increase the chance of unauthorized access or over-collection. Cross-system access also makes it harder to limit use to the minimum necessary information.
risks.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Linking multiple systems can widen the attack surface and increase privacy risk if access controls are not tightly managed.

risks.description: Because the system is web based and intranet accessible, unauthorized internal users could potentially gain access if authentication or authorization controls fail. The PIA does not describe specific safeguards for access control or transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: Electronic Debt and Loan Restructuring System (eDALR$) is an Intranet web-based program developed to assist authorized agency officials
risks.rationale: Web-based systems require strong access controls because networked access can be abused if protections are weak.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to borrower records to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis and enforce strong authentication and role-based permissions.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive borrower data will be exposed to unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Add validation checks and supervisory review for manually entered borrower data before it is used in restructuring calculations.
mitigations.rationale: Review and validation help prevent incorrect data from affecting borrower servicing decisions.

mitigations.description: Apply periodic records review and purge or archive controls consistent with the approved retention schedule so only required permanent records remain active.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Retention controls reduce the amount of sensitive data kept in readily accessible systems over time.

mitigations.description: Use the system only as a decision-support tool and require human review of restructuring outcomes before final action is taken.
mitigations.evidence_quote: web based application (support tool) to be used by field office employees in computing a debt restructuring plan.
mitigations.rationale: Human review can catch errors or inappropriate use of sensitive information before it affects the borrower.

mitigations.description: Limit cross-system queries to the minimum necessary data and document which fields are retrieved from FLPIDS, DLS, FBP, and MRT.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing cross-system data retrieval reduces unnecessary exposure of borrower information.

mitigations.description: Implement and regularly test access controls for the intranet application, including authentication, authorization, and audit logging of user activity.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access control and logging help prevent and detect unauthorized access to the web-based system.

risks.description: The system retains borrower PII indefinitely, which increases the chance of unnecessary long-term exposure, misuse, or breach impact over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention keeps sensitive loan and identity data available longer than needed, expanding the window of risk.

risks.description: The system collects and stores highly sensitive identity, financial, and credit information that could cause significant harm if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: This data set includes direct identifiers and financial/credit records that are especially sensitive in a loan context.

risks.description: Sharing name and Tax ID with a third party creates disclosure risk beyond the agency’s direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: External disclosure of identifying information increases the number of parties that can access or mishandle the data.

risks.description: Using Microbilt for creditworthiness determinations may expose borrowers to additional privacy risk from commercial credit data processing.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance
risks.rationale: Creditworthiness checks require sensitive financial evaluation, which can reveal more about a borrower than is needed for basic servicing.

risks.description: County office staff enter borrower data manually, which creates a risk of unauthorized viewing, transcription errors, or improper handling during collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry by staff can expose data to more people and increase the chance of mistakes or misuse.

risks.description: The system uses borrower financial and credit data to make loan eligibility and servicing decisions, which can lead to overuse of personal information beyond the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Using detailed personal data for multiple decision-making purposes increases the privacy impact of each record.

risks.description: The system integrates with other loan systems and provides them with business data, which can broaden dissemination of borrower information across multiple systems.
risks.evidence_quote: interaction with the Direct Loan Making, Direct Loan Servicing, FLPRA and eDALR$ systems to ensure that loan requests have approved Farm Business Plans and to provide those systems with business data.
risks.rationale: System-to-system sharing can multiply access paths and make it harder to control downstream use.

mitigations.description: Apply a records retention schedule that limits how long borrower data is kept and automatically deletes or archives records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed to future misuse or breach.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to borrower financial and credit records to personnel with a documented need to know and monitor access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access is an appropriate safeguard for highly sensitive identity and financial information.

mitigations.description: Minimize the data sent to Microbilt by transmitting only the specific identifiers required for the creditworthiness check and protecting the transfer with secure transmission controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
mitigations.rationale: Sending only necessary data reduces the privacy impact of the external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice to borrowers that creditworthiness checks are performed and that commercial credit data may be used in loan eligibility decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance
mitigations.rationale: Notice helps borrowers understand how their information is used in a sensitive decision process.

mitigations.description: Train county office staff on privacy handling requirements and implement data-entry quality checks for borrower information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
mitigations.rationale: Training and validation reduce the chance of mishandling or inaccurate entry of personal data.

mitigations.description: Limit use of borrower data to the stated loan-making and loan-servicing purposes and document any secondary use review before expanding use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: and for loan making and loan servicing.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation reduces unnecessary reuse of personal information.

mitigations.description: Establish data-sharing controls and agreements for the connected loan systems so that only the business data needed for approved Farm Business Plans is shared.
mitigations.evidence_quote: interaction with the Direct Loan Making, Direct Loan Servicing, FLPRA and eDALR$ systems to ensure that loan requests have approved Farm Business Plans and to provide those systems with business data.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling downstream sharing limits the spread of borrower information across integrated systems.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive borrower identifiers, including Social Security Numbers, which creates a risk of identity theft or misuse if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: ADPS uses the customer’s name, address, Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: SSNs are high-value personal data and their presence increases harm if the system is breached or improperly accessed.

risks.description: Borrower information is accessed through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number, which increases the risk of unauthorized lookup or overbroad access.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Using direct identifiers for retrieval can make it easier for users to search for or view records beyond what they need.

risks.description: The system shares borrower information, including loan account information, with multiple external organizations, increasing the risk of unnecessary disclosure or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: Treasury, NFC, HUD IRS Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank Credit Bureaus, Borrowers – Borrower information including loan account information.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient expands the number of entities handling the data and the chance of disclosure outside the original purpose.

risks.description: Borrower data is reported to credit bureaus, which can affect individuals' financial reputation and creates risk if inaccurate information is shared.
risks.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
risks.rationale: Credit reporting can have significant consequences for borrowers, so errors or stale data can cause harm.

risks.description: The system reports delinquent borrowers to Treasury and IRS for offset, which may expose sensitive debt and tax-related information to government entities beyond the original loan program context.
risks.evidence_quote: The DCIA processes evaluate accounts for amount and date of delinquency and reported to Treasury for offset.
risks.rationale: Debt and offset reporting involves sensitive financial status information that can have privacy and dignity impacts.

risks.description: Information is retained indefinitely, creating a long-term exposure risk if records are no longer needed for active operations.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention increases the window in which records can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

risks.description: The system supports official accounting records and detailed transaction history, which may reveal extensive financial behavior over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The application is also used to view borrower status information and detailed history of transactions processed to a borrower’s account.
risks.rationale: Detailed histories can reveal patterns about a person's finances and loan status beyond a single transaction.

risks.description: A public-facing Customer Self Service effort is underway, which could expand exposure of borrower information if not carefully designed and secured.
risks.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
risks.rationale: Public-facing access typically increases the attack surface and the risk of accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Mask or tokenize Social Security Numbers wherever possible and restrict full SSN display to narrowly authorized users.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of SSNs reduces the harm if records are viewed or intercepted.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and logging for all online queries and batch access using name or Social Security Number.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls and audit trails help prevent and detect improper record lookups.

mitigations.description: Apply data-sharing agreements and minimum-necessary disclosure rules for each external recipient.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is shared and formalizing recipient obligations reduces unnecessary dissemination.

mitigations.description: Add a data quality review step before reporting information to credit bureaus.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing records before disclosure helps prevent harm from inaccurate credit reporting.

mitigations.description: Provide borrower notices about Treasury and IRS offset reporting and ensure only required delinquency data is transmitted.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and data minimization improve transparency and reduce unnecessary disclosure of sensitive financial information.

mitigations.description: Apply and periodically review records schedules to ensure indefinite retention is justified and no records are kept longer than required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Retention review limits the amount of data exposed over time while staying aligned with approved schedules.

mitigations.description: Limit access to detailed transaction histories to users with a business need and provide audit logging for those views.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive financial histories are viewed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Conduct a privacy and security review before the customer self-service function becomes public facing.
mitigations.rationale: A pre-launch review helps identify and reduce disclosure risks introduced by public access.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information that could be exposed if access controls or internal handling are insufficient. The collected data includes names and contact details for loan-related individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
risks.rationale: Even limited contact information can create privacy harm if improperly accessed or disclosed.

risks.description: Manual data entry by multiple FLP staff increases the chance of inaccurate, incomplete, or inconsistent records. Errors in appraisal-related records can affect the privacy and integrity of the information held about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Manually entered data is more prone to mistakes than automated collection.

risks.description: Broad access by County, State, Regional, and National FLP staff increases the number of people who can view or handle the information. Wider internal access raises the risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: provides County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals
risks.rationale: The more users who can access PII, the greater the exposure risk.

risks.description: The system keeps information permanently, which increases the long-term risk of outdated records, secondary use beyond the original purpose, or exposure from a future breach. Indefinite retention also expands the time period during which the data can be compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention directly increases the window of vulnerability.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the minimum set of users who need the information and enforce strong role-based access controls with audit logging.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood that contact information is viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Add validation checks and supervisory review for manually entered records before they are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Review and validation help catch entry errors before they affect the record.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege permissions and periodic access reviews for County, State, Regional, and National FLP users.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure only authorized staff retain access over time.

mitigations.description: Establish a records review process to confirm that only records required by the approved schedule remain in the system and that any eligible records are archived or disposed of appropriately.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: A formal records review process helps manage the risks created by permanent retention.

risks.description: The system collects highly sensitive personal and financial data, including SSNs/TINs, race, ethnicity, gender, credit card numbers, credit reports, and employment history, creating a risk of harm if that data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the collected data increase the impact of any privacy incident.

risks.description: The system uses and maintains permanent records, so any inaccurate or outdated borrower information may persist indefinitely and affect loan servicing and eligibility decisions over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long-term retention increases the chance that stale data will continue to be relied on.

risks.description: The system relies on data from many internal, state, local, and third-party sources, which creates a risk that inaccurate or inconsistent source data will be imported into borrower records.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected directly from farm loan borrower and information is received from other FSA applications, state and local agencies and other third party financial sources.
risks.rationale: More source systems and manual file-based collection increase the chance of errors entering the system.

risks.description: FBP collects and uses creditworthiness and financial profile information to determine loan eligibility, which creates a risk of unfair or overly broad profiling if the analysis is not accurate or explainable.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Eligibility decisions based on financial profiling can materially affect the borrower.

risks.description: The system supports manual data entry by field staff, which creates a risk that staff may enter, view, or handle borrower information incorrectly or beyond what is needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual handling is more error-prone than automated collection and can increase privacy exposure.

risks.description: DLS and FBP consolidate borrower and loan data from multiple sources into a single view, which increases the impact of any unauthorized access because more information is available in one place.
risks.evidence_quote: Loan Making provides a consolidated view of direct loan borrower data consisting of loan request information and loan obligation information
risks.rationale: Aggregated records are more sensitive because they reveal a fuller profile of the individual.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive borrower fields to only staff with a documented need to know and apply strong role-based access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that highly sensitive data is exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Provide a formal correction and review process so borrowers can request updates to inaccurate information before it is relied on for decisions.
mitigations.rationale: A review process helps prevent stale permanent records from driving future decisions.

mitigations.description: Validate and reconcile data imported from other FSA, state, local, and third-party sources before it is used in servicing or eligibility decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Source validation reduces the risk that erroneous external data becomes part of the official record.

mitigations.description: Require human review and documented decision criteria for creditworthiness and restructuring determinations.
mitigations.rationale: Human review helps ensure that automated or semi-structured analysis is applied fairly and accurately.

mitigations.description: Train field staff on privacy handling and data-entry quality, and use input checks to reduce accidental disclosure or entry errors.
mitigations.rationale: Training and validation reduce mistakes during manual processing.

mitigations.description: Segment borrower data views so staff only see the specific loan and personal data needed for the task at hand.
mitigations.rationale: Data segmentation reduces the privacy impact of any account or screen-level exposure.

risks.description: The system retains PII indefinitely, which increases the risk of over-retention and unauthorized disclosure over time. Long-term retention also expands the impact if records are later breached or accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention preserves PII longer than necessary for many operational purposes, increasing exposure over time.

risks.description: The system stores names and mailing addresses for trainees and state personnel, creating a risk of disclosure of contact information if access controls are weak or records are mishandled. This is especially relevant because the system maintains multiple web-based applications with oversight and workflow functions.
risks.evidence_quote: DDORS Name FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
risks.rationale: Names and mailing addresses are directly identifying and can be misused if exposed.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which could expose sensitive draft or pre-decisional information before it is finalized. Public collection also increases the chance that individuals submit information without understanding how it will be used.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Pre-approval collection can reveal information before it is intended for release.

risks.description: The system is web-based and used for oversight, training, and workflow management, so unauthorized access could reveal personal information about staff, trainees, or public submitters. The PIA does not describe any specific transmission or access safeguards in the provided text.
risks.evidence_quote: The Farm Loan Program Risk Assessment and Compliance System (FLPRAC) consists of multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
risks.rationale: Web-based systems are exposed to broader access risks if controls are not sufficiently strong.

risks.description: Because data are entered by county offices, state offices, and state personnel, there is a risk of inaccurate or inconsistent records being stored about individuals. Errors in names or addresses could affect oversight, training, or case-management decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
risks.rationale: Multiple manual entry points increase the chance of data quality problems that can affect individuals.

mitigations.description: Apply a records schedule that limits retention to the minimum period required for oversight, training, and compliance, and periodically review whether permanent retention is still necessary for each record type.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review can reduce unnecessary long-term exposure while still honoring approved records requirements.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to names and mailing addresses to only users with a documented need to know and log access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that directly identifying information is viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear public notice and intake controls for SDMS submissions so people understand what information is being collected and that some directives or policies are not yet approved by OMB.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice helps prevent unintended disclosure and improves informed submission by the public.

mitigations.description: Implement role-based access controls and strong authentication for all web applications, with periodic review of user permissions.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access control is a basic safeguard for web-based systems that handle PII.

mitigations.description: Add data validation and periodic record review procedures to correct inaccurate names and mailing addresses entered by county, state, or state personnel.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and review reduce the privacy harm caused by inaccurate personal data.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and business identifiers, creating a risk of identity theft or misuse if the data is exposed or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is defined as information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual. risks.rationale: The system includes direct identifiers and contact information that can be used to identify and contact individuals.

risks.description: The system maintains a very large volume of records, increasing the impact of any privacy incident and the chance that data will be accessed beyond what is necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities
risks.rationale: A larger record set increases both the number of affected people and the consequences of unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system retains historical farm and customer data for a long period, which increases the amount of personal information exposed over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window in which older records can be disclosed, breached, or reused in ways that are no longer needed.

risks.description: Farm and business partner data are shared across multiple USDA agencies, creating a risk of broader disclosure than the original collection context.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Sharing the same records across agencies increases the number of users and systems that can see the information.

risks.description: The system supports access and updates at any County Office, which can increase the risk of inconsistent access control or local overexposure of records.
risks.evidence_quote: allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
risks.rationale: Broader operational access can make it harder to ensure each user only sees the minimum data needed.

risks.description: The system uses role-based create, edit, and view capabilities, so incorrect role assignment could expose records to unauthorized users or allow inappropriate changes.

risks.rationale: If roles are misconfigured, users may gain access beyond their job duties.

risks.description: The system includes historical data from 1999 to the current program year, which may contain outdated or no-longer-necessary personal information that still remains accessible.

risks.rationale: Older records can contain stale information that should be minimized or archived with tighter controls.

risks.rationale: Location-linked records can expose where a producer operates and the extent of their land holdings.

mitigations.description: Apply strict data minimization, masking, and field-level access controls for SSNs, TINs, phone numbers, and mailing addresses.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of direct identifiers reduces the harm if records are viewed or disclosed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Implement stronger monitoring, auditing, and breach-response controls proportionate to the size of the dataset.
mitigations.rationale: Large datasets warrant tighter oversight because incidents affect many more individuals.

mitigations.description: Review retention schedules regularly and purge or further restrict archived records once the business need ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention of unnecessary historical data lowers long-term privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and least-privilege access rules for NRCS, RMA, and FSA exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting shared fields and recipient access limits unnecessary disclosure across agencies.

mitigations.description: Require county-office users to access only the records needed for their assigned cases and activities.
mitigations.evidence_quote: allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the chance that local staff can see unrelated records.

mitigations.description: Conduct periodic role reviews and approval checks for create, edit, and view permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps catch incorrect or excessive permissions before they lead to unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Separate active records from historical records and apply tighter access controls to older data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
mitigations.rationale: Segregating older records reduces the number of users who can access long-retained information.

mitigations.description: Limit access to geospatial boundary data and use it only for farm-record maintenance purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting location data helps prevent unnecessary disclosure of where farms are located.

mitigations.description: Continue encrypting data in transit for inter-agency transfers.

mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the risk that shared records are intercepted during transmission.

risks.description: The system keeps producer information permanently, which increases the long-term exposure of names, addresses, and other records if they are later misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the amount of data available for unauthorized access over time.

risks.description: The system stores and uses names and street addresses across many program components, creating broad exposure of identifying information for farmers and ranchers.
risks.evidence_quote: What information is collected, used, disseminated or maintained? ELAP Name, street address LFP Name, street address LIP Name, street address NAP Name, street address TAP Name, street address CFAP Name, street address CFAP 2.0 Name, street address QLA Name, street address PARP Name, street address PLIP Name, street address PATHH Name, street address OTECP Name, street address SMHPP Name, street address ELRP Name, street address
risks.rationale: Collecting the same identifying details in many modules expands the privacy impact if any one module is accessed improperly.

risks.description: County office employees enter producer information into the system, which creates a risk of unnecessary internal exposure or mishandling of personal data during manual entry and processing.
risks.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
risks.rationale: Manual handling by staff increases the number of people and steps through which personal information passes.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, so producer information could be exposed to non-federal personnel even with need-to-know controls.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access broadens the set of individuals who can view sensitive producer records.

risks.description: The system uses producer data to generate names and street addresses for printed forms and mailed letters, which creates a disclosure risk through physical mail handling.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
risks.rationale: Producing paper correspondence increases the chance that address information is seen by unintended recipients or intercepted in transit.

risks.description: NAP notifications are centralized and sent to a print shop, creating an additional disclosure point for producer information outside the originating application.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
risks.rationale: Routing notifications through another system and a print shop adds another place where personal data may be exposed.

risks.description: NAP data is disclosed to external systems such as CARS and LFP, which creates a risk of broader internal dissemination than the producer may expect.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: Sharing data with other systems increases the number of environments where the information must be protected.

risks.description: The system allows access by producer identifiers and last name for NAP payment processing, which could enable unauthorized lookup if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
risks.rationale: Using easily known identifiers for retrieval can make records easier to find if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system processes overpayments and payment history, which can reveal financial and eligibility information about producers over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Processing functions include: • Payment/Overpayment processing • ... • Retain producer payment history information • Payment History Reporting
risks.rationale: Payment and history records can expose sensitive financial and program participation details.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce a records disposal schedule so permanent retention is limited to records that must truly be kept indefinitely, and review whether any fields can be shortened or minimized.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention where possible lowers the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection and storage of names and street addresses to only the fields needed for each specific program workflow.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name, street address
mitigations.rationale: Limiting stored identifiers reduces the impact of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access and quality checks for county office data entry, with periodic review of user actions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter controls on manual entry reduce the chance of mishandling by staff.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary and conduct regular access recertification for all contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and reviewing contractor access reduces unnecessary exposure to non-federal personnel.

mitigations.description: Use secure mailing processes and suppress printed address details unless a paper notice is required for the program.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
mitigations.rationale: Reducing printed address exposure lowers the risk of physical disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit the data sent to the KC Print Shop to the minimum needed for mailing and apply contractual privacy requirements to the print vendor path.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing and controlling the print workflow reduces disclosure risk in notification delivery.

mitigations.description: Document and review each internal disclosure to external systems, and ensure only the minimum NAP data needed is shared.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting internal sharing lowers the number of systems holding the data.

mitigations.description: Require stronger authentication or multi-factor controls for NAP payment lookup functions that accept producer ID or last name.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication reduces the chance that simple identifiers can be used to access records inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to payment history and overpayment records to staff with a direct business need and log all access to those records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: • Payment/Overpayment processing • ... • Retain producer payment history information • Payment History Reporting
mitigations.rationale: Payment history is sensitive, so access logging and need-to-know limits help deter misuse.

risks.description: The system maintains highly sensitive identifiers and financial data, which could expose producers to identity theft or financial harm if mishandled or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: ARCPLC Name, mailing address, last 4 digits SSN SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: The collected data includes direct identifiers and payment information that are sensitive if exposed.

risks.description: ARCPLC displays producer PII retrieved from another system, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure to users who only need limited eligibility information.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
risks.rationale: Displaying retrieved PII increases the chance of overexposure beyond what is needed to determine eligibility.

risks.description: SWIMS uses a shared database accessible to a limited set of employees, which creates a risk that more users than necessary can access producer PII.
risks.evidence_quote: using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: Shared access broadens the number of people who can reach the data and increases insider access risk.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, increasing the amount of time producer PII remains available for unauthorized access or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases cumulative exposure risk over time.

risks.description: PII is obtained from SCIMS rather than directly from the individual, which can make it harder for producers to understand what data are being used and to correct inaccuracies in the displayed information.
risks.evidence_quote: The data that is PII is not collected in ARC/PLC. The name, address and last 4 are maintained in SCIMS.
risks.rationale: Using externally maintained source data can create transparency and accuracy issues for affected individuals.

risks.description: The system processes farm tract numbers and payment amounts along with identity data, which could reveal detailed financial and operational information about producers if accessed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: Combining identity data with farm and payment details can expose a fuller profile of a producer's business activity.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the minimum set of users who need producer identifiers and payment data, and enforce strong auditing of access to those records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers and financial data are exposed.

mitigations.description: Display only the minimum PII necessary for the task and mask or truncate identifiers where full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is shown lowers the risk of unnecessary exposure from the SCIMS lookup.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls to the shared database so each employee can access only the records needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based controls reduce insider access to producer PII in the shared database.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce periodic review of permanent records to confirm that indefinite retention remains necessary and that records are protected throughout their lifecycle.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure permanently retained PII is justified and safeguarded over time.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice to producers explaining that ARC/PLC uses SCIMS-maintained data and a process for requesting correction of inaccurate source records.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice and correction procedures improve transparency and data accuracy for individuals.

mitigations.description: Separate payment and tract information from direct identifiers in user views and reports unless the full combination is required for an approved business purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Separating data elements reduces the amount of detailed producer information exposed at one time.

risks.description: County office users can search for a specific farmer or producer using personal information, which creates a risk of unauthorized lookup or overbroad access to sensitive identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII allows County Office users to search for a specific user (farmer or producer)
risks.rationale: Search capability increases the chance that users could access information about individuals without a legitimate need.

risks.description: The system uses SSN as a second authentication method, exposing highly sensitive identifiers to misuse if accessed or handled improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: If a farmer or producer has an eAuth account, the SSN can be used as a second authentication method to validate the farmer / producer
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive and their use for authentication raises the impact of any unauthorized disclosure or misuse.

risks.description: FSAfarm+ pulls PII from SCIMS, so any weakness in access controls or data handling during retrieval could expose personal data to county office users.
risks.evidence_quote: the other application (FSAfarm+) does contain PII. This PIA is required since FSAfarm+ uses personal information of farmers and producers.
risks.rationale: Because the application uses personal information to support user functions, improper access to the retrieved data would create a privacy exposure.

risks.description: Contractor access to the FSCOMS/FSAfarm+ environment creates a risk that contractors could view or mishandle PII while supporting the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the number of people who may encounter PII and therefore increases exposure risk.

risks.description: Although the system says memory and cache are cleared on logout, transient PII could still be exposed if the clearing process fails or is incomplete.
risks.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: Automatic clearing reduces risk, but any failure in that process could leave sensitive data available in memory or cache.

risks.description: The system relies on the statement that it does not store PII, so any unexpected persistence of data would create a privacy risk because there is no stated retention control for stored records.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is not stored in FSCOMS, therefore PII is not retained by the system.
risks.rationale: If data were inadvertently stored despite the design intent, it would lack an explicit retention period or disposal control in the description.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and need-to-know restrictions for county office searches, with audit logging of each lookup.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and recording searches reduces the chance of unauthorized or unnecessary access to farmer and producer information.

mitigations.description: Minimize SSN use for authentication by masking the SSN on screen and using an alternative second factor where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing exposure of the SSN lowers the harm if the identifier is observed or mishandled.

mitigations.description: Restrict retrieval from SCIMS to only the minimum fields needed for the specific user task and protect the transfer with strong access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FSAfarm+ requests and receives PII from SCIMS, which resides in the FPCMS system.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting the amount of PII retrieved reduces the impact of any unauthorized access during the lookup process.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to specific support functions and require backgrounded privileged access approval for any contractor account that can reach PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
mitigations.rationale: Tightening contractor permissions reduces the number of people who can encounter PII.

mitigations.description: Test logout and cache-clearing behavior to confirm that no PII remains in memory or cache after session end.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the county office users log out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps ensure the stated clearing behavior actually removes transient PII as intended.

mitigations.description: Continuously monitor the application to verify that no PII is being stored unexpectedly and alert on any deviation from the no-retention design.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring for unintended storage helps preserve the system's stated no-retention posture.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains personally identifiable information about producers, including name, mailing address, ethnicity, and race, which creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive identity and demographic data.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: These data elements can identify individuals and include sensitive demographic information.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to determine who is eligible to vote in committee elections, which creates a risk of profiling or unfair treatment if eligibility decisions are inaccurate or improperly applied.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
risks.rationale: Eligibility determinations based on coded administrative data can affect who receives election materials and voting access.

risks.description: County office staff collect data from producers and enter it into the system, creating a risk of human error or unauthorized entry that could compromise accuracy and privacy.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry increases the chance of incorrect or improperly handled personal data.

risks.description: The system builds and sends county-specific lists of eligible producers for ballot printing, which creates a risk that election-related mailing lists could be exposed or misused if not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
risks.rationale: Mailing lists tie identities and addresses to election participation and should be restricted to authorized use.

risks.description: The system collects and reports election data from returned ballot forms, creating a risk that ballot-related records could reveal participation or voting-related information beyond what is necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Collect and report election data from returned ballot forms (The County Election and Media Outreach Report).
risks.rationale: Returned ballot processing can expose sensitive election participation data if access is not limited.

risks.description: The system creates and stores a directory of COC members and information related to their terms, which creates a risk of unnecessary retention and exposure of member records over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Create the COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms.
risks.rationale: A directory of members and term information can remain sensitive long after the election cycle ends.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely as permanent records, which increases the risk that personal data will persist longer than needed and be exposed in future incidents.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window during which records can be misused or compromised.

risks.description: Because the system is a major application on DISC Midrange Systems, it concentrates election and producer data in a central environment, which increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: FSFOSS resides on the DISC Midrange Systems
risks.rationale: Centralized storage can amplify harm if system access controls fail.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to producer records containing name, address, ethnicity, and race to only personnel with a documented need to know, and monitor access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal data.

mitigations.description: Validate committee and LAA code-based eligibility determinations before ballots or lists are generated, and provide a correction process for producers who are misclassified.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction help prevent inaccurate eligibility decisions from affecting voting access.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access, staff training, and data-entry validation checks for county office collection and entry of producer information.
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce manual-entry errors and limit unauthorized handling of producer data.

mitigations.description: Limit distribution of county-specific eligible-producer lists to authorized election staff and use secure handling procedures for ballot printing files.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting list distribution lowers the risk that election mailing data will be exposed or misused.

mitigations.description: Apply access controls and minimization to returned ballot records so only the information needed for election reporting is retained and viewed.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access to ballot-related records reduces exposure of voting-related information.

mitigations.description: Review the COC Directory contents periodically and remove any member-term information that is no longer required for the system's stated election purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review limits the amount of member information kept in the directory to what is necessary.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review and archival control process for permanent records so only approved records are retained indefinitely and inactive data is protected.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: Records controls help ensure indefinite retention is limited to approved records and managed securely.

mitigations.description: Harden the DISC Midrange Systems environment with strong authentication, least-privilege access, and logging for all access to FSFOSS records.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger system access controls reduce the impact of a centralized repository being compromised.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, so a breach could expose identities, account details, and employment history. The breadth of data increases the privacy impact if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: All Program and financial data for the Agency is stored in the EDW. This includes Farm Program, Farm Loan, Commodity Operations, Human Resources and Financial data. Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: The system explicitly contains multiple categories of sensitive PII and financial information.

risks.description: Consolidating data from multiple source systems into a central warehouse creates a larger single point of exposure if the warehouse is misused or compromised. Centralized reporting can reveal more about individuals than any one source system alone.
risks.evidence_quote: The Enterprise Data Warehouse is designed to facilitate data retrieval and reporting by providing a central stable location for data storage across FSA’s business enterprise.
risks.rationale: Centralization increases the amount of personal information available in one place.

risks.description: The system uses reporting tools and web-based access, which can increase the risk of unauthorized internal access to detailed personal data if permissions are too broad. Reporting environments often expose more records than are needed for a user's job.
risks.evidence_quote: Oracle Business Intelligence (OBIEE) and web based tools will be used to analyze the data.
risks.rationale: Web-based analytics commonly require careful role-based access to prevent overexposure.

risks.description: Batch transfers from source systems to the warehouse can expose personal data in transit or during loading if the transfer process is not securely protected. Repeated automated transfers also increase the chance of accidental disclosure or interception.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems shares the information through batch processes.
risks.rationale: Automated batch sharing creates a recurring transmission risk.

risks.description: The system receives data from multiple agencies and source systems, so inaccurate or mismatched records could lead to incorrect reporting or decisions about individuals. Errors in identity or eligibility data can affect privacy and fairness.
risks.evidence_quote: The EDW will extract transform and load information from multiple SAP source systems including MIDAS, WBSCM and FMMI, as well as non-SAP systems, such as Farm Records, GIS, Eligibility, and Financial data from SQL Server systems.
risks.rationale: Combining many sources increases the chance that incorrect data about a person will be stored and reused.

risks.description: Information is collected from producers at county offices and from other federal agencies, which creates a risk that individuals may not fully understand how their data will be reused across the warehouse. Secondary use for reporting may exceed the context in which the data was originally provided.
risks.evidence_quote: Most PII data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff. In some cases information is collected via other federal agencies which provide this information to the FSA.
risks.rationale: Data collected in one setting may be reused in broader reporting contexts.

risks.description: The system supports Congressional, program-level, and end-user reporting, which can create privacy risk if reports disclose more detail than necessary. Broad reporting use may make it harder to limit personal data to the minimum needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the EDW is used for Congressional, program level and end user reporting.
risks.rationale: Multiple reporting audiences increase the need for data minimization.

risks.description: The system shares information with other organizations and external entities, creating a risk of disclosure beyond the originating purpose. Even limited validation or one-time sharing can expose personal identifiers to additional parties.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Any sharing with other organizations increases the number of parties handling PII.

risks.description: Retention tied to the NARA schedule means personal data may be kept for a long time, increasing the window for misuse or breach. Longer retention also increases the amount of historical information available for profiling or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases privacy exposure over time.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive fields such as TIN/SSN, account numbers, and employment history to only those users with a documented need to know, and enforce strong auditing of access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the chance that highly sensitive data is unnecessarily exposed.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization in the warehouse by retaining only the fields needed for reporting and by segregating especially sensitive datasets where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of centralized personal data lowers the impact of any compromise.

mitigations.description: Use role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions for OBIEE and web-based reporting tools, with report-level restrictions for sensitive datasets.
mitigations.rationale: Tight permissions help ensure users can only view the data required for their duties.
