risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
risks.rationale: The site can collect personally identifying and sensitive consumer-finance-related information from public interactions.

risks.description: User-submitted comments, videos, links, and images may be publicly exposed, which could reveal personal details or sensitive opinions to other visitors. The system explicitly says users can control how much of their information is made public, implying some submissions may be public by default or through user choice.
risks.evidence_quote: Depending on how you use ConsumerFinance.gov, you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website.
risks.rationale: Public-facing posting increases the chance of unintended disclosure of personal information.

risks.description: The site collects information about a visitor's use of the website, which can create tracking and profiling risks across sessions or pages. Even if used for analytics, usage data can reveal browsing behavior and interests.
risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
risks.rationale: Website-use data can be privacy-sensitive because it reflects behavior and interests.

risks.description: Demographic information may be collected, which can increase the sensitivity of the data set and support inference about individuals or groups. Combined with other information, it may enable identification or categorization beyond what users expect.
risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
risks.rationale: Demographic data becomes more privacy-sensitive when combined with other collected information.

risks.description: Information about consumer financial products that users and others have used may reveal highly sensitive financial behavior or circumstances. Such information can expose personal financial history even when the site is used for education or feedback.
risks.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
risks.rationale: Financial-product usage information can be sensitive and may reveal personal circumstances.

risks.description: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the path to the online complaint intake system, so information entered on the site may flow into another system and be used in a more sensitive context. This creates a risk of secondary use or broader exposure than a visitor expects when interacting with the public website.
risks.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system.
risks.rationale: Routing users into a complaint system can extend data use beyond the website itself.

risks.description: Google Analytics is used to evaluate aggregate web traffic, which creates a third-party processing risk for visitor data. Even if the stated purpose is aggregate analysis, analytics tools can still collect or infer detailed browsing information.
risks.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov to be able to inform future changes and upgrades to the site based on former trends and behaviors, and possibly add new resources or products when there is a demand.
risks.rationale: Third-party analytics can expose visitor behavior to an external provider.

risks.description: The site may collect directly identifiable PII when a user knowingly provides it, which creates a risk of accidental over-collection if disclosures are not clearly understood. Users may not realize what counts as directly identifiable information or how it will be used.
risks.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
risks.rationale: Even voluntary collection can be risky if users do not fully understand the consequences.

mitigations.description: Minimize collection of directly identifiable information and clearly warn users before they submit contact details or other identifying content.
mitigations.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting collection and warning users reduces unnecessary disclosure of identity information.

mitigations.description: Provide prominent pre-publication notices and clear controls that let users decide whether comments, videos, links, or images are public.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Depending on how you use ConsumerFinance.gov, you can limit how much information you give to us and how much of that information is made public through the website.
mitigations.rationale: User-controlled publishing helps prevent unintended public disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit analytics collection to aggregated or de-identified website-use data and restrict any detailed usage logs to what is necessary for site improvement.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov to be able to inform future changes and upgrades to the site based on former trends and behaviors, and possibly add new resources or products when there is a demand.
mitigations.rationale: Using aggregate data only reduces the risk of tracking individual browsing behavior.

mitigations.description: Collect demographic information only when needed for a specific website function and explain why it is requested.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose-limited collection reduces the sensitivity and volume of demographic data held.

mitigations.description: Avoid collecting consumer financial product-use information unless it is necessary for the specific interaction, and separate it from other identifiers where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When you visit and use ConsumerFinance.gov, we may collect information such as your contact information, information about your use of the website, demographic information, information about consumer financial products you and others have used, as well as input and feedback in the form of comments, videos, links, or images.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing collection and linkage lowers the chance that financial behavior can be tied to a person.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear notice at the point of transition to the complaint intake system explaining that information will be used in another system and may be subject to different handling rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ConsumerFinance.gov serves as the method by which most consumers reach our online complaint intake system.
mitigations.rationale: A transition notice helps users understand when their information leaves the public website.

mitigations.description: Use privacy-preserving analytics settings, such as limiting cookies or other identifiers and configuring Google Analytics to collect only what is needed for aggregate reporting.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov to be able to inform future changes and upgrades to the site based on former trends and behaviors, and possibly add new resources or products when there is a demand.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting analytics identifiers reduces the chance of third-party tracking.

mitigations.description: Use plain-language notices that explain what counts as directly identifiable PII and when users are knowingly providing it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
mitigations.rationale: Clear definitions and notices help users make informed disclosures.

risks.description: The system collects and stores Social Security Numbers, which creates a high-impact risk if those identifiers are exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: The following PII information is collected when a user registers for GSAFleet.gov:  First and Last Name  Email address  Telephone number  IP Address  Social Security Numbers
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive and can enable identity theft if compromised.

risks.description: Accident records can include highly sensitive personal and health information about third parties, including race, birth date, health records, driver’s license numbers, and home contact details.
risks.evidence_quote: The following PII information (data elements for accident investigation and recovery) for non government entities include:   Name  Gender  Race (for Police report only)  Birth date  Geo-location indicator  Personal email address  Home address  Home phone number  Health records  Driver’s License Number
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the accident data increases harm if it is disclosed beyond what is necessary.

risks.description: Vehicle sales processing collects Social Security Numbers and transmits them to Experian for credit-worthiness checks, creating disclosure and secondary-use risk.
risks.evidence_quote: Data elements collected during the sales process include Name, Organization, Address of the successful bidder as well as the amount paid, and social security numbers. GSAFleet.gov collects, transmits, and stores social security numbers. Social security numbers are transmitted to Experian to determine a user's credit worthiness to purchase a vehicle.
risks.rationale: Sharing SSNs with a credit bureau expands exposure beyond the core sales transaction.

risks.description: The system creates or aggregates new data about individuals, which can amplify privacy impact by combining accident, sales, and account information.
risks.evidence_quote: 3.2: Will the system, application, or project create or aggregate new data about the individual? Yes
risks.rationale: Aggregation can reveal more about a person than any single source of data alone.

risks.description: Accident and claims data are transmitted to multiple internal systems and offices, increasing the risk of unauthorized access during sharing and transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: When GSA seeks to recover expenses for an accident/incident in which a nongovernment 3rd party is at fault, a file of requisite data is transmitted to OCFO ... only in case of fraud or courts it is sent over to GSA IG for investigative purposes.
risks.rationale: Each additional transfer creates another point where data could be intercepted, mishandled, or over-shared.

risks.description: Accident documents are handled through email, fax conversion, and attachment workflows, which can expose personal data if messages or files are misdirected or retained outside the system.
risks.evidence_quote: The Police Report and SF91 are sent electronically (i.e., as attachments) to the Accident Management Center's (AMC) inbox. Documents faxed from the police station are converted to digital format and emailed to the AMC account.
risks.rationale: Email and fax-to-email workflows are vulnerable to routing mistakes and unintended retention.

risks.description: Although the system says it does not store police reports locally, the reports are stored in EDMS, so a compromise of that connected repository could expose accident PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The AMC uploads the Police Report and SF91 associated with the specific incident/accident record, however, the system does not store these documents or associated data locally. The Police Report is collected in PDF or image format and stored in EDMS.
risks.rationale: Storing sensitive documents in a connected repository still creates a privacy exposure if that repository is breached or misconfigured.

risks.description: The system logs GSA employees and contractors with access to transactions, which can create employee monitoring and behavioral tracking concerns.
risks.evidence_quote: GSAFleet.gov is not designed to monitor the public, GSA employees or contractors with the ability to log into system transactions are logged via the audit logs.
risks.rationale: Audit logs can reveal detailed user activity and should be limited to legitimate security and accountability needs.

risks.description: Individuals may have difficulty correcting inaccurate accident or sales data because verification depends heavily on police reports and user-submitted information, with limited cross-verification.
risks.evidence_quote: It is the responsibility of the individual or the police report that provides this information ... No other cross verification is done for non-government 3rd party information collected where 3rd party is responsible for the accident.
risks.rationale: If the source data is wrong, the system may persist inaccurate personal information that affects individuals.

mitigations.description: Limit SSN collection to cases where it is strictly necessary, and apply strong encryption and access controls to SSNs at rest and in transit.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GSAFleet.gov collects, transmits, and stores social security numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing collection and protecting storage lowers the likelihood and impact of SSN exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict accident-case access to authorized personnel only and keep sensitive third-party fields tied to the specific claim purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The PII information is transmitted for both the driver of the 3rd party vehicle and the owner (if different from the driver).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to need-to-know users reduces the chance of unnecessary disclosure of sensitive third-party data.

mitigations.description: Minimize the use of SSNs in vehicle sales and use the credit check only for the stated eligibility purpose, with strict controls on transmission to Experian.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Social security numbers are transmitted to Experian to determine a user's credit worthiness to purchase a vehicle.
mitigations.rationale: Purpose limitation and controlled sharing reduce the risk of secondary use and overexposure.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization reviews before combining records so only the minimum necessary personal data is aggregated.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 3.2: Will the system, application, or project create or aggregate new data about the individual? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing aggregation reduces the privacy impact of combining multiple data sources.

mitigations.description: Use formal data-sharing agreements and restrict downstream recipients to the minimum data needed for recovery, fraud, or court purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: 4.4Formal Agreement: Is a formal agreement(s) in place? Yes
mitigations.rationale: Agreements and scope limits help ensure transferred data is used only for authorized purposes.

mitigations.description: Replace email-based handling of accident attachments with a secure portal or encrypted transfer workflow and limit inbox access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Police Report and SF91 are sent electronically (i.e., as attachments) to the Accident Management Center's (AMC) inbox.
mitigations.rationale: A secure transfer channel reduces the chance of accidental disclosure through email handling.

mitigations.description: Ensure the EDMS repository uses strong encryption, role-based access control, and audit monitoring for stored accident documents.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Police Report is collected in PDF or image format and stored in EDMS.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the repository directly reduces the risk from storing sensitive documents outside the core system.

mitigations.description: Limit audit log content and retention to what is needed for security and accountability, and restrict who can review the logs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GSA employees or contractors with the ability to log into system transactions are logged via the audit logs.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining logs and access to them reduces unnecessary employee surveillance risk.

mitigations.description: Provide a stronger correction workflow that lets individuals submit supporting documentation and have disputed data revalidated.
mitigations.evidence_quote: GSAFleet.gov users have the ability to amend PII by submitting an email request, written request or by phone call to the GSA Fleet Accident Management Center (AMC).
mitigations.rationale: A structured dispute process can improve accuracy when source records are incomplete or wrong.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, creating a significant harm risk if the data is exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: That may include additional personally identifiable information (PII) information, Social Security Number (SSN), annuitant claim numbers, compensation claim numbers, insurance account numbers, insurance claim numbers, military serial numbers, birth date, financial institution routing number, and financial institution account number.
risks.rationale: This data could enable identity theft, financial fraud, or other serious privacy harms if improperly accessed.

risks.description: The system aggregates and links multiple inquiries to the same constituent, which can create a broader profile of a person’s interactions and issues than any single inquiry alone.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also links together all the inquiries submitted by or on behalf of the same constituent.
risks.rationale: Linking records increases the sensitivity of the profile and the impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system stores communications and documents from multiple parties, including non-public agency records, which may reveal information beyond the original inquiry.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also stores all communications and documents connected to the inquiry. This may include letters, emails, and attachments between OPM and the staffer, constitution, or other parties that may have information to help answer the inquiry (e.g., other federal agencies). This may also include legal, administrative, or similar non-public agency records relevant to the inquiry.
risks.rationale: Collecting and retaining connected correspondence and records can capture additional sensitive information unrelated to the immediate request.

risks.description: The system collects information about constituents through congressional staffers, which may create a risk that people are included in the system without direct awareness or control over the disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA receives hundreds of inquiries from congressional staffers on behalf of their congressional office or someone in their district.
risks.rationale: When a third party submits information on someone’s behalf, the constituent may not know what data is shared or how it is used.

risks.description: The system allows staffers to submit inquiries and documents through a web portal, which creates a risk of unauthorized access if account controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: CS Portal is a secure web interface where congressional staffers can submit the inquiries and other messages to the Office of Personnel Management.
risks.rationale: A web-based intake point is a common target for account compromise or unauthorized submission if protections are insufficient.

risks.description: The system depends on staffer account registration and identity verification, so weak approval or authentication processes could allow unauthorized users to access case information.
risks.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
risks.rationale: If account review or multifactor authentication is bypassed or improperly implemented, unauthorized access becomes more likely.

risks.description: Using cloud services for the system may increase exposure of sensitive records to misconfiguration or third-party access risks.
risks.evidence_quote: The new system uses a cloud-version of Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics Portal, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems require careful configuration and access control to prevent unintended disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit collection of sensitive identifiers to only what is necessary for each inquiry and apply strong access controls and encryption to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing and tightly protecting high-risk identifiers lowers the chance and impact of misuse.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to linked constituent case histories to staff with a need to know and log access to linked records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting visibility into aggregated case histories reduces unnecessary exposure of a broader profile.

mitigations.description: Apply retention limits and periodic review to communications and attached documents so records are kept only as long as needed to resolve the inquiry and meet legal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter retention reduces the amount of sensitive correspondence and non-public records available for disclosure.

mitigations.description: Provide clear notice to staffers about what constituent information they may submit and require them to confirm they have authority to share it on the constituent’s behalf.
mitigations.rationale: Notice and authorization checks help ensure third-party submissions are appropriate and expected.

mitigations.description: Harden the portal with secure session management, strong authentication, and regular security testing for the submission interface.
mitigations.rationale: Portal security controls reduce the chance that unauthorized users can submit or view information.

mitigations.description: Keep multifactor authentication mandatory and require documented approval checks for each staffer account request.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To access the CS Portal, staffers must register and create an account, which requires them to verify their identity through multifactor authentication. Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
mitigations.rationale: The stated identity verification and approval steps directly reduce the risk of unauthorized account access.

mitigations.description: Use least-privilege cloud access controls and configuration reviews for Dynamics 365, Dataverse, and SharePoint Online.
mitigations.rationale: Tight cloud permissions and configuration management help prevent accidental exposure of sensitive records.

risks.description: The repository combines enrollment, claims, pharmacy, encounter, provider, and Medicare-related data into person-level longitudinal records, creating a high risk of re-identification and broad internal exposure of highly sensitive health information.
risks.evidence_quote: ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program
risks.rationale: A repository that links multiple health and enrollment datasets over time can reveal detailed individual health and coverage histories even when some analyses are non-identifiable.

risks.description: The system uses identifiable records for longitudinal analysis, which increases the risk that data could be repurposed or accessed beyond the minimum necessary for a given analysis.
risks.evidence_quote: OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
risks.rationale: Identifiable longitudinal records are more privacy-sensitive than aggregated data because they enable ongoing tracking of individuals across plan changes and time.

risks.description: The data may be used to identify potential fraud, waste, abuse, overpayments, and improperly disbursed amounts, which can lead to adverse individual scrutiny or decisions based on analytical flags.
risks.evidence_quote: the data will be used to detect patterns indicative of potential fraud, waste, and abuse, including but not limited to identifying potential overpayments and improperly disbursed amounts.
risks.rationale: Analytical detection of suspected misuse can incorrectly implicate individuals or families if the underlying data are incomplete or misinterpreted.

risks.description: Enrollment data may reveal that an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract, exposing potentially sensitive coverage anomalies if accessed or disclosed inappropriately.
risks.evidence_quote: For example, enrollment data may reveal instances where an enrollee is covered under more than one FEHB contract.
risks.rationale: Coverage anomalies can reveal personal circumstances and can be sensitive if not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system receives and shares data through multiple external systems and data sharing agreements, increasing the risk of unauthorized disclosure or inconsistent protections across partners.
risks.evidence_quote: These systems include the FEHB Data Hub ... the EHRI warehouse ... and the Centralized Enrollment Reconciliation ... through data sharing agreements.
risks.rationale: Each external exchange adds another point where privacy safeguards must be consistently applied.

risks.description: CMS provides service use and cost data for FEHB enrollees and eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare, creating a risk of exposing dual-coverage and utilization information across programs.
risks.evidence_quote: Centers for Medicare Clearinghouse System (CLER) operated for OPM by NFC ... provides service use and cost data3 to OPM, including health claims information for FEHB enrollees and their eligible family members who are also enrolled in Medicare programs.
risks.rationale: Combining FEHB and Medicare data can reveal more about an individual's health coverage and service use than either program alone.

risks.description: The system analyzes service use and cost across population groups, geographic areas, health plans, providers, and disease conditions, which can create privacy risks from small-cell or inferential disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: These analyses may include examination of the cost of care, utilization of services, and comparing these across specific population groups, geographic areas, health plans, health care providers, and disease conditions.
risks.rationale: Cross-tabulated health analyses can make it easier to infer information about identifiable people or small groups.

risks.description: The repository includes pharmacy manufacturer payments and rebate information, which may expose commercially sensitive and potentially linkable benefit details if not protected.
risks.evidence_quote: Pharmacy claims data also includes pharmacy manufacturer payments and rebate information to allow for a comprehensive assessment of pharmacy benefits in the FEHB program.
risks.rationale: Detailed pharmacy benefit data can reveal both individual utilization patterns and sensitive payment arrangements.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the repository and require de-identification or aggregation for routine analysis, using identifiable longitudinal records only when specifically needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While much of the analyses based on service use and cost data conducted by OPM will be completed using non-identifiable data, OPM also requires record-level identifiable data to create person-level longitudinal records.
mitigations.rationale: Using non-identifiable data by default reduces the chance that sensitive health histories are exposed.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access controls and data minimization so identifiable longitudinal records are available only to staff with a documented need.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to the minimum necessary reduces the privacy impact of person-level tracking.

mitigations.description: Require human review and corroboration before any fraud, waste, or abuse flag is used for action against an individual.
mitigations.rationale: A review step helps prevent harmful decisions based on false positives or incomplete analytical signals.

mitigations.description: Handle dual-enrollment findings as sensitive exceptions and disclose them only to authorized personnel for reconciliation purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Typically, such an occurrence would be identified and addressed outside of ROVR, but data from ROVR may be used as part of the analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting handling of enrollment anomalies to authorized reconciliation reduces unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Ensure all data sharing agreements specify permitted uses, retention, storage protocols, and privacy safeguards before any exchange occurs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Agreements constitute the methods of use and applicable retention and storage protocols.
mitigations.rationale: Clear contractual controls reduce the risk that partner systems handle data inconsistently or beyond the authorized purpose.

mitigations.description: Segregate Medicare-related data and apply enhanced access controls for dual-enrollee records.
mitigations.rationale: Separating the most sensitive cross-program records limits unnecessary exposure of combined coverage information.

mitigations.description: Suppress or aggregate small groups in reports and analyses to reduce inferential disclosure from comparisons across populations, geographies, and conditions.
mitigations.rationale: Small-cell suppression helps prevent readers from inferring information about specific individuals.

mitigations.description: Treat pharmacy manufacturer payment and rebate fields as sensitive analytical data and restrict their disclosure to authorized analytic uses only.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to detailed pharmacy payment data reduces the chance of revealing sensitive benefit or commercial information.

risks.description: The system retains debtor data indefinitely on the mainframe, which increases the privacy impact if records are no longer needed or if a breach occurs.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
risks.rationale: Long-term retention expands the amount of personal data exposed over time and makes any compromise more consequential.

risks.description: The system contains highly sensitive identifiers, including Social Security Numbers stored as debtor IDs and debtor numbers, creating a risk of identity theft or misuse if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO)
risks.rationale: SSNs are high-risk identifiers because disclosure can enable identity fraud and improper linkage across records.

risks.description: The system maintains mailing addresses and debt information about federal employees, separated employees, retirees, and vendors, which could reveal financial distress or other sensitive personal circumstances if disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount
risks.rationale: Debt and contact information are sensitive because they can expose financial status and facilitate unwanted contact or stigma.

risks.description: Many authorized users across approximately 35 USDA agencies and about 160 Federal agencies can access agency-specific data, creating a broad internal access surface and risk of overexposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized agency users of approximately 35 USDA agencies have access to this data.
risks.rationale: The more organizations and users that can access the data, the greater the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse.

risks.description: Contractors may access the system, which introduces additional privacy risk from non-federal personnel handling debtor information.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized by agency functional manager and submitted by the agency security officer.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the set of people who can view or process personal data beyond federal staff.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to their ABCO records, which can make it harder for them to review, correct, or challenge inaccurate debt information.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
risks.rationale: Without direct access, individuals may have limited ability to detect and seek correction of errors affecting them.

risks.description: The system sends personal data to external Treasury systems and Iron Mountain, creating disclosure and transmission risk outside USDA.
risks.evidence_quote: ABCO provides data to the following:  Department of Treasury – Treasury Offset Program  Department of Treasury – Intra Governmental Payment and Collection System  Iron Mountain - Digital Records Center for Images System
risks.rationale: Sharing with external recipients increases the number of entities that must protect the information and can widen exposure.

risks.description: Payroll reports are converted to PDF, encrypted, and transmitted to Iron Mountain by contractors at a local facility, which creates handling risk during file preparation and transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Iron Mountain contractors at a local facility in Harahan, LA, convert Payroll reports from ABCO into PDF files, encrypt the files, and transmit them to Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA.
risks.rationale: Manual file conversion and contractor handling introduce opportunities for accidental disclosure or mishandling before transmission.

risks.description: The system relies on data provided by agencies and employees, so inaccurate or outdated source data could lead to incorrect billing or debt collection records.
risks.evidence_quote: Federal agencies and employees can provide data for use in the system.
risks.rationale: If source data is wrong, the system may maintain or disseminate incorrect personal and financial information.

mitigations.description: Apply a documented records review and deletion schedule for mainframe records so data is not kept indefinitely when no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the volume and age of personal data exposed to breach or misuse.

mitigations.description: Replace SSNs with a non-SSN unique identifier wherever possible and restrict access to SSN-bearing fields to the minimum necessary users.
mitigations.evidence_quote: their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as “Debtor ID” in ABCO)
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN use lowers the risk of identity theft if records are accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Limit display and reporting of mailing addresses and debt amounts to only what is necessary for billing and collection functions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: their mailing addresses used to send bills to, information about the debt owed (to be collected) such as amount
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing exposure of contact and debt details reduces the sensitivity of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Continuously review and recertify user access across USDA and Federal agencies to ensure least-privilege access remains appropriate.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is based on the principle of least Privacy Impact Assessment Administrative Billings and Collections System (ABCO) Page 7 privilege, which refers to granting the minimum required system resources to a user that enables them to perform their duties/access their data.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access review helps ensure broad multi-agency access does not exceed operational need.

mitigations.description: Require contractor-specific access approvals, training, and periodic access reviews before and during system access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes, if authorized by agency functional manager and submitted by the agency security officer.
mitigations.rationale: Additional controls for contractors reduce the risk of unauthorized disclosure by non-federal personnel.

mitigations.description: Provide an individual access and correction process through the responsible agency even though direct ABCO access is not available.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to ABCO data. Only authorized agency users have access to data in the system.
mitigations.rationale: A formal correction path helps individuals identify and fix inaccurate debt records affecting them.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and minimum-necessary disclosures for Treasury and Iron Mountain exchanges, with periodic verification of recipient safeguards.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ABCO provides data to the following:  Department of Treasury – Treasury Offset Program  Department of Treasury – Intra Governmental Payment and Collection System  Iron Mountain - Digital Records Center for Images System
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what is shared and confirming recipient protections lowers the risk from external disclosures.

mitigations.description: Move file preparation and transmission to a controlled, audited automated workflow with role-based access and logging.
mitigations.rationale: Automation and audit logs reduce the handling risk created by manual contractor conversion and transfer of payroll reports.

mitigations.description: Strengthen validation and reconciliation with routine source-data verification against authoritative agency records before billing is generated.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ABCO application code provides reconciliation routines at the application level.
mitigations.rationale: Better source-data verification helps prevent inaccurate personal and debt information from being billed or shared.

risks.description: The system may collect more personal information from members of the public than is necessary because correspondence can include voluntary details beyond basic contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: In a few cases, it may also include other information about the individual voluntarily provided by that individual in the correspondence.
risks.rationale: The PIA shows the system can ingest free-form correspondence that may contain extra PII beyond the core contact fields.

risks.description: The system stores and uses contact information that could expose individuals if improperly accessed or handled.
risks.evidence_quote: The system will include information regarding individuals, primarily information such as the name, address, phone number, and email address incidental to their correspondence addressed to the Secretary of Agriculture and various other officers and employees of USDA.
risks.rationale: Names and contact details are directly identifying and are retained in a centralized system.

risks.description: Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information, which could create an unwanted disclosure or use beyond the original correspondence purpose if not controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
risks.rationale: Using contact details for follow-up increases the privacy impact of the collected information.

risks.description: Centralizing correspondence in a single content management system increases the impact of any unauthorized access because many users can access and interact with the records.
risks.evidence_quote: AgWrite is a content management (CMS) system owned and managed by the Office of the Executive Secretariat (OES). AgWrite is being leveraged to provide standardized processes and role-based controls to support the receipt and processing of correspondence and other artifacts that require ingestion, review, and approval by business units across USDA.
risks.rationale: A centralized repository holding correspondence and PII creates a larger concentration of sensitive data.

risks.description: Tracking package movement and workflow status can create internal visibility into who submitted correspondence and how it is handled, which may expose sensitive interaction history if improperly disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: A typical transaction in the system is a user accessing a package record, reviewing the content and metadata, documenting changes to the metadata or producing research or a response to received correspondence, and tracking the movement of the packages between different users and user groups.
risks.rationale: Workflow and metadata records can reveal more about a person's interaction with USDA than the correspondence alone.

risks.description: Using NLP and machine learning to analyze historical correspondence and generate results from similar inquiries may surface personal information in ways users do not expect.
risks.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
risks.rationale: Automated retrieval based on historical content can expose information embedded in prior correspondence.

risks.description: Search, dashboard, and report outputs may reveal correspondence status and categories tied to individuals, increasing the chance of overexposure through internal reporting.
risks.evidence_quote: To analyze data, Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used. Search data produced could pertain to correspondence as they progress through workflows within the system (e.g., stage/status agency, priority or categorization, time in a particular status, time to progress from initiated to completed, congressional inquiries, etc.).
risks.rationale: Aggregated views and reports can expose operational details that are not necessary for every user.

risks.description: The system may retain physical and email addresses for correspondence purposes without a clearly stated retention limit in the provided context, increasing the risk of keeping PII longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Physical and e-mail addresses will be particularly maintained for correspondence purposes.
risks.rationale: The context confirms ongoing maintenance of address data but does not specify a retention boundary here.

mitigations.description: Limit collection to only the PII needed to process the correspondence and instruct users to redact or avoid unnecessary personal details in submissions.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is accepted and retained reduces the chance of over-collection from public correspondence.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls so only authorized staff handling the correspondence can view identifying contact information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: standardized processes and role-based controls
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access lowers the risk of improper viewing or disclosure of contact data.

mitigations.description: Use phone numbers only when necessary for follow-up and document the purpose for each contact attempt.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Phone numbers may be used to contact individuals for more information.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting follow-up contact to necessary cases reduces unnecessary use of personal contact information.

mitigations.description: Continue enforcing role-based controls and limit access to correspondence records to business units that need them for ingestion, review, or approval.
mitigations.evidence_quote: role-based controls to support the receipt and processing of correspondence and other artifacts that require ingestion, review, and approval by business units across USDA
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access helps protect the centralized repository from broad internal exposure.

mitigations.description: Restrict metadata editing and workflow-tracking views to authorized personnel and log all changes to package records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: documenting changes to the metadata or producing research or a response to received correspondence, and tracking the movement of the packages between different users and user groups.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter control and auditability reduce the chance that workflow history is misused or improperly disclosed.

mitigations.description: Review and test NLP and ML search results to ensure they do not surface unnecessary personal information from historical correspondence.
mitigations.evidence_quote: the system will use enhance searching capabilities driven by Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to return results based on historical content and responses from similar inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Testing and review can limit unintended disclosure through automated retrieval.

mitigations.description: Limit dashboard and report access to authorized users and suppress personal identifiers in routine reporting where possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Appian tasks, dashboards, and reports will be used.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting reporting access and reducing identifiers in outputs lowers the risk of overexposure.

mitigations.description: Establish and enforce a retention schedule that deletes correspondence PII when it is no longer needed for processing or records obligations.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention limit prevents unnecessary long-term storage of address information.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive discrimination and employee complaint records, which could cause significant harm if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information includes complaints of discrimination against USDA programs and services and employee complaints.
risks.rationale: Complaint files can reveal sensitive employment and civil rights allegations.

risks.description: The system collects direct personal contact and identifying information, creating a risk of identity exposure if the records are breached or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: It uses complainant personal information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and miscellaneous identification numbers (generates a case number).
risks.rationale: Names, contact details, and identifiers are directly linkable to individuals.

risks.description: Information is entered from mail, email, telephone, and interviews, which increases the risk of collecting inaccurate or incomplete data.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is received by mail, email, telephone or interviews. It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
risks.rationale: Multiple intake channels can introduce transcription or source errors.

risks.description: Because approved users manually input the information, there is a risk of insider mishandling or unauthorized disclosure by staff with access.
risks.evidence_quote: It is then inputted into the system by approved users.
risks.rationale: Manual handling by users creates opportunities for misuse or accidental exposure.

risks.description: Contractor access creates a risk that non-government personnel could access complaint PII beyond what is necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Will Department contractors have access to the system? YES
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the set of people who may view sensitive records.

risks.description: The system is connected to the public Internet, which increases exposure to external cyber threats.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway
risks.rationale: Internet connectivity increases the attack surface for unauthorized access or interception.

risks.description: Because the system is co-located at a contractor site and the contractor provides security services, there is a risk of reduced direct government control over the data environment.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES is co-located at MicroPact Engineering, Inc. MicroPact Engineering provides system, network, development, and administrative security under contract with The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
risks.rationale: Third-party hosting and administration can complicate oversight and accountability.

risks.description: The system retains files until destruction based on judicial regulations, which may keep complaint data longer than necessary if retention is not tightly managed.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES’s files are destroyed, based on the judicial’ s regulations.
risks.rationale: Long or unclear retention increases the time sensitive PII remains exposed.

risks.description: The system collects information when individuals contact OASCR and states they cannot decline to provide it, which limits individual control over their personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: Do individuals have the opportunity and/or right to decline to provide information? N/A. When the individual contacts OASCR, they provide the information necessary for OASCR to investigate the case.
risks.rationale: Individuals may have limited ability to avoid disclosure once they seek assistance.

mitigations.description: Limit access to complaint records to only personnel with a demonstrated need to know and enforce role-based permissions with logging and periodic review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance of improper viewing of sensitive complaint data.

mitigations.description: Minimize the personal identifiers collected and mask or truncate identifiers such as case numbers where full values are not needed for daily work.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting less identifying information reduces the impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Validate intake data against source documents and use standardized entry checks before records are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Verification helps catch errors introduced through multi-channel manual intake.

mitigations.description: Train approved users on privacy handling and require disciplinary controls for improper access or disclosure.
mitigations.rationale: Training and accountability reduce insider misuse risk.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary functions and require the same privacy and security controls that apply to federal users.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege contractor access lowers exposure from non-government personnel.

mitigations.description: Harden the Internet-facing gateway with strong authentication, continuous monitoring, and regular vulnerability management.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CRES server environment is interconnected to the public Internet via a MicroPact managed gateway that includes a Cisco routers and switches, Fortigate and Firebox Firewall appliances, and Linksys switches.
mitigations.rationale: Internet-facing systems need layered controls to reduce external attack risk.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular government oversight of the contractor-hosted environment, including security reviews and access audits.
mitigations.rationale: Oversight helps ensure the contractor environment remains compliant and controlled.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retention schedules and destroy records as soon as the approved retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The OASCR Records Manager and Department Records Manager have developed the goals and timelines for reporting and adhering to records management requirements issued by the National Archive Records and Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Office of Personnel Management.
mitigations.rationale: Timely destruction limits how long sensitive records remain exposed.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear privacy notice at intake explaining what information is required and why it is needed for the investigation.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice improves transparency when individuals must provide information to proceed.

risks.description: Users can enter unrestricted free-text in the "About Me" section, which may lead to collection of unnecessary or highly sensitive personal information beyond what the system needs.
risks.evidence_quote: there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: Unrestricted free-text fields commonly create overcollection and sensitive-disclosure risk because users may enter more than is necessary.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information that is not required for operation, increasing the impact if the data is misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
risks.rationale: Collecting optional PII still creates privacy exposure because the system maintains identifying data that is not essential to the service.

risks.description: Photographs combined with names create a stronger identifier and increase the risk of unauthorized identification or profile exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
risks.rationale: A photo paired with a name makes it easier to identify a person and increases the privacy impact of any disclosure.

risks.description: The system collects address information and miscellaneous identification numbers, which could be used to locate or track individuals if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: - Name - Address information - Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers and permit numbers can be sensitive because they can link a person to a place, service, or request.

risks.description: Sharing data through Tableau dashboards and reports across multiple administrative domains can expose personal information more broadly than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions. The information shared will span data from different various administrative domains including IT, Finance, HR, Property, Operations, Homeland Security, and Property & Fleet.
risks.rationale: Broad internal dissemination increases the chance that people who do not need the information for their duties will see it.

risks.description: Moving data into the USDA Data Lake creates a centralized repository that could increase the impact of unauthorized access or secondary use.
risks.evidence_quote: The information will be transmitted to the USDA Data Lake via secure file transfer methods such as SFTP, API, and Web Service. Once in the USDA data Lake, data will be shared via a series of Tableau dashboards.
risks.rationale: Centralized aggregation raises privacy risk because one repository can expose data from multiple functions if access controls fail.

risks.description: Contractors with access to the system may pose a privacy risk if their authorization or clearance is not tightly limited to the minimum necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Only specifically authorized Department contractors have access to the system. Those individuals must first obtain relevant security clearances along with specific authorization to access information at various levels.
risks.rationale: Even authorized contractor access can broaden exposure if permissions are not carefully scoped and reviewed.

risks.description: Collecting information by email to create accounts may expose personal data during transmission or through misdirected messages.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected by email from each user initially to create the account within Salesforce.
risks.rationale: Email-based intake is prone to accidental disclosure because messages can be intercepted, forwarded, or sent to the wrong recipient.

mitigations.description: Restrict the "About Me" field with validation, guidance, or removal so users can only enter approved, minimal information needed for the system.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting free-text entry reduces the chance that users will disclose unnecessary or sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Make PII collection optional only where needed and clearly minimize the fields collected to the smallest set required for the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII is not required for the proper operation of the OSCAR system and is provided solely at the discretion of the user.
mitigations.rationale: Because the system does not require PII to function, minimizing collection directly reduces privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Keep profile photos optional and provide clear notice that photos are PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Upon Salesforce user access, the user has the option to update their profile within Salesforce to include a photo, which is considered PII when combined with a name.
mitigations.rationale: Optional collection and notice help users avoid adding an identifier they may not want associated with their account.

mitigations.description: Limit access to names, addresses, and permit numbers to staff who need them for parking permits or request handling.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the number of people who can see direct identifiers and permit-related data.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and report-level filtering so Tableau dashboards show only the minimum personal information necessary for each audience.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting what each audience can view reduces unnecessary internal disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict access controls and data governance in the USDA Data Lake to prevent secondary use beyond the approved reporting purpose.
mitigations.rationale: Controls on the centralized repository help prevent broader exposure and misuse of aggregated data.

mitigations.description: Regularly review contractor permissions and remove access when it is no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review helps ensure contractor access stays limited to authorized personnel and current business needs.

mitigations.description: Replace email intake with a more secure account-creation workflow or require encryption and verification for any email submissions.
mitigations.rationale: A controlled intake process lowers the chance of accidental disclosure during account setup.

risks.description: The system centralizes physical access and visitor identity data across USDA facilities, which creates a broad privacy impact if the database is misused or breached because it links names, photos, card status, access rights, and location data in one place.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS provides a centralized infrastructure for the use of the USDA standard identification card (LincPass) for access to federally controlled facilities
risks.rationale: Centralizing access-control PII increases the sensitivity and potential impact of unauthorized access or misuse.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains visitor data for the Washington, D.C. visitor management function, including background-check-related processing, which can expose non-employee visitors to privacy risk beyond ordinary facility access control.
risks.evidence_quote: With the addition of the VMS to ePACS, visitor data will be registered when meetings are scheduled by the meeting sponsor. The VMS will provide an integrated solution for background checking of visitors.
risks.rationale: Visitor screening and registration can reveal personal information about people who are not USDA employees.

risks.description: The system uses manually collected non-authoritative data at card issuance, which creates a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records affecting access decisions and privacy rights.
risks.evidence_quote: Also, Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
risks.rationale: Manually entered data is more prone to error than authoritative sources and can lead to incorrect access records.

risks.description: The system shares limited PII and credential read activity with EDAPT for executive management dashboards, which can expand internal visibility into employee movement and access patterns beyond the original access-control purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: EDAPT receives last name, first name and credential card read activity.
risks.rationale: Access-activity data can reveal behavioral patterns and should be tightly limited to need-to-know use.

risks.description: The system sends employee name and status information to the Credit Card Service Center by email, which creates a privacy risk if email is intercepted, misaddressed, or retained improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The Fleet report provides last name, first name and employee status.
risks.rationale: Email is a common source of accidental disclosure unless additional controls are applied.

risks.description: The system allows access to USDA employees and select contractors, which increases the number of people who may view sensitive PII and access records.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: Broader access populations increase the chance of unauthorized disclosure or insider misuse.

risks.description: The system retains live and archived access-control data for 5.5 years, which increases the amount of historical personal information available if records are searched, disclosed, or compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases exposure time and the volume of personal data held by the system.

risks.description: The system stores and disseminates personal identity data through a staging table and multiple databases, which creates additional internal handling points where unauthorized access or leakage could occur.
risks.evidence_quote: This identity data is provided from a series of USDA Human Resources databases which are consolidated into ICAM Shared services. The staging table then disseminates the current identity data to the information systems as applicable.
risks.rationale: Each transfer and storage location adds a potential point of compromise.

risks.description: The system includes emergency responder information and emergency response responsibilities, which could reveal sensitive role-based information about individuals if improperly disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS generally handles physical access Security Management Information including: x Physical access card holder emergency response responsibilities
risks.rationale: Role-specific emergency information can be sensitive because it identifies special duties or preparedness roles.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the centralized ePACS databases and reports to strictly necessary personnel and apply strong auditing and monitoring for all access to PII and access logs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The disclosure of information is prohibited based on the "Need-to-Know" principle as those with authorized interest will have been granted access.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the chance that centralized data will be viewed or used unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Restrict visitor data collection to the minimum needed for scheduling and access control, and apply a clear visitor notice describing background-check processing and retention.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The VMS will only include visitors arriving at USDA National Capitol Region (NCR) Headquarters (HQ includes South, Whitten, and Yates buildings).
mitigations.rationale: Limiting collection and providing notice reduces unnecessary exposure for visitors.

mitigations.description: Validate manually entered card-issuance data against authoritative sources before activation and provide a correction process for affected individuals.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Non-Authoritative data is manually collected at the time of card issuance and stored into ePACS.
mitigations.rationale: Verification and correction controls reduce the risk that inaccurate data will drive access decisions.

mitigations.description: Minimize the information sent to EDAPT to only what is necessary for executive reporting and suppress card-read activity unless it is required for a specific approved purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limited ePACS data is transmitted to the Enterprise Data Analytics Platform & Toolset (EDAPT) via secure file transfer method at 2 a.m. daily.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing shared fields lowers the privacy impact of internal analytics and dashboards.

mitigations.description: Replace email transmission of the Fleet report with a more secure delivery method or encrypt the report end-to-end and limit distribution to approved recipients only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Fleet report is utilized for employee status to disable credit cards.
mitigations.rationale: More secure delivery lowers the chance of accidental disclosure through email.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls, periodic access reviews, and contractor-specific least-privilege permissions for all users and contractors.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
mitigations.rationale: Least-privilege controls help ensure only necessary users can view sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Periodically review archived records and purge or de-identify data that is no longer needed before the full retention period ends when allowed by records rules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary stored history decreases the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Harden the staging table and database interfaces with access controls, encryption, and logging for all data transfers between source systems and ePACS.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The staging table then disseminates the current identity data to the information systems as applicable.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting intermediate transfer points reduces the chance of unauthorized access during data movement.

mitigations.description: Classify emergency responder fields as sensitive and limit their display to personnel who need them for emergency operations or access administration.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ePACS generally handles physical access Security Management Information including: x Physical access card holder emergency response responsibilities
mitigations.rationale: Restricting sensitive role information reduces unnecessary disclosure of special responsibilities.

risks.description: The system collects personally identifiable information from USDA employees, creating a risk of exposure if the cloud-based travel platform is breached or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Based on the Privacy Threshold Assessment submitted in December 2023, this system does collect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from USDA employees, and therefore, a PIA is necessary.
risks.rationale: Any system that collects employee PII must protect it against unauthorized access and disclosure.

risks.description: The system retains user information and bill-related data for long periods, increasing the amount of personal data exposed over time.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase the consequences of a security incident and extend the window in which data can be accessed.

risks.description: Travel preference profiling can reveal behavioral patterns about employees, which may create unnecessary privacy exposure if used beyond travel booking.
risks.evidence_quote: The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference data can be sensitive because it reveals recurring choices and habits tied to identifiable users.

risks.description: Authorization and voucher data are transmitted to another financial system, creating a risk of disclosure or misuse during sharing between systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Transmitting personal and financial travel records to another system expands the number of places where the data must be protected.

risks.description: Enterprise-wide use and access by authorized agency users expand the number of people who can view travel records, increasing insider-access risk.
risks.evidence_quote: This system is used Enterprise-wide. Authorized USDA agency users access the ConcurGov system the same way as ACFO-FMS internal users.
risks.rationale: Broader access increases the chance that sensitive information could be viewed by users who do not need it.

risks.description: The system relies on centralized authentication and cloud access, so compromise of credentials or session controls could expose employee travel data.
risks.evidence_quote: USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
risks.rationale: Centralized login systems are high-value targets because they gate access to many users and records.

mitigations.description: Limit access to PII through restrictive roles and protect data in transit with TLS 1.2 and other session-authentication controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Limitations are applied through the assignment of restrictive roles. Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
mitigations.rationale: Role restriction and encrypted transmission reduce the chance that employee PII is exposed to unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Apply the approved NARA and USDA retention schedule consistently and delete records when the retention period ends.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention to the approved schedule reduces the amount of personal data kept unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Restrict use of preference data to travel convenience functions and avoid secondary use or sharing of predictive preference profiles.
mitigations.rationale: Keeping preference profiling narrowly scoped reduces privacy impact from behavioral inferences.

mitigations.description: Continue validating Authorization and Voucher data with audit checks before transmission and encrypt the transfer end to end.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and encryption help ensure only authorized, accurate records are shared with the receiving system.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews so enterprise-wide users only receive the minimum roles needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting user privileges reduces insider-access exposure across a broad user base.

mitigations.description: Maintain strong multi-factor authentication and session protection for eAUTH and the cloud application, including monitoring for abnormal logins.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CCPS employs the following solutions to protect authenticity of communication sessions and communications leveraging: • Multifactor authentication
mitigations.rationale: Strong authentication and session monitoring reduce the risk that compromised credentials lead to unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system retains USDA employee information for a long period, which increases the chance that personal data could be exposed, misused, or repurposed over time. The retention of billing-related records for six full years also extends the window in which sensitive travel and financial information remains available.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases exposure if records are breached or accessed inappropriately.

risks.description: The system creates and retains traveler preferences and predictive patterns, which may reveal personal habits or travel behavior beyond what is strictly necessary for a transaction. Storing preferences such as airline seating, rental car companies, and hotel details can build a profile of an employee’s choices.
risks.evidence_quote: Travelers can set up preferences within their profiles that are retained for future reference. The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Preference profiling can expose behavioral information that users may not expect to persist in a government travel system.

risks.description: The system shares authorization and voucher data with another financial system, which creates a privacy risk if only the minimum necessary information is not transferred. Once data leaves the travel system, it is subject to additional handling and potential access in the receiving environment.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
risks.rationale: Sharing personal travel and payment data across systems expands the number of places where it can be accessed or exposed.

risks.description: The system is accessible through standard web browsers and mobile applications, which increases exposure to interception or unauthorized access if endpoints or sessions are compromised. Mobile and browser-based access can broaden the attack surface for PII in travel records.
risks.evidence_quote: Users access CCPS by using standard web browsers via a uniform resource locator (URL) or by using SAP Concur mobile applications.
risks.rationale: More access channels generally create more opportunities for account compromise or data leakage.

risks.description: The system is multi-tenant and enterprise-wide, so data from many customers and users is processed in a shared environment, increasing the impact of a tenant isolation failure or misconfiguration. If role restrictions or tenancy controls fail, one user could see another user’s travel information.
risks.evidence_quote: Concur Cloud for Public Sector (CCPS) is a multi-tenant, end-to-end, fully integrated travel, and expense platform
risks.rationale: Shared environments require strong segregation to prevent cross-user or cross-tenant disclosure.

risks.description: The system relies on centralized authentication for access, so compromise of authentication credentials could expose travel and expense records. Because access is tied to USDA eAuthentication, a stolen or misused account could provide broad access to PII.
risks.evidence_quote: USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
risks.rationale: Centralized login systems are high-value targets and can enable broad unauthorized access if compromised.

mitigations.description: Enforce the approved records schedule and periodically review stored records to delete or archive data when the retention period expires.
mitigations.evidence_quote: User information is retained in compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention guidelines for financial management data. Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Limit traveler preference and predictive-profile data to what is necessary for booking, and provide users a way to review and clear saved preferences.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored preference data reduces unnecessary behavioral profiling.

mitigations.description: Apply strict data-minimization and field-level review before transmitting authorization and voucher data to FMMI so only the information needed for budget and accounting validation is shared.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Authorization and Voucher data are validated for Travel Policy by employing Audit checks before the Authorization and Voucher are transmitted to the Financial Management Modernization Initiative (FMMI) for budget and accounting validation.
mitigations.rationale: Sending only necessary fields lowers the privacy impact of intersystem sharing.

mitigations.description: Require strong endpoint security and session protections for browser and mobile access, including device hygiene checks and session timeout controls.
