risks.description: The system depends on account disabling when a user leaves, so stale accounts could remain a privacy risk if deprovisioning is delayed or incomplete.
risks.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
risks.rationale: Delayed account disabling can leave former users with unnecessary access to personal data.

mitigations.description: Limit profile fields to the minimum required for authorization and business operations, and periodically review whether each field is still needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab contains a minimal amount of contact information related to CoLab users.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing stored data reduces the amount of personal information at risk.

mitigations.description: Restrict collection of personal contact information to only cases where it is necessary and document why those extra fields are needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: For some individuals, personal contact information is maintained in their profile.
mitigations.rationale: Collecting extra contact details only when necessary lowers privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Require strong eAuth authentication and periodic access reviews for CoLab project membership and profile access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When establishing authorization privileges for users to access CoLab, the identity of the person must be known to NRCS via their USDA eAuth User ID.
mitigations.rationale: Strong identity verification and review help prevent unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege role assignments and routinely audit contractor and partner access to ensure it matches current duties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, authorized contractors and partners will have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to what each role needs reduces insider and overexposure risk.

mitigations.description: Add validation and user guidance for profile edits so users can only change approved fields and are warned not to enter unnecessary personal data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
mitigations.rationale: Controls on self-service edits help keep profile data accurate and limited.

mitigations.description: Set and enforce a defined deletion schedule for inactive or unneeded profiles instead of retaining them for the full production life of the application.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Deleting data when it is no longer needed reduces the duration of privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Automate offboarding so accounts are promptly disabled when users leave and verify completion through periodic account reconciliation.
mitigations.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
mitigations.rationale: Prompt deprovisioning prevents former users from retaining access after separation.

risks.description: The system stores vendor names and contact information in the IDEA DataMart, which creates a risk of unauthorized access to identifiable personal data if the data store is compromised or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Persisting PII in a reporting datastore increases exposure compared with purely transitory use.

risks.description: The system processes transitory PII through read-only web service calls, creating a risk that personal data could be exposed during retrieval or processing even if it is not stored long term.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of these IDEA reports rely upon transitory read-only vendor PII that is obtained from SCIMS via web service calls, noting that this transitory PH is not maintained in the application database.
risks.rationale: Data in transit or temporary processing can still be intercepted, logged, or mishandled.

risks.description: The system uses selectable criteria from drop-down menus to produce reports, which could allow users to infer or assemble more personal information than intended from report outputs.
risks.evidence_quote: While IDEA does not process any transactions, the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
risks.rationale: Flexible reporting can increase the chance of unintended disclosure through overly broad queries or outputs.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, so vendor PII could be viewed or handled by personnel beyond direct government staff if access controls are not tightly enforced.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any non-employee access raises the risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: PII is refreshed periodically from SCIMS, so outdated or incorrect vendor contact information may persist between refreshes and be used in reports.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Periodic refreshes create a window in which stale data can be retained and used.

risks.description: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production, which can extend the exposure period for any PII stored in the DataMart.
risks.evidence_quote: Application-specific information is retained while the application remains in production.
risks.rationale: Longer retention generally increases the chance of unauthorized access or secondary use.

mitigations.description: Minimize the amount of vendor PII stored in IDEA DataMart and apply strict role-based access controls and encryption to the stored records.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing stored PII and protecting it at rest lowers the impact of any datastore compromise.

mitigations.description: Keep the read-only SCIMS integration limited to the minimum necessary fields and log or suppress any temporary copies of vendor PII during web service processing.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting fields and temporary handling reduces the chance that transitory data is exposed.

mitigations.description: Restrict report criteria and outputs to approved business needs and review report templates to prevent unnecessary disclosure of vendor PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: While IDEA does not process any transactions, the application allows the user to produce reports using selectable criteria from drop-down menus.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining report generation reduces the chance of overbroad or unintended disclosure.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews for contractors and verify that only users with a documented need to know can access vendor PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors, with a need to know, will have access to FSA Compliance as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access controls reduce the insider disclosure risk from contractor access.

mitigations.description: Shorten the refresh interval or validate report data against SCIMS at the time of use to reduce the chance of stale vendor information being reported.
mitigations.rationale: More frequent validation reduces the window in which outdated PII can be used.

mitigations.description: Apply a defined retention schedule that deletes vendor PII from IDEA DataMart as soon as it is no longer needed for reporting, legal, audit, or operational purposes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per NARA General Records Schedule 20, application-specific information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the time personal data remains exposed.

risks.description: Core Services handles identifiable customer data that can be linked to highly sensitive identifiers, creating a risk of improper disclosure or re-identification if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number
risks.rationale: A customer ID that can be associated with SSNs or TINs increases the sensitivity and impact of any unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system transmits PII between multiple internal systems and client applications, increasing the chance of exposure during data exchange or integration failures.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services shares and transmits USDA application data and metadata between several USDA internal systems to include client applications, back-end databases and adjacent systems.
risks.rationale: More system-to-system movement creates more opportunities for interception, misrouting, or unintended disclosure.

risks.description: A single external-facing gateway serves as the entry point for requests, so a compromise or misconfiguration there could expose data or allow unauthorized access to the service.
risks.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
risks.rationale: Concentrating ingress through one gateway makes that component a high-value privacy and security control point.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of insider misuse or overbroad access to customer information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any nonemployee access expands the insider threat surface and requires strict limitation and oversight.

risks.description: Core Services returns requested information to users in JSON format, which could expose more data than necessary if responses are not minimized or filtered.
risks.evidence_quote: will return the data to the user in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) format.
risks.rationale: Structured API responses can inadvertently include excess fields unless output is tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system relies on replicated or copied access to SCIMS data, which raises the risk that stale or duplicated customer information could be exposed beyond its source system controls.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication.
risks.rationale: Replicated data can be harder to govern consistently than data kept only in the source system.

risks.description: Core Services accesses race, sex, national origin, and disability data for reporting, which creates a risk of sensitive demographic information being exposed or used beyond the intended purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
risks.rationale: Demographic attributes are sensitive and warrant tighter access and purpose limitation.

risks.description: Although Core Services says it does not store PII, it stores administrative and transactional information, which may still reveal user activity or customer interactions if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
risks.rationale: Operational logs and transaction records can still be privacy-relevant even when direct PII is not retained.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to only the minimum fields needed for each request and mask or tokenize customer identifiers wherever possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Core Services uses the PII information obtained from the SCIMS database copy to associate a request to a specific client.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposed identifiers reduces the impact of any unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Apply strict API authorization, field-level filtering, and encrypted transport for all system-to-system exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS 4.
mitigations.rationale: Strong transport and authorization controls reduce exposure during internal data exchanges.

mitigations.description: Harden and continuously monitor the API gateway, including intrusion detection, rate limiting, and configuration review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Requests from outside the NRCS firewall are first received by the external-facing CA API Gateway appliance, serving as a single point of entry into the Core Services platform.
mitigations.rationale: A heavily protected gateway lowers the risk that a single entry point becomes a privacy breach path.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege contractor access with periodic access reviews and audit logging of contractor activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review and logging help detect and prevent inappropriate contractor access.

mitigations.description: Implement response minimization so APIs return only the specific fields required for the requesting application.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing API output reduces the chance that unnecessary personal data is disclosed in JSON responses.

mitigations.description: Synchronize replicated SCIMS data with source-system controls and regularly validate that copied data remains current and authorized for use.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS has access to a copy of the SCIMS database via replication.
mitigations.rationale: Replication governance helps prevent stale or improperly exposed customer records.

mitigations.description: Limit access to demographic reporting to authorized personnel and separate reporting datasets from operational client data when possible.
mitigations.evidence_quote: It also allows NRCS managers to generate reports on the race, sex, national origin, and disability of program applicants and participants.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and separating sensitive demographic data reduces the risk of inappropriate use or disclosure.

mitigations.description: Minimize retention of administrative and transactional records and apply retention and disposal controls to those records as well.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The Core Services database is used to store administrative and transactional information for the services only.
mitigations.rationale: Even non-PII operational records can create privacy risk if retained longer than necessary.

risks.description: Emergency Action Plans contain personally identifying details that could expose emergency responders and property owners if the documents are mishandled or disclosed beyond the intended emergency context.
risks.evidence_quote: EAPs contain the name, home address, and telephone number of emergency responders, as well as the names and addresses of property owners that could be impacted by an emergency involving a dam.
risks.rationale: Home addresses and phone numbers are sensitive contact details, and the system stores them in documents that may be shared during reviews or activations.

risks.description: The system may retain PII for a long time, increasing the chance that outdated contact information remains accessible or is exposed over time.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods increase the amount of time PII remains in the system and therefore the window for misuse or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: PII is disclosed in hardcopy or electronic form during review cycles or when an EAP is activated, creating a risk of unauthorized access during transmission or handling.
risks.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
risks.rationale: Each disclosure event creates an opportunity for loss, interception, or improper handling of the documents.

risks.description: State and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site receive access to PII, which broadens the number of people who can view sensitive contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond NRCS staff increases the number of authorized users who could inadvertently or intentionally misuse the information.

risks.description: Contractors with access to the system may pose a privacy risk if their access is not carefully controlled and monitored.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DamWatch as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access introduces additional non-government users who can view sensitive PII and therefore require strong oversight.

risks.description: PII is sourced from publicly accessible information resources and voluntary submissions, which can lead to inaccurate or outdated records being stored and used in emergencies.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII can be obtained from publicly accessible information resources, from organizations involved in emergency response, or submitted voluntarily by individual responders or property owners.
risks.rationale: Information from public sources and voluntary submissions may not be current, and incorrect contact details can affect both privacy and operational use.

risks.description: Because the system stores emergency contact information for each dam, a breach could reveal a centralized set of contact details for multiple people involved in dam response and affected properties.
risks.evidence_quote: The system will also include emergency contact information for each dam.
risks.rationale: Centralizing contact information concentrates sensitive data in one system, increasing the impact of any compromise.

mitigations.description: Limit EAP access to only the specific responders and officials who need the information for a particular dam and require secure handling for all copies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access to site-specific need-to-know users reduces the chance that personal contact details are exposed unnecessarily.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review and purge schedule so EAP PII is removed or updated when no longer needed, rather than relying only on maximum retention periods.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review helps ensure stale PII is not kept longer than operationally necessary.

mitigations.description: Use encrypted secure communications and controlled distribution procedures for both hardcopy and electronic EAP disclosures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: EAPs are considered controlled documents and will be shared via secure communications methods at all times.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transfer and controlled distribution reduce the likelihood of interception or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit responder access to only those assigned to the relevant dam site and review access periodically to confirm the need-to-know still exists.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access is also limited to NRCS employees and contractors support of the DamWatch project as well as state and local emergency responders assigned to a particular dam site.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps prevent unnecessary exposure of PII to users who no longer need it.

mitigations.description: Maintain background investigations for contractors and add periodic access recertification and audit logging for contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Background checks are helpful, and recertification plus logging further reduce the risk of improper contractor access.

mitigations.description: Verify publicly sourced and voluntarily submitted contact information with the originating organization or individual before storing it in an EAP.
mitigations.rationale: Verification improves data quality and reduces the chance that inaccurate PII will be retained and used.

mitigations.description: Encrypt stored EAP files and restrict access with role-based controls so the centralized contact information is protected if the system is compromised.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting the data at rest and limiting access lowers the impact of a breach involving the centralized repository.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers in scanned documents, creating a risk of harm if the records are exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Bulk scanning and metadata extraction can introduce privacy risk if paper records are digitized incorrectly or if metadata is extracted inaccurately, exposing the wrong information or associating records with the wrong person.
risks.evidence_quote: Initially, bulk scanning of paper records and metadata extraction will be staged and retrieved using a bulk submission to metadata stores.
risks.rationale: Bulk processing of records can propagate errors at scale and mislabel or misfile sensitive records.

risks.description: Because individuals do not have direct access to DRMS, they may have limited ability to inspect or correct their own records without going through staff-mediated request procedures.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS. Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Restricted direct access can make it harder for individuals to verify accuracy and exercise privacy rights promptly.

risks.description: Allowing contractors access to records creates a risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse of sensitive records by non-federal personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to DRMS as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the set of people who can see sensitive records and therefore increases insider-risk exposure.

risks.description: Storing records in a cloud system on shared infrastructure increases the risk of misconfiguration or unauthorized access to the records repository.
risks.evidence_quote: The Digital Record Management System (DRMS) is a cloud system that resides on FPAC_AWS_Shared_GSS (FPAC_AWS_GSS).
risks.rationale: Cloud-hosted systems require strong configuration and access controls to prevent exposure of sensitive records.

risks.description: Keeping records for long periods increases the chance that outdated or unnecessary personal information remains available longer than needed.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention periods expand the window in which records can be accessed, misused, or breached.

risks.description: The system relies on scanned PDFs and Adobe PDF plug-ins for viewing, which can expose records through insecure document handling or vulnerable client-side software.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields.
risks.rationale: Document-based systems depend on secure viewing and handling controls to protect embedded personal data.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive documents and metadata to authorized users with documented need-to-know, and monitor access to detect unusual viewing or download activity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and monitoring access reduces the likelihood of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Validate scanned documents and extracted metadata before they are accepted into the system, with quality-control checks for misclassification and indexing errors.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing bulk imports helps prevent incorrect or mismatched records from being stored and retrieved.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear, timely records-access and correction workflow so individuals can request information and corrections without needing direct system access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A formal request process helps individuals exercise privacy rights even when the system itself is not directly accessible to them.

mitigations.description: Apply least-privilege access reviews, enhanced background screening, and periodic auditing for contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Additional oversight of contractor access lowers the risk that non-federal users misuse sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Harden the cloud environment with configuration baselines, segmentation, and continuous security assessment of the host environment.
mitigations.rationale: Strong cloud security controls reduce the chance that shared infrastructure exposes stored records.

mitigations.description: Enforce records schedules and dispose of records when no longer required under the approved retention schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention to approved periods reduces unnecessary long-term exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Use secure PDF handling practices, including patching viewer software and restricting plug-in use to approved, managed devices.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents
mitigations.rationale: Securing the document viewer reduces the risk that records are exposed through client-side vulnerabilities or unsafe handling.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers in documents, creating a significant harm if the repository is exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes the following: • Name • Legal Name • Address • Tax ID number (individual or business) • SSN • Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number • Registration in Central Contractor Registration database • Legal description of farm location • Tract Number • Deeds • Farm Shareholder salaries • Location • Farm ownership detail • Bank routing numbers • Deposit Account numbers • Contract numbers • Vendor ID
risks.rationale: A breach of this repository could expose data that can enable identity theft, financial fraud, or disclosure of sensitive farm and ownership information.

risks.description: Users can upload documents directly into the system, which increases the chance that sensitive information is added without adequate review or minimization.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Direct uploads can introduce unnecessary or overly broad personal data into the repository.

risks.description: The system relies on PDF files and Adobe PDF plug-ins for viewing, which can increase exposure if documents are opened on insecure endpoints or if plugin vulnerabilities are exploited.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is stored in PDF files and is not collected via data entry fields. ... Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents.
risks.rationale: PDF viewing tools and client-side plugins can be a security weak point for sensitive records.

risks.description: DMS uses name and address information from FSA SCIMS to identify the correct producer, which risks misidentification or inappropriate association of records if the matching is wrong.
risks.evidence_quote: DMS uses PII (address and name) from FSA SCIMS to determine which producer is the correct producer.
risks.rationale: Using limited identifiers for matching can lead to linking records to the wrong person.

risks.description: The system permits disclosure to contractors and technical service providers, which creates a risk of secondary use or over-disclosure beyond the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant. Such disclosure is subject to the purposes for which the contractor or technical service provider is hired.
risks.rationale: External recipients increase the number of parties handling sensitive records and the chance of misuse.

risks.description: Conservation district employees and contractors have access to the system, so there is a risk of unauthorized viewing or misuse by non-federal personnel with broad operational access.
risks.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond core agency staff increases the insider-risk surface.

risks.description: Individuals do not have direct access to DMS, which can make it harder for them to see, verify, or correct their own information promptly.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Lack of direct access can delay correction of inaccurate personal data.

risks.description: The system retains records for long periods, including until a participant no longer qualifies for conservation programs, which increases the amount of personal data exposed over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.
risks.rationale: Long retention increases cumulative exposure if records are later breached or improperly accessed.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict access controls, encryption, and audit logging for the repository and document access, and limit access to only those with a documented need to know.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DMS features will allow users to view documents and/or upload new documents, version documents, and delete documents within the scope for those locations where their role has jurisdiction.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and monitoring activity reduces the chance that highly sensitive records are exposed or altered inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Add upload review and data-minimization controls so users are prompted to avoid uploading unnecessary personal information and to confirm the business need for each document.
mitigations.rationale: Review and minimization reduce the chance that unnecessary sensitive data is introduced into the system.

mitigations.description: Harden client-side viewing by keeping PDF software patched, restricting plugin use to approved versions, and requiring secure managed endpoints for document viewing.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing client-side attack surface helps protect sensitive PDF records from exploitation.

mitigations.description: Use stronger identity-matching controls and exception handling when comparing DMS records to FSA SCIMS data, with periodic quality checks for mismatches.
mitigations.rationale: Improved matching and review lower the risk of associating a record with the wrong producer.

mitigations.description: Require documented written authorization before any external disclosure and log each disclosure to contractors or technical service providers for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant.
mitigations.rationale: Authorization and logging help ensure external sharing stays within the permitted purpose.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access reviews and periodic revalidation for all NRCS employees, conservation district employees, and contractors with DMS access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: System access is restricted to authorized NRCS employees and conservation district employees working to assist with the implementation of natural resources programs.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access review reduces the risk of unnecessary or stale access by non-federal personnel.

mitigations.description: Provide an efficient correction and amendment workflow for individuals through the district conservationist or designated office, with clear response timelines.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any individual may request information regarding this system of records, or information as to whether the system contains records pertaining to him/her by contacting the respective district conservationist or other designee.
mitigations.rationale: A clear correction path helps individuals identify and fix inaccurate records even without direct system access.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition rules to remove or archive records as soon as they are no longer needed under the applicable NARA schedule and SORN.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Following the approved retention schedule limits how long sensitive records remain exposed.

risks.description: The system stores borrower PII permanently, which creates a long-term exposure risk if the records are ever mishandled, breached, or retained longer than needed for the original purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the time window in which sensitive borrower data can be exposed or misused.

risks.description: The system contains sensitive financial and loan-related borrower data that could reveal a person's financial hardship and repayment status if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property.
risks.rationale: Financial and loan information is highly sensitive because it can expose private economic circumstances.

risks.description: The system uses direct identifiers such as name and Tax ID, which increases the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers make it easier to link records to specific individuals and heighten harm if disclosed.

risks.description: Field office employees manually input borrower information, creating a risk of human error, inconsistent entry, or unauthorized viewing during data entry.
risks.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
risks.rationale: Manual handling of PII can introduce mistakes and unnecessary exposure during collection.

risks.description: The system relies on field office employees to determine the most optimal servicing solutions, so an incorrect or overly broad use of borrower data could affect individuals' debt restructuring outcomes.
risks.evidence_quote: To support field office employees in determining the most optimal servicing solutions applicable and available concerning the restructuring of customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
risks.rationale: Using personal financial data to make servicing decisions creates privacy risk if the data is inaccurate or used beyond what is necessary.

risks.description: The system accesses other internal web applications and databases, which can expand the number of systems that can see borrower data and increase exposure through interconnected access paths.
risks.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
risks.rationale: Each additional connected system increases the number of places where borrower data may be accessible or copied.

risks.description: The PIA does not describe any internal or external sharing controls, so there is limited transparency about how borrower PII is protected when accessed within the agency.
risks.evidence_quote: 4.1 With which internal organization(s) is the information shared, what information is shared and for what purpose? N/A
risks.rationale: Lack of documented sharing details makes it harder to verify that access is limited to authorized uses.

risks.description: The PIA does not describe transmission or disclosure safeguards, which leaves uncertainty about how borrower PII is protected while moving between systems or users.
risks.evidence_quote: 4.2 How is the information transmitted or disclosed? N/A
risks.rationale: Without stated transmission protections, the privacy risk from internal disclosure or interception cannot be assessed from the record.

mitigations.description: Limit retention of borrower records to the minimum period allowed by the approved records schedule and implement periodic review to confirm records are still needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary retention lowers the duration of exposure for sensitive borrower data.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to borrower financial and security-property data to staff with a documented need to know and log all access to those records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access and audit logging reduce the chance of improper viewing or misuse of sensitive financial information.

mitigations.description: Apply strong identity and access controls, including role-based permissions and multifactor authentication, for records containing Name and Tax Id.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Some examples of info collected is Name, Tax Id, and Borrower Case Id.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting direct identifiers reduces the likelihood that a disclosure can be tied back to a specific borrower.

mitigations.description: Use data-entry validation and training for FSA Field Agents to reduce manual input errors and unnecessary exposure of borrower information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: How is the information collected? Manual system input from FSA Field Agent.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and training help prevent mistakes and limit avoidable handling of PII during collection.

mitigations.description: Require review and quality checks of the borrower data used in restructuring calculations so employees rely on accurate information when making servicing decisions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To support field office employees in determining the most optimal servicing solutions applicable and available concerning the restructuring of customer debt from loans originating from the USDA farm loan programs.
mitigations.rationale: Accuracy checks help ensure that privacy-sensitive financial data is not used in a way that harms the borrower.

mitigations.description: Document and limit data exchanges with connected internal applications to only the fields needed for the restructuring task, and monitor those interfaces for unauthorized access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Functionality includes: - Accessing various other web applications for information. - Accessing the Farm Loan Program Information Delivery System (FLPIDS) Direct Loan System (DLS) database, Farm Business Plan (FBP) and the Master Reference Tables (MRT).
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing interface data and monitoring connections reduces the privacy impact of system-to-system access.

mitigations.description: Publish a clear internal access and sharing policy that identifies who may access borrower records, for what purpose, and under what approval process.
mitigations.rationale: Documented access rules improve accountability and make it easier to verify that access is limited to authorized uses.

mitigations.description: Define and implement transmission safeguards such as encrypted connections and secure disclosure procedures for any movement of borrower data between users or systems.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit transmission protections reduce the risk of interception or improper disclosure during data movement.

risks.description: The system stores sensitive borrower PII and financial data indefinitely, which increases the chance of unnecessary long-term exposure if records are no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention raises privacy risk because older records remain available far longer than necessary.

risks.description: The system shares borrower name and Tax ID with Microbilt, creating a disclosure risk to an external organization.
risks.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
risks.rationale: External sharing expands the number of parties that can access sensitive identifiers.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains highly sensitive identifiers and financial records, including Tax ID numbers and credit reports, which could cause harm if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: The data consists of borrower information with regard to loan(s), financials, and security property. Some examples of info collected is Name, date of birth, address, Tax Id number, employment history, credit numbers and credit reports.
risks.rationale: These data elements are sensitive because they can be used for identity theft or financial harm.

risks.description: County office staff enter data collected from borrowers, so manual entry errors or over-collection could lead to inaccurate or excessive privacy-sensitive records.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual collection and entry increase the risk that incorrect or unnecessary personal data will be stored.

risks.description: The system uses credit reports and commercial data to determine credit worthiness, which creates a privacy risk of profiling borrowers based on external data sources.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: Using external credit information for eligibility decisions can affect individuals based on compiled personal data.

risks.description: The system supports loan eligibility decisions and processing using detailed financial and personal information, which could create transparency concerns for borrowers about how their data is used.
risks.evidence_quote: The resulting formal business plan, outlining the details of the producer, is required to begin their loan eligibility decisions and processing.
risks.rationale: Decision-making based on detailed personal data requires clear notice so borrowers understand the purpose and impact of collection.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce a records retention schedule that deletes or archives records when they are no longer needed for the loan and servicing purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Data is stored indefinitely. Some exists until the user is deleted from the database. 5 years on average for some systems as per the procedures in FSA 25-AS Handbook.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of legacy PII exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Limit the shared data with Microbilt to the minimum necessary fields and document the purpose of the disclosure in a data-sharing agreement.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Name and Tax ID is shared with Microbilt to obtain creditworthiness.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing shared identifiers reduces the privacy impact of external disclosure.

mitigations.description: Protect borrower records containing Tax ID numbers, credit reports, and financial data with strong access controls and encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Sensitive financial and identity data should be protected against unauthorized access and misuse.

mitigations.description: Train county office staff on accurate data collection and require validation checks before records are saved.
mitigations.rationale: Training and validation help reduce inaccurate or excessive personal data entry.

mitigations.description: Provide borrowers with clear notice that creditworthiness determinations use external credit information and commercial data.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice improves transparency when external data is used for eligibility decisions.

mitigations.description: Explain in the privacy notice how the formal business plan and related financial information are used in loan eligibility decisions and servicing.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The resulting formal business plan, outlining the details of the producer, is required to begin their loan eligibility decisions and processing.
mitigations.rationale: Explaining the use of the data helps borrowers understand how their information affects the process.

risks.description: The system uses Social Security Numbers to access borrower records, which creates a high risk of identity theft or unauthorized disclosure if those identifiers are exposed or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive identifiers and are explicitly used for querying the system.

risks.description: The system maintains borrower account information indefinitely, increasing the chance that sensitive data will remain available longer than necessary and be exposed in a future breach or improper access event.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Permanent retention expands the window of exposure for sensitive borrower data.

risks.description: Borrower information is shared with many internal and external organizations, creating a broad disclosure surface and a higher risk that data will be accessed beyond the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers. Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
risks.rationale: Each additional recipient increases the number of parties that must protect the data.

risks.description: The system reports borrower information to credit bureaus, which can affect borrowers' financial reputation and creates a risk of harm if inaccurate or outdated information is disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
risks.rationale: Credit reporting can cause lasting harm if borrower data is incorrect or incomplete.

risks.description: The system sends borrower information to IRS and Treasury for offset and tax reporting, which exposes sensitive financial data to government matching and collection processes.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is reported to the IRS for taxation purposes as legally required by Section 6050J of the IRS Code.
risks.rationale: Tax and offset reporting involves disclosure of borrower account details to other agencies.

risks.description: The system supports online queries and batch processing, which can increase the risk of unauthorized access or accidental disclosure if access controls and monitoring are insufficient.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
risks.rationale: Query and batch interfaces are common points where access controls must be tightly enforced.

risks.description: The system includes a public-facing customer self-service effort, which could expose borrower information to the public if not carefully designed and secured.
risks.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
risks.rationale: Public-facing functionality raises the risk of unauthorized disclosure through external access.

risks.description: The system records detailed history of transactions processed to a borrower's account, which creates a comprehensive profile of borrower activity that could be misused if accessed improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: The application is also used to view borrower status information and detailed history of transactions processed to a borrower’s account.
risks.rationale: Detailed histories can reveal extensive personal and financial behavior.

mitigations.description: Mask or tokenize Social Security Numbers in user interfaces and logs, and restrict full SSN display to only narrowly authorized users.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing SSN exposure lowers the chance of identity theft and misuse.

mitigations.description: Apply and periodically review records schedules to ensure only legally required permanent retention is kept, and archive older records with stronger access controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Retention review and archival controls reduce long-term exposure while preserving required records.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing to the minimum necessary data and enforce recipient-specific data use agreements or access controls for each internal and external recipient.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is shared with FSA and RD application users & accounting managers, FPAC IT support personnel (system, operations, DBAs), and FSA application developers. Additional sharing of information (which are outside the boundaries of this application) include Treasury, NFC, HUD, IRS, Dan & Bradstreet, US Bank, Credit Bureaus, and Borrowers.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing shared fields and binding recipients to specific purposes reduces disclosure risk.

mitigations.description: Add a data quality review before credit reporting so disputed or incorrect borrower information can be corrected before disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Credit Reporting – Provides information to Equifax, Dun & Bradstreet, and Experian
mitigations.rationale: Pre-disclosure validation helps prevent harmful inaccurate credit reporting.

mitigations.description: Restrict IRS and Treasury reporting to the specific data elements required by law and document the legal basis for each disclosure.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is reported to the IRS for taxation purposes as legally required by Section 6050J of the IRS Code.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting disclosures to required fields reduces unnecessary exposure in government reporting.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access control, strong authentication, and audit logging for all online queries and batch processing activities.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information is accessed on ADPS through online queries and batch processing using name or Social Security Number.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access control and logging help prevent and detect unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Perform a privacy and security review before launching the public-facing customer self-service function, including testing for exposure of borrower data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: There is work going on for Customer Self Service which will be public facing.
mitigations.rationale: A pre-launch review can identify disclosure risks before public access is enabled.

mitigations.description: Limit detailed transaction history access to users with a business need and log all access to borrower histories for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The application is also used to view borrower status information and detailed history of transactions processed to a borrower’s account.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and monitoring access reduces the chance of misuse of detailed borrower profiles.

risks.description: The system retains personal information permanently, which increases the risk of over-retention and long-term exposure if records are no longer needed.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the amount of time sensitive contact information remains available for misuse or unauthorized access.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains identifiable contact information, which could be exposed if the application or database is improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: Name, mailing address, phone number
risks.rationale: Contact information is personally identifiable and can be misused if access controls fail.

risks.description: Information is entered manually by multiple FLP staff groups, creating a risk of inaccurate or inconsistent records from human input errors.
risks.evidence_quote: Manual system input from County FLP teams, State, Regional and National FLP members
risks.rationale: Manual entry by many users increases the chance of mistakes that can affect the accuracy of personal data.

risks.description: The system centralizes appraisal-related information for county, state, regional, and national staff, which broadens internal access and increases the risk of unauthorized viewing or excessive access.
risks.evidence_quote: provides County, State, Regional and National Farm Loan Program (FLP) staff with the means to facilitate, track status and complete appraisals
risks.rationale: A broader user base creates more opportunities for inappropriate access to personal information.

risks.description: The system stores case file and document management information, which can expose personal data if document controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: document management (approval tracking, action alerts, case file storage, etc.)
risks.rationale: Stored case files may contain personal details and require strong protection to prevent disclosure.

risks.description: The system supports centralized information and robust analysis and reporting, which can increase the risk of secondary use of personal data beyond the original appraisal purpose if not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: centralizing information allowing for robust analysis and reporting
risks.rationale: Centralized reporting can enable broader internal use of personal information than users originally expect.

mitigations.description: Apply and periodically review a records schedule so permanent retention is limited to records that truly must be kept indefinitely.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: A formal records schedule helps ensure only required records are retained long term.

mitigations.description: Enforce role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions for all users who can view or edit contact information.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the chance that identifiable contact information is seen by unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Add validation and supervisory review for manually entered records before they are finalized.
mitigations.rationale: Review steps can catch data-entry errors introduced by multiple manual users.

mitigations.description: Limit access to appraisal records to staff with a documented need to know and periodically review user permissions.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access reduces the number of people who can view personal information.

mitigations.description: Protect case files and documents with access controls and logging so viewing and changes are traceable.
mitigations.evidence_quote: document management (approval tracking, action alerts, case file storage, etc.)
mitigations.rationale: Controls and logs help prevent and detect inappropriate access to stored case files.

mitigations.description: Restrict reporting outputs to aggregated or minimized data unless a specific user role requires more detail.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report detail reduces the chance that centralized analysis reveals more personal information than necessary.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains highly sensitive personal and financial data that could cause significant harm if misused or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number. eDALR$ Name, personal identification number (SSN) and Agency assigned number. FBP Name. date of birth, street address, personal identification number (SSN/TIN), financial data (credit card number, loan number, credit Reports) and employment history.
risks.rationale: The data includes direct identifiers, demographic data, and financial records, which are all privacy-sensitive.

risks.description: The system combines data from many internal, government, and third-party sources, increasing the chance of inaccurate or outdated information being used in decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS 1. Other FSA Applications: Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS), Farm Business Plan (FBP), Electronic Loan Deficiency Payments, Master Reference Tables (MRT), Appraisal System COTS (Appraisal), Program Loan Accounting System (PLAS) and Automated Discrepancy Processing System (ADPS). 2. The other sources listed below do not have a direct connect to/from the application. Information is obtained through files etc. - State and Local Agencies: County offices, Tax records, Courthouse Records (UCC filings) and Deed Recorder. - Other Sources: Other lenders, credit reporting agencies, private appraisers, Crop insurance companies, multi list data, Farm Credit System, sales data, Ag Lenders, and business owners.
risks.rationale: Using many sources creates a risk that incorrect or stale data will be propagated into loan servicing and eligibility decisions.

risks.description: Creditworthiness and loan eligibility decisions may be made using personal and financial information in ways that affect individuals' access to federal loan benefits.
risks.evidence_quote: FBP To determine credit worthiness for FSA Farm Loan Program assistance and to analyze balance sheet and income and expense information on agricultural customers applying for assistance from FSA Farm Loan Programs, and for loan making and loan servicing.
risks.rationale: The system is used to evaluate applicants for loan assistance, so errors or unfair treatment could directly affect access to benefits.

risks.description: The system processes demographic information such as ethnicity, race, and gender, which can create a risk of inappropriate use or bias in loan processing.
risks.evidence_quote: DLS Name, street address, personal identification number (TIN/SSN), user ID, ethnicity, race, gender and case number.
risks.rationale: Collecting protected-class information in a lending context can increase the risk of discriminatory or otherwise inappropriate use.

risks.description: Permanent retention of all records increases the long-term exposure of sensitive borrower information.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Keeping records forever expands the time window in which a breach, misuse, or unauthorized access could affect individuals.

risks.description: Borrowers' loan and account information is accessible through web-based applications, which creates exposure if authentication or session controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: provide field office staff the ability to process and service loan applications and allows producers access to their Farm Loan Program (FLP) account information.
risks.rationale: Web access broadens the attack surface and can expose sensitive account data if access controls are not strong enough.

risks.description: Manual data entry by field staff can introduce errors or inconsistent records that affect borrower files and decisions.
risks.evidence_quote: eDALR$ Manual system input from FSA Field Agent. FBP Data collected from the borrower at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manually entered information is more likely to contain mistakes that can affect the accuracy of sensitive records.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the minimum necessary and apply strong role-based access controls to all sensitive borrower records.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that highly sensitive personal and financial data will be viewed or used inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Implement data quality checks and source verification before using external or cross-system data in loan decisions.
mitigations.rationale: Verifying incoming data helps prevent inaccurate or outdated information from affecting borrower outcomes.

mitigations.description: Provide a documented review and appeal process for applicants affected by creditworthiness or servicing determinations.
mitigations.rationale: A review path helps correct decisions that may be based on incomplete or erroneous information.

mitigations.description: Limit use of ethnicity, race, and gender data to authorized reporting or statutory purposes and monitor for improper use.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining and monitoring use of protected-class data reduces the risk of discriminatory treatment.

mitigations.description: Apply record segmentation and periodic review to ensure only records that must be retained permanently remain accessible in active systems.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary active exposure lowers the privacy risk created by indefinite retention.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and secure session management for producer and staff web access.
mitigations.rationale: Strong login and session controls reduce the risk of unauthorized access to account information.

mitigations.description: Use validation rules and supervisory review for manually entered borrower data.
mitigations.rationale: Validation and review help catch data entry errors before they affect records or decisions.

risks.description: The system retains personal information indefinitely, which increases the risk of long-term exposure, misuse, or unauthorized access over time. This is especially sensitive because the records are permanent rather than time-limited.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases the amount of personal data exposed if the system is breached or access controls fail.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains names and mailing addresses for multiple user groups, creating privacy risk if those identifiers are exposed or used beyond the intended oversight and workflow purposes. Even limited PII can enable unwanted contact or linkage across records.
risks.evidence_quote: DDORS Name FLOTrack Name, mailing address SDMS Name, mailing address
risks.rationale: Names and mailing addresses are directly identifying and should be protected against unnecessary disclosure.

risks.description: The system uses information entered by county, state, and state personnel, so inaccurate or outdated entries could affect oversight, training, or directives workflows and harm the individuals represented in the records. Manual entry also increases the chance of mistaken association of a person with the wrong record.
risks.evidence_quote: County Offices enter the data
risks.rationale: Manually entered records are more prone to error, which can create privacy and fairness problems.

risks.description: SDMS collects information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB, which could expose public commenters or submitters to unintended disclosure if their submissions are linked to their identity. This creates a privacy risk around early-stage or sensitive policy input.
risks.evidence_quote: collect information from the public on directives or policies that have not yet been approved by OMB.
risks.rationale: Public submissions can contain identifying information or viewpoints that should be handled carefully.

risks.description: The system supports oversight, monitoring, and tracking of employees and trainees, which can create a privacy risk of excessive internal surveillance if access is broader than necessary. Monitoring progress and management activities can reveal performance-related information about named individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: provide District Directors (DD) the ability to oversee the management of the service centers and FLM users.
risks.rationale: Oversight systems can reveal sensitive employment-related information even when they are not designed as personnel systems.

risks.description: Because the system is web-based and includes multiple applications, unauthorized access could expose stored PII if authentication, authorization, or session protections are weak. The PIA does not describe specific access controls beyond stating that contractors do not have access.
risks.evidence_quote: consists of multiple Web-based applications that provide oversight and compliance for the Farm Loan Program (FLP) loan portfolio.
risks.rationale: Web-based systems holding PII are common targets and need strong access protections.

mitigations.description: Apply and enforce a records disposal schedule so data is not kept longer than necessary, and periodically review whether all permanent records still need indefinite retention.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, in accordance with USDA Directive DR 3080-001: Appendix A: Scheduling Records.
mitigations.rationale: A formal schedule limits unnecessary long-term exposure while preserving records required by law.

mitigations.description: Limit access to names and mailing addresses to only staff with a need to know and mask or suppress those fields in reports where full identifiers are unnecessary.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing routine visibility of direct identifiers lowers the chance of improper disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement validation and review procedures for manually entered data, including periodic audits for accuracy and correction of mismatched records.
mitigations.rationale: Quality controls reduce the privacy harm caused by incorrect or misattributed personal information.

mitigations.description: Provide a clear public notice and submission guidance explaining what information should not be included in comments or submissions before OMB approval, and minimize collection to only what is needed.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notice and data minimization reduce the risk that public submissions contain unnecessary personal information.

mitigations.description: Restrict oversight and trainee-monitoring views to authorized personnel and use role-based access so users only see the records needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access limits exposure of performance and management information about named individuals.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce strong authentication, authorization, and logging for the web applications, and review access logs for unauthorized activity.
mitigations.rationale: Strong access controls and monitoring help prevent and detect unauthorized disclosure of PII.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and business identifiers, creating a risk of identity theft or misuse if the data is exposed or mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: ☒ Social Security number ☒ Employee Identification Number ☒ Taxpayer Identification Number ☒ Business Taxpayer Identification Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Personal Mobile Number ☒ Business Mobile Number (sole proprietor) ☒ Name (including nicknames) ☒ Gender ☒ Business Mailing Address (sole proprietor)
risks.rationale: These data elements can directly identify people and businesses and are valuable if accessed improperly.

risks.description: The system maintains a very large volume of records, increasing the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.
risks.evidence_quote: This system contains an estimated 14 million records of individuals and entities
risks.rationale: A larger dataset increases the number of affected people if privacy controls fail.

risks.description: The system retains historical farm and customer records for a long period, which increases the amount of personal data available over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends exposure and creates more opportunity for secondary use or unauthorized disclosure.

risks.description: Multiple USDA agencies share farm record and business partner data, creating a risk of broader disclosure than necessary for the original collection purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
risks.rationale: Sharing across agencies expands the number of recipients and the chance of improper access or use.

risks.description: County Office access to customer and farm information could expose data to many local users if role controls are not tightly limited.
risks.evidence_quote: allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
risks.rationale: Broader operational access increases the chance that a user can view or change information beyond what is needed.

risks.description: The system centralizes employee access and roles, so misconfigured permissions could allow unauthorized create, edit, or view access.
risks.evidence_quote: Organizational Structure – this application centralizes CRM employee access and roles to associated counties and positions from source systems.
risks.rationale: Centralized access control is a high-value target and errors can affect many records at once.

risks.description: The system uses geospatial boundary data for farms, tracts, and fields, which can reveal detailed property and operational information about producers.
risks.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
risks.rationale: Precise location and boundary data can expose sensitive land-use and operational details.

risks.description: Historical data from 1999 to the current program year increases the chance that outdated or unnecessary personal information remains accessible.
risks.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
risks.rationale: Older records may no longer be needed for current operations but still create privacy exposure.

mitigations.description: Limit access to sensitive identifiers using role-based access controls and least-privilege permissions, and log access to those fields.
mitigations.evidence_quote: authorizations which are assigned using USDA eAuthentication and CRM Organizational Structure, which controls the user’s create, edit and view capabilities and drive workflows for approvals.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive identifiers are viewed or changed inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Apply strong monitoring, intrusion detection, and incident response controls to protect the large records repository.
mitigations.rationale: A dataset of this size warrants heightened detection and response to limit the impact of a breach.

mitigations.description: Enforce retention schedules so archived records are deleted or de-identified when no longer required by program or legal needs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The current requirement is to maintain 20 years of historical data and archive records that are older.
mitigations.rationale: Removing data after the required period reduces the amount of historical personal information exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Use data-sharing agreements and purpose limitations so only the minimum Farm Record and Business Partner data needed for program delivery is shared.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NRCS, RMA, and FSA agencies share/receive/transmit -Farm Record and Business Partner data for program delivery purposes.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared data to the stated purpose reduces unnecessary disclosure across agencies.

mitigations.description: Restrict County Office access to only the records and functions required for each user’s duties and review access periodically.
mitigations.evidence_quote: allowing access to update customer and farm information at any County Office.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic access review helps ensure local access stays aligned with job responsibilities.

mitigations.description: Regularly review and test role mappings in the Organizational Structure application to prevent excessive or incorrect permissions.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Organizational Structure – this application centralizes CRM employee access and roles to associated counties and positions from source systems.
mitigations.rationale: Validating centralized role assignments helps prevent unauthorized access caused by configuration errors.

mitigations.description: Limit access to geospatial boundary data and apply privacy reviews before combining it with other customer records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAIP imagery is used to establish and maintain the geospatial footprint of the delineated farm, tract, and field boundaries in Farm Records.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting detailed location data lowers the risk of revealing sensitive farm and property information.

mitigations.description: Archive older records in a more restricted environment and periodically assess whether they still need to be retained.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Business Partner and Farm Records (including Historical data from 1999 to current program year) is the System of Record and Entry for customer records and farm data
mitigations.rationale: Tighter controls on older records reduce exposure while preserving required history.

risks.description: The system retains producer information indefinitely, which increases the risk of unnecessary long-term exposure, misuse, or breach impact over time. This affects all FPDS components that maintain personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention expands the amount of time sensitive producer data remains available and vulnerable.

risks.description: The system uses and stores names and street addresses across many program applications, creating broad exposure of direct identifiers tied to disaster, revenue, and payment records. Because multiple components collect the same identifiers, the privacy impact is wider than a single program.
risks.evidence_quote: ELAP Name, street address LFP Name, street address LIP Name, street address NAP Name, street address TAP Name, street address CFAP Name, street address CFAP 2.0 Name, street address QLA Name, street address PARP Name, street address PLIP Name, street address PATHH Name, street address OTECP Name, street address SMHPP Name, street address ELRP Name, street address
risks.rationale: Direct identifiers stored across many related programs increase the chance of unauthorized disclosure and linkage of records.

risks.description: County office staff enter producer information into the system, which creates a risk of unauthorized access or insider misuse at the point of collection and data entry. The system relies on many local users handling the information.
risks.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
risks.rationale: Human data entry points are common sources of privacy errors and inappropriate access.

risks.description: The system allows Department contractors to access producer data, which increases the number of people who can view sensitive records. Even with controls, contractor access creates an additional exposure path.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Expanding access to contractors increases the attack surface and the risk of inappropriate disclosure.

risks.description: NAP notifications are physically mailed to producers, which can expose personal information through postal handling, misdelivery, or household interception. Printed letters also create a persistent paper trail outside the system.
