risks.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
risks.rationale: Physical mail introduces confidentiality risks that do not exist with purely electronic delivery.

risks.description: The system transmits premium collection data to another system and stores it, which creates a risk that financial and identity-linked records could be exposed through system-to-system transfers. This is especially sensitive because the data supports payments and receivables.
risks.evidence_quote: The County Office records premium collection data in the System and the system transmits premium collection data to NRRS and stores it.
risks.rationale: Financial data transfers increase the number of systems that must be secured correctly.

risks.description: Some NAP functions allow records to be accessed by partial identifiers such as last name or last four digits of an ID, which can make unauthorized searching or record enumeration easier. This increases the risk of exposing producer records to users with broad access.
risks.evidence_quote: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
risks.rationale: Searchable access by partial identifiers can facilitate lookup of records beyond what is necessary.

risks.description: The system generates name and street address for printed forms in several programs, which can disclose personal contact information through output handling even where the data is not otherwise stored or collected. This creates a privacy risk in print workflows and form distribution.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
risks.rationale: Generated output can still reveal personal information if printed forms are mishandled or overdistributed.

risks.description: The system shares some data with external internal systems such as CARS and LFP, which creates a risk of secondary use or broader dissemination beyond the original program need. Even internal disclosures can reduce control over who sees producer data.
risks.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
risks.rationale: Each additional system receiving data increases the chance of unauthorized access or incompatible use.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review and deletion schedule so only records with a documented business or legal need remain accessible, and periodically revalidate whether permanent retention is still necessary for each component.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention limits the duration of exposure and the amount of data at risk.

mitigations.description: Minimize stored identifiers by limiting name and street address use to what is strictly required for each program and masking or segregating them where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.

mitigations.description: Require role-based access controls, logging, and periodic review of county office user activity for producer record entry and edits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Producers will provide information to the county office employees who will enter data into the application which will be saved in the database.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring and limiting user permissions reduces insider misuse and accidental errors.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary records and functions, and conduct recurring access recertification for all contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Yes, Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter access review reduces the number of people who can see sensitive producer data.

mitigations.description: Offer electronic delivery or secure address verification for notices where permitted, and use privacy-protective mailing practices for any required paper letters.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP Notifications is a centralized system which maintains and delivers NAP notifications (letters) from individual NAP Signup systems to the KC Print Shop (NAP producers).
mitigations.rationale: Safer delivery methods reduce the chance of disclosure through mail handling.

mitigations.description: Encrypt and authenticate all system-to-system transfers of premium collection data and restrict the receiving system to only the fields needed for receivables processing.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting transfers and limiting shared fields reduces exposure during inter-system exchange.

mitigations.description: Require stronger search controls for NAP lookups, such as full authentication, audit logging, and restrictions on searches by partial identifiers unless operationally necessary.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Application for Payment (AFP) can be accessed from the NAP menu and can be processed by Last 4 of the ID, Producer Id and Type or Producer’s Last Name.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter search controls make unauthorized record discovery harder.

mitigations.description: Use secure print controls, minimize printed distribution, and suppress street addresses on forms unless the address is required for the specific document.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFAP process will generate name and street address, but not store, process or collect the address
mitigations.rationale: Reducing printed exposure lowers the chance that contact information is seen by unintended recipients.

mitigations.description: Establish data-sharing agreements and field-level restrictions for any internal disclosures so recipient systems receive only the minimum data needed for the stated purpose.
mitigations.evidence_quote: NAP SS is a component of the NAP system and is used to disclose NAP data to external systems, for example CARS, and LFP.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting shared data reduces secondary-use and propagation risks.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive identifiers, including SSNs, which creates a risk of identity theft or misuse if the data is exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: ARCPLC Name, mailing address, last 4 digits SSN SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: SSNs and related identifiers are high-impact personal data if compromised.

risks.description: The system maintains payment amounts and farm tract information, which could reveal financial status and business operations of producers if improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: SWIMS Name, mailing address, SSN/EIN. farm tract numbers, payment amounts
risks.rationale: Payment and tract data can expose sensitive financial and operational details about individuals and farms.

risks.description: ARCPLC displays PII from another system after calling SCIMS, so unauthorized viewing or misuse of displayed data is a risk if access controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
risks.rationale: Displaying retrieved PII increases the chance of exposure to users who should not see it.

risks.description: SWIMS is a shared database accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office employees, which creates an insider-access risk if permissions are excessive or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: SWIMS is a centralized database that has been created for users to import and export the SURE Workbook .xml files using a shared database that is accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
risks.rationale: Shared internal access expands the number of people who can view or handle PII.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, increasing the amount of time sensitive records could be exposed through breach, misuse, or unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Longer retention increases cumulative exposure risk.

risks.description: ARCPLC uses producer information to determine eligibility and identify the person signing up, which creates a risk of profiling or unnecessary exposure if more data than needed is displayed or used.
risks.evidence_quote: To determine eligibility.
risks.rationale: Eligibility processing can expose personal information beyond what is necessary for the immediate transaction.

mitigations.description: Encrypt SSNs and other sensitive identifiers at rest and in transit, and restrict access to only authorized users with a need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and strict access limits reduce the chance that sensitive identifiers can be read or misused if the system is compromised.

mitigations.description: Minimize the display of payment amounts and farm tract numbers to only the fields needed for the current task, and mask them in default views.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting visible financial and tract data reduces unnecessary exposure of sensitive business information.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and audit logging to all ARCPLC views that display SCIMS-derived PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: ARC/PLC simply calls SCIMS with a CCID and displays the information within the application.
mitigations.rationale: Controlling and logging access helps prevent and detect improper viewing of displayed PII.

mitigations.description: Periodically review and recertify the access of National, State, and County Office users who can use the shared SWIMS database.
mitigations.evidence_quote: accessible to a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees.
mitigations.rationale: Regular access reviews help ensure only authorized employees retain access to shared PII.

mitigations.description: Apply a records management review to confirm whether all permanently retained data is still necessary, and segregate or archive older records with tighter controls.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing long-term retention can reduce the amount of sensitive data exposed in active systems.

mitigations.description: Limit eligibility screens to the minimum information needed and avoid showing unnecessary PII when identifying the person signing up for ARC-PLC.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To identify the person who will be signing up for ARC-PLC sign up.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the privacy impact of eligibility processing.

risks.description: County office users can search for a specific farmer or producer using PII, which creates a risk of unauthorized internal access or misuse of sensitive identity data.
risks.evidence_quote: the FSAfarm+ application uses PII to allow county office users to search for a specific farmer or producer.
risks.rationale: Search access to identity data increases the chance that users could view information beyond what they need.

risks.description: The system uses SSN as a second authentication method, which creates a high-impact exposure risk if SSNs are accessed or entered improperly.
risks.evidence_quote: If a farmer or producer has an eAuth account, the SSN can be used as a second authentication method to validate the farmer / producer
risks.rationale: SSNs are highly sensitive, so using them for authentication raises the consequences of disclosure or misuse.

risks.description: The system pulls a broad set of personal and demographic data from another database, which increases the amount of information exposed to county office users.
risks.evidence_quote: the specific user information is pulled from the SCIMS database (which resides on the FPCMS system); this information includes: • First Name, Last Name • Entity (business) information • Address Information • Email • Phone Number • Demographic Information • EIN / SSN (via a search screen)
risks.rationale: The more data elements exposed in one search, the greater the privacy impact if access is unnecessary or excessive.

risks.description: Contractor access to the system creates a risk that non-federal personnel could view or handle farmer and producer PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Contractor access is limited to contractors supporting the FSCOMS system / FSAfarm+ application.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the number of people who may encounter sensitive personal information.

risks.description: Because the system relies on memory and cache clearing at logout rather than storing data, there is a residual risk that PII could remain accessible during a session or if logout does not occur properly.
risks.evidence_quote: When a user logs out of FSCOMS, the memory and cache are automatically cleared (no PII is stored in FSCOMS).
risks.rationale: Session-based handling can leave data exposed until logout or cleanup occurs.

risks.description: PII is requested from the SCIMS database in another system boundary, which creates a risk that data may be exposed during retrieval or due to cross-system access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: FSAfarm+ requests and receives PII from SCIMS, which resides in the FPCMS system.
risks.rationale: Moving data across system boundaries can introduce access and transmission risks even when the receiving system does not store it.

mitigations.description: Restrict county office search access to users with a documented need to know and log all searches for monitoring and review.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing search access reduces the chance of unauthorized viewing or misuse.

mitigations.description: Avoid using SSN as an authentication factor and replace it with a less sensitive verification method where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Replacing SSN-based validation lowers the impact of exposure of a highly sensitive identifier.

mitigations.description: Limit the fields returned to county office users to only the minimum needed for the specific search or validation task.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces unnecessary exposure of personal and demographic information.

mitigations.description: Require contractor access to be role-based, approved, and monitored, with the least privilege needed to support the system.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access controls reduce the privacy risk created by contractor visibility into PII.

mitigations.description: Use automatic session timeout and secure in-session handling controls so cached or memory-resident PII is cleared promptly even if a user is inactive.
mitigations.rationale: Shorter-lived sessions reduce the window in which PII could remain exposed in memory or cache.

mitigations.description: Protect cross-system retrieval from SCIMS with strong access controls and secure transmission safeguards between the systems.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the data flow between systems reduces the risk of unauthorized access during retrieval.

risks.description: The system collects and maintains personally identifiable information about producers, including name and mailing address, which creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of identity and contact information.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: Name and mailing address are directly identifying and sensitive enough to warrant strong access controls.

risks.description: The system collects race and ethnicity information, which increases sensitivity because improper access or disclosure could expose highly sensitive personal data.
risks.evidence_quote: COC-ES Name, mailing address, ethnicity and race.
risks.rationale: Race and ethnicity are sensitive attributes that can cause privacy harm if disclosed inappropriately.

risks.description: County office staff enter data collected from producers, creating a risk of inaccurate or incomplete records being stored and used to determine election eligibility and ballot mailing lists.
risks.evidence_quote: Data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff.
risks.rationale: Manual entry introduces the possibility of errors that can affect both privacy and the fairness of election-related processing.

risks.description: The system uses producer information to identify who is eligible to vote in committee elections, which creates a risk of improper profiling or exclusion if eligibility logic is wrong or overly broad.
risks.evidence_quote: identifies producers eligible to vote in committee elections based on information such as committee and Local Administrative Area (LAA) codes
risks.rationale: Eligibility decisions based on stored attributes can have privacy and due-process consequences if misapplied.

risks.description: The system builds and sends county-specific lists of all eligible producers for ballot printing, which could expose a broad set of producers' names and addresses if the lists are mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: Build and send county-specific list of all producers eligible to vote (for printing onto ballot self-mailer forms, FSA-681).
risks.rationale: Mass mailing lists concentrate personal data and increase exposure if access is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: The system collects and reports election data from returned ballot forms, which may reveal a producer's participation in an election and related voting activity.
risks.evidence_quote: Collect and report election data from returned ballot forms (the County Election and Media Outreach Report).
risks.rationale: Ballot-related records can disclose participation in a protected civic process.

risks.description: The system creates and stores the COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms, which can expose membership and tenure information about individuals serving on committees.
risks.evidence_quote: Create the COC Directory showing all members and information related to their terms.
risks.rationale: Committee membership and term data can reveal organizational roles and history about identifiable people.

risks.description: The information is retained indefinitely, increasing the risk that personal data will remain available longer than necessary and be exposed in future unauthorized access or breach events.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention expands the window during which records can be misused or compromised.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to producer records to authorized personnel only and enforce role-based access controls with regular access reviews.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access reduces the chance that identifying information is seen or used by unauthorized users.

mitigations.description: Apply heightened protections to race and ethnicity fields, such as minimizing access, encrypting stored data, and monitoring access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Extra safeguards are appropriate because the system stores sensitive demographic information.

mitigations.description: Validate county office entries and require periodic record quality checks to correct inaccurate or incomplete producer data.
mitigations.rationale: Data quality controls reduce the risk that manual entry errors affect eligibility and mailing decisions.

mitigations.description: Document and test the eligibility rules used to select voters, and require supervisory review of the producer lists before use.
mitigations.rationale: Reviewing the logic and outputs helps prevent incorrect eligibility determinations.

mitigations.description: Limit distribution of county-specific eligible-producer lists to only the staff and systems needed for ballot production, and protect the lists during printing and handling.
mitigations.rationale: Tight handling controls reduce the chance that large mailing lists are exposed or copied inappropriately.

mitigations.description: Minimize ballot-return data to only what is needed for reporting and store it separately from other producer records when possible.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization lowers the privacy impact of election participation records.

mitigations.description: Limit access to the COC Directory to users with a need to know and publish only the minimum member and term information required for committee administration.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing access and detail limits unnecessary exposure of committee membership information.

mitigations.description: Apply a records review process to confirm that permanent retention is still necessary for each record category and purge any records no longer required by the approved schedule.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Even with an approved schedule, periodic review can reduce unnecessary long-term retention risk.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial data, including identifiers and employment information, creating a risk of harm if the warehouse is breached or misused.
risks.evidence_quote: All Program and financial data for the Agency is stored in the EDW. This includes Farm Program, Farm Loan, Commodity Operations, Human Resources and Financial data. Possible information contained in the databases, but not limited to; Name, date of birth, address, TIN/SSN, account numbers, employment history, misc. account numbers.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the data increase the privacy impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Consolidating data from multiple source systems into a central warehouse increases the risk that information about many programs and individuals could be exposed in one place.
risks.evidence_quote: The Enterprise Data Warehouse is designed to facilitate data retrieval and reporting by providing a central stable location for data storage across FSA’s business enterprise.
risks.rationale: Centralized storage concentrates data and can amplify the consequences of a security failure.

risks.description: The system uses batch extraction, transformation, and loading from source systems, which creates a risk of unauthorized access or leakage during data transfer and processing.
risks.evidence_quote: EDW DV will consolidate the data from source applications using the same process as current in the Informix DB (i.e. getting the data from source as flat files and using an extract transfer and load (ETL) process to load it into Oracle DB).
risks.rationale: Moving data through batch and ETL processes increases the number of points where data can be intercepted or mishandled.

risks.description: PII is collected from county office staff and other federal agencies, which creates a risk that information may be entered or transferred inaccurately or without proper notice and control.
risks.evidence_quote: Most PII data collected from the producer at the county office and entered by the county office staff. In some cases information is collected via other federal agencies which provide this information to the FSA.
risks.rationale: Multiple collection paths increase the chance of inconsistent handling or inaccurate records.

risks.description: Information is used for Congressional, program level, and end user reporting, which creates a risk of overexposure if reports reveal more personal detail than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the EDW is used for Congressional, program level and end user reporting.
risks.rationale: Reporting use can expose data to broader audiences than the original collection purpose.

risks.description: The system supports analytics with business intelligence and web-based tools, which creates a risk that users can infer or extract more personal information than intended.
risks.evidence_quote: Oracle Business Intelligence (OBIEE) and web based tools will be used to analyze the data.
risks.rationale: Analytic tools can enable broad querying and aggregation that increases disclosure risk.

risks.description: Information is shared internally with NRCS, RD, and RMA, which creates a risk of unnecessary internal disclosure if access is broader than needed for the business purpose.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems (not EDW) share PII with NRCS, RD, and RMA.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII across organizations expands the set of users who may access it.

risks.description: Information is transmitted through batch processes, which creates a risk that data may be exposed if transfer channels are not adequately protected.
risks.evidence_quote: FSA source systems shares the information through batch processes.
risks.rationale: Batch transmission can move large volumes of PII at once, making secure transport controls important.

risks.description: External disclosures to IRS Treasury, the University of Illinois, and Dunn and Bradstreet create a risk of secondary use or disclosure outside FSA control.
risks.evidence_quote: However, FSA shares with IRS Treasury, one time data share with the University of Illinois, Dunn and Bradstreet (Name and address validation).
risks.rationale: Once data leaves the system, the privacy risk depends on the recipient's handling and limitations on use.

risks.description: Retaining records according to the NARA schedule means personal data may be kept for long periods, increasing the chance of later misuse or exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: The archiving and retention strategy for EDW DV will be retained in accordance with the NARA Retention Schedule.
risks.rationale: Longer retention extends the time during which data can be accessed, breached, or repurposed.

mitigations.description: Apply strong role-based access controls, encryption, and audit logging to all sensitive records in the warehouse.
mitigations.rationale: These controls reduce the likelihood and impact of unauthorized access to highly sensitive PII and financial data.

mitigations.description: Limit warehouse access to approved users and segment datasets so users only see the minimum data needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing access reduces the privacy impact of centralizing many datasets in one repository.

mitigations.description: Protect ETL and flat-file transfers with secure transmission controls and integrity checks, and monitor jobs for unauthorized access or failure.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the transfer and load process lowers the risk of leakage during movement between systems.

mitigations.description: Use validation and reconciliation checks when county office staff and other agencies supply data to reduce inaccurate or improperly handled records.
mitigations.rationale: Verification at collection and ingestion helps prevent privacy harms caused by bad or inconsistent data.

mitigations.description: Apply disclosure review and data minimization to reports so Congressional and program reporting only includes the least amount of personal detail necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting report content reduces the chance that reporting will expose unnecessary personal information.

mitigations.description: Restrict analytic tool permissions and use query controls to prevent users from extracting more personal information than their role requires.
mitigations.rationale: Access and query limits reduce the risk that analytics tools become a path to excessive disclosure.

mitigations.description: Use formal data-sharing agreements and least-privilege access rules for NRCS, RD, and RMA recipients.
mitigations.rationale: Clear sharing terms and limited access help ensure internal recipients only receive PII for approved purposes.

mitigations.description: Encrypt batch transfers and authenticate the receiving systems before any data is sent.
mitigations.rationale: Protecting batch transmissions reduces the chance that PII is intercepted or sent to the wrong destination.

mitigations.description: Require recipient-specific sharing terms, including limits on use, retention, and onward disclosure, for external disclosures.
mitigations.rationale: Binding recipients to narrow terms helps control secondary use after data leaves FSA.

mitigations.description: Implement records review and disposal procedures so data retained under the NARA schedule is deleted or archived when no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Regular disposal reduces the amount of personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system holds highly sensitive financial and identity data, including SSNs/TINs, bank account numbers, routing numbers, and signatures, creating a risk of identity theft or financial fraud if improperly accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: FDIS Images could contain information such as: Name, street address, SSN/TIN, phone number, Claim/NRRS number, agency case number, promissory number. bank account number, schedule of deposit numbers and image of the signature.
risks.rationale: The listed data elements are directly usable for impersonation or unauthorized financial transactions.

risks.description: Producer financial information is available through a web application that provides both summary and detailed views, increasing the risk of unauthorized internal access or overexposure of account details.
risks.evidence_quote: The FI resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is a web application designed to provide access to a producer's financial information on- line. Producers have access to both summary and detailed information.
risks.rationale: Web-based access to detailed financial records expands the number of users and sessions that could mishandle sensitive information.

risks.description: The public-facing financial services system lets producers and farmers update banking and assignment information, which creates a risk that account or payment data could be altered by an unauthorized user if access controls fail.
risks.evidence_quote: The Financial Services System resides on NITC Midrange Systems and is public facing, with producers and farmers able to update their own information (i.e. banking and assignment information).
risks.rationale: Allowing direct updates to payment-related data makes integrity protections critical to prevent misdirected funds or account manipulation.

risks.description: The system generates and transmits delinquent debt information to credit bureaus and Treasury-related collection processes, creating a risk of privacy harm from broad downstream disclosure of debt status.
risks.evidence_quote: Commercial Credit Bureaus are supplied delinquent debt status via encrypted e-mail attachment.
risks.rationale: Debt status is sensitive personal information, and dissemination beyond the originating system increases exposure and misuse risk.

risks.description: The system creates and mails letters about receivables, notes, and delinquent debt, which could disclose sensitive financial information to the wrong recipient if mailing or address data is inaccurate.
risks.evidence_quote: NRRS generates letters to customers associated with a receivable and records the receipt of monies that have been collected to satisfy a receivable.
risks.rationale: Physical correspondence about debt can reveal private financial status and is vulnerable to misdelivery.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely as permanent records, increasing the long-term risk of unauthorized access, secondary use, or breach over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which sensitive data can be exposed or repurposed.

risks.description: Contractors have access to the system, which creates a risk of insider misuse or accidental disclosure of sensitive producer financial information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need to know will have access as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Any contractor access expands the trusted user base and therefore the insider threat surface.

risks.description: The system stores images imported from faxed and scanned materials, which may capture more personal information than needed and increase exposure through document imaging repositories.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from document storage, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Imaged source documents can contain incidental or unnecessary personal data that persists in storage.

risks.description: The system compiles payment, debt, and tax reporting information for approximately 1.4 million customers annually, creating a large-scale concentration risk if access controls or safeguards fail.
risks.evidence_quote: Program and loan benefits are processed and disbursed through these systems to approximately 1.4 million FSA customers annually.
risks.rationale: A larger repository of sensitive records increases the impact of any unauthorized access or breach.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to the minimum necessary users and enforce strong encryption and masking for SSNs, bank account numbers, routing numbers, and signatures in storage and display.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting exposure of the most sensitive fields reduces the likelihood and impact of identity theft or fraud.

mitigations.description: Apply role-based access controls and separate summary views from detailed financial views so users only see the level of detail required for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting detailed financial visibility reduces unnecessary internal exposure of producer records.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and step-up verification for any banking or assignment changes, with transaction review or confirmation before updates take effect.
mitigations.rationale: Additional verification helps prevent unauthorized changes to payment instructions.

mitigations.description: Limit external debt disclosures to the minimum necessary data elements and maintain documented disclosure controls for Treasury and credit bureau transmissions.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is shared reduces the privacy impact of downstream collection and credit reporting.

mitigations.description: Use address validation, mail-quality controls, and periodic reconciliation of recipient information before generating and mailing debt letters.
mitigations.rationale: Better address accuracy reduces the chance that sensitive correspondence is sent to the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review process to periodically reassess whether all permanently retained data remains necessary and whether any portions can be archived with tighter access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review can reduce long-term exposure even when records must be kept permanently.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to named roles, monitor contractor activity, and periodically revalidate need-to-know access for all contractor accounts.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All roles are approved on a need-to-know basis via FPAC BC management
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know approval is already stated, and periodic validation and monitoring strengthen that control.

mitigations.description: Screen scanned, faxed, and imaged documents for unnecessary personal data before ingestion and redact extraneous sensitive fields where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary data in images lowers the amount of sensitive information stored in document repositories.

mitigations.description: Apply enhanced monitoring, logging, and breach response controls to the large customer data stores to detect and contain unauthorized access quickly.
mitigations.rationale: A large centralized repository warrants stronger detection and response to limit the impact of any incident.

risks.description: The system retains employee information permanently, which creates an indefinite privacy exposure if the data is no longer needed or if future access is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long-term retention increases the amount of time the data could be misused, disclosed, or accessed improperly.

risks.description: The system stores personally identifiable information about employees, including names and mailing addresses, which could be exposed if the database or application is compromised.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS Name & mailing address
risks.rationale: Names and mailing addresses are directly identifying and can be sensitive when linked to authorization records.

risks.description: The system centrally maintains authorization data about users' roles, groups, offices, and attributes, creating a profile of employee access and organizational affiliation.
risks.evidence_quote: providing storage and retrieval of authorization data pertaining to users’ roles, groups, offices, and any specially defined attributes to business applications
risks.rationale: Aggregating access-related attributes can reveal workplace relationships and permissions beyond what is needed for a single transaction.

risks.description: Administrators can manage access rights in real time, which creates a risk of excessive or unauthorized privilege changes if administrative controls are weak.
risks.evidence_quote: EAS allows administrators to use a web browser to manage security access rights, assigning and removing roles/groups/attributes to users on-line in real time.
risks.rationale: Real-time privilege changes can have immediate privacy and security consequences if misused.

risks.description: The system is designed to facilitate role-based access to applications, so any failure in access control could expose employee authorization data or other protected application data to unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: Facilitate Role-Based Access Control system.
risks.rationale: A system that governs access to other applications is a high-value target because compromise can broaden access across systems.

risks.description: The system is an online application that lets users submit security requests and track status, which could expose request details if web access is not properly secured.
risks.evidence_quote: The Farm Service Security Services System (FSSSS) is an online security request application and approval system that allows users to submit security requests on line and track the status.
risks.rationale: Online submission and status tracking increase exposure to interception, account takeover, or unauthorized viewing if safeguards fail.

risks.description: Although the system says no information is shared outside USDA, any future external disclosure would create privacy risk because the records contain employee PII and authorization data.
risks.evidence_quote: No application information is being shared outside of the USDA environment.
risks.rationale: A stated no-sharing posture reduces current exposure, but the underlying data would still be sensitive if sharing were introduced later.

mitigations.description: Apply a documented records review schedule to remove or archive records that are no longer required for operational or legal purposes, even if some records remain permanent.
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review limits unnecessary retention while preserving records that must legally remain permanent.

mitigations.description: Encrypt the stored employee PII and restrict database access to only those users with a demonstrated need to know.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and least-privilege access reduce the chance that names and mailing addresses are exposed through unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Minimize the authorization attributes stored to only what is necessary for access control and periodically review the retained fields for necessity.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of stored role and attribute data lowers the privacy impact of the authorization profile.

mitigations.description: Require strong administrator authentication, role separation, and audit logging for all real-time role or attribute changes.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter administrative controls help prevent unauthorized privilege changes and support accountability.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular access-control testing and periodic reviews of role assignments to verify that the role-based access control rules are working as intended.
mitigations.rationale: Testing and reviews help detect misconfigurations that could expose data through incorrect access decisions.

mitigations.description: Protect the online request and status functions with secure session management and transport encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Securing the web workflow helps prevent interception or unauthorized viewing of request information.

mitigations.description: Maintain the current no-external-sharing restriction and require privacy review before any future sharing arrangement is approved.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No application information is being shared outside of the USDA environment.
mitigations.rationale: Preserving the existing boundary keeps employee PII and authorization data from expanding beyond USDA.

risks.description: The system stores highly sensitive personal and financial records, so unauthorized access could expose identity, account, and debt information. The data types include names, SSNs, tax IDs, passport or driver’s license numbers, financial data, health data, biometric data, criminal history, and employment history.
risks.evidence_quote: Full name, mother’s maiden name, maiden f h i di id l i k li ) Date and/or place of birth. Address Information (street & email address). Personal identification number (social security number, tax identification number, passport number, driver’s license number or a unique identification number, etc.) Financial data (Credit card numbers, bank account etc.) Health data (including height, weight, blood pressure, etc.) Biometric data (fingerprints, iris scans, voice signature, facial geometry, DNA, etc.) Criminal history Employment history
risks.rationale: A compromise would reveal multiple categories of sensitive PII and financial information.

risks.description: The system retains records indefinitely, increasing the chance that stale sensitive records remain exposed for a long period. Long retention also expands the window in which old records can be misused or breached.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases exposure duration and the amount of data available in any incident.

risks.description: The system accepts data from faxed and scanned materials, which can create collection errors or include documents for the wrong person. Misfiled or inaccurate images could expose one individual’s records to another user or preserve incorrect records.
risks.evidence_quote: All data is directly input by the user from electronically stored documents, faxed, and scanned materials.
risks.rationale: Manual and paper-based intake can introduce misassociation and data quality risks.

risks.description: The system allows browser-based access to stored images on a network device, so weak access controls could let unauthorized users view records. Because the system is used for retrieval across multiple workflows, overbroad access would expose large volumes of images.
risks.evidence_quote: FileNet allows client access from desktop browser to the stored images on a network device managed by the server.
risks.rationale: Browser access to stored images requires strong authentication and authorization to prevent improper viewing.

risks.description: The system stores and retrieves historical archive documents, including read-only systems, which may still contain sensitive legacy information. Even without updates, archived records can remain accessible to users who no longer need them.
risks.evidence_quote: It is used to store and view FRB check images and pertinent information on CCC checks. It is used to pull up images of CCC checks. The KCFRB system is used to research historical archives of treasury checks. No new content is being added to the system. No updating is possible, only retrieval.
risks.rationale: Historical archives can retain sensitivity long after the original operational need has ended.

risks.description: The system includes workflow processing for financial information, so users involved in different stages may see more information than necessary. If workflow permissions are not tightly limited, sensitive records could be exposed beyond the minimum needed for a task.
risks.evidence_quote: Additionally, FileNet controls the workflows associated with the financial information being imaged.
risks.rationale: Workflow systems often broaden access unless role-based restrictions are enforced.

risks.description: The system stores images imported from the Federal Reserve Bank, so any upstream source errors or unauthorized content could be brought into the repository. Imported records may also include sensitive information not fully controlled by the local system at ingestion.
risks.evidence_quote: KCFRB Imaging (FRB) downloads and imports Federal Reserve Bank images into the system.
risks.rationale: Imported content can introduce integrity and confidentiality risks if source handling is not controlled.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access with strong authentication, role-based permissions, and regular access reviews for all users who can view or retrieve images.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive records are viewed without a need to know.

mitigations.description: Replace indefinite retention with a records schedule that deletes or archives records when no longer required by law or approved business need.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting retention reduces the amount of sensitive data exposed over time.

mitigations.description: Add intake validation and quality review steps for faxed and scanned documents to confirm correct identity, document type, and completeness before storage.
mitigations.rationale: Verification at intake lowers the chance that documents are misfiled or linked to the wrong person.

mitigations.description: Require multi-factor authentication and session controls for browser access, and restrict access to authorized devices or networks where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication and session protections reduce the risk of unauthorized viewing through the browser interface.

mitigations.description: Apply periodic access recertification and archive-specific permissions so users can retrieve only the historical records needed for their duties.
mitigations.rationale: Tighter archive access limits exposure of legacy records that remain sensitive.

mitigations.description: Configure workflow roles so each user can see only the images and metadata required for their step in the process.
mitigations.rationale: Workflow minimization prevents unnecessary exposure during processing.

mitigations.description: Validate imported records from external sources and log all imports so questionable or unauthorized content can be detected and traced.
mitigations.rationale: Import validation and auditability help protect the integrity of stored records.

risks.description: Users can export work lists to Excel on their own devices, which creates a risk of unauthorized copying, local storage, or onward sharing of PII outside the system. This is especially sensitive because the work lists contain names, addresses, and contract-related status data.
risks.evidence_quote: Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device.
risks.rationale: Exporting PII to endpoint devices increases the chance of loss, misuse, or uncontrolled retention.

risks.description: Users can subscribe to e-mail alerts that contain the same data and fields as the work lists, which can expose PII through email delivery and mailbox retention. The alerts also include new deltas, increasing the amount of personal data distributed over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
risks.rationale: Email is a higher-risk delivery channel because messages can be forwarded, misaddressed, or retained beyond the intended need.

risks.description: The system exposes detailed personal and program-status information, including eligibility and payment-related statuses, which could reveal sensitive information about landowners and applicants if accessed by someone without a need to know. The data includes identifiers and multiple status fields that can be combined to profile an individual's participation in programs.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII that is used, processed or maintained by FA Tracker includes name, address, as well as the following: o Application # o Contract # o Contract Item # o State o County o Field Office o Number of days until/passed a specific date of interest o Contract Modification Reason o Contract Modification Status o Status of a Payment (E.g. "Waiting for participant signed date") o Other Eligibility (Yes/No) o AD-1026 (Y/N) o FTE (Y/N) o AGI (Y/N) o Member AGI (%) o Vendor Code (E.g. "Pending") o Application Status (E.g. "Eligible") o Adequacy Status (E.g. "Pending") o Obligation Status (E.g. "Pending")
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the fields make unauthorized access more consequential.

risks.description: FA Tracker pulls information from a replicated copy of SCIMS through PT-FM, so any weakness in the replication or upstream data flow could expose customer information beyond the original source system. The system depends on multiple linked databases and services, increasing the attack surface for PII.
risks.evidence_quote: FA Tracker pulls its information from NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM) which pulls the information from the SCIMS database.
risks.rationale: Each additional system and transfer point creates another opportunity for unauthorized access or leakage.

risks.description: Although access is constrained by roles, users can filter and sort the data on the client side and then view additional details through a link to PT-FM, which may expose more information than is necessary for the immediate work-list task. This creates a risk of overexposure if role boundaries or client-side controls are misused.
risks.evidence_quote: A user can then filter and sort this data on the client side. Optionally, they can export this work list to MS Excel on their device. Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts.
risks.rationale: Client-side manipulation and linked access can increase the amount of data visible to a user beyond the minimal work-list view.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to the system, which creates a risk of broader internal disclosure if contractor handling is not tightly controlled. The system relies on administrative controls and behavior rules to limit contractor misuse of USDA data.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes. If a user has access to NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM), they may have access to FA Tracker.
risks.rationale: Contractor access expands the population of users who can see PII and therefore raises insider-risk concerns.

risks.description: The system retains information for long periods, potentially as long as the participant remains in conservation programs, which increases the duration of exposure if the data is breached or improperly accessed. Long retention also increases the chance that data will outlive its original operational need.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Longer retention periods generally increase cumulative privacy risk over time.

mitigations.description: Disable or tightly restrict Excel export, or require approved secure export controls such as encryption, watermarking, and logging for any exported file.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting export reduces the chance that PII leaves managed USDA systems onto personal devices.

mitigations.description: Send only the minimum necessary fields in e-mail alerts, and use secure delivery controls with strong recipient verification and retention limits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users can also subscribe to e-mail alerts. The e-mail alerts will contain the same data and fields as the work lists, but will be comprised of only the additional records not present in their previous e-mail alert (new deltas).
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the data in alerts lowers the privacy impact if email is misdelivered or retained.

mitigations.description: Apply strict role-based access and field-level minimization so users see only the specific identifiers and statuses needed for their task.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This data will be constrained to what the user has access to in ProTracts using zRoles.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to need-to-know fields reduces the chance of unnecessary disclosure of sensitive program information.

mitigations.description: Maintain encryption for the data transfer path and monitor the replicated data flow for unauthorized access or integrity issues.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FA Tracker pulls NRCS’ ProTracts-FundManager (PT-FM) data via encrypted web services on the USDA network.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and monitoring help protect PII as it moves between linked systems.

mitigations.description: Enforce server-side authorization for all detailed views and limit client-side filtering to data already approved for the user's role.
mitigations.rationale: Server-side enforcement prevents users from manipulating the client to reveal more data than intended.

mitigations.description: Continue and strengthen contractor onboarding controls, including background checks, need-to-know approval, NDAs, and prohibitions on downloading, sharing, storing, or printing USDA data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Contractors are required to undergo mandatory background investigations commensurate with the sensitivity of their responsibilities, in compliance with Federal requirements and must obtain Level 2 eAuthentication access
mitigations.rationale: Tight contractor controls reduce the likelihood of insider misuse or unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Periodically review retained records and purge or archive data according to the approved records schedule as soon as it is no longer needed for the participant's program status.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), “Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs”.
mitigations.rationale: Regular review and disposal reduce the amount of personal data exposed over time.

risks.description: The system collects and stores direct contact and banking identifiers for exporters, financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks, which could expose sensitive business contact and payment information if mishandled.
risks.evidence_quote: GSM Point of contact names, email addresses, and phone numbers for exporters, US financial institutions, importers, and foreign banks. Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions.
risks.rationale: These data elements can be used to identify and contact specific parties and to facilitate financial transactions, so unauthorized access would create privacy and confidentiality harm.

risks.description: External users can enter and review their own program information through the public internet interface, creating a risk of unauthorized access if authentication or authorization is weak.
risks.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
risks.rationale: A public-facing interface increases exposure to account takeover or improper access to program records if access controls fail.

risks.description: The system produces nightly files and ad hoc reports that are posted to the intranet and submitted to multiple government recipients, increasing the risk that more information is disclosed than necessary to users who do not need it.
risks.evidence_quote: Nightly files are used by the GSM data warehouse team and its users to create (as of COB) ad hoc EPM11 queries/reports, and for the GSM data warehouse system to produce EPM11 canned reports that are posted to the intranet for use by FAS and FSA. Reports are for internal use only by Government employees and contractors; however, the reports generated from the system are submitted to auditors, Department of Treasury, Department of State, etc.
risks.rationale: Broad reporting and distribution paths can expand access beyond the minimum necessary if report content is not tightly controlled.

risks.description: Department contractors have access to the system, which increases the number of people who can view or handle the collected information.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
risks.rationale: More users with access raises the chance of inappropriate disclosure or misuse of the information.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely, which increases the long-term exposure of personal and financial contact data.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the period during which records can be breached, misused, or disclosed improperly.

risks.description: The system uses taxpayer identification numbers and payment bank information, which are highly sensitive if exposed or linked to specific parties.
risks.evidence_quote: Tax identification number and payment bank information for exporters and US financial institutions
risks.rationale: Financial identifiers can enable fraud or unauthorized financial activity if disclosed.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to contact, tax identification, and payment bank information to users with a documented business need and log all access to those fields.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and auditing access reduces the chance that sensitive business and financial data will be viewed or used improperly.

mitigations.description: Require strong authentication and role-based authorization for the public interface, with periodic review of user entitlements.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These entities can enter and review only their specific program information through the public interface of the GSM application.
mitigations.rationale: Tight access control is necessary to ensure users can only reach their own program information.

mitigations.description: Apply data minimization and disclosure review to reports before posting them or sending them to auditors and other agencies, so only necessary fields are included.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing report content lowers the risk of unnecessary disclosure through routine reporting channels.

mitigations.description: Limit contractor access to the minimum necessary functions and data, and require privacy and security training before access is granted.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Department contractors do have access to the System.
mitigations.rationale: Constraining contractor access and training users reduces the likelihood of misuse or accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement a records review process to confirm whether any subset of records can be safely disposed of or further restricted even though the system states permanent retention.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
mitigations.rationale: Periodic review can reduce unnecessary accumulation of records and limit long-term exposure.

mitigations.description: Encrypt tax identification numbers and payment bank information at rest and in transit, and mask them in user interfaces and reports wherever full values are not required.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and masking reduce the impact of disclosure of highly sensitive financial identifiers.

risks.description: The system may store highly sensitive personal data, including identifiers, financial data, criminal history, and signatures, which could cause significant harm if exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the documents includes (is estimated, but may not be limited to): • Name • Date and/or place of birth • Address information (street or email address) • Personal identification number (e.g. social security number, tax identification number, passport number, driver’s license number or a unique identification number, etc.) • Financial data • Criminal history • Employment history • Photographic image • Handwriting or an image of the signature
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored PII increases the privacy impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: Internal and external sharing of files creates a risk of unauthorized disclosure if access controls are misapplied or users share data beyond the intended audience.
risks.evidence_quote: Users can upload documents and photos to a shared files folder, determine how their content can be shared with other users, and invite others to view and/or edit shared files.
risks.rationale: User-controlled sharing expands the number of people who may access the files and increases the chance of accidental or excessive disclosure.

risks.description: Because sharing with contractors and partners is based on role and task need, there is a risk that users with legitimate access may still see more PII than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: PII information is shared with FPAC employees, contractors, and partners when deemed required to complete assigned task.
risks.rationale: Need-to-know sharing can still be overbroad if roles and task boundaries are not tightly enforced.

risks.description: The system stores PII in a third-party cloud service, which creates a dependency on the vendor to maintain and secure the information.
risks.evidence_quote: Any PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of third-party applications will be maintained and secured by the vendor, Box Inc.
risks.rationale: When a vendor holds the data, the agency must rely on the vendor’s controls and operations to protect privacy.

risks.description: PII obtained from public web applications is manually stored in the cloud repository, which can lead to handling errors or inconsistent protection during ingestion.
risks.evidence_quote: Information from the affected members of the public (i.e., farmers, landowners, etc.) may be entered in through FPAC Web applications, then is only manually stored in FPAC Box.
risks.rationale: Manual transfer steps increase the chance of mistakes that could expose or misplace PII.

risks.description: PII used to create and update user profiles from LDAP can be exposed or altered inappropriately if account administration is not tightly controlled.
risks.evidence_quote: For administration, FPAC Box uses the PII that was initially obtained from LDAP to establish the user’s profile. FPAC Box can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: Profile data is a privacy-sensitive account asset, and unauthorized changes or access could affect identity and access management.

risks.description: The system retains records for long periods, which increases the window during which stored PII could be accessed or exposed.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the time that sensitive records remain available to insiders, attackers, or accidental disclosure.

risks.description: PII is not periodically purged from third-party applications, which can leave data available longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: 10.6 Is the PII that becomes available through the agency’s use of 3rd party websites and/or applications purged periodically? • No
risks.rationale: Without periodic purging, unnecessary copies of PII may accumulate and remain exposed in vendor systems.

risks.description: Disabling an account when a user leaves may not fully remove or protect the user’s stored data, leaving residual PII accessible in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: If the user leaves, their account gets disabled.
risks.rationale: Account disablement alone does not necessarily delete stored files or other retained personal data.

mitigations.description: Apply stricter file-level access controls and minimize storage of sensitive PII by limiting uploads to only what is necessary for the mission.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of sensitive data stored lowers the impact of any unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Require explicit sharing approval or warning prompts before files are shared externally or with broader groups.
mitigations.rationale: Extra confirmation helps prevent accidental over-sharing of files containing PII.

mitigations.description: Enforce least-privilege access reviews for employees, contractors, and partners to verify that each user still needs access.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to FPAC Box is controlled through role-based authorization, eAuthentication, and DRM, which includes FIPS 140-2 certified encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Role-based controls are intended to limit access to what each user needs, reducing unnecessary exposure.

mitigations.description: Add contractual and oversight requirements for Box Inc. security and privacy controls, including audit rights and incident reporting.
mitigations.rationale: Vendor oversight helps ensure the third party maintains the protections needed for agency PII.

mitigations.description: Use a documented intake and validation process for manually stored documents, with checks for correct classification and secure handling.
mitigations.rationale: A controlled intake process reduces the chance that manually transferred PII is mishandled.

mitigations.description: Limit who can update profile information and log all profile changes for review.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC Box can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting and auditing updates helps prevent unauthorized or mistaken changes to identity-related data.

mitigations.description: Apply records schedules consistently and review stored files periodically to delete records as soon as they are no longer required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary from five to ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal reduces the amount of sensitive data retained and the duration of exposure risk.

mitigations.description: Implement periodic purging for PII held in third-party applications.
mitigations.rationale: Regular purging limits unnecessary retention of PII in vendor-managed environments.

mitigations.description: Delete or archive a departing user’s data according to retention rules instead of only disabling the account.
mitigations.rationale: Removing or securing residual data prevents dormant accounts from leaving PII behind.

risks.description: User information is transmitted between farmers or producers and external agencies, creating a risk that sensitive application data could be intercepted or exposed during transit.
risks.evidence_quote: As a result, information will be sent to (and from) users (farmers and producers) to DOL and USCIS, even though FPAC CASP / H2A does not assess or perform any actions on the data.
risks.rationale: Any system that passes data between multiple parties increases exposure if transmission protections fail.

risks.description: The system relies on external websites and services, so users' information may be handled by organizations outside USDA's direct control.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A is, however, used as a ‘pass through’ system to allow farmers and producers to access DOL and USCIS from a single (common) entry point.
risks.rationale: Passing information to external agencies expands the privacy boundary beyond the hosting system.

risks.description: A stored DOL case number could be linked back to a producer's inquiry and may expose case-related information if improperly accessed or disclosed.
risks.evidence_quote: The only information stored by FPAC CASP / H2A is to allow a producer to save their inquiry and a DOL case number; this will allow the producer to retrieve their information from DOL and continue with their inquiry.
risks.rationale: Even limited stored identifiers can become sensitive when they enable retrieval of case information.

risks.description: Because the system uses single authentication to access multiple federal agencies, compromise of that access path could affect information across more than one agency.
risks.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A allows users to access several US Federal agencies only using a single authentication.
risks.rationale: A shared authentication path concentrates risk if credentials or session controls are weak.

risks.description: The system expects PII to be inside its boundary even though it says it does not store most of it, which creates a risk of accidental retention or logging of sensitive data.
risks.evidence_quote: the H2A application is expected to have PII inside its system boundary.
risks.rationale: Systems that handle but do not persist PII can still inadvertently capture it in logs, caches, or error records.

mitigations.description: Require strong end-to-end encryption for all data exchanges between FPAC CASP, Login.gov, DOL, and USCIS, and monitor for transmission failures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov occur using HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Encrypted transport reduces the chance that transmitted data can be read in transit.

mitigations.description: Limit the data passed to external agencies to the minimum necessary for the transaction and document the external sharing boundaries.
mitigations.rationale: Minimizing what is sent outside USDA reduces privacy exposure when external services are involved.

mitigations.description: Protect the stored DOL case number with access controls, restrict who can retrieve it, and delete it as soon as it is no longer needed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The only information stored by FPAC CASP / H2A is to allow a producer to save their inquiry and a DOL case number; this will allow the producer to retrieve their information from DOL and continue with their inquiry.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access and retention lowers the chance that a case number can be misused or exposed.

mitigations.description: Use strong multi-factor authentication and session protections for the single sign-on path to the external agencies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A allows users to access several US Federal agencies only using a single authentication.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger authentication helps protect a single entry point that gates access to multiple systems.

mitigations.description: Implement controls to prevent accidental storage of PII in logs, caches, or temporary files, and regularly test that only the DOL case number is retained.
mitigations.evidence_quote: FPAC CASP / H2A does not store any PII with the exception of a case where a producer can save their inquiry and a DOL case number is stored by FPAC CASP / H2A.
mitigations.rationale: Controls that enforce the intended data-minimization design reduce the risk of unintended retention.

risks.description: DRMS stores scanned paper records that may contain highly sensitive personal and financial identifiers, creating a risk of exposure if the stored documents are mishandled or breached. The system explicitly includes items such as SSNs, tax IDs, bank account details, and farm ownership information.
risks.evidence_quote: Potential PII found in the encrypted documents includes: Name, Legal Name, Address, Tax ID number (individual or business), SSN, Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number, Registration in Central Contractor Registration database, Legal description of farm location, Tract Number, Deeds, Farm Shareholder salaries, Location, Farm ownership detail, Bank routing numbers, Deposit Account numbers, Contract numbers, Vendor ID.
risks.rationale: The breadth and sensitivity of the stored identifiers increase the impact of any unauthorized access or disclosure.

risks.description: TeamMate+ contains PII from audit documents and can include information from many FPAC programs and external parties, creating a risk that audit files expose sensitive personal or business information. The data may include financial, HR, grants, purchase card, real property, and producer records.
risks.evidence_quote: The data could be in the form of Financial Management, Human Resources, Grants and Agreements, Purchase Cards, Real Property, Producer Applications, Producer Payments, Producer Contracts and Producer Records.
risks.rationale: Audit repositories often aggregate information from multiple sources, which increases the sensitivity of the records held in one place.

risks.description: DRMS permits broad internal search and specialized unconstrained searching for legal and audit purposes, which creates a risk of overbroad access to records beyond what is necessary for a user's job. The system says all staff can upload and search, with special roles able to perform unconstrained searching.
risks.evidence_quote: All staff are able to upload and search for documents, limited by their organizational role and rights. Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Broad search capability increases the chance that users can view records unrelated to their assigned duties.

risks.description: TeamMate+ allows customer-uploaded audit documents and, in rare cases, auditor uploads, creating a risk that incorrect or excessive PII is introduced into the system. The system depends on users to provide the documents rather than collecting only narrowly defined fields.
risks.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
risks.rationale: User-supplied uploads can bring in unnecessary or misfiled personal information that is then retained in the audit record.

risks.description: DRMS ingests scanned paper documents and stores metadata in multiple databases, which creates a risk that documents or metadata could be linked, copied, or exposed across components. The system uses MS SQL, Alfresco, and Elasticsearch for storage and retrieval.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
risks.rationale: Multiple storage layers increase the number of places where personal information must be protected consistently.

risks.description: The system retains information for very long periods, including permanent records, which increases the risk that old PII will remain available longer than necessary. The retention language says most applications are retained indefinitely.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Long retention extends the window in which records can be misused, disclosed, or become stale.

risks.description: Contractors may have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod, creating a risk that non-federal personnel can view sensitive records if access controls are not tightly enforced. The system explicitly allows contractor access on a need-to-know basis.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Expanding access beyond federal staff increases the number of people who can potentially see sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to DRMS documents containing sensitive identifiers by enforcing role-based access, encryption at rest, and periodic review of who can open or download records.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting and protecting access reduces the likelihood that sensitive identifiers will be exposed.

mitigations.description: Apply strict need-to-know access controls and minimize the audit documents retained in TeamMate+ to only what is necessary to support findings.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data are used in the FPAC financial audit process and serve as proof/documentation of findings.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of stored audit material lowers the privacy impact of any disclosure.

mitigations.description: Limit DRMS search and retrieval permissions so that specialized unconstrained searching is approved, logged, and periodically reviewed for necessity.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
mitigations.rationale: Approval and review help prevent overbroad access while preserving legitimate business needs.

mitigations.description: Require pre-upload review or validation of TeamMate+ attachments to ensure customers and auditors do not submit unnecessary PII.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The data can be either uploaded directly into TeamMate+ by the customer (most common) or it can be uploaded by auditors (in rare cases).
mitigations.rationale: Checking uploads before storage reduces the chance that excess personal information enters the system.

mitigations.description: Synchronize access controls and auditing across MS SQL, Alfresco, and Elasticsearch so that scanned documents and metadata are protected consistently end to end.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The information is collected when scanned into the system and into the databases. Databases: MS SQL Database, Alfresco database, Elasticsearch database.
mitigations.rationale: Consistent controls across all repositories reduce the risk of exposure through a weaker component.

mitigations.description: Apply records disposition controls to delete or archive records according to the approved NARA schedule instead of defaulting to indefinite retention where not required.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
