risks.rationale: Retaining personal information longer than necessary increases the risk of exposure or misuse.

risks.description: Risk of improper handling of personal information during transfer.
risks.evidence_quote: Transferring of PII information is transmitted via email from the AskUSDA Contact Center to SME Contacts and through Cisco Telephony Integration.
risks.rationale: Email transfers and telephony integrations can expose personal information to interception or unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate user consent for data collection.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be collected on a regular basis directly from the customer. The customer has the ability up and until the point at which they submit the inquiry to AskUSDA Contact Center (webform, email, chat or phone call) to decide whether they provide their contact information or not.
risks.rationale: Users may not fully understand the extent of data collection and subsequent uses of their information.

mitigations.description: Implement robust cybersecurity measures to protect against unauthorized access.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced security protocols reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access to sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough security assessments and audits of third-party integrations.
mitigations.rationale: Regular assessments ensure that third-party integrations meet the necessary security standards.

mitigations.description: Establish clear policies for data retention and periodic purging of unnecessary data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: No purging or archiving is setup currently but expecting to keep at least for 7 years prior to archival, since this is a pilot this will would be reassess after the pilot phase to get a better idea of data storage required.
mitigations.rationale: Clear retention policies minimize the risk associated with storing excess data.

mitigations.description: Use secure methods for transferring personal information.
mitigations.rationale: Secure methods like encrypted emails and secure APIs reduce the risk of data interception during transfers.

mitigations.description: Provide clear and comprehensive privacy notices to inform users about data collection practices.
mitigations.rationale: Transparent communication builds trust and ensures users are aware of their rights regarding their personal information.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to video footage by unauthorized personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to VSS will be granted for both USDA employees and select non-employees with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: The system grants access to non-USDA employees, increasing the risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of improper retention and deletion of video footage.
risks.evidence_quote: The intent is a 6-month retention period for all video footage, however, depending on storage, camera counts and other factors, video may be retained for longer, but will be over-written on a first in first out basis.
risks.rationale: There is ambiguity in the retention policy leading to potential over-retention of footage.

risks.description: Risk of video footage being shared beyond necessary recipients.
risks.evidence_quote: Video footage will only be shared with internal organizations in response to formal requests, such as criminal investigations and disciplinary actions.
risks.rationale: The sharing of video footage may extend beyond formal requests, risking unnecessary dissemination.

risks.description: Risk of video footage capturing sensitive personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The VSS cameras may capture facial images of employees and visitors to USDA buildings and images of license plates that are parked or driving through the parking lot.
risks.rationale: Cameras capture detailed personal information, increasing privacy concerns.

risks.description: Risk of metadata misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: Regarding a VSS, some examples are camera name, location, time, and date. The data is used to manage the VSS feeds and footage files.
risks.rationale: Metadata can provide extensive details about the footage and its context, posing risks if misused.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and continuous monitoring for access logs.
mitigations.rationale: Strict controls reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Develop and enforce a clear retention policy with specific criteria for exceptions.
mitigations.rationale: Clear policies ensure consistent compliance with retention requirements.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing of video footage to only those with a need-to-know basis.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting sharing limits unnecessary exposure of sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Place cameras in locations that minimize capture of sensitive personal information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Cameras are not placed in places with a reasonable expectation of privacy such as inside a bathroom or changing room.
mitigations.rationale: Proper placement reduces incidental capture of sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Anonymize metadata where possible and restrict access to metadata.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of identifiable data in metadata decreases privacy risks.

risks.description: Collection of personal information without adequate consent.
risks.evidence_quote: On certain occasions or in free-form comment boxes, the VoC tool will also be collecting some limited PII including: • First and Last Name; • Email Address; and • Zip Code.
risks.rationale: Customers might provide PII without fully understanding how it will be used.

risks.description: Potential misuse of personal information by authorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: A small number of users will have access to all the data across all the mission areas.
risks.rationale: Users with broad access could potentially misuse PII.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data.
risks.evidence_quote: Approved USDA employees will undergo in-person training on platform functionality, privacy, and security controls.
risks.rationale: Training alone may not prevent all unauthorized access attempts.

risks.description: Retention period not officially approved.
risks.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
risks.rationale: Uncertainty around retention periods can lead to improper handling of data.

mitigations.description: Implement clear and concise privacy notices informing users about the collection and usage of PII.
mitigations.rationale: Ensures users are informed and consent to the collection of their PII.

mitigations.description: Limit access to PII to only those who require it for specific tasks.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Users of the VoC platform will be selected based on their mission need to access the system and their permission levels.
mitigations.rationale: Reduces the risk of misuse by restricting access.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for accessing sensitive data.
mitigations.rationale: Adds an additional layer of security against unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Obtain approval from NARA for the established retention schedules.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Has the retention period been approved by the component records officer and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)? No
mitigations.rationale: Clarifies retention policies and ensures compliance with regulations.

risks.description: Users' mandatory personal information like names and emails must be provided, potentially leading to over-collection of PII.
risks.evidence_quote: First name, last name, email address and username are mandatory fields for account creation. This information cannot be omitted.
risks.rationale: Requiring non-essential PII increases privacy risk.

risks.description: Publicly accessible data stored in Wdesk could expose sensitive financial information.
risks.evidence_quote: All information on the document will be publicly accessible data. No, the data used on wDesk will be for the USDA Annual Financial Report. This information contains information that is mandated to be available to the public.
risks.rationale: Sensitive financial details should not be made public.

risks.description: The lack of consent for the use of personal information raises privacy concerns.
risks.evidence_quote: User information is not shared outside of the Workiva wDesk internal system.
risks.rationale: Users should be informed and give consent for how their information is used.

risks.description: External hosting of the system poses a risk due to potential breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: Wdesk is hosted outside of the ACFO-SS-FMS boundary.
risks.rationale: Third-party hosting increases vulnerability to breaches.

mitigations.description: Only collect necessary PII and ensure that users understand why the information is required.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing unnecessary PII lowers privacy risks.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption to protect sensitive data even when it's publicly accessible.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced security measures protect sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Provide clear documentation and consent forms outlining how personal information will be used.
mitigations.rationale: Transparency and consent enhance user trust.

mitigations.description: Ensure robust security agreements and compliance audits with the third-party host.
mitigations.rationale: Strong security agreements mitigate third-party risks.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive financial and personal information due to the system's reliance on external connections and manual entry.
risks.evidence_quote: The data sources for FNS FM-GSS are sourced through the applications hosted in FNS FM-GSS and transferred to connecting systems that process such data. Also other sources of data are entered by USDA FNS employees who have been approved for FNS FM-GSS access.
risks.rationale: External connections and manual data entry increase the attack surface, potentially exposing sensitive information.

risks.description: Risk of improper handling of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) when sharing data with external organizations.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS award results related information can be shared with a number of external parties, including, but not limited to, non-profit organizations, state and local organizations, individuals, corporations, and entities outside the US.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII with external organizations poses a risk of misuse or breach.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches during transmission due to inadequate encryption methods.
risks.evidence_quote: Applications within FNS FM-GSS are covered by SORN FNS-10, Persons Doing Business with Food and Nutrition Service (FNS). Sharing of PII is limited to review panelists involved in the grants process. Application systems will redact received EIN/TIN from applications. Other PII will be encrypted before distributing to review panelists.
risks.rationale: While some data is encrypted, there is a risk that not all transmissions are properly secured.

risks.description: Risk of data loss or corruption during backups and system maintenance operations.
risks.evidence_quote: Yes, FNS contractors have access to the FNS FM-GSS applications for the following reasons: Retrieval and upload of Grants.gov files; Back-Up of files and data; Application and database support; Account management; and Operating system support.
risks.rationale: Contractors performing backups and maintenance operations can introduce errors or vulnerabilities.

risks.description: Risk of data retention beyond necessary periods, leading to unnecessary exposure of sensitive information.
risks.evidence_quote: GIMS information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after the closeout of the program and archived per FNS archival policy. FMAT information is retained and archived in primary storage for six (6) years after final Payment or cancellation.
risks.rationale: Long-term retention increases the likelihood of data breaches or accidental disclosures.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and regular audits for all external connections and manual data entry points.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits and strict controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Establish clear policies and training for proper handling and redaction of PII before sharing with external organizations.
mitigations.rationale: Clear policies and training ensure compliance with data protection regulations.

mitigations.description: Ensure all data transmissions are fully encrypted, including those between internal systems and contractors.
mitigations.rationale: Full encryption protects data during transmission from potential interception.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security assessments and penetration testing for backup and maintenance operations performed by contractors.
mitigations.rationale: Security assessments help identify and mitigate vulnerabilities introduced by contractors.

mitigations.description: Develop and enforce strict data retention policies aligned with regulatory requirements to minimize unnecessary data exposure.
mitigations.rationale: Strict retention policies reduce the risk of data breaches or accidental disclosures.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive personal and financial information due to the centralized storage of SNAP participant data.
risks.evidence_quote: Data will be sent via the secure MoveIt or Box managed file transfer application. SNAP participant data to be contained in the SNAP Information Database will include detailed and sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) which is required to perform the integrity checks as designed, as well as financial data (e.g., amount of benefit received).
risks.rationale: The centralized storage of sensitive data increases the risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches during transmission of SNAP participant data between states and the central database.
risks.evidence_quote: Data will be sent via the secure MoveIt or Box managed file transfer application.
risks.rationale: Transmission of sensitive data between entities creates vulnerabilities for interception or breach.

risks.description: Risk of identity theft and fraud due to the extensive collection and cross-referencing of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: In addition, this initiative will focus on detecting duplicate enrollments across states, verifying immigration status eligibility, and performing other fraud prevention checks using lawfully shared internal and interagency data across a number of Federal agencies.
risks.rationale: Cross-referencing large volumes of personal data increases the potential for identity theft and fraud.

risks.description: Risk of excessive data retention leading to long-term exposure of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Data from all participants since 2000 to present will be collected, with quarterly updates submitted by states or their EBT processors thereafter.
risks.rationale: Long-term retention of data increases the duration and extent of privacy exposure.

risks.description: Risk of misuse of personal information beyond the scope intended for integrity checks.
risks.evidence_quote: States will transmit data from
risks.rationale: While data is collected for integrity checks, there is a risk it could be misused for other purposes without explicit consent.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption protocols to protect data at rest.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Use end-to-end encryption for all data transmissions between states and the central database.
mitigations.rationale: End-to-end encryption minimizes the risk of interception during data transmission.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits and implement robust authentication mechanisms to prevent identity theft.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits and strong authentication reduce the risk of identity theft and fraud.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear data retention policy and securely purge data that is no longer needed.
mitigations.rationale: Proper data retention policies minimize the long-term exposure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Limit access to data based on need-to-know principles and monitor usage for compliance.
mitigations.rationale: Need-to-know access limits and monitoring help ensure data is not misused.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to affiliate data due to limited access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: The Affiliates system is only accessible by NRCS employees.
risks.rationale: Since only NRCS employees have access, there is a risk if proper access controls are not enforced.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches due to sharing of sensitive affiliate information between internal systems.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is shared between the Affiliates application and the NRCS zRoles application for the purpose of assigning specific roles in eAuth.
risks.rationale: Data transfer between systems increases the attack surface and potential for breaches.

risks.description: Risk of inaccurate affiliate information leading to inappropriate access grants.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is provided directly to an NRCS employee by the affiliate.
risks.rationale: Human error during data entry can result in incorrect affiliate details, compromising security.

risks.description: Risk of prolonged retention of personal data beyond necessary periods.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Retention periods longer than necessary may expose individuals to unnecessary risks.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and multi-factor authentication for NRCS employees accessing the system.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Use encrypted channels for data transfer between the Affiliates application and the zRoles application.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures that even if data is intercepted, it cannot be read without decryption keys.

mitigations.description: Implement a verification process where NRCS employees cross-check entered affiliate information with official documents.
mitigations.rationale: Cross-checking reduces the chances of human error affecting data accuracy.

mitigations.description: Develop a policy to regularly review and purge outdated affiliate records to ensure compliance with minimum retention guidelines.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of stored data minimizes exposure to unnecessary risks.

risks.description: Collection of sensitive personal information without direct consent.
risks.evidence_quote: The BAD data warehouse does not collect information directly from individuals; information is obtained from FSA and RMA. The right to decline to provide information on the part of the individual is not applicable to this project.
risks.rationale: Individuals cannot opt-out or give consent when their data is collected by FSA and RMA.

risks.description: Potential for data breaches due to the storage of personally identifiable information (PII).
risks.evidence_quote: The BAD Data Warehouse provides access to and maintains weather and crop loss data by way of a web application known as Hyper Dynamic Reporting Application (HyDRA).
risks.rationale: PII stored in the BAD Data Warehouse could be exposed if the system is compromised.

risks.description: Data inaccuracies may occur during the transformation and loading process.
risks.evidence_quote: Identifying and correcting the files that do not load ensures the completeness of the data load.
risks.rationale: Inaccurate data handling can lead to incorrect analyses and decision-making.

risks.description: Sharing of sensitive data with multiple internal organizations.
risks.evidence_quote: Currently the information described previously is provided to FSA, RMA, and OIG within USDA.
risks.rationale: Multiple sharing points increase the risk of data leakage or misuse.

risks.description: Long-term retention of personal data raises concerns about prolonged exposure to potential threats.
risks.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
risks.rationale: Prolonged retention increases the chance of unauthorized access over time.

mitigations.description: Provide clear public notices regarding the collection and use of PII.
mitigations.rationale: Notices can inform individuals indirectly about the collection practices.

mitigations.description: Implement robust encryption and secure access controls.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and access controls minimize the risk of data breaches.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough data validation and standardization processes.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) tools and post cleansing scripts are used to clean up the data.
mitigations.rationale: Standardization helps ensure data accuracy.

mitigations.description: Limit access permissions to only necessary personnel within each organization.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to data stored in the BAD data warehouse is restricted to authorized users in RMA, FSA and AIPs.
mitigations.rationale: Limited access reduces the likelihood of misuse or unauthorized disclosure.

mitigations.description: Establish strict data retention schedules and regular audits.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Information will be retained for the life of the project then returned to RMA.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits ensure compliance with retention policies and reduce exposure.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to PII due to potential vulnerabilities in eAuth and RBAC mechanisms.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to CoLab is controlled through eAuth and Role Based Access Control (RBAC).
risks.rationale: If eAuth or RBAC mechanisms are compromised, unauthorized individuals could gain access to PII.

risks.description: Risk of PII exposure during user profile creation and modification processes.
risks.evidence_quote: CoLab uses the PII that was initially obtained from eAuth to establish the user’s profile. CoLab can also be used to update the PII that is maintained for individual users, if they choose to modify their own profile.
risks.rationale: During these processes, PII might be exposed if security protocols are not strictly followed.

risks.description: Risk of data breach due to unauthorized contractor access.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors have access to the system consistent with their roles and responsibilities.
risks.rationale: Unauthorized or malicious actions by contractors could lead to a data breach.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate data retention policies leading to prolonged storage of unnecessary PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Information has been authorized by the NRCS Records Manager for erasure or deletion when the agency determines that this information is no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes.
risks.rationale: Lack of strict adherence to these policies could result in prolonged storage of PII, increasing risk.

mitigations.description: Implement regular security audits and penetration testing for eAuth and RBAC mechanisms.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits and testing help identify and mitigate vulnerabilities.

mitigations.description: Encrypt all PII data during transmission and storage.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures that even if data is intercepted or accessed without authorization, it cannot be read.

mitigations.description: Conduct background checks and require non-disclosure agreements for all contractors accessing CoLab.
mitigations.rationale: Background checks and NDAs reduce the risk of contractors misusing or leaking PII.

mitigations.description: Develop and enforce strict guidelines for data retention and deletion.
mitigations.rationale: Strict guidelines ensure that PII is only retained for necessary periods, reducing exposure risk.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to vendor PII stored in the IDEA DataMart.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of this SCIMS PII is maintained in the IDEA DataMart to ensure efficient performance during the generation of IDEA reports.
risks.rationale: Maintaining vendor PII in the IDEA DataMart increases the risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of outdated vendor PII due to periodic refreshes.
risks.evidence_quote: This PII is refreshed periodically from the SCIMS source system to ensure that it remains current.
risks.rationale: Periodic updates mean there could be a window where the data is outdated, potentially leading to incorrect reports.

risks.description: Risk of accidental disclosure of vendor PII during report generation.
risks.evidence_quote: Some of these financial reports contain vendor PH that is obtained from the Service Center Information Management System (SCIMS) system via read-only web service calls.
risks.rationale: Access to vendor PII during report generation increases the likelihood of accidental disclosure.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for the IDEA DataMart.
mitigations.rationale: Strict access controls and encryption would help prevent unauthorized access to sensitive vendor PII.

mitigations.description: Automate the refresh process to minimize the window of outdated data.
mitigations.rationale: An automated refresh process would reduce the risk of using outdated PII in reports.

mitigations.description: Provide training on data handling and confidentiality policies for users generating reports.
mitigations.rationale: Training would enhance awareness and reduce the likelihood of accidental disclosure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: Core Services accesses the following information for Program Participants, Farmers, Ranchers and Producers: • Full name or alias • Street Address or email address • SCIMS Customer ID that can be associated to a Social security number or tax identification number • bank account numbers (last few digits only) • case number (caseId, casename)
risks.rationale: Sensitive personal information could be accessed by unauthorized individuals leading to identity theft or misuse.

risks.description: Potential for data breaches during transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: The transmission of API requests and formatted data between the client applications and Core Services is accomplished by way of Port 443, HTTPS
risks.rationale: Data transmitted over HTTPS can still be intercepted if the encryption is compromised or if there are vulnerabilities in the implementation.

risks.description: Risk of data exposure due to contractor access.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Core Services as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractors, despite background checks, may pose a risk if they misuse the information or if their systems are compromised.

risks.description: Possibility of privacy violations through misuse of SCIMS data.
risks.evidence_quote: NRCS has a view of the SCIMS database and access to the data from SCIMS for NRCS users is via NPAD and through eAuthentication (eAuth). NRCS users do not have direct access to SCIMS.
risks.rationale: Access to SCIMS data might be misused if proper controls and audits are not in place.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and multi-factor authentication.
mitigations.rationale: Multi-factor authentication adds an additional layer of security beyond just usernames and passwords.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments.
mitigations.rationale: Regular security audits can help identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities before they are exploited.

mitigations.description: Ensure contractors sign confidentiality agreements and undergo regular security training.
mitigations.rationale: Confidentiality agreements and security training can reinforce the importance of protecting sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Limit access to SCIMS data to authorized personnel only and log all access attempts.
mitigations.rationale: Logging access attempts can help in tracking and auditing who accessed sensitive data.

risks.description: Collection of sensitive personal information without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: The PII can be obtained from publicly accessible information resources, from organizations involved in emergency response, or submitted voluntarily by individual responders or property owners.
risks.rationale: The collection of sensitive personal information such as home addresses and phone numbers raises privacy concerns.

risks.description: Potential misuse of personal information stored in Emergency Action Plans (EAPs).
risks.evidence_quote: DamWatch does not share PII data with any other system. NRCS personnel may access EAPs containing PII, as needed;
risks.rationale: Access to sensitive personal information increases the risk of misuse.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
risks.rationale: While access controls are in place, there is always a risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Data retention beyond necessity.
risks.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Retaining data for extended periods increases the risk of exposure and misuse.

risks.description: Sharing of personal information with external organizations.
risks.evidence_quote: The EAPs within DamWatch are created and maintained by NRCS and other state and local dam project sponsors. The PII contained within the EAPs is shared with state and local emergency responders in the event of activation of an EAP.
risks.rationale: Sharing personal information externally exposes individuals' data to additional parties.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent for the collection of personal information.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent ensures that individuals are aware of and agree to the collection of their personal information.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and logging for EAPs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Strict access controls and detailed logging help prevent and detect unauthorized use.

mitigations.description: Regularly audit access logs for suspicious activities.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access to DamWatch is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits can help identify and mitigate unauthorized access attempts.

mitigations.description: Review and justify the necessity of data retention periods.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All information will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
mitigations.rationale: Justifying retention periods helps ensure that data is kept only as long as necessary.

mitigations.description: Limit sharing of personal information to emergencies only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: PII contained within EAPs will be disclosed via hardcopy or electronic copy during EAP review cycles or when an EAP is activated.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting sharing to emergencies minimizes unnecessary exposure of personal information.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive personal and financial information due to potential vulnerabilities in the system.
risks.evidence_quote: Access to DRMS is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
risks.rationale: The current authentication method may not be robust enough to prevent unauthorized access.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches during the process of scanning and storing paper records.
risks.evidence_quote: DRMS collects scanned paper records to include digitized forms and its related metadata.
risks.rationale: Scanning and storage processes may introduce vulnerabilities that could lead to data breaches.

risks.description: Risk of misuse of personal information by authorized personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized FPAC staff has access to the documents maintained in DRMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Authorized personnel may misuse their access to personal information.

risks.description: Risk of improper retention periods leading to unnecessary storage of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29.
risks.rationale: Improper retention periods could result in excessive storage of sensitive information.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate security measures during the transfer of paper documents to electronic formats.
risks.evidence_quote: The KOFAX application enables the capture of paper documents to transferred to electronic.
risks.rationale: Transfer processes may lack adequate security measures, exposing data to potential threats.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for accessing the DRMS.
mitigations.rationale: MFA provides an additional layer of security beyond just passwords.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and penetration testing of the DRMS system.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits help identify and mitigate security vulnerabilities.

mitigations.description: Implement strict logging and monitoring of access and activities within the DRMS.
mitigations.rationale: Monitoring helps detect and prevent unauthorized or inappropriate access.

mitigations.description: Adopt a data minimization policy to retain only necessary personal information.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization reduces the risk associated with retaining unnecessary data.

mitigations.description: Ensure encryption of data during the transfer process from KOFAX to DRMS.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects data integrity and confidentiality during transfer.

risks.description: Unauthorized access to sensitive documents containing PII.
risks.evidence_quote: The information collected is transmitted primarily from ProTracts - Fund Manager, CST, and CCG via DMS web services. In addition, DMS allows NRCS users to upload the documents directly into the application.
risks.rationale: Direct upload and transmission capabilities increase exposure to unauthorized access.

risks.description: Data breaches due to vulnerabilities in third-party tools like Adobe PDF.
risks.evidence_quote: Adobe PDF plug-ins are used to view the documents.
risks.rationale: Third-party tools may introduce security risks.

risks.description: Retention of sensitive personal information beyond necessary periods.
risks.evidence_quote: All information contained will be retained in compliance with NARA Guidelines, which vary on average in years from less than one year to more than ten years according to the NARA General Records Schedules Transmittal 29, issued December 2017.
risks.rationale: Excessive retention increases the risk of data exposure.

risks.description: Disclosure of PII to contractors without proper safeguards.
risks.evidence_quote: Disclosure may be made to contractors or to technical service providers when written authorization has been received by the agency from the owner, operator, producer or participant.
risks.rationale: Lack of detailed disclosure controls could lead to misuse of data.

risks.description: Limited user access control and oversight.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DMS. Authorized NRCS staff has access to the documents maintained in DMS and they are able to update incorrect information.
risks.rationale: Broad access permissions reduce accountability and increase risk.

risks.rationale: Although HTTPS is used, there remains a risk of interception if the connection is compromised or improperly configured.

risks.description: Risk of misuse of DOL case numbers due to retention policies.
risks.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
risks.rationale: Retention of DOL case numbers for 90 days may lead to misuse or unauthorized access over time.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for stored DOL case numbers.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access and encrypting stored data minimizes the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Ensure proper configuration and regular audits of HTTPS connections.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Communications between FPAC CASP / H2A and DOL, USCIS, and Login.gov occur using HTTPS.
mitigations.rationale: Proper configuration and auditing of HTTPS connections reduce the risk of interception.

mitigations.description: Reduce the retention period for DOL case numbers to minimize potential misuse.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This DOL case number is retained in FAPC CASP for 90 days.
mitigations.rationale: Shortening the retention period limits the window during which DOL case numbers are vulnerable to misuse.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors with a need-to-know will have access to Pipeline FPAC Mod as part of their regular assigned duties.
risks.rationale: Contractors may pose a risk if not adequately vetted or monitored.

risks.description: Risk of data breaches during transmission or storage.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is securely stored for retrieval when needed for a business use by FPAC.
risks.rationale: The secure storage claim does not specify the exact security measures.

risks.description: Risk of excessive data retention leading to unnecessary exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the risk of exposure over time.

risks.description: Risk of inadequate user access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: Specialized roles for records managers and legal staff allow for lifecycle management of records or unconstrained searching for audit, legal discover, litigation holds, or Freedom Of Information Act inquiries.
risks.rationale: Unconstrained searching and lifecycle management can lead to misuse.

risks.description: Risk of lack of individual access rights.
risks.evidence_quote: Individuals do not have access to DRMS and TeamMate+.
risks.rationale: Lack of individual access rights may violate privacy principles.

mitigations.description: Implement strict background checks and continuous monitoring for contractors.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced vetting reduces the risk posed by contractors.

mitigations.description: Use encryption for data at rest and in transit.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures data remains confidential even if accessed improperly.

mitigations.description: Establish clear data retention policies aligned with legal requirements.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any deviations from the NARA Retention Schedule will be approved by NARA when the archiving and retention strategy is defined.
mitigations.rationale: Compliance with legal requirements minimizes unnecessary data exposure.

mitigations.description: Implement granular access controls and audit trails.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Access granted to end users, is approved by IAL2 and are given privileges based on a least privileged model.
mitigations.rationale: Granular controls reduce the risk of misuse and unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Provide individuals with the right to request corrections to their personal information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: An individual may obtain information about a record in the system which pertains to such individual by submitting a written request to the above listed System Manager.
mitigations.rationale: Individual access rights enhance privacy protection.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The Pipeline RMA HVA shares data with the RMA Strategic Data Analysis Division, which performs the forensic data mining of RMA's data, looking for indications of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse.
risks.rationale: Sensitive personal information is shared within the organization for forensic analysis, which could expose the data to unauthorized access.

risks.description: Long-term retention of personal information without clear necessity.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Data is retained indefinitely, raising concerns about the necessity and proportionality of retaining sensitive personal information.

risks.description: Possibility of data breaches during transmission.
risks.evidence_quote: The data is transmitted via a dedicated VPN line
risks.rationale: Transmitting sensitive data over a dedicated network still poses a risk of interception or breach.

risks.description: Inadequate protection of Social Security Numbers and Taxpayer Identification Numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: This data is being collected to determine the eligibility of producers, agents and loss adjusters for the Federal Crop Insurance Program, to detail the amount and types of claims to be processed and/or paid by the RMA on behalf of the FCIC, and to track certain actuarial trends and data to determine viability of current and future insurance products.
risks.rationale: Collection and storage of SSNs and TINs require stringent protections, which may be insufficient based on the provided information.

risks.description: Third-party access to sensitive data without adequate safeguards.
risks.evidence_quote: Department contractors have access to the system.
risks.rationale: Contractors accessing the system pose additional risks due to their third-party status and potential lack of adherence to strict internal security protocols.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and audit trails for forensic data analysis.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access and monitoring who accesses the data can help prevent unauthorized use.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear retention schedule based on actual needs.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Any deviations from the NARA Retention Schedule will be approved by NARA when the archiving and retention strategy is defined.
mitigations.rationale: Following a defined retention schedule ensures that only necessary data is kept.

mitigations.description: Encrypt all data transmissions using robust encryption standards.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption provides an added layer of security against interception.

mitigations.description: Apply advanced encryption and tokenization methods for SSNs and TINs.
mitigations.rationale: Tokenization and encryption can significantly reduce the risk of exposing sensitive identifiers.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough background checks and sign confidentiality agreements for contractors.
mitigations.rationale: Ensuring contractors are vetted and legally bound to confidentiality helps mitigate risks associated with third-party access.

risks.description: Collection of personally identifiable information (PII) without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may collect or use a limited amount of Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) when using social media to further its ability to interact with the public.
risks.rationale: The collection of PII without explicit consent from users could lead to unauthorized use of personal data.

risks.description: Potential misuse of collected PII by the CFPB or unauthorized third parties.
risks.evidence_quote: Social media platforms are generally controlled and operated by non-government third parties.
risks.rationale: Third-party involvement increases the risk of unauthorized access or misuse of collected PII.

risks.description: Lack of clear notice regarding the collection and use of PII on social media platforms.
risks.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB may collect PII through social media interactions, this information would be covered by the Social Networks and Citizen Engagement System (CFPB.006) System of Records Notice.
risks.rationale: Insufficient notice to users about the collection and use of their PII could violate privacy expectations.

risks.description: Transparency issues regarding the purpose and scope of PII collection.
risks.evidence_quote: What is the purpose? • Engage the public in CFPB’s mission and its work • Increase operational transparency
risks.rationale: Vague descriptions of the purpose and scope of PII collection can lead to misuse or misunderstanding of collected data.

risks.description: Limited control over how user data is shared with third parties.
risks.evidence_quote: Social media platforms are generally controlled and operated by non-government third parties.
risks.rationale: Third-party control over social media platforms limits the Bureau's ability to ensure data is shared securely.

mitigations.description: Require explicit consent before collecting PII.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent ensures that users are aware and agree to the collection of their personal data.

mitigations.description: Implement robust encryption and secure transmission protocols for PII.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and secure protocols reduce the risk of unauthorized access or misuse of PII.

mitigations.description: Provide clear and detailed notices regarding PII collection and usage.
mitigations.rationale: Detailed notices help users understand how their data will be used and processed.

mitigations.description: Specify the exact purposes and scopes for which PII is collected and used.
mitigations.rationale: Specific descriptions of purpose and scope increase transparency and reduce ambiguity.

mitigations.description: Establish strict contractual agreements with third parties regarding data handling practices.
mitigations.rationale: Contractual agreements provide legal safeguards against improper sharing or misuse of data.

risks.description: Sensitive personal information such as names, addresses, and contact details are exposed to the public.
risks.evidence_quote: Information about individuals associated with HUD‐approved housing counseling agencies includes:  Names (individuals and organizations)  Organization address and contact information including: o Street address o City, state, ZIP code o Phone number o Fax number o Email addresses and website address
risks.rationale: Exposure of such detailed personal information increases the risk of identity theft and unauthorized use.

risks.description: Social Security numbers and financial information may be disclosed, leading to severe identity fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: The Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”) administers the housing counseling program2, which provides counseling to consumers on seeking, financing, maintaining, renting, or owning a home.
risks.rationale: Social Security numbers and financial information are highly sensitive and their disclosure can lead to significant privacy breaches.

risks.description: ZIP codes entered by users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool can potentially reveal user locations.
risks.evidence_quote: PII collected from users of the CFPB housing counselor locator tool includes:  ZIP code entered for search results.
risks.rationale: Users' geographical information could be inferred from the ZIP codes, posing privacy risks.

risks.description: Publicly accessible datasets increase the risk of scraping and misuse of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB housing counselor locator tool and HUD API connection to its counselor dataset are intended for use by the public.
risks.rationale: Public accessibility without adequate protections can lead to unauthorized data harvesting and misuse.

risks.description: Biographical details like dates of birth could aid in social engineering attacks.
risks.evidence_quote: Data Subject includes biographical information such as date of birth.
risks.rationale: Such specific biographical information can be used to impersonate individuals effectively.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization principles to reduce exposure of sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the amount of personal information displayed can mitigate the risk of identity theft and unauthorized use.

mitigations.description: Mask or remove SSNs and financial information from public datasets.
mitigations.rationale: Removing or masking such sensitive information can prevent severe privacy breaches.

mitigations.description: Anonymize ZIP codes or limit their display to protect user locations.
mitigations.rationale: Anonymizing or limiting the display of ZIP codes can reduce the risk of location inference.

mitigations.description: Implement CAPTCHA mechanisms and rate limits to deter automated scraping.
mitigations.rationale: These measures can significantly reduce the likelihood of data being scraped by bots.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to biographical details to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access to such sensitive information can prevent social engineering attacks.

risks.description: The system may inadvertently disclose sensitive personal information due to the inclusion of direct identifying PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Administrative Data collected for Market Research may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number
risks.rationale: Direct identifying PII can lead to unauthorized disclosures if not properly secured.

risks.description: The aggregation and matching of records across different datasets pose a risk of re-identification.
risks.evidence_quote: Market Research may involve the matching of records across different datasets. For example, the CFPB may obtain updates or supplements to a dataset and, in those circumstances, may use record locators unique to the entity providing the update in order to update or supplement the individual records.
risks.rationale: Matching records increases the risk of re-identification when combined with other datasets.

risks.description: The indefinite retention of Administrative Data without a specific retention schedule approved by NARA increases the risk of unauthorized access over time.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases exposure to potential breaches or misuse.

risks.description: Sharing of aggregated data with third parties, such as federal financial regulators, may still contain indirect identifiers that could potentially be linked back to individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the results of Market Research with the general public, the source of the Administrative Data, and/or federal financial regulators. Any such results do not include information that directly identifies any individual.
risks.rationale: Aggregated data may still contain indirect identifiers leading to potential re-identification.

risks.description: Third-party data sources may not adhere to adequate privacy standards, increasing the risk of compromised personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB collects Administrative Data only from third parties, commercial sources and public databases, not directly from consumers, and it is those third parties’ responsibility to determine whether notice is required and to provide any requisite notice.
risks.rationale: Reliance on third parties introduces risks related to their privacy practices.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for all data containing direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized disclosures.

mitigations.description: Anonymize data before performing aggregations and implement strict policies for record matching.
mitigations.rationale: Anonymization reduces the risk of re-identification during data processing.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear and defined retention schedule for Administrative Data.
mitigations.rationale: Defined retention schedules minimize long-term storage risks.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough re-identification risk assessments before sharing aggregated data with third parties.
mitigations.rationale: Risk assessments help ensure shared data is truly anonymized.

mitigations.description: Audit third-party data sources regularly to ensure compliance with privacy standards.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits maintain oversight over third-party privacy practices.

risks.description: Risk of re-identification despite redaction: Although the dataset does not include direct personal identifiers, there is still a possibility that individuals could be re-identified using indirect identifiers.
risks.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset does not include any information that directly identifies an individual.
risks.rationale: Even without direct identifiers, unique combinations of indirect identifiers can potentially lead to re-identification.

risks.description: Risk of sensitive information exposure: The dataset contains sensitive information such as financial details and property types that could be misused if accessed by unauthorized parties.
risks.evidence_quote: The HMDA Public Use Dataset includes the following information: • Loan data o Application year o Loan or application type, purpose, amount (rounded to nearest thousand)
risks.rationale: Financial details can be considered sensitive and could be exploited for malicious purposes.

risks.description: Risk of misuse by third-party organizations: The dataset is shared with federal and state agencies as well as private sector organizations, increasing the risk of misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB is republishing, on consumerfinance.gov, a Dataset that is publicly available on the FFIEC website. As with the dataset available on the FFIEC website, the HMDA Public Use Dataset will be available to the public, including federal and state agencies and private sector organizations.
risks.rationale: Third-party entities might misuse the dataset for unintended purposes beyond the scope of the original regulations.

mitigations.description: Implement de-identification techniques: Apply advanced de-identification methods to further reduce the risk of re-identification.
mitigations.rationale: Advanced de-identification techniques can significantly reduce the likelihood of re-identification.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive information: Limit access to sensitive information to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The public has read-only access to the HMDA Public Use Dataset made available on consumerfinance.gov.
mitigations.rationale: Limiting access helps prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Establish strict usage guidelines: Provide clear guidelines to third parties on the appropriate use of the dataset.
mitigations.rationale: Clear guidelines can help ensure that third parties use the dataset responsibly.

risks.description: Directly collecting and storing sensitive personal information like SSNs and financial details increases the risk of identity theft and fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: Social Security number (“SSN”) or other identifier Financial Information
risks.rationale: Sensitive information such as SSNs and financial details are directly collected and stored, making them vulnerable to unauthorized access.

risks.description: Potential for misuse of aggregated and matched datasets, leading to re-identification of individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases, Consumer Experience Research may involve the matching of records, such as credit score to Response Data, creating new assemblies of information about the Respondent.
risks.rationale: Aggregating and matching datasets can lead to the creation of detailed profiles that might be used to re-identify individuals.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access due to indefinite retention of data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention of data increases the risk of unauthorized access over time.

risks.description: Potential for accidental disclosure when sharing aggregated data externally.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB does not typically share the Response Data generated in the course of Consumer Experience Research in un-aggregated form, unless it is stripped of direct identifying PII and subject to disclosure-protection procedures.
risks.rationale: Sharing aggregated data externally without proper safeguards could lead to accidental disclosure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Risks associated with the monitoring of individuals' behaviors without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB follows an individual’s behavior in the course of conducting Consumer Experience Research, the CPFB obtains the individual’s consent.
risks.rationale: Monitoring individuals' behaviors without explicit consent raises privacy concerns.

mitigations.description: Implement strong encryption and access controls for sensitive data storage.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and strict access controls can significantly reduce the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Use robust anonymization techniques before aggregating and sharing datasets.
mitigations.rationale: Anonymization techniques can prevent the re-identification of individuals in shared datasets.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear and defined retention policy for all collected data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
mitigations.rationale: A defined retention policy limits the exposure period of data to breaches.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits of data sharing processes to ensure compliance with disclosure-protection procedures.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These external products are subject to disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations, and typically do not include direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits help maintain compliance and reduce the risk of accidental disclosures.

mitigations.description: Ensure explicit consent is obtained before monitoring any individual’s behavior.
mitigations.evidence_quote: To the extent that the CFPB follows an individual’s behavior in the course of conducting Consumer Experience Research, the CPFB obtains the individual’s consent.
mitigations.rationale: Obtaining explicit consent aligns with privacy principles and ensures transparency.

risks.description: Direct identifying PII may be exposed during data matching and updating processes.
risks.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does use direct identifying PII in analyses, it does so in order to a) match across datasets; b) update data sets; c) weight datasets in order to make generalizations regarding a given population; d) proxy based on population characteristics; and e) contact potential recipients of surveys and then use those surveys to solicit information on consumer experiences with consumer financial products and services.
risks.rationale: Direct identifying PII is temporarily exposed during data matching and updating, posing a risk of unauthorized exposure.

risks.description: Individuals may not be aware that their information is being collected or used for Market Research.
risks.evidence_quote: In these cases, the use and disclosure of information is controlled by applicable federal law, regulations, discovery rules, and court orders. In cases where notice cannot be provided or is not required, the CFPB has provided constructive notice of how it may use such information through this PIA.
risks.rationale: Lack of direct notice to individuals about the collection and use of their information can lead to a lack of informed consent.

risks.description: Potential misuse of sensitive information like SSNs and financial account numbers.
risks.evidence_quote: In some cases they may include direct identifying PII, including: • Name • Phone number • Home address • Email • Financial account number • Social Security number
risks.rationale: Sensitive information such as SSNs and financial account numbers could be misused if not properly secured.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to SEFL Data due to indefinite retention without NARA approval.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the risk of unauthorized access over time.

risks.description: Third-party sharing of aggregated data may still pose re-identification risks.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may share the products of Market Research with the general public and federal financial regulators. Any such results do not include information that directly identifies any individual.
risks.rationale: Aggregated data could potentially be re-identified, leading to privacy breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for PII during data matching and updating.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and strict access controls reduce the risk of unauthorized exposure.

mitigations.description: Provide clear and accessible notices about data collection and use on the CFPB website.
mitigations.rationale: Clear notices help ensure individuals are informed about how their data is being used.

mitigations.description: Restrict access to sensitive information to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Only CFPB personnel with a need to know are granted access to SEFL Data used for Market Research.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting access limits the risk of misuse.

mitigations.description: Establish a clear and timely records disposition schedule approved by NARA.
mitigations.rationale: Timely disposal of records reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits to assess re-identification risks in shared data.
mitigations.rationale: Regular audits help ensure that shared data remains effectively anonymized.

risks.description: Directly identifiable personal information such as names, phone numbers, email addresses, and SSNs may be exposed in case of a breach.
risks.evidence_quote: The Bureau may use the following direct identifying PII to facilitate and administer Consumer Education: • Names • Phone Number • Email Address • Mailing Address The Bureau may also use this information, as well as a Social Security number or account number, in order to facilitate matching.
risks.rationale: This information is sensitive and can lead to identity theft if compromised.

risks.description: Consumer biographic and contact information could be misused for targeted marketing or fraud.
risks.evidence_quote: The Bureau may use the following direct identifying PII to facilitate and administer Consumer Education: • Names • Phone Number • Email Address • Mailing Address
risks.rationale: This detailed personal data could be exploited for malicious purposes.

risks.description: Financial information collected might expose participants to financial fraud or misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: The Bureau may also use this information, as well as a Social Security number or account number, in order to facilitate matching.
risks.rationale: Financial details are highly sensitive and can lead to severe financial harm if leaked.

risks.description: Online usage information, such as IP addresses and browsing behaviors, could be used to track individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The Bureau may also collect some information related to the use of its website and online tools – specifically how visitors are using the website or tools (including IP address, visit timestamps, browser version and operating system, pages viewed, time on the site, the day and time of access, and the address that linked the user directly to the website or tool)
risks.rationale: This data can be used to infer personal behavior and preferences, leading to potential privacy invasions.

risks.description: Aggregation of various types of information might allow re-identification of participants even when direct identifiers are removed.
risks.evidence_quote: In some special cases, Consumer Education may involve the matching of records, such as credit score to Response Data, creating new information about the Participant.
risks.rationale: Combining different datasets increases the risk of re-identification.

risks.description: Long-term retention of personal data poses a risk due to potential future vulnerabilities in data storage.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until the National Archives and Records Administration (“NARA”) approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Holding onto data for extended periods increases the chance of breaches over time.

risks.description: Sharing aggregated data with third parties could still reveal personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does share Response Data, the CFPB provides notice to the Participants through the notice mechanisms discussed in Section 2.2, and Participants can then choose whether they want to participate given that sharing.
risks.rationale: Even aggregated data can sometimes be reverse-engineered to identify individuals.

risks.description: Limited security measures for transferring data between systems may compromise data integrity.
risks.evidence_quote: These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
risks.rationale: Use of encrypted email alone may not be sufficient to secure all data during transfer.

risks.description: Data collected from third parties without explicit consent from participants poses a risk of unauthorized data sharing.
risks.evidence_quote: Consumer Education primarily relies on information collected directly from the individual and with the individual’s consent to collect information from third parties, such as those that offer or provide consumer financial products or services.
risks.rationale: Collecting data from third parties can bypass participant control over their own data.

risks.description: Public dissemination of research results might inadvertently disclose sensitive participant information.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB may also share the products of Consumer Education or Response Data with the general public, but any products disclosed do not include direct identifying PII, and will typically be subject to further disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, generalized sentiments of Participants, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations.
risks.rationale: Even with protections, public dissemination carries risks of accidental exposure.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for storing and transmitting personally identifiable information.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and access controls can significantly reduce the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Limit the use of personal information to essential purposes and ensure proper disposal of unnecessary data.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB conducts Consumer Education to carry out its statutory mandates. In some cases, direct identifying PII is necessary to facilitate Consumer Education initiatives and research and information collected is limited to only that which is necessary to recruit or schedule Participants in Consumer Education, or establish a basis for comparison in evaluating the effectiveness of specific Consumer Education.
mitigations.rationale: Restricting data usage and proper disposal help minimize the risk of misuse.

mitigations.description: Anonymize financial data before storing or analyzing it.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Direct identifying PII is separated from Participants’ Response Data and (where relevant) Administrative Data for the CFPB’s research purposes. Consumer Education research does not typically involve analysis of direct identifying PII.
mitigations.rationale: Anonymization helps protect financial details from being used for fraudulent activities.

mitigations.description: Ensure that online tracking data is anonymized and aggregated to prevent individual identification.
mitigations.evidence_quote: This information is generally collected in aggregate and is not directly identifying.
mitigations.rationale: Aggregation and anonymization reduce the risk of tracking individuals.

mitigations.description: Regularly review and update data de-identification techniques to adapt to evolving threats.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Such matching is only conducted subject to the Participant’s informed consent.
mitigations.rationale: Continuous improvement of de-identification methods can help mitigate re-identification risks.

mitigations.description: Establish clear guidelines and timelines for data retention and destruction.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until the National Archives and Records Administration (“NARA”) approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
mitigations.rationale: Clear guidelines reduce the risk of long-term data storage vulnerabilities.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough reviews of aggregated data to ensure no personally identifiable information is revealed.
mitigations.evidence_quote: When the CFPB does share Response Data, the CFPB provides notice to the Participants through the notice mechanisms discussed in Section 2.2, and Participants can then choose whether they want to participate given that sharing.
mitigations.rationale: Thorough reviews help prevent accidental disclosure of personal information.

mitigations.description: Use secure and robust data transfer protocols for all data exchanges.
mitigations.evidence_quote: These transfers can also take place via an encrypted email client.
mitigations.rationale: Robust protocols ensure data integrity during transfers.

mitigations.description: Require explicit consent from participants before collecting data from third parties.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Consumer Education primarily relies on information collected directly from the individual and with the individual’s consent to collect information from third parties, such as those that offer or provide consumer financial products or services.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent ensures participants' control over their data.

mitigations.description: Implement strict publication policies to avoid accidental disclosure of sensitive participant information.
mitigations.evidence_quote: The CFPB may also share the products of Consumer Education or Response Data with the general public, but any products disclosed do not include direct identifying PII, and will typically be subject to further disclosure-protection procedures such as aggregation of response categories, generalized sentiments of Participants, rounding, exclusion of some variables, or exclusion of observations.
mitigations.rationale: Strict publication policies help prevent accidental disclosures.

risks.description: Personal data collected during Market Research in the Field could potentially be misused or improperly accessed.
risks.evidence_quote: When conducting Market Research in the Field, the CFPB may collaborate with third parties, including consumer financial products or service providers, innovators, entrepreneurs, non- profit or academic institutions, community-based organizations, or nonprofits; and social science researchers who are active in or may contribute insight into the consumer financial market.
risks.rationale: Collaborating with multiple third parties increases the risk of data breaches or unauthorized access.

risks.description: There is a risk that the personal data collected may be retained longer than necessary, leading to increased exposure to potential misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: For example, a financial company may request a waiver from financial regulation requiring disclosures of information to
risks.rationale: The lack of specific retention policies allows for indefinite storage of data, increasing exposure risks.

risks.description: Data subjects may not be fully informed about the nature of the research and their rights regarding their data.
risks.evidence_quote: What opportunities do I have for participation? Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
risks.rationale: General mention of notice and consent does not guarantee detailed information is provided to participants.

mitigations.description: Implement strict data access controls and encryption for data shared with third parties.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption and access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access or misuse of data.

mitigations.description: Establish clear data retention policies that specify the duration for which data will be stored.
mitigations.rationale: Specified retention periods minimize unnecessary data storage and associated risks.

mitigations.description: Provide detailed notices to participants explaining the purpose of the research, types of data collected, and their rights.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Generally applicable: Appropriate opportunities for notice, consent, access, and redress.
mitigations.rationale: Detailed notices ensure participants are fully informed about their data and their rights.

risks.description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive financial data during submission.
risks.evidence_quote: In 2018, financial institutions will submit HMDA information collected in 2017 to the CFPB about the following transactions:
risks.rationale: There is no specific mention of secure transmission protocols for the submission of HMDA data.

risks.description: Risk of misuse of detailed personal information included in the reports.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB will collect HMDA data, from certain financial institutions, that are required by Regulation C regarding originations of, purchases of, and applications for covered loans.
risks.rationale: The data includes personal information that could be misused if accessed improperly.

risks.description: Risk of non-compliance due to complex reporting requirements.
risks.evidence_quote: The 2015 HMDA rule narrows the scope of depository institutions subject to Regulation C in 2017.
risks.rationale: Financial institutions may struggle to comply with the detailed and changing regulations.

mitigations.description: Implement secure transmission protocols for data submissions.
mitigations.rationale: Secure transmission would prevent unauthorized access to sensitive financial data.

mitigations.description: Anonymize or aggregate personal data where feasible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing the specificity of personal details would mitigate the risk of misuse.

mitigations.description: Provide clear guidance and training on compliance requirements.
mitigations.rationale: Clear guidance would help financial institutions comply with complex regulations.

risks.description: Collection of sensitive personal information such as age and credit scores could potentially expose individuals to identity theft.
risks.evidence_quote: Age and credit score are new data points under the 2015 HMDA Rule. These data will be collected beginning in 2018 and first reported to Federal HMDA agencies, including the CFPB, in 2019.
risks.rationale: Personal details like age and credit scores can be used by malicious actors to impersonate individuals.

risks.description: Self-identification using disaggregated ethnic and racial categories might lead to profiling and discrimination.
risks.evidence_quote: Beginning in 2018, Regulation C will require lenders to permit applicants and borrowers to self-identify using disaggregated ethnic and racial categories.
risks.rationale: Disaggregated ethnic and racial categories can be misused to discriminate against certain groups.

risks.description: Quarterly reporting of HMDA data for large financial institutions increases the frequency of data exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: Beginning in 2020, larger covered financial institutions will submit HMDA data on a quarterly basis.
risks.rationale: More frequent data submissions increase the risk of unauthorized access or breaches.

risks.description: Public disclosure of HMDA data may reveal sensitive information about individuals' mortgage applications and loans.
risks.evidence_quote: See Regulation C, 12 C.F.R. § 1 003.1(c), effective Jan. 1, 2018 (requiring a financial institution, as defined in § 1 003.2(g), to the submit data to the appropriate federal agency for the financial institution, and to disclose certain data to the public, about covered loans for which the financial institution receives applications, or that it originates or purchases, and that are secured by a dwelling located in a state, the District of Columbia, or Commonwealth of Puerto Rico).
risks.rationale: Publicly available data can be exploited for various forms of misuse.

risks.description: Transferring HMDA data to multiple federal agencies increases the risk of data breaches.
