risks.rationale: Cloud storage introduces potential security vulnerabilities.

risks.description: Sensitive personal information such as SSNs and financial account numbers are collected and stored.

risks.rationale: Storage of sensitive data increases the risk of data breaches.

risks.description: Personal information is shared with other federal agencies and third parties without explicit consent.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for cloud storage.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and implement data minimization practices.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent from individuals before sharing their data with third parties.

risks.description: Service use and cost data could be misused for purposes beyond administrative and analytical needs.

mitigations.description: Implement robust encryption and access controls.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments.

risks.description: PII may be collected without explicit consent.

risks.description: Sensitive PII like mobile numbers are collected.

risks.rationale: Mobile numbers can be considered sensitive personal information and may be used for targeted communications.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent for collecting PII.
mitigations.rationale: Ensures that only necessary PII is collected with the individual's knowledge.

mitigations.description: Implement additional safeguards for sensitive PII.
mitigations.rationale: Protect sensitive information such as mobile numbers from unauthorized access and use.

mitigations.description: Encrypt stored PII.
mitigations.rationale: Ensure that PII is stored securely to prevent unauthorized access and breaches.

risks.description: The system lacks data analysis capabilities, potentially leading to inaccurate reporting.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for data transmitted over the internet.

mitigations.description: Integrate data analytics tools to enhance reporting accuracy.

risks.description: Sensitive personal information is stored in an unencrypted format.

mitigations.description: Require explicit user consent for storing and using photographs.

mitigations.description: Encrypt sensitive personal information stored in the system.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit user consent before sharing personal information with senior leadership.

risks.description: PII is stored without encryption.

risks.description: PII is shared with third parties without explicit consent.

risks.description: Consumer complaints containing sensitive information like Social Security Numbers may be stored insecurely.

risks.description: Collection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) for fake data during beta testing.

mitigations.description: Ensure all data, even fake data, is stored securely and follows strict access controls.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments to identify and mitigate system weaknesses.

risks.evidence_quote: Documents uploaded to the NBR System may include the following PII on individuals (e.g., consumer, consenting party, defendant) identified or listed in documents provided to the registry (e.g., covered orders): • Full name;13 • Title; • Work address; • Email address; and • Telephone number.

risks.evidence_quote: Finally, the NBR System maintains PII collected from CFPB Staff assigned to maintain the NBR System, which includes full names and email address, along with usernames and passwords.
risks.rationale: Credentialed users can access sensitive information without proper authorization controls.

risks.description: Public dissemination of sensitive information may lead to privacy breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: The Orders Rule allows the CFPB to publish some of the information collected from nonbanks for use by members of the public as well as other regulatory agencies.
risks.rationale: Publicly accessible information may expose individuals to potential harm.

mitigations.description: Implement strict data redaction policies for all covered orders before storing them in the system.
mitigations.rationale: Redacting sensitive information minimizes exposure risks.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict access controls and regular audits for PII access and usage.
mitigations.evidence_quote: All CFPB Staff with access to CFPB systems, such as the NBR System, must sign the CFPB “Acceptable Use of CFPB Information Technology Resources” policy.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls and audits help prevent unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular privacy training for CFPB staff to ensure compliance with privacy policies.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Finally, all CFPB Staff are required to comply with privacy policy and complete privacy training when they initially onboard and on an annual basis thereafter.

mitigations.description: Restrict public access to PII and only disclose aggregated data where possible.

mitigations.rationale: Aggregated data reduces the risk of exposing sensitive information to the public.

risks.description: PII about CFPB Staff and other individuals is collected and stored in the system.

risks.rationale: The system stores personal information which could be misused.

risks.rationale: Sensitive information is shared with another organization, which may increase the risk of data exposure.

risks.rationale: Personal information of individuals involved in enforcement matters could be misused if not properly protected.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for PII stored in the system.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security audits and training for staff handling personal information.

risks.description: Data breaches due to the storage of personally identifiable information (PII) in Salesforce.
risks.evidence_quote: Salesforce manages CFPB’s technical cloud infrastructure on behalf of the CFPB, including general cloud environment tools such as data storage, system computing resources (such as routers and firewalls, data centers), software maintenance (such as security patches and secure upgrades Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Salesforce Platform (August 2025)
risks.rationale: Data stored in the cloud is vulnerable to unauthorized access or breaches.

risks.description: Unauthorized access to PII by internal CFPB staff due to lack of strict access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: All third-party cloud systems that connect with Salesforce are assessed according CFPB’s assessment and authorization (A&A) processes to ensure risks are identified and mitigated prior to use. Authorized CFPB program managers, business product and system owners, system developers and business analysts, and other internal CFPB stakeholders and users, can access Salesforce to leverage these technical capabilities to build systems and applications in a secure, consistent method. (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Salesforce Platform (August 2025)
risks.rationale: Access controls are essential to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information.

risks.description: Potential misuse of PII by external parties if data is shared with third parties without proper authorization.
risks.evidence_quote: Individual Salesforce applications may share with external entities on a need to know basis. The entities with whom applications may share information are identified in application specific PIAs that can be found on the CFPB’s website located at https://www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/privacy-impact-assessments/. (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Salesforce Platform (August 2025)
risks.rationale: External sharing requires clear authorization to prevent misuse of PII.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for accessing Salesforce.
mitigations.rationale: Enhances security by requiring more than one method of authentication.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict role-based access control policies.
mitigations.rationale: Limits access to PII based on job roles to minimize unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Ensure all external sharing is documented and approved in application specific PIAs.
mitigations.rationale: Maintains accountability and compliance with sharing regulations.

risks.description: PII is collected from various sources without direct user consent.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program primarily uses PII collected by indirect sources such as CFPB employment applications and contractor onboarding forms housed within ABIS5 and HR Connect6, and from other federal agency sources such as USAstaffing7, USAccess8, and Login.gov.
risks.rationale: Without direct consent, users may not be aware that their data is being collected.

risks.description: PII is stored centrally, increasing the risk of data breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: The ICAM program centrally manages all staff (i.e., employees, contractors, detailees, volunteers, and interns) identification, authentication, and access privileges to all CFPB systems.
risks.rationale: Centralized storage can lead to a single point of failure if not adequately secured.

mitigations.description: Implement a mechanism for users to provide explicit consent before their data is collected.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent will ensure users are aware and agree to their data being collected.

mitigations.description: Enhance security measures to protect the central database containing PII.
mitigations.rationale: Stronger security measures will reduce the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches.

risks.description: PII of consumers and employees may be accessed by unauthorized individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES contains PII regarding consumers of depository and non-depository entities products as well as employees of those entities serving as points of contact. It also contains information about CFPB staff assigned to duties related to the supervision of these entities.
risks.rationale: Access to sensitive information by unauthorized individuals could lead to data breaches or misuse.

risks.description: PII may be shared with unauthorized recipients without proper authorization.
risks.evidence_quote: The SES established the CFPB Supervision Portal to facilitate the secure exchange of communication and files between external entities and state regulators.
risks.rationale: Unauthorized sharing could result in the exposure of sensitive personal information.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and authentication mechanisms.
mitigations.rationale: Enhanced access controls and authentication will reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Ensure that all data sharing is conducted through secure channels and with proper authorization.
mitigations.rationale: Proper authorization and secure data transfer methods will minimize the risk of unauthorized data sharing.

risks.description: Personal data, including Social Security Numbers, is stored in a database accessible to multiple parties.
risks.evidence_quote: The CRS is a database and information management system, which operates on a vendor-provided service and cloud platform.
risks.rationale: Data breaches could expose sensitive personal information.

risks.description: Sensitive information like Social Security Numbers are sometimes submitted with complaints, potentially leading to misuse.
risks.evidence_quote: For some complaints, submission of a Social Security Number can be helpful to validate the consumer’s identity and their association with a particular account, such as a credit report.
risks.rationale: SSNs are valuable for identity theft.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for the CRS database.
mitigations.rationale: Enhances security and reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit the collection of SSNs to only when necessary and use alternative methods to verify identities when possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reduces the exposure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Personal data may be accessed by unauthorized personnel due to the use of a contractor-owned environment.
risks.evidence_quote: To supplement CFPB’s eDiscovery workload, Enforcement has procured the services of a federal contractor to provide eDiscovery and litigation support services. However, these tools are housed in a contract-owned environment.
risks.rationale: The contractor environment introduces the risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Personal data could be exposed in case of a data breach in the contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: A data breach in the contractor environment could lead to exposure of sensitive personal information.

risks.description: There is a risk that personal data may not be adequately protected against physical theft or loss in the contractor-owned environment.
risks.rationale: Physical security measures in the contractor environment may differ from CFPB standards.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and authentication mechanisms for the contractor environment.
mitigations.rationale: This ensures that only authorized personnel can access the data.

mitigations.description: Establish a robust incident response plan to address potential data breaches.
mitigations.rationale: An incident response plan helps minimize damage in case of a breach.

mitigations.description: Require the contractor to implement physical security measures equivalent to CFPB standards.
mitigations.rationale: Ensures that physical security is maintained at the same level as at CFPB.

risks.description: Personal data of small business owners and employees could be exposed through the SBL system.
risks.evidence_quote: No information related to actual applicants or individuals associated with applicants is collected by the CFPB during beta-testing activities.
risks.rationale: While no actual personal data is collected during beta testing, the potential for exposure exists.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and monitoring to prevent unauthorized access to the system.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls and monitoring can help ensure that only authorized personnel can view sensitive information.

risks.description: Personal data of nonbank representatives and executives is stored in a system accessible to multiple staff members.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System maintains PII collected from nonbanks, including personally identifiable information (PII) collected as part of the registration and document management process. The NBR System also maintains PII on CFPB Staff authorized to access and manage the NBR System.
risks.rationale: Multiple staff members have access to sensitive PII.

risks.description: PII of individuals identified in covered orders may be stored without adequate safeguards.
risks.evidence_quote: Documents provided to the registry could include other PII as well, depending on the content of the document and applicable court and agency practices and rules. For example, a covered order could include additional PII regarding respondent’s counsel, officers, or other representatives, individual respondents, or a point of contact designated in a notice provision.
risks.rationale: PII of individuals in covered orders may be stored without specific safeguards.

risks.description: Sensitive information may be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
risks.evidence_quote: information may only be shared with CFPB employees, contractors, or consultants when such disclosure is relevant to the performance of their assigned duties.
risks.rationale: There is potential for unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

risks.description: Public access to PII through the helpdesk feature could lead to privacy breaches.
risks.evidence_quote: The NBR System also maintains the following PII on members of the public that submit a question related to the Orders Rule through the helpdesk feature: • Full name; and • Email address.
risks.rationale: Public access to PII through the helpdesk feature is possible.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for PII stored in the NBR System.
mitigations.rationale: Enhance data security and limit access to sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Develop specific guidelines and safeguards for storing PII in covered orders.
mitigations.rationale: Ensure proper handling and protection of sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with access control policies.
mitigations.rationale: Monitor and enforce access control policies to prevent unauthorized disclosures.

mitigations.description: Limit public access to non-sensitive information through the helpdesk feature.
mitigations.rationale: Reduce the risk of privacy breaches by limiting public access to sensitive data.

risks.description: Personal Identifiable Information (PII) is stored in a cloud-based system.
risks.evidence_quote: The system is hosted in CFPB’s Salesforce environment. Salesforce provides a cloud-based solution that allows the CFPB to develop and implement enterprise applications that focus on customer service, project management, and analytics.
risks.rationale: Cloud-based systems can be vulnerable to security breaches.

risks.description: PII is shared with external entities without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: Information maintained in the Enforcement Matter Management System is shared in accordance with all laws, regulations, policies, and applicable CFPB SORNs, or in response to FOIA requests.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII without explicit consent can lead to unauthorized access and misuse.

risks.description: PII is retained for long periods without clear retention policies.
risks.evidence_quote: The information in a matter record varies depending on the stage and complexity of the enforcement matter.
risks.rationale: Long-term retention of PII increases the risk of data breaches and unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Implement robust security measures for the cloud-based system.
mitigations.rationale: Enhance security to protect against unauthorized access and data breaches.

mitigations.description: Ensure explicit consent for sharing PII with external entities.
mitigations.rationale: Require explicit consent before sharing PII to prevent unauthorized disclosures.

mitigations.description: Establish clear retention policies for PII.
mitigations.rationale: Define retention periods to minimize the risk of data breaches and unauthorized access.

risks.description: PII may be stored temporarily on the GIS server.
risks.evidence_quote: Within a week after the final output has been transmitted, the PII is deleted from the GIS server.
risks.rationale: Temporary storage of PII increases the risk of accidental exposure.

risks.description: PII may be accessed by unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: Authorized GIS users are comprised of Bureau employees and contractors.
risks.rationale: Access by unauthorized users could lead to data breaches.

risks.description: Geocoded data may reveal sensitive information about individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: While the technology allows CFPB users to match and layer CPFB data with these public datasets to gain additional insights and context into a specific geographic location, no new PII is generated about individuals using this technology.
risks.rationale: Geocoded data can indirectly reveal sensitive personal information.

mitigations.description: Implement automated deletion of PII after processing.
mitigations.rationale: Automated deletion reduces the time PII is stored on the server.

mitigations.description: Enforce strict access controls and regular audits.
mitigations.rationale: Strict access controls and audits can prevent unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Conduct thorough data minimization and anonymization practices.
mitigations.rationale: Data minimization and anonymization reduce the risk of revealing sensitive information.

risks.description: Sensitive information, such as Social Security numbers and biometric information, is collected and stored.
risks.evidence_quote: The Directory Database includes PII regarding employees or others associated with institutions under the CFPB’s authority, including: • Name; • Age and date of birth • Contact information such as address, email address, and phone number; • Social Security number (SSN), alien number, passport number, driver’s license or state identification number, or other unique number used to establish identity of the owner or responsible person; and • Title, position, or other identifying information about the person as it relates to their association with an organization.
risks.rationale: Storing sensitive information increases the risk of data breaches.

risks.description: Information is collected from multiple sources without direct notice to individuals.
risks.evidence_quote: However, the CFPB may also collect PII from third parties, including existing federal databases and other agencies responsible for related regulatory functions. In such cases, individuals may not receive actual notice that the CFPB has collected information about them.
risks.rationale: Lack of direct notice may violate individuals' right to be informed about data collection.

risks.description: The system does not verify the accuracy and completeness of the collected data.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB presently gathers the information from federal, state, and local data sources and does not take steps to verify the accuracy or completeness of such data.
risks.rationale: Unverified data could lead to incorrect decisions or actions based on inaccurate information.

risks.description: The system retains information indefinitely until NARA approves a records disposition schedule.
risks.evidence_quote: The CFPB maintains computer and paper records indefinitely until NARA approves the CFPB’s records disposition schedule.
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention increases the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for sensitive information.
mitigations.rationale: Enhances security and reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Provide direct notice to individuals about data collection from third parties.
mitigations.rationale: Ensures individuals are informed and can exercise their rights.

mitigations.description: Implement a data validation process to verify the accuracy and completeness of collected data.
mitigations.rationale: Reduces the risk of using inaccurate data for decision-making.

mitigations.description: Establish a records retention schedule and dispose of outdated information.
mitigations.rationale: Limits the duration data is at risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: Collection of personally identifiable information (PII) without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: We will only collect your directly identifiable PII through ConsumerFinance.gov when you knowingly provide it to us.
risks.rationale: Users might be unaware that their PII could be collected without explicit consent.

risks.description: Use of Google Analytics to track user behavior.
risks.evidence_quote: Google Analytics aids CFPB in evaluating aggregate web traffic to ConsumerFinance.gov to be able to inform future changes and upgrades to the site based on former trends and behaviors, and possibly add new resources or products when there is a demand.
risks.rationale: Tracking user behavior could lead to profiling or loss of privacy.

mitigations.description: Clearly inform users about what data is collected and obtain explicit consent.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent ensures users are aware of data collection practices.

mitigations.description: Limit the amount of data collected and anonymize data where possible.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing data collection minimizes privacy risks associated with tracking.

risks.description: Social Security Numbers (SSNs) are collected and transmitted to Experian without encryption.
risks.evidence_quote: Social security numbers are transmitted to Experian to determine a user's credit worthiness to purchase a vehicle.
risks.rationale: Transmitting SSNs in clear text increases the risk of exposure.

risks.description: PII is collected from third parties involved in accidents and stored in unencrypted formats.
risks.evidence_quote: The information is collected through an online screen by the authorized users (Accident Management Specialist) and stored in the database for retrieval and sending the data to OCFO Pegasys System.
risks.rationale: Storing PII in unencrypted formats poses a risk of unauthorized access.

risks.description: PII from third parties is shared with OCFO without proper security measures.
risks.evidence_quote: When GSA seeks to recover expenses for an accident/incident in which a nongovernment 3rd party is at fault, a file of requisite data is transmitted to OCFO.
risks.rationale: Sharing PII without encryption exposes it to potential breaches.

mitigations.description: Encrypt SSNs during transmission and storage.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption protects SSNs from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Encrypt PII from third parties before storing in the database.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption ensures the security of PII stored in the database.

mitigations.description: Ensure data transmitted to OCFO is encrypted.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the risk of data exposure during transmission.

risks.description: Personal data may be accessed by unauthorized personnel within OLA.
risks.evidence_quote: Each staffer account request is reviewed and approved by OLA CS staff.
risks.rationale: Without strict access controls, unauthorized personnel could access sensitive personal data.

risks.description: Sensitive information may be stored indefinitely without clear retention guidelines.
risks.evidence_quote: OLA Tracking also stores all communications and documents connected to the inquiry.
risks.rationale: Lack of defined retention policies may lead to unnecessary storage of sensitive data.

risks.description: Data breaches could compromise personal information due to cloud storage.
risks.rationale: Storing data in the cloud increases the risk of data breaches.

risks.description: Multifactor authentication might not be applied consistently to all users.
risks.rationale: If MFA is not consistently enforced, some users may remain vulnerable to unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access control policies.
mitigations.rationale: Ensure only authorized personnel have access to sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Establish clear data retention policies.
mitigations.rationale: Define how long data should be retained to minimize storage risks.

mitigations.description: Enhance security measures for cloud storage.
mitigations.rationale: Implement robust security protocols to protect against data breaches.

mitigations.description: Enforce multifactor authentication across all user accounts.
mitigations.rationale: Ensure consistent application of MFA to reduce unauthorized access risks.

risks.description: Personal data may be accessed by unauthorized personnel.
risks.evidence_quote: The term “service use and cost data” includes, but is not limited to, medical claims data, pharmacy claims data, encounter data, and provider data. This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted because ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program (e.g., annuitants who suspended their FEHB or PSHB coverage).
risks.rationale: The system handles sensitive personal data that could be misused if accessed by unauthorized personnel.

risks.description: Data breaches could lead to the exposure of personal information.
risks.evidence_quote: This Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is being conducted because ROVR collects, maintains, and uses personally identifiable information (PII) about FEHB and PSHB enrollees, annuitants, and their family members, as well as eligible employees and annuitants who have not enrolled in the FEHB and PSHB Program (e.g., annuitants who suspended their FEHB or PSHB coverage).
risks.rationale: Sensitive personal data stored in ROVR could be exposed if a data breach occurs.

risks.description: Lack of proper anonymization techniques could lead to re-identification of individuals.
risks.rationale: Without proper anonymization, personally identifiable information (PII) could potentially be re-identified, leading to privacy risks.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and authentication mechanisms.
mitigations.rationale: To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive personal data.

mitigations.description: Regularly perform security audits and penetration testing.
mitigations.rationale: To identify and mitigate vulnerabilities that could lead to data breaches.

mitigations.description: Apply robust anonymization techniques to protect against re-identification.
mitigations.rationale: To ensure that personally identifiable information (PII) cannot be re-identified, thus protecting individual privacy.

risks.description: SSNs are stored in plaintext.
risks.evidence_quote: "their social security number (SSN) (which is stored as ‘Debtor ID’ in ABCO)",
risks.rationale: Storing SSNs in plaintext is a significant privacy risk.

risks.description: Data is retained indefinitely without explicit opt-out.
risks.evidence_quote: "ABCO data on the mainframe is retained indefinitely.",
risks.rationale: Indefinite retention without user consent is a privacy risk.

risks.description: Access controls are not explicitly detailed.
risks.evidence_quote: "Access is determined by agencies functional managers and submitted by the agency security officers.",
risks.rationale: Lack of detailed access controls can lead to unauthorized access or misuse of data.

risks.description: Transmissions are made via unencrypted methods.
risks.evidence_quote: "Agencies submit data and file transfers via connect direct and secure FTP over a VPN connection.",
risks.rationale: Unencrypted data transmission poses a risk of interception and data theft.

risks.description: No notice was given to individuals prior to collection.
risks.evidence_quote: "No. The ABCO system uses personal data provided by agencies to generate reports or notices.",
risks.rationale: Absence of prior notice to individuals can lead to non-compliance with privacy regulations.

mitigations.description: Encrypt SSNs stored in the system.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption would protect sensitive data from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Implement a retention policy with periodic review and deletion options.
mitigations.rationale: A more granular retention policy would allow for regular data purging and compliance with privacy laws.

mitigations.description: Document and enforce strict access control policies.
mitigations.rationale: Detailed access control policies would ensure that only authorized personnel have access to sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Use fully encrypted connections for all data transmissions.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption during transmission would prevent data interception and ensure secure data transfer.

mitigations.description: Provide notice to individuals prior to data collection.
mitigations.rationale: Prior notice would inform individuals of data collection practices and enhance transparency.

risks.description: There is a risk that the system may inadvertently collect unnecessary PII.
risks.evidence_quote: Information in the system will be used to document proposed policies and program activities for approval by USDA officials.
risks.rationale: This could lead to over-collection of PII beyond what is necessary.

risks.description: The system may not adequately protect PII from unauthorized access.
risks.rationale: The system needs robust security measures to prevent unauthorized access to PII.

mitigations.description: Implement data minimization principles to collect only essential PII.
mitigations.rationale: This will reduce the amount of PII stored and minimize the risk of over-collection.

mitigations.description: Ensure the system implements strong encryption and access controls.
mitigations.rationale: This will help protect PII from unauthorized access.

risks.description: Personal information of complainants, including names, addresses, and phone numbers, may be accessed by unauthorized users.
risks.evidence_quote: Only designated/approved users have access to the system
risks.rationale: There is no explicit statement regarding the security measures to prevent unauthorized access.

risks.description: Personal information may be stored in a way that could allow for data breaches, given the system is connected to the public internet.
risks.evidence_quote: CRES is co-located at MicroPact Engineering, Inc. MicroPact Engineering provides system, network, development, and administrative security under contract with The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR).
risks.rationale: The system is connected to the public internet, which increases the risk of data breaches.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and authentication mechanisms.
mitigations.rationale: This would ensure that only authorized personnel can access the system.

mitigations.description: Deploy advanced cybersecurity measures, including firewalls and intrusion detection systems.
mitigations.rationale: These measures would help protect against unauthorized access and data breaches.

risks.description: Photographic images could be used to identify individuals, potentially compromising their privacy.
risks.evidence_quote: Photographic image (photographs are at the discretion of the user and are not required), and Other information that may be seen as personal (there is an “About Me” section within the Salesforce model that is not restricted as to what the user can input.
risks.rationale: Photographs can be linked to names, creating a privacy concern.

risks.description: Personal identification numbers (such as parking permit numbers and building permit numbers) may be collected and stored, posing a risk of unauthorized access.
risks.evidence_quote: Miscellaneous identification numbers (Parking permit number and building permit number)
risks.rationale: These numbers are sensitive and could be misused if accessed improperly.

risks.description: Information is shared with senior leadership and various USDA departments through Tableau dashboards and reports, which could lead to inappropriate disclosure.
risks.evidence_quote: Information may be shared with senior leadership across USDA through a series of Tableau dashboards and reports for the purpose of promoting data-driven decisions.
risks.rationale: Sharing sensitive information through unsecured channels could result in data breaches or misuse.

mitigations.description: Implement a policy requiring users to disable the photo upload feature.
mitigations.rationale: Disabling photo uploads would reduce the risk of identifying individuals.

mitigations.description: Encrypt personal identification numbers during storage and transmission.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption would protect these sensitive numbers from unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Ensure all Tableau dashboards and reports are secured and require authentication for access.
mitigations.rationale: Securing access to dashboards would prevent unauthorized viewing and misuse of the data.

risks.description: Sensitive PII is stored without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: ePACS generally handles physical access Security Management Information including: x Physical access card status x Physical access card category x Physical access card expiration date x Physical access card holder emergency response responsibilities The ePACS application generates access rights based on authoritative data elements, which are: o Federal Agency Smart Credential Number (FASC-N) o Card Category o Card Status o Card Expiration Date o Photo o First Name o Middle Name o Last Name o Employee Type o Employee Status o Emergency Responder o Department o Agency o Sub-agency o City o State o Data of birth (visitors only registered but not stored)
risks.rationale: The system stores sensitive PII without explicit user consent.

risks.description: PII is shared with external organizations without explicit consent.
risks.evidence_quote: If information contained in ePACS is shared outside of USDA it is consistent with applicable laws and policy. A SORN is pending to cover the collection of data for ePACS, see section 6.1.
risks.rationale: The system shares PII with external organizations without explicit consent.

risks.description: PII is retained longer than necessary.
risks.evidence_quote: Information within ePACS will be retained for 5.5 calendar years. ePACS keep 6 months of live data and 5 years of archived data.
risks.rationale: The system retains PII for 5.5 years, which is longer than necessary.

risks.description: PII is accessible to unauthorized users due to poor access controls.
risks.evidence_quote: 8.2 Will Department contractors have access to the system? Yes. Access to ePACS will be granted for both USDA employees and select contractors with appropriate background checks and security clearances in place.
risks.rationale: The system grants access to contractors without specifying detailed access controls.

mitigations.description: Implement explicit consent mechanisms for storing PII.
mitigations.rationale: Users should give explicit consent before their PII is stored.

mitigations.description: Ensure explicit consent for sharing PII with external organizations.
mitigations.rationale: Users should give explicit consent before their PII is shared with external organizations.

mitigations.description: Reduce the retention period to the minimum necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Only retain PII for the minimum time necessary.

mitigations.description: Implement detailed access controls for contractors.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls should be implemented to ensure that only authorized users can access PII.

risks.description: Personal data may be accessed by unauthorized users due to vulnerabilities in the authentication process.
risks.evidence_quote: USDA’s eAuthentication (eAUTH) solution serves as the centralized authentication service for USDA employees to access USDA Web Services, including access to the FR ASCCPS application.
risks.rationale: Without robust authentication measures, unauthorized access could occur.

risks.description: Data may be exposed during transmission due to outdated encryption standards.
risks.evidence_quote: Data leaving the system/application is secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 encryption authentication schemas.
risks.rationale: Using TLS 1.2 encryption might not be sufficient against modern threats.

risks.description: Traveler preferences and transaction data could be used for unauthorized profiling or marketing purposes.
risks.evidence_quote: The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: There is no explicit statement that data will not be used for such purposes.

mitigations.description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all user access.
mitigations.rationale: Multi-factor authentication significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Update to the latest version of TLS encryption.
mitigations.rationale: Using the latest encryption standard improves data security.

mitigations.description: Clearly communicate data usage policies and obtain explicit consent for any profiling activities.
mitigations.rationale: Explicit consent ensures that data is used only as intended.

risks.description: Data is retained for a minimum of six years, which may exceed legal requirements and employee expectations.
risks.evidence_quote: Bill related data is retained for a minimum of six full years.
risks.rationale: Excessive data retention can lead to unnecessary storage costs and potential privacy concerns.

risks.description: Traveler preferences and patterns are analyzed without explicit consent from users.
risks.evidence_quote: The system analyzes and uses the data to create a predictive pattern for preferred airline seating, rental car companies, hotel details, etc.
risks.rationale: Analysis of personal data without user consent can infringe on privacy rights.

mitigations.description: Review and update the data retention policy to comply with the least restrictive legal requirements and align with employee expectations.
mitigations.rationale: Aligning with legal requirements and expectations can reduce privacy risks.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent from users before analyzing their travel preferences and patterns.
mitigations.rationale: User consent is essential for ethical and lawful data processing.

risks.description: Personal identification numbers (e.g., Social Security numbers) are stored.
risks.evidence_quote: "data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data"
risks.rationale: Storing SSNs increases the risk of identity theft.

risks.description: Financial data such as bank account numbers and check information are stored.
risks.evidence_quote: "data elements include Name, Date of birth, Address information, Personal identification number (e.g. social security number), and financial data (check numbers, bank account numbers, and cancelled and returned check information)."
risks.rationale: Storing financial data can lead to fraud and financial loss.

mitigations.description: Implement encryption for sensitive data like SSNs.
mitigations.rationale: Encryption reduces the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information.

mitigations.description: Limit access to financial data to authorized personnel only.
mitigations.rationale: Access controls minimize the risk of accidental or intentional exposure of financial data.

risks.description: Personal data is retained indefinitely, which could lead to potential misuse or unauthorized access over time.
risks.evidence_quote: Information is retained in perpetuity.
risks.rationale: Long-term storage increases the risk of data breaches and misuse.

risks.description: Sensitive case-related data and personally identifiable information (PII) are stored without adequate protection mechanisms.
risks.rationale: The system does not specify any additional security measures beyond the secure login page.

risks.description: Historical data is retained for 20 years, which could increase storage costs and risks.

mitigations.description: Implement stricter access controls and encryption for personal data.

risks.description: Personal Identifiable Information (PII) is stored indefinitely without periodic purging.

risks.description: PII is shared with a limited number of National, State, and County Office FSA employees without explicit consent.

mitigations.description: Obtain explicit consent from individuals before sharing their PII with employees.

risks.description: PII is temporarily stored in memory and cache during user sessions.

risks.description: PII is requested from an external system (SCIMS) without additional security measures.

mitigations.description: Implement secure session management to ensure PII is not stored in memory or cache.

mitigations.description: Establish a formal agreement with SCIMS to ensure their system meets appropriate security standards.

risks.description: Personal data is stored indefinitely without a clear expiration policy.

risks.description: Sensitive personal information (PII) is stored and processed in the system.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and encryption for PII stored in the system.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular data quality checks and implement data validation procedures.

risks.description: Personal data, including sensitive information like social security numbers and financial data, is stored indefinitely without a defined retention schedule.

risks.description: Data is retained indefinitely without a defined retention schedule.

risks.description: PII may be stored indefinitely without explicit user consent.

risks.description: PII may be accessible to unauthorized third parties through the use of third-party applications.

mitigations.description: Provide users with options to opt-out of indefinite PII storage.

mitigations.description: Conduct regular security assessments of third-party applications to ensure compliance with security standards.

risks.description: Data transmission over unencrypted channels could expose sensitive information.

risks.rationale: HTTPS ensures secure communication, but the use of 'occurs' suggests potential issues.

risks.description: Temporary storage of DOL case numbers could lead to unauthorized access.

mitigations.description: Limit the retention period of DOL case numbers to the minimum necessary.
mitigations.rationale: Reducing retention periods minimizes the window for data exposure.

risks.description: PII is stored in unencrypted form in various databases.

risks.rationale: Unencrypted PII can be accessed by unauthorized personnel.

risks.description: PII is accessible to all staff without proper authorization.

risks.rationale: Lack of strict access controls increases the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information.

risks.description: PII may be exposed during data transmission over unsecured networks.

risks.description: PII is retained indefinitely in some cases, beyond necessary periods.
risks.evidence_quote: Information on most applications is retained indefinitely (permanent records).
risks.rationale: Retaining PII longer than necessary increases the risk of data breaches and non-compliance.

mitigations.description: Encrypt PII stored in databases.

mitigations.description: Implement strict access controls and least privilege model.
mitigations.evidence_quote: DRMS access is determined via a Level 2 eAuth ID and password on a valid need-to-know basis, determined by requirements to perform applicable official duties.
mitigations.rationale: Least privilege ensures only authorized personnel can access sensitive data.

mitigations.description: Ensure all data transmission uses secure protocols like HTTPS.

mitigations.description: Implement a retention policy that complies with NARA guidelines.
mitigations.evidence_quote: Per the NRCS-1 System of Record Notice (SORN), ‘Records are maintained as long as the owner, operator, producer, or participant qualifies for conservation programs.’
mitigations.rationale: Complying with NARA guidelines ensures PII is retained only as necessary.

risks.rationale: SSNs and EINs are sensitive identifiers that could be misused.

risks.rationale: Sharing sensitive data without explicit consent can violate individual privacy rights.

risks.rationale: Retaining data indefinitely could expose individuals to prolonged privacy risks.
